title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE SALARIES, PENSIONS AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, to provide for the grant of Constituency Travelling Allowance and enhancement of payment for telephone calls.
scope: This act applies to members of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. It amends the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2002, and it comes into force with effect from April 1, 2003.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 8 of the principal Act by substituting 'ten rupees' for 'eight rupees'.

Amends section 12 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary values and replacing a clause related to rent with a provision for rent as specified by the Board, and also enhances the monthly allowance for telephone calls.

important_rules: Rule 1: Members are entitled to a Constituency Travelling Allowance of fifteen thousand rupees per annum, payable in two equal installments in April and October.
Rule 2: The monthly allowance for meeting expenditure on telephone calls is enhanced to six thousand five hundred rupees per month.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, which are enforced upon commencement.

rights: Right to receive Constituency Travelling Allowance.
Right to receive an enhanced monthly allowance for telephone calls.
Right to receive rent as specified by the Board.

key_procedures: Constituency Travelling Allowance is payable in two equal installments in April and October.
Rent is to be specified by the Board from time to time.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The act comes into force from April 1, 2003.
The amendments replace specific monetary values for allowances and reimbursements for members of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.

title: THE KARNATAKA TOWN AND COUNTRY PLANNING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, to provide for the definition and regulation of heritage buildings and heritage precincts, to replace comprehensive development plans and outline development plans with master plans for procedural simplification, and to introduce provisions for deemed changes in land use.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. It affects planning authorities, their jurisdictions, and the planning and development of areas within those jurisdictions.

key_definitions.heritage_building: A building possessing architectural, aesthetic, historic or cultural values which is declared as a heritage building by the Planning Authority or any other competent authority within whose jurisdiction such building is situated.
key_definitions.heritage_precinct: An area comprising heritage building or buildings and precincts thereof or related places declared as such by the Planning Authority or any other Competent Authority within whose jurisdiction such area is situated.
key_definitions.master_plan: A plan for the development or re-development of the area within the jurisdiction of a planning authority.
key_definitions.building_line: The line up to which the plinth of a building adjoining a street may lawfully extend and includes the lines prescribed, if any, in any scheme.
key_definitions.floor_area_ratio: The quotient of the ratio of the combined gross floor area of all the floors, excepting areas specifically exempted under the regulations, to the total area of the plot.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by omitting clause (1-d) and inserting definitions for 'Heritage Building', 'Heritage Precinct', and 'Master Plan'.
Substitutes the heading 'OUTLINE DEVELOPMENT PLAN' in Chapter III of the principal Act with 'MASTER PLAN'.
Substitutes Section 9 of the principal Act, detailing the process for the preparation, publication, and submission of a Master Plan by a planning authority.
Amends Section 10 of the principal Act regarding the declaration of intention to prepare a Master Plan, public notices, and inspection of plans.
Substitutes Section 12 of the principal Act, outlining the contents of a Master Plan, including zoning, street patterns, reservations, and special control areas.
Substitutes Section 13 of the principal Act, detailing the process for the approval of a Master Plan by the State Government, including public comments and final approval.
Inserts new sections concerning Interim Master Plans, preparation of Master Plans for additional areas, and deeming existing development plans as Master Plans.

important_rules: Every planning authority shall prepare and publish a master plan for its jurisdiction not later than two years from the date of declaration of the local planning area.
If a planning authority fails to prepare a master plan, the State Government may authorize the Director to prepare it and recover the cost from the planning authority.
A Master Plan shall consist of maps and documents indicating development and improvement proposals, including zoning, street patterns, recreational areas, and special control areas.
The State Government shall give final approval to the Master Plan after considering public comments and recommendations from the planning authority.
Pending the preparation of a Master Plan, a Planning Authority may prepare an Interim Master Plan for its area.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Planning Authority and the State Government, acting through the Director.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the preparation, approval, and enforcement of Master Plans and Interim Master Plans as per the provisions of the Act.

rights: Public right to inspect Master Plans and related reports.
Public right to provide comments on proposed Master Plans.
duties: Duty of Planning Authority to prepare and publish Master Plans and Interim Master Plans.
Duty of Planning Authority to carry out surveys of its area.
Duty of Planning Authority to notify the public about its intention to prepare a Master Plan and invite suggestions.
Duty of the State Government to approve Master Plans.
Duty to conserve Heritage Buildings and Heritage Precincts.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Master Plan.
Obligation for planning authorities to prepare and publish plans within prescribed timelines.
Obligation to recover costs from defaulting planning authorities if the Director prepares a Master Plan.

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of Master Plan by Planning Authority to the State Government.
Publication of Master Plan and invitation of public comments.
Consideration of public comments and resubmission of the plan with recommendations.
Final approval of the Master Plan by the State Government.
Publication and permanent display of the finally approved Master Plan.
administration: The Karnataka Town and Country Planning Department, through Planning Authorities and the Director of Town Planning.
important_notes: The Act deems existing Outline Development Plans or Comprehensive Development Plans published prior to the commencement of this Amendment Act as declarations of intention to make a Master Plan.
The Act makes provisions for the deemed change of land use from commercial or industrial to residential, and from industrial to commercial.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, to dispense with the use of stamps and stamp papers and to start using impressed stamps.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, affecting instruments and their stamping within the state.

key_definitions.duly_stamped: An instrument that bears an impressed stamp of not less than the proper amount, and such stamp has been impressed in accordance with the law in force in the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.impressed_stamp: Includes impression made with a franking machine, or a certificate or endorsement made and attested as prescribed by the Deputy Commissioner or the authorised or proper officer in the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.stamp_paper: Means a paper bearing the impressed stamp.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it will come into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting definitions for 'Duly stamped' and 'Impressed stamp', and inserting a new definition for 'Stamp' and 'Stamp paper'.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act by substituting clause (b) in sub-section (2), regarding the manner of recording certificates of stamp.
Omit sections 11 and 12 of the principal Act.
Omit section 60 of the principal Act.
Substitutes section 63 of the principal Act with a new section titled 'Penalty for franking, recording certificate or embossing contrary to the Act or the rules'.

Provides for the continued application of provisions of the principal Act as they were in force immediately before the commencement of this Act, to stamps used or in the process of use, or to any proceedings pending or commenced after such date.
Empowers the Government to make necessary or expedient provisions by notification in the official Gazette to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Instruments must bear an impressed stamp of not less than the proper amount, impressed according to law.
Rule 2: 'Impressed stamp' can be through franking machine or a certificate/endorsement made and attested by prescribed authorities.
Rule 3: A person authorized to frank, record certificates, or emboss duty, if acting contrary to the Act or rules, shall be punishable.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than one month but not exceeding six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, for contravention of the Act or rules by authorized persons (franking, recording certificate, embossing).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka, through notifications and prescribed authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penal provisions for contravention of the Act and rules, and by Government notifications to appoint commencement dates and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to have instruments stamped with the proper impressed stamp.
duties: Duty to ensure instruments bear impressed stamps of the proper amount.
Duty to ensure stamps are impressed according to law.
obligations: Obligation for authorized persons not to act in contravention of the Act or rules regarding franking, recording certificates, or embossing duty.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointing the commencement date of the Act via government notification.
Procedure for the Government to issue notifications for removing difficulties.
Procedure for issuing certificates or endorsements by the Deputy Commissioner or authorised officer as part of impressed stamps.
administration: The Government of Karnataka, Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is involved in the enactment and likely oversight. Specific administrative roles are implied for the Deputy Commissioner or authorised officers in defining 'impressed stamp'.
important_notes: The Act is a second amendment to the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
The amendment aims to transition from traditional stamps and stamp papers to the use of impressed stamps.
Transitional provisions ensure continuity for stamps in use or proceedings initiated before the amendment's commencement.

title: The Karnataka Prohibition of Violence Against Medicare Service Personnel and Damage to Property in Medicare Service Institutions Act, 2009
purpose: To prohibit violence against medicare service personnel and damage to property in medicare service institutions and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to all Medicare Service Institutions in Karnataka, the personnel working in them, and any person who commits violence against such personnel or damages property within these institutions.

key_definitions.medicare_service_institutions: Includes all institutions providing medicare services under State/Central Government or Local Bodies control, private hospitals, private maternity homes, and private nursing homes for reception and treatment of sick, injured, or infirm individuals. Also includes maternity or convalescent homes.
key_definitions.medicare_service_personnel: Includes Registered Medical Practitioners (with provisional registration), Registered nurses, Medical students, Nursing students, and Para medical workers employed in Medicare Service Institutions.
key_definitions.offender: Any person who commits, attempts to commit, abets, or incites the commission of violence under this Act, either individually, as part of a group, or an organization.
key_definitions.violence: Activities causing harm, injury, endangering life, intimidation, obstruction, or hindrance to medicare service personnel in the discharge of their duties, or damage to property in a medicare service institution.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Prohibition of Violence against Medicare Service Personnel and Damage to Property in Medicare Service Institutions Act, 2009, and that it comes into force at once.
Provides definitions for 'Medicare Service Institutions', 'Medicare service personnel', 'Offender', and 'Violence' as used in the Act.
Prohibits any violence against medicare service personnel or damage to property in a medicare service institution.
Prescribes punishment for contravention of Section 3 with imprisonment for three years and a fine up to fifty thousand rupees.
States that offences committed under Section 3 are cognizable and non-bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of loss for the damage caused to the property
main_sections.description: In addition to the punishment under Section 4, the offender is liable for a penalty twice the amount of the purchase price of damaged medical equipment and property loss, as determined by the Court. If not paid, it can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other existing laws.

important_rules: Rule 1: Violence against medicare service personnel is prohibited.
Rule 2: Damage to property within a medicare service institution is prohibited.
Rule 3: Offenders are liable for imprisonment and/or fine.
Rule 4: Offenders must compensate for the damage caused to property and medical equipment.

penalties: Imprisonment for a period of three years.
Fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.
Penalty of twice the amount of the purchase price of medical equipment damaged and loss caused to the property.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Courts and law enforcement agencies responsible for cognizable and non-bailable offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are cognizable and non-bailable. Recovery of penalties for property damage can be done under the provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, as arrears of land revenue.

rights: Right to discharge duty without hindrance or intimidation.
Right to be protected from violence.
Right to have property within medicare institutions protected.
duties: Duty to not commit violence against medicare service personnel.
Duty to not damage property in medicare service institutions.
obligations: Obligation to pay penalties for damages caused.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Cognizance of offences by the appropriate authority (implied courts).
Trial of offenders under the Act.
Determination of the amount of loss and damage to property by the Court.
Recovery of penalties for property damage as arrears of land revenue if not paid.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as per the signing authority).
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.
The provisions of this Act are supplementary to other existing laws.

title: THE KARNATAKA DEVADASIS (PROHIBITION OF DEDICATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1982, to empower magistrates to issue injunctions prohibiting dedication, provide for the rescue, care, protection, welfare, and rehabilitation of women from dedication, make offenses cognizable and non-bailable, and appoint Devadasis dedication prohibition officers with powers to prevent such dedication.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1982, and applies to the State of Karnataka. It aims to prohibit the dedication of women as Devadasis.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) (Amendment) Act, 2009, and that it comes into force at once.

Inserts new sections (3A, 3B, 3C, 3D, and 3E) into the Karnataka Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1982, detailing powers of magistrates, rehabilitation measures, offense classification, appointment of prohibition officers, and their status as public servants.

important_rules: Rule: The District Magistrate or Executive Magistrate, upon being satisfied that a dedication in contravention of the Act is about to take place, shall issue a prohibitory injunction. This can be done suo motu or upon application/complaint. Notice and an opportunity to show cause are generally required, except in cases of urgency where an interim injunction can be issued.

Rule: The State Government shall take all necessary steps to rehabilitate women rescued from dedication through the 'Devadasi Rehabilitation Programme', including counseling, economic empowerment, protection, and shelter, aiming for self-sustainability.
Rule: An offence punishable under this Act shall be cognizable and non-bailable.

Rule: The State Government may appoint Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers, who will have jurisdiction over specified areas. Deputy Directors, Assistant Directors of the Women and Child Development Department, or Project Officers will also serve as these officers within their respective jurisdictions.

Rule: Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers have duties including preventing dedication, collecting evidence, advising against dedication, creating awareness, sensitizing the community, reporting incidents, and discharging other functions assigned by the State Government.
Rule: Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers are deemed to be public servants under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

penalties: Disobeying a prohibitory injunction issued under sub-section (1) of Section 3A is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years but shall not be less than two years, or with a fine which shall not be less than rupees two thousand but which may extend to rupees ten thousand, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate, Executive Magistrate, and Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through issuance of prohibitory injunctions, taking suo motu cognizance, investigations, rehabilitation programs, and by exercising powers vested in them as public servants. The Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers can also be invested with powers of a police officer.

rights: Right to receive counselling, awareness, and economic empowerment through income-generating activities for rescued women.
Right to protection or shelter in a remand home up to six months for rescued women.
Right to be heard before an injunction is issued, unless in cases of urgency.
Right to apply for rescission or alteration of an injunction.
duties: Duty of the District Magistrate or Executive Magistrate to issue injunctions prohibiting dedication.
Duty of the State Government to take necessary steps for rehabilitation of rescued women.
Duty of Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers to prevent dedication, collect evidence, advise the community, create awareness, and report incidents.
obligations: Obligation for any person to comply with a prohibitory injunction issued by a Magistrate.

Obligation for members of a Gram Panchayath, Municipality, Government, public sector undertaking, or non-governmental organization to assist the Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officer when requested.

key_procedures: Procedure for issuing prohibitory injunctions: Application or complaint is made to the District Magistrate/Executive Magistrate, or they take suo motu cognizance. Notice is issued to the concerned parties, who are given an opportunity to show cause. In urgent cases, an interim injunction can be issued without notice. The injunction can be confirmed or vacated after hearing the parties. The Magistrate can also rescind or alter the injunction.

Procedure for rehabilitation: The State Government initiates the Devadasi Rehabilitation Programme, involving counseling, awareness, economic empowerment through income-generating activities, and providing shelter if necessary.
administration: Women and Child Development Department, Government of Karnataka (implied through the role of Deputy Directors, Assistant Directors, and Project Officers).
important_notes: Interim injunctions can be issued without notice in cases of urgency.
Devadasi Dedication Prohibition Officers are considered public servants.
The Act aims to prevent en-mass dedication, particularly on days like full moon during Jathras.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION ACT, 2020
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the services of the Financial year 2020-21, in pursuance of Article 204 of the Constitution of India.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and pertains to the financial year 2020-21. It covers the appropriation of funds for various services and purposes as detailed in the schedule.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation Act, 2020.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 24473357.15 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2020-21
main_sections.description: This section authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees two crores forty-four lakhs seventy-three thousand three hundred fifty seven lakh and fifteen thousand only, towards defraying the several charges to be paid during the financial year 2020-21 in respect of the services specified in column 2 of the Schedule.

This section states that the sums authorized to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the State Legislature and executive authorities responsible for financial management.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of passing the Appropriation Bill and subsequent executive actions for fund disbursement as per the sanctioned amounts.

rights: The right of the State Legislature to authorize payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund.
duties: Duty to enact legislation for appropriation of funds for the financial year.
Duty to ensure that funds are used for the specified services and purposes.
obligations: Obligation to maintain the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Obligation to adhere to the provisions of Article 204 of the Constitution of India.

key_procedures: Introduction of an Appropriation Bill in the State Legislature.
Debate and approval of the Bill by the Legislature.
Assent of the Governor to the Bill.
Authorization of payment and appropriation of funds as specified in the Act and Schedule.
Disbursement of funds for the services and purposes outlined in the Schedule.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signature of the Secretary). The overall financial administration would involve the Finance Department and other relevant departments as per the schedule.
important_notes: The total appropriation authorized by this Act is Rupees 2,44,73,357.15 Lakhs, which is equivalent to Rupees 24,473,357,150.
The schedule provides a breakdown of appropriations for various departments and services, categorized as Revenue and Capital expenditure.
The Act is published in the official Gazette under clause (3) of Article 348 of the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA PREVENTION OF SLAUGHTER AND PRESERVATION OF CATTLE ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for a comprehensive legislation for the prevention of slaughter and preservation of cattle in the State of Karnataka, and to organize agriculture and animal husbandry in terms of Article 48 of the Constitution of India.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and covers all cattle (defined as cow, calf of a cow and bull, bullock of all ages and he or she buffalo below the age of thirteen years), their slaughter, transport, sale, purchase, and disposal.

key_definitions.beef: Flesh of the cattle in any form.
key_definitions.cattle: Cow, calf of a cow and bull, bullock of all ages and he or she buffalo below the age of thirteen years.
key_definitions.competent_authority: The competent authority appointed under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.gau_shala: A shelter established for the protection and preservation of cattle registered as such with the department of Animal Husbandry and Fisheries under the State or Central Act.
key_definitions.slaughter: Killing by any method whatsoever and includes maiming and infliction of physical injury which in the ordinary course will cause death.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provisions for its commencement.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act.
Empowers the State Government to appoint a Competent Authority, who can be a Tahasildar or an officer of the Animal Husbandry and Fisheries Department.
Prohibits the slaughter, causing slaughter, offering for slaughter, or intentionally killing of any cattle.
Restricts the transport of cattle within the State for the purpose of slaughter, with an exception for bona-fide agricultural or animal husbandry purposes as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on transport of cattle outside the State
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transport of cattle from within the State to outside the State for slaughter, allowing permits for bona-fide agricultural or animal husbandry purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of sale, purchase or disposal of cattle for slaughter
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale, purchase, or disposal of cattle for slaughter, or with the knowledge that they will be slaughtered.

Grants powers to police officers (not below the rank of Sub-Inspector) and the Competent Authority to inspect, seize cattle, premises, and materials used in the commission of an offense under the Act, with provisions for confiscation and release on bank guarantee.
Allows the Government to designate any court as a Special Court for speedy disposal of disputes under the Act.
Provides for an appeal to the Sessions Judge against orders passed under section 8.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions, including imprisonment and fines, with enhanced penalties for second and subsequent offenses and contravention of rules.

Outlines exemptions from the Act's provisions for cattle used for vaccine lymph, research, public health emergencies, those suffering from contagious diseases or incurable terminal illness, and buffaloes above thirteen years with certification.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of institutions for taking care of cattle
main_sections.description: Enables the State Government to establish or direct the establishment of institutions, including Gau Shalas, for the care of cattle.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the State Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Repeals the Karnataka Prevention of Cow Slaughter and Cattle Preservation Act, 1964, and provides for savings.

important_rules: No person shall slaughter or cause to be slaughtered any cattle (Section 4).
No person shall transport cattle within the State for slaughter, except for bona-fide agricultural or animal husbandry purposes as prescribed (Section 5).
No person shall transport cattle outside the State for slaughter, except with a permit for bona-fide agricultural or animal husbandry purposes (Section 6).
No person shall purchase, sell, or dispose of cattle for slaughter or with knowledge that they will be slaughtered (Section 7).
Cattle slaughtered under exemptions must be disposed of under the supervision of a Veterinary Officer (Section 18(2)).

penalties: Contravention of Section 4: Imprisonment not less than three years but up to seven years, or fine not less than fifty thousand rupees per cattle up to five lakh rupees, or both. Second and subsequent offenses: further fine not less than one lakh rupees up to ten lakh rupees along with imprisonment up to seven years.
Contravention of provisions other than Section 4: Imprisonment not less than three years up to five years, or fine not less than fifty thousand rupees up to five lakh rupees, or both.
Contravention of rules: Imprisonment not less than three years up to five years and fine up to fifty thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers not below the rank of Sub-Inspector, and the Competent Authority appointed under Section 3.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of search and seizure, apprehension of offenders, confiscation of materials and cattle, constitution of Special Courts for speedy disposal of cases, and appeals to the Sessions Judge.

rights: Right to appeal to the Sessions Judge against orders passed under Section 8.
Right to be heard before confiscation of property (Section 8(5)).
duties: Duty not to slaughter cattle.
Duty not to transport cattle for slaughter.
Duty not to sell, purchase, or dispose of cattle for slaughter.
Duty to allow access to premises for inspection and to answer questions truthfully.
Duty of owners to produce seized property as and when required by the magistrate.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to prescribed rules for transport of cattle for agricultural or animal husbandry purposes.
Obligation to provide bank guarantee for the release of materials (vehicle, etc.) pending disposal of proceedings.

key_procedures: Procedure for search and seizure: Police officer or Competent Authority inspects and seizes cattle, premises, and materials if an offense is believed to have been committed. The seizure is reported to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for confiscation. The Magistrate may release materials on bank guarantee and order cattle to be handed over to an institution established under Section 19.

Procedure for appeals: Any person aggrieved by an order under Section 8 can appeal to the Sessions Judge within thirty days of receiving the order. The Sessions Judge will hear the affected parties and pass an appropriate order.

Procedure for confiscation: Sub-Divisional Magistrate, upon satisfaction that an offense has been committed or intended, may order confiscation of seized properties. An opportunity of being heard must be given to the person who committed the offense. Confiscated cattle are to be handed over to institutions under Section 19 and cannot be sold or given to the accused.
administration: State Government and its designated authorities, including the Competent Authority and Special Courts.
important_notes: The Act came into force w.e.f. 25.02.2021 by Notification No.AHf261 AID 2015 (part -1) Dated 25.02.2021.
The Act supersedes the Karnataka Prevention of Cow Slaughter and Cattle Preservation Act, 1964.

Exemptions apply to cattle undergoing specific medical procedures, those certified as necessary for public health, suffering from contagious or incurable diseases, or buffaloes above thirteen years with certification.
Confiscated cattle shall not be handed over to the accused or sold in public auction, but shall be handed over to institutions established under Section 19.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To retrospectively amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, for the validation of fee and penalty collected by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike at the time of sanction of building plan and grant of Commencement Certificate and Completion Certificate, and to provide exemption or concession for certain government-owned or controlled entities from paying such fees.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka, specifically amending the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020. It concerns the levying and collection of fees and penalties related to building plan sanctions, commencement certificates, and completion certificates within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force from November 16, 2021.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 14 of 1977
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 299A, 299B, and 299C into the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. These sections deal with the levy of imposts, restrictions, and conditions by the Commissioner, the power of the State Government to exempt or reduce fees for certain entities, and the validation of previously collected fees and penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 53 of 2020
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 240A, 240B, and 240C into the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020. These sections are analogous to those inserted in the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and deal with the levy of imposts, restrictions, and conditions by the Chief Commissioner, the power of the State Government to exempt or reduce fees, and the validation of previously collected fees and penalties.
This section is mentioned in the table of contents but the details are truncated in the provided text. Typically, it would outline what is being repealed and any savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule: The Commissioner (for Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976) or the Chief Commissioner (for Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020) may grant permission for construction subject to restrictions and conditions as specified in zoning regulations or building bye-laws.

Rule: Fees can be charged and levied for various aspects of building plan approval, commencement certificates, and completion certificates, with rates based on guidance value fixed by the Department of Stamps and Registration.

Rule: The State Government can, by notification, exempt or reduce fees for Boards, Corporations, or Organizations owned or controlled by the Central or State Government, subject to restrictions and conditions.

Rule: If restrictions or conditions for fee exemption/reduction are contravened, or a wrong declaration is furnished, the person is liable to pay double the difference between the payable fee and the paid fee.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of exemption/reduction conditions: An amount equal to twice the difference between the fee payable and the fee paid.
Penalty for not obtaining commencement certificate: Imposed at the time of occupancy certificate issuance.
Penalty for violation or deviation from sanctioned plan or zonal regulation: Up to 5% of the violation.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner (under Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976) and the Chief Commissioner (under Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020) are responsible for granting permissions and levying fees/penalties. The State Government has the power to issue notifications for exemptions/reductions and to vary them. Enforcement also involves judicial and tribunal proceedings as per the validation clauses.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes levying fees and penalties as specified, refusing licenses, and through legal proceedings. The Act also validates past collections and prevents legal challenges for refunds.

rights: Right for entities owned or controlled by Central/State Government to be considered for fee exemption or reduction.
Right to a reasonable opportunity of being heard before action is taken for contravening exemption/reduction conditions.
duties: Duty to comply with restrictions and conditions specified in zoning regulations or building bye-laws.
Duty to pay applicable fees for building plan approvals, commencement certificates, and completion certificates.
Duty to ensure construction is in accordance with the sanctioned plan.
Duty to comply with any conditions attached to fee exemptions or reductions.
obligations: Obligation to pay penalties if violations or deviations occur.
Obligation to pay double the difference in fee if exemption/reduction conditions are not met.
Obligation for all persons to accept the validation of past fee and penalty collections.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining building permission: Applicant submits site plan, ground plan, elevations, and sections of the building to the Commissioner/Chief Commissioner, who may grant permission subject to restrictions or refuse based on specified conditions.

Procedure for fee exemption/reduction: State Government issues a notification specifying conditions and periods for exemption/reduction. Any contravention or wrong declaration by the applicant leads to penalty.
Procedure for validation: All past levies, assessments, and collections of fees and penalties are deemed valid and effective, preventing suits or proceedings for refund.
administration: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and its officers, along with the State Government of Karnataka, are responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: Retrospective effect: The amendments are deemed to have come into force from November 16, 2021, and specific fee levies are deemed to have always been in force from September 4, 2015 (for KMC Act) and January 11, 2021 (for BBMP Act).
Validation of past collections: All fees and penalties collected prior to the commencement of this Act, even if contrary to any court orders, are validated, and no refunds will be granted.
No penal proceedings for certain retrospective amendments: No penal proceedings will be commenced against any person for contraventions arising from the retrospective amendments.

title: THE KARNATAKA GRAM SWARAJ AND PANCHAYAT RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, to comply with a High Court direction for conducting elections to rural local bodies within a time limit, by prescribing a population limit for Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat elections and excluding specific taluks of Shivamogga district based on their population.
scope: The act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically amends provisions related to elections to Taluk Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats within the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2023, and it is deemed to have come into force from September 16, 2023.

Inserts the words 'Shivamogga (excluding Bhadravati, Shivamogga and Shikaripura Taluks),' before the word 'Chikkamagalur' in the first proviso of section 160 of the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993. This relates to the population limits for elections.

Repeals the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 (Karnataka Ordinance 03 of 2023) and states that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Amendment to Section 160 of the Principal Act to insert specific exclusions for Shivamogga district (Bhadravati, Shivamogga, and Shikaripura Taluks) when prescribing population limits for Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat elections.
Rule: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from September 16, 2023.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for conducting Panchayat Raj elections in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendment of the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, specifically by modifying Section 160.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Governor of Karnataka assented to the Act on January 29, 2024.
Procedure: The Act was published in the official Gazette extraordinary on January 30, 2024.
Procedure: The Act replaces the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as evidenced by the signature of the Secretary to Government).
important_notes: Note: The amendment is made to comply with a direction from the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Note: The exclusion of specific taluks from Shivamogga district is based on population proportion.
Note: The Act has retrospective effect from September 16, 2023.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION (No.2) ACT, 2020
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Services of the Financial year 2019-20.
scope: The act applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the financial year 2019-20. It authorizes the appropriation of funds for various services and purposes within the state.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation (No.2) Act, 2020.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 1180372.94 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2019-20
main_sections.description: This section authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Eleven thousand Eight hundred and Three crore Seventy two lakhs and ninty four thousand, from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka towards defraying charges for services during the Financial Year 2019-20.

This section states that the sums authorized to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

important_rules: Rule: Sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule are authorized to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Rule: The appropriated sums are for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule for the Financial Year 2019-20.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature, in accordance with the Constitution of India.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the authorization and appropriation of funds as outlined in the Act and detailed in the Schedule.

rights: The right to draw funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for specified services and purposes.
duties: Duty to appropriate funds for the services and purposes as expressed in the Schedule.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the amounts specified in the Schedule for each service and purpose.

key_procedures: Procedure: Introduce a Bill in pursuance of Article 205(1)(a) of the Constitution of India to provide for appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Procedure: Obtain assent of the Governor for the Act.
Procedure: Publish the Act in the official Gazette.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: Note: The Act is based on Article 205(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.
Note: The amounts specified in the Schedule are in lakhs of rupees.
Note: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 24th Day of March 2020 and was first published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on the 26th Day of March 2020.

title: THE KARNATAKA SALES TAX AND CERTAIN OTHER LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 and the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 to give effect to proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2003-04.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka and amends specific provisions of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, and Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is the first day of February, 2004.

Inserts new sections 6-D (Levy of road cess) and 6-E (Levy of infrastructure cess) into the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957. These sections introduce additional cesses on sales and purchases for specific funds.

Substitutes sub-section (1) of section 3-B of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, introducing an additional duty on instruments of conveyance, exchange, settlement, gift, or lease in perpetuity of immovable property for infrastructure projects.

Amends section 3-A and inserts a new section 10-A (Levy of cess in the case of fleet owner) into the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. Introduces a cess on motor vehicles and public service vehicles owned by fleet owners for infrastructure projects.

Empowers the State Government to make provisions by notification in the Official Gazette to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, for a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Levy of road cess at a rate of ten percent of the tax payable under sections 5, 5-A, 5-B, 5-C, or 6 of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, for the purpose of establishing a Road Maintenance Fund. This cess does not apply to goods specified in the Fourth Schedule.

Rule: Levy of infrastructure cess at a rate of five percent of the tax payable under sections 5, 5-A, 5-B, 5-C, or 6 of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, for various infrastructure projects, equity investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Mantri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi. This cess also does not apply to goods specified in the Fourth Schedule.

Rule: Levy of additional duty at the rate of ten percent on the duty chargeable on instruments of conveyance, exchange, settlement, gift, or lease in perpetuity of immovable property for infrastructure projects, equity investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Mantri Grameena Rasthe Aabhivrudhi Nidhi.

Rule: Levy of cess at the rate of ten percent of the tax levied under section 3 on Motor Vehicles for infrastructure projects, equity investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Mantri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi.

Rule: Levy of cess at the rate of ten percent of the tax levied under section 10 on public service vehicles owned by a fleet owner for infrastructure projects, equity investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Mantri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi. This cess is in addition to any tax levied under section 10.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and authorities empowered under the amended Acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy, assessment, collection, and refund mechanisms provided in the respective amended Acts and their rules.

rights: Right of goods specified in the Fourth Schedule to be exempted from road cess and infrastructure cess under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
duties: Duty to pay road cess and infrastructure cess as stipulated by the amended Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
Duty to pay additional duty on instruments related to immovable property as per the amended Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
Duty to pay cess on motor vehicles and public service vehicles owned by fleet owners as per the amended Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
obligations: Obligation for dealers to pay cess on sales/purchases as per sections 6-D and 6-E of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
Obligation for individuals executing instruments of conveyance, exchange, settlement, gift, or lease in perpetuity of immovable property to pay additional duty.
Obligation for owners of motor vehicles and fleet owners to pay cess on vehicles as per the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.

key_procedures: Procedure for Levy and Collection of Road Cess and Infrastructure Cess: In addition to existing taxes, a cess is levied and collected on sales or purchases at specified rates. The provisions of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act and its rules apply to the levy, assessment, collection, or refund of these cesses.

Procedure for Levy of Additional Duty on Immovable Property Instruments: A ten percent additional duty is levied on instruments of conveyance, exchange, settlement, gift, or lease in perpetuity of immovable property. The duty is chargeable on such instruments.

Procedure for Levy of Cess on Motor Vehicles: A cess is levied and collected on motor vehicles registered under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, at a specified rate. The provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act and its rules apply to the levy, assessment, and collection of this cess.

Procedure for Levy of Cess on Fleet Owners: A cess is levied and collected on public service vehicles owned by fleet owners at a specified rate. The provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act and its rules apply to the levy, assessment, and collection of this cess.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act itself), and respective departments administering the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, Karnataka Stamp Act, and Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act.
important_notes: The State Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for two years from its commencement.
The cesses introduced by this Act are in addition to the existing taxes payable under the respective principal Acts.
Specific goods mentioned in the Fourth Schedule of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, are exempted from the newly introduced road cess and infrastructure cess.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, specifically to restrict the territorial jurisdiction of Tumkur University to Tumkur district, following requests from students in Kolar and Bangalore Rural districts.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000. Its geographical scope pertains to the territorial jurisdiction of universities established under the principal Act, with a specific focus on the districts of Tumkur, Kolar, and Bangalore Rural.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the date of commencement of the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2004 (Karnataka Act No. 10 of 2004).

Amends Section 3 of the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000. It modifies sub-section (1) to include Bangalore Rural and Kolar districts, and sub-section (1B) to restrict the jurisdiction of Tumkur University to Tumkur district.
Amends sub-section (3) of Section 5 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'Kolar, Tumkur and Bangalore Rural Districts excluding Kanakapura and Hoskote Taluks' with 'Tumkur District'.

Repeals the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004 (Karnataka Ordinance No. 1 of 2004). It also includes a savings clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the repealed ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the State Government or authorities under the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but related to the administration of state universities in Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.
The amendment has retrospective effect from the commencement of Karnataka Act No. 10 of 2004.
The Kolar and Bangalore Rural districts are excluded from the territorial jurisdiction of Tumkur University, which is now restricted to Tumkur district.

title: THE CHIT FUNDS (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To amend the Chit Funds Act, 1982, in its application to the State of Karnataka, to enable the State Government to delegate the power to hear appeals to subordinate officers for expeditious disposal of appeals.
scope: This Act applies to the Chit Funds Act, 1982, as it is applicable to the State of Karnataka. It amends sections related to appeals against orders passed by the Registrar or nominee.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Chit Funds (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2007, and that it comes into force at once.

This section amends section 70 of the principal Act by renumbering it as sub-section (1) and inserting provisions to allow the State Government to delegate the power to hear appeals to an empowered officer or authority. It also inserts sub-sections (2) and (3) detailing the procedure for passing orders on appeals and the transfer of pending appeals.
This section amends section 84 of the principal Act by omitting the words 'to hear appeals or', which relates to the delegation of powers.

important_rules: Appeals against orders passed by the Registrar or nominee may be heard by the State Government or an officer/authority empowered by the State Government.
The empowered officer or authority, after providing an opportunity for representation, can pass final orders on the appeal.
Appeals pending before the State Government on the date of notification empowering a subordinate officer shall be transferred to that officer for disposal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and officers/authorities empowered by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of hearing and deciding appeals related to orders passed under the Chit Funds Act, 1982.

rights: Right of an aggrieved party to appeal against an order of the Registrar or nominee.
Right of an appellant to an opportunity of making his representation.

key_procedures: Filing an appeal against an order of the Registrar or nominee.
Hearing the appeal by the empowered authority.
Providing the appellant an opportunity to make representations.
Passing of final orders by the empowered authority.
Transfer and disposal of pending appeals.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory). The administration of the Chit Funds Act, 1982, generally falls under the Registrar of Chit Funds, whose orders are subject to appeal.
important_notes: The amendment aims to expedite the disposal of appeals.
The Act is an amendment to the Central Chit Funds Act, 1982, specifically for its application in Karnataka.

title: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, by inserting a new section 108A to provide for the levy and calculation of property tax on the basis of unit area value in the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area, aiming to bring a uniform property tax policy.
scope: This Act applies to the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area. It amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, specifically concerning the property tax levied on buildings and vacant lands within its jurisdiction.

key_definitions.unit_area_value: An average rate of expected returns from the property per sq.ft., per month, determined by the Commissioner, Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, based on factors like location, construction type, usage, area, age, and parking facilities.
key_definitions.principal_act: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1977).

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2009, and deems it to have come into force with effect from January 13, 2009.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act to rename the 'Corporation of City of Bangalore' as the 'Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike'.
Inserts a new section 108A to provide for the levy and calculation of property tax in the Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area on the basis of unit area value.

This section is mentioned in the arrangement of sections but not detailed in the provided text. It typically deals with repealing previous provisions and ensuring continuity or saving existing rights and liabilities.

important_rules: Property tax shall be levied by the Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike at a percentage between 20% and 25% of the taxable annual value.
Taxable annual value is calculated by multiplying 'unit area value' with the total built-up area, minus depreciation based on the building's age.
Property tax can be levied on buildings constructed in violation of byelaws, in unauthorized layouts, or without occupancy certificates, except for those on government or statutory body land.
Property tax is reduced by fifty percent for self-occupied residential buildings and notified self-occupied non-residential buildings.
Property tax is to be paid in two equal installments by May 30th and November 29th of each financial year, with provisions for a lump sum payment and rebates for early payment.
Returns for property tax must be submitted annually, and assessments are generally deemed final unless subjected to random scrutiny.

penalties: If re-assessed tax is more than 5% higher than the tax remitted, the evaded tax is payable along with a penalty not less than twice the evaded tax, plus interest at 24% per annum on the difference.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner, Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, or officers authorized by him.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves assessment, re-assessment, inspection, survey, measurement of properties, and demanding payment of taxes, penalties, and interest. Authorized officers can enter properties between sunrise and sunset for inspection after giving notice.

rights: Right to make representations or suggestions regarding the 'unit area value' before it comes into force.
Right to be informed before entry into an occupied dwelling by a woman, and to be afforded reasonable facilities to withdraw.
Right to show cause in writing against a re-assessment notice.
Right to file objections against re-assessment within thirty days.
duties: The person primarily liable must pay property tax in two equal installments or in one.
Owner/occupier must pay tax in advance based on their declared return.
Owner/occupier must submit an annual return in the prescribed form and manner.
Owner/occupier must furnish necessary information when required during inspection or survey.
Owner/occupier must pay re-assessed tax and penalties within thirty days of receiving the notice.
obligations: The Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike is obligated to collect property tax as per the Act.
The Commissioner is obligated to issue guidelines for determining unit area value and property tax.
The Commissioner or authorized officer must consider objections and pass orders on re-assessment.

key_procedures: Determination of 'unit area value' by the Commissioner based on various criteria, followed by publication in the official gazette and opportunity for public representation.
Annual submission of property tax returns by owners/occupiers.
Assessment of property tax, which is deemed final unless subject to random scrutiny.
Random scrutiny and re-assessment by the Commissioner or authorized officer if evasion of tax is suspected.
Issuance of a re-assessment notice and demand for payment of re-assessed tax and penalty.
Consideration of objections and passing of orders by the Commissioner or authorized officer on re-assessment.
Time limits for assessment and re-assessment: three years after filing the tax return or after evidence of facts comes to knowledge, whichever is later.
administration: The Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, headed by the Commissioner, is responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act concerning property tax collection.
important_notes: Land appurtenant to a building, not exceeding thrice the area occupied by the building, is exempted from property tax.
Lumpsum amounts can be fixed as annual tax for small built-up areas in slum areas, parking areas in non-residential buildings, and other specified classes of buildings by the Commissioner.
Levy and collection of property tax from certain unauthorized constructions do not confer any right to regularization or legal status.
Property tax is subject to revision once in three years by enhancing 15%, with the Municipal Corporation potentially enhancing it up to 30%.
The State Government may prescribe separate procedures, forms, or registers for property assessed by the Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE CIVIL SERVICES (REGULATION OF TRANSFER OF MEDICAL OFFICERS AND OTHER STAFF) ACT, 2011
purpose: To regulate the transfer of medical officers and other staff in the Health and Family Welfare Department and Ayush Department to ensure the availability of medical officers and other staff in government hospitals in rural areas, with objectives of transparency in transfer through counseling, ensuring minimum service in rural areas, and ensuring specialists work in commensurate posts.
scope: This Act applies to Medical Officers and other staff (Group B, C, and D) of the Health and Family Welfare Department and Ayush Department of the Government of Karnataka. It covers their initial appointment, transfer, and promotion, with a focus on ensuring services in rural areas and appropriate placement of specialists.

key_definitions.appointment: Appointment by direct recruitment, absorption, promotion, or by change of cadre of a Medical Officer or other staff.
key_definitions.competent authority: The authority competent to make orders of transfer of a Medical Officer or other staff.
key_definitions.government hospital: Includes various types of government medical facilities like district hospitals, primary health centers, AYUSH hospitals, etc.
key_definitions.medical officer: A medical officer appointed by the Appointing Authority to categories of posts specified in Schedule-I.
key_definitions.other staff: A person appointed by the Appointing Authority to categories of posts specified in Schedule-II (Group B, C, and D staff of Health and Family Welfare and Ayush Departments).
key_definitions.process of counseling: A process giving opportunity to opt for a place/post based on length of service and other prescribed criteria.
key_definitions.rural area: Any area other than urban areas.
key_definitions.urban area: Areas within the limits of city corporations, municipal councils, town panchayats, or other notified areas under Karnataka Municipal Acts, and areas notified as such by the Government.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and states that it comes into force on a date notified by the State Government.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including appointment, competent authority, government hospital, medical officer, other staff, process of counseling, rural area, urban area, and zones.

main_sections.section_title: Initial appointment, transfer or promotion to be through counseling
main_sections.description: Mandates that initial appointments, transfers, or promotions of Medical Officers and other staff are to be done through a prescribed counseling process, with exceptions for certain project posts and administrative positions.

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory appointment of a medical Officer or other staff in rural areas
main_sections.description: Ensures vacancies in rural areas are filled first during initial appointments or promotions. It also mandates transfer of existing staff who haven't served the prescribed rural period, with an age exemption (50 years).

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory appointment or transfer or promotion of a specialist or senior specialist to appropriate post
main_sections.description: Ensures Specialists and Senior Specialists are posted or transferred to posts commensurate with their postgraduate qualifications and specializations, with exceptions for certain administrative and leadership roles.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of Medical Officer or Other Staff in public interest
main_sections.description: Allows for transfers in the public interest through counseling, prioritizing those with longer service in an area/zone. It also specifies the order of transfer priority (rural, Zone-B urban, Zone-A urban) and limits total transfers to 5% of cadre strength. It also states that a reinstated officer shall not be posted to a higher zone than before suspension.
States that any competent authority or government servant making an order of posting, appointment, or transfer in contravention of the Act or rules will be liable for disciplinary action.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other existing laws.

Grants the Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided such orders are published in the official gazette and made within three years of the Act's commencement.
Empowers the Government to amend the schedules by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects government officers from legal proceedings for anything done in good faith or intended to be done under the Act.
Authorizes the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which can be made with retrospective effect and are subject to legislative approval.
Ensures that existing rules, notifications, orders, or appointments made under previous legislation are continued in force if not inconsistent with this Act, until superseded.

important_rules: Initial appointments, transfers, and promotions for Medical Officers and other staff must be conducted through a prescribed counseling process.
Vacancies in rural areas must be filled first during initial appointments or promotions.
Medical Officers and other staff who have not completed the prescribed number of years of service in rural areas must be transferred to rural areas, unless they have attained the age of fifty years.
Specialists and Senior Specialists must be posted or transferred to roles commensurate with their postgraduate qualifications and specialization.
Transfers in the public interest are to be conducted through counseling, prioritizing those with longer service. The order of transfer priority is rural area, then Zone-B urban, then Zone-A urban.
The total number of transfers in a year shall not exceed five percent of the working strength in that cadre.

penalties: Any competent authority or government servant making an order of posting, appointment, or transfer in contravention of the Act or rules shall be liable for disciplinary action under applicable civil service rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authorities and government servants responsible for making appointments, transfers, and promotions, overseen by the Government of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary action for contravention of the Act's provisions, and by the Government making rules and notifications to implement the Act.

rights: Right to opt for a place or post through the process of counseling based on service length and other prescribed criteria.
Protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act for government officers.
duties: Duty of the Appointing Authority or Competent Authority to ensure rural vacancies are filled first.
Duty of Medical Officers and other staff to serve in rural areas as prescribed.
Duty of Specialists and Senior Specialists to serve in posts commensurate with their qualifications.
Duty of competent authorities and government servants to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act and rules.
obligations: Obligation to follow the prescribed counseling process for appointments, transfers, and promotions.
Obligation to comply with compulsory rural service requirements.
Obligation for specialists to be posted to appropriate specialized posts.

key_procedures: Counseling process for initial appointment, transfer, or promotion: A process where individuals considered for appointment or transfer are given an opportunity to opt for a place or post based on their length of service in their current zone and other prescribed criteria.

Transfer in public interest: Medical Officers or other staff with completed prescribed service in a government hospital or institution may be transferred through counseling, prioritizing longer service, to another government hospital or institution within the same area/zone or to a different area/zone in the order of rural, Zone-B, and Zone-A urban.
Removal of difficulties: The Government may issue orders published in the official gazette to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, within three years of commencement.
administration: Government of Karnataka (Department of Health and Family Welfare and Ayush Department are implied by the subject matter). The power to make rules and remove difficulties rests with the Government.
important_notes: The Act overrides any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
Rules made under the Act can have retrospective effect, with reasons to be specified and laid before the State Legislature.
The provisions relating to transfers through counseling do not apply to certain identified project posts and senior administrative positions.
Compulsory transfer to rural areas does not apply to persons who have attained the age of fifty years.
The total number of transfers in a year for public interest shall not exceed five percent of the working strength in that cadre.

title: The Karnataka Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Epidemic Diseases Act, 2020, to make provisions for imposing penalties for contravention of rules and regulations made under the Act and for compounding of such offences.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Epidemic Diseases Act, 2020.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act, 2020, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 5 of the Principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (3A) to prescribe punishment for contravention of sub-section (1), and by omitting the figure and brackets '(1)' from sub-section (4).
Substitutes the existing section 10 of the Principal Act with new provisions for the composition of certain offences.

important_rules: Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 5 shall be punished with a fine up to fifty thousand rupees or with imprisonment for up to three months or with both.

Offences punishable under sub-section (3A) of section 5 may be compounded by an officer authorised by the Government on payment of a notified amount. Upon compounding, an offender in custody shall be discharged.
Offences punishable under sub-section (4) of section 5 may be compounded with the permission of the court by the person against whom the act of violence is committed.

penalties: Fine up to fifty thousand rupees
Imprisonment for a term which may extend up to three months
Both fine and imprisonment
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: An officer authorised by the Government (for compounding certain offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines and/or imprisonment for contravention of provisions. Offences can also be compounded upon payment of a specified amount or with court permission.

key_procedures: Compounding of offences under sub-section (3A) of section 5: An authorised officer of the Government can compound the offence on payment of a notified amount. The offender, if in custody, is discharged, and no further proceedings are taken.
Compounding of offences under sub-section (4) of section 5: This can be compounded with the permission of the court by the victim of the act of violence.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (likely involved in the legislative process and gazetting). The Government is responsible for notifying amounts for compounding.
important_notes: The amendment makes provisions for penalties for contravention of rules and regulations made under the Act.
The Act came into force at once upon publication.
The authoritative text in the English language is as per clause (3) of Article 348 of the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 to specify a separate rate of property tax for industrial buildings in Corporations and other urban local bodies, thereby encouraging the establishment of industries in the State.
scope: The Act applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1977) and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 22 of 1964). It specifically addresses property tax rates for industrial buildings within areas governed by these Acts.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Municipal Corporations and Certain other Law (Second Amendment) Act, 2021' and that it comes into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 14 of 1977
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. It inserts provisions for property tax on industrial buildings in section 108(2) and modifies sections related to taxation of commercial and industrial properties in section 110(1).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 22 of 1964
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It inserts provisions for property tax on industrial buildings in section 101(2) and modifies sections related to taxation of commercial and industrial properties in section 94(1-A).

important_rules: Rule 1: For industrial buildings, the property tax rate shall be a percentage not less than seventy percent of the rate levied for commercial buildings. This percentage must also not be less than the rate levied for residential buildings and other non-commercial buildings.
Rule 2: The term 'industrial building' is to be considered alongside 'commercial' and 'residential' buildings in the context of property tax levies under the amended Acts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Municipal Corporations and Urban Local Bodies governed by the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, respectively.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and collection of property taxes as per the amended provisions of the respective Acts.

rights: The right to establish industries in the State, facilitated by potentially lower property tax rates.
duties: The duty to pay property tax on industrial buildings at rates determined by the amended provisions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Insertion of new clause (d) in Section 108(2) of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to define the property tax rate for industrial buildings relative to commercial buildings.
Procedure 2: Amendment of Section 110(1) of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to include 'industrial' alongside 'commercial' in relevant clauses and provisos.
Procedure 3: Amendment of Section 94(1-A) of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to include 'industrial' alongside 'commercial' in relevant clauses and provisos.
Procedure 4: Insertion of new clause (d) in Section 101(2) of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to define the property tax rate for industrial buildings relative to commercial buildings.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as the publishing authority for the Act), and the respective Municipal Corporations and Urban Local Bodies for day-to-day administration of property tax.
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon publication.
The amendments are designed to encourage industrial development by providing differential property tax rates.
The property tax rate for industrial buildings is explicitly linked to the rates for commercial and residential buildings, ensuring a minimum floor.

title: THE KARNATAKA GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, to incorporate amendments relating to online gaming, online money gaming, specified actionable claims, and virtual digital assets, following recommendations from the GST Council and amendments to the Central Goods and Services Tax Act.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and specifically addresses the taxation of online gaming, online money gaming, specified actionable claims (including betting, casinos, gambling, horse racing, lottery), and virtual digital assets.

key_definitions.online gaming: Offering of a game on the internet or an electronic network and includes online money gaming.
key_definitions.online money gaming: Online gaming in which players pay or deposit money or money's worth, including virtual digital assets, in the expectation of winning money or money's worth, including virtual digital assets, in any event including game, scheme, competition or any other activity or process, whether or not its outcome or performance is based on skill, chance or both and whether the same is permissible or otherwise under any other law for the time being in force.
