key_definitions.specified actionable claim: The actionable claim involved in or by way of betting; casinos; gambling; horse racing; lottery; or online money gaming.
key_definitions.virtual digital asset: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (47A) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 2023, and it is deemed to have come into force from October 1, 2023.

Inserts new clauses into Section 2 of the principal Act to define 'online gaming', 'online money gaming', 'specified actionable claim', and 'virtual digital asset'. It also adds a proviso deeming persons organizing or operating platforms for supply of specified actionable claims as suppliers.
Amends Section 24 of the principal Act by omitting the word 'and' and inserting a new clause making every person supplying online money gaming from outside India to a person in India liable.
Substitutes the words 'specified actionable claims' for 'lottery, betting and gambling' in paragraph 6 of Schedule III of the principal Act.

Clarifies that the amendments made by this Act are without prejudice to other laws regulating betting, casino, gambling, etc. It also states that the imposition of tax does not regularize these trades and does not grant immunity from criminal action.
Repeals the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023, and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Any person supplying online money gaming from outside India to a person in India is required to comply with this Act.

Persons who organize, arrange, or operate digital/electronic platforms for the supply of specified actionable claims are deemed to be suppliers of such claims, irrespective of how consideration is paid or conveyed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and mechanisms established under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

duties: Suppliers of online money gaming (including those outside India) have a duty to comply with the GST Act.
Organizers/operators of platforms for specified actionable claims have a duty to act as suppliers and comply with the GST Act.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (for enactment and publication). Administration of the Goods and Services Tax itself is managed by the Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The imposition of tax on Casinos, Horse racing, and Online Gaming does not regularize these trades.
Any crime committed in the course of betting, casino, gambling, horse racing, lottery, or online gaming is not immune from criminal action.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend certain taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka. Specifically, it aims to incorporate provisions for levying tax on civil works like asphalting and repairing of roads retrospectively, to address tax on works contracts for processing and supplying photographs, to establish a Settlement Commission for reducing pending disputes and recovering tax arrears, to increase the sales tax rate on Camphor to the floor rate of 8%, to provide tax relief under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, and to omit provisions related to the collection of service charges by theatre owners under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958.
scope: The act applies to taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, and the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.

key_definitions.case: Any proceeding under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, by way of appeal or revision in connection with assessment, reassessment, levy of penalty, or interest, pending before a Sales Tax authority or Appellate Tribunal on the date an application for settlement is made. Certain conditions apply regarding appeals filed after the expiry of the specified period or ex-parte proceedings.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Settlement Commission.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Settlement Commission, including the Chairman.
key_definitions.Settlement Commission: The Sales Tax Settlement Commission constituted under section 4B of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Sales Tax Authority: A Sales Tax authority specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2004, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957. It inserts a new Chapter IIA titled 'SETTLEMENT OF CASES' with sections 4A to 4J, establishing a Sales Tax Settlement Commission, defining its powers, procedures for applications, and settlement of cases. It also makes other amendments as specified within the Act.
Amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, by omitting provisions relating to the collection of service charges by owners of theatres.
Amends the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, to provide tax relief to certain clubs and senior citizens.
This section is mentioned in the arrangement but not detailed in the provided text. It likely deals with validating past assessments or collections made under the amended provisions.

important_rules: Rule: An assessee or aggrieved person can apply for settlement of cases at any stage, provided the tax payable or penalty/interest exceeds twenty-five thousand rupees.
Rule: Applications for settlement must be accompanied by prescribed fees.
Rule: An application for settlement cannot be withdrawn without permission from the Settlement Commission.
Rule: The Settlement Commission must dispose of an application within ninety days from the date of admission.
Rule: A settlement can be annulled if obtained by fraud or misrepresentation, or if the tax, penalty, or interest is not paid within ninety days of the order's pronouncement.
Rule: The rate of sales tax on Camphor is increased to 8%.

penalties: Settlement is annulled if tax, penalty, or interest is not paid within ninety days of the order's pronouncement.
Proceedings can be revived if settlement is annulled due to fraud or misrepresentation.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Sales Tax Authority, Appellate Tribunal, and the Sales Tax Settlement Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, reassessment, levy of penalty and interest under the respective taxation laws, and through the procedures laid out for the Settlement Commission.

rights: Right to apply for settlement of cases under specific conditions.
Right to be heard before an application for settlement is rejected or a settlement is annulled.
Right to tax relief under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979 (for specific categories of clubs and individuals).
duties: Duty to pay tax, penalty, and interest as determined under the law.
Duty to comply with the terms of settlement if an application is admitted.
Duty to cooperate with the Settlement Commission and provide necessary reports and records.
Duty to pay tax on civil works like asphalting and repairing of roads.
Duty to pay tax on works contracts for processing and supplying photographs, photo prints, and photo negatives.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on civil works retrospectively from April 1, 1986.
Obligation to pay tax on works contracts for processing and supplying photographs retrospectively from July 1, 1989.
Obligation to adhere to the 8% floor rate for sales tax on Camphor.
Obligation to fulfill the terms of settlement, including payment of dues.

key_procedures: Procedure for Settlement of Cases: An assessee applies to the Settlement Commission, which calls for a report from the Sales Tax Authority. The Commission then decides to admit or reject the application. If admitted, further investigation may occur, and a settlement order is passed. The order specifies terms of settlement, payment methods, and conditions for voiding the settlement. Non-payment or fraud can lead to annulment.
Procedure for Omission of Service Charges: Provisions related to service charges in theatres under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, are omitted.
administration: The administration of the amended provisions falls under the respective departments overseeing sales tax, entertainments tax, and luxury tax in the State of Karnataka. The Sales Tax Settlement Commission is a newly constituted body for a specific purpose.
important_notes: The amendments related to civil works and photograph processing contracts are retrospective.
The Settlement Commission is constituted to reduce long-pending disputes and recover tax arrears expeditiously.
The settlement order is void if obtained by fraud or misrepresentation of facts.
If a settlement is annulled due to non-payment, the case is restored to its previous stage.
Tax relief is provided to clubs outside municipal corporations and to senior citizens/youth club members under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to provide for the constitution of Area Sabhas and Ward Committees in the State of Karnataka to institutionalize community participation in municipal functions.
scope: Applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and specifically to such Corporations as may be notified by the State Government. It establishes Area Sabhas and Ward Committees within the wards of these corporations.

key_definitions.Area: An area determined in the manner specified in section 13B.
key_definitions.Area Sabha: A body of all persons registered as voters in the electoral rolls pertaining to any polling station within an Area.
key_definitions.Association: A trust, society, association, or organization registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and fulfilling specified conditions related to its registered office, representation of residents/groups, active engagement for at least three years, and fiduciary capacity of its members.
key_definitions.Polling Station: A polling station set up for conducting elections to the Corporation.
key_definitions.Ward Development Scheme: A development scheme prepared by the Ward Committee for the budget allotted to it by the Corporation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Substitutes section 13A in the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, with a new Chapter IIIA titled 'Area sabhas and Ward Committees'. This new chapter includes definitions, provisions for determining areas, constitution and representation of Area Sabhas and Ward Committees, their meetings, functions, and duties, as well as provisions for byelaws and rules.

important_rules: Rule 1: Area Sabhas are to be constituted for each area, comprising all registered voters within that area's polling stations.
Rule 2: Each Area will have an Area Sabha Representative nominated by the Corporation on the recommendation of the ward councilor.
Rule 3: Area Sabhas must meet at least once in three months, with the Area Sabha Representative presiding. A nodal officer will provide administrative assistance and act as convener.
Rule 4: Decisions in Area Sabha meetings are to be made by consensus as far as possible, or by majority vote if consensus is not achievable.

Rule 5: Area Sabhas have functions including forwarding proposals for schemes, selecting beneficiaries for schemes, cross-verifying beneficiary eligibility, supporting tax collection, identifying deficiencies in public amenities, and promoting public awareness.
Rule 6: A Ward Committee shall be constituted for each ward, with the Councillor as Chairperson.
Rule 7: Ward Committees will consist of the Councillor and ten other nominated members, with specific representation for Scheduled Castes/Tribes, women, and resident associations.
Rule 8: Ward Committees shall meet at least once a month. Decisions are generally by majority, but the Chairperson has a veto power.

Rule 9: Ward Committees are responsible for preparing Ward Development Schemes, ensuring fund utilization, approving beneficiaries, scrutinizing ineligible beneficiaries, supervising Corporation programs, ensuring collection of taxes and fees, and maintaining public amenities like water supply, sewerage, waste management, and street lighting.
Rule 10: Every Corporation to which this chapter applies must notify bye-laws for the working of Area Sabhas and Ward Committees within six months of the chapter coming into force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government (for making rules and removing difficulties), The Corporation (for nominations and allotting funds), The Commissioner (for nominating Area Sabha Representatives if councilor recommendations are not received, and designating nodal officers and secretaries).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution of Area Sabhas and Ward Committees, delegation of functions, financial allocations for Ward Development Schemes, and the power of the State Government to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to participate in Area Sabha meetings for registered voters.
Right to have Area Sabha Representatives nominated.
Right to have Ward Committees constituted with specified representation.
Right of the Chairperson to exercise veto power over Ward Committee decisions.
Right to receive administrative assistance from nodal officers and secretaries.
duties: Duty of Area Sabha members to participate in meetings.
Duty of Area Sabha to forward proposals and select beneficiaries.
Duty of Area Sabha to support tax collection and encourage tax payment.
Duty of Ward Committee to prepare and implement Ward Development Schemes.
Duty of Ward Committee to ensure maintenance of public amenities.
Duty of Ward Committee to ensure timely collection of taxes and fees.
Duty of Corporation to notify bye-laws for Area Sabhas and Ward Committees.
obligations: Obligation to register as a voter to be a member of an Area Sabha.
Obligation to adhere to the conditions for being nominated as a Ward Committee member.
Obligation to comply with bye-laws and rules governing Area Sabhas and Ward Committees.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining Areas: The State Government determines the areas within each ward, comprising one or more contiguous polling areas, not exceeding five such polling stations.
Procedure for constitution of Area Sabha: All registered voters in an Area automatically become members of the Area Sabha.
Procedure for nomination of Area Sabha Representative: Nomination by the Corporation on the councilor's recommendation; Commissioner nominates if no recommendation is received within ninety days.
Procedure for meetings of Area Sabha: Meets at least once in three months, presided by the Area Sabha Representative, convened by a nodal officer.
Procedure for constitution of Ward Committee: For each ward, comprising the Councillor as Chairperson and ten nominated members with specified reservations.
Procedure for meetings of Ward Committee: Meets at least once a month, convened by the Secretary in consultation with the Chairperson.
Procedure for decision making in Ward Committee: Normally by majority, with the Chairperson having a veto power.
Procedure for preparing Ward Development Scheme: Ward Committee prepares and submits the scheme to the Corporation for fund allotment.
Procedure for bye-laws: Corporations must notify bye-laws for Area Sabhas and Ward Committees within six months of the chapter's commencement.
administration: The State Government and the respective Municipal Corporations, with roles for the Commissioner and designated officers (nodal officers and secretaries).
important_notes: Note 1: The provisions of Chapter IIIA apply only to such Corporations as may be notified by the State Government.
Note 2: Any person disqualified for being elected as a Councillor is also disqualified from being nominated as an Area Sabha Representative or a Ward Committee member.
Note 3: The term of office for Area Sabha Representatives and nominated Ward Committee members is co-terminus with the term of the Corporation.
Note 4: The Chairperson of a Ward Committee can exercise a 'veto' over any decision by providing written reasons, and their decision is final and binding.
Note 5: The Commissioner or their nominee is entitled to participate in Ward Committee meetings and deliberations.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2020-21 and to amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It applies to motor vehicles taxed under the said act within the state of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section names the act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2020, and specifies its commencement date as April 1, 2020.

This section details the amendments made to the Schedule of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. These amendments include changes to tax rates and classifications for various types of motor vehicles, particularly contract carriages and sleeper coaches. It also involves the substitution of 'sales tax' and 'entry tax' with 'Goods and Services Tax' in certain parts of the schedule.

important_rules: Rule 1: For item No. 5, sub-item (a), clause (i) in Part-A, the figure '12' in column (2) is replaced with '20'.

Rule 2: A new clause (iii) is inserted after clause (ii) in item No. 5, Part-A, for 'Motor vehicles (Contract carriages) plying for hire or reward and constructed or adopted to carry more than 12 passengers but not more than 20 passengers (excluding driver and conductor/attendant) and comply with Rule 151(2) of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, for every passenger', with a tax of 900.00.

Rule 3: Sub-item (b) of item No. 6 in Part-A is substituted with a new entry for 'Motor vehicles (Sleeper Coaches) plying for hire or reward and constructed or adopted to carry passengers (excluding driver and conductor/attendant) and comply with Rule 125(c) with AIS 119 standards of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, granted permits under section 88 (9) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, for every sleeper', with a tax of 4000.00.

Rule 4: In Part A1, notes, item 3, sub-item (a), the words 'sales tax' are omitted and 'entry tax' is substituted with 'Goods and Services Tax'. The words 'whichever is higher' are inserted after 'as payable in the State of Karnataka'.

Rule 5: Similar substitutions of 'sales tax' with 'Goods and Services Tax' and the addition of 'whichever is higher' are made in Part A5, A7, and A8, in the notes, item 3 (or item 2 for A8), sub-item (a).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Transport Department of Karnataka or the State Government, as per the general administration of motor vehicles taxation laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the existing mechanisms for motor vehicles taxation and enforcement as per the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.

duties: Duty to pay motor vehicle tax as per the amended rates and classifications.
Duty to comply with the conditions for specific vehicle classifications (e.g., Rule 151(2) of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, Rule 125(c) with AIS 119 standards).

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for enactment and publication), and likely the Transport Department of Karnataka for administration and enforcement.
important_notes: The amendments are effective from the first day of April, 2020.
The act aims to align tax structures with budget proposals and potentially broader tax reforms (e.g., GST implications).

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to revise the property tax structure, simplify the property tax base, improve municipal revenues by linking property tax to prevailing guideline values, and enable the State Government to achieve an additional borrowing limit.
scope: Applies to the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and concerns property tax assessment and levy within municipalities governed by this act. Geographically, it applies to the state of Karnataka.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 22 of 1964).
key_definitions.Financial year: The year commencing on the first day of April.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Municipalities (Second Amendment) Act, 2021, and states it is deemed to have come into force from January 19, 2021.
Amends section 101 of the principal Act by revising the property tax rates for certain categories of buildings and lands, and modifying the exemption for vacant land appurtenant to a building.

Amends section 102 of the principal Act by inserting the word 'prevailing' and substituting 'fifty percent of the market value guidelines' with 'twenty five percent of the prevailing market value guidelines' in relation to property tax assessment.
Substitutes section 102A of the principal Act, introducing provisions for the enhancement of property tax based on the revision of guidance values and an annual enhancement rate.
Repeals the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, and provides for the continuity of actions taken under the ordinance as if they were taken under the amended Act.

important_rules: Property tax rates in section 101 have been revised, with specific percentage changes for different clauses.
Vacant land up to one thousand square feet appurtenant to a building is exempted from property tax; land exceeding this area will be levied tax.
Property tax shall be assessed in the year of revision of guidance value under section 45B of the Karnataka Stamps Act, 1957.

Property tax shall stand enhanced by three percent for every financial year without a revision of guidance value, but the Municipal Council can enhance it up to five percent annually, with differential rates allowed for different areas and building/land classes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Municipal Councils and the State Government of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and levy of property tax as per the amended provisions of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and by the State Government's power to direct earlier revisions of property tax.

rights: The right of the Municipal Council to enhance property tax up to five percent for every financial year in which no revision of guidance value is made, with differential rates possible.
duties: Municipalities have a duty to assess and levy property tax according to the revised structure.
Municipalities have a duty to implement the annual enhancement of property tax as stipulated.
obligations: Obligation to assess property tax in the year of guidance value revision.
Obligation to levy property tax on vacant land exceeding one thousand square feet.

key_procedures: Assessment and levy of property tax in accordance with the revised rates and provisions of section 101.
Property tax assessment in the year of guidance value revision as per section 102A(1).
Annual enhancement of property tax by three percent or up to five percent by the Municipal Council as per section 102A(2).
Exemption of vacant land up to one thousand square feet appurtenant to a building, and levy of tax on land exceeding this area.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the act's promulgation), and Municipalities (for administration and enforcement of property tax).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from January 19, 2021.
The State Government has the power to direct an earlier revision of property tax.
Different rates of enhancement for property tax may be made for different areas and different classes of buildings and lands.

title: THE KARNATAKA COMPULSORY SERVICE BY CANDIDATES COMPLETED MEDICAL COURSES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To amend Sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Karnataka Compulsory Service by Candidates Completed Medical Courses Act, 2012, to restrict counseling and mandatory posting of doctors to existing vacancies specified by the State Government, to allow the Government to decide stipends, and to exempt candidates selected for Central or State Government service from compulsory rural service.
scope: This Act applies to candidates who have completed medical courses in Karnataka and are subject to compulsory service requirements as per the principal Act. Geographically, it applies within the State of Karnataka. The subject matter scope is the amendment of specific sections related to compulsory medical service for newly qualified doctors.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is deemed to have come into force from 8th November 2023.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act to specify that compulsory rural service is to be in existing vacancies, introduces an exemption for candidates selected for regular Central or State Government service, allows the State Government to specify stipends, and includes provisions for refusing to work or non-compliance.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act to specify that compulsory service is to be in existing vacancies, allows the State Government to specify stipends, and introduces an exemption for candidates selected for regular Central or State Government service after post-graduation.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act to specify that compulsory service is to be in existing vacancies, allows the State Government to specify stipends, and further provides an exemption for candidates selected for regular Central or State Government service.

Repeals the Karnataka Compulsory Service by Candidates Completed Medical Courses (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023, and provides that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Compulsory rural service shall be in existing vacancies as specified by the State Government.
Rule 2: Candidates selected for regular Central or State Government service are exempted from compulsory service.
Rule 3: The stipend for compulsory service will be as specified by the State Government.
Rule 4: Refusal to work or non-compliance with conditions specified by the State Government will be considered a violation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (implied through the amendments specifying 'State Government' to specify vacancies, stipends, and conditions)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms established by the principal Act and its amendments, including counseling, mandatory posting, and penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to exemption from compulsory rural service if selected for regular Central or State Government service.
duties: Duty to undergo compulsory service in specified vacancies.
Duty to comply with conditions set by the State Government.
Duty to undergo compulsory service for one year (as per principal Act sections being amended).
obligations: Obligation to serve in designated posts.
Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of service as determined by the State Government.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Candidates complete medical courses.
Procedure 2: Candidates are offered counseling and mandatory posting in existing vacancies specified by the State Government.
Procedure 3: Exemption is granted to candidates selected for regular Central or State Government service.
Procedure 4: Stipend is determined by the State Government.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as per publication details and role in enacting the law), and the Health and Family Welfare Department (implied as the administering department for medical services).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from 8th November 2023.
The amendments are made to clarify existing provisions regarding the nature of service, exemptions, and financial remuneration.
The Act specifically addresses the issue of compulsory service for medical graduates, including those who have completed post-graduation.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAX ON LOTTERIES ACT, 2004
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of tax on lotteries (gambling) and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to lotteries organized by the Government of India, State Governments, Union Territories, or any country with a bilateral agreement with the Government of India. It also applies to promoters and sellers of lottery tickets within Karnataka.

key_definitions.Assistant Commissioner: An Assistant Commissioner of Commercial Taxes appointed under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes appointed under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Joint Commissioner: A Joint Commissioner of Commercial Taxes appointed under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Lottery: A scheme, by whatever name called, for the distribution of prizes by lot or chance to those participating by purchasing tickets, organized by specified governmental entities or countries.
key_definitions.Promoter: The Government of India, State Government, Union Territory, or any country organizing a lottery, and includes any person appointed to sell lottery tickets in the State on their behalf.
key_definitions.Tax: The tax levied and collected on lotteries under this Act.
key_definitions.Week: The week commencing from Monday to Sunday.
key_definitions.Year: The year commencing on the first day of April.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Tax on Lotteries Act, 2004', states its extent to the whole of Karnataka, and specifies its deemed commencement date as December 10, 2003.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Assistant Commissioner', 'Commissioner', 'Joint Commissioner', 'Lottery', 'Promoter', 'Tax', 'Week', and 'Year'.

Empowers the State Government or the Commissioner to issue orders, instructions, and directions for the administration of the Act to officers and persons employed in its execution. Also requires officers to follow administrative instructions from the Joint Commissioner within their jurisdiction.

Specifies the rates at which tax is levied and collected on lotteries: one lakh and fifty thousand rupees for every bumper draw, and one lakh rupees for any other draw. The tax is payable by every promoter.

Mandates registration for every promoter and every person selling lottery tickets. Prescribes manner, fee, and period for registration, with an exemption for persons selling retail lottery tickets (excluding computerized network lotteries). Registration can be renewed annually. The Government of India or State/Union Territory Governments are exempt unless they sell lottery tickets directly.

Requires promoters to submit returns to the Assistant Commissioner. Pre-assessment payment of tax is mandatory. The Assistant Commissioner assesses based on the return if correct and complete, or to the best of their judgment if incorrect, incomplete, or no return is filed. Penalties may be imposed for non-disclosure or failure to submit returns.

Allows the Assistant Commissioner to assess or re-assess any draw that has escaped assessment or was assessed at a lower rate, within three years from the expiry of the relevant period. Penalties may be imposed for willful non-disclosure. Time limitations can be extended under certain conditions.

Requires every promoter to submit a statement every Monday regarding draws for the upcoming week and pay the full amount of tax in advance. Tax for draws immediately after the Act's commencement is payable within five days. If Monday is not a working day, the statement is filed on the next working day.
Specifies penalties related to registration under the Act.
Deals with penalties for fraudulent evasion of tax.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of the Karnataka Tax on Lotteries Ordinance, 2003, and savings in respect of actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: Tax is levied at ₹1,50,000 for every bumper draw and ₹1,00,000 for any other draw.
Every promoter and seller of lottery tickets must get registered under the Act.
Promoters must pay tax in advance for draws planned for the upcoming week, based on submitted statements.
Returns must be submitted by promoters, and advance tax payment must be made before submission.
The State Government has the power to reduce the rate of tax by notification.

penalties: Penalties relating to registration (Section 22).
Penalties relating to statements or returns (Section 23).
Penalties relating to keeping of records (Section 24).
Penalties relating to production of records and furnishing of information (Section 25).
Penalties relating to seals and unaccounted lottery tickets (Section 26).
Penalty for obstruction, etc. (Section 27).
Penalty for fraudulent evasion of tax (Section 28).
Penalty equal to one half of the tax due not disclosed in the return or one half of the assessed tax in case of failure to submit a return (Section 9(5)).
Penalty equal to one half of the tax assessed if escapement from assessment is due to willful non-disclosure (Section 10(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assistant Commissioners, Joint Commissioners, and the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (as defined and empowered by the Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, re-assessment, imposition of penalties, and initiation of proceedings for offences. Powers of entry, search, and seizure are also provided.

rights: The right to a reasonable opportunity of proving the correctness and completeness of a submitted return before assessment to the best of judgment.
The right to be heard before a penalty is imposed.
The right to appeal against assessment orders.
The promoter may demand that proceedings be re-opened or they be re-heard by the succeeding officer.
Right to appeal to the Appellate Authority.
duties: Duty of promoters and sellers to get registered.
Duty to submit returns as prescribed.
Duty to pay tax in advance.
Duty to maintain accounts and records.
Duty to produce documents and allow inspection when required.
Duty to observe and follow orders, instructions, and directions issued by the State Government, Commissioner, or Joint Commissioner.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on lotteries at the prescribed rates.
Obligation to comply with assessment and recovery procedures.
Obligation to adhere to penalties and enforcement measures.
Obligation to follow rules and notifications issued under the Act.

key_procedures: Registration of promoters and sellers: Application on payment of fee within a prescribed period, with renewal on payment of fee.
Filing of returns and advance tax payment: Promoters submit returns after paying tax in advance for the period, along with proof of payment.
Assessment: Assistant Commissioner assesses based on return or to the best of judgment, with provisions for penalties in case of incorrect returns or failure to file.
Assessment of draw escaping assessment: Assistant Commissioner can re-assess within three years if a draw escaped assessment or was under-assessed, with notice and inquiry.
Appeals and Revisions: Procedures for filing appeals and exercising revisional powers by Joint Commissioner and Commissioner.
Recovery of tax: Mechanisms for recovery of tax, penalty, or any other amount due under the Act.
administration: Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Karnataka (implied through the reference to Assistant Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, and Commissioner of Commercial Taxes).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from December 10, 2003.
A person ordinarily selling lottery tickets in retail (other than computerized network lottery) is exempt from mandatory registration.
The Government of India, State Governments, or Union Territory Governments are exempt from registration unless they sell lottery tickets directly.
The State Government can reduce tax rates by notification.
The Act provides for penalties for various offences, including fraudulent evasion of tax, and for offences by companies.

title: THE KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, specifically to enable the functioning of the Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Company by transferring assets and liabilities from MESCOM and to replace the Karnataka Electricity Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Electricity Reforms Act, 1999. It specifically concerns the establishment and operation of electricity distribution companies (ESCOMS) within the state, including the Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Company and the Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (MESCOM).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Electricity Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on December 24, 2004.
Amends sub-sections (5) and (8) of section 14 of the Karnataka Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, by inserting the words 'or a licencee as the case may be' after the letters 'KPTC' wherever they occur.

Repeals the Karnataka Electricity Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004, and states that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Insertion of 'or a licencee as the case may be' in section 14(5) and 14(8) of the principal Act to ensure entities other than KPTC can be covered.
Rule: The amendment is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from December 24, 2004, aligning with the Ordinance it replaces.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government of Karnataka (implied through the legislative process and the administration of electricity reforms)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and subsequent enforcement of the amended Karnataka Electricity Reforms Act, 1999.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of Section 14 of the Karnataka Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, to include 'licencee' alongside 'KPTC' in specific sub-sections.
Procedure: Repeal of the Karnataka Electricity Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004.
Procedure: Validation of actions taken under the Ordinance as if they were taken under the Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory G. Dakshina Moorthy)
important_notes: Note: The Act is a replacement for the Karnataka Electricity Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004, which was promulgated to address immediate operational needs.
Note: The amendment aims to facilitate the smooth functioning of newly established electricity distribution companies by ensuring they are on an equal footing with existing ones.

title: THE KARNATAKA VALUE ADDED TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, to give effect to proposals made in the Budget and for matters connected therewith, including certain consequential and incidental amendments.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It applies to dealers registered under the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, within the state of Karnataka. The amendments cover various aspects of Value Added Tax, including definitions, tax rates, eligibility for composition, deduction of tax at source, and procedures related to returns and assessments.

key_definitions.body_corporate: Means a corporation, a company as defined under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) and a company incorporated outside India. It does not include a corporation sole, a co-operative society registered under any law relating to co-operative societies, and any other body corporate, not being a company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956, which the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.
key_definitions.capital_goods: For the purposes of section 12, means plant, including cold storage and similar plant, machinery, goods vehicles, equipments, moulds, tools and jigs, and used in the course of business other than for sale.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2006, and it comes into force with effect from the first day of April, 2006.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act by renumbering clause (5-A) to (5-B) and inserting a new definition for 'Body corporate'. It also substitutes the definition of 'Capital goods' for the purposes of section 12 and amends clause (28) to include 'revised return'.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (c) in sub-section (1) to provide for tax on transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract specified in the Sixth Schedule. It also amends sub-section (3) regarding restrictions and conditions for notifications.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by inserting words related to restrictions and conditions in sub-section (1).

Amends section 9-A of the principal Act concerning deduction of tax for works contracts. It substitutes sub-section (4) regarding procedures when tax payable is less than the calculated tax, and omits words in sub-section (10).
Amends section 11 of the principal Act by substituting clauses (2), (3), (4), and (5) of sub-section (a) to modify the conditions for tax paid on goods and capital goods.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act by omitting words related to apportionment of tax over a specified period in sub-section (2).

Substitutes section 14 of the principal Act with a new section titled 'Special rebating scheme', which allows deduction of input tax on the purchase of specified goods to the extent of input tax charged at a rate higher than four percent or any lower rate notified by the Government.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act regarding composition of tax. It substitutes clause (a) in sub-section (1), inserts 'or bakery or any other class of dealers as may be notified by the Government' in clause (c) of sub-section (1), and substitutes 'granite or any other metals' for 'granite metals' in clause (d). It also inserts a new sub-section (5) detailing eligibility and conditions for dealers executing works contracts to opt for composition.

Substitutes section 18 of the principal Act with provisions for deduction of tax at source in the case of canteens. It details the procedure for factories or establishments running canteens to deduct tax from payments to dealers, conditions for deduction, payment of deducted tax, interest on default, and furnishing of certificates.
Amends section 20 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (1), clause (b).
Amends section 21 of the principal Act by omitting the words 'located in the State'.
Amends section 22 of the principal Act by substituting 'before the commencement of his business' for 'after his first sale' in sub-section (9).
Amends section 27 of the principal Act by substituting 'twelve consecutive months' for 'twenty four consecutive months' in sub-section (1), clause (c).
Amends section 29 of the principal Act by inserting 'or a dealer permitted to pay tax under section 16' after 'prescribed value' in sub-section (3).

Amends section 30 of the principal Act by inserting 'or is not payable on account of goods sold being returned within the prescribed period' in sub-section (1). It also substitutes sub-section (3) regarding the declaration of credit notes or debit notes in returns.
Indicates the insertion of a new section 63-A, though its content is not provided in the excerpt.
Indicates an amendment to the First Schedule.
Indicates an amendment to the Third Schedule.
Indicates the insertion of a Sixth Schedule.

important_rules: Rule related to 'Body corporate' definition: Specifies what is included and excluded from the definition.
Rule related to 'Capital goods' definition: Defines capital goods for the purpose of section 12.
Rule for works contract tax: Tax is levied on the transfer of property in goods involved in works contracts as specified in the Sixth Schedule.
Rule for tax deduction for works contracts: Details the procedure when the tax payable is less than calculated, including the process for issuing certificates and making deductions.

Rule for eligible purchases for VAT credit: Outlines conditions and goods eligible for input tax credit, including those purchased for resale, manufacture, or for use in goods despatched outside the state.
Rule for special rebating scheme: Allows deduction of input tax on certain purchased goods if the input tax charged is at a higher rate than 4% or a lower notified rate.

Rule for composition of tax for works contracts: Details conditions under which dealers executing works contracts can opt for composition, including provisions for goods obtained from outside the state or India, payments to sub-contractors, and sale of goods other than by transfer in works contracts.

Rule for deduction of tax at source in canteens: Mandates factories or establishments running canteens to deduct tax at 4% on payments to dealers for sale of food and drinks to employees, with certain conditions and timelines for payment and reporting.
Rule for tax returns: Registered dealers issuing or receiving credit/debit notes must declare them in their returns.

penalties: Interest is payable on delayed payment of tax deducted at source for canteens, at the rate specified in section 37.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner and officers empowered by the Commissioner, as well as authorities responsible for deduction of tax under sub-section (1) of section 9-A and factories/establishments making deductions under section 18.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, including changes to definitions, tax rates, eligibility criteria, and procedural requirements for dealers and specified establishments. Enforcement involves assessment, tax collection, and penalties for non-compliance, including interest on delayed payments.

rights: Right to claim input tax credit under specified conditions.
Right to opt for composition of tax under certain circumstances (e.g., for dealers executing works contracts).
Right to receive a certificate from the prescribed authority regarding tax deduction at source for canteens.
Right to have tax payable reduced by the amount of tax already remitted under sub-section (3) of section 18.
Right to seek a certificate for deduction of tax for works contracts within ten days of application.
duties: Duty to pay Value Added Tax as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty to correctly calculate and pay tax on works contracts.
Duty to comply with conditions for claiming input tax credit.
Duty for factories/establishments to deduct tax at source in canteens and pay it to the prescribed authority.
Duty to declare credit notes and debit notes in tax returns.
Duty to maintain records and furnish information as required by the Act.
Duty to pay interest on delayed tax payments.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the amended provisions of the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003.
Obligation for dealers executing works contracts to comply with specific rules for composition and tax liability.
Obligation for factories/establishments to submit monthly statements of tax deducted.
Obligation for dealers to prove that tax on their turnover has been remitted and to establish the quantum of such remittance when claiming reduction.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending definitions in Section 2.
Procedure for amending tax provisions related to works contracts in Section 4.
Procedure for determining eligibility and applying for tax deduction certificates for works contracts under Section 9-A.
Procedure for claiming input tax credit on various types of purchases under Section 11.
Procedure for applying for composition of tax for dealers executing works contracts under Section 15.
Procedure for deduction of tax at source by factories/establishments running canteens, including payment, reporting, and issuance of certificates under Section 18.
Procedure for registered dealers to declare credit and debit notes in their returns under Section 30.
administration: The Karnataka State Legislature, through the provisions of the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, as amended by this Act. The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Karnataka, and designated officers would be responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Act.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (Karnataka Act 32 of 2004).
The amendments come into force from April 1, 2006.
Certain amendments are deemed to have been inserted and shall always be deemed to have been inserted, indicating retrospective effect for specific provisions.
The Sixth Schedule is introduced to specify works contracts for tax purposes.
Notifications by the State Government or Commissioner are crucial for the application of several amended provisions.

title: THE KARNATAKA VALUE ADDED TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, to give effect to budget proposals, simplify tax compliance, avoid disputes, and rationalize certain provisions. Key objectives include introducing optional tax payment schemes based on Maximum Retail Price (MRP), enhancing tax collection on tobacco products, establishing an Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings, mandating electronic filing of returns and tax payments for specified dealers, and empowering the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes with powers related to goods vehicle inspection and penalty for incorrect return particulars.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It specifically addresses various classes of dealers, goods (including tobacco products), and tax transactions within Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2010, and specifies its commencement date as April 1, 2010.

Introduces amendments to Section 4 of the principal Act, modifying tax rates for certain goods (including tobacco products), introducing tax payment on MRP for specific tobacco products, and adding provisions regarding the validity of notifications and tax adjustments.

Inserts a new sub-section (1-A) into Section 5 of the principal Act, stating that any notification issued under sub-section (1) remains valid until cancelled or varied, even if tax payable for such goods is modified by an amendment to the Act.
Amends Section 18 of the principal Act by increasing the monetary threshold from 'two lakh rupees' to 'five lakh rupees' in sub-section (2).
Amends Section 18-A of the principal Act by substituting 'provisions of this sub-section' with 'provisions of sub-section (4)' in sub-section (5).

Amends Section 22 of the principal Act by omitting sub-section (1) and increasing monetary thresholds in sub-sections (2) and (3) from 'two lakh rupees' to 'five lakh rupees' and 'fifteen thousand rupees' to 'forty thousand rupees', respectively.
Amends Section 27 of the principal Act by increasing the monetary threshold from 'two lakh rupees' to 'five lakh rupees' in sub-section (1), clause (c).

Amends Section 31 of the principal Act by increasing the monetary threshold from 'forty lakh rupees' to 'sixty lakh rupees' in sub-section (4) and introducing a proviso mandating account audits for dealers whose total turnover for the year ending March 31, 2010, exceeds forty lakh rupees.

Amends Section 35 of the principal Act by adding provisos to sub-section (1) that empower the Commissioner to notify specified classes of dealers for mandatory electronic filing of returns and tax payment through the internet.

Amends Section 53 of the principal Act by inserting new sub-sections (2-A) and (2-B) related to reporting at check posts, producing proof of online particulars entry, and levying penalties for contraventions or incomplete/incorrect particulars. It also modifies sub-section (3) regarding places for interception and inspection.
Amends Section 54 of the principal Act by substituting 'sub-section (3) of Section 52' with 'section 53'.

Inserts a new Section 60 titled 'Clarification and Advance Rulings'. This section allows the Commissioner to constitute an 'Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings' to clarify tax rates, exigibility, input tax deductions, or tax deduction at source. It outlines the application process, binding nature of rulings, and provisions for voiding rulings obtained by fraud.
Amends Section 72 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'particulars for preparation of a return or furnishes' after 'tax period furnishes' in sub-section (2).
Amends the Third Schedule to the principal Act by omitting the heading 'GOODS TAXABLE AT FOUR PER CENT'.

Amends the Sixth Schedule to the principal Act by substituting 'Four per cent' with 'Five per cent' for specified serial numbers and 'Twelve and one half per cent' with 'Thirteen and one half per cent' for serial number 23.

important_rules: Rule: Tax on cigarettes, cigars, gutkha, and other manufactured tobacco is levied at fifteen per cent.
Rule: Tax on other goods is levied at thirteen and one half per cent.

Rule: Registered dealers selling cigarettes, cigars, gutkha, and other manufactured tobacco are liable to pay tax on the maximum retail price after a reduction equal to the tax payable, provided the sale consideration exceeds five hundred rupees or a higher notified amount.

Rule: Dealers whose sale of specified tobacco products is not liable to tax under the MRP scheme can claim a refund or adjustment of tax collected on their purchases if it exceeds the tax payable on their turnover.
Rule: A specified class of dealers, as notified by the Commissioner, must furnish return particulars and pay tax electronically through the internet.
Rule: Owners or persons in charge of goods vehicles carrying specified goods must report at the first check post or barrier and produce proof of online entry of particulars of goods carried.
Rule: Penalties will be levied for contravention of provisions related to reporting at check posts, online entry of particulars, or providing incorrect/incomplete particulars.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of or non-compliance with provisions related to goods vehicle reporting and online particulars entry, or for providing incorrect/incomplete particulars for which sufficient cause is not furnished.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of Commercial Taxes and officers empowered under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes inspection of goods vehicles, levying penalties for non-compliance with reporting and documentation requirements, and facilitating electronic filing and payment of taxes. The Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings can also declare orders obtained by fraud as void.

rights: Right of registered dealers to claim refund or adjustment of tax collected on purchases if it exceeds tax payable on sales of specific goods under the MRP scheme.
Right of persons who are not dealers to claim refund of excess tax paid on their purchases.
Right of registered dealers to seek clarification and advance rulings from the Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings.
duties: Duty of registered dealers to pay tax as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty of registered dealers to comply with mandatory electronic filing of returns and tax payments if notified by the Commissioner.
Duty of owners or persons in charge of goods vehicles to report at check posts and provide particulars of goods carried.
Duty of dealers to furnish correct particulars for the preparation of returns.
obligations: Obligation for specified dealers to file returns and pay tax electronically.
Obligation to adhere to the MRP-based tax payment scheme for specified tobacco products.
Obligation to cooperate with officers during the interception and inspection of goods vehicles.

key_procedures: Procedure for optional tax payment scheme on goods based on MRP for specified tobacco products.
Procedure for application to the Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings, including form, fee payment, and binding nature of rulings.
Procedure for electronic filing of returns and payment of tax by notified classes of dealers.
Procedure for reporting and inspection of goods vehicles, including online entry of goods particulars.
Procedure for levying penalties for non-compliance with goods vehicle inspection and documentation rules.
administration: Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Karnataka
important_notes: Notifications issued under specific sub-sections remain valid even if tax rates are amended.
The Act establishes an Authority for Clarification and Advance Rulings to provide clarity on tax matters and avoid disputes.
The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes is empowered to notify specific classes of dealers for mandatory electronic filing and payment, and to notify websites for goods particulars entry.

title: THE KARNATAKA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959, primarily to insert a new section for the constitution of a common cadre for employees of primary agriculture and rural development banks and to amend existing provisions regarding election procedures for co-operative credit structure societies.
scope: The Act applies to co-operative societies in Karnataka, with specific provisions concerning Primary Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development (PCARD) Banks and the Karnataka State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development (KASCARD) Bank. It also addresses election processes for Co-operative Credit Structure Societies.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959 (Karnataka Act 11 of 1959)
key_definitions.PCARD Bank: Primary Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Bank
key_definitions.KASCARD Bank: Karnataka State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Bank

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it will come into force on a date appointed by the State Government, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Inserts a new section (97A) into the principal Act. This section deals with the constitution of a common cadre for the employees of Primary Agriculture and Rural Development Banks.
Amends section 98Q of the principal Act, specifically substituting the wording related to the timing of elections for existing committees with a reference to sub-section (2) of section 39A.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Registrar can authorize the KASCARD Bank to make regulations for the appointment, transfer, and disciplinary action of certain categories of PCARD Bank employees, overriding existing powers of PCARD Banks.

Rule 2: PCARD Banks must contribute annually to KASCARD Bank towards the expenditure incurred for the common cadre, and failure to do so can lead to enforcement orders similar to awards under section 71.

penalties: Orders for the payment of contributions by PCARD Banks that fail to do so are enforceable as if they were an award under section 71 of the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar, or an officer specified by the Registrar.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through enquiry and orders for payment of amounts owed, which are then enforceable as awards.

rights: Right of the Registrar to authorize the creation of a common cadre and to specify employee categories for it.
Right of the Registrar to require PCARD Banks to make contributions towards the expenditure of KASCARD Bank for the common cadre.
Right of KASCARD Bank to make regulations for appointment, transfer, and disciplinary action for specified employee categories.
duties: Duty of PCARD Banks to adhere to regulations made by KASCARD Bank regarding specified employee categories.
Duty of PCARD Banks to contribute annually towards the expenditure incurred by KASCARD Bank for the common cadre.
Duty to hold elections for Co-operative Credit Structure Societies in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 39A.
obligations: Obligation for PCARD Banks to comply with the Registrar's directives regarding common cadre employee management.
Obligation for PCARD Banks to make financial contributions as mandated.

key_procedures: Procedure for the creation of a common cadre: The Registrar, if deeming it necessary for the co-operative movement, authorizes the KASCARD Bank to create regulations for appointment, transfer, and disciplinary action of specified PCARD Bank employee categories. PCARD Banks then cede such powers to the KASCARD Bank.

Procedure for financial contributions: The Registrar can require PCARD Banks to contribute annually to KASCARD Bank. If a PCARD Bank defaults, the Registrar can order payment after an enquiry, with the order being enforceable as an award.
Procedure for elections: Elections for Co-operative Credit Structure Societies must be held in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 39A.
administration: The Registrar, in conjunction with the Karnataka State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Bank (KASCARD Bank), and the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for legislative aspects).
important_notes: The purpose of inserting section 97A is to continue the existing system of the Common Cadre Committee to prevent adverse effects on the functioning of PCARD Banks, pending a decision by the Government of India on the Prof. A. Vaidyanathan package.
The amendment to section 98Q aligns election procedures for Co-operative Credit Structure Societies with those outlined in section 39A (2).

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE CIVIL SERVICES (REGULATION OF TRANSFER OF TEACHERS) ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for regulation of transfer of teachers in Government Primary Schools and Government High schools to ensure the availability of teachers in these institutions and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to teachers in Government Primary Schools and Government High schools in Karnataka. It defines 'teacher' to include those appointed to various posts specified in the Schedule, belonging to State Civil Services. It also covers the regulation of transfers, rationalization of posts, and redeployment of teachers.

key_definitions.appointment: Appointment by direct recruitment, absorption, or promotion.
key_definitions.appointing_authority: The authority competent to make an appointment to the post of a teacher.
key_definitions.competent_authority: The authority competent to make orders of transfer of teachers as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.minimum_period_of_service: A continuous service of three years in a school, including service rendered in a school from which the teacher has been re-deployed.
key_definitions.order_of_priority: A priority list of teachers prepared based on a weighted score obtained by the teacher according to prescribed criteria for the purpose of counselling.
key_definitions.re_deployment: Re-deployment of a post from a school where it is in excess to a school where it is in deficit, as per pupil-teacher ratio and other norms specified by the State Government.
key_definitions.schedule: The schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.specified_posts: Posts of Cluster Resource Person, Block Resource Person, Educational Coordinator, Technical Assistant, Block Resource Coordinator, Assistant Project Coordinator, Subject Inspector, and Assistant Director (mid-day meal), and such other posts as may be notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.teacher: A person appointed to a category of posts of a teacher in a primary school or a high school or composite high school or composite junior college or such other posts belonging to the State Civil Services as specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.transfer: Posting of a teacher from one place of working to another place of working in the same cadre.
key_definitions.unit_of_seniority: For primary school teachers, the Unit of Seniority is an Educational District; for high school teachers, it is a Revenue Division.
key_definitions.zone: Zone-A, Zone-B, and Zone-C as defined and prescribed by the State Government.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointment', 'appointing authority', 'competent authority', 'minimum period of service', 'order of priority', 're-deployment', 'schedule', 'specified posts', 'teacher', 'transfer', 'unit of seniority', and 'zone'.

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory appointment of a teacher to Zone-C
main_sections.description: This section mandates that vacancies in Zone-C shall be filled first during initial appointments or promotions. It outlines procedures for creating vacancies in Zone-C by transferring willing teachers from Zone-C to Zone-B and from Zone-B to Zone-A, with provisions for exceptions and further posting orders if vacancies in Zone-C are not available.

This section requires rationalization of sanctioned posts and working teachers every alternate year based on the pupil-teacher ratio. Excess teachers are to be redeployed to schools with deficits through counselling based on the order of priority.

This section mandates zonal transfers every alternate year. Teachers who have not served a minimum of ten years in Zone-C and have served more than ten years continuously in Zone-A are to be transferred to Zone-C or Zone-B. If vacancies are unavailable, willing teachers in Zone-C or Zone-B may be transferred to Zone-A.

Teachers who have completed the minimum period of service in a school can seek transfer, subject to vacancy availability and prescribed conditions. Service in previous schools after rationalization or zonal transfer is reckoned for calculating the minimum service period. Special conditions apply for teachers in Kalyana Karnataka region seeking transfer outside the region.

This section details the process of teacher transfers through computerized counselling, typically conducted in April and May. Transfers can be made outside these months in special circumstances. Provisions exist for transfers in public interest and for teachers facing disciplinary or criminal proceedings. Limits on the number of transfers are specified, with exemptions for mutual transfers and special categories.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of teachers to specified posts
main_sections.description: Specified posts are to be filled through counselling based on merit lists from prescribed examinations. The State Government may also post eligible teachers discretionarily. Minimum and maximum posting periods for these posts are three and five years, respectively.

A Grievance Redressal Officer (not below the rank of Joint Director of Public Instruction) is designated to oversee transfers and hear complaints. Appeals against the Officer's orders lie with specified Additional Commissioners or the Director (Transfer Cell). Violations by officers are to be reported to the Disciplinary Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Exemptions from rationalization, zonal transfers and priority for request transfers
main_sections.description: This section outlines exemptions for teachers from rationalization, zonal transfers, and priority in request transfers based on various criteria, including terminal illness, benchmark disability, widow/widower/divorcee status, spouse in defence forces, spouse working in government or aided institutions, age (above 50 for females, 55 for males), and pregnant teachers or those with young children. Categories are specified for eligibility for exemptions and priority.
This section specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.

main_sections.section_title: An Act to override other laws
main_sections.description: This section states that the provisions of this Act override other laws where there is inconsistency.
This section grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every appointing authority must ensure that vacancies in Zone-C are filled first during initial appointments or promotions.
Rationalization of posts and teachers based on pupil-teacher ratio shall occur every alternate year.
Teachers who have served a minimum of ten years in Zone-C and more than ten years continuously in Zone-A shall be transferred to Zone-C or Zone-B every alternate year.
Teachers must have completed a minimum period of service (defined as three years continuously in a school) to be eligible for request transfers.
Transfers are ordinarily done through computerized counselling in April and May, but can be done at other times for special reasons or public interest.
Specified posts have minimum and maximum posting periods of three and five years, respectively.
Exemptions from rationalization, zonal transfers, and priority for request transfers are provided for specific categories of teachers and their families.
The total number of transfers under sections 5 and 6 for any cadre and unit of seniority shall not exceed fifteen percent, with exceptions for mutual transfers and special categories.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 12).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Competent authority as defined in the Act, and departmental officers responsible for overseeing transfers and grievance redressal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed procedures of transfer, rationalization, redeployment, and counselling. Grievances are addressed by designated Grievance Redressal Officers and their appellate authorities. Penalties are enforced for violations.

rights: Teachers have the right to seek transfer based on eligibility criteria and prescribed procedures (Request Transfer).
Teachers have the right to opt for a school in Zone A if they have continuously worked in Zone C and B for extended periods.
Certain categories of teachers and their families have rights to exemptions and priority in transfers.
Teachers have the right to have their grievances redressed during the transfer process.
duties: Appointing authorities have a duty to ensure vacancies in Zone-C are filled first.
Teachers have a duty to serve in their assigned postings and follow the transfer regulations.
The State Government and its authorities have a duty to ensure equitable opportunities and availability of teachers in schools.
obligations: Teachers are obligated to complete the minimum period of service in a school before seeking a request transfer.
Teachers are obligated to participate in rationalization and zonal transfers as prescribed.
Teachers facing disciplinary or criminal proceedings may be obligated to transfer to Zone-C regardless of the minimum service period.

key_procedures: Compulsory appointment to Zone-C for first postings and promotions, with mechanisms for creating vacancies through willing teacher transfers.
Rationalization of teachers every alternate year based on pupil-teacher ratio, followed by redeployment of excess teachers through counselling.
Zonal transfers occurring every alternate year for teachers who have served extended periods in higher zones.
Request transfer process for teachers who have completed the minimum service period, subject to vacancy and other conditions.
Transfer by computerized counselling, generally during April and May, with provisions for special circumstances.
Grievance redressal mechanism involving designated officers and appellate authorities.
administration: The State Government, through its relevant departments (e.g., Department of Public Instruction), administers this Act.
important_notes: The Act partially repeals the Karnataka Civil Services (Regulation of transfer of teachers) Act, 2007, specifically excluding matters pertaining to PUC teachers and principals.
The Act aims for transparency and equitable opportunities in teacher transfers.
It provides for a 'teacher friendly approach' with exemptions and priorities for various teacher categories.
The Act can override other laws in case of inconsistency (Section 14).
The State Government has the power to remove difficulties and make rules for the implementation of the Act (Sections 15 and 18).

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, in order to revise the property tax structure, provide a simplified property tax base, improve Municipal Corporation revenues by linking the property tax base to prevailing guidelines value, and enable the State Government to become eligible for additional borrowing limit by strengthening Municipal Corporations through property tax reforms.
scope: This Act applies to Municipal Corporations established under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. Its subject matter scope pertains to the revision and enhancement of property tax structures and rates within these corporations. Geographically, it applies to the areas within the jurisdiction of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2021, and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force with effect from January 19, 2021.

This section amends Section 108 of the principal Act (Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976). It modifies the percentages for property tax on buildings and vacant land, and introduces an exemption for vacant land appurtenant to a building up to one thousand square feet.

This section amends Section 109 of the principal Act by substituting 'fifty percent of the market value guidelines' with 'twenty five percent of the prevailing market value guidelines' in both sub-sections (1) and (2).

This section substitutes Section 109A of the principal Act. It introduces provisions for enhancing property tax based on the year of revision of guidance value, with a standard enhancement of three percent annually and the possibility of up to five percent enhancement by the Municipal Corporation.

This section repeals the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, and states that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Property tax rates on buildings are revised to 0.2 percent (rupees two per thousand) and 1.5 percent (rupees fifteen per thousand).

Rule 2: Property tax on vacant land shall be at a percentage not less than 0.2 percent (rupees two per thousand) and not more than 0.5 percent (rupees five per thousand) of the taxable capital value of land.

Rule 3: Vacant land appurtenant to a building up to one thousand square feet is exempted from property tax, while land exceeding this area is subject to property tax as per clause (c) of sub-section (2) of Section 108.

Rule 4: Property tax shall be assessed in the year of revision of guidance value. In years without guidance value revision, the property tax shall be enhanced by three percent for every financial year, with the Municipal Corporation having the power to enhance it up to five percent.
Rule 5: The Municipal Corporation may set different rates of enhancement for property tax for different areas and different classes of buildings and lands.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Municipal Corporations established under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By assessing and levying property tax according to the revised rates and enhancement provisions stipulated in the Act.

rights: Right of Municipal Corporations to enhance property tax up to five percent for every financial year in which no revision of guidance value is made, with variations for different areas and classes of properties.
Right of the State Government to direct an earlier revision of property tax.
duties: Duty of Municipal Corporations to revise and levy property tax as per the amended provisions.
Duty to link property tax base to prevailing guidelines value.
obligations: Obligation to pay property tax as assessed and levied under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending property tax rates by substituting specified percentages in Section 108(2)(b).
Procedure for assessing property tax on vacant land by inserting a range of percentages and omitting specific sub-clauses in Section 108(2)(c).
Procedure for exempting and levying property tax on vacant land appurtenant to buildings in Section 108(3).
Procedure for substituting the basis for property tax assessment from 'market value guidelines' to 'prevailing market value guidelines' in Section 109.
Procedure for enhancing property tax annually based on guidance value revisions or at a specified rate by the Municipal Corporation under Section 109A.
Procedure for repealing the Ordinance and saving actions taken under it.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (responsible for publishing and enacting the act, likely overseen by the Urban Development Department for implementation).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from January 19, 2021.
The purpose of the amendment is to strengthen Municipal Corporations by reforming property tax.
The State Government's eligibility for an additional borrowing limit of 0.25 percent of GSDP for 2020-21 is linked to these property tax reforms.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, to enhance the rate of Stamp Duty in certain cases and to make a separate provision regarding the levy of Stamp Duty on Bank Guarantee.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, and applies to instruments and transactions subject to Stamp Duty in the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2023, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends Section 30 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, by substituting the entries relating to Article No. 52(b) with new entries for Article No. 56, specifically for paper bank guarantee and e-bank guarantee.
