Time limits for appeal disposal: Appellate authorities have specific timeframes (e.g., 120 days, 180 days) to dispose of appeals once a stay order is granted, failing which the stay order stands vacated.
Definition of banking companies: For the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 'banking companies' include banks governed by the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Tax on uncharged or concessional luxury in hotels: In hotels, if luxury is not charged or is charged at a concessional rate, tax will be levied as if the full charges were paid.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely tax authorities as per the respective amended Acts (e.g., Luxury Tax Officer, Appellate Authority, Appellate Tribunal).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, appeal processes, and enforcement of tax payment obligations as stipulated in the amended Acts.

rights: Right to appeal against orders or proceedings of tax authorities.
Right to seek a stay on payment of disputed tax amount during appeal, subject to conditions and security.
Right to have appeals disposed of within stipulated timeframes.
duties: Duty to pay tax as per assessment or other orders.
Duty to provide proof of payment of disputed tax amounts when filing appeals.
Duty to furnish security as required for stay orders.
obligations: Obligation for licensees to pay totalisator tax either directly or through composition.
Obligation for proprietors to pay entertainment tax on cinematograph shows, unless exempted.
Obligation for hotels to levy and collect luxury tax on provided services.

key_procedures: Appeals Process: Filing an appeal within specified timeframes, accompanying it with proof of payment of a portion of the disputed tax, furnishing security if a stay is sought, and awaiting disposal of the appeal within stipulated time limits.
Composition of Totalisator Tax: A licensee electing to pay totalisator tax by way of composition pays a fixed percentage of the total amount paid into the totalisator, subject to conditions.
Tax Levy on Luxury Services in Hotels: If luxury services are provided at a concessional rate or not charged, tax is levied as if full charges were applied.
administration: The specific administrative department or agency is not explicitly mentioned, but it would typically be the State Government's Finance Department or the respective tax departments overseeing the amended Acts.
important_notes: Amendments are often retrospective or deemed to have been in effect from specific past dates (e.g., April 1, 2002, April 1, 2003).
The Act significantly alters procedures and conditions for appeals, particularly regarding the payment of disputed tax amounts and the timelines for appellate authorities to dispose of cases.
The provisions for staying recovery of tax amounts during appeals are subject to strict conditions and time limits to prevent undue delays.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, specifically to raise the fiscal deficit limit to 3.5 percent of estimated Gross State Domestic Product for the year 2008-09 as a one-time relaxation and to facilitate capital expenditure as part of an economic stimulus package.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. It specifically pertains to fiscal management and deficit limits for the financial year 2008-09.

key_definitions.fiscal_deficit: The difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts, excluding borrowings.
key_definitions.Gross_State_Domestic_Product: The total monetary or market value of all the finished goods and services produced within the state in a specific time period.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2009' and states that it is deemed to have come into force from the 28th day of February 2009.

Amends sub-section (3) of Section 4 of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to allow the fiscal deficit during the year 2008-09 to exceed the limit up to 3.5 percent of estimated Gross State Domestic Product. It mandates that additional market borrowings under this relaxed limit must be used for capital expenditure and requires an accompanying report on the impact of such expenditure to be placed before the Legislature.

important_rules: Rule 1: The fiscal deficit during the financial year 2008-09 may be allowed to exceed the prescribed limit up to 3.5 percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product.
Rule 2: Any additional market borrowings availed due to the relaxed fiscal deficit limit must be exclusively utilized for undertaking capital expenditure during the financial year 2008-09.
Rule 3: An accompanying report detailing the use of additional borrowings for capital expenditure and its likely impact must be presented before both Houses of the Legislature.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature and the State Government (implied through the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. Compliance is monitored through reports submitted to the Legislature.

rights: The right for the State to relax its fiscal deficit limit under specific circumstances (economic stimulus).
duties: Duty to utilize additional borrowings only for capital expenditure.
Duty to report on the utilization of funds and their impact to the Legislature.
obligations: The obligation to adhere to the amended fiscal deficit limit for 2008-09.
The obligation to ensure that capital expenditure is undertaken with the additional borrowings.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Legislature amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to allow for a higher fiscal deficit limit for a specific financial year.
Procedure 2: The State Government avails additional market borrowings within the relaxed fiscal deficit limit.
Procedure 3: The additional borrowed funds are used for capital expenditure.
Procedure 4: A report detailing the capital expenditure and its likely impact is prepared and submitted to both Houses of the Legislature.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (implied through the signing of the act).
important_notes: This amendment is a one-time relaxation for the financial year 2008-09.
The relaxation is specifically to meet capital expenditure as part of an economic stimulus package.
The Act is deemed to have come into force from February 28, 2009.

title: THE KARNATAKA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959, to remove restrictive provisions, enable cooperative societies to function transparently, accountably, vibrantly, and democratically, and to implement a revival package for the short-term cooperative credit structure as per the MoU signed with the Government of India and NABARD.
scope: This Act applies to cooperative societies in Karnataka and specifically amends provisions related to the cooperative credit structure. It aims to improve the functioning, governance, and financial management of these societies.

key_definitions.agriculture_and_rural_development_bank: A Co-operative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank registered or deemed to be registered under the Act and admitted as a member of the State Agriculture and Rural Development Bank, including notified classes of cooperative societies.
key_definitions.backward_class: Backward Classes as notified under clause (a) of section 2 of the Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1995.
key_definitions.cooperative_credit_structure: Includes Primary Agricultural Credit Co-operative Societies, Central Co-operative Banks, State Co-operative Bank, Agricultural and Rural Development Banks, and State Agricultural and Rural Development Bank.
key_definitions.central_cooperative_bank: A federal society engaged in the business of banking.
key_definitions.chartered_accountant: A member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different sections, with some sections deemed to have come into force from November 3, 2009, and others from the date of enactment.

Amends section 2 of the Principal Act by substituting words in the definition of 'Assisted Society' and inserting new definitions for 'Agriculture and Rural Development Bank', 'Backward Class', 'Co-operative Credit Structure', 'Central Co-operative Bank', and 'Chartered Accountant'.
Proposes to incorporate a separate chapter (Sections 98A to 98Y) making special provisions applicable to societies in the cooperative credit structure, as envisaged in the revival package.
Grants the State Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of the Karnataka Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009, and savings.

important_rules: Rule: The period of an administrator in a society within the cooperative credit structure shall not exceed three months.
Rule: The State Government shall not postpone elections of a society in the cooperative credit structure for a period exceeding three months.
Rule: A cooperative society can make loans to another cooperative society without the sanction of the Registrar.
Rule: Every society is obligated to get its accounts audited every year, and the scope of audit is elaborated.
Rule: An application shall be decided within a period of twelve months, which may be extended up to eighteen months.
Rule: A dispute relating to disciplinary action against or service conditions of an employee shall be filed within twelve months from the date of cause of action.
Rule: A dispute shall be decided within a period of twelve months, which may be extended up to eighteen months.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies and other authorities as prescribed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes audit, inquiry, inspection, appointment of administrators, and legal proceedings for misappropriation.

rights: Members' right to elect the committee.
Right of cooperative societies to make loans to other cooperative societies.
Right to receive inquiry and inspection reports and report action taken.
Right to appeal against certain orders.
duties: Duty of societies to get accounts audited annually.
Duty to report action taken on inquiry and inspection reports to the Registrar within three months.
Duty of Government nominees as enunciated in Section 29.
obligations: Obligation to deposit 25% of the amount due before filing an appeal.
Obligation to comply with directions from the High Court in certain cases.
Obligation to implement the revival package and amendments required by the MoU.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of section 20 to give a notice of forty-five days to defaulters instead of thirty days.
Procedure: Appointment of an administrator when necessary, with a stipulated period limit for societies in the cooperative credit structure.
Procedure: Conducting elections with multi-level holding and limitations on postponement for cooperative credit structure societies.
Procedure: Filing appeals against orders, requiring deposit of a portion of the amount due, with specified decision timelines.
Procedure: Filing of disputes related to employee service conditions within a specific timeframe.
Procedure: Sanction of the Registrar required for launching criminal cases in respect of all matters concerning a cooperative credit structure society, except for misappropriation.
administration: Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act replaces the Karnataka Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009.
Certain amendments are made to give effect to the revival package for the short-term cooperative credit structure agreed upon in a tripartite MoU.
The Act introduces special provisions for societies in the cooperative credit structure.
The sanction of the Registrar is not necessary for filing criminal complaints against individuals for misappropriation.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE SALARIES, PENSIONS AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for family pension to the family of deceased members of the Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly who were members wholly or partly after 1st day of January, 1952, whether they were in receipt of pension or not.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956. It applies to members of the Karnataka Legislative Council and Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force at once.
Amends sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 3 of the principal Act by replacing 'seventy five thousand rupees' with 'two lakhs rupees'.

Amends sub-section (2), clause (d) of section 8 of the principal Act by replacing 'rupees eight hundred' with 'rupees one thousand' and in the first proviso, replacing 'one thousand rupees' with 'one thousand two hundred rupees'.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 11A of the principal Act by omitting the words 'after serving for a period of more than three years' from the sixth proviso.
Inserts a new sub-section (1A) to provide family pension to the family of deceased members who were members after 1st January 1952, and amends the Explanation of section 11B.
Amends sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 11C of the principal Act by replacing 'seventy five thousand rupees' with 'one lakh rupees'.

important_rules: Family pension is to be provided to the family of a deceased member of the Legislative Council or Assembly who was a member after January 1, 1952, regardless of whether they were receiving a pension.
Salaries/allowances for members are amended, with specific monetary increases mentioned in sections 2, 3, and 6.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the relevant departments of the Karnataka Government responsible for legislative affairs and finance.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956.

rights: Right of families of deceased members to receive family pension.
Right of members to receive salaries and allowances as amended.
obligations: Obligation of the government to disburse family pensions and salaries/allowances as per the Act.
Obligation of members to meet the conditions for receiving these benefits.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment makes provisions for family pension retrospective to members who served after January 1, 1952.
Specific financial figures for salaries, pensions, and allowances have been revised.

title: THE KARNATAKA REGULATION OF PAY AND PENSION OF TEACHER IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS ACT, 2020
purpose: To regulate the pay, pension, and pensionary benefits admissible to teachers working in Government Colleges, Universities established by law, and in Government-aided Higher Educational Institutions under the control of the State Government.
scope: The Act applies to teachers working in Government Colleges, Universities established by law, and Government-aided Higher Educational Institutions under the control of the State Government of Karnataka, who draw UGC/AICTE/ICAR or modified AICTE pay scales. It covers the regulation of their pay and pensionary benefits.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and when it comes into force.
Defines terms used in the Act to ensure clarity and consistent interpretation.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of pay and allowances of a teacher
main_sections.description: Outlines the rules and procedures for regulating the pay and allowances of teachers covered by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of pension and pensionary benefits of a teacher
main_sections.description: Details the regulations governing pension and other pensionary benefits for teachers.

main_sections.section_title: Revision of Pension of a Teacher
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions and procedures for revising the pension of teachers.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of Proceedings and extinguishment of claims
main_sections.description: Addresses the validation of past proceedings and the extinguishment of certain claims, likely related to pay and pension disputes.
Provides for a mechanism for reviewing decisions or actions taken under the Act.
Allows for the delegation of powers vested in certain authorities under the Act to other specified officers or bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Government to give directions
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to issue directions to ensure the effective implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Offers protection to individuals acting in good faith in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the government to make orders to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Specifies that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law or rules.
Confers the power on the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with provisions that are temporary in nature, often to bridge the gap between the old and new legal regimes.
Provides for the repeal of any previous enactment on the subject and savings for actions taken under the repealed law.

important_rules: Teachers in Government Colleges, Universities, and Government-aided Higher Educational Institutions drawing UGC/AICTE/ICAR or modified AICTE pay scales are covered by this Act.
The pension and pensionary benefits of such teachers are determined with reference to the applicable Rules/orders governing pension at the time of retirement, superannuation, or death.
Retired teachers drawing UGC/ICAR/AICTE or modified AICTE pay scales are to be treated on par with other State Government pensioners for pension and pensionary benefits.
The State Government's policy is that pension and pensionary benefits for these teachers shall be determined as per State Government Rules.
The cut-off date for pay and pension revision is decided considering financial implications and other relevant factors, including central government assistance.

The pension of retired teachers who retired prior to a subsequent pay revision cut-off date may be subjected to further revision when corresponding pay scales are effected as per State Government decision.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and authorities designated by it.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Act's provisions, rules made thereunder, and potentially judicial review of administrative decisions.

rights: Teachers are entitled to have their pay and allowances regulated according to the Act.
Teachers are entitled to have their pension and pensionary benefits determined and regulated according to the Act.
Retired teachers drawing UGC/ICAR/AICTE or modified AICTE pay scales have a right to be on par with other State Government pensioners for pensionary benefits.
duties: Teachers have a duty to adhere to the pay scales and regulations prescribed by the Act.
The State Government has a duty to ensure the proper regulation of pay and pension for the covered teachers.

key_procedures: Regulation of pay and allowances as per the Act.
Regulation of pension and pensionary benefits based on applicable rules at retirement.
Revision of pension under specific conditions outlined in the Act.
The State Government may issue directions for the implementation of the Act.
Rules may be made by the State Government to carry out the purposes of the Act.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka, with potential involvement of departments responsible for higher education, finance, and personnel.
important_notes: The Act addresses the ambiguity in the fixation of pension and grant of pensionary benefits to teachers who retired before the revision of UGC/ICAR/AICTE scales.
It replaces the Karnataka Regulation of Pay and Pension of Teachers in Higher Educational Institutions Ordinance, 2020 (Karnataka Ordinance No. 1 of 2020).

The Act is enacted based on the legislative powers derived from Articles 309 of the Constitution of India and Entries 14, 32, and 41 of List II and Entry 25 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons refers to judicial pronouncements by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India concerning pay and pension revisions for teachers, including the principle that artificial classification by fixing cut-off dates without a justifiable rationale may be impermissible under Article 14 of the Constitution.
The Act acknowledges the financial implications of pay revisions and the discretion of the State Government in extending benefits.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROTECTION OF INTEREST OF DEPOSITORS IN FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004, to enhance the protection of depositors, streamline investigation and enforcement mechanisms, and improve the process of asset attachment and sale for the recovery of depositors' funds.
scope: This act applies to financial establishments operating within Karnataka and deals with the protection of interest of depositors in such establishments. It amends the Principal Act of 2004.

key_definitions.market_intelligence: The process of gathering information from all available sources about a financial establishment regarding its financial position and market trends, and analyzing it for accurate decision-making in determining fraudulent activities.
key_definitions.financial_establishment: Though not explicitly defined in the provided text, the context implies entities that accept deposits from the public and fail to return them or provide promised services.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2020, and it comes into force at once.
This section inserts a new clause (4a) defining 'Market intelligence'.

This section amends section 3 of the Principal Act to authorize the Government or District Magistrates, suo moto or based on market intelligence or police complaints, to investigate fraudulent transactions. It also empowers the Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, or nominated authorities with civil court powers for investigation.

This section amends section 4 of the Principal Act to grant powers to the Competent Authority, Police Authority, or other authorized entities to enter, search, seize, freeze bank accounts, and attach properties believed to be acquired through fraudulent means.

This section amends section 5 of the Principal Act. It provides for the appointment of a single Competent Authority for cases spread across multiple districts and allows for the appointment of officers to assist the Competent Authority. It also allows the Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, to extend the time limit for making applications to the special court.

This section amends section 6 of the Principal Act by mandating the Government to empanel agencies for asset valuation and sale, and for forensic and digital audits. It also permits the utilization of services of agencies empanelled by SEBI, Nationalised Banks, and Indian Bankers' Association until the State empanels its own.
This section amends section 7 of the Principal Act to extend the time limit for making applications to the special court.

This section substitutes section 9 of the Principal Act, enhancing the punishment for fraudulent default by financial establishments, including imprisonment terms and fines. It also includes provisions for repeat offenders and defines liability for persons in charge of the financial establishment's business.

This section amends section 10 of the Principal Act, allowing the Government to appoint a single competent authority for cases of financial establishments spread across multiple districts, with concurrence of the Court.

important_rules: Financial establishments are required to return deposits after maturity or on demand, and pay promised interest or other benefits.
Investigations into fraudulent transactions can be initiated suo moto, based on market intelligence, or on receiving a complaint.
Authorities have the power to seize, freeze, and attach properties and assets acquired by financial establishments through fraudulent means.
The Government shall empanel agencies for asset valuation, sale, and forensic/digital audits.
Individuals responsible for the management of financial establishments are liable for fraudulent defaults.

penalties: For fraudulent default, imprisonment for a term not less than three years and extending to seven years, with a fine up to ten lakh rupees.
The financial establishment is liable for a fine up to five lakh rupees or twice the amount of aggregate funds collected, whichever is more.
For subsequent convictions after a previous conviction, imprisonment not less than five years and up to seven years, with a fine not less than ten lakh rupees and up to fifty crore rupees.
Persons in conduct of business, or those with consent, connivance, or negligence, are also deemed guilty and liable for punishment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, District Magistrates, Police Authorities, the Competent Authority, Secretary to Government (Revenue Department), and other nominated authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of complaints and fraudulent transactions, seizure and attachment of properties, freezing of bank accounts, summoning persons and documents, and prosecution in special courts.

rights: Depositors have the right to receive their deposits after maturity or on demand, along with any promised benefits.
Depositors have the right to receive services assured against their deposits.
duties: Financial establishments have a duty to repay deposits and provide promised services.
Persons summoned during investigations have a duty to attend and state the truth, and produce required documents.
obligations: Financial establishments have an obligation to conduct their business transparently and avoid fraudulent practices.
Individuals responsible for the management of financial establishments have an obligation to exercise due diligence to prevent offences.

key_procedures: Upon receiving a complaint or market intelligence, the Government or District Magistrate may cause an investigation into fraudulent transactions.
The Competent Authority can enter, search, seize, freeze accounts, and attach properties believed to be acquired fraudulently.
The Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, or Competent Authority can extend time limits for applications to the special court.
The Government shall empanel agencies for asset valuation and sale, and forensic audits.
Cases pertaining to one financial establishment spread across districts can be handled by a single Competent Authority and transferred to one special court.
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka, and other nominated authorities.
important_notes: The Act empowers authorities with the powers of a civil court for investigation, including summoning persons and compelling production of documents.
Proceedings under Section 3 are deemed judicial proceedings under the Indian Penal Code.
The Act aims to ensure more transparency and fair assessment of property values for release.
The amendment enhances the term of imprisonment and penalty to align with the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019.

title: THE KARNATAKA SCHEDULED CASTES SUB-ALLOCATION AND TRIBAL SUB-ALLOCATION (PLANNING, ALLOCATION AND UTILIZATION OF FINANCIAL RESOURCES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Scheduled Castes sub-allocation and Tribal sub-allocation (Planning, Allocation and Utilization of Financial Resources) Act, 2013, to give effect to budget proposals and to include the Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Tribal Welfare as Ex-officio Members in the State Council for Development of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes, and the Minister for Tribal Welfare as the Vice-Chairman in the Nodal Agency for the Scheduled Castes sub-allocation or Tribal sub-allocation.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Scheduled Castes sub-allocation and Tribal sub-allocation (Planning, Allocation and Utilization of Financial Resources) Act, 2013. It amends specific sections related to membership and roles within state councils and nodal agencies concerning the planning, allocation, and utilization of financial resources for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Scheduled Castes sub-allocation and Tribal sub-allocation (Planning, Allocation and Utilization of Financial Resources) (Amendment) Act, 2023, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the Principal Act by inserting 'The Deputy Chief Minister – Ex-officio Member' and 'The Minister for Tribal Welfare – Ex-officio Member' as members of the State Council for Development of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes.

Amends section 5 of the Principal Act by inserting 'The Minister for Tribal Welfare – Vice Chairman' as the Vice Chairman of the Nodal Agency for the Scheduled Castes sub-allocation or Tribal sub-allocation.
Amends section 7 of the Principal Act by omitting clause (d).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through publication in the Official Gazette and by virtue of the Governor's assent.

key_procedures: Insertion of new ex-officio members into the State Council for Development of Scheduled Castes/Tribes.
Appointment of the Minister for Tribal Welfare as Vice Chairman of the Nodal Agency.
Omission of clause (d) from section 7 of the Principal Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Scheduled Castes sub-allocation and Tribal sub-allocation (Planning, Allocation and Utilization of Financial Resources) Act, 2013 (Karnataka Act 65 of 2013).
The amendments are made to give effect to proposals in the Budget Speech of 2023-24.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary No.57 in part-IVA dated:03.02.2024.
The assent of the Governor was received on the 3rd day of February, 2024.

title: The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment etc.,) (Amendment) Act, 2004
purpose: To amend Section 13 of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment etc.,) Act, 1990, to provide for laying of rules made under this Act before both Houses of the State Legislature.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment etc.,) Act, 1990.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Inserts a new sub-section (3) into Section 13 of the principal Act. This new sub-section mandates that every rule made under the Act must be laid before each House of the State Legislature for a total period of thirty days in session(s). If both Houses agree on modifications or annulment of the rule, it will have effect only in the modified form or be of no effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under the rule.

important_rules: Rule: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before each House of the State Legislature as soon as may be after it is made, while it is in session for a total period of thirty days, which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions. If before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, both Houses agree in making any modifications in the rule or agree that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of laying rules before the State Legislature for approval or modification.

duties: Duty of the State Government to make rules under the principal Act.
Duty of the State Legislature to consider and approve/modify rules laid before it.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to lay rules before the Legislature.
Obligation of the Legislature to act on the laid rules within the prescribed period.

key_procedures: Procedure for laying of rules: Rules made under the Act must be laid before each House of the State Legislature during a session. The period of laying must be a total of thirty days, which can be in one or more successive sessions. If modifications or annulment are agreed upon by both Houses before the expiry of the relevant session, the rule's effect is altered accordingly.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is based on the necessity to provide for the laying of rules before the State Legislature, as per constitutional provisions (Article 15(4) and 16(4) and Entry 23 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India).
The Governor of Karnataka assented to the Act on the twenty-second day of February, 2004.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on the twenty-third day of February, 2004.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, specifically to retain the power of the State Government in respect of granting exemptions of land to an extent not exceeding half hectare in the areas under Bangalore Rural District and Bangalore District.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. Its provisions regarding exemptions apply to areas under Bangalore Rural District and Bangalore District. The primary subject matter is land reforms and the powers of the Deputy Commissioner in granting exemptions.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it comes into force at once.

Amends the proviso to sub-section (1-A) of section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It substitutes the words 'the Deputy Commissioner may' with 'the Deputy Commissioner other than the Deputy Commissioner of Bangalore Rural District and the Deputy Commissioner of Bangalore District, may'. This means the power to grant exemptions (not exceeding half hectare) is restricted from being exercised by the Deputy Commissioners of Bangalore Rural District and Bangalore District.

important_rules: Rule: Deputy Commissioners, other than those of Bangalore Rural District and Bangalore District, may exercise the power to grant exemptions to an extent not exceeding half hectare of land.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioners (with specific exclusions for Bangalore Rural and Bangalore Districts regarding certain powers)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By implementing the amended provisions of Section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, which governs the granting of land exemptions.

rights: The right for Deputy Commissioners (excluding Bangalore Rural and Bangalore Districts) to grant exemptions not exceeding half hectare of land.
duties: Duty for the State Legislature to enact laws for land reforms.
Duty for relevant authorities to implement the provisions of the amended Act.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the amended Section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka)
important_notes: The amendment is specifically to retain the power of the State Government (exercised by Deputy Commissioners) to grant exemptions in Bangalore Rural and Bangalore Districts.

The original power of Deputy Commissioners to grant exemptions to an extent not exceeding half hectare of land is now explicitly limited in its application to the Deputy Commissioners of Bangalore Rural District and Bangalore District.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech and to make consequential amendments to the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 34 of 1957). It applies to all instruments and transactions covered by the principal Act within the state of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2006 and that it shall come into force on April 1, 2006.

Introduces amendments to Section 45A of the principal Act, primarily concerning the insertion of sub-clauses and the substitution of figures and letters within clauses, and the imposition of interest on delayed payment of duty.

Introduces various amendments to the Schedule of the principal Act, including changes to Articles 6, 14, 20, 30, 41, and 53, pertaining to stamp duty rates and explanations for different types of instruments and transactions.

important_rules: Interest at twelve percent per annum is liable to be paid on duty if not paid within ninety days from the date of order of the Deputy Commissioner, with a proviso that this interest is not applicable to instruments executed prior to March 31, 2006.

For the purpose of clause (1) of Article 6, any letter, note, memorandum or writing relating to the deposit of title deeds, irrespective of when it was made or for what loan, shall be deemed to be an instrument evidencing an agreement relating to the deposit of title deeds, in the absence of a separate agreement.

Cancellation of instruments: The duty for cancellation of instruments varies depending on whether the original instrument was paid stamp duty as per any article of the Schedule, or if it was executed by or on behalf of the Central Government or a Local Authority, or in any other case. The duty is generally the same as on the original instrument or one hundred rupees.

penalties: Liable to pay duty with interest at twelve percent per annum if not paid within ninety days from the date of order of the Deputy Commissioner. (Note: This does not apply to instruments executed prior to 31st March, 2006).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner (as indicated by reference to 'order of the Deputy Commissioner').
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Deputy Commissioner and subsequent collection of duty and interest.

rights: Right to pay stamp duty on instruments.
Right to have instruments cancelled on payment of prescribed duty.
duties: Duty to pay stamp duty as per the Schedule to the Act.
Duty to pay interest on delayed payment of stamp duty.
obligations: Obligation to pay the correct stamp duty on instruments as determined by the Act.
Obligation to comply with the orders of the Deputy Commissioner regarding stamp duty and interest.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 45A: Involves specific insertions and substitutions of text within sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 45A of the principal Act. This includes adding references to sub-clauses and altering references to articles, as well as inserting provisions for interest on delayed payments.

Amendment of the Schedule: Involves substitutions and additions to various articles within the Schedule. For example, Article 14 (Cancellation of instruments) is replaced with new entries specifying duties for different scenarios. Article 20 (Conveyance) has its duty rates revised. Article 30 (Lease) includes new provisions for leases granted for rent or premium in addition to refundable deposits.

Determination of market value: Section 45A, as amended, relates to the determination of the market value of properties for the purpose of stamp duty calculation, with provisions for interest on delayed payments.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signature of the Secretary to Government). The enforcement is likely handled by revenue or stamp duty collection authorities, with the Deputy Commissioner playing a key role.
important_notes: The payment of interest is not applicable to instruments executed prior to 31st day of March, 2006.

The definition of an instrument evidencing an agreement relating to the deposit of title deeds is expanded to include letters, notes, or memorandums relating to deposit of title deeds, even if made at any time related to the deposit and for any loan amount.
The stamp duty rates for certain instruments, such as Conveyance and Transfer of lease, have been revised.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2008-2009 by amending the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and to make certain consequential amendments.
scope: This Act applies to motor vehicles within the state of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and specifically targets taxation rates and categories for motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, private service vehicles, and contract carriages.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 35 of 1957).
key_definitions.Cost of the vehicle: For a vehicle manufactured in India, it means the cost as per the purchase invoice including excise duty, sales tax, surcharge or cess, entry tax etc., payable in Karnataka. For an imported vehicle, it means the total cost incurred in importing, including customs duty, freight, and other taxes levied by the Customs Department or any other Department.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2008, and states that it comes into force from August 1, 2008.
Omit sub-section (4) of section 3 of the principal Act.
Substitutes 'five per centum' for 'seven per centum' in clause (ii) of section 10 of the principal Act.

Makes extensive amendments to the Schedule of the principal Act, including substitution of Part A5 with new lifetime tax rates for motor cars, jeeps, omni buses and private service vehicles based on cost and age, amendments to Part B concerning contract carriages, omission of Part D, and omission of item (5) in the explanation at the end of the Schedule.

important_rules: Lifetime tax for motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, and private service vehicles is levied at varying percentages of the vehicle's cost at the time of registration (12%, 13%, or 16% based on cost tiers).
For already registered vehicles, the lifetime tax is a percentage of the initially levied tax, decreasing with the age of the vehicle.
In respect of vehicles for which lifetime tax was due before August 1, 2008, but not paid, such tax will be collected at the rates prevailing before that date, along with any applicable penalty.
Amendments are made to the taxation of contract carriages based on passenger capacity and whether they are liable to be taxed under specific items in Part B.

penalties: Penalties may be applicable for unpaid lifetime tax due before August 1, 2008, collected at prior rates.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature enacted this act. Enforcement would typically be by the Motor Vehicles Department or other relevant state authorities responsible for taxation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and collection of motor vehicle taxes as stipulated in the amended Act and its Schedule.

rights: Right to register motor vehicles in Karnataka.
Right to pay lifetime tax according to the prescribed rates.
duties: Duty to pay lifetime tax on motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, and private service vehicles at the time of registration or renewal.
Duty to pay taxes for contract carriages as per the Schedule.
Duty to pay any accrued penalties for delayed tax payment.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the tax provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Collection of lifetime tax for new motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, and private service vehicles based on their cost and floor area at the time of registration.
Collection of reduced lifetime tax for already registered vehicles based on their age.
Collection of tax for contract carriages based on passenger capacity and hire status.
administration: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, as amended, is administered by the State Government of Karnataka, likely through its Transport Department and associated agencies.
important_notes: The amendment to Part A5 regarding substitution of rates is deemed to have been effective from April 1, 2003, and omitted from April 1, 2007.
The Act introduces a specific definition for 'Cost of the vehicle' for taxation purposes.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend certain taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka to give effect to budget proposals and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to various taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka. It amends the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932, the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, and the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force from the First day of April, 2009.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Mysore Act IX of 1932
main_sections.description: Amends the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932, specifically substituting Sections 6 (Betting Tax) and 7 (Payment of betting tax).
Amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, by modifying Sections 3, 4-G, 6-A, and inserting a new Section 8-F related to revision by the High Court.

Amends the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, by inserting new sub-sections in Sections 5, 6-A, and substituting sub-sections in Section 7. It also makes amendments in Sections 21, 26, and the Schedule.
Amends the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, by substituting sub-sections in Sections 3, and making modifications in Sections 3-B, 3-C, and 4.

important_rules: Rule 1: Betting tax on bets made by backers in an enclosure set apart by a licensee, through a licensed bookmaker, on any race, will be levied at a rate not exceeding fifty thousand rupees for each day of a race meeting, as specified by the State Government.
Rule 2: Every licensed bookmaker is liable to pay the betting tax levied under Section 6 in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed time, along with a return.
Rule 3: Admission to a game or sport involving proprietary teams, played for prize moneys and organized on a commercial basis, is not exempted from entertainment tax.

Rule 4: Assessment proceedings under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, for any prescribed period shall not be made after one year from the date of submission of the return, with certain exceptions.

Rule 5: In the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, a penalty of one thousand rupees for an employer and five hundred rupees for any other person will be imposed for failure to apply for registration or enrolment within the specified time.

Rule 6: A penalty of two hundred and fifty rupees will be imposed on an employer for failing to furnish a statement or pay the tax due on any statement furnished under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976.

Rule 7: Every employer under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, is deemed to have been assessed to tax based on the return filed, unless the Commissioner notifies otherwise.

Rule 8: Tax on luxury provided in a hotel is levied at varying rates (4%, 6%, 10%) based on the charges for lodging per room per day, with exemptions for members of Foreign Diplomatic Missions in India (subject to notification).
Rule 9: The tax on luxury provided in a hotel is to be levied and collected on lower charges where such lower charges are allowed as a reasonable concession.

penalties: Failure to apply for registration or enrolment under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, within the time specified: Rs. 1000 for employer, Rs. 500 for others.
Failure to furnish a statement or pay tax due under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976: Rs. 250.
Penalties related to incorrect or incomplete tax returns or non-compliance with assessment orders under various amended acts are implied through the amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority, Commissioner, High Court, Appellate Tribunal (as applicable under the respective amended Acts).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment proceedings, imposition of penalties, legal challenges through appeals and revisions, and court orders.

rights: Right to be heard before assessment or penalty imposition.
Right to prefer petitions to the High Court against orders of the Appellate Tribunal on questions of law.
Right to seek review or amendment of High Court orders.
Right to refund of overpaid tax.
Exemption from luxury tax for certain members of Foreign Diplomatic Missions.
duties: Duty to pay Betting Tax as a licensed bookmaker.
Duty to pay Entertainments Tax.
Duty to pay tax on professions, trades, callings and employments.
Duty to pay tax on luxuries provided in a hotel.
Duty to file tax returns accurately and on time.
Duty to produce accounts and documents when required by assessing authorities.
Duty to comply with assessment orders and directions from authorities.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to ensure their employees are assessed for tax on professions, trades, callings and employments.
Proprietors have an obligation to pay entertainment tax.
Hotel owners have an obligation to collect and remit luxury tax.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of betting tax, including payment and filing of returns.
Procedure for assessment of entertainment tax, including time limits for assessment and the role of the Commissioner in directing random assessments.
Procedure for revision of orders by the High Court, including grounds for petition, time limits, fees, and the process of hearing and determination.

Procedure for imposing penalties for failure to register or file statements under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, including the requirement of providing an opportunity to be heard.
Procedure for assessment under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, based on returns or best judgment assessment.
Procedure for levying and collecting luxury tax in hotels, including the computation of charges and exemptions.
administration: Various departments and authorities responsible for the administration of taxation laws in the State of Karnataka, including the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes and assessing authorities.
important_notes: The Act comes into force from April 1, 2009.
Assessment proceedings under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, related to periods before the commencement of this amendment Act must be completed within one year from such commencement.
The High Court can allow petitions for revision to be preferred after the stipulated period if sufficient cause is shown.
The Government may notify certain classes of employers for deemed assessment based on their returns under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976.
Exemptions from luxury tax apply to certain members of the Foreign Diplomatic Mission in India.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2010-11 and to safeguard Government revenue by ensuring that disputed amounts are paid when appeals are filed.
scope: This act applies to motor vehicles in the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 35 of 1957).
key_definitions.Construction Equipment Vehicles: As defined in clause(ca) of rule 2 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
key_definitions.Cost of the vehicle: For vehicles manufactured in India, it includes the cost as per the purchase invoice, including excise duty, sales tax, surcharge, cess, and entry tax payable in Karnataka. For imported vehicles, it's the total cost incurred in importing, including Customs Duty, freight, and other taxes assessed under the Customs Act, 1962.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2010, and states its commencement date as April 1, 2010.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by changing the weight limit in a proviso from '3000 kgs' to '5500 kgs' and introduces a provision for levying tax on Construction Equipment Vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators.
Amends Section 15 of the principal Act by inserting a requirement that an appeal must be accompanied by proof of payment of the disputed amount.

Amends various parts of the Schedule to the principal Act, including altering tax rates for different vehicle categories (e.g., Item No. 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 14 in Part A), substituting entire parts (A1, A5, A6, A7) with new tax structures, particularly for lifetime tax on two-wheelers, motor cars, jeeps, omni buses, private service vehicles, and goods vehicles, and introducing a new Part A7 for Construction Equipment Vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators.
Grants the Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule for Construction Equipment Vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators: Tax shall be levied at the rate specified in Part A-7 of the Schedule.
Rule for appeals: An appeal must be accompanied by proof of payment of the disputed amount.
Rule for vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2007: Purchase invoices must be produced.
Rule for vehicles where lifetime tax was due before April 1, 2010, but not paid: Tax shall be collected at pre-April 1, 2010 rates along with any due penalty.
Definition of 'Cost of the vehicle' for imported motor vehicles includes the value assessed under the Customs Act, 1962, plus Customs Duty, freight, and other levied taxes/duties.

penalties: Penalties may be levied on unpaid taxes due before April 1, 2010.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the motor vehicles taxation authorities in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, including changes to tax rates and requirements for appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against orders, subject to payment of disputed amounts.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicle tax as per the rates and schedules specified.
Duty to accompany appeals with proof of payment of disputed amounts.
Duty to produce purchase invoices for vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2007.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax at the time of registration of new vehicles.
Obligation to pay tax based on the age of the vehicle if already registered.

key_procedures: Procedure for calculating Lifetime Tax for Two Wheelers: Varies based on the cost of the vehicle at registration and its age.
Procedure for calculating Lifetime Tax for Motor Cars, Jeeps, Omni Buses and Private Service Vehicles: Varies based on the cost and floor area of the vehicle at registration and its age.
Procedure for calculating Lifetime Tax for Goods Vehicles: Varies based on the gross vehicle weight and age of the vehicle.
Procedure for levying tax on Construction Equipment Vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators: 10% of cost at registration, with reduced percentages based on age.
Procedure for filing appeals: Appeals must be accompanied by proof of payment of the disputed amount.
administration: Implied to be the Karnataka Transport Department or relevant taxation authorities.
important_notes: Tax rates and structures for various vehicle categories have been significantly revised.
Specific provisions are made for vehicles where tax was due before April 1, 2010, but not paid.
The definition of 'Cost of the vehicle' is detailed for both Indian manufactured and imported vehicles.
The Act requires proof of payment to accompany appeals, aiming to secure government revenue.

title: THE KARNATAKA LABOUR WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965, specifically to increase the ratio of contributions payable to the welfare fund from Labourers, Employers, and the Government.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965. It applies to all aspects covered by the original Act, with the specific amendment relating to contribution ratios within the labour welfare fund system in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010, and states that it shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 7A of the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965. It substitutes the existing ratio of contributions (three rupees : six rupees : three rupees) for Labourers, Employers, and Government, respectively, with a new ratio of six rupees : twelve rupees : six rupees.

important_rules: The contribution ratio to the Labour Welfare Fund shall be 6 rupees from Labourers, 12 rupees from Employers, and 6 rupees from the Government, replacing the previous ratio of 3:6:3.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in this amendment, but implied to be the authority responsible for the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and mechanisms established by the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965, as amended.

duties: Employers and Labourers have a duty to contribute to the Labour Welfare Fund according to the revised ratio.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka is responsible for issuing the act. The administration of the Labour Welfare Fund itself is managed by the relevant authorities under the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965.
important_notes: The amendment is to the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965 (Karnataka Act 15 of 1965).
The amendment increases the financial contribution to the Labour Welfare Fund.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 to extend the time limit for payment of property tax for the financial year 2020-21 and to provide a rebate of five percent on property tax if paid within one month from the commencement of the Amendment Act.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, specifically concerning property tax payments for the financial year 2020-21.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2021, and it comes into force at once.

Amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It inserts provisions for a five percent rebate on property tax for the financial year 2020-2021 if paid within one month of the commencement of this Amendment Act. It also stipulates that for the financial year 2020-2021, property tax shall be paid within one month after the commencement of this Act. It also addresses the adjustment of rebates for future tax payments if tax was paid in full before the commencement of this Act.

Amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. It inserts provisions for property tax payment for the financial year 2020-2021 to be made within one month from the commencement of this Amendment Act. It also provides for a five percent rebate on property tax for the financial year 2020-2021 if paid within one month of the commencement of this Amendment Act, and specifies how rebates will be adjusted if tax was paid in full before the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: For the financial year 2020-2021, property tax payers in municipalities covered by the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, who file returns and pay tax within one month of the commencement of this Amendment Act, will receive a five percent rebate on the tax payable.

For the financial year 2020-2021, property tax payers in areas covered by the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, who file returns and pay tax within one month of the commencement of this Amendment Act, will receive a five percent rebate on the tax payable.
For the financial year 2020-2021, property tax under the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, must be paid by the person primarily liable within one month after the commencement of this Amendment Act.

For the financial year 2020-2021, property tax under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, must be paid by the person primarily liable within one month from the date of commencement of this Amendment Act.
If property tax for the financial year 2020-21 was paid in full before the commencement of this Amendment Act, any rebate allowed shall be adjusted in the payment of tax for future years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the municipal authorities and corporations governed by the amended acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, as amended by this Act.

rights: Right to receive a five percent rebate on property tax for the financial year 2020-2021 if paid within one month of the commencement of the Act, subject to conditions.
Right to have any rebate adjusted in future tax payments if property tax for FY 2020-21 was paid in full before the commencement of the Act.
duties: Duty to pay property tax for the financial year 2020-2021 within one month from the date of commencement of this Amendment Act.
obligations: Obligation for owners or occupiers liable to pay tax to file returns and pay the due tax within the stipulated time to avail the rebate.

key_procedures: Procedure for availing a 5% property tax rebate for FY 2020-21: File returns and pay the due tax within one month from the commencement of the Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2021.

Procedure for tax payment for FY 2020-21: Property tax must be paid by the person primarily liable within one month after the commencement of the Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2021.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory of the Act). The actual administration of property tax collection would fall under the respective Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations.
important_notes: The Act specifically addresses the financial year 2020-2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The rebate of five percent is applicable if the property tax is paid within one month from the date of commencement of this Amendment Act.
If property tax for FY 2020-21 was paid in full before the commencement of this Act, the allowed rebate shall be adjusted in future tax payments.

title: THE KANNADA LANGUAGE COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To amend the Kannada Language Comprehensive Development Act, 2022 (Karnataka Act 13 of 2023) to appoint the Director, Directorate of Kannada and Culture as a Member and the Secretary, Kannada Development Authority as the convener of the State Level Committee, and to mandate that name boards of certain undertakings display 60% of their content in Kannada, with Kannada in the upper half of the board.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Kannada Language Comprehensive Development Act, 2022. Specifically, it impacts the composition of the State Level Committee and the display requirements for name boards of commercial, industrial, business undertakings, trusts, counseling centers, hospitals, laboratories, amusement centers, and hotels functioning with government or local authority approval.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kannada Language Comprehensive Development (Amendment) Act, 2024' and states that it will come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Amends Section 7 of the Principal Act (Kannada Language Comprehensive Development Act, 2022). It substitutes item (vii) in clause (a) of sub-section (2) to include 'The Director, Directorate of Kannada and Culture - Member' and inserts a new clause (vii-a) stating 'The Secretary, Kannada Development Authority shall be the convener of the Committee.'

Amends Section 17 of the Principal Act by substituting sub-section (6). The substituted sub-section mandates that name boards of Commercial, Industrial and Business Undertakings, Trusts, Counseling Centre’s, Hospitals, Laboratories, Amusement Centers and Hotels etc., functioning with the approval and sanction of the Government or Local Authorities, shall ensure that their name board displays 60% in Kannada language and Kannada shall be displayed in the upper half of the name board.

important_rules: Rule 1: Name boards of commercial, industrial, and business undertakings, trusts, counseling centers, hospitals, laboratories, amusement centers, and hotels must display at least 60% of their content in the Kannada language.
Rule 2: Kannada language must be displayed in the upper half of the name board for the aforementioned entities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act itself does not explicitly state the enforcement authority or penalties. However, it amends existing legislation, implying enforcement mechanisms would be under the purview of the 'Principal Act' and relevant government departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act's provisions regarding name boards would likely be enforced through inspections and directives by relevant government bodies or local authorities responsible for ensuring compliance with language display regulations.

rights: Citizens have a right to see commercial and public signage predominantly in Kannada as per the regulations.
The right to promote and develop the Kannada language is being strengthened through this amendment.
duties: Commercial, industrial, and business undertakings, trusts, counseling centers, hospitals, laboratories, amusement centers, and hotels functioning with government or local authority approval have a duty to display their name boards with 60% content in Kannada and Kannada in the upper half.
obligations: The State Government has the obligation to notify the commencement date of the Act.
The Directorate of Kannada and Culture and the Kannada Development Authority have an obligation to fulfill their roles as specified in the amended sections.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government may notify the date of commencement of the Act in the Official Gazette.

Procedure 2: The State Level Committee's composition is amended to include the Director, Directorate of Kannada and Culture as a member, and the Secretary, Kannada Development Authority as the convener.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (which published the Act) and likely the Directorate of Kannada and Culture and the Kannada Development Authority, based on the amendments.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kannada Language Comprehensive Development Act, 2022 (Karnataka Act 13 of 2023).
The amendments are made in accordance with Article 345 and Article 348(3) of the Constitution of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor of Karnataka on the 25th day of February, 2024.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary No.113 on 26.02.2024.

title: The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment Etc.,) (Second Amendment) Act, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment Etc.,) Act, 1990. Specifically, to address the issue of unfilled vacancies reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and to provide an appropriate appellate authority for caste verification matters.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and governs reservation of appointments in services or posts in establishments in the public sector for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. It also deals with appeals related to the verification of these community statuses.

key_definitions.unfilled_vacancies: Includes backlog in direct recruitment, vacancies not filled by SC/ST persons during regularization of daily wage employees, and any shortfall in representation of SC/ST persons in direct recruitment to reach 15% for SC and 3% for ST.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment Etc.,) (Second Amendment) Act, 2004' and states that it shall come into force at once.
Inserts a new clause (8) in Section 2 of the principal Act to define 'Unfilled vacancies'.

Inserts a new sub-section (1A) in Section 4 of the principal Act, mandating appointing authorities to identify and fill unfilled reserved vacancies for SC/ST as a one-time measure. It also clarifies that appointments already made are not affected.

Substitutes Section 4D of the principal Act, establishing the appellate authorities for orders passed by Verification Committees concerning SC, ST, and OBC status. It also provides for the transfer of pending appeals.

important_rules: Rule: Appointing authorities must identify and fill unfilled vacancies reserved for SC/ST as a one-time measure within a specified time as notified by the State Government.
Rule: Appointments already made of SC/ST persons to fill unfilled vacancies before the commencement of this Act are not affected.
Rule: Appeals against orders of the Verification Committee must be filed within thirty days of receipt of the order to the respective Commissioner/Director for SC, ST, or BC.
Rule: Appeals pending before Divisional Commissioners or other authorities stand transferred to the new Appellate Authorities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the appointing authorities, the State Government, and the designated Appellate Authorities (Commissioner/Director, Social Welfare; Director, Tribal Welfare; Director, Backward Classes Department).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through mandatory identification and filling of vacancies, appellate review of caste verification decisions, and the legal framework established by the Act.

rights: Right of SC/ST persons to have reserved vacancies filled.
Right to appeal against decisions of Caste Verification Committees.
duties: Duty of appointing authorities to identify and fill unfilled reserved vacancies.
Duty of State Government to specify the manner of computation, procedure, and time for filling vacancies.
Duty of Appellate Authorities to hear appeals and pass orders.
obligations: Obligation to comply with reservation policies for SC/ST and OBC in public sector appointments.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for caste verification and appeals.

key_procedures: Procedure for filling unfilled vacancies: Appointing authorities identify vacancies, the State Government notifies the computation method, filling procedure, and timeline. This is a one-time measure.

Procedure for appeals against caste verification: An aggrieved person files an appeal within 30 days to the designated Commissioner/Director. The Appellate Authority hears both parties and passes an order. Pending appeals are transferred and disposed of.
administration: Department of Social Welfare, Department of Tribal Welfare, Department of Backward Classes, and the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act itself).
important_notes: The Second Amendment Act would not affect any appointment already made on the ground that the procedure prescribed was not fully or partially followed.
The provisions of the inserted sub-section (1A) in Section 4 do not apply to unfilled vacancies in Karnataka State Civil Services or posts for which provisions have already been made.
The Act aims to provide a legal basis for recruitment already completed by Universities and other institutions which were not covered by previous rules.
The amendments concerning appellate authorities address the abolition of Divisional Commissioner posts and conferment of powers on other authorities.

title: THE BANGALORE METROPOLITAN REGION DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985, specifically to confine the jurisdiction of the Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority to Bangalore urban and rural districts by deleting Malur taluk of Kolar district from the Bangalore Metropolitan region.
scope: This act applies to the Bangalore Metropolitan Region, as defined by the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985, and specifically amends its geographical scope. It directly impacts the Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority.

key_definitions.Bangalore Metropolitan Region: As defined in the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985, prior to this amendment included Malur taluk of Kolar district. This amendment redefines it.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the act as the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2005, and states that it comes into force immediately upon enactment.

Amends clause (c) of section 2 of the Principal Act (Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985) by substituting the words 'Malur Taluk of Kolar District' with 'Bangalore Rural District'.

important_rules: Rule: The jurisdiction of the Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority shall be confined to Bangalore urban and rural districts.
Rule: Malur taluk of Kolar district is to be excluded from the Bangalore Metropolitan region.
Rule: The amendment to section 2(c) of the Principal Act takes effect immediately.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority and relevant government departments for administering the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985.

duties: Duty of the Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority to operate within the revised geographical jurisdiction.

key_procedures: Procedure: Substitution of text in Section 2(c) of the Principal Act. This involves replacing specific words to alter the definition of the Bangalore Metropolitan Region.
Procedure: Commencement of the Act at once, meaning its provisions are effective immediately upon enactment.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (for legislative process), and the Bangalore Metropolitan Development Authority (for operational administration).
important_notes: Note: This is an amendment act, intended to modify an existing principal act.
Note: The amendment is based on the need to redefine the geographical boundaries of the Bangalore Metropolitan Region.
Note: The assent of the Governor was received on twenty third day of March, 2005.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROFESSIONAL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (REGULATION OF ADMISSION AND DETERMINATION OF FEE) ACT, 2006
purpose: To provide for the regulation of admission and determination of fee in professional educational institutions in the State of Karnataka and to provide for reservation of seats to persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in professional educational institutions.
scope: This Act applies to professional educational institutions in the State of Karnataka, including government, aided, and unaided institutions (both minority and non-minority). It covers the regulation of admissions and the determination of fees for professional educational courses.

key_definitions.admission: Admission made at the admission centre.
key_definitions.admission_centre: The centre where selection and allotment of seats to candidates for various courses in professional institutions are made through the Common Entrance Test based on merit.
key_definitions.aided_institution: A private professional educational institution receiving financial aid or grant-in-aid from the State Government, including minority and non-minority institutions.
key_definitions.common_entrance_test: The entrance test conducted for determining the merit of candidates, followed by centralized counseling for admission to professional educational courses through a single window procedure.
key_definitions.fee_regulatory_committee: The committee constituted for the determination and regulation of fees for admission to private unaided professional educational institutions.
key_definitions.professional_educational_institution: A college, school, or institute, by whatever name called, imparting professional education or conducting professional educational courses leading to the award of a degree, diploma, or certificate, approved or recognized by the competent statutory body and affiliated to a university.
key_definitions.reserved_seats: Seats reserved in Government colleges, constituent colleges of universities, private aided and unaided professional educational institutions in favour of persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes as notified by the State Government.
