main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and mentions that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Admission', 'Admission Centre', 'Aided institution', 'Common Entrance Test', 'Fee Regulatory Committee', 'Government seats', 'Professional Educational Institution', 'Reserved seats', and others.
Establishes the State Common Entrance Test Committee and outlines its composition, including a Chairperson and Members.

main_sections.section_title: Method of admission in unaided professional educational institutions
main_sections.description: Details the method of admission in unaided professional educational institutions.
Constitutes the Admission Overseeing Committee for regulating admissions in private unaided professional educational institutions.
Constitutes the Fee Regulatory Committee for determining and regulating fees in private unaided professional educational institutions.
Specifies the factors to be considered for determining fees.
Outlines the penalties for violations of the Act.
States that this Act will have an overriding effect on other laws in force.

important_rules: All institutions of the same or similar type, whether minority or non-minority, must fill their seats through a single common entrance test followed by centralized counseling to ensure transparency and merit.
The State can regulate admission by providing a centralized and single window procedure to ensure fair and merit-based admissions and prevent maladministration.
Sixty-six percent of reservation in minority institutions is provided for students from that community within the State.

Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes is provided to the extent of fifty percent in Government, aided, and unaided non-minority professional educational institutions.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act are specified in Section 19.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and committees constituted under the Act (State Common Entrance Test Committee, Admission Overseeing Committee, Fee Regulatory Committee) are responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes conducting common entrance tests, centralized counseling, regulating admissions, determining fees, and imposing penalties for violations. The State Government has the power to issue directions.

rights: Right to admission based on merit through a single window system.
Right to have fees determined and regulated by the Fee Regulatory Committee.
Right of minority communities to have seats reserved for students from their community within the State in minority institutions.
Right to reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.
duties: Duty of professional educational institutions to comply with admission regulations.
Duty of professional educational institutions to adhere to fee structures determined by the Fee Regulatory Committee.
Duty of the State Government to constitute committees for regulation and to issue notifications.
Duty of candidates to participate in the common entrance test and centralized counseling.
obligations: Obligation to conduct a single common entrance test followed by centralized counseling.
Obligation to reserve seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.
Obligation to adhere to fee determination criteria.

key_procedures: Conducting a Common Entrance Test for admission to professional courses.
Centralized counseling for allotment of seats based on merit.
Regulation of admissions in private unaided professional educational institutions by the Admission Overseeing Committee.
Determination and regulation of fees for admission to private unaided professional educational institutions by the Fee Regulatory Committee.
administration: The State Government and various committees constituted under the Act, including the State Common Entrance Test Committee, Admission Overseeing Committee, and Fee Regulatory Committee, are responsible for the administration of the Act.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
The Act overrides other laws in force, providing a comprehensive framework for regulating admissions and fees in professional educational institutions.
Minority educational institutions are subject to specific provisions regarding reservation for students from their community within the State.
The State Government has the power to remove difficulties and to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2008-2009, and to make consequential amendments to the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. It applies to instruments falling under the purview of stamp duty in Karnataka. Specifically, it amends provisions related to loans, debts, pawn or pledge of jewels and goods, and certain financial instruments.

key_definitions.money advanced: In Article 30(1)(c), it means and includes the security deposit, whether refundable or adjustable towards the rent.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2008, and specifies its commencement date as the first day of August, 2008.

Details the specific amendments made to various articles within the Schedule of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. These amendments include changes to stamp duty rates and exemptions for various instruments.

important_rules: Rule 1 (Article 6(1)(a)): Specifies revised stamp duty rates for loan or debt repayment instruments repayable on demand for more than three months, based on the loan amount. It introduces a maximum stamp duty of Rupees five lakhs.
Rule 2 (Article 6(1)(b)): Modifies the stamp duty for certain loan or debt instruments to be calculated 'for the amount secured subject to a maximum of Rupees five lakhs'.

Rule 3 (Article 6(2)): Substitutes the exemption clause for instruments of pawn or pledge of jewels and goods. Jewels with loans up to Rupees ten thousand are exempted. Unattested instruments of pawn or pledge of goods are also exempted.

Rule 4 (Article 20(4)(a) and (b)): Amends the stamp duty for certain instruments under Article 20(4) to be '5% on the market value of the property', replacing the previous 'same duty as a conveyance under Article 20(1) on the market value of the property'.

Rule 5 (Article 20(4)(c)): Introduces an exemption for 'Amalgamation of sick companies with others, under the orders of Board of Industrial Finance and Reconstruction (BIFR)' from stamp duty under Article 20(4).
Rule 6 (Article 30(1)(a)): Substitutes 'more than five years' for 'less than five years' in item (iii) of sub-clause (a) of Article 30(1).
Rule 7 (Article 30(1)(c)(ii)): Inserts an explanation for the term 'money advanced' in Article 30(1)(c)(ii) to include security deposits.
Rule 8 (Article 30(1)(d)): Omission of sub-clause (d) and its related entries under Article 30(1).
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendments aim to align stamp duty with budget proposals for 2008-2009.
Specific maximum limits have been introduced for stamp duty on certain loan and debt instruments (e.g., Rupees five lakhs).
Exemptions have been clarified or introduced for specific types of pawn/pledge instruments and company amalgamations.

title: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, in order to give effect to the Budget Speech for the year 2009-10 by amending the taxation rates for certain classes of motor vehicles.
scope: This act applies to motor vehicles registered in the state of Karnataka. It specifically amends the taxation structure for two-wheelers, motor cars, jeeps, omnibuses, and private service vehicles.

key_definitions.cost_of_vehicle: In relation to a motor vehicle, it means: (a) for vehicles manufactured in India, the cost as per the purchase invoice including excise duty, sales tax, surcharge, cess, entry tax, etc., payable in Karnataka; and (b) for imported vehicles, the total cost incurred in importing, including assessed value in the Bill of Entry, Customs Duty, freight charges, and other applicable taxes and penalties.
key_definitions.lifetime_tax: The tax levied on motor vehicles, particularly detailed in Parts A1 and A5 of the Schedule, with different rates based on vehicle cost and age.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2009, and it came into force from the first day of April 2009.

Amends the Schedule of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It substitutes Part A1 (Lifetime Tax for Two-wheelers) and Part A5 (Lifetime Tax for Motor cars, Jeeps, Omni Buses and Private Service Vehicles) with new provisions detailing tax rates based on vehicle cost, type, and age.

important_rules: Lifetime tax for two-wheelers is to be 8% of the cost for motorcycles not exceeding Rs. 50,000, 10% for motorcycles exceeding Rs. 50,000, and 4% for electric motorcycles, calculated at the time of registration. Subsequent years will have reduced percentages of this initial tax.

Lifetime tax for motor cars, jeeps, omnibuses, and private service vehicles with floor area up to 5 Sq.Mtrs is to be 12% of the cost if it does not exceed Rs. 5 Lakhs, 13% if it exceeds Rs. 5 Lakhs but not Rs. 10 Lakhs, and 16% if it exceeds Rs. 10 Lakhs. Electric cars/vans will have a 4% tax rate. Subsequent years will have reduced percentages of this initial tax.
For vehicles where lifetime tax was due before April 1, 2009, but not paid, the tax will be collected at the rates prevailing before that date, along with any applicable penalty.

penalties: Penalties are mentioned in relation to the collection of due tax for vehicles where the tax was due prior to April 1, 2009, and has not been paid.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the state transport or taxation authorities responsible for motor vehicle taxation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection of taxes as per the amended schedule and the imposition of penalties for non-payment of due taxes.

rights: Right to have tax calculated based on the amended rates.
Right to have tax calculated based on the vehicle's cost and age.
duties: Duty to pay lifetime tax for motor vehicles as per the amended provisions.
Duty to pay tax at the rates prevailing prior to April 1, 2009, along with penalty, if the tax was due before that date and not paid.
obligations: Obligation to register new vehicles and pay the applicable lifetime tax at the time of registration.
Obligation to comply with the revised tax structure for existing registered vehicles.

key_procedures: Calculation of Lifetime Tax for New Vehicles: Determine the class of vehicle (e.g., two-wheeler, car), its cost, and whether it's electric. Apply the specified percentage of the cost (e.g., 8%, 10%, 4% for two-wheelers; 12%, 13%, 16%, 4% for cars/vans) at the time of registration.

Calculation of Lifetime Tax for Registered Vehicles (after initial period): Determine the age of the vehicle from its registration month. Apply the corresponding percentage of the initially levied lifetime tax (e.g., 93% for vehicles up to 2 years old, reducing incrementally with age).
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (responsible for drafting and enactment), and implied administrative authorities for motor vehicle taxation in Karnataka.
important_notes: In respect of vehicles for which lifetime tax was due prior to April 1, 2009, but has not been paid, such tax shall be collected at the rates prevailing prior to such day along with the penalty due, if any.
The definition of 'cost of the vehicle' is crucial for calculating the tax, covering both Indian-manufactured and imported vehicles, and includes various associated costs and duties.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech 2010-11 by further amending the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. It affects instruments and transactions related to stamp duty within Karnataka.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 34 of 1957)
key_definitions.Depository Act, 1996: The Depository Act, 1996, as referred to in Article 4, clause (1)(d)(i) concerning de-mat accounts.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Stamp (Second Amendment) Act, 2010 and specifies its commencement date as April 1, 2010.
Amends Section 9 of the principal Act concerning the reduction or remission of stamp duty by the State Government in public interest.
Amends Section 45-A of the principal Act, specifically concerning Transferable Development Rights.
Introduces various amendments to the Schedule of the principal Act, modifying stamp duty rates and conditions for different types of instruments like agreements, conveyances, leases, and licenses.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may, in public interest, reduce or remit stamp duty on instruments executed for agricultural loans, loans for public sector undertakings, or loans for education and water harvesting/non-conventional energy.

Rule 2: The State Government may, in public interest, by notification, reduce or remit stamp duty on instruments related to housing programs (like Indira Awaas Yojana) implemented by Rajiv Gandhi Housing Corporation, and instruments in favour of local bodies for public amenities.

Rule 3: Stamp duty on a deed of cancellation of an earlier agreement will not exceed Rs. 500 if executed between the same parties for the same property and proper stamp duty was paid on the original agreement.
Rule 4: Stamp duty on agreements for sale, etc., is to be calculated on the market value equal to the amount of consideration, subject to maximum and minimum limits.
Rule 5: Specific stamp duties are prescribed for contracts related to de-mat accounts and stock market operations between Depository Participants/stock brokers and clients.

rights: Right to obtain stamp duty reductions or remissions under specific public interest conditions as outlined in Section 9.
duties: Duty to pay the prescribed stamp duty on various instruments as amended by this Act.
Duty to adhere to the conditions for stamp duty concessions or remissions.
obligations: Obligation to pay stamp duty on Transferable Development Rights.
Obligation to pay stamp duty on agreements for sale, leases, and licenses based on market value and consideration as per the amended rates.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for reduction or remission of stamp duty by the State Government in public interest, as detailed in the amended Section 9.

Procedure 2: Calculation of stamp duty for various instruments (agreements, conveyances, leases, licenses) based on market value, consideration, term of agreement, or other specified criteria, as per the amended Schedule.
administration: The Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, and its amendments are administered by the Department of Stamps and Registration, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act comes into force with effect from April 1, 2010.
Specific conditions apply for stamp duty calculation and concessions, particularly concerning agreements, cancellations, powers of attorney, leases, and licenses.
The amendments introduce specific stamp duty rates for electronic transactions and financial market operations.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 to include Chikkaballapur and Ramanagara districts into the jurisdiction of Bangalore University; to include Yadagiri district into the jurisdiction of Gulbarga University; to specify the qualifications for the appointment of the Registrar; and to enhance the retirement age of the Vice-Chancellor.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka State Universities and their jurisdictions within the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2011' and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting clauses (a) and (b) of sub-section (1) to include Chikkaballapur and Ramanagara districts in the jurisdiction of Bangalore University, and Yadagiri district in the jurisdiction of Gulbarga University.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (5) to stipulate that no person shall be appointed or hold office of the Vice-Chancellor if they have attained the age of sixty-seven years.

Amends section 17 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) to state that the Registrar shall be a whole-time officer of the University and that the State Government may appoint an officer not below the rank of Group-A officer of the super time scale or a member of the faculty of any university working as a Professor for at least five years, to be a Registrar of a University.

Repeals the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010 (Karnataka Ordinance No.2 of 2010) and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The jurisdiction of Bangalore University now includes Chikkaballapur and Ramanagara districts.
Rule 2: The jurisdiction of Gulbarga University now includes Yadagiri district.
Rule 3: A person cannot be appointed or hold the office of Vice-Chancellor if they are sixty-seven years of age or older.
Rule 4: The Registrar must be a whole-time officer of the University.
Rule 5: The State Government can appoint a Registrar who is a Group-A officer of super time scale or a Professor with at least five years of experience.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for appointment of Registrar)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 and potential administrative actions by the State Government.

duties: Universities must adhere to the amended jurisdictional boundaries.
The State Government has the duty to appoint qualified Registrars.
Vice-Chancellors must comply with the age limit for their office.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The Act replaces the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010.
The amendments are considered to have been in force retroactively from the time of the Ordinance.
The Act is enacted under Entry 25 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, with the objectives of controlling unauthorized construction by collecting property tax and penalty equal to property tax on such buildings, and to levy fees and annual track rent on cables laid by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.
scope: This Act applies to the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and buildings constructed within its jurisdiction in Karnataka. It specifically addresses unauthorized constructions and the laying of cables.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2020, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 108-A of the Principal Act to introduce a penalty for constructing or reconstructing any building or part thereof without permission or in contravention of permission. The penalty is an additional amount equal to the property tax leviable on the unauthorized construction area, payable annually as long as it remains unlawful.
Amends section 423, sub-section (7), clause (bb) of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'such fee or' with 'such one time fee and'. This likely relates to the fees for laying cables.

important_rules: Unauthorized construction or reconstruction of buildings or parts thereof without permission or in violation of permission conditions will be liable to pay an annual penalty equal to the property tax on the unauthorized area.
The penalty for unauthorized construction is payable as long as the construction remains unlawful.
The act allows for the levy of fees and annual track rent on cables, including optional fibre cables, laid by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.

penalties: Annual penalty for unauthorized construction equal to the property tax leviable on the unauthorized floor area or deviation.
Proceedings may be instituted in respect of unlawful construction, in addition to the penalty.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and relevant authorities under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition and collection of penalties and by instituting legal proceedings for unlawful construction.

rights: Right to obtain permission for building construction.
Right to have fees and annual track rent levied on cables by the BBMP.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before constructing or reconstructing a building or part thereof.
Duty to comply with the conditions specified in building permissions.
Duty to pay property tax and penalties as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to pay an additional annual penalty equal to the property tax for unauthorized construction.
Obligation to pay a one-time fee and annual track rent for cables laid by the BBMP.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission for building construction (implied by the amendments).
Procedure for levying and collecting property tax and penalties on unauthorized construction.
Procedure for levying and collecting fees and annual track rent on cables.
administration: Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) and the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (for legislative enactment and oversight).
important_notes: The amendment specifically targets unauthorized construction within the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.
The penalty for unauthorized construction is levied annually and continues as long as the construction remains unlawful.

title: The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Second Amendment) Act, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, specifically to enable an employee to carry forward forty-five days of leave instead of thirty days to a succeeding year.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, and amends specific provisions related to employee leave. The geographical scope is Karnataka. The subject matter scope is the regulation of leave entitlement for employees in shops and commercial establishments in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Second Amendment) Act, 2020' and specifies that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (7) of section 15 of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961. It substitutes the first proviso to allow employees to carry forward a maximum of forty-five days of leave to a succeeding year, replacing the previous limit of thirty days.

important_rules: Rule: The total number of leave days that may be carried forward to a succeeding year shall not exceed forty-five days.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement authority is not explicitly mentioned in this amendment, but it would be the authorities responsible for enforcing the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The methods of enforcement are not detailed in this amendment, but would likely involve inspections and compliance checks by relevant labor authorities.

rights: Right to carry forward up to forty-five days of leave to a succeeding year.

administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is responsible for the legislative process, and the administration of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, would typically fall under the purview of the Labour Department of the Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: This amendment specifically modifies the leave carry-forward provision within the existing Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.
The act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on February 19, 2021, and received the Governor's assent on February 17, 2021.

title: THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To provide for speedy disposal of cases involving persons having no sustained strength to fight prolonged litigation, specifically small or marginal farmers and persons of economically weaker sections, by stipulating a reasonable time frame for case disposal.
scope: This act applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908) in its application to Karnataka. The subject matter scope covers civil suits and other proceedings where small farmers or economically weaker sections are parties.

key_definitions.small_farmer: A person who, on the date of commencement of this Act, holds land (owner, mortgagee with possession, or both) up to a limit determined by the State Government, deriving annual income not exceeding the amount determined by the State Government from agriculture, and having no income from any other source.
key_definitions.persons_belonging_to_weaker_section: Persons whose annual income from all sources does not exceed an amount specified by the Government from time to time.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Code of Civil Procedure (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2023, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of Karnataka, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new rule 4 in Order XVII C.P.C.
main_sections.description: This section inserts a new rule (Rule 4) into Order XVII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, concerning the priority of disposal of cases involving small farmers and persons belonging to economically weaker sections.

important_rules: Rule 4(1): Cases involving small farmers or economically weaker sections (as plaintiff or defendant) shall be taken up on priority over other cases listed for the day.

Rule 4(2): Such cases should be heard and disposed of, as far as possible, within six months from the date of commencement of the Act (for pending cases) or from the date of appearance (for newly filed cases).

Rule 4(3): A party claiming the benefit can apply to the Court with an affidavit proving their beneficiary status for preferential disposal. The Court shall summarily try disputed beneficiary status within fifteen days.
Rule 4(4): In disposing of cases under this rule, the Court may adopt procedures from Order X, Order XII, and Order XXXVII of the Code.
Rule 4(5): No adjournment shall be granted at the instance of the opponent of the beneficiary, except for compelling reasons recorded by the Court.

penalties: Compensatory costs may be imposed in cases where the beneficiary status is disputed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts in the State of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By prioritizing and expediting the hearing and disposal of cases involving eligible beneficiaries, and by imposing restrictions on adjournments for opponents.

rights: Right to have cases involving small farmers and economically weaker sections taken up on priority.
Right to have such cases disposed of within a reasonable timeframe (six months).
duties: Duty of the Court to hear and dispose of eligible cases on priority within the stipulated time.
Duty of the Court to grant adjournments to the opponent only for compelling reasons.
obligations: Obligation for beneficiaries to apply for preferential treatment with proof of status (if disputed).
Obligation for the Court to summarily try disputed beneficiary status.

key_procedures: Application for preferential treatment: A party claiming benefit under this rule may apply to the Court with an affidavit proving their status. If the applicant is a defendant, the application can be made on their first appearance.

Summary trial of beneficiary status: If the beneficiary status is disputed, the Court shall summarily try the question and dispose of the application within fifteen days, potentially with compensatory costs.
Prioritization of cases: The Court shall take up eligible cases on priority over other cases listed for the day.
Time-bound disposal: The Court shall strive to hear and dispose of eligible cases within six months.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: Explanation 1: A 'case' includes a suit or other proceeding arising out of such suit pending in the High Court or other Civil Courts.
Explanation 2: The State Government determines the units of land and the annual income threshold for 'small farmers'.
Explanation 3: The Government specifies the annual income threshold for 'persons belonging to weaker sections'.

title: THE KARNATAKA VETERINARY, ANIMAL AND FISHERIES SCIENCES UNIVERSITY ACT, 2004
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a separate University for Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences in the State of Karnataka and to provide for matters connected therewith, including imparting education, advancing learning, prosecuting research, and undertaking extension of specialized knowledge to the needy people in these fields.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Karnataka. It establishes the Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, which has jurisdiction all over the State. It also covers the establishment of new colleges, recognition of institutions, affiliation of colleges, and the functioning of the University and its officers within the State.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council established under section 29.
key_definitions.affiliated_college: A college or institution situated within the University area and affiliated to the University in accordance with the statutes prescribed and providing courses of study for admission to the examination for degrees, diplomas or other academic distinctions of the University.
key_definitions.animal: Includes livestock and all domesticated animals and wild animals, fish, birds, reptiles and all other animal life forms, except the human beings.
key_definitions.board: The Board of Management of the University.
key_definitions.college: Any college or institution established or maintained by, or, affiliated to, the University and providing courses of study and training or providing for prosecution of research or providing extension education. in Veterinary, Animal and Fishery sciences.
key_definitions.constituent_college: The Veterinary College, Bangalore, Veterinary College, Bidar, Dairy Science College, Bangalore, Fishery Science College at Mangalore and any other institution under the direct management of the University and includes such other college notified from time to time by the State Government.
key_definitions.dean: The Head of the Constituent College of the University.
key_definitions.extension_education: Educational activities concerned with the training of livestock farmers, housewives and other groups concerned with animal health or welfare or improved animal husbandry practices and various phases of scientific technology related to animal production and marketing and includes demonstration to carry the new technology and innovation to livestock farms and farm homes through the departments of Animal husbandry, Fisheries and the like.
key_definitions.fishery: The art and science of understanding the biology, commercial exploitation and conservation of aquatic life as well as its surroundings including the constituents of the surroundings.
key_definitions.university: The Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fishery Sciences University established under section 3.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University Act, 2004' and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, Affiliated college, Animal, Board, College, Constituent College, Dean, Extension Education, Fishery, Hostel, Prescribed, Regulations, Statutes, Schedule, Specified date, University, University area, and Veterinary.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University, declaring it a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It specifies the headquarters in Bidar district, jurisdiction over the entire State of Karnataka, and the power to acquire property and enter into contracts. It also states that no immovable property can be transferred without State Government approval and that legal proceedings will be signed by the Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of new colleges and recognition of institutions by the University
main_sections.description: Prohibits the establishment of new colleges in veterinary, animal, and fishery sciences except as constituent or affiliated colleges of the University. It also requires prior approval from the State Government and the concerned University for recognizing institutions affiliated with other Universities.

Outlines the main objectives of the University: to provide education in veterinary, animal, and fishery sciences; to advance learning and research; to extend specialized knowledge to the needy; and any other objects specified by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of the University
main_sections.description: Details the extensive powers and functions of the University, including providing instruction, training, and research; disseminating research findings through extension education; instituting and conferring degrees; holding examinations; conferring honorary degrees; providing lectures and certificates to field workers; cooperating with other institutions; establishing and maintaining colleges and institutions; affiliating and withdrawing affiliation from colleges; establishing and maintaining laboratories, libraries, research stations, etc.; instituting and appointing teaching and administrative posts; instituting scholarships and publishing works; establishing and maintaining hostels and residential accommodation; fixing fees; controlling University unions and student discipline; managing properties; and accepting endowments and donations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, University officers (Registrar for legal proceedings), University itself for academic and administrative matters.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutes and regulations, State Government notifications, inspections, affiliation/disaffiliation processes, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right to establish and maintain colleges and institutions.
Right to affiliate colleges and withdraw affiliation.
Right to institute and confer degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions.
Right to conduct research and disseminate findings.
Right to fix and demand fees.
Right to manage and control its properties and funds.
duties: Duty to provide education, training, and research in veterinary, animal, and fishery sciences.
Duty to advance learning and prosecute research.
Duty to undertake extension of specialized knowledge.
Duty to ensure student health, well-being, and discipline.
Duty to comply with State Government approvals for property transfer and recognition of institutions.

key_procedures: Establishment and incorporation of the University.
Establishment of new colleges and recognition of institutions.
Imparting education, training, and research.
Affiliation and withdrawal of affiliation of colleges.
Making of Statutes and Regulations.
administration: The Karnataka State Legislature (enactment), State Government (notifications, approvals), and the University's own administrative bodies and officers.
important_notes: The University's headquarters shall be located in Bidar district.
The University shall have jurisdiction all over the State of Karnataka.
No new college in veterinary, animal and fishery sciences can be established except as a constituent or affiliated college of the University.
No donation from a foreign country can be accepted without prior approval of the State Government.

title: THE KARNATAKA SECONDARY EDUCATION EXAMINATION BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, to provide for laying of audited reports of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board before each house of the legislature and to empower the State Government to issue directions after perusal of the audited accounts and reports.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, and applies to the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board. The geographical scope is Karnataka.

key_definitions.year: For the purposes of section 25, 'year' means the financial year.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (Amendment) Act, 2006, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 25 of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966. It substitutes sub-section (3) to mandate the Board to prepare and forward an annual audited accounts and report to the State Government within nine months of the year's end, and to lay it before each House of the State Legislature. It also inserts a new sub-section (4) empowering the State Government to issue directions after perusing the audited accounts and report.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Board shall prepare and forward to the State Government, within nine months from the end of the year, an annual audited accounts and report detailing its activities. This report must be laid before each House of the State Legislature.
Rule 2: The State Government may issue directions to the Board after reviewing its audited statement of accounts and report.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of directions after perusal of audited accounts and reports.

rights: The right of the State Legislature to have the Board's annual audited accounts and report laid before it.
The right of the State Government to issue directions to the Board based on audited accounts and reports.
duties: Duty of the Board to prepare and forward an annual audited accounts and report to the State Government within nine months of the year's end.
Duty of the Board to have its annual audited accounts and report laid before each House of the State Legislature.
Duty of the Board to comply with directions issued by the State Government.
obligations: The obligation to amend the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, as specified.
The obligation to adhere to the financial year as the definition of 'year' for reporting purposes.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Board prepares an annual audited accounts and report within nine months of the financial year's end and submits it to the State Government. The State Government then lays this report before each House of the Legislature.
Procedure 2: The State Government peruses the audited accounts and report and may issue directions to the Board based on its findings.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka)
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately upon its enactment.
The 'year' referred to in section 25 is defined as the financial year.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech 2009-10, it is considered necessary to amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. Certain consequential amendments have also been proposed.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, specifically dealing with stamp duties on various instruments and documents related to property, leases, licenses, and other transactions.

key_definitions.lessee: A holder of a lease for a period exceeding thirty years or more, or in perpetuity or does not purport to be for any definite term.
key_definitions.building: A building having more than one apartment or flat or office accommodation or portion of a multi-storied building or both.
key_definitions.money_advanced: In the context of Article 30, it means and includes the security deposit whether refundable or adjustable towards the rent.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2009, and it shall come into force with effect from the first day of April, 2009.
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 45-A of the principal Act by substituting clause (h) and related entries and modifying the wording in clause (i).

This section details various amendments to the Schedule of the Principal Act, including modifications to Articles 5, 11, 20, 22, 28, 30, 32-A, 41, 45, and 48, pertaining to different types of instruments and their corresponding stamp duties.

important_rules: Rule related to lease agreements where possession is not delivered: Stamp duty of 0.25 rupee for every one hundred rupees or part thereof on the market value equal to the amount of consideration.

Rule related to construction or development or sale of an immovable property: Stamp duty of one rupee for every one hundred rupees or part thereof on the market value of the property, or the estimated cost of construction/development, or consideration, whichever is higher.
Rule for Award (Article 11): Same duty as a conveyance on the amount or market value of the property subject to the award, whichever is higher.
Rule for Conveyance (Article 20(1)): Stamp duty reduced to six percent from seven and a half percent.
Rule for Lease of immovable property (Article 30): Different rates are prescribed based on the lease term, with higher rates for longer terms and specific provisions for leases to family members.

Rule for Licence of immovable or moveable property (Article 32-A): Stamp duty rates are prescribed based on the term of the license, varying from one rupee to four rupees for every one hundred rupees of rent/fee/money advanced/security deposit.
key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of Section 45-A of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, involving substitution of specific clauses and entries.

Procedure for amending various Articles in the Schedule of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, which involves substituting existing entries with new rates, definitions, or conditions for stamp duty calculation.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act provides for adjustment of stamp duty already paid on an agreement towards the total duty leviable on a subsequent conveyance or mortgage.
In cases where a proper power of attorney is stamped under Article 5(e) or (f) for an agreement, the duty chargeable under Article 41(f) will be as per Article 41(f).
For leases executed in favour of certain family members, the stamp duty is specifically fixed at rupees one thousand.

The explanation for Article 45(b) clarifies that 'family members' in the context of release deeds extends to include the wife/children of a predeceased brother and the husband/children of a predeceased sister.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, to reduce or remit stamp duty in public interest payable on instruments executed by key projects in special economic zones and by new and existing micro, small, medium enterprises, large scale industrial units, mega projects, including expansion, modernization, or diversification projects, as per the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2009-14.
scope: This act applies to instruments executed in the State of Karnataka. It specifically addresses stamp duty reductions or remissions for Special Economic Zone Developers, Co-Developers, Land Owners, Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board, Financial Institutions, specified new and existing micro, small, medium enterprises, Large Scale Industrial Units, mega projects (including expansion, modernization, or diversification projects), and key projects of core areas, as defined under relevant State policies.

key_definitions.Special Economic Zone Developer, Co-Deve: Defined in the State policy for Special Economic Zones – 2009, vide Government Order No. CI 114 SPI 2007, Bangalore, dated: 28-02-2009.
key_definitions.specified new and existing micro, small,: Specified in Government Order No. CI 233 SPI 2008, Dated: 28-02-2009.
key_definitions.key projects of core area: As defined in the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2009-14 or specified by the State Government from time to time.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2010, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends sub-section (1), clause (a) of Section 9 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, by substituting the second proviso with new provisos that allow the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty in public interest on specified instruments.

important_rules: The State Government may, in public interest, by notification, reduce or remit the stamp duty payable on any instrument to be specified therein, executed by or between Special Economic Zone Developer, Co-Developer, Land Owners, Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board and Financial Institutions as defined in the State policy for Special Economic Zones – 2009.

The State Government may, in public interest, by notification, reduce or remit, till 31st March 2014, the stamp duty payable on any instrument to be specified therein executed by specified new and existing micro, small, medium enterprises, Large Scale Industrial Units and mega projects including expansion or modernization or diversification projects, as defined in the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2009-14, or by such key projects of core area as defined in the said policy or specified by State Government from time to time.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government of Karnataka (through notifications and orders)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through Government Orders and notifications issued by the State Government.

rights: Right of specified entities (SEZ developers, industrial units, etc.) to potentially benefit from reduced or remitted stamp duty.
Right of the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty in public interest.

key_procedures: The State Government issues a notification to reduce or remit stamp duty for specified instruments.
The reduction or remission is applicable to instruments executed by designated entities as per the specified government orders and policies.
The stamp duty reduction/remission for industrial units and mega projects is applicable till March 31, 2014.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the act's enactment), and likely the Department of Industries and Commerce or Revenue Department for the administration of stamp duty and related notifications.
important_notes: The amendment is made in light of the new Industrial Policy 2009-14.
The purpose is to encourage entrepreneurs and combat the global financial crisis.
The stamp duty reduction/remission for certain industrial projects is time-bound, expiring on March 31, 2014.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE PUBLIC RECORDS ACT, 2010
purpose: To regulate the management, administration and preservation of public records of the State Government, State Public Sector Undertakings, Statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the State Government and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Act aims to implement suggestions for maintaining public records, ensure proper maintenance and preservation of government records for administration and research, manage records from various state entities and private sources of historical importance, and constitute a State Archival Advisory Board.
scope: The Act applies to public records of the State Government, State Public Sector Undertakings, Statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the State Government within the State of Karnataka. It also covers records received from private sources that are of historical or national importance.

key_definitions.Board: The State Archival Advisory Board constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of Archives appointed by the State Government, or any officer authorized by the government to perform the duties of the Director.
key_definitions.Head of the Archives: The person in charge of the Archives of the State.
key_definitions.Public records: Includes any document, manuscript, file, microfilm, microfiche, facsimile copy of a document, reproduction of image or images embodied in microfilm, and any other material produced by a computer or any other device of any records creating agency.
key_definitions.records creating agency: Includes any Ministry, Department or office of the State Government, and offices of statutory bodies, corporations, commissions or committees wholly or substantially controlled or financed by the State Government.
key_definitions.Records Officer: An officer nominated by a records creating agency to discharge functions under the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka State Public Records Act, 2010, and mentions that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Director', 'Head of the Archives', 'Public records', 'records creating agency', 'Records Officer', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the State Government to co-ordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with administration, management etc., of public records
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to coordinate, regulate, and supervise all operations related to the administration, management, preservation, selection, disposal, and destruction of public records. It also authorizes the Director of Archives to carry out specific functions related to archival management.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against taking of public records out of the State
main_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of public records from the State without prior approval from the State Government.
Mandates every records creating agency to nominate a Records Officer to discharge functions under the Act and allows for the establishment of record rooms managed by Records Officers.

Outlines the responsibilities of a Records Officer, including arrangement, maintenance, preservation, periodic review, appraisal, destruction, compilation of retention schedules, downgrading of classified records, adoption of standards, compilation of indices and organizational history, assisting the State Archives, submission of reports, and transfer of records from defunct bodies.

main_sections.section_title: Records Officer to take appropriate action in the event of unauthorized removal, destruction etc., of Public Records in his custody
main_sections.description: Requires Records Officers to take immediate action for the recovery or restoration of unauthorizedly removed, destroyed, defaced, or altered public records. They must report such incidents to the Director and can seek assistance from government officers or other persons.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction or disposal of public records
main_sections.description: States that no public record shall be destroyed or disposed of except in a prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions. Records over one hundred years old cannot be destroyed unless they are defaced or unusable for archival purposes.
Specifies penalties for contravening sections 4 or 8, which include imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees, or both.
States that public records with security classification shall not be transferred to the State Archives.

main_sections.section_title: Receipt of records from private sources
main_sections.description: Allows the State Archives to accept records of historical or national importance from private sources through gift, purchase, or otherwise, and to make these records available to bona-fide research scholars under prescribed conditions.

Governs access to public records. Unclassified records over thirty years old, transferred to the State Archives, may be made available to bona-fide research scholars, subject to exceptions. Records creating agencies can also grant access to their records.
Provides for the constitution of an Archival Advisory Board by the State Government, detailing its composition including ex-officio members and nominated members.

Specifies the functions of the Archival Advisory Board, including advising the State Government on public records management, setting guidelines for Archivist training, directing acquisition of records from private custody, and dealing with other prescribed matters.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Director to lay down norms and standards for courses in archival science
main_sections.description: Empowers the Director of Archives to set norms and standards for courses, curricula, assessment, and examinations related to archival science training.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, specifying various matters that such rules may provide for, related to record acceptance, destruction, review, reporting, and access.

important_rules: No public record shall be destroyed or disposed of except in a prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions (Section 8(1)).
Public records bearing security classification shall not be transferred to the State Archives (Section 10).

Unclassified public records, more than thirty years old and transferred to the State Archives, may be made available to bona-fide research scholars, subject to exceptions and restrictions (Section 12(1)).
Records Officers must take immediate action to recover or restore any unauthorizedly removed, destroyed, defaced, or altered public records under their charge (Section 7(1)).

penalties: Contravention of Section 4 or Section 8 of the Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with a fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees or with both (Section 9).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, the Director of Archives, and Records Officers are involved in enforcement. The Director of Archives exercises direction over Records Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the powers vested in the State Government and the Director of Archives to regulate and supervise record management. Records Officers are responsible for implementing provisions related to record handling, preservation, and reporting unauthorized actions. Penalties are prescribed for specific contraventions.

rights: Right to access unclassified public records older than thirty years, subject to exceptions (Section 12(1)).
Right of bona-fide research scholars to access public records under prescribed conditions (Section 11(2) and 12(1)).
Right of records creating agencies to grant permission for access to their public records (Section 12(2)).
duties: Duty of Records Officers to ensure proper arrangement, maintenance, preservation, and review of public records under their charge (Section 6(1)).
Duty to report unauthorized removal, destruction, defacement, or alteration of public records to the Director (Section 7(2)).
Duty to comply with prescribed methods and conditions for destruction or disposal of public records (Section 8(1)).
obligations: Obligation of every records creating agency to nominate a Records Officer (Section 5(1)).
Obligation not to take public records out of the State without prior approval (Section 4).
Obligation to follow the direction of the Director while discharging responsibilities (Section 6(2)).

key_procedures: Nomination of a Records Officer by each records creating agency (Section 5).
Actions by Records Officer upon unauthorized removal, destruction, defacement, or alteration of public records, including reporting to the Director (Section 7).
Procedure for destruction or disposal of public records as prescribed (Section 8).
Process for State Archives to accept records from private sources and make them available to research scholars (Section 11).
Process for granting access to public records to research scholars and other persons (Section 12).
Constitution of the Archival Advisory Board (Section 13).
administration: The administration of the Act primarily involves the State Government, the Director of Archives, and the Archival Advisory Board. The Department of Culture is likely involved through the ex-officio Chairman of the Board.
important_notes: Public records bearing security classification are exempt from transfer to the State Archives (Section 10).
Records over one hundred years old have specific restrictions on destruction (Section 8(2)).
The Act protects actions taken in good faith (Section 16).

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, to provide for deemed exemption for purchase of land for industrial purposes as approved by the State High Level Clearance Committee or the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee, and to permit the sale of exempted lands after seven years of utilization for the permitted purpose to another company or organization for the same purpose.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, specifically concerning provisions related to industrial development, land exemptions, and the sale of exempted lands.

key_definitions.industrial_development: Includes mining of minor minerals (whether specified or non-specified) and stone crushing activity under the Karnataka Regulation of Stone Crushers Act, 2011.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2020, and its deemed commencement date as November 20, 2019.
Amends section 109 of the principal Act to redefine the provisions for industrial development exemptions and the conditions for selling exempted land.

Repeals the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019, and clarifies that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Lands for industrial development are deemed exempted to an extent approved by the Government, with the approval of the State High Level Clearance Committee or the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee constituted under the Karnataka Industries (Facilitation) Act, 2002. This exemption applies to provisions of section 63, 79A, or 80 of the principal Act.

A company or organization that has utilized exempted land for the purpose it was purchased for not less than seven years may, under certain circumstances beyond its control, apply for permission from the Government to sell the land for the same purpose after seven years from the date of purchase.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Karnataka, State High Level Clearance Committee, State Level Single Window Clearance Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, and potentially through rules and regulations issued under the Act.

rights: Right for companies/organizations to seek permission for sale of exempted land after seven years of utilization under specific conditions.
duties: Duty to utilize the purchased land for the specified industrial purpose for at least seven years.
Duty to adhere to the approvals and guidelines set by the State High Level Clearance Committee or State Level Single Window Clearance Committee for land purchase and development.

key_procedures: Application for permission to sell exempted land after seven years of utilization due to reasons beyond control.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka. Enforcement and oversight would likely involve revenue and industrial development departments.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from November 20, 2019, replacing the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019.
The exemption for industrial development is limited to the extent approved by specific committees and for specific purposes.
Sale of exempted land after seven years is permitted only for the same purpose it was originally permitted for and requires Government approval.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicle Taxation Act, 1957, to give effect to amendments made by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highway by defining 'Combined Harvesting' and reducing the tax for Sugar Cane Combine Harvester vehicles from 6% to 3% prospectively.
scope: This act applies to vehicles registered in Karnataka. Specifically, it amends the taxation rates and refund provisions for 'Combined Harvester Vehicles', with a particular focus on 'Sugar Cane Combine Harvester Vehicle'.

key_definitions.Combined Harvesting: Defined in clause (cb) of rule 2 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
key_definitions.Cost of the Vehicle: In relation to a motor vehicle, means: (a) for vehicles manufactured in India, the cost as per the purchase invoice (including excise duty, surcharge, cess, GST, etc., payable in Karnataka, whichever is higher); and (b) for imported vehicles, the total cost incurred in importing the vehicle as assessed under the Customs Act, 1962, including customs duty, freight, and other taxes.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the act and its commencement. It is deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2015, except for a specific part of the schedule which comes into force at once.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (e) to specify that tax shall be levied at the rates specified in Part-A9 of the Schedule for Combined Harvester Vehicles.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by inserting 'Part C6, Part C7 and Part C8' after 'and Part C5'.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by inserting a new 'Part A9' for lifetime tax for Combine Harvester Vehicles and a new 'Part C8' for Refund Table for Combined Harvester Vehicles.

important_rules: Rule 1: The tax for Combine Harvester Vehicle used for Sugar Cane Harvesting only is 3% of the cost of the vehicle from the date of publication of the Act.
Rule 2: The tax for Combine Harvester Vehicle (including Sugar Cane Harvester) is 6% of the cost of the vehicle from April 1, 2015.
Rule 3: Lifetime tax for registered vehicles is a percentage of the tax levied under serial number A, decreasing with the age of the vehicle.
Rule 4: If a vehicle's registration is cancelled or removed, a percentage of the lifetime tax paid is refunded based on the time elapsed since registration, with no refund after 15 years.

rights: Right to pay reduced tax (3%) for Sugar Cane Combine Harvester vehicles.
Right to a refund of lifetime tax paid based on the age of the vehicle if registration is cancelled or removed.
duties: Duty to pay lifetime tax for Combine Harvester Vehicles.
Duty to pay tax at the specified rates based on the class and usage of the vehicle.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the tax rates defined in the Schedule, particularly Part A9 for Combine Harvester Vehicles.
Obligation to comply with the refund provisions outlined in Part C8 for Combined Harvester Vehicles.

key_procedures: Procedure for calculating lifetime tax for new and used Combine Harvester Vehicles, differentiating between sugar cane harvesting and general use.
Procedure for determining the refund amount of lifetime tax when a vehicle's registration is cancelled or removed, based on the vehicle's age.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is responsible for the order and name of the Governor of Karnataka in this act.
important_notes: The act is deemed to have come into force with effect from April 1, 2015, for most provisions.
The definition of 'Combined Harvester Vehicle' is based on rule 2(cb) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
The 'Cost of the Vehicle' definition includes various components of cost for both Indian manufactured and imported vehicles.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the agricultural produce marketing regulation within the state of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) (Second Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 65 of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act may be called the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) (Second Amendment) Act, 2001.
Rule 2: The Act shall come into force at once.

Rule 3: Section 65 of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, shall be amended. This amendment pertains to the marketing of agricultural produce and specifies that no market fee shall be levied and collected again in respect of any agricultural produce on which such market fee has already been levied and collected in the State during such crop season.
Rule 4: Similar market fee shall not be levied and collected in respect of any agricultural produce as may be specified by the State Government by notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Karnataka is responsible for implementing and enforcing this Act, including issuing notifications and specifying agricultural produce for exemptions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing acts and government notifications specifying exemptions from market fee collection.

rights: Producers have the right to not have market fees levied and collected again on the same agricultural produce within a crop season.
duties: The State Government has the duty to notify exemptions for agricultural produce to prevent double taxation of market fees.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government may issue notifications to specify agricultural produce for which market fees will not be levied and collected again.
Procedure 2: Amendments to Section 65 of the principal Act are enacted to implement the provisions of this Act.
administration: State Government of Karnataka
important_notes: Note 1: The act aims to prevent double levying and collection of market fees on the same agricultural produce within a crop season.
Note 2: The State Government has the power to exempt certain agricultural produce from this rule through notification.

title: THE KARNATAKA DETERMINATION OF SENIORITY OF THE GOVERNMENT SERVANTS PROMOTED ON THE BASIS OF RESERVATION (TO THE POSTS IN THE CIVIL SERVICES OF THE STATE) ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for the determination of seniority of Government servants promoted on the basis of reservation to posts in the civil services of the State.
scope: The Act applies to the Government servants of the State of Karnataka who are promoted on the basis of reservation.

main_sections.description: This section likely deals with the name of the Act and when it comes into effect.
This section will define key terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of Seniority of Government Servants Promoted on the basis of Reservation
main_sections.description: This is the core section of the Act, outlining how seniority will be determined for those promoted based on reservation.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of consequential seniority already accorded
main_sections.description: This section likely addresses the protection of seniority that has already been granted.
This section grants the government the authority to create rules for implementing the Act.
This section likely empowers the government to resolve any issues or difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the Act.
This section deals with the repeal of any previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule 2(c), Rule 4, and Rule 4A of the Karnataka Government Servants (Seniority) Rules, 1997 (as amended) have been examined. It has been observed that there is no specific rule therein prescribing the manner of determination of inter-se seniority among persons promoted on the basis of reservation.
The Act aims to provide a clear method for determining seniority of promoted Government servants, specifically addressing the basis of reservation.
The Act aims to resolve ambiguities and ensure that the Government's policy of reservation in promotions is implemented in accordance with the determined seniority.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the Act and any rules made thereunder, and by ensuring that promotions are made in accordance with the determined seniority.

rights: Right to have seniority determined in accordance with the provisions of this Act for Government servants promoted on the basis of reservation.
duties: Duty of the Government to ensure that promotions are made in accordance with the policy of reservation and the seniority determined under this Act.
Duty of the Government to ensure that seniority is determined consistently with the principles laid down in the Act.
obligations: Obligation to follow the seniority determination method prescribed by the Act.
Obligation to adhere to the policy of reservation in promotions.

key_procedures: Determination of seniority for Government servants promoted on the basis of reservation as per the Act.
The Act likely implies a procedure for reviewing and correcting any existing seniority lists that do not comply with its provisions.
administration: The Karnataka Government
important_notes: The Act was enacted due to the absence of specific rules for determining seniority for promotions based on reservation in existing Karnataka Government Servants (Seniority) Rules.
The Act aims to ensure that seniority is determined in accordance with the reservation policy, thereby clarifying the positions of promoted Government servants.
The Act aims to remove any ambiguity and ensure that Government servants are placed in the correct seniority order based on the policy of reservation.

title: KARNATAKA COURT FEES AND SUITS VALUATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1958, to dispense with the use of stamps and stamp papers and to start using impressed stamps, in order to give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech for the year 2002-2003.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1958, and applies to all matters governed by that principal Act within the state of Karnataka. It specifically affects the collection of court fees and the valuation of suits.

main_sections.description: This section names the act as the Karnataka Court Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 2003, and states that it comes into force on April 1, 2003.
This section omits sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 43 of the principal Act.

This section amends sub-sections (1), (3), and (4) of section 58 of the principal Act, replacing phrases related to 'cause the probate or letters to be duly stamped' with 'cause the deficit fee to be recovered'.

This section amends section 59 of the principal Act by omitting the words 'before letters stamped' from the heading and substituting the phrase 'shall require the administrator to give such security to the court' for the original wording regarding the administrator giving security.
This section amends sub-section (2) of section 60 of the principal Act, substituting the wording related to a refund of excess court fees and endorsement of a certificate.

This section substitutes the existing section 71 with a new section outlining the methods for collecting fees: in cash for amounts not exceeding five hundred rupees, and through the Government Treasury or Demand Draft for amounts exceeding five hundred rupees.
This section omits section 72 of the principal Act.

This section substitutes section 73 of the principal Act with a new section stating that no fresh fee is necessary for amended documents that merely correct a mistake to conform to the original intention of the parties.
This section omits sections 74, 75, and 76 of the principal Act.
This section omits clauses (e) to (j) from sub-section (2) of section 78 of the principal Act.

This section provides that notwithstanding the amendments, the provisions of the principal Act as they were in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall continue to apply to stamps used or proceedings pending on the date of commencement.
This section empowers the State Government to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of this Act by notification.

important_rules: Rule 1: Court fees exceeding five hundred rupees must be paid either in the Government Treasury or through a Demand Draft.
Rule 2: For amendments to documents solely to correct mistakes and align with the original intent of the parties, a fresh fee will not be imposed.
Rule 3: Deficit court fees related to probates or letters of administration will be recovered, rather than requiring the documents to be duly stamped.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and relevant court authorities implicitly enforce this act through the procedures outlined in the principal Act and its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the established judicial and administrative processes for fee collection and the administration of justice as governed by the principal Act and its amendments.

duties: Duty to pay court fees as prescribed by the Karnataka Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1958, as amended.
Duty to comply with security requirements for administrators as stipulated in amended section 59.
Duty to follow the prescribed methods of fee payment as per amended section 71.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Payment of court fees exceeding five hundred rupees must be made via Government Treasury or Demand Draft.
Procedure 2: When a document is amended to correct a mistake and conform to the original intention, no fresh fee is required.
Procedure 3: Recovery of deficit court fees will be the method employed instead of requiring the stamping of probates or letters of administration.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka), and the State Government for removal of difficulties.
important_notes: The Act specifies that any difficulties in its implementation can be resolved by the State Government through notification.
Transitional provisions ensure that the pre-amendment rules regarding stamps and proceedings continue to apply for a certain period or for pending cases.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, for the purpose of bifurcating Bangalore University and establishing a separate Tumkur University to reduce workload and promote student convenience.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, specifically focusing on the establishment and functioning of Tumkur University and its territorial jurisdiction over the districts of Tumkur, Kolar, and Bangalore Rural (excluding Kanakapura and Hoskote Taluks). It also addresses the transition of affiliated colleges and students from Bangalore University to Tumkur University.

main_sections.description: States that the act may be called the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2004, and it shall come into force on a date notified by the State Government.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act to redefine the territorial jurisdiction of Bangalore Rural District and to establish Tumkur University with headquarters at Tumkur, covering Tumkur, Kolar, and Bangalore Rural Districts (excluding Kanakapura and Hoskote Taluks).

Inserts a new sub-section (3) into Section 5 of the principal Act. This provision states that privileges enjoyed by colleges in Kolar, Tumkur, and Bangalore Rural districts from Bangalore University shall be deemed withdrawn, and these institutions shall be deemed affiliated to Tumkur University.
Inserts a new proviso into sub-section (4) of Section 14 of the principal Act, stating that the first Vice Chancellor of Tumkur University shall be appointed by the State Government.
Defines the powers and functions of a Special Officer appointed by the State Government to establish Tumkur University, exercisable until the first Vice Chancellor is appointed.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of the first vice chancellor
main_sections.description: Outlines the duties of the first Vice Chancellor of Tumkur University, including making arrangements for the constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities within six months (or an extended period) of the Act's commencement.

Deals with transitional arrangements, allowing the first Vice Chancellor to discharge University functions and deeming statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules of Bangalore University applicable to Tumkur University's affiliated colleges until Tumkur University makes its own.

Provides for savings related to examinations, allowing students studying for Bangalore University degrees to continue their examinations with Bangalore University until Tumkur University makes its provisions. It also clarifies how results and degrees will be handled.
