Empowers the State Government to make orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Amendment Act, within two years of its commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and appointed authorities (e.g., Vice Chancellor, Special Officer, University authorities)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and the principal Act, including the establishment of university authorities, appointment of officials, and making necessary orders by the State Government.

rights: Colleges and educational institutions in the specified districts have the right to be affiliated with Tumkur University.
Students studying for degrees in the specified districts have the right to complete their examinations and receive degrees/diplomas.
duties: The first Vice Chancellor has the duty to constitute university authorities.
The State Government has the duty to notify commencement dates, appoint officials, and remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Notification of commencement date by the State Government.
Appointment of the first Vice Chancellor by the State Government.
Constitution of Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities by the first Vice Chancellor.
Transfer of affiliation of colleges from Bangalore University to Tumkur University.
Handling of ongoing examinations and conferment of degrees/diplomas.
Removal of difficulties by the State Government through orders.
administration: Department of Higher Education, Government of Karnataka (implied, as it deals with universities). The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is mentioned for publishing the act.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st October 2004, vide Notification No. ED 308 URC 2004.
The establishment of Tumkur University aims to reduce the workload of Bangalore University and improve student convenience.
The State Government has the power to remove difficulties within two years of the Act's commencement.
Existing statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules of Bangalore University are temporarily applicable to Tumkur University's affiliated colleges.

title: THE KAGINELE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 2009
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an Authority for development and maintenance of the heritage sites in and around Kaginele and Bada villages in Haveri district into international pilgrim, cultural and tourist centers.
scope: The Act extends to the area of Kaginele and Bada villages as defined in clause (c) of section 2. Kaginele means and includes the limits of Kaginele and Bada villages, lands acquired by the Government for development of heritage sites at Kaginele and Bada, and any other area declared by the State Government. It also applies to heritage sites as specified in the Schedule, excluding areas protected under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958.

key_definitions.amenity: Includes roads, streets, sub-ways, lighting, drainage, sanitation, electricity and water supply or other conveniences, public works, market places, post offices, banks, hospitals, dispensaries, police stations, fair price shops, milk booths, libraries, recreation centers, service stations of any public utility service authorized by the Authority or other facility; and such other amenity as the State Government may, by notification, specify.
key_definitions.authority: The Kaginele Development Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.kaginele: Means and includes the limits of Kaginele and Bada villages and lands acquired by Government from time to time for development of heritage sites at Kaginele and Bada and such other area declared by the State Government, by notification.
key_definitions.chairperson: Means the Chairman of the Authority.
key_definitions.commissioner: Means the Commissioner of the Authority appointed under section 10.
key_definitions.fund: Means the fund of the Authority.
key_definitions.heritage_site: Means the whole of the area comprising the sites specified in the Schedule but excluding the area referred to as protected area under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958 (Central Act 24 of 1958).
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Authority.
key_definitions.regulations: Means regulations of the Authority made under section 46.
key_definitions.schedule: Means the Schedule appended to this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kaginele Development Authority Act, 2009. Defines its territorial extent to Kaginele and Bada villages. It is deemed to have come into force from June 30, 2005.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Amenity', 'Authority', 'Kaginele', 'Chair-person', 'Commissioner', 'Fund', 'Heritage Site', 'Member', 'Regulations', and 'Schedule'.

Provides for the constitution of the Kaginele Development Authority. Specifies its headquarters, corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, and power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and enter into contracts. Lists the members of the Authority, including ex-officio members (Chief Minister, Ministers, local representatives, secretaries of various departments, district officials, directors of relevant departments) and nominated members.

Grants the Authority general power to do anything necessary to give effect to the Act's intent. Specifically includes powers to enter into contracts (with State Government sanction for expenditures over five lakhs), borrow funds (with State Government sanction), and lease, sell, or transfer property, subject to certain conditions and prior approval of the State Government for development schemes.

Establishes the fund for the Authority.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations.
Deals with the repeal of previous provisions and savings.

important_rules: Contracts involving expenditure of rupees five lakhs and more require previous sanction of the State Government (Section 8(2)(a)).
Borrowing sums for the Act's purposes requires previous sanction of the State Government and adherence to prescribed conditions (Section 8(2)(b)).
Leasing, selling, or transferring movable or immovable property and appropriating or applying land for development schemes requires prior approval of the State Government (Section 8(2)(c)).
Non-official members nominated by the State Government hold office for three years, subject to the State Government's pleasure (Section 4(1)).

A member can be disqualified for several reasons including conviction for an offense involving moral turpitude, being of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, prior dismissal from government service, or having an interest in contracts with the Authority (Section 5).
The State Government shall remove a member if they become subject to disqualifications, refuse to act, are incapable of acting, or absent from three consecutive meetings without leave (Section 6).

The Commissioner, appointed by the State Government, is the Chief Executive and Administrative Officer of the Authority and is responsible for carrying out resolutions, conducting business, executing schemes, managing accounts, and supervising staff (Section 11).

penalties: Section 40: Default in performance of duty. This section likely outlines penalties for failure to perform duties under the Act, though specific details are not provided in the extracted text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kaginele Development Authority, with oversight and direction from the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the powers vested in the Authority, including its power of entry (Section 24), its role as the Development Authority and Grama Panchayat (Section 22), and the State Government's power of control and to give directions (Sections 42, 43).

rights: The Authority has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 3(3)).
The Authority has the right to enter into contracts (Section 8(2)(a)).
The Authority has the right to borrow funds (Section 8(2)(b)).
The Authority has the right to lease, sell, or transfer property (Section 8(2)(c)).
The Authority has the power of entry (Section 24).
duties: The Authority has a duty to develop and maintain heritage sites in and around Kaginele and Bada villages (Preamble, Section 20, 21).
The Authority is responsible for carrying out the resolutions of the Authority (Section 11(2)(a)).
The Commissioner is responsible for implementing schemes of the Authority (Section 11(2)(d)).
The Authority has a duty to maintain streets, etc. (Section 27).
obligations: No other authority or person is to undertake development without permission of the Authority (Section 23).

The Authority must obtain prior approval of the State Government for certain actions like making contracts over five lakhs and for development schemes involving land appropriation or transfer (Section 8(2)(a), 8(2)(c)).
The Authority must adhere to conditions and limitations prescribed by the State Government for property transactions and development schemes (Section 8(2)(c)).

key_procedures: Appointment of the Kaginele Development Authority (Section 3).
Appointment of the Commissioner by the State Government (Section 10).
Preparation, approval, and execution of development plans (Section 20).
Preparation of the Authority's budget (Section 34).
Conducting accounts and audit of the Authority's finances (Section 35).
Making rules by the State Government (Section 45).
Making regulations by the Authority (Section 46).
administration: The Kaginele Development Authority, with ultimate control and direction from the State Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from June 30, 2005 (Section 1(3)).
The Authority shall not sell any land within its jurisdiction (Section 37).
Certain persons defined in the Act are to be considered public servants (Section 38).
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Section 39).
The State Government has the power to control the Authority and give directions (Sections 42, 43).
The Schedule appended to the Act specifies the heritage sites, and the Authority has the power to amend this Schedule (Section 19).

title: THE UNIVERSITIES OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES ACT, 2009
purpose: To replace the present enactment relating to Universities of Agricultural Sciences by a comprehensive enactment to consolidate and amend the law relating to Universities of Agricultural Sciences for providing development of Agriculture and allied Sciences in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment, incorporation, jurisdiction, objectives, authorities, officers, education, research, extension, funds, accounts, affiliation, recognition, statutes, regulations, and miscellaneous provisions related to Universities of Agricultural Sciences in the State of Karnataka. It specifically establishes the Universities of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore, Dharwad, and Raichur, with defined territorial jurisdictions.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.Affiliated college: A college or institution within the University jurisdiction and affiliated to the University in accordance with the statutes prescribed and providing courses of study for admission to the examination for Degrees, Diplomas or other academic distinctions of the University.
key_definitions.Agriculture: Includes basic and applied sciences such as Natural Resource Management, Soil and Water Management, Crop Improvement, Horticulture, Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Dairy Science and Technology, Psiciculture and Fisheries Management, Forestry, Agricultural Engineering and Technology, Food Science and Technology, Agricultural Marketing and cooperation, Agri. Business management, Basic Sciences and Humanities related to Agriculture, Agricultural Biotechnology, Post-harvest Technology, Land Use Planning and Management, Sericulture, Apiculture, Home Science, Agricultural Technology and Rural Development, Agricultural Economics, and any other subject related to agriculture.
key_definitions.University: An Agricultural University established under section 3.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Universities of Agricultural Sciences Act, 2009, and that it is deemed to have come into force from 22nd November 2008.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, Affiliated college, Agriculture, University, Vice-Chancellor, and many others.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and Incorporation of the Universities
main_sections.description: Deems the Universities of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore and Dharwad (established under the 1963 Act) to be established under this Act with their territorial jurisdictions. It also establishes the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, with specific territorial jurisdiction, superseding Dharwad's jurisdiction over that area. It outlines the corporate nature of the Universities, their perpetual succession, common seal, power to sue and be sued, and ability to acquire property and enter into contracts.

Defines the responsibility of each University for maintenance of training/educational centers and research stations in Agriculture, Husbandry, Fishery, Sericulture, and Forestry. It also states that all colleges, research stations, KVKs, and Extension Education and Training centers under the University's management or jurisdiction are constituent units.

important_rules: Each University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal, and may sue and be sued by its name.

The University shall be competent to acquire and hold both movable and immovable property and to borrow money from the Central Government, State Government or any other approved sources and to enter into any contract and to do all other things necessary for the purpose of this Act.
The University shall not lease, sell or otherwise transfer any immovable property which may have become vested in it or been acquired by it without obtaining prior approval of the Government.

In all suits and other legal proceedings by or against the University, the pleading shall be signed and verified by the Registrar and all processes in such suits and proceedings shall be issued to and served on, the Registrar of the University.

Each University shall be responsible for the maintenance of Agriculture, Husbandry, Fishery, Sericulture and Forestry Training or Educational Centres and Research and experimental stations, and for the programme of training of field extension workers and for the establishment, development and operation of such centers as may be required in various parts within its territorial jurisdiction.

All colleges, research and experimental stations, KVKs and Extension Education and other Training centres under the management of the University or other institutions, which are under the jurisdiction and authority of each University, shall be constituent units of that University and under the management and control of the University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act provides for the establishment and governance of Universities, implying administrative oversight by State authorities and the governing bodies of the Universities themselves.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would occur through the powers vested in the Universities' authorities, the State Government's oversight powers (e.g., power to issue directions, order auditing), and legal proceedings as outlined in the Act.

rights: The Universities have the right to acquire and hold property, borrow money, and enter into contracts.

The Universities have a duty to implement programmes for training field extension workers.
The Universities have a duty to manage and control their constituent units.
The Universities have a duty to obtain prior approval of the Government before leasing, selling, or transferring immovable property.
obligations: The Universities are obligated to operate within their defined territorial jurisdictions.
The Universities are obligated to adhere to statutes and regulations governing their functioning.
The Universities are obligated to ensure that students admitted are for pursuing courses of study for degrees, diplomas or other academic distinctions duly instituted.

Procedures for affiliation of colleges and recognition of institutions.

Procedures for legal proceedings involving the University.

The establishment of the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, is a significant new provision.
The Act allows for the reception of donations and admission of institutions functioning outside India to University privileges.
The Act incorporates provisions for nomination of eminent educationists/scientists by the Chancellor and representation for Agro-Industrialists on the Board of Management.
The term of nominated members on authorities is limited to a maximum of three years and they are not eligible for re-nomination for more than one term.
Separate Boards of Studies for Undergraduate and Postgraduate studies are introduced.
Research Council and Extension Council have been reorganized with wider representation.
The term of office of the Vice-Chancellor is for a period of four years.
A State Co-ordination Committee for Agricultural Education and Research is established.
The Act allows for the establishment of private colleges and their affiliation.
The Act is a comprehensive legislation replacing previous enactments and ordinances.

title: THE HAMPI WORLD HERITAGE AREA MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority Act, 2002, to substitute the words 'State Level Committee' for 'State Level Advisory Committee' and to revise the composition of the committee, with the Chief Minister as Chairperson and the Minister in charge of Bellary District as Vice-chairperson.
scope: This act amends the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority Act, 2002, which pertains to the management of the Hampi World Heritage Area in Karnataka.

key_definitions.State Level Committee: The committee constituted under section 6 of the principal Act, as amended.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority (Amendment) Act, 2011, and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by omitting clause (a) and inserting a new clause (r) defining 'State Level Committee'.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the heading 'State Level Advisory Committee' with 'State Level Committee'. It also revises sub-section (1) to change the Chairperson to the Chief Minister, the Vice Chairperson to the Minister in charge of Bellary District, and includes the Minister in charge of Kannada and Culture as a Member. Further, it substitutes 'Advisory Committee' with 'State Level Committee' in sub-sections (2), (3), (4), and (5).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority, as established by the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and powers vested in the Authority by the principal Act and its amendments.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2: Insertion of definition for 'State Level Committee' and omission of existing clause (a).

Amendment of Section 6: Substitution of 'State Level Advisory Committee' with 'State Level Committee', and restructuring of the committee's composition to include the Chief Minister as Chairperson and the Minister in charge of Bellary District as Vice Chairperson.
administration: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority, with its governing structure as amended by this Act.
important_notes: The amendment aims to streamline the governance of the Hampi World Heritage Area by updating the committee's nomenclature and leadership.
The act is enacted based on Entries 5 and 32 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 to provide voters with the option of 'None of the Above' (NOTA) on ballot papers and electronic voting machines.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends two existing state acts: the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. The subject matter scope is limited to electoral procedures within municipalities and municipal corporations, specifically regarding the casting of votes.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2020' and specifies that it comes into force immediately upon enactment.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 22 of 1964
main_sections.description: Amends Section 38 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, by inserting a new sub-clause (vi-b) under sub-section (2) and clause (j). This new sub-clause provides for the manner of casting a vote in favour of 'None of the Above' (NOTA) candidates when a voter does not wish to vote for any particular candidate.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 14 of 1977
main_sections.description: Amends Section 55 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, by inserting a new sub-clause (vi-b) under sub-section (2) and clause (h). This new sub-clause similarly provides for the manner of casting a vote in favour of 'None of the Above' (NOTA) candidates when a voter chooses not to vote for any candidate.

important_rules: Rule 1: Voters in Karnataka Municipalities and Municipal Corporations elections have the option to vote for 'None of the Above' (NOTA) if they do not wish to support any contesting candidate.
Rule 2: The manner of casting a NOTA vote will be prescribed within the respective amended sections of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The authorities responsible for enforcing the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, would be responsible for ensuring compliance with these amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would involve the implementation of the amended electoral procedures by election officials and bodies responsible for conducting municipal and municipal corporation elections in Karnataka, including the proper functioning of ballot papers and electronic voting machines to accommodate the NOTA option.

rights: The right of a qualified voter to abstain from voting for any candidate by choosing the NOTA option.
The right of voters to have their choice of not supporting any candidate registered through the NOTA option.
duties: The duty of election authorities to ensure the NOTA option is available and functional on ballot papers and EVMs.
The duty of qualified voters to cast their vote in accordance with the established procedures, including the option to use NOTA.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Voters are presented with the option of 'None of the Above' (NOTA) on the ballot paper or electronic voting machine.
Procedure 2: If a voter does not wish to vote for any of the contesting candidates, they can select the NOTA option.

Procedure 3: The casting of the NOTA vote is to be done in a manner prescribed by the respective amendments to the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is involved in the legislative process. The administration of the amended acts would fall under the respective municipal administration departments and election commissions responsible for local body elections in Karnataka.
important_notes: This amendment specifically addresses electoral procedures and does not introduce new substantive laws regarding municipal governance.
The Act came into force at once upon its publication, meaning the NOTA option was immediately available for relevant elections.

title: THE UNIVERSITY OF HORTICULTURAL SCIENCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the University of Horticulture Sciences Act, 2009 to reduce the number of members of the Board of Management of the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalakote as per the directions of the Indian Council of Agriculture Research.
scope: This act amends the University of Horticultural Sciences Act, 2009 (Karnataka Act 11 of 2010). It specifically pertains to the composition of the Board of Management of the University of Horticultural Sciences, Bagalakote.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the University of Horticultural Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2020. (2) It shall come into force at once.
Amends section 12 of the University of Horticultural Sciences Act, 2009 (Karnataka Act 11 of 2010) by substituting sub-section (2) to redefine the composition of the Board of Management.

important_rules: The Board of Management shall consist of specific members including the Vice-Chancellor, representatives from government departments (Horticulture, Finance, Agriculture), an eminent educationist, representatives from the State Legislative Assembly and Council, a women social worker, a progressive farmer, an agriculture entrepreneur, a representative from ICAR, a Director nominated by the Vice-Chancellor, a Dean nominated by the Vice-Chancellor, and the Registrar who shall be the Member Secretary.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University of Horticultural Sciences, Bagalakote and relevant government departments as implied by the composition of the Board of Management.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendment of the existing University of Horticultural Sciences Act, 2009, specifically concerning the composition of its Board of Management.

rights: The right to have a Board of Management constituted as per the amended provisions.
duties: The duty to constitute the Board of Management with the specified members.
The duty to ensure the Board functions effectively for the management of the University.

key_procedures: Nomination of members to the Board of Management by the Chancellor, State Government, Director General of ICAR, and the Vice-Chancellor as per the specified criteria.
administration: University of Horticultural Sciences, Bagalakote; Department of Horticulture; Finance Department; Department of Agriculture; Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation.
important_notes: The amendment is based on directions from the Indian Council of Agriculture Research.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on 08.03.2021 and received the assent of the Governor on 05.03.2021.
The Act is enacted under Entry 14 of List II and Entry 25 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2001
purpose: This act serves to further amend the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, with the objective of bringing into force provisions related to information technology, biotechnology, and research centres, thereby enabling flexible working hours and extending services or establishments, especially those related to information technology and biotechnology and research centres.
scope: The act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically targets Information Technology, Biotechnology, and research establishments, allowing for flexible working hours and the establishment of related services.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2001. It also specifies that it comes into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint. The notification dates for commencement are given as 1st April, 2001.

This section details the amendment to Section 3 of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961. It introduces new clauses to allow for flexibility in working hours and the establishment of services or establishments, specifically mentioning Information Technology, Biotechnology, and research centres.

This section pertains to the amendment of Section 11 of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961. It appears to involve the insertion of new clauses (p) and (s) and the amendment of clause (q) under sub-section (2) of Section 11, which likely relates to the establishment of Information Technology, Biotechnology, and research centres.

important_rules: The Act aims to provide flexible working hours for establishments in the Information Technology, Biotechnology, and research sectors.
Establishments in these specified sectors are allowed to operate outside of traditional working hours.
The Act facilitates the establishment of related services and operations within these sectors.
The amendment clarifies that the State Government may notify specific dates for the commencement of these provisions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is responsible for appointing the commencement date of the act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The act is enforced through amendments to existing legislation (Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961) and government notifications.

rights: Establishments in IT, Biotech, and research sectors have the right to implement flexible working hours.
These establishments have the right to establish related services and operations.
duties: Duty to comply with the amended provisions of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.

key_procedures: The State Government may issue notifications to bring specific sections or the entire act into force on a designated date.
Amendments are made to Section 3 and Section 11 of the principal Act to accommodate the new provisions.
administration: The Act amends the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, implying that the administrative responsibility would fall under the department that oversees labour and commercial establishments in Karnataka.
important_notes: The act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on April 1st, 2001.
The act's commencement date was notified as April 1st, 2001.
The act references amendments to the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, Act No. 8 of 1961.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To give effect to budget proposals and rationalize certain provisions of various taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka by amending specific sections of those acts.
scope: This Act amends several taxation laws applicable within the State of Karnataka, specifically targeting amendments to the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932, the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979, and the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (implicitly through references in amendments). The amendments cover various aspects of taxation including tax rates, penalties, time limits for assessments, and specific tax levies.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it came into force on April 1, 2005.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Mysore Act IX of 1932
main_sections.description: Amends the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932, by inserting a proviso to Section 3-A regarding liability to pay composition amounts for a specific period.

Amends the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, by modifying tax rates in Sections 12-B, 13, and 18-AA, inserting an explanation for 'default' in Section 18-AA, extending time limits in Section 23, and adding a new entry to the Fifth Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Act No.30 of 1958
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, by exempting circus admissions from tax, reducing tax rates for various categories, modifying penalty provisions in Section 6-A, and amending interest provisions in Section 9.

Amends the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, by inserting a proviso to Section 10 regarding deemed enrollment, amending tax rates in Section 11, and revising the tax structure for legal practitioners in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Act No.27 of 1979
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979, by inserting definitions, modifying tax rates and inserting an explanation for 'default' in Section 3-BB, making cross-references to the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, and introducing new sections (4-B and 4-BB) for levy and reduction of tax on motor vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Act No.4 of 2004
main_sections.description: Not detailed in the provided text snippet, but likely amends the Karnataka Tax on Lotteries Act, 2004.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Act No.29 of 2004
main_sections.description: Not detailed in the provided text snippet, but likely amends the Karnataka Special Tax on Entry of Certain Goods Act, 2004.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Act No.32 of 2004
main_sections.description: Not detailed in the provided text snippet, but likely amends the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (which is often referred to as 2003, but the amendment act is from 2004, suggesting a potential numbering or enactment date discrepancy in the provided text or common reference).
Provides for the validation of past assessments, penalties, or actions taken under the amended laws.

important_rules: Licensees under the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932, are liable to pay composition amounts only until the commencement of the Karnataka Taxation Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 2004.

Non-payment of tax during periods when recovery is stayed by an order of an authority or court in an appeal or proceeding disputing the amount is deemed a 'default', unless the appeal or proceeding is allowed.
Tax rates for various categories under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, have been reduced.
Circus admissions are exempt from entertainment tax.

Penalties for non-payment of tax due to willful mis-statement or suppression of facts under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, are defined, with higher penalties for subsequent offenses in the same financial year.
Interest on unpaid tax under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, is set at one and a quarter percent per month.
Legal practitioners' tax liability under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, has been revised based on their standing in the profession and location.

penalties: For wilful mis-statement or suppression of facts leading to incorrect tax payment under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958: equal to the difference between assessed tax and paid tax for the first instance in a financial year, and double the difference for subsequent instances in the same financial year.
Interest on unpaid tax under the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, at 1.25% per month.

rights: Right to appeal or dispute tax amounts, with non-payment during stay of recovery not being considered a default.
Reduction of tax liability under the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979, to the extent of tax already paid under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, or the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003.
duties: Liabilities of licensees to pay composition amounts under the Mysore Betting Tax Act, 1932.
Duty to pay the correct amount of tax under the various amended Acts.
Duty to pay interest on unpaid tax.
Duty of proprietors to pay penalties in case of wilful mis-statement or suppression of facts.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on the purchase value of motor vehicles entering a local area under the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.
Obligation for legal practitioners to pay profession tax according to revised rates.

key_procedures: Amendments to tax rates and levies in specific sections of various Acts.
Insertion of explanations for 'default' in tax payment under certain circumstances.
Extension of time limits for assessments.
Introduction of a new tax levy on motor vehicles entering local areas.

title: THE MYSORE (RELIGIOUS AND CHARITABLE) INAMS ABOLITION (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the review by the State Government of the order of basic annual sum (Tasdic amount) determined by the Divisional Commissioner under section 21A of the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition Act, 1955, prior to the commencement of the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2005. The amendment allows the Government to revise the basic annual sum if it was incorrectly determined, provides for an opportunity to be heard for the affected person, and specifies the recovery mechanism for excess amounts paid.
scope: This act amends the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition Act, 1955. It applies to orders concerning the basic annual sum (Tasdic amount) determined by the Divisional Commissioner under section 21A of the Principal Act, specifically those determined prior to the commencement of the Karnataka Amendment Act, 2005. The geographical and subject matter scope is within Karnataka, pertaining to religious and charitable inams.

key_definitions.basic_annual_sum: Also referred to as 'Tasdic amount', this is the sum determined by the Divisional Commissioner under section 21A of the Principal Act.
key_definitions.Divisional_Commissioner: An authority empowered to determine the basic annual sum under section 21A of the Principal Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it shall come into force at once.
This section inserts a new section, 21B, into the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition Act, 1955, which deals with the review of basic annual sums.

important_rules: The State Government may review the basic annual sum determined by the Divisional Commissioner if it was incorrectly or erroneously determined, or requires revision due to new information, mistakes, or for any other sufficient reason.
Before passing an order on the review, the person or persons affected must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
If an excess amount has been paid, it shall be adjusted in the subsequent basic annual sum to be paid.
If the excess amount cannot be adjusted, it shall be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

penalties: If any excess amount of basic annual sum has been paid and cannot be adjusted in subsequent payments, it will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and potentially other relevant revenue authorities for the recovery of arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through a review process initiated by the State Government and the subsequent recovery of excess payments as arrears of land revenue.

rights: The right of an aggrieved party to apply for a review of the basic annual sum determined by the Divisional Commissioner.
The right of affected persons to be heard before any order is passed on the review.
duties: Duty of the State Government to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to affected persons before passing a review order.
Duty to adjust excess payments in subsequent basic annual sums.
Duty to recover unadjusted excess amounts as arrears of land revenue.
obligations: Obligation on the State Government to review basic annual sums when necessary.
Obligation on the State Government to ensure correct determination of basic annual sums.

key_procedures: Review by the State Government: The State Government can initiate a review of the basic annual sum on its own motion or upon application by an aggrieved party.
Opportunity to be heard: The affected party must be given a reasonable opportunity to present their case before any review order is passed.

Adjustment or recovery of excess payments: If an excess amount has been paid, it will first be adjusted in future payments. If adjustment is not possible, it will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory of the Act). The administration of the basic annual sum and its review would likely involve revenue departments and divisional commissioners.
important_notes: This amendment specifically targets basic annual sums determined prior to the commencement of the 2005 Amendment Act.
The amendment provides for both increasing or decreasing the basic annual sum during review.
The recovery of excess amounts is a significant enforcement mechanism.

title: The University of Horticultural Sciences Act, 2009
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a separate University for Horticulture in the State of Karnataka, to impart instructions, training and research in Horticulture and allied Sciences, to confer degrees, diplomas, certificates and other academic distinctions, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka with respect to teaching at the University or college level, research, and extension education programmes in the field of horticulture. It covers the establishment and incorporation of the University, its authorities, officers, funds, affiliation of colleges, and miscellaneous provisions.

key_definitions.University: University of Horticultural Sciences established under section 3.
key_definitions.Horticulture: Includes basic and applied sciences related to vegetables, fruits, flowers, spices, plantation crops, medicinal and aromatic crops, agricultural crops, natural resource management, soil and water management, crop improvement, irrigation and weed management, production of seed and plant material, land use planning and management, landscaping, horti-silviculture, farm-forestry and forest and wildlife management, economics, marketing, cooperation and business management, food science and technology, post harvest management, bio-technology, mushroom culture, engineering, veterinary and animal sciences, dairy science and technology, pisciculture and fisheries management, rural development, basic sciences and humanities, apiculture, and any other subject related to Horticulture as suggested by the Government/ICAR.
key_definitions.Extension Education: Educational activities concerned with the training of farmers, home makers, entrepreneurs and other groups concerned with horticulture and allied sciences and various phases of scientific technology related to horticultural production and marketing, including demonstration to carry forward new technology and innovation to farms and farm homes through the departments of University, Vignan Kendras and its affiliated colleges.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the University of Horticultural Sciences Act, 2009, and its commencement from 22nd November 2008.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academic Council, Affiliated college, Authority, Board, Board of Studies, Campus, College, Chancellor, Comptroller, Dean, Dean-Student Welfare, Director, Distance Education, Extension Education Council, Extension Education, Faculty, Government, Head of the Department, Horticulture, Horticultural Research Station, Hostel, Officer, Public Private Partnership, Research, Revolving Fund, Prescribed, Registrar, Regulations, Research Council, Schedule, Statutes, Student, Teacher, Transfer of Technology (TOT) units, Unit, University, University area, Vice-Chancellor, and Vignana Kendras.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the University of Horticultural Sciences as a corporate body with perpetual succession and a common seal, competent to acquire property, borrow money, and engage in legal proceedings. Its headquarters are in Bagalkot.

Defines the territorial jurisdiction of the University to extend to the State of Karnataka for teaching, research, and extension education in horticulture. It also states that no new Horticulture college shall be established without being a constituent or affiliated college of the University and that all existing Horticulture Colleges, Research Stations, and Vignan Kendras come under its constituent units.

important_rules: All Horticulture Colleges, Horticultural Research Stations, Thotagarike Vignan Kendras and other institutions coming under the jurisdiction and authority of the University shall come in as constituent units of the University under the full management and control of the University officers and authorities.
No unit shall be recognized as an affiliated college unless otherwise recognized as affiliated college by the University.

The University shall be competent to acquire and hold property, both movable and immovable, to lease, sell or otherwise transfer any movable or immovable property and to borrow money from the Central Government, State Government or any other approved sources.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement by the University authorities and the Government of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and functions vested in the University's authorities and officers as defined in the Act and Statutes.

rights: The University has the right to acquire and hold property, sue and be sued, and do all things necessary for the purpose of the Act.
Students have the right to pursue courses of study for degrees, diplomas, or other academic distinctions.
Teachers have the right to impart instructions and conduct research and extension education programmes.
duties: The University has a duty to provide for teaching, training, and research in Horticulture and allied Sciences.
Colleges and institutions affiliated with the University have a duty to adhere to the prescribed statutes and regulations.
The Government has a role in approving certain transactions of the University and providing grants.
obligations: The University has an obligation to establish, develop, and operate its constituent bodies.
The University must ensure that all new Horticulture colleges are its constituent or affiliated colleges.
The University must ensure that students admitted to its courses meet the required standards.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University: Section 3 outlines the process of establishing the University.
Transfer of Colleges and Institutions: Section 6 details the transfer of certain colleges, institutions, and employees to the University.
Affiliation of Colleges: Chapter VII outlines the procedures for affiliation of colleges and recognition of institutions.
Making of Statutes and Regulations: Chapter VIII describes the process of making Statutes (Section 53) and Regulations (Section 54).
administration: The University is administered by its various authorities and officers, including the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Board of Management, Academic Council, Research Council, Extension Education Council, and others as set forth in the Act or Statutes.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from 22nd day of November 2008.
The Headquarters of the University shall be at Bagalkot.
The territorial jurisdiction of the University extends to the entire State of Karnataka.

title: THE KARNATAKA OPEN PLACES (PREVENTION OF DISFIGUREMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Act, 1981, to extend its applicability to other areas declared under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, areas under the Bangalore Development Authority, or any other Urban Development Authority or Local Planning Authority.
scope: Geographically, the act applies to areas within municipal corporation areas or larger urban areas declared under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, areas under the Bangalore Development Authority, or any other Urban Development Authority or Local Planning Authority constituted under relevant law in force. The subject matter scope relates to the prevention of disfigurement of open places.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) (Amendment) Act, 2020, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (2) of section 1 of the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Act, 1981. It inserts a new clause (i-a) to extend the force of the Act to specified urban and planning authority areas upon notification by the State Government.

important_rules: Rule: The Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Act, 1981, is amended to extend its applicability to certain designated urban and planning authority areas. The commencement of this extended applicability in these areas will be on such date as may be notified by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notification for commencement of applicability in new areas, and impliedly, the authority responsible for enforcing the original Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the State Government notifying the date of commencement of the extended applicability of the Act to the specified urban and planning authority areas. Enforcement of the Act's provisions would then fall under the relevant authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure: The State Government issues a notification to bring into force the extended applicability of the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Act, 1981, to any other area falling within a municipal corporation area or larger urban area declared under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, or areas falling under the Bangalore Development Authority or any other Urban Development Authority or any other Local Planning Authority.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka)
important_notes: Note: The extension of the Act's applicability to the new areas mentioned in section 2(i-a) is contingent upon notification by the State Government.
Note: This is an amendment act to the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Act, 1981.

title: The Rai Technology University, Bangalore (Amendment) Act, 2018
purpose: To amend the Rai Technology University, Bangalore Act, 2012 to disallow the Rai Technology University, Bangalore from conducting courses pertaining to Agriculture Science Technology, any other emerging area of study, and Earth Science due to non-compliance with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) guidelines.
scope: This Act amends the Rai Technology University, Bangalore Act, 2012 (Karnataka Act 40 of 2013). It applies to the Rai Technology University, Bangalore. The subject matter scope relates to the courses offered by the university, specifically those concerning Agricultural Sciences and Technology, emerging areas of study, and Earth Sciences.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Rai Technology University, Bangalore (Amendment) Act, 2018 and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act (Rai Technology University, Bangalore Act, 2012) by omitting the words 'Agricultural Sciences and Technology' wherever they appear.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by omitting certain phrases from clause (i): 'and any other emerging areas' from item (a), entire item (c), and 'Earth Sciences' and 'any other emerging area of study' from item (e).

Provides that the amendment Act shall not affect the interests of students already admitted to Agricultural Science and Technology courses before the commencement of this amendment Act, provided the University obtains accreditation for these courses from National accreditation bodies and makes necessary arrangements for course completion for such students.

important_rules: Rule: The Rai Technology University, Bangalore is disallowed from conducting courses in Agriculture Science Technology, any other emerging area of study, and Earth Science.
Rule: The University must obtain accreditation from concerned National accreditation bodies for courses that students were admitted to before the commencement of this amendment Act.
Rule: The University must make necessary arrangements for the completion of courses by students admitted before the commencement of this amendment Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be through existing university governance and potentially relevant educational regulatory bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act and oversight of university compliance with the new provisions, particularly regarding accreditation and student course completion.

rights: Students admitted to Agricultural Science and Technology courses before the commencement of the amendment Act have the right to complete their courses.
Students have the right to courses that meet national accreditation standards.
duties: The Rai Technology University, Bangalore has the duty to cease conducting courses in Agriculture Science Technology, any other emerging area of study, and Earth Science if they do not comply with ICAR guidelines.
The University has a duty to obtain accreditation for existing courses from National accreditation bodies.
The University has a duty to make arrangements for the completion of courses for students admitted prior to the amendment.
obligations: The University is obligated to comply with the amendments introduced by this Act.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: This amendment Act is in effect from March 22, 2021, as published in the Karnataka Gazette.
The Act aims to ensure that courses offered by the university adhere to the norms, standards, and regulations mandated by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).

title: THE KARNATAKA IMPROVEMENT BOARDS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Improvement Boards Act, 1954 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically concerns amendments to the Karnataka Improvement Boards Act, 1954, particularly regarding the insertion of a new section 35A.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Improvement Boards (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force at once.

After Section 35 of the Karnataka Improvement Boards Act, 1954 (Karnataka Act 11 of 1954), the following shall be inserted, namely:-
35A. Power of the Bagalkot Town Development Authority to make bulk allotment of lands for the purposes of any development scheme. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any rules or regulations made thereunder, the Bagalkot Town Development Authority may make bulk allotment of lands to any category listed in (i) to (v) of sub-section (1) of section 35 or to any housing co-operative society registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959 or to any trust created for charitable, educational or religious purposes or any organization owned or controlled by the Central Government or the State Government or the State Government or any other body or organization as may be approved by the State Government for the purposes of any development scheme.

important_rules: Rule 1: Bulk allotment of lands can be made by the Bagalkot Town Development Authority.
Rule 2: This allotment is for development schemes and is notwithstanding anything in existing acts, rules, or regulations.

Rule 3: Allotments can be made to categories listed in section 35(1) (i) to (v), housing co-operative societies, charitable/educational/religious trusts, or organizations owned/controlled by the government, or other approved bodies.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bagalkot Town Development Authority and the State Government are implied authorities for the enforcement and approval related to this act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of making bulk allotments as specified in the new section 35A.

rights: The right of the Bagalkot Town Development Authority to make bulk allotments of land.
The right of eligible categories (as listed in section 35(1), co-operative societies, trusts, government-controlled organizations, etc.) to receive bulk allotment of land for development schemes.
obligations: Obligation of the Bagalkot Town Development Authority to follow the procedures outlined for bulk allotment.
Obligation of the State Government to approve entities for bulk allotment if they are not already covered.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Bagalkot Town Development Authority identifies land for a development scheme.

Procedure 2: The Authority makes a bulk allotment of this land to an eligible entity (housing co-operative society, trust, government-controlled organization, etc.) as per the provisions of section 35A and subject to State Government approval where necessary.
administration: State Government of Karnataka
important_notes: This amendment allows for bulk allotment of land for development schemes, which is an exception to regular land allocation procedures.
The specific categories for bulk allotment are detailed in section 35(1) of the principal Act and further expanded by this amendment.
The State Government has the power to approve entities for bulk allotment.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION AND OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To give effect to the announcement made in the Budget Speech by amending the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 and the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, specifically to change the purpose for which certain funds are allocated from equity investment in Infrastructure Development Corporation (Karnataka) Limited to various infrastructure projects across the State and equity investment in it.
scope: This act amends two existing Karnataka Acts: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 and The Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. The amendments affect provisions related to the allocation of funds derived from these acts within the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation and Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2002' and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the First day of April, 2002.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 3A (1) of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It substitutes specific words to change the purpose of fund allocation.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 3B (1) of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. It substitutes specific words to change the purpose of fund allocation.

important_rules: Rule: In the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, Section 3A (1), the phrase 'for the purpose of equity investment in the infrastructure Development Corporation (Karnataka) Limited and' is replaced with 'for the purpose of various infrastructure projects across the State and for the purpose of equity investment in the'.

Rule: In the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, Section 3B (1), the phrase 'for the purpose of equity investment in the infrastructure Development Corporation (Karnataka) Limited and' is replaced with 'for the purpose of various infrastructure projects across the State and for the purpose of equity investment in the'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely related to the authorities responsible for enforcing the amended Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957 and the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Enforcement would be through the mechanisms of the principal Acts being amended.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely administered by the departments responsible for finance, transport, and revenue in the Karnataka Government.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from April 1, 2002.
The amendments are aimed at re-directing funds towards broader infrastructure development projects within the State.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, to give effect to proposals made in the Budget speech.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and applies to motor vehicles registered in the State of Karnataka. The amendments primarily relate to taxation rates and structures for various classes of vehicles.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it comes into force on April 1, 2005.
Amends sub-section (3) of Section 7 of the principal Act by substituting 'Part C, Part C1, Part C2 and Part C3' with 'Part C, Part CC, Part C1, Part C2 and Part C3'.

Introduces amendments to various parts of the Schedule of the principal Act, including changes to taxation rates for specific vehicle types, introduction of lifetime tax for two-wheelers based on cost and age, and definitions for tax on three-wheeler auto rickshaws. It also introduces a new 'PART CC' for refund tables for two-wheelers.
Empowers the State Government to make provisions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, for a period of two years from the commencement date.

important_rules: Rule 1: In respect of vehicles for which lifetime tax was due prior to April 1, 2005, but not paid, such tax shall be collected at the rates prevailing prior to that day along with any applicable penalty.
Rule 2: For motor vehicles registered in other States prior to April 1, 2005, and migrated to Karnataka after that day, tax shall be levied as per Part-A1 as it existed prior to April 1, 2005.
Rule 3: For vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2005, the purchase invoice shall be produced for the levy of tax under Part A1.
Rule 4: If lifetime tax has been paid under Part A1 prior to April 1, 2005, the refund of tax shall be under the refund table in force prior to April 1, 2005.

penalties: Penalty for delayed payment of lifetime tax prior to April 1, 2005, as per existing provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government/Karnataka Motor Vehicles Department
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through collection of taxes as per the amended schedules and imposition of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to claim refund of lifetime tax for two-wheelers under specified conditions after registration removal or cancellation.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicles tax as per the rates and schedules specified in the Act.
Duty to produce purchase invoice for tax levy on vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2005.
obligations: Obligation to pay lifetime tax for two-wheelers based on their cost and age.
Obligation to comply with the amended taxation rules for various classes of motor vehicles.

key_procedures: Procedure for calculating and paying lifetime tax for two-wheelers, with rates varying based on vehicle cost and age.
Procedure for claiming a refund of lifetime tax for two-wheelers, with refund percentages decreasing over time.
Procedure for levying tax on migrated vehicles based on the tax structure prior to April 1, 2005.
administration: Department of Transport, Government of Karnataka (implied by the nature of the Act)
important_notes: The Act comes into force on April 1, 2005.
The State Government has the power to remove difficulties for two years from the commencement of the Act.
Specific amendments are made to Section 7 and the Schedule of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
The Act introduces a new Part CC for refund tables for two-wheelers.

title: THE ELECTRICITY (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend Section 151 of the Electricity Act, 2003, to empower Vigilance Police Stations of Electricity Supply Companies in Karnataka to file complaints before designated courts (Special Courts) for cognizance of offences under the Act.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Electricity Act, 2003 (Central Act 36 of 2003). It specifically addresses the institution of prosecution for offences related to electricity matters within the state.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Electricity (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2005' and states that it comes into force immediately upon enactment.

Replaces Section 151 of the Electricity Act, 2003, with new provisions regarding the institution of prosecution for offences under the Act. The substituted section clarifies who can institute a prosecution.

important_rules: Rule 1: Prosecution for offences under the Electricity Act, 2003, or any rules, regulations, licenses, or orders made thereunder, can only be instituted at the instance of the State Government, a licensee, a generating company, an officer authorized by any of these entities, or by any person affected by the alleged offence.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implicitly empowers Vigilance Police Stations of Electricity Supply Companies to initiate proceedings, and prosecution can be instituted by the State Government, a licensee, a generating company, or authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the institution of prosecution before designated courts (Special Courts) for cognizance of offences.

rights: Right of the State Government to institute prosecution.
Right of a licensee to institute prosecution.
Right of a generating company to institute prosecution.
Right of an authorized officer to institute prosecution.
Right of any person affected by an alleged offence to institute prosecution.

key_procedures: Procedure for Institution of Prosecution: The substituted Section 151 outlines the procedure, requiring that no prosecution be instituted except at the instance of specific authorities or affected persons.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and indirectly the State Government, licensees, and generating companies in relation to electricity matters.
important_notes: The amendment is specifically to Section 151 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
The purpose is to streamline and clarify the process of initiating legal action against electricity-related offences.

title: THE KARNATAKA BORDER AREA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Karnataka Border Area Development Authority for the development of border areas of Karnataka and for monitoring and evaluating the implementation of projects and programmes related to the development of these areas. It also aims to protect Kannada people in border areas from the influence of neighboring state languages and cultures, promote Kannada language and culture, improve living conditions, and foster self-respect among Kannadigas in border regions.
scope: The Act applies to the border areas of Karnataka, specifically the taluks and other areas enumerated in the Schedule. It aims to develop people in these areas in all spheres of life, including language, culture, education, irrigation, environment, industry, and agriculture. It also seeks to protect the Kannada people from the influence of neighboring state languages and cultures.

key_definitions.Authority: The Karnataka Border Area Development Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Border area: The Taluks and other areas situated in the border areas of Karnataka enumerated in the Schedule.
key_definitions.Department: All departments of the State Government, including any body or corporation established by the State Government by or under any law or any institution or body of organisations receiving financial aid from the State Government.
key_definitions.Projects and programmes: The annual projects and programmes in various departments prepared by the Authority for the development of the border areas of Karnataka.
key_definitions.Regulations: The regulations made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and the provision for its commencement by notification by the State Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Authority', 'Border area', 'Chairman', 'Department', 'Member', 'Projects and programmes', 'Secretary', and 'Regulations'.

Establishes the Karnataka Border Area Development Authority with its headquarters at Bangalore. It is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It outlines the composition of the Authority, including nominated and ex-officio members.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for nominated Chairman and members (three years), conditions for resignation, filling of casual vacancies, and allowances payable to members, which are to be defrayed from the Authority's fund. It also states that no act or proceeding is invalid due to vacancy or defect in constitution.

Lists grounds for disqualification from being a member, including conviction involving moral turpitude, unsound mind, undischarged insolvency, dismissal from government service, or having a share or interest in works or contracts of the Authority. It also clarifies an exception for shareholding in newspapers that publish Authority advertisements.

Details the grounds for removal of a Chairman or member by the State Government, including becoming subject to disqualification, refusal to act, prolonged absence from meetings, or abuse of position detrimental to public interest. It includes provisions for the member to make a representation before removal.

Outlines the appointment of the Secretary, who must be a Group A officer. It describes their salary and allowances, leave of absence, and defines their role as Chief Executive responsible for implementing projects, operating the fund, maintaining accounts, and other functions as conferred by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Officers of the Authority and conditions of service
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government or authorized officer to appoint officers and employees for the efficient discharge of the Authority's functions and prescribes rules for their recruitment and terms of service.

Governs the convening of meetings by the Chairman or Secretary (with Chairman's approval), frequency (at least once every two months), quorum (nine members), and procedures for presiding over meetings. Special meetings can be convened if necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings presumed to be good and valid
main_sections.description: Ensures that any act or proceeding of the Authority is not invalidated due to any disqualification or defect in the appointment of a Chairman or member, provided the act or proceeding is otherwise in accordance with the Act.
Allows the Authority to constitute Sub-Committees for specific purposes, with a maximum of six members, and the Chairman of the Authority also serves as the Chairman of the Sub-Committee.

Defines the powers and duties of the Sub-Committee, which include exercising delegated powers of the Authority, meeting monthly, making decisions on urgent matters, reviewing implementation, and suggesting actions to the State Government. It also follows prescribed rules of procedure.
Grants the Authority the power to obtain the services or assistance of experts as deemed fit for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with prescribed honorarium and allowances.
Mandates the Authority to prepare annual projects and programmes for border area development and submit them to the State Government for approval, which may be with or without modifications.

Outlines the key functions of the Authority, including implementing, supervising, and evaluating development works in border areas; improving educational, social, and cultural conditions of Kannada speakers; providing assistance for Kannada medium schools and teachers; opening libraries; and granting aid to Kannada organizations for pro-Kannada activities.
Deals with the establishment and management of the Fund of the Authority.
Specifies the provision for grants to be made by the State Government to the Authority.
Covers the maintenance of accounts by the Authority and their subsequent audit.
Details the requirement for the Authority to submit an annual report.
Pertains to the preparation and approval of the Authority's annual budget.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to make regulations
main_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to make regulations for the transaction of its business, subject to rules made by the State Government.

important_rules: The Authority must prepare annual projects and programmes for the development of border areas and submit them to the State Government for approval (Section 14).
The Authority shall meet at least once in every two months (Section 9(2)).
Nine members shall form the quorum for Authority meetings (Section 9(6)).
The Sub-Committee shall meet at least once in a month (Section 12(2)).
Nominated Chairman and members shall hold office for three years, subject to the pleasure of the State Government (Section 4(1)).
The Secretary shall be the Chief Executive responsible for implementing projects, operating the fund, and maintaining accounts (Section 7(3)).
No act or proceeding of the Authority shall be invalid due to the existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Authority (Section 4(6), Section 10).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Border Area Development Authority, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of projects and programs, monitoring and evaluation of development works, and by making regulations and rules as provided in the Act.

rights: Right to receive allowances for Chairman and members (Section 4(4)).
Right to be heard before removal from office under certain circumstances (Section 6(a) proviso, Section 6(d) proviso).
duties: Duty of the Authority to develop people in border areas in all spheres of life (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
Duty of the Authority to protect Kannada people from influence of neighboring state languages and cultures (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
Duty of the Authority to implement, supervise, and evaluate development works (Section 15(1)).
Duty of the Authority to provide assistance for Kannada medium schools, teachers, and textbooks (Section 15(2), 15(3)).
Duty of the Authority to open libraries and grant aid to Kannada organizations (Section 15(4), 15(5)).
Duty of the Secretary to implement approved projects, operate the fund, and maintain accounts (Section 7(3)).
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to appoint officers and employees for the Authority (Section 8(1)).
Obligation of the State Government to make rules and the Authority to make regulations for the proper functioning of the Act.

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of annual projects and programmes by the Authority to the State Government for approval (Section 14).
Convening of meetings of the Authority by the Chairman or Secretary (Section 9(1), 9(3)).
Procedure for removal of a member, including providing an opportunity for representation (Section 6).
Appointment of officers and employees by the State Government or authorized officer (Section 8(1)).
Procedure for the Sub-Committee to review urgent matters and suggest actions to the State Government (Section 12(3)).
administration: The Karnataka Border Area Development Authority, with the State Government holding powers for appointment, rule-making, and overall oversight.
important_notes: The Act aims to safeguard and promote Kannada language, culture, and the well-being of Kannada-speaking people in border regions.
The State Government has the power to appoint the commencement date of the Act.
The Authority is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Provisions are made to ensure that minor defects in the constitution or appointment of members do not invalidate the Authority's proceedings.

title: THE KARNATAKA VALUE ADDED TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, to give effect to budget proposals, empower the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes to notify websites for online registration and transit pass information, and to rationalize certain provisions.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It applies to dealers and the taxation of goods within the state of Karnataka. Specific amendments relate to tax rates, reimbursement of tax, assessment periods, and penalties.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it comes into force with effect from April 1, 2011.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act regarding tax rates. It specifies a 5% rate for goods in the Third Schedule and revises rates for declared goods, manufactured tobacco, and other goods (14%).

Substitutes section 21 of the principal Act to allow for reimbursement of tax collected on certain purchases made by specialized UN agencies, multilateral financial institutions, and notified organizations, as well as Consulates or Embassies, subject to prescribed conditions.
Inserts a proviso in section 25 of the principal Act, empowering the Commissioner to notify a website for electronic submission of applications.
Amends section 31 of the principal Act by increasing the threshold from 'sixty lakh rupees' to 'one hundred lakh rupees' and omitting sub-section (6).
Amends section 37 of the principal Act by substituting 'one and a quarter per cent' with 'one and one half per cent'.

Amends section 40 of the principal Act by reducing the assessment/re-assessment period from five years to four years in certain cases, with a proviso for tax periods ending March 31, 2007, allowing a five-year period. It also adjusts references to ten years to eight years.
Inserts a proviso in section 53 of the principal Act. For goods with a leviable tax rate less than four percent, the penalty under sub-clause (ii) will be five times the amount of tax leviable.
Inserts a proviso in section 54 of the principal Act, allowing the Commissioner to notify a website for furnishing information by the driver or person-in-charge of a vehicle.
Amends section 62 of the principal Act by substituting 'one hundred twenty days' with 'two hundred forty days'.
