Omitted entries relating to serial numbers 2 and 3 in the Second Schedule of the principal Act.
Amends the Third Schedule of the principal Act by omitting 'used for cooking food' from serial number 5 and omitting entries related to serial number 30.

Amends the Sixth Schedule of the principal Act by omitting serial number 7, substituting the rate for declared goods in serial number 12, and increasing the rate from 'Thirteen and one half per cent' to 'Fourteen per cent' for serial number 23.

important_rules: Rule regarding electronic submission of applications for registration via a notified website.
Rule regarding electronic furnishing of information for goods in transit via a notified website.
Reimbursement of tax collected on certain purchases made by specified international organizations and diplomatic entities.
Specific tax rates are defined for declared goods, manufactured tobacco, and other goods.
Penalties for tax evasion are modified, with a higher penalty for goods taxed at less than four percent.

penalties: Penalty for offenses related to tax evasion where the leviable tax rate is less than four percent is equivalent to five times the amount of tax leviable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of Commercial Taxes
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing sections of the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003, relating to tax rates, assessment periods, and penalties. Enforcement also includes the mandate for electronic filing and information submission via notified websites.

rights: Right for specialized agencies of the United Nations Organisation, Multilateral Financial Institutions, and notified organizations, as well as Consulates or Embassies (excluding those notified), to claim reimbursement of tax on prescribed purchases.
Right to register as a dealer electronically through a notified website.
duties: Duty of dealers to comply with tax rates as amended.
Duty to furnish information regarding transit of goods electronically via a notified website.
Duty to comply with the prescribed periods for assessment and re-assessment.
Duty to pay penalties as stipulated in the amended provisions.

key_procedures: Electronic application for dealer registration via a notified website.
Electronic furnishing of information by vehicle operators regarding goods in transit via a notified website.
Procedure for reimbursement of tax for eligible organizations.
Assessment and re-assessment procedures within specified timeframes.
administration: Commissioner of Commercial Taxes
important_notes: The Act came into force on April 1, 2011.
Amendments to the Second, Third, and Sixth Schedules of the principal Act are made, affecting specific goods and tax rates.
A specific proviso addresses assessment or re-assessment relating to tax periods ending March 31, 2007, allowing a five-year period.

title: THE KARNATAKA TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC PROCUREMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, to increase the limit for the value of procurement of goods and services for the application of the Act's provisions from rupees one lakh to rupees five lakhs, and to make consequential changes in the scope of applicable procurements.
scope: The Act applies to public procurements in Karnataka. The amendment specifically alters the financial threshold for when the Act's provisions apply and broadens the types of procurements covered.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements (Amendment) Act, 2020, and that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 4 of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999. It substitutes 'goods and services including construction works and consultancy services' for 'construction works and consultancy services' in sub-clause (i) of clause (e), and omits sub-clause (ii).

important_rules: Rule: The limit for the value of procurement of goods and services subject to the provisions of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, is increased from rupees one lakh to rupees five lakhs.
Rule: The scope of procurements covered by the Act is expanded to include 'goods and services including construction works and consultancy services'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the relevant authorities responsible for enforcing the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is mentioned as responsible for publishing the translated act.
important_notes: The amendment was enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature in the seventy-first year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 24th day of April, 2020.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on the 27th day of April, 2020.

title: The Karnataka Money Lenders (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To amend sections 38 and 39 of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961, to enhance penalty amounts and conviction terms to ensure stricter adherence to the Act's provisions.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka and relates to the regulation of money lending activities as defined by the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Money Lenders (Amendment) Act, 2021, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 38 of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961, by substituting the penalty clause. The previous penalty of imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, is replaced with imprisonment up to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.

Amends section 39 of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961, by substituting clauses (a) and (b). For the first offense, imprisonment may extend to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both. For the second or subsequent offense, imprisonment may extend to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.

important_rules: For the first offense under section 39, the penalty is simple imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.
For the second or subsequent offense under section 39, the penalty is simple imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.
The penalty for offenses under section 38 has been enhanced to imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.

penalties: For offenses under Section 38: Imprisonment up to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.
For first offense under Section 39: Simple imprisonment up to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.
For second or subsequent offense under Section 39: Simple imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the authorities responsible for enforcing the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961, likely including police and judicial officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and imposition of penalties as prescribed in the amended sections.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka is indicated as the issuing authority for the gazette notification. The overall administration of the Money Lenders Act would typically fall under a finance or cooperative department.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 25th day of March, 2021.
Published in Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary No. 305 in part-IVA dated: 26.03.2021.
The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961 (Karnataka Act 12 of 1962).

title: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (Amendment) Act, 2023
purpose: To amend the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, for the proper maintenance of the property tax register and to exempt recognized educational institutions from paying property tax.
scope: This act amends the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, and applies to the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) area. Its subject matter scope pertains to property tax registration and exemptions for educational institutions.

key_definitions.Principal Act: Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020 (Karnataka Act 53 of 2020)

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (Amendment) Act, 2023, and it shall come into force at once.
This section amends section 144 of the Principal Act by omitting the words 'double the tax payable which shall be' from sub-section (6).

This section amends section 152 of the Principal Act by substituting sub-clause (b) of clause (i) in sub-section (1) with a new clause. The substituted clause refers to 'educational institutions established for the purpose of education, recognized by the Government or Local Authority.'

important_rules: Rule 1: Omission of specific wording related to double tax payable from section 144(6) of the Principal Act.
Rule 2: Substitution of sub-clause (b) in section 152(1)(i) of the Principal Act to define eligible educational institutions for exemption from property tax.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation and administration of the amended Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020.

rights: Right for recognized educational institutions to be exempt from paying property tax.
duties: Duty of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike to properly maintain the property tax register.
Duty to implement the amendments made by this Act.
obligations: Obligation for recognized educational institutions to meet the criteria specified in the amended section 152(1)(i)(b).

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment aims to ensure proper maintenance of the property tax register.
The exemption from property tax for educational institutions is conditional on their recognition by the Government or Local Authority and their establishment for the purpose of education.

title: THE KARNATAKA MINISTERS' SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: This act amends the Karnataka Ministers' Salaries and Allowances Act, 1997, to revise the salaries and allowances of the Chief Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
scope: This act applies to the Chief Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers of the Karnataka Government. It specifies their salaries and allowances.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the act and when it comes into force. It is the Karnataka Ministers' Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2000, and it came into force from the 23rd day of December 2000.
This section amends section 3 of the Karnataka Ministers' Salaries and Allowances Act, 1997. It deals with the salary of the Chief Minister.
This section amends section 4 of the principal Act. It pertains to the salary of Cabinet Ministers.
This section amends section 6A of the principal Act, which relates to the allowances for Cabinet Ministers.
This section amends section 6B of the principal Act, concerning allowances for Ministers of State.
This section amends section 7 of the principal Act, relating to allowances for Deputy Ministers.
This section amends section 8 of the principal Act. It pertains to the allowances for Deputy Ministers.
This section amends section 12 of the principal Act. It relates to the provisions regarding allowances.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Chief Minister shall receive a salary of fourteen thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 3)
Rule 2: A Cabinet Minister shall receive a salary of twelve thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 4)
Rule 3: A Minister of State shall receive a salary of eleven thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 6A)
Rule 4: A Deputy Minister shall receive a salary of ten thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 6B and 7)
Rule 5: Allowances for Deputy Ministers shall be seven thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 8)
Rule 6: Section 12 of the principal Act is amended to specify the allowances for Deputy Ministers as seven thousand rupees per mensem. (Amendment of section 12)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text. Likely the Karnataka government or relevant finance department.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly stated in the provided text.

rights: Right to receive prescribed salaries.
Right to receive prescribed allowances.
duties: Duty to perform official functions as per the roles of Chief Minister, Cabinet Minister, Minister of State, or Deputy Minister.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Karnataka Government's Finance Department or General Administration Department.
important_notes: This act is an amendment to the Karnataka Ministers' Salaries and Allowances Act, 1997.
The amendments came into effect from December 23, 2000.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, to provide for representation and to enable further amendments to the Act.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966. It specifically addresses agricultural produce marketing and related regulations.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) (Amendment) Act, 2002. It will be deemed to have come into force on the eleventh day of April, 2002.

This section amends Section 2 of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966. It refers to the insertion of new clauses, specifically mentioning the addition of 'backward classes' and 'scheduled tribes' as categories.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 11, 2002.
Amendments are made to Section 2 of the principal Act regarding 'backward classes' and 'scheduled tribes'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely the state government or authorities established under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2 of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, by inserting new clauses related to 'backward classes' and 'scheduled tribes'.
administration: The Karnataka State Government or relevant departments responsible for agricultural marketing.
important_notes: The 'Statement of Objects and Reasons' indicates that the amendment aims to provide representation and to ensure social justice for backward classes.
The Act aims to bring about representation of "backward classes" and "scheduled tribes" in scheduled castes and scheduled tribes committees.
The amendments are made to Section 2 of the principal Act, which defines various terms used in the Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA REPEALING AND AMENDING ACT, 2002
purpose: To repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments. It aims to update Codal Volumes of Karnataka Acts by repealing spent Acts and amendment Acts.
scope: Applies to enactments in Karnataka. It repeals and amends various State Acts listed in its Schedules. The act's scope is primarily to clean up and update the legal framework by removing obsolete laws and modifying existing ones.

key_definitions.Schedule: Means a Schedule annexed to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the 'Karnataka Repealing and Amending Act, 2002' and states that it comes into force at once.
Defines 'Schedule' as a schedule annexed to the Act.
Repeals the enactments specified in the First Schedule.
Amends the enactments specified in columns (2) and (3) of the Second Schedule to the extent and in the manner mentioned in the corresponding entries in column (4).

Provides provisions regarding the effect of the repeal of enactments, ensuring that past actions, acquired rights, liabilities, and legal proceedings are not affected. It also clarifies that the repeal does not revive any jurisdiction or matter not currently in force and applies the provisions of the Karnataka General Clauses Act, 1899.

important_rules: Rule 1: The repeal of any enactment by this Act does not affect other enactments where the repealed enactment was applied, incorporated, or referred to.
Rule 2: The repeal does not affect the validity, effect, or consequences of anything already done or suffered, nor any acquired rights, obligations, liabilities, remedies, or proceedings.
Rule 3: The repeal does not affect any principle or rule of law, jurisdiction, pleading, practice, procedure, usage, custom, privilege, restriction, exemption, office, or appointment.

Rule 4: The repeal does not revive or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or any other matter or thing not currently existing or in force.
Rule 5: The repeal of Appropriation Acts does not affect audit, examination, accounting, investigation, inquiry, or any other action related to them.
Rule 6: The repeal of Act 2 of 1973 and Act 38 of 1987 does not affect proceedings initiated or to be initiated under these enactments to challenge or enforce rights conferred by them.

Rule 7: For the removal of doubts, it is declared that where an enactment is repealed by this Act that amended another enactment by addition, omission, insertion, or substitution, the repeal does not affect the continuance of such amendment.

Rule 8: Where an enactment is repealed by this Act and it validated or saved any action taken (including rules, orders, bye-laws, regulations, taxes, cesses, or fees assessed or collected), or transferred proceedings, or made declarations or gave directions, the repeal does not affect the operation of such validation, saving, transfer, declaration, or direction.

Rule 9: Where an enactment is repealed by this Act and it amended, repealed, or extended another enactment to the State of Karnataka, the repeal does not affect the operation of such amendment, repeal, extension, or provision.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified for the repeal and amendment process itself, but implied to be the relevant authorities overseeing the legal system and the acts being amended or repealed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of repeal and amendment. The 'Savings' section outlines how existing legal situations are preserved despite the repeal.

rights: Right to continue proceedings initiated under repealed enactments (Section 5(1) and 5(2)(iii)).
Right to the continued validity of actions taken under repealed enactments (Section 5(2)(ii)).
Right to continued application of amendments made by repealed enactments (Section 5(2)(i)).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Karnataka General Clauses Act, 1899 in relation to the repeal of enactments (Section 5(3)).

key_procedures: Procedure for repeal: Enactments listed in the First Schedule are repealed by operation of Section 3.
Procedure for amendment: Enactments specified in the Second Schedule are amended as per the details in column (4) of that Schedule, as per Section 4.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Karnataka State Legislature and the relevant departments responsible for legislative affairs.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 31st day of March, 2003, upon publication in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary.
The Act repeals a significant number of State Acts, many of which are amendment acts or acts that have become spent or obsolete.
The 'Savings' section (Section 5) is crucial for understanding the extent to which the repeal affects ongoing matters and existing legal statuses.

title: THE KARNATAKA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959 to provide for conversion of Co-operatives under the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997 into Co-operative Societies, grant voting rights to Co-operative Societies after 12 months of admission, require prior sanction of RBI for Co-operative Banks in certain cases, empower the Registrar to conduct general meetings in case of committee failure, mandate elections within three months of registration or amalgamation/reorganisation/division with administrator appointment, vest powers under specific sections with the Registrar, provide for appeals against Registrar's orders, and vest compounding of audit-related offences with the Director of Co-operative Audit.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959. It applies to Co-operative Societies registered or to be registered under the principal Act within the State of Karnataka. Specific amendments relate to Co-operative Banks and Co-operatives registered under the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997.

key_definitions.Co-operative: A Co-operative registered under the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997, and includes the Union Co-operative and the Federal Co-operative.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2004, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification, with different dates possible for different provisions.
Inserts a new clause (d-2) in section 2 of the principal Act to define 'Co-operative'.

Inserts a new clause (g) in sub-section (2) of section 6 of the principal Act, requiring an application for conversion into a Co-operative Society under this Act to be accompanied by a resolution of the general meeting approving such conversion.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 26A to require prior permission of the Registrar for assisted societies and the Reserve Bank of India for Co-operative Banks to enter into partnerships.
Inserts a new sub-section (3) in section 27 of the principal Act, empowering the Registrar or an authorized person to convene a general meeting if the committee fails to do so.

Amends sub-section (4) of section 28A to mandate the first general meeting of newly formed or reorganized Co-operative Societies to be held within three months for electing the first committee. Amends sub-section (5) to require the Registrar to appoint an administrator for three months to arrange for elections in such cases.
Amends section 106 of the principal Act to include appeals against orders of the Registrar under sections 12(4), 12(6), 17, and 31(1) (appointing a special officer).

Amends section 110A to allow the Director of Co-operative Audit to accept composition for offences related to contravention of section 63, not exceeding one thousand rupees. Also modifies provisions regarding the Registrar or Director of Co-operative Audit accepting compositions.

important_rules: A Co-operative Society must contribute two percent of its net profits to the Co-operative Education Fund administered by the Karnataka State Co-operative Federation Limited.
No Co-operative Society that has failed to contribute to the Co-operative Education Fund shall pay dividends to its members.

The first general meeting of a Co-operative Society or Societies formed after amalgamation, reorganisation, or division must be held within three months from the date of registration to elect the first committee.

An administrator shall be appointed by the Registrar for a period of three months to arrange for elections to the committee of a Co-operative Society formed after amalgamation, reorganisation, or division.
Prior permission of the Reserve Bank of India is required for a Co-operative Bank to enter into partnerships or collaborations.
The Director of Co-operative Audit may accept a composition sum not exceeding one thousand rupees for an offence related to the contravention of section 63.

penalties: Failure to contribute to the Co-operative Education Fund results in the inability to pay dividends to members.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Director of Co-operative Audit, Reserve Bank of India (for Co-operative Banks).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notifications for commencement, appointing administrators, convening general meetings, accepting compositions for offences, and through appeal provisions against orders.

rights: Right of members to receive dividends if the Co-operative Society contributes to the Co-operative Education Fund.
Right to appeal against certain orders of the Registrar.
duties: Duty of Co-operative Societies to contribute to the Co-operative Education Fund.
Duty to hold general meetings within specified periods.
Duty to obtain prior permission from RBI for Co-operative Banks' partnerships/collaborations.
obligations: Obligation to register Co-operatives under the principal Act after conversion from Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997.
Obligation to hold elections for the first committee within three months of registration of new or reorganized societies.
Obligation for the Registrar to appoint an administrator to facilitate elections where needed.

key_procedures: Procedure for conversion of a Karnataka Souharda Sahakari into a Co-operative Society: Requires a resolution of the general meeting approving such conversion.

Procedure for election of the first committee in newly formed or reorganized Co-operative Societies: First general meeting must be held within three months of registration, with an administrator appointed if necessary to facilitate elections.
Procedure for appeal against Registrar's orders: Appeals can be filed against specified orders of the Registrar.
Procedure for compounding of offences related to audit: The Director of Co-operative Audit can accept a composition sum for certain offences.
administration: Registrar of Co-operative Societies and Director of Co-operative Audit, under the overall purview of the Karnataka State Government.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date specified by the State Government by notification, which may differ for different provisions.
The amendments are made in view of a judgment by the Hon'ble High Court.
Voting rights for Co-operative Societies as members of other Co-operative Societies are to be exercised by a committee member appointed by the society's committee.

title: THE BASAVAKALYAN DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Board for the preservation, development, and maintenance of heritage sites in and around Basavakalyan Town in Bidar District, and to develop Basavakalyan into an international pilgrimage, cultural, and tourist center.
scope: The Act extends to the area of Basavakalyan as defined in clause (b) of section 2, which includes the limits of Basavakalyan Town Municipal Committee, an area within twelve kilometers from the town, lands acquired by the Government for heritage sites, and any other area declared by the State Government. It applies to the development and maintenance of heritage sites and related amenities.

key_definitions.amenity: Includes road, streets, sub-ways, lighting, drainage, sanitation, electricity and water supply or other convenience, public works, market places, post office, bank, hospital, dispensary, police station, fair price shop, milk booth, library, recreation centers, service stations of any public utility service authorised by the Board or other facility; and such other amenity as the State Government may, by notification specify.
key_definitions.board: The Basavakalyan Development Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.basavakalyan: Means and includes limits of Basavakalyan Town Municipal Committee and area within twelve kilo meters from the town and lands acquired by Government from time to time for development of Basavakalyan heritage sites and such other area declared by the State Government, by notification.
key_definitions.heritage_site: The whole of the area comprising the sites specified in the Schedule but excluding the area referred to as protected area under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958 (Central Act 24 of 1958).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Amenity', 'Board', 'Basavakalyan', 'Chairman', 'Commissioner', 'Fund', 'Heritage Site', 'Member', 'Regulations', and 'Schedule'.

Establishes the Basavakalyan Development Board as a body corporate, specifies its headquarters, and lists its ex-officio and nominated members, with the Chief Minister as ex-officio Chairman and the Commissioner as Member-Secretary.

Grants the Board general powers to do what is necessary to give effect to the Act's intent and provisions, including entering into contracts, borrowing money, and leasing or selling property, subject to rules and government sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Designates the Commissioner as the Chief Executive and Administrative Officer of the Board, responsible for carrying out resolutions, conducting business, executing schemes, managing accounts, and supervising staff.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation of developmental plan, its approval and execution
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for preparing, approving, and executing a developmental plan for Basavakalyan.
Establishes the fund of the Board and its sources.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations for the transaction of its business and other incidental matters.
Deals with the repeal of any existing provisions and savings thereof.

important_rules: Non-official members nominated by the State Government shall hold office for a period of three years.

A member can be disqualified if convicted of an offense involving moral turpitude, declared of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, has been removed from government service, or has a direct or indirect interest in any work or contract of the Board.

The State Government shall remove a member who becomes subject to disqualifications, refuses to act, becomes incapable of acting, or absents from three consecutive meetings without leave (except ex-officio members).
No contract involving expenditure of rupees five lakhs and more can be made by the Board without the previous sanction of the State Government.
The Board can borrow money with the previous sanction of the State Government and subject to prescribed conditions.
The Board shall not sell any land within its jurisdiction.

penalties: Section 40: Default in performance of duty by the Board or Commissioner can lead to action by the State Government, including supersession of the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Basavakalyan Development Board, under the overall control and direction of the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board and its Commissioner, including power of entry (Section 24), levy of fee (Section 25), and general powers to do necessary acts for implementing the Act. The State Government also has control and power to give directions and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to develop and maintain heritage sites and Basavakalyan into an international center.
Right to enter into contracts, borrow money, and manage property.
Right to levy fees for services and amenities.
Right to promote tourism and cultural programs.
duties: Duty to preserve, develop, and maintain heritage sites.
Duty to prepare and execute developmental plans.
Duty to maintain streets, etc. (Section 27).
Duty of the Commissioner to carry into effect resolutions of the Board, conduct its business, and implement schemes.
Duty of the Board to comply with directions from the State Government.
obligations: Obligation to seek permission for development from the Board (Section 23).
Obligation to maintain accounts and submit reports for audit.
Obligation to comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board with specific ex-officio and nominated members.
Appointment of a Commissioner not below the rank of Deputy Secretary.
Preparation, approval, and execution of developmental plans.
Lease, sale, or transfer of movable or immovable property subject to restrictions and government approval.
Procedure for making contracts, including government sanction for contracts above a certain value.
Borrowing money with government sanction.
administration: The Basavakalyan Development Board, with the Chief Minister as ex-officio Chairman and the State Government exercising control and providing directions.
important_notes: The Basavakalyan Development Board is also designated as the Urban Development Authority for Basavakalyan (Section 22).
No other authority or person can undertake development in Basavakalyan without the permission of the Board (Section 23).
The Board is not authorized to perform acts specifically assigned to other authorities.
The Act provides for the dissolution of the Board under certain circumstances (Section 41).

title: THE KARNATAKA PROFESSIONAL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (REGULATION OF ADMISSION AND FIXATION OF FEE) (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2006
purpose: To provide for recognition of the consensual agreement entered into between the State Government and the Private Unaided Educational Institutions imparting Professional Educational Courses and for other matters, as provided in the judgment of the Supreme Court of India in P.A. Inamdar and others Vs. State of Maharashtra.
scope: This Act applies to Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions in Karnataka offering Professional Educational Courses. Specifically for the academic year 2006-07, it governs admissions and fee fixation, superseding the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006.

key_definitions.common_entrance_test: The entrance test conducted for the determination of merit of candidates, followed by centralized counseling for admission to professional educational courses through a single window procedure.
key_definitions.common_entrance_test_cell: The agency of the State Government that conducts the common entrance test.
key_definitions.consensual_arrangement_or_agreement: Any agreement entered into between the State Government and an association of unaided Private Professional Educational Institutions relating to admission and fee fixation in professional courses.
key_definitions.institution: Professional Educational Institutions offering Professional Educational courses.
key_definitions.one_man_regulatory_committee: The committee constituted by the State Government under section 3.
key_definitions.professional_educational_courses: Includes Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery; Bachelor of Dental Surgery; Bachelor of Engineering; Bachelor of Technology; Bachelor of Architecture; and other courses as may be notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.unaided_institution: Any privately managed professional educational institution not receiving aid or grant-in-aid from the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Fixation of Fee) (Special Provisions) Act, 2006. It came into force at once and for the academic year 2006-07, admissions and fee fixation in un-aided private Professional Educational Institutions are governed by this Act, notwithstanding anything in the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including Common Entrance Test, Common Entrance Test Cell, Consensual arrangement or agreement, Institution, One Man Regulatory Committee, Professional Educational Courses, and Unaided institution.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of One Man Regulatory Committee
main_sections.description: Establishes a One-Man Regulatory Committee appointed by the State Government, consisting of a former Vice-Chancellor of a University in the State. This committee is tasked with overseeing admission to professional courses and the implementation of consensual arrangements or agreements.

Empowers the State Government to fix the fee payable for admission to Unaided Private Professional Educational Institutions in accordance with the consensual agreement, by notification. Different fee rates may be fixed for different categories of students and institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of admission and seat matrix
main_sections.description: Details the manner of filling seats in Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions to implement the consensual arrangement. It specifies the percentage of seats to be filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell for Engineering, Medical, and Dental courses, based on whether the institution is minority or non-minority. The remaining seats are to be filled through a Common Entrance Test conducted by the association of Private Professional Educational Institutions or minority institutions, followed by centralized counseling. The State Government may also publish the seat matrix for different categories of students and institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Invalidation of admissions made in violation of this Act
main_sections.description: Declares all admissions made in violation of this Act or the consensual arrangement by any Private Unaided Professional Educational Institution for the academic year 2006-07 as invalid. The State Government can direct the concerned university to cancel such admissions or affiliation of the institution.
Grants the State Government the power to make necessary or expedient orders, not inconsistent with the Act, to remove any difficulties arising in the implementation of the Act's provisions.

Authorizes the State Government to make rules, prospectively or retrospectively, for carrying out the purposes of the Act, by notification in the official Gazette. These rules are subject to legislative scrutiny by both Houses of the State Legislature.

important_rules: Rule 1: Admissions and fee fixation in un-aided private Professional Educational Institutions for the academic year 2006-07 are governed by this Act, superseding the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006.

Rule 2: At least 60% of seats in non-minority Engineering institutions and 50% in minority Engineering institutions, and at least 50% of seats in non-minority Medical and Dental institutions and 40% in minority Medical and Dental institutions, must be filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell.
Rule 3: Remaining seats are to be filled through a common entrance test by the associations, followed by centralized counseling based on merit.
Rule 4: Admissions made in violation of the Act or the consensual arrangement for the academic year 2006-07 are invalid, and the State Government can order cancellation of admissions or affiliation.

penalties: Invalidation of admissions made in violation of the Act.
Cancellation of admissions by the concerned university.
Cancellation of affiliation of the institution by the concerned university.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and the One Man Regulatory Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders published in the official Gazette, notifications for fee fixation and seat matrix, and directions to universities for cancellation of admissions or affiliations. The One Man Regulatory Committee oversees admissions and implementation of agreements.

rights: Students have the right to admission based on merit through centralized counseling for a specified percentage of seats.
Institutions have the right to fill remaining seats through their own common entrance tests and counseling, subject to merit and agreement.
The State Government has the right to fix fees and regulate admissions through notifications and consensual agreements.
duties: Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions have a duty to comply with the admission and fee fixation regulations stipulated in the Act and the consensual agreement.
The State Government has a duty to protect the interests of Karnataka domicile students and students from educationally and socially backward classes.
The Common Entrance Test Cell has a duty to conduct the common entrance test for determining merit.
obligations: Unaided private professional educational institutions are obligated to adhere to the seat matrix and admission procedures outlined.
The State Government is obligated to ensure fair and transparent admission processes.
Institutions are obligated to have their admissions validated under this Act for the academic year 2006-07.

key_procedures: 1. For the academic year 2006-07, admissions and fee fixation in unaided private professional educational institutions are governed by this Act.
2. The State Government, in accordance with the consensual agreement, may fix fees for admissions through notification.
3. A specific percentage of seats are to be filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell based on merit.
4. The remaining seats are filled through an association-conducted Common Entrance Test followed by centralized counseling.
5. The State Government may publish the seat matrix for different categories.
6. Admissions violating the Act or agreement are invalid and can lead to cancellation of admissions or affiliation.
administration: State Government (specifically, the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is mentioned as the signing authority for the Governor's order). The One Man Regulatory Committee is appointed by the State Government.
important_notes: This Act is a 'Special Provisions' Act and applies specifically to the academic year 2006-07, overriding the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006 for this period.
The Act aims to give effect to a consensual agreement reached between the State Government and private unaided institutions, as per a Supreme Court judgment.
The Act seeks to protect the interests of students of Karnataka domicile and those belonging to educationally and socially backward classes.

title: THE KARNATAKA SAMSKRITA VISHWAVIDYALAYA ACT, 2009
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of the Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya for the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in Sanskrit language, its literature, Vedic studies, and associated Shastras and disciplines.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment, incorporation, and functioning of the Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya. Its jurisdiction and affiliations are primarily within Karnataka, with provisions for recognizing institutions both within and outside India. The subject matter scope covers Sanskrit language, literature, Vedic studies, Shastras, and related allied areas including modern applications and inter-disciplinary studies.

key_definitions.appointed_date: The date appointed for the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.constituent_college: A constituent college of the university.
key_definitions.hostel: A unit of residence for the students of the university maintained or recognised by the university.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by the statutes.
key_definitions.statutes: The statutes of the university made under this Act.
key_definitions.teachers: Includes Professors, emeritus Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other like persons as may be declared by the statutes to be teachers.
key_definitions.university: The Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya established under section 3.
key_definitions.university_grants_commission: The Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
key_definitions.university_library: A library maintained by the Vishwavidyalaya whether instituted by it or not.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya Act, 2009, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed date', 'constituent college', 'Government', 'hostel', 'prescribed', 'Regulations', 'Statutes', 'teachers', 'University', 'University Grants Commission', and 'University library'.

Provides for the establishment of the Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya, declaring it a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It specifies its headquarters location, powers to acquire and hold property, and conditions for transferring immovable property. It also outlines procedures for suits and legal proceedings involving the University.

Enumerate the objectives of the University, which include functioning as a high-level teaching and research organization in Sanskrit, preserving and promoting traditional learning, highlighting the relevance of Vedic and Shastric knowledge to the modern world, facilitating advanced study and research in various related fields, consolidating and reviving Bharatiya Jnana Parampara, creating awareness about authentic interpretations of Vedas, networking with similar institutions, producing literature in modern languages, translating and publishing Sanskrit works, digitizing manuscripts, organizing academic events, and establishing Directorates and Chairs for research.

Details the powers of the University, including instituting and conferring degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions, supervising hostels, controlling students, co-operating with other institutions, establishing libraries and research stations, instituting research posts, awarding fellowships and scholarships, and accepting endowments and donations.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall sue and be sued by its name.

Rule 2: No institution affiliated to, or associated with, or maintained by any other University in the State shall be recognized by the Karnataka Samskrita Vishwavidyalaya without prior approval of the Government and the concerned University.
Rule 3: The University shall not lease, sell or otherwise transfer any immovable property without obtaining the prior approval of the Government.

Rule 4: Degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions may be conferred on persons who have carried out research in the University or recognized institutions, irrespective of religion, race, creed, caste, gender, or class.
Rule 5: The University shall not accept donations from a foreign country, foreign foundation, or foreign person without the approval of the Government.

rights: Right to establish and function as a University for Sanskrit studies.
Right to acquire and hold property.
Right to institute and confer degrees and academic distinctions.
Right to supervise and control hostels and students.
Right to co-operate with other institutions.
Right to accept endowments and donations.
duties: Duty to function as a high-level teaching and research organization in Sanskrit.
Duty to preserve, foster, and promote the traditional system of learning in Vedic and related disciplines.
Duty to highlight the wisdom contained in Vedic and Shastric disciplines.
Duty to facilitate and regulate advanced study and research in specified fields.
Duty to consolidate, revive, and promote Bharatiya Jnana Parampara.
Duty to create a network of Vedic and Sanskrit institutions.
Duty to translate/publish Sanskrit works and related texts.
Duty to build audio and audio-visual records of Vedic chanting.
Duty to collect, preserve, critically edit and publish rare manuscripts.
Duty to computerize and digitize Sanskrit texts.
Duty to organize seminars, conferences, and workshops.
Duty to admit educational institutions as affiliated colleges.
Duty to provide teaching and guidance to affiliated colleges.
Duty to do acts necessary to promote the objectives of the University.
obligations: Obligation to obtain prior approval of the Government for transferring immovable property.
Obligation to obtain prior approval of the Government and concerned University for recognizing institutions affiliated with other Universities.
Obligation to obtain permission from concerned authorities for recognizing institutions outside India.
Obligation to conform to the 'prescribed' manner and conditions for conferring honorary degrees.
Obligation to obtain approval from the Government for accepting donations from foreign sources.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment of the University including incorporation and location of headquarters.
Procedure for recognition of institutions by the University, requiring prior approval from the Government and concerned University.
Procedure for transferring immovable property by the University, requiring prior approval from the Government.
Procedure for conferring degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions.
Procedure for conferring honorary degrees.
Procedure for accepting endowments, donations, or funds.
administration: The State Government (through relevant departments, though not explicitly named for day-to-day administration in the provided text). The University itself is administered by its own officers and authorities (Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate, Academic Council, etc.).
important_notes: The Act shall prevail over other enactments in case of conflict, as per Section 66.
The Vice-Chancellor and other officers are deemed to be public servants under Section 71.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to implement measures prescribed by the Government of India based on the recommendation of the XIII Finance Commission, as a condition precedent to the release of specific grants and debt relief measures to the State.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. It specifically deals with fiscal matters, debt management, and financial reporting within the state government.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2011, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act. It inserts a clause (g) to ensure outstanding debt at the end of specific financial years (2010-11 to 2014-15) remains within specified percentages of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product. It also inserts a proviso allowing the fiscal deficit during 2010-11 to exceed the limit for counter-recessionary measures, with a requirement to place a report before the Legislature.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by inserting a clause (c) after clause (b) in sub-section (2). This new clause mandates the inclusion of details regarding tax expenditure, compliance costs of major tax proposals, Revenue Consequences of Capital Expenditure (RCCE), assets, liabilities (explicit and implicit in public-private partnership), and the values of parameters underlying projections for receipts and expenditures in financial reports.

Substitutes sub-section (2) of Section 6 of the principal Act. It provides for the constitution of a Fiscal Management Review Committee headed by the Chief Secretary, with other Secretaries as members. This committee is to meet at least twice a year to review the fiscal and debt position of the State, progress on its fiscal correction path, and advise on corrective measures. It also introduces sub-section (2A) requiring the Minister in charge of finance to review receipt and expenditure trends, remedial measures, and place the outcome of such reviews before both Houses of the Legislature.

Substitutes the proviso in sub-section (1) of Section 11 of the principal Act. It stipulates that no order shall be made under this section after the expiry of two years from the commencement date of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2011.

important_rules: Rule 1: The outstanding debt at the end of financial years 2010-11, 2011-12, 2012-13, 2013-14, and 2014-15 shall not exceed 26.2%, 26%, 25.7%, 25.4%, and 25.2% respectively of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product for those years.

Rule 2: The fiscal deficit during the financial year 2010-11 may exceed the limit but not by more than 3.44% of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product as part of counter-recessionary measures. A report detailing these measures and expenditure must be placed before both Houses of the Legislature.

Rule 3: Financial reports must include detailed information on tax expenditure, compliance costs of major tax proposals, Revenue Consequences of Capital Expenditure (RCCE), assets, liabilities (explicit and implicit in public-private partnership), and underlying projection parameters.

Rule 4: A Fiscal Management Review Committee, headed by the Chief Secretary, must review the State's fiscal and debt position and its fiscal correction progress at least twice a year, providing advice on corrective measures.

Rule 5: The Minister in charge of finance shall review trends in receipts and expenditures against the budget, remedial measures, and place the outcome of these reviews before both Houses of the Legislature every half-year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, through its various departments and the Minister in charge of Finance.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution of review committees, mandated reporting to the legislature, and by enacting legislation that sets financial targets and responsibilities for the State Government.

duties: Duty of the State Government to ensure outstanding debt remains within specified percentages of GSDP.
Duty of the State Government to report to the Legislature on fiscal deficit deviations for counter-recessionary measures.
Duty to include comprehensive financial information in reports.
Duty of the Fiscal Management Review Committee to review fiscal and debt positions and advise corrective measures.
Duty of the Minister in charge of Finance to review financial trends and remedial measures and report to the Legislature.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Formation of a Fiscal Management Review Committee comprising the Chief Secretary and other Secretaries, which will meet twice annually to review the State's fiscal health and advise on corrective actions.
Procedure 2: Regular review by the Minister in charge of finance of budgetary trends, remedial actions, and submission of these review outcomes to the State Legislature.
Procedure 3: Reporting to the Legislature regarding any deviation in fiscal deficit for counter-recessionary measures during the 2010-11 financial year.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation and the Finance Department of the Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The provisions of Section 11 of the principal Act, as amended, will cease to apply after two years from the commencement of this Amendment Act.
The Act is based on recommendations from the XIII Finance Commission of India, concerning grants and debt relief.

title: THE NATIONAL LAW SCHOOL OF INDIA (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the National Law School of India Act, 1986, to provide for horizontal reservation of seats for students of Karnataka in the National Law School of India, Bangalore.
scope: This act applies to the National Law School of India, Bangalore, and students seeking admission to its undergraduate courses. It specifically concerns the reservation of seats for Karnataka students.

key_definitions.student of Karnataka: A student who has studied in any one of the recognized educational institutions in the State for a period of not less than ten years preceding to the qualifying examination.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The National Law School of India (Amendment) Act, 2020' and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends Section 4 of the National Law School of India Act, 1986, by inserting a new sub-section (3) which mandates that the school shall reserve twenty-five percent of seats horizontally for students of Karnataka. It also includes an explanation for the term 'student of Karnataka'.

important_rules: The National Law School of India, Bangalore, shall reserve twenty-five percent of seats horizontally for students of Karnataka.
A 'student of Karnataka' is defined as a student who has studied in a recognized educational institution in the State for at least ten years prior to the qualifying examination.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the administration of the National Law School of India, Bangalore.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By enacting the amendment to the National Law School of India Act, 1986, and by the National Law School of India, Bangalore, implementing the reservation as per the amended Act.

rights: Students of Karnataka have the right to a horizontal reservation of 25% of seats in the National Law School of India, Bangalore.
duties: The National Law School of India, Bangalore, has a duty to reserve 25% of seats horizontally for students of Karnataka.
obligations: The National Law School of India, Bangalore, is obligated to adhere to the provisions of the amended Act regarding seat reservation.

key_procedures: Insertion of a new sub-section (3) into Section 4 of the National Law School of India Act, 1986, to provide for the reservation.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is based on the precedent set by Supreme Court judgments allowing institutional preference/reservation up to 50% in undergraduate courses.
The Act draws upon Entry 25 and 26 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for the appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka towards defraying the several charges which will come in course of payment during the Financial Year 2021-22.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with the appropriation of funds for the financial year 2021-22, covering various services and purposes listed in the schedule.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation Act, 2021.

This section authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding a specified aggregate amount (Rupees 2,52,39,197.86 lakhs) from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the financial year 2021-22, towards defraying charges for services specified in the schedule.

This section states that the sums authorized to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule for the said year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act is enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature and assented to by the Governor of Karnataka. The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is involved in its administration and publication.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act authorizes the payment and appropriation of funds, implying enforcement through the state's financial and administrative machinery.

key_procedures: Authorization of payment and application of sums from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the financial year 2021-22.
Appropriation of these sums for specific services and purposes as detailed in the Schedule.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is based on Article 204 of the Constitution of India.
The schedule lists various services and their corresponding amounts (in lakhs) to be appropriated, categorized as 'Charged on the consolidated Fund' and 'Voted by the Legislative Assembly'.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATIVE SALARIES, PENSIONS AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1957 and the Karnataka Act 2 of 1955 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force on the first day of April, 2001.

In section 3 of the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 2 of 1957) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-sections (1) and (2), for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 4 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.

In section 8 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2): (i) in clause (i), for the words "two thousand" the words "five thousand" shall be substituted; (ii) in clause (ii), in the proviso, for the words "one thousand" the words "two thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 10A of the principal Act, in sub-sections (1) and (2), for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 10B of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 10E of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 10F of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 10K of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 11 of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 11A of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.
In section 11C of the principal Act, for the words "five thousand" the words "ten thousand" shall be substituted.

important_rules: Rule 1: Salaries and allowances are to be increased.
Rule 2: Specific monetary amounts in different sections of the principal Act are to be substituted with higher amounts, indicating an increase in salaries, pensions, and allowances.
Rule 3: The Act comes into force from April 1, 2001.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

administration: Not specified in the provided text.
important_notes: The amendment pertains to increases in monetary figures related to salaries, pensions, and allowances for members of the Karnataka Legislature.

The specific increases involve substituting amounts like 'five thousand' with 'ten thousand', 'two thousand' with 'five thousand', and 'one thousand' with 'two thousand' in various sections of the principal Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, to allow for the establishment of information technology or information technology enabled services, allowing women to work in such establishments during night hours, and to provide facilities for transportation and security to such women employees.
scope: The act applies to Karnataka and specifically amends the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, concerning employment of women during night hours in IT/ITeS establishments.

main_sections.description: This section states that the act is the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2002, and it will come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

This section details the amendment to Section 25 of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961. It mandates that the State Government may, by notification, exempt any establishment of Information Technology or Information Technology enabled services from the provisions of section 25 relating to employment of women during night subject to conditions that the establishment provides facilities for transportation and security to such women employees and subject to any other conditions as may be specified in the notification.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may exempt establishments providing Information Technology or Information Technology enabled services from the provisions of Section 25 (relating to night employment of women).
Rule 2: Such exemption is conditional upon the establishment providing adequate facilities for transportation and security for women employees working during night hours.
Rule 3: The exemption can also be subject to any other conditions specified by the State Government in the notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through government notifications and potentially inspections to ensure compliance with the conditions for exemption.

rights: Right of women to be employed during night hours in IT/ITeS establishments, subject to conditions.
Right of women employees to have adequate transportation and security facilities.
duties: Duty of the State Government to specify conditions for exemption.
obligations: Obligation of IT/ITeS establishments to provide adequate transportation and security for women employees working at night if they seek exemption from Section 25.
Obligation of the State Government to issue notifications for commencement and conditions of the act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government issues a notification to bring the act into force on a specified date.

Procedure 2: The State Government issues a notification specifying conditions under which IT/ITeS establishments can employ women during night hours, including provisions for transportation and security.
administration: State Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The act specifically addresses the employment of women during night hours in IT/ITeS establishments.
The amendment aims to facilitate the growth of the IT sector while ensuring the safety and well-being of women employees.

title: THE KARNATAKA SECONDARY EDUCATION EXAMINATION BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, to include Composite Junior Colleges within the definition of recognised High Schools and to add specific Directors as Ex-officio Members of the Board.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board and its functioning within the state of Karnataka. It specifically amends definitions and membership related to secondary education examinations.

key_definitions.recognised High School: The amendment expands this definition to include 'a Composite Junior College'.
key_definitions.Board: The Act amends the composition of the Board by adding new ex-officio members.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (Amendment) Act, 2002, and states that it comes into force immediately.
Amends clause (j) of section 2 of the principal Act to include 'a Composite Junior College' in the definition of a recognized High School.
Amends sub-section (4) of section 4 of the principal Act by substituting item (a) and inserting new items (db), (dc), (dd), and (de) to include specific Directors as ex-officio members of the Board.

important_rules: Rule: Composite Junior Colleges are to be considered as recognized High Schools for the purposes of the Act.
Rule: The Director, Pre-University Education or their nominee shall be an Ex-officio Member of the Board.
Rule: The Director, Directorate of State Educational Research and Training shall be an Ex-officio Member of the Board.
Rule: The Director, Secondary Education shall be an Ex-officio Member of the Board.
Rule: The Director of the Board in charge of other Examinations shall be an Ex-officio Member of the Board.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board and relevant educational authorities in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendment and enforcement of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966. This involves legislative processes including passing the bill and receiving the Governor's assent.
Procedure: Inclusion of new members in the Board. The Act mandates the addition of specific Directors as ex-officio members.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is involved in the legislative process, and the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board administers the Act.
important_notes: Note: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966 (Karnataka Act 16 of 1966).
Note: The amendments aim to reflect changes in the educational structure by recognizing Composite Junior Colleges and expanding the Board's membership to include key educational directors.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROHIBITION OF CHARGING EXORBITANT INTEREST ACT, 2004
purpose: To prohibit the charging of exorbitant interest by any person and to provide for stringent punishment thereof, with the objective of obviating difficulties experienced by the public, particularly farmers, who are falling prey to exorbitant interest rates.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to any person charging exorbitant interest on loans.

key_definitions.debtor: A person who receives loan for exorbitant interest.
key_definitions.exorbitant_interest: Charging of interest on hourly basis, daily basis, installment basis, monthly basis or in any other form which works out to be an interest at a rate more than that fixed by the State Government under section 28 of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961.
key_definitions.loan: An advance of money given to a debtor for exorbitant interest.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and its commencement date (deemed to have come into force on September 5, 2003).

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'debtor', 'exorbitant interest', and 'loan'. It also states that undefined words and expressions will have the meanings assigned in the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961.
Explicitly prohibits any person from charging exorbitant interest on any loan advanced by them.

Specifies the punishment for contravening Section 3 or molesting/abetting molestation of a debtor for loan recovery. The penalty includes imprisonment up to three years and/or a fine up to thirty thousand rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of money and presentation of petition to court and the procedure thereof
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for a debtor to deposit the due amount (principal plus interest at the government-fixed rate) with the court and file a petition to record satisfaction of the loan. The court will issue notice to the lender and pass orders after inquiry.

Empowers the court to order the restoration of possession of any movable or immovable property that was forcibly taken by a person towards repayment of a loan or its interest, upon a petition by the debtor.

Provides a window of one month from the Act's publication for persons charging exorbitant interest to file a petition disclosing their intention to charge only the government-fixed rate. Such disclosure prevents prosecution for offenses under the Act for that loan.
Allows the court, upon a debtor's petition, to order the adjustment of any interest paid over and above the government-fixed rate towards the principal loan amount.

Deems a person who advanced a loan to have abetted the commission of suicide by a debtor or a family member, if such suicide occurred immediately after the debtor or family member was subjected to molestation by the lender. The burden of proof to the contrary lies with the lender.
Specifies a fixed court fee of fifty rupees for any petition filed under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to be in derogation to other laws
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other existing laws. It also specifies that certain provisions of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961 are not applicable to offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of provisions of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961 are applicable mutatis mutandis to persons referred to in Section 3 of this Act, subject to this Act's provisions. It also clarifies that if an act constitutes an offense under both Acts, prosecution will be under this Act.
Prohibits any action to recover a loan against a debtor who is a farmer or agricultural laborer for a period of one year from the Act's commencement.

Repeals the Karnataka Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Ordinance, 2003, and states that anything done or action taken under that Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: No person shall charge interest on any loan at a rate exceeding that fixed by the State Government under section 28 of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961.
Molesting or abetting the molestation of a debtor for loan recovery is prohibited.
Debtors can deposit the loan amount with interest (at the government-fixed rate) into court and seek satisfaction of the loan.
Lenders charging exorbitant interest have one month from the Act's publication to voluntarily disclose their intention to charge only the government-fixed rate, to avoid prosecution.
Interest paid above the government-fixed rate can be adjusted towards the principal loan amount.
No recovery action against farmers or agricultural laborers for one year from the Act's commencement.

penalties: Contravention of Section 3 (charging exorbitant interest) or molesting/abetting molestation of a debtor: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also with fine which may extend to thirty thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts are empowered to hear petitions and pass orders related to loan satisfaction, property restoration, and adjustment of interest. Prosecution for offenses would be handled through the judicial system.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court procedures initiated by debtors, voluntary disclosures by lenders, and penalties for violations. The Act also integrates with the enforcement mechanisms of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961 where applicable.

rights: Debtors have the right to file a petition to deposit money and record loan satisfaction.
Debtors have the right to petition for the restoration of forcibly taken property.
Debtors have the right to have excess interest adjusted towards the loan principal.
Farmers and agricultural laborers have the right to a deferment of loan repayment for one year.
duties: Lenders have a duty not to charge exorbitant interest.
Lenders have a duty not to molest or abet the molestation of debtors for loan recovery.
Lenders have a duty to comply with court orders regarding loan satisfaction and property restoration.
obligations: Lenders charging exorbitant interest have an obligation to make a voluntary disclosure within one month of the Act's publication if they wish to avoid prosecution.
Debtors have an obligation to deposit the correct amount of money when petitioning for loan satisfaction.

key_procedures: Debtor files a petition with the court, depositing principal and interest (at the government-fixed rate), to record loan satisfaction.
Court issues notice to the lender to reply within 15 days.
Court conducts an inquiry and passes an order for full or partial satisfaction of the loan.
Debtor files a petition for restoration of property forcibly taken by the lender.
Person charging exorbitant interest files a petition for voluntary disclosure within one month of publication.
Court adjusts excess interest paid by the debtor towards the loan principal upon petition.
administration: The Act is administered through the judicial system (Courts) and potentially through departments responsible for money lending regulations in Karnataka, in conjunction with the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 5, 2003.
The Karnataka Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Ordinance, 2003, has been repealed but actions taken under it are saved.
The provisions of this Act are in addition to other laws.
Specific sections of the Karnataka Money Lenders Act, 1961 are explicitly excluded from applying to offenses under this Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA EXCISE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To make the excise law more stringent in order to net more revenue, check evasion of excise duties, by taking away the existing compounding powers and making the law more stringent by rendering the offences under the Act cognizable and non-bailable.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965. It applies to the state of Karnataka and deals with matters related to excise duties and offences under the Excise Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the act may be called the Karnataka Excise (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it comes into force at once.

This section amends section 29 of the principal Act. It changes the discretion to cancel or suspend a license or permit to a mandatory cancellation, with exceptions for certain contraventions of sub-section (1) of section 36. It also mandates that a license or permit shall not be cancelled or suspended without giving an opportunity of being heard.

This section amends section 32 of the principal Act by increasing the imprisonment term and fine amounts for offences under sub-sections (1) and (2), including increased minimum rigorous imprisonment and fine amounts in the provisos.
This section amends section 33 of the principal Act by increasing the imprisonment term and fine amounts, including increased minimum rigorous imprisonment and fine amounts in the provisos.
This section amends section 34 of the principal Act by increasing the imprisonment term and fine amounts, including increased minimum imprisonment and fine amounts in the provisos.

This section amends section 37 of the principal Act by significantly increasing the imprisonment term and fine amounts for offences under sub-sections (1) and (2), including increased minimum imprisonment and fine amounts in the provisos.
