This section substitutes sub-section (1) of section 45 of the principal Act, empowering specified Excise Officers to accept a sum of money as compensation for offences under sub-section (3) of section 32 and sub-section (1) of section 36 (excluding certain clauses), with specified minimum and maximum amounts.
This section omits sections 45A and 45B of the Principal Act.
This section amends section 49 of the principal Act by increasing the imprisonment term and fine amounts for offences.

important_rules: Rule: Licenses or permits shall not be cancelled or suspended without giving an opportunity of being heard to the licensee or permit holder.
Rule: Offences under certain sections (amended by this Act) are made cognizable and non-bailable, as indicated by the increased penalties and removal of compounding powers.

penalties: Increased imprisonment terms and fine amounts for offences under sections 32, 33, 34, 37, and 49.
Minimum fine amounts are stipulated for compounding of offences under section 45.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or any Excise Officer specially empowered.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of increased fines and imprisonment, mandatory cancellation or suspension of licenses/permits in certain cases, and acceptance of compensation for certain offences.

rights: Right of the licensee or permit holder to be heard before cancellation or suspension of a license or permit.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, as amended.
Duty to pay excise duties and adhere to license/permit conditions.
obligations: Obligation to face enhanced penalties for excise offences.
Obligation for authorized officers to provide an opportunity of being heard before cancelling or suspending a license/permit.

key_procedures: Procedure for cancellation or suspension of licenses/permits: An opportunity of being heard must be provided to the licensee/permit holder. Mandatory cancellation is prescribed for certain contraventions, with discretion to cancel/suspend for others.
Procedure for compounding of offences: Specified Excise Officers may accept a sum of money as compensation for certain offences, with minimum and maximum limits for the compensation amount.
administration: Department of Excise, Government of Karnataka (implied through the principal Act and the context of excise laws).
important_notes: The Act aims to make excise laws more stringent to increase revenue and curb evasion.
Existing compounding powers for certain offences have been removed or modified.
Offences under the amended Act are intended to be cognizable and non-bailable.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend section 4 of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to raise the fiscal deficit to 4 percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product for the year 2009-10 as a one-time relaxation.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. It specifically addresses fiscal deficit targets for the financial year 2009-10.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Second Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it is deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2009.

Amends sub-section (3) of Section 4 of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, by inserting a proviso that the fiscal deficit during the financial year 2009-10 shall not exceed four percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product.

important_rules: The fiscal deficit during the financial year 2009-10 shall not exceed four percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement is implied to be by the State Government of Karnataka through the mechanisms established by the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. Specific enforcement authorities are not detailed in this amendment.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the monitoring and reporting mechanisms under the parent Act, with the primary enforcement being the adherence to the amended fiscal deficit limit.

duties: The State Government has a duty to ensure that the fiscal deficit does not exceed the prescribed limit for the financial year 2009-10.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory). The overall administration of fiscal responsibility lies with the Finance Department of the Government of Karnataka, as per the parent act.
important_notes: This is a second amendment to the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002.
The amendment is a 'one-time relaxation' for the financial year 2009-10.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on July 31, 2009.

title: THE AZIM PREMJI UNIVERSITY ACT, 2010
purpose: To establish and incorporate in the State of Karnataka a University in the private sector to promote, conceptualize and bring about a paradigm shift through the development of outstanding leadership, research, knowledge and ideas for education and allied development sectors.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to the establishment and functioning of the Azim Premji University. The university may have campuses, regional centers, and study centers anywhere in India or overseas, subject to the permission of the concerned government. The university's focus is on teaching, training, research, and development in elementary education, secondary education, education management, finance, and technology in education, particularly in science, social science, humanities, and management.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University as specified in section 24.
key_definitions.agenda_matters: Matters and business to be designated in the Statutes each of which can be either included in the Agenda or be taken up for discussion and decision at a meeting of the Board of Governors or the Board of Management or any Committees, only subject to the prior written approval of the Chancellor.
key_definitions.board_of_governors: The Board of Governors of the University as specified in section 22.
key_definitions.board_of_management: The Board of Management of the University as specified in section 23.
key_definitions.foundation: The Azim Premji Foundation, registered under section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956, or any other Foundation formed and registered by Mr. Azim Premji for this purpose.
key_definitions.sponsoring_authority_or_sponsoring_body: The Foundation, in relation to this Act.
key_definitions.university: The Azim Premji University established and incorporated under section 4.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Azim Premji University Act, 2010, that it extends to the whole of Karnataka, and that it is deemed to have come into force from November 24, 2009.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Agenda Matters', 'Board of Governors', 'Board of Management', 'Chancellor', 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Pro Vice-Chancellor', 'Campus', 'Committees', 'Constituent College', 'Distance Education', 'Distance Education Committee', 'Finance Committee', 'Foundation', 'Government', 'National Accreditation bodies', 'Prescribed', 'Principal', 'Registrar', 'Regional Centre', 'Sponsoring Authority' or 'Sponsoring Body', 'State', 'Statutes' and 'Regulations', 'Study Centre', 'Teacher', 'University Grants Commission', 'University', and 'Visitor'.

main_sections.section_title: Proposal for the establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Foundation to propose the establishment of the University to the State Government, including the required particulars for the proposal and the constitution of a Screening Committee.

Details the process by which the State Government can sanction the establishment of the Azim Premji University after considering the screening committee's recommendations. It also specifies the headquarters, potential for campuses and centers, the University as a body corporate, and the vesting of its properties.

Declares the University as self-financing and generally not entitled to maintenance grants or financial assistance from the State. However, it allows for financial support for specific research, development activities, or for the benefit of similar universities, and permits the university to receive financial support from any other source.
States that the University shall employ a broad range of strategies to achieve its vision and objectives, including providing instruction and teaching.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (implied through the establishment and oversight process)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including proposal scrutiny, sanctioning, and potential rule-making by the State Government.

rights: The Foundation has the right to establish the University.
The University has the right to establish constituent colleges, regional centers, and study centers.
The University has the right to receive financial support from any other source.
The University has the right to sue and be sued in its name.
duties: The University shall provide instruction, teaching, research, and development.
The University's land, building, and other properties shall not be used for any other purpose.
The Foundation must provide detailed particulars in its proposal for establishing the University.
obligations: The Foundation must establish the Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund before the University can be sanctioned.
The University must adhere to the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Proposal for establishment: The Foundation submits a detailed proposal to the State Government, which is then examined by a Screening Committee.
Establishment of the University: Upon satisfaction with the proposal and establishment of the Endowment Fund, the State Government issues a notification sanctioning the University.
Constitution of University bodies: The Act outlines the structure and powers of various authorities of the University, such as the Board of Governors, Board of Management, and Academic Council.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka is involved in the establishment and oversight of the University. Specific administrative functions within the university are managed by its officers and authorities (e.g., Registrar, Board of Governors, Board of Management).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from November 24, 2009.
The University is primarily self-financing, with limited provisions for state financial assistance.
The University may establish campuses, regional centers, and study centers anywhere in India or overseas, subject to the permission of the concerned government.

title: THE KARNATAKA OFFICIAL LANGUAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend Section 5A of the Karnataka Official Language Act, 1963, to simplify the procedure for publication of Kannada translations of official documents by empowering the State Government instead of the Governor to authorize such translations in public interest.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Official Language Act, 1963. It concerns the authoritative translation of Central and State Acts, Ordinances, rules, regulations, bye-laws, schemes, and orders into the Kannada language.

key_definitions.authoritative text: A translation in Kannada Language published under the authority of the Governor or the State Government in the Official Gazette, which is considered the definitive version of the original text in Kannada.
key_definitions.Official Gazette: The official publication of the government where legal and administrative notices are published.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2020, and states that it comes into force immediately upon enactment.
Replaces Section 5A of the Karnataka Official Language Act, 1963, with new provisions regarding the authorization of Kannada translations.

important_rules: Rule 1: Translations of Central Acts, Presidential Ordinances (related to List III of Seventh Schedule), State Acts, and Governor's Ordinances published under the Governor's authority in the Official Gazette are deemed authoritative Kannada translations.

Rule 2: Translations of rules, regulations, bye-laws, schemes, and orders issued by the State Government (under the Constitution, Central Act, State Act, or other law) published under the State Government's authority in the Official Gazette are deemed authoritative Kannada translations.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Governor (as per the amended Section 5A). The specific enforcement authority for violations related to this act is not detailed within the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ensuring that translations published in the Official Gazette under the specified authorities are considered authoritative.

rights: The right to have official documents translated into Kannada which are recognized as authoritative.
duties: The duty of the Governor's office to authorize translations of certain legal instruments in the Official Gazette.
The duty of the State Government to authorize translations of its issued rules, regulations, etc., in the Official Gazette.

key_procedures: Procedure: To publish a Kannada translation of a Central Act, Presidential Ordinance, State Act, or Governor's Ordinance in the Official Gazette under the authority of the Governor.
Procedure: To publish a Kannada translation of rules, regulations, bye-laws, schemes, or orders issued by the State Government in the Official Gazette under the authority of the State Government.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment aims to simplify the procedure by empowering the State Government, replacing the requirement for the Governor's approval for translations of State Government's own issuances.
The act is enacted under Article 345 of the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION (NO.2) ACT, 2021
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Services of the Financial year 2020-21.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka and pertains to the financial year 2020-21.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation (No.2) Act, 2021.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 1315825.53 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2020-21
main_sections.description: Authorizes payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees Thirteen thousand one hundred and fifty eight crore twenty five lakhs and fifty three thousand, towards defraying charges during the Financial Year 2020-21 for specified services.

States that the sums authorized to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule for the said year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor of Karnataka (assent granted)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative enactment and subsequent implementation via the State Legislature and relevant government departments.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Legislative introduction of a Bill to authorize appropriation from the Consolidated Fund.
Procedure 2: Obtaining assent from the Governor of Karnataka for the Bill to become an Act.
Procedure 3: Publication of the Act in the Official Gazette for public notification.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (likely involved in drafting and promulgation)
important_notes: The act is introduced in pursuance of Article 205(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.
The total appropriation includes both sums voted by the Legislative Assembly and sums charged on the Consolidated Fund.
The schedule details appropriations for various services and purposes, categorized into Revenue and Capital expenses.

title: THE KARNATAKA EXCISE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: This act amends the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, to allow for further amendment of certain sections and to bring it in line with the second schedule of the Finance Act, 1999.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends specific sections of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Excise (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

After section 15 of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, the following section 15A shall be inserted: Section 15A: Consumption or Use of Liquor in public place. No person shall consume or use liquor in any public place.

After section 24 of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, the following section 24A shall be inserted: Section 24A: Grant of exclusive or other privilege in respect of. (1) The Excise Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner may subject to such rules as may be prescribed grant to any person the exclusive or other privilege for the whole State or for any local area, or for the purpose of manufacturing or by wholesale or by retail or for bottling or for a fixed or agreed rate or sum.
This section is mentioned as being amended, but the specific details of the amendment are not provided in the given text extract.
This section is mentioned as being amended, but the specific details of the amendment are not provided in the given text extract.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall consume or use liquor in any public place.

Rule 2: The Excise Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner may grant exclusive or other privileges for the whole State or any local area for manufacturing, wholesale, retail, bottling, or for a fixed or agreed rate or sum.
Rule 3: The grant of such privileges is subject to prescribed rules.

penalties: For the purposes of section 15A: public passenger vehicle, means a vehicle used for carrying passengers for hire or reward, whether the owner or operator of the vehicle is a private person or a State Government or any other person. Violation includes any public place, any place of business, or any private residence not including any private residence in which the business is conducted.

For the purposes of section 24A: Grant of exclusive or other privilege. The Excise Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner may grant such privileges. The grant of such privileges is subject to prescribed rules and may be granted for a fixed or agreed rate or sum.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Excise Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the grant of exclusive or other privileges and by prescribing rules for such grants. Enforcement also occurs through penalties associated with the consumption of liquor in public places and the illicit manufacturing, sale, or transport of liquor.

rights: Right to obtain exclusive or other privileges for liquor trade as granted by the Excise Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner.
Right to consume liquor in private residences (with certain limitations regarding business conducted there).
duties: Duty not to consume or use liquor in any public place.
Duty to comply with rules prescribed for the grant of exclusive or other privileges.
Duty not to engage in illicit manufacture, sale, or transport of liquor.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of any granted privilege.
Obligation to not engage in activities that are prohibited under the Act, such as illicit liquor trade or consumption in public places.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining exclusive or other privileges for liquor trade: Application to the Excise Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner, subject to prescribed rules. The privilege may be granted for a fixed or agreed rate or sum.
Procedure for amendments to the Act: Insertion of new sections and amendment of existing sections as specified in the Act.
administration: The Excise Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner are responsible for administration and granting privileges. The State Government is responsible for appointing commencement dates.
important_notes: The Act aims to further amend the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965.
Section 15A prohibits the consumption or use of liquor in any public place.
Section 24A allows for the grant of exclusive or other privileges for liquor trade.
The Act mentions amendments to sections 32 and 45, but the details are not fully provided in the extract.
The Act brings into force amendments based on the Finance Act, 1999.

title: THE KARNATAKA CIVIL SERVICES (PENSION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1957, to provide that no guaranteed compassionate family pension shall be charged in respect of compassionate family pensions extended during the period from 1st April, 2002 to 31st March, 2002.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka state and specifically to the Karnataka Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1957, concerning the provision of compassionate family pensions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Civil Services (Pension) (Amendment) Act, 2002. It shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the first day of April, 2001.

In section 3 of the Karnataka Civil Services (Pension) (Amendment) Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 11 of 1957), after sub-section (2), the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:- Provided that no guaranteed compassionate family pension shall be charged in respect of compassionate family pensions extended during the period from the first day of April, 2001 to the thirty-first day of March, 2002.

important_rules: No guaranteed compassionate family pension shall be charged in respect of compassionate family pensions extended during the period from 1st April, 2001 to 31st March, 2002.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Karnataka State Government and its administrative departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administration and application of the amended pension rules by the relevant government authorities.

rights: Right to receive compassionate family pension without the charge of guaranteed compassionate family pension for the specified period.
duties: Duty of the State Government to ensure the implementation of this amendment.
obligations: Obligation for the relevant departments to process compassionate family pensions according to the amended rules.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 3 of the Karnataka Civil Services (Pension) (Amendment) Act, 1957. Insertion of a proviso to ensure no charge for guaranteed compassionate family pension for the period 1st April 2001 to 31st March 2002.
administration: Karnataka State Government, Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from 1st April, 2001.
The amendment specifically addresses the period between 1st April, 2001, and 31st March, 2002.

title: THE KARNATAKA EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (PROHIBITION OF CAPITATION FEE) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Educational Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee) Act, 1984, to expand the definition of 'Educational Institution' to include those established under any law for the time being in force, thereby covering universities established after the original Act.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Educational Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee) Act, 1984. It applies to educational institutions in Karnataka that confer degrees. The amendment specifically broadens the definition of educational institutions covered by the Act.

key_definitions.educational institution: An institution leading to a degree conferred by a university established under any law for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Educational Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee) (Amendment) Act, 2002, and that it comes into force at once.

Amends clause (c) of section 2 of the principal Act (Karnataka Act 37 of 1984). It substitutes the existing definition of 'Educational Institution' (referring only to universities under the Karnataka State Universities Act, 1976) with a broader definition that includes universities established under any law for the time being in force.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authority responsible for enforcing the original Karnataka Educational Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee) Act, 1984.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the Secretary's signature). The original Act is administered by the relevant education department.
important_notes: The amendment aims to rectify an omission in the original Act of 1984, which did not cover degrees conferred by universities established by later legislation like the Kannada University Act, 1991, Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992, Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences Act, 1994, and Visveswaraiah Technological University Act, 1994.
The amendment is retrospective, meaning it shall be and shall be deemed always to have been substituted.

title: THE NATIONAL LAW SCHOOL OF INDIA (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the National Law School of India Act, 1986, to change the nomenclature of the post of 'Director' and 'Visitor' to 'Vice-Chancellor' and 'Chancellor' respectively, aligning it with other Universities.
scope: This act applies to the National Law School of India University established under the National Law School of India Act, 1986 (Karnataka Act 22 of 1986).

key_definitions.vice_chancellor: Means the Vice-Chancellor of the School.
key_definitions.chancellor: Means the Chancellor of the School.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the National Law School of India (Amendment) Act, 2004, and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act (National Law School of India Act, 1986) by substituting the definitions for 'Vice Chancellor' and 'Chancellor'.
Mandates the substitution of the words 'Visitor' and 'Director' with 'Chancellor' and 'Vice Chancellor' respectively, wherever they appear in the principal Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative enactment and publication in the official gazette.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
The definitions of 'Vice Chancellor' and 'Chancellor' in Section 2 of the principal Act are amended.
The terms 'Visitor' and 'Director' are replaced with 'Chancellor' and 'Vice Chancellor' throughout the principal Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment is based on a suggestion to align the nomenclature of the 'Director' and 'Visitor' with 'Vice-Chancellor' and 'Chancellor' to be on par with other Universities.
The Act is enacted during the fifty-fifth year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the Fourth day of March, 2004.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on the Sixth day of March, 2004.

title: THE KARNATAKA ADVOCATES WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Advocates Welfare Fund Act, 1983, by introducing new provisions and modifying existing ones to enhance the welfare fund for advocates.
scope: The Act applies to advocates practicing in the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Advocates Welfare Fund Act, 1983.

key_definitions.interlocutory_application: Includes all applications filed before any Court, Tribunal or Authority in respect of any pending or disposed of case or proceeding.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and outlines that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by inserting a definition for 'interlocutory application' and modifying a reference to other sections.
Amends Section 15 of the principal Act concerning admission fees, late fees, and periodic declarations by members.
Amends Section 16 of the principal Act concerning amounts payable to members upon cessation of practice, with different provisions based on enrollment date and age.
Amends Section 18 of the principal Act by omitting clause (b).
Amends Section 23 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1A) regarding the affixing of Welfare Fund stamps on interlocutory applications.
Amends Section 23A of the principal Act concerning contributions by designated Senior Advocates and consequences of non-payment.

important_rules: Every Advocate practicing in Karnataka must be a member of the Fund.
Advocates enrolled on or after the commencement of the Amendment Act, 2004, or those already enrolled, must pay an admission fee of rupees two thousand.
A late fee of rupees fifty per month or part of a month may be levied for delayed payment of admission fees from April 2, 1997.
Every member must pay a fee of rupees five hundred every five years from their enrollment date.
Failure to pay the five-year fee can result in deemed suspension of practice.
Welfare Fund stamps of the value of rupees five must be affixed on every interlocutory application.
Designated Senior Advocates must pay their contribution by March 31st annually, with a grace period and late fee.

penalties: Late fee of rupees fifty per month or part of a month for delayed admission fee payment.
Penalty of fifty rupees per month for late payment of the five-year fee, up to a certain limit.
Late fee of rupees one hundred per month or part of a month, subject to a maximum of rupees five hundred, for delayed contribution by Senior Advocates.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Karnataka State Bar Council (implied through its role in enrollment and administration of the fund).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification of commencement dates, levy of fees and penalties, and deeming suspension of practice for non-compliance.

rights: Right to receive amounts from the fund upon cessation of practice (under specified conditions).
Right to have practice not be construed as deemed suspension if late fees are paid within the provided grace periods.
duties: Duty to become a member of the Fund.
Duty to pay admission fee.
Duty to pay periodic fees (every five years).
Duty to pay Welfare Fund stamps on interlocutory applications.
Duty to pay contributions as a Senior Advocate by the due date.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the principal Act.
Obligation to file declarations as prescribed.

key_procedures: Enrollment as an Advocate and subsequent payment of admission fee within one month.
Payment of a periodic fee (rupees 500) every five years from the date of becoming a member.
Payment of Welfare Fund stamp (rupees 5) on interlocutory applications.
Payment of annual contribution by Senior Advocates by March 31st, with a grace period for payment up to six months with late fees.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the Karnataka State Bar Council (implied).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Advocates Welfare Fund Act, 1983.
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
Provisions regarding admission fees have different applicability based on enrollment dates.
The Act introduces the concept of 'deemed suspension of practice' for non-compliance with fee payments.
Specific provisions exist for Senior Advocates regarding their contributions.

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC PREMISES (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, to extend its provisions to Co-operative Societies and Federations of Co-operative Societies established by law in the State in which Government Property or Share is involved.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, specifically to include Co-operative Societies and Federations of Co-operative Societies where Government Property or share is involved.

key_definitions.public_premises: Defined in the Principal Act (Karnataka Act 32 of 1974) and now extended to include Co-operative Societies or Federations of Co-operative Societies established under any law in force in the State in which the Government Property or share is involved.
key_definitions.unauthorised_occupant: Implied to be persons occupying public premises without proper authorization, subject to eviction under the Principal Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) (Second Amendment) Act, 2005, and it comes into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, by inserting a new item (viii) to clause (e), thereby including Co-operative Societies or Federations of Co-operative Societies established under any law in force in the State in which the Government Property or share is involved within the definition of 'public premises'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Principal Act, Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, likely designates an 'authorized officer' for eviction proceedings. This amendment does not specify a new enforcement authority but extends the scope of the existing one.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures outlined in the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, for the eviction of unauthorised occupants from public premises.

rights: The right for the Government to evict unauthorised occupants from public premises, now extended to include those occupying premises of specified Co-operative Societies and Federations.
duties: Duty of Co-operative Societies and Federations of Co-operative Societies to ensure their premises are occupied lawfully, especially when Government Property or share is involved.
obligations: Obligation of unauthorised occupants to vacate public premises upon being served notice as per the Principal Act.

key_procedures: The amendment itself is a procedural change to the Principal Act. The procedures for eviction under the Principal Act would involve serving notice to unauthorised occupants and subsequent eviction proceedings.
administration: The administration would fall under the purview of the relevant department responsible for public premises and legislation in Karnataka, as indicated by the Secretary to Government, Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation.
important_notes: This is an amendment act, further amending the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974.
The amendment specifically targets Co-operative Societies and Federations where Government Property or share is involved, not all Co-operative Societies.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, primarily to establish the Davanagere University with headquarters at Davanagere and territorial jurisdiction over the districts of Davanagere and Chitradurga, and to redefine the jurisdiction of existing universities.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, and its provisions are relevant to educational institutions and students within the territorial jurisdiction of the universities in Karnataka, with a specific focus on the newly established Davanagere University and its affiliated colleges.

key_definitions.Principal Act: The Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 (Karnataka Act 29 of 2001).
key_definitions.Davanagere University: A university to be established with headquarters at Davanagere and territorial jurisdiction over the districts of Davanagere and Chitradurga.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2009, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act to omit 'Chitradurga, Davanagere' from the existing clause (d) and inserts a new sub-section (1C) establishing the Davanagere University.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act to insert a new sub-section (4) regarding the privileges of colleges/educational institutions in Chitradurga and Davanagere districts, deeming them withdrawn from Kuvempu University and affiliated to Davanagere University.
Amends Section 14 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso that the first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University shall be appointed by the State Government.
Outlines the powers and functions of a Special Officer appointed by the State Government to establish Davanagere University until the first Vice-Chancellor is appointed.
Specifies the duties of the first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University to arrange for the constitution of its authorities within six months (extendable to one year) of the Act's commencement.

Addresses transitional arrangements, including the first Vice-Chancellor discharging functions and existing Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Rules of Kuvempu University being deemed applicable to Davanagere University until new ones are made.
Provides for students already studying for degrees of Kuvempu University to continue their examinations with Kuvempu University and for pending examination results or degree conferrals.
Empowers the State Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, within two years of its commencement.

important_rules: Colleges or educational institutions situated in Chitradurga and Davanagere districts that enjoyed privileges from Kuvempu University before the commencement of this Amendment Act shall be deemed to be admitted to the privileges of, or affiliated to, Davanagere University.
The first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University shall be appointed by the State Government.
The first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University must arrange for the constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities within six months of the Act's commencement.

Existing Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Rules made by Kuvempu University applicable to colleges affiliated to Davanagere University shall continue to be in force until Davanagere University makes its own.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders published in the Official Gazette, and the establishment and functioning of the Davanagere University.

rights: Colleges and educational institutions in Davanagere and Chitradurga districts have the right to be affiliated with Davanagere University.
Students studying for degrees at Kuvempu University before the amendment have the right to complete their examinations and receive degrees/diplomas from Kuvempu University.
duties: The first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University has the duty to constitute the university's authorities.
The State Government has the duty to appoint the first Vice-Chancellor of Davanagere University.
obligations: Educational institutions previously affiliated with Kuvempu University in the specified districts are obligated to transition to Davanagere University's affiliation.
The State Government is obligated to make provisions for the establishment of Davanagere University.

key_procedures: Establishment of Davanagere University by the State Government.
Appointment of the first Vice-Chancellor for Davanagere University by the State Government.
Constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities of Davanagere University by its first Vice-Chancellor within six months to one year of the Act's commencement.
Transition of affiliation of colleges from Kuvempu University to Davanagere University.
Removal of difficulties by the State Government through orders published in the Official Gazette.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (implied by the signatory of the Act), and the State Government for overall implementation and appointment of authorities.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date notified by the State Government.
Any difficulty in giving effect to the Act must be resolved by the State Government via order, but no such order can be made after two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE BANGALORE WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE AND CERTAIN OTHER LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964, the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999, based on recommendations from a review committee aimed at adopting best practices for the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board.
scope: The Act primarily amends the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964, extending its provisions to the whole of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area. It also amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999.

key_definitions.apartment: A part of a property intended for independent use, including one or more rooms on one or more floors, for residential purposes, with direct exit to a public street, road, or highway, or a common area leading to one.
key_definitions.bangalore_metropolitan_area: The area within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and such other adjacent areas as the State Government may specify by notification.
key_definitions.bruhat_bangalore_mahanagara: The areas falling within the jurisdiction of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike.
key_definitions.building: Includes residential buildings, houses, outhouses, apartments, high-rise buildings, commercial buildings, temporary structures, industrial buildings, stables, latrines, urinals, sheds, huts, or any other structure made of various materials, but excludes portable shelters.
key_definitions.high_rise_building: Buildings having more than four floors (ground floor + 3 floors and above). Multistoried buildings are also known as high-rise buildings.
key_definitions.pro_rata_charges: Proportionate charges levied by the Board for the cost of improvement of water supply and sewerage systems, payable by the owner, occupier, or developer of any building.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage and Certain Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2009, and it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by substituting definitions for 'Apartment', 'Bangalore Metropolitan Area', 'Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara', 'Building', 'high rise building', and inserting definitions for 'Mahanagara Palike' and 'Pro-rata charges'.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act regarding the composition of the Board, specifying the number of members (not less than three and not more than nine), and disqualifies members of Parliament, State Legislature, or any local authority from being appointed to the Board.

Amends Section 12 of the principal Act to specify the appointment of staff, including the Chief Administrative Officer cum Secretary, Engineer in Chief, Chief Engineers, Sanitary Engineers, Water Supply Engineers, and other officers. It requires prior approval of the State Government for appointments of key positions.
Amends Section 15 of the principal Act to empower the Board to insist on owners, occupiers, or builders adopting water conservation methods like rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling.

Amends Section 16 of the principal Act, allowing the Board to levy rates, fees, rentals, pro-rata charges, deposits, taxes, and other charges to cover operating expenses, taxes, interest payments, maintenance, depreciation, loan repayments, and finance improvements for water supply and sewage disposal.
Inserts a new Section 24C granting the Board the power to write off irrecoverable amounts, with the sanction of the State Government required for amounts exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees.
Amends Section 61 of the principal Act, adding a provision to insist on rainwater harvesting systems for water conservation and increasing the monetary penalties for certain offenses.

Amends Section 62 of the principal Act to include imprisonment as a penalty for certain offenses and revises the penalty table for various violations, increasing fines significantly and introducing daily fines for some offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to exempt buildings of the Board from property taxes.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999, to appoint specific officers from the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board and KUWSS Board as appropriate authorities.

important_rules: Owners or occupiers/builders must adopt water conservation methods like rainwater harvesting and recycling of wastewater for non-potable or potable purposes (Section 15).

No building, wall, or structure shall be erected over any Board's water main; a minimum clearance of 1.0 meter or half the pipe diameter, whichever is greater, must be maintained from structures to pipelines (Section 29).
The Board may require owners, lessees, or occupants to obtain water supply from Board mains if available within 35 meters of a super structure (Section 32).

Water supply may be cut off on requisition from a statutory authority due to violation of statutory provisions by the owner, occupier, or developer, after a notice of at least seven days, unless it involves contamination (Section 53).
Rainwater harvesting systems are to be insisted upon for water conservation (Section 61).

penalties: Increased monetary penalties for various offenses under the Act, with some offenses now punishable with imprisonment up to six months.

Specific maximum fines and daily fines are outlined for violations related to trespassing, failure to maintain connections, occupying premises without proper water supply, use of water for non-domestic purposes, waste or misuse of water, refusal of admittance, improper laying of pipes or construction of latrines near pipes, execution of work by unlicensed plumbers, and willful or neglectful acts relating to water works.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board and designated authorities under the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for offenses, imposition of fines and imprisonment, and enforcement of mandatory requirements for water conservation and infrastructure.

rights: Right to receive water supply from Board mains if available within specified distance (Section 32).
Right to have water supply continued unless cut off under specific conditions (Section 53).
duties: Duty to adopt water conservation methods like rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling.
Duty to maintain house connections in conformity with regulations.
Duty to comply with requisitions to make house connections.
Duty not to waste or misuse water.
Duty to grant admittance to authorized persons.
Duty to ensure proper laying of water pipes and construction of latrines to prevent injury or pollution.
Duty to employ licensed plumbers for work.
Duty for licensed plumbers not to demand more than prescribed charges and not to contravene regulations.
obligations: Obligation for owners/occupiers/developers to comply with water conservation mandates.
Obligation to ensure structures do not encroach upon or pose a risk to water mains.
Obligation to obtain water supply when required by the Board.
Obligation to adhere to regulations regarding plumbing and water works.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining water supply: Notice issued by the Board requiring owners, lessees, or occupants to obtain supply if a main is within 35 meters (Section 32).
Procedure for cutting off water supply: Notice of at least seven days given to the owner/occupier, unless in cases of contamination (Section 53).
administration: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board, and relevant departments under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Karnataka Ground Water (Regulation for Protection of Sources of Drinking Water) Act, 1999.
important_notes: The Act amends multiple existing laws to achieve its objectives.
The scope of the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act is extended to the entire Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area.
The Board's powers are enhanced regarding water conservation and enforcement of regulations.
Financial powers related to levying charges and writing off amounts are modified.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend certain taxation laws in force in the State of Karnataka, including extending the application of certain acts, omitting redundant provisions, repealing certain enactments, and giving effect to budget proposals.
scope: The act amends various taxation laws applicable within the State of Karnataka. Specifically, it extends the application of the Betting Tax Act, 1932 and the Mysore Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952 to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It also amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, and the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.

key_definitions.Additional Commissioner: Means the Additional Commissioner of Commercial Taxes appointed under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957 or the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003. This definition is inserted into the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958 and the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2011 and it shall come into force from April 1, 2011.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Mysore Act IX of 1932
main_sections.description: Amends the Betting Tax Act, 1932 by extending its application to the whole of Karnataka, substituting section 3-A for payment of totalisator tax by way of composition, and omitting sections 12, 13, and 14.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Mysore Act VIII of 1952
main_sections.description: Amends the Mysore Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952 by substituting 'Karnataka' for 'Mysore' in the title, long title, preamble, and section 1, and omitting sections 12, 13, 14, and the Schedule.

Amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958 by inserting the definition of 'Additional Commissioner', omitting clause (da) in section 2, making changes to section 5 regarding approval for certain actions, amending the title and content of section 6-A to include submission of returns and furnishing of information, inserting new section 8-CC regarding revision powers of the Additional Commissioner, and omitting section 10A.

Amends the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976 by inserting provisos to section 5 allowing the Commissioner to notify websites for electronic applications for registration and enrolment.

Amends the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979 by inserting the definition of 'Additional Commissioner', inserting a proviso to section 4-A for electronic applications for registration, making extensive amendments to section 10 regarding the powers of the Joint Commissioner and Additional Commissioner for revision, and substituting section 12-A to grant the State Government power to exempt or reduce tax or permit composition payment for specified classes of hotels, marriage halls, clubs, and hospitals.

Amends the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979 by inserting a proviso to section 4(1) allowing the Commissioner to notify websites for electronic applications, and amending section 18-B to clarify references to other acts and modify the explanation regarding joint and several liability for tax and penalty for hired vehicles.
Repeals the enactments specified in the Schedule as they were in force in the Belgaum, Gulbarga, Mangalore and Kollegal Areas of the State.

important_rules: Rule 1: Section 3-A of the Betting Tax Act, 1932 allows the State Government to accept a composition in lieu of totalisator tax from licensees in Bangalore City (8% of total moneys paid into totalisator) and Mysore City (4% of total moneys paid into totalisator), subject to prescribed conditions.

Rule 2: Proprietors of cinema theatres belonging to a specified class (as notified by the Commissioner) must enter particulars of each cinematograph show into a website within a specified time, as per amendments to the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958.

Rule 3: Applications for registration and enrolment under the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, and applications for registration under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, and applications under the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979, may be required to be made electronically through websites notified by the Commissioner.

Rule 4: The Additional Commissioner in the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, has the power to revise orders passed by officers below the rank of Joint Commissioner if they are prejudicial to the revenue, subject to certain conditions and limitations regarding time for appeal and prior revisions.

Rule 5: The State Government can, in the public interest, exempt or reduce tax, or permit composition payment for certain classes of hotels, marriage halls, clubs, and hospitals under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.

Rule 6: In cases where a vehicle is hired for transportation of goods, both the owner of the vehicle and the person hiring it are deemed to be the owner and are jointly and severally liable for tax and penalty under the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.

penalties: While the act primarily focuses on amendments to taxation laws and does not explicitly detail new penalties, the amendments to existing acts imply that penalties and enforcement mechanisms as provided in those original acts (and as amended) would apply. For instance, sections related to revision by Additional Commissioner in the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, and Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, deal with rectifying erroneous assessments which could lead to increased tax liability and potential penalties.
Joint and several liability for tax or penalty on hired vehicles under the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement authorities would be the respective tax departments and officers of the State of Karnataka, including Commissioners, Additional Commissioners, Joint Commissioners, and other officers appointed under the amended acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would occur through assessment, reassessment, revision of orders, collection of taxes and penalties, and audits as per the provisions of the amended taxation laws.

rights: Right to pay totalisator tax by way of composition under specified conditions in Bangalore and Mysore Cities (under Betting Tax Act, 1932).
Right to an opportunity of being heard before the Additional Commissioner passes an order prejudicial to the person concerned.

Right to seek exemption or reduction of tax, or permit payment of composition amount from the State Government for specified classes of hotels, marriage halls, clubs, and hospitals (under Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979).
Right to appeal against orders passed by tax authorities as per the provisions of the respective amended acts.
duties: Duty to pay taxes as per the amended laws.
Duty to comply with electronic filing requirements if notified.
Duty to furnish information and submit returns as required under the amended Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958.
Duty to cooperate with tax authorities during examinations or inquiries.
obligations: Obligation for proprietors of specified cinema theatres to enter cinematograph show particulars on a website.
Obligation for licensees to elect for composition of totalisator tax if desired and eligible.
Obligation for owners of hired vehicles to be jointly and severally liable for tax or penalty.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for registration and enrolment electronically through notified websites, as introduced in the Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976, Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, and Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.

Procedure for revision of orders by the Additional Commissioner, involving examination of records, calling for information, opportunity of being heard, and passing orders to correct erroneous assessments prejudicial to revenue, as introduced in the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, and expanded in the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979.
Procedure for the State Government to grant exemptions or reductions in tax, or permit composition payments under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1979, through notification.
Procedure for repeal of certain enactments as specified in the schedule, which implies the cessation of force of those previous laws in specific areas of Karnataka.
administration: The administration of this Act and the amended taxation laws would fall under the purview of the Commercial Taxes Department of the Government of Karnataka, and various tax authorities appointed under the respective Acts.
important_notes: The Act is a consolidation and amendment of several existing taxation laws, rather than a standalone new law with entirely new subject matter.
The amendments aim to modernize tax administration through e-governance initiatives (electronic filing) and to streamline tax collection and enforcement by empowering higher tax officials.

The repeal of certain enactments in Section 8 is specific to particular geographical areas of Karnataka (Belgaum, Gulbarga, Mangalore and Kollegal Areas), indicating a move towards uniformity in taxation laws across the state.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE LAW UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009, to reflect consequential changes in designations of certain authorities and departments.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka State Law University and amends provisions within the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009. It specifically addresses amendments related to the Vice-Chancellor of the National Law School of India University and the designation within the State Audit and Accounts Department.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka State Law University (Amendment) Act, 2020, and that it comes into force at once.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 33 of the Principal Act by substituting clause (g) to refer to 'The Vice-Chancellor, National Law School of India University, Bengaluru'.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 56 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'controller of State Accounts' with 'The Principal Director, Karnataka, The State Audit and Accounts Department'.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Karnataka State Law University (Amendment) Act, 2020 shall be the short title of this Act.
Rule 2: The Act shall come into force immediately upon its enactment.
Rule 3: Section 33(1)(g) of the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009, is amended to include the Vice-Chancellor of the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru.

Rule 4: Section 56(2) of the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009, is amended to replace 'controller of State Accounts' with 'The Principal Director, Karnataka, The State Audit and Accounts Department'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature is responsible for enacting this amendment, and the administrative department responsible for the Karnataka State Law University would likely be involved in its enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The amendment process involves the legislative process of the Karnataka State Legislature, including the introduction and passing of a bill.
Procedure 2: Upon enactment, the amended provisions of the Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009, are to be followed.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, as indicated by the signatory.
important_notes: The amendments are consequential to the renaming of certain offices and departments.
The act is based on Entry 25 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to provide for specific fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and total liabilities percentages for the financial year 2021-2022, especially in light of the economic recovery post-COVID-19.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. Its scope is primarily financial, relating to the state's fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and total liabilities.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2021' and states that it comes into force from the first day of April, 2021.
Amends Section 4 of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, by inserting new provisos related to the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and total liabilities for the financial year 2021-22.

important_rules: Rule 1: The fiscal deficit during the financial year 2021-22 shall not exceed four percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product.
Rule 2: During the financial year 2021-2022, the State revenue deficit may arise due to slow recovery of the economy to the Pre Covid-19 levels.
Rule 3: During the financial year 2021-22, the total Liabilities may exceed twenty five percent of the estimated Gross State Domestic Product.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signing authority)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and adherence to the financial targets set by the Act.

duties: Duty to adhere to the fiscal deficit limit of 4% of estimated GSDP for FY 2021-22.
Duty to manage revenue deficit arising from economic recovery.
Duty to manage total liabilities not exceeding 25% of estimated GSDP for FY 2021-22.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendments are made in response to the economic conditions, including slow recovery post-COVID-19, and allow for temporary deviations from standard fiscal responsibility norms for the financial year 2021-2022.
The Act came into force with effect from the first day of April, 2021.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION ACT, 2022
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Services of the Financial year 2021-22.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the appropriation of funds from its Consolidated Fund for the financial year 2021-22. It covers various government services and purposes as detailed in the schedule.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation Act, 2022.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 2695332.83 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2021-22
main_sections.description: Authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees Twenty six thousand nine hundred and fifty three crore thirty two lakh and eighty three thousand, from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka towards defraying the several charges that will come in course of payment during the Financial Year 2021-22, in respect of the services specified in column 2 of the schedule.

The sums authorized to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

important_rules: Sums authorized for payment and application from the Consolidated Fund must not exceed the amounts specified in the schedule.
Appropriations are to be made for the services and purposes detailed in the schedule for the financial year 2021-22.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature, Governor of Karnataka, and by implication, the departments responsible for managing the Consolidated Fund and government finances.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative enactment and subsequent financial management and oversight by the government.

rights: The right to authorize the payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund for specified services and purposes.
duties: The duty to ensure that funds are appropriated for the services and purposes as expressed in the Schedule.
obligations: The obligation to adhere to the amounts specified in the Schedule for appropriation.
The obligation to authorize payment and appropriation of funds in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of India, particularly Article 204 (1) (a).

key_procedures: Introduction of a Bill in the Karnataka State Legislature, in pursuance of Article 204 (1) (a) of the Constitution of India.
Authorization of payment and appropriation of sums from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Specification of services and purposes for which funds are appropriated in a Schedule.
Publication of the Act in the official Gazette.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Government of Karnataka) is involved in the legislative process and publication. The Finance Department and other relevant departments would be involved in the actual management and disbursement of funds.
important_notes: The Act is based on Article 204 (1) (a) of the Constitution of India.
The Act provides for further sums towards defraying charges for the Financial Year 2021-22.
The total amount authorized for appropriation is Rupees 26,95,332.83 Lakhs (Twenty six thousand nine hundred and fifty three crore thirty two lakh and eighty three thousand).

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, to bifurcate Gulbarga University and establish Raichur University with headquarters at Raichur, having territorial jurisdiction over the districts of Raichur and Yadagiri, with the aim of reducing regional imbalance and promoting the development of the region.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, and specifically deals with the establishment of Raichur University, its territorial jurisdiction, and the transfer of colleges and institutions from Gulbarga University. It covers the districts of Raichur and Yadagiri for the new university, and the remaining districts previously under Gulbarga University's jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2020, and it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. It modifies the territorial jurisdiction of Gulbarga University to exclude Raichur and Yadagiri districts, limiting it to Bidar and Kalaburagi (formerly Gulbarga). It also establishes Raichur University with its headquarters at Raichur and territorial jurisdiction over the districts of Raichur and Yadagiri.

Inserts a new sub-section (13) into Section 5 of the principal Act. This sub-section states that any privileges enjoyed by colleges/institutions in Raichur and Yadagiri districts from Gulbarga University before the commencement of this Amendment Act shall be deemed withdrawn and these institutions shall be deemed affiliated to Raichur University.
Inserts a new proviso in sub-section (4) of Section 14 of the principal Act, stating that the first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University shall be appointed by the State Government.

Empowers a Special Officer appointed by the State Government to establish Raichur University to exercise specified powers and perform functions of the University and Vice-Chancellor until the first Vice-Chancellor is appointed.

Mandates the first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University to arrange for the constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities within six months (or an extended period up to one year) from the commencement of the Amendment Act. These authorities will commence their functions on a date specified by the Chancellor.

Provides for the first Vice-Chancellor to discharge functions of Raichur University with the Chancellor's approval until its authorities are constituted. It also states that existing statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules of Gulbarga University applicable to the newly affiliated colleges of Raichur University shall continue until Raichur University makes its own.

Ensures continuity for students studying for degrees from Gulbarga University. Students can be admitted to examinations of Gulbarga University until Raichur University provides its own examinations. Examinations already held or results published by Gulbarga University before the commencement of the Amendment Act are deemed to have been held by Gulbarga University.

Empowers the State Government to make provisions by notification or order to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Amendment Act, provided such provisions are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within two years of its commencement.

important_rules: Colleges and educational institutions previously affiliated with Gulbarga University located in Raichur and Yadagiri districts shall be deemed to be affiliated with the newly established Raichur University.
The first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University is responsible for establishing the university's governing bodies (Syndicate, Academic Council, etc.) within a specified timeframe.
Existing statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules of Gulbarga University will apply to the newly affiliated colleges of Raichur University until Raichur University formulates its own.
Students enrolled in Gulbarga University prior to the amendment will continue their examinations and degree conferral under Gulbarga University until Raichur University is equipped to conduct them.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the authorities of the newly established Raichur University.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, appointment of authorities, and by operation of the amended Act.

rights: Students of Gulbarga University in the specified districts have the right to continue their examinations and receive degrees under Gulbarga University until Raichur University establishes its examination system.
Colleges/institutions in Raichur and Yadagiri districts have the right to be affiliated with Raichur University.
The State Government has the right to appoint the first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University and make orders for the removal of difficulties.
duties: The first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University has the duty to constitute the University's authorities.
The State Government has the duty to appoint the first Vice-Chancellor and to issue notifications for the commencement of the Act and removal of difficulties.
obligations: Colleges and educational institutions in Raichur and Yadagiri districts are obligated to transfer their affiliation from Gulbarga University to Raichur University.
The State Government is obligated to take steps to establish Raichur University.

key_procedures: Establishment of Raichur University by the State Government.
Appointment of the first Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University by the State Government.
Constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities of Raichur University by the first Vice-Chancellor.
The State Government issuing a notification to bring the Act into force.
The State Government issuing notifications or orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation of the Government of Karnataka is responsible for the official publication and administration of this act.
important_notes: The Act aims to address regional imbalance as highlighted by the Dr. Nanjundappa Committee Report.
The bifurcation of Gulbarga University is for the convenience of students and the development of the Hyderabad Karnataka Region.
The removal of difficulties clause has a time limit of two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: The Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders And Slum-Grabbers Act, 1999 (Amendment Act), 2000
purpose: To provide for the prevention of dangerous activities of bootleggers, drug-offenders, gamblers, goondas, immoral traffic offenders and slum-grabbers and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and deals with individuals engaged in dangerous activities that threaten public tranquility and order, including bootlegging, drug offenses, gambling, goondaism, immoral trafficking, and slum grabbing.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders And Slum-Grabbers Act, 1999. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the first day of May 2001.

In clause (g) of section 2 of the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders and Slum-Grabbers Act, 1999 (Karnataka Act 16 of 1999), for the words and figures 'Chapter XXVI' the words and figures 'Chapter XXVI, Chapter XXVI-A' shall be substituted.

important_rules: The Act provides for the prevention of dangerous activities of various offenders to maintain public order and tranquility.
Offences covered include bootlegging, drug offenses, gambling, goondaism, immoral trafficking, and slum grabbing.
The Act details amendments to Section 2 of the principal Act (Karnataka Act 16 of 1999), specifically relating to the inclusion of 'Chapter XXVI-A' in the definition of dangerous activities.

penalties: The act aims to prevent dangerous activities through preventive detention.
Penalties are likely to be imprisonment and other measures as per the provisions of the Act and related laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Karnataka is responsible for the enforcement of this act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves identifying and detaining individuals involved in the specified dangerous activities to prevent them from engaging in such acts.

rights: Right to public tranquility.
Right to be protected from dangerous activities.
duties: Duty to refrain from engaging in bootlegging, drug offenses, gambling, goondaism, immoral trafficking, and slum grabbing.
obligations: Individuals engaging in the specified dangerous activities have obligations to cease such practices to avoid legal repercussions.

key_procedures: The Act allows for the detention of individuals engaged in dangerous activities.
The procedure involves amendment of definitions within the principal Act to encompass additional categories of offenses or activities.
administration: Home Department, Government of Karnataka (implied, as law and order is typically under their purview).
important_notes: This specific document is an amendment act, further amending the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders And Slum-Grabbers Act, 1999.
The amendment clarifies and potentially expands the scope of 'dangerous activities' by referencing 'Chapter XXVI-A'.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for fiscal responsibility of the Government of Karnataka and to promote fiscal prudence and discipline in the State and to enhance transparency in fiscal management, accountability in the implementation of fiscal policies and to strengthen the framework for fiscal stabilization.
scope: This Act applies to the Government of Karnataka and its fiscal operations.

key_definitions.fiscal deficit: The difference between revenue receipts and expenditure, or the sum of market borrowings and other liabilities less loans and advances.
key_definitions.medium term fiscal plan: A plan which sets out the strategy of the Government for the medium term fiscal position covering a period of at least three years.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and when it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as fiscal deficit, medium term fiscal plan, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Medium Term Fiscal Plan to be laid before the Legislature
main_sections.description: Requires the Government to lay a medium term fiscal plan before the Legislature.
Outlines principles for fiscal management.
Specifies measures to ensure fiscal transparency.
Details measures for enforcing compliance with the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before Legislature
main_sections.description: Requires any rules made under the Act to be laid before the Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not prevent the application of other laws.
Grants power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
