important_rules: The State Government shall prepare and lay before the Legislature, a Medium Term Fiscal Plan.
The State Government shall make endeavours to enhance fiscal transparency, accountability, and prudent debt management.
The State Government shall take suitable measures to ensure greater transparency in fiscal operations and to minimise fiscal deficits.
The State Government shall aim at achieving gradual reduction in fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.
The State Government shall take appropriate measures to ensure greater transparency in fiscal operations and to minimize fiscal deficits and contain the growth of public expenditure.
The State Government shall ensure that the fiscal deficit is brought down to 3% of GSDP by the end of March 2006.
The State Government shall endeavour to take suitable measures to ensure greater transparency in fiscal operations and to minimise fiscal deficits and contain the growth of public expenditure.

The State Government shall prepare and lay before the Legislature, a Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) which sets out the strategy of the Government for the medium term fiscal position covering a period of at least three years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government (implied through its fiscal management and rule-making powers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through fiscal management principles, measures for fiscal transparency, compliance enforcement, and the framework established by the Act.

rights: Right to transparency in fiscal operations.
Right to accountability in fiscal policy implementation.
duties: Duty of the Government to lay a Medium Term Fiscal Plan before the Legislature.
Duty of the Government to ensure fiscal prudence and discipline.
Duty to enhance transparency and accountability in fiscal management.
Duty to minimize fiscal deficits and contain public expenditure growth.
obligations: Obligation to reduce fiscal deficit to 3% of GSDP by the end of March 2006.
Obligation to conduct regular reviews of fiscal performance.

key_procedures: Preparation and laying of the Medium Term Fiscal Plan before the Legislature.
Regular review of fiscal performance.
Taking measures to ensure fiscal transparency and reduce deficits.
administration: The Finance Department of the Government of Karnataka is implied to be responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to establish a legal framework for fiscal responsibility.
The Act seeks to improve the financial health of the State by setting targets for deficit reduction.
The Act mandates transparency and accountability in government financial dealings.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE OPEN UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992, specifically to provide for the continuation of Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations of the Mysore University that were in force until new ones were issued under the Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992, and to validate actions taken under those adopted provisions.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka State Open University and its administrative and regulatory framework. It addresses the continuation and validation of rules and actions related to its establishment and operation, referencing the Mysore University's adopted statutes.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka State Open University (Amendment) Act, 2002' and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section inserts a new section, section 42, into the principal Act (The Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992). This new section deals with the continuation of Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations and Rules of the Mysore University.

This section provides for the validation of actions, proceedings, appointments, delegations, and orders made by the University or its authorities/officers/employees under the adopted statutes, ordinances, regulations, or rules of the Mysore University, with effect from June 1, 1996. These actions are deemed valid as if the provisions of the newly inserted section 42 were in force at all relevant times.

important_rules: Rule: Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations and Rules of the Mysore University that were in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall continue to be in force for the Karnataka State Open University until new ones are made under the Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992. These adopted rules can be adapted or modified by the Vice-chancellor with the approval of the Chancellor obtained through the Government, provided they are not inconsistent with the principal Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature and the authorities established under the Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative enactment and the administrative mechanisms of the Karnataka State Open University.

key_procedures: Procedure: Insertion of a new section (Section 42) into the Karnataka State Open University Act, 1992, to govern the continuation of existing regulations.
Procedure: Validation of past actions taken under the adopted regulations to ensure continuity and legal standing.
administration: The Karnataka State Open University and the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: Note: The adopted Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations from Mysore University are deemed to be Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations of the Karnataka State Open University, subject to adaptations or modifications.
Note: Actions taken from June 1, 1996, under the adopted rules are retrospectively validated.

title: THE KARNATAKA VILLAGE DEFENCE PARTIES (REPEAL) ACT, 2004
purpose: To repeal the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964, as the institution of Dalapthis has lost its utility and become obsolete, and in light of a High Court direction to take a decision on the request of petitioners for remuneration.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka. It concerns the repeal of the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Village Defence Parties (Repeal) Act, 2004, and that it comes into force at once.

This section formally repeals the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 34 of 1964). It includes a proviso that the repeal will not affect anything done, any action taken, or any right, obligation, or liability accrued or incurred under the repealed Act prior to the date of repeal.

important_rules: The Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964 is repealed.
The repeal does not affect any actions, rights, obligations, or liabilities incurred before the repeal date.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the state legislature and relevant government departments for the repeal process.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the enactment and official publication of the Act.

rights: Any rights accrued under the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964 prior to its repeal are preserved.
duties: Any duties or obligations incurred under the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964 prior to its repeal are preserved.
obligations: Any obligations incurred under the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964 prior to its repeal are preserved.

key_procedures: Enactment of the Karnataka Village Defence Parties (Repeal) Act, 2004.
Coming into force of the Act at once.
Formal repeal of the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Act, 1964.
Preservation of actions, rights, obligations, and liabilities accrued under the repealed Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The repeal is based on the obsolescence of the institution of Dalapthis and a High Court direction.
The High Court of Karnataka had directed a decision on the request of Village Defence Parties and Dalapathis for remuneration as per the Karnataka Village Defence Parties Rules, 1965.

title: THE KARNATAKA SOUHARDA SAHAKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997, incorporating suggestions from the Reserve Bank of India regarding banking business and other operational aspects of Souharda Sahakaris.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997. It applies to Souharda Sahakaris registered under that Act. The amendments specifically relate to their status as cooperative societies for banking regulations, the primary object of Cooperative Banks, election procedures, disqualification of directors, and supersession/liquidation orders by the Registrar based on RBI directives.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act by: (i) inserting a provision to deem Souharda Sahakaris as Co-operative Societies for the purposes of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961, and the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981; and (ii) substituting 'its primary object' for 'one of its objects' in clause (ee) concerning Cooperative Banks.
Omits clause (ix) of sub-section (2) of section 10 of the principal Act.

Inserts sub-sections (4) and (5) into section 25 of the principal Act. These new sub-sections provide for the Federal Co-operative to decide on disqualification of a board member after hearing them, and allow an appeal to the Registrar against such an order within thirty days.
Omit clause (e) of sub-section (7) of section 53 of the principal Act.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 67A of the principal Act to state that the Registrar shall pass an order of supersession of a Board or Liquidation of a Co-operative Bank when required by the Reserve Bank of India in writing.

important_rules: A Souharda Sahakari shall be deemed to be a Co-operative Society for the purposes of specific central banking and financial acts (Banking Regulation Act, 1949, RBI Act, 1934, DICGC Act, 1961, NABARD Act, 1981).
The primary object of a Co-operative Bank shall be the Business of Banking.
Questions regarding disqualification of a board member will be decided by the Federal Co-operative, with an appeal process to the Registrar.
The Registrar must pass an order of supersession of a Board or Liquidation of a Co-operative Bank when so required by the Reserve Bank of India in writing.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar (in relation to supersession/liquidation based on RBI directives and appeals against disqualification), Federal Co-operative (in relation to disqualification decisions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Registrar and Federal Co-operative, and potential notifications by the State Government for commencement.

rights: A member aggrieved by a disqualification order has the right to appeal to the Registrar within thirty days.
duties: The Federal Co-operative has the duty to decide disqualification of directors after giving a hearing.
The Registrar has the duty to pass supersession or liquidation orders as required by the RBI in writing.

key_procedures: Procedure for deciding disqualification of a board member: The Federal Co-operative must provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the person concerned, then decide the question of disqualification.
Procedure for appeal against disqualification: A person aggrieved by the order of disqualification can prefer an appeal to the Registrar within thirty days from the date of the order.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for enactment), State Government (for commencement notification). The Registrar of Co-operative Societies is involved in enforcement.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997.
The amendments are based on suggestions from the Reserve Bank of India.
The Act came into force on a date to be appointed by the State Government, as it was published in the Gazette on May 24, 2005, but its commencement date is to be notified.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE SALARIES, PENSIONS AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, to provide for enhancements in salaries, allowances, and pensions for Legislators, and to include the status and provisions for the Opposition Chief Whip.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, and its provisions are related to the salaries, pensions, and allowances of Members of the Karnataka Legislature, Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, Government Chief Whip, and Opposition Chief Whip within the state of Karnataka.

key_definitions.Opposition Chief Whip: A member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council designated as such by the Leader of the Opposition.
key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956 (Karnataka Act 2 of 1957).

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2009, and deems it to have come into force from January 1, 2009.
Amends the Preamble of the principal Act to include 'Opposition Chief Whips' alongside 'Government Chief Whips'.
Inserts a definition for 'Opposition Chief Whip' in section 2 of the principal Act.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 3 of the principal Act, substituting 'Six thousand rupees' with 'Twelve thousand rupees' for salary, effective from August 24, 2005.
Makes extensive amendments to Section 8 of the principal Act to include provisions and references for the 'Opposition Chief Whips' in various sub-sections concerning their roles and benefits.
Inserts a new section 10K, which establishes a salary of ten thousand rupees per mensem for each Opposition Chief Whip.
Amends section 11A of the principal Act to reflect the 2009 amendment Act, increase pension amounts, and introduce reimbursement of travel expenses for ex-members.
Amends section 11B of the principal Act to provide family pension for life to the dependent of a Member.
Amends various clauses within section 12 of the principal Act to revise allowances and salaries for different positions, including the Opposition Chief Whip.

important_rules: Rule: Salary of Legislators enhanced from Rs. 8000/- per month to Rs. 10,000/- per month.
Rule: Telephone allowance enhanced from Rs. 7500/- per month to Rs. 10,000/- per month.
Rule: Constituency allowance enhanced from Rs. 3500/- per month to Rs. 15,000/- per month.
Rule: Postal charges enhanced from Rs. 1000/- per month to Rs. 4000/- per month.
Rule: Salary of Room Boy enhanced from Rs. 2000/- per month to Rs. 5000/- per month.
Rule: Pension enhanced from Rs. 5000/- per month to Rs. 15,000/- per month.
Rule: Maximum pension enhanced from Rs. 10,000/- per month to Rs. 25,000/- per month.
Rule: Family pension payable for life to the dependent of a Member.
Rule: Ex-members are reimbursed for actual travel expenses in first class/second class A/C by train in India up to a maximum of 35,000 km.
Rule: Salary of Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, and Government Chief Whip increased from Rs. 8000/- per month to Rs. 10,000/- per month.
Rule: Sumptuary allowance increased from Rs. 50,000/- per annum to Rs. 75,000/- per annum.
Rule: Salary for Opposition Chief Whip is Rs. 10,000/- per mensem.
Rule: State Government may provide a suitable motor car for the use of each Opposition Chief Whip.
Rule: Conveyance allowance for Opposition Chief Whip equal to the cost of 500 litres of petrol per mensem.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text. Likely the relevant departments of the Karnataka Government responsible for legislative matters and finance.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, by the relevant administrative authorities.

rights: Right to receive enhanced salaries and allowances as specified in the Act.
Right to receive enhanced pension and family pension.
Right to reimbursement of travel expenses for ex-members.
Right for Opposition Chief Whip to receive a salary and conveyance allowance, and potentially a motor car.
duties: Duty to adhere to the provisions of the amended Act regarding salaries, pensions, and allowances.
Duty of the State Government to provide for the salaries, pensions, and allowances as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to implement the salary and allowance enhancements.
Obligation to provide for the pension and family pension benefits as amended.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of the principal Act through legislative process.
Procedure: Designation of the Opposition Chief Whip by the Leader of the Opposition.
Procedure: Payment of salaries, pensions, and allowances as per the revised rates.
Procedure: Reimbursement of travel expenses for ex-members subject to prescribed rules.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, as indicated by the signature of the Secretary.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from January 1, 2009.
Some amendments have retrospective effect, e.g., amendment to section 3 is effective from August 24, 2005, and amendment to section 10J is effective from August 14, 2008.
Sub-section (1A) of section 11A is deemed to have been omitted with effect from August 24, 2005.

title: THE BANGALORE METROPOLITAN REGION DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985, specifically to provide for placing of Audited Accounts and the report of the Auditor of the Authority before both Houses of the State Legislature.
scope: This act applies to the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority and its financial reporting procedures, amending the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985 (Karnataka Act 39 of 1985).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2009, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (3). The substituted sub-section mandates the Authority to publish audited accounts and the Auditor's report in the prescribed manner, send a copy to the State Government, and requires the State Government to lay these before both Houses of the State Legislature.

important_rules: The Authority shall publish its audited accounts and the Auditor's report in the prescribed manner.
The Authority shall send a copy of its audited accounts and the Auditor's report to the State Government.
The State Government shall cause the audited accounts and the report of the Auditor to be laid before both Houses of the State Legislature as soon as, after it is received by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ensuring audited accounts and auditor's reports are laid before the State Legislature.

duties: The Authority has the duty to publish its audited accounts and the Auditor's report.
The Authority has the duty to send copies of audited accounts and Auditor's report to the State Government.
The State Government has the duty to lay the audited accounts and Auditor's report before both Houses of the State Legislature.

key_procedures: Procedure for submission andtabling of audited accounts and auditor's report: 1. Authority audits its accounts and obtains Auditor's report. 2. Authority publishes the audited accounts and Auditor's report in the prescribed manner. 3. Authority sends a copy of the audited accounts and Auditor's report to the State Government. 4. State Government lays these documents before both Houses of the State Legislature.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (implied by the signature of the Secretary to Government). The Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority is the entity whose accounts are being amended.
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
This is an amendment to the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1985.
The amendment is a consequence of a recommendation by the Legislative Committee on papers to be laid on the floor of the House.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech 2011-12 by further amending the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. It applies to instruments and transactions governed by stamp duty laws in Karnataka. The amendments relate to various types of instruments including loan agreements, land allotment agreements, powers of attorney, agreements for sale, conveyances, and trusts.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act 34 of 1957).
key_definitions.aggregate value of shares: For the purpose of Article 20(4), it means the face value of shares or its market value, whichever is higher.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2011, and specifies that it comes into force from April 1, 2011.

Amends section 9 of the principal Act. It inserts new clauses for remission or reduction of stamp duty for 'Joint Liability Groups' obtaining loans, for farmers receiving developed lands or purchasing lands with compensation, and for instruments related to the State's tourism policy. It also substitutes words in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 9.

Amends various articles in the Schedule of the principal Act, including changes to Article 5 (Agreements relating to sale of property), Article 14 (Revocation of Trust), Article 20 (Conveyance), Article 36, Article 41 (Power of Attorney), Article 52 (Transfer of Trust Property), and Article 54 (Declaration of Trust).

important_rules: Rule regarding stamp duty on loan agreements for 'Joint Liability Groups' for non-agricultural purposes.
Rule regarding stamp duty for farmers receiving developed lands or purchasing lands with compensation for public purposes.
Rule allowing the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty for instruments related to the State's tourism policy.
Substitution of words in section 9(1)(b) concerning marketable securities, brokers' notes, policies of insurance, and receipts.
Changes to stamp duty rates and conditions for agreements relating to sale of property (Article 5).
Omission of clause (f) and its related entries in Article 5.
Omission of 'Revocation of Trust (No 54-B)' from Article 14(c).
Reduction in stamp duty percentages for certain types of conveyances under Article 20(4).
Omission of 'Ten rupees' from Article 36 in column 3.
Changes to the provisos for power of attorney, making duty paid adjustable towards duty on agreements for sale or instruments of sale/transfer (Article 41(e) and 41(eb)).
Insertion of new clauses (f) and (g) in Article 41 for powers of attorney related to trading operations and demat accounts.
Substitution of clause (d) in Article 52 regarding the transfer of trust property, specifying duty rates and a concession for public religious and charitable trusts.

Substitution of Article 54 for 'Trust' and its related entries, specifying stamp duty for declarations of trust based on their purpose (public religious/charitable, management/custody, or involving transfer/disposition of property).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the State Government and its revenue/stamp duty authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administration of stamp duty on instruments as prescribed by the amended Act and its Schedule.

rights: Right for 'Joint Liability Groups' to obtain loans for non-agricultural purposes with reduced stamp duty.
Right for farmers to receive developed lands or purchase lands with compensation for public purposes with specific stamp duty provisions.
Right for parties to adjust stamp duty paid on certain powers of attorney towards duty payable on subsequent agreements or instruments of sale/transfer.
Right to benefit from reduced stamp duty for trading operations and demat account management under specific powers of attorney.
Right to reduced stamp duty for public religious and charitable trusts during property transfers between trusts.
duties: Duty to pay stamp duty on instruments as per the amended Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding the execution and stamping of various instruments.
obligations: Obligation to pay the specified stamp duty on conveyances, agreements, powers of attorney, and trusts.
Obligation to adhere to the conditions for stamp duty remission or reduction where applicable.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for remission or reduction of stamp duty by the State Government through notification.
Procedure for adjusting stamp duty paid on powers of attorney towards subsequent agreements or instruments of sale/transfer.
Procedure for calculating stamp duty on various instruments as detailed in the amended Schedule, considering market value, consideration, and specific conditions.
Procedure for stamp duty calculation and adjustment for the transfer of trust property.
Procedure for determining stamp duty on declarations of trust based on their nature and purpose.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the State Government's revenue and stamp duty administration.
important_notes: The Act comes into force from the first day of April 2011.
Explanations are provided within Article 5 of the Schedule to clarify when possession is deemed delivered and how stamp duty paid on an agreement is adjusted towards conveyance or mortgage.

A proviso in Article 5(e) clarifies that if proper stamp duty is paid on a power of attorney between the same parties for the same property, the stamp duty on the agreement shall not exceed rupees two hundred.
An Explanation to Article 20(4) defines 'aggregate value of shares'.
A proviso to Article 52(d) provides a specific stamp duty rate for public religious and charitable trusts for property transfers.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to remove discrimination against persons suffering from leprosy, which is a curable disease, in accordance with the directions of the Honourable Supreme Court of India.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, and amends Section 245. It pertains to the management of markets within municipal areas in Karnataka. The scope is subject matter regarding expulsion from markets based on disease and behavior.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 2021, and that it shall come into force at once.

Substitutes Section 245 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. The substituted section deals with the power to expel disturbers and persons suffering from dangerous or contagious diseases from markets.

important_rules: The person in charge of a market shall prevent the entry into the market of, and shall expel from the market, any person suffering from any dangerous or contagious disease, who sells or exposes for sale any article, or who handles any article exposed for sale without purchasing it.
The person in charge of a market may expel any person who is creating a disturbance in the market.

penalties: Expulsion from the market.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The person in charge of a market.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By preventing entry and expelling individuals who meet the criteria outlined in the substituted Section 245.

rights: Right of the person in charge of a market to expel individuals from the market under specific conditions.
duties: Duty of the person in charge of a market to prevent entry and expel persons suffering from dangerous or contagious diseases from markets.
Duty of the person in charge of a market to expel persons creating disturbances in markets.

key_procedures: Procedure for market managers to identify and remove individuals from markets who are suffering from dangerous or contagious diseases and are engaging in prohibited activities related to selling or handling goods.
Procedure for market managers to identify and remove individuals from markets who are causing disturbances.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (indicated by the signatory). The overall administration would fall under the municipal bodies responsible for market management.
important_notes: The amendment specifically addresses the removal of discrimination against persons suffering from leprosy, recognizing it as a curable disease.
The amendment is made in conformity with the direction of the Honourable Supreme Court of India in Writ petition Civil No.1151/2017 (PIL-W).

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION (NO.2) ACT, 2022
purpose: To provide for the appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State towards defraying the several charges which will come in course of payment during the Financial Year 2022-23.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka and authorizes payment and appropriation of certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State for the services of the Financial year 2022-23.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation (No.2) Act, 2022.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 27154222.75Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2022-23
main_sections.description: Authorizes payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees two crores seventy-one lakhs fifty-four thousand two hundred twenty-two lakh and seventy-five thousand only, towards defraying the several charges that will come in course of payment during the Financial Year 2022-23 for the services listed in column 2 of the Schedule.

The sums authorized to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Governor of Karnataka (through assent) and the Karnataka State Legislature.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative enactment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

key_procedures: The process involves legislative authorization for the payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State for specific services and purposes during a financial year.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is involved in publishing and overseeing the Act.
important_notes: The Act is enacted in pursuance of Article 204 of the Constitution of India.
The total authorized amount is Rupees 2,71,54,222.75 Lakhs (which translates to Rs. 271,542,227,500).

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, specifically to allow the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty for specified industrial units and projects until March 31, 2006.
scope: This act applies to instruments executed by specified new Tiny, Small Scale, Medium Scale, or Large Scale Industrial Units, Mega Projects, or key projects of core areas, as defined by the new industrial policy and government orders, within Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2002, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2001.

This section amends section 9 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, by substituting the existing provisos and explanation in sub-section (1), clause (a). The amendment allows the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty on instruments executed by specified industrial units and projects until March 31, 2006.

important_rules: Rule: The State Government may, in the public interest, reduce or remit the stamp duty payable on any instrument, to be specified therein, executed by specified new Tiny, Small Scale, Medium Scale, or Large Scale Industrial Units or Mega Projects as defined in the new industrial policy, or by such key projects of core areas as defined in the said policy or specified by the State Government from time to time, until March 31, 2006.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the State Government.

rights: Right of the State Government to reduce or remit stamp duty for specified industrial units and projects.

key_procedures: Procedure: The State Government may issue notifications to specify the instruments and the industrial units/projects for which stamp duty can be reduced or remitted.
administration: State Government
important_notes: Note: The reduction or remission of stamp duty is applicable only until March 31, 2006.

Note: The definition of 'new industrial policy', 'Tiny, Small Scale, Medium Scale or Large Scale Industrial Units', 'Mega Projects', and 'key projects of core area' are based on Government Order CI 167 SPI 2001, dated: 30.6.2001, and subsequent specifications by the State Government.

title: The Karnataka State Civil Services (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To reduce the period of 30 days specified in clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978 to 15 days, to enable more expeditious completion of the process of making rules.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978. It applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically affects the process of making rules related to the Karnataka State Civil Services.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka State Civil Services (Amendment) Act, 2002, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 3 of the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978, by substituting the words 'fifteen days' for 'thirty days' in clause (a) of sub-section (2).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the administrative bodies responsible for the Karnataka State Civil Services.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendment of the existing Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978.

key_procedures: The procedure for making rules under the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978, is expedited by reducing the mandatory notice period from 30 days to 15 days for a specific clause.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is made to the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1990).
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the fourth day of April, 2003.
The amendment is based on Entry 41 of List-II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) LAW AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2003 and the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 2003 to extend the period for payment of property tax without penalty up to March 31, 2004, and to provide for the adjustment of excess property tax paid.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends specific provisions within the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 2003 and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 2003, particularly concerning property tax payment deadlines and valuation for residential buildings.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 34(1) of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2003 (Karnataka Act 32 of 2003) to change the property tax payment deadline from September 30, 2003, to March 31, 2004, with retrospective effect from August 20, 2003.

Amends Section 32(i) of the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 2003 (Karnataka Act 31 of 2003) to change the property tax payment deadline from September 30, 2003, to March 31, 2004, with retrospective effect from August 20, 2003.

Deals with the taxable capital value of residential buildings for the years 2002-2003 and 2003-2004. If the value determined for 2004-2005 is lesser than the previous year's value, the reduced value will be considered the taxable value for the specified years, and any excess property tax paid will be adjusted in subsequent years.

important_rules: Property tax for the years 2002-2003 and 2003-2004 can be paid without penalty until March 31, 2004.

For residential buildings, if the taxable capital value determined for 2004-2005 is less than the value determined for the previous year, the reduced value will be applied for 2002-2003 and 2003-2004.
Any excess property tax paid for 2002-2003 and 2003-2004 will be adjusted against future tax payments.

penalties: The act primarily provides relief by extending the penalty-free period for property tax payment. Specific penalties for non-compliance with the extended deadline are not explicitly detailed in this extract, but it implicitly allows for penalties after March 31, 2004, as per the original acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Municipal Corporations and Municipalities in Karnataka, as governed by the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1977, and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, respectively.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and collection of property taxes by the respective municipal authorities.

rights: Right to pay property tax for 2002-2003 and 2003-2004 without penalty until March 31, 2004.
Right to have excess property tax paid for 2002-2003 and 2003-2004 adjusted against future tax liabilities.
duties: Duty to pay property tax.
Duty to comply with the amended deadlines and valuation rules.
obligations: Obligation to pay property tax as per the amended provisions.
Obligation to accept the adjusted taxable capital value for residential buildings for the specified years.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing laws (Karnataka Act 32 of 2003 and Karnataka Act 31 of 2003) to extend property tax payment deadlines.
Retrospective application of the extended deadline from August 20, 2003.
Adjustment of excess property tax paid for 2002-2003 and 2003-2004.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the respective Municipal Corporations and Municipalities.
important_notes: The extension of the tax payment period without penalty is for the years 2002-2003 and 2003-2004.
The amendments have retrospective effect from August 20, 2003, for the purpose of substitution of dates.
The transitional provision specifically addresses residential buildings and the adjustment of taxable capital value and excess tax paid.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for an appeal to the Revenue Appellate Tribunal from an order passed by the Deputy Commissioner or an Officer authorised under sub-section (1) of section 77A by suitably amending sub-section (2) of section 118 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 (Karnataka Act 10 of 1962). It applies to matters concerning land reforms within the state of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Land Reforms (Second Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends sub-section (2) of Section 118 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, by inserting the words, figures, brackets and letters 'or sub-section (1) of section 77A' after the existing words, figures and brackets 'sub-section (1) of section 77'.

important_rules: Rule: An appeal shall lie to the Revenue Appellate Tribunal from an order passed by the Deputy Commissioner or an Officer authorised under sub-section (1) of section 77A.
Rule: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 is further amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the authorities under the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, including the Deputy Commissioner and the Revenue Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendment of the appeal process within the existing framework of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act.

rights: Right to appeal to the Revenue Appellate Tribunal against orders passed under section 77A.

key_procedures: Procedure: Filing an appeal to the Revenue Appellate Tribunal against an order passed by the Deputy Commissioner or an Officer authorised under sub-section (1) of section 77A.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for promulgation of the act), and likely the Revenue Department for the administration of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
important_notes: The amendment specifically adds the right to appeal against orders passed under section 77A, which was not explicitly covered before.
The Act came into force immediately upon its enactment.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE (PREVENTION OF DISQUALIFICATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1956, to exempt certain offices from disqualifying their holders for being chosen as or for being a member of either House of the State Legislature, thereby avoiding unnecessary expenditure and financial burden on the State exchequer and enabling the utilization of the experience of people's representatives in managing various boards and corporations.
scope: This Act applies to members of the Karnataka State Legislature and offices that would otherwise lead to disqualification under the principal Act. It amends the Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) (Amendment) Act, 2006' and specifies that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act (Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1956) by substituting or omitting various clauses to redefine which offices do not disqualify a person from being a member of the State Legislature. It specifically mentions offices like Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers, Parliamentary Secretaries, leaders of the Opposition, Government Chief Whips, Presidents and Vice-Presidents of Municipal Councils, Mayor and Deputy Mayor of Municipal Corporations, and Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha of Panchayats, as well as members of governing bodies of committees or societies.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision as to validation and other matters
main_sections.description: Provides for the validation of offices specified in Section 3 of the principal Act, irrespective of any court judgments or orders, to prevent disqualification as if the amended Act had always been in force. It clarifies that those who have vacated seats due to previous judgments are not entitled to reinstatement. It also states that pending petitions or references will be disposed of according to the amended Act.

important_rules: Offices of Chairman, Speaker, Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, Minister of State, Deputy Minister, Parliamentary Secretary, leaders of the Opposition or the Government Chief Whip in the Legislative Assembly or Council are not disqualifying.
Offices of President and Vice-President of a Municipal Council under the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, are not disqualifying.
Offices of Mayor or Deputy Mayor of a Municipal Corporation constituted under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, are not disqualifying.
Offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha of Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats and Grama Panchayats constituted under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, are not disqualifying.

Offices of Chairman, Vice-Chairman, President, Vice-President, Director, of the Governing body or a Member of any Committee or Society registered under any law relating to registration of societies are not disqualifying.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The principal Act is likely enforced by the relevant authorities responsible for legislative conduct and disqualification in Karnataka, potentially the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or Chairman of the Legislative Council, and the Election Commission of India for electoral matters.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would involve the scrutiny of offices held by members of the State Legislature and determining if such offices lead to disqualification as per the Act. This may involve legal challenges, petitions, and decisions by presiding officers or judicial bodies.

rights: Right of individuals to hold specified offices without being disqualified from being a member of the State Legislature.
Right to have pending legal matters concerning disqualification disposed of under the amended Act.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1956, as amended.
Duty of authorities to correctly apply the provisions of the Act in determining disqualification.
obligations: Obligation for the legislature to ensure that members do not incur disqualification for holding exempted offices.
Obligation to ensure that the amended Act is applied retrospectively for validation purposes, except for claims of reinstatement.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 3 of the principal Act by substitution and omission of specific clauses to redefine exempted offices.
Validation of past acts and decisions regarding disqualification based on the amended provisions, with certain limitations.
Disposal of pending legal proceedings in accordance with the amended Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is retrospective, meaning it applies to past situations as if the amended Act had always been in force, for validation purposes.
Despite the retrospective validation, individuals who have already vacated their seats due to court orders are not entitled to claim reinstatement or any other claim.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 to facilitate the State Election Commission to use Electronic Voting Machines in the elections to urban local bodies.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 concerning elections to urban local bodies within the state.

key_definitions.voting_machine: Any machine or apparatus whether operated electronically or otherwise used for giving or recording of votes. Any reference to a ballot box or ballot paper shall be construed as including a reference to such voting machine wherever such voting machine is used in any election.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force from May 28, 2009.

Amends specific sections (36, 37, 38) of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 to include provisions for voting machines in place of or alongside ballot papers and ballot boxes. It also inserts a new section (38B) allowing the State Election Commission to adopt voting machines for elections.

Amends specific sections (52, 53, 55) of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 to include provisions for voting machines in place of or alongside ballot papers and ballot boxes. It also inserts a new section (55A) allowing the State Election Commission to adopt voting machines for elections.

Repeals the Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 and clarifies that any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The heading of section 36 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, is amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot papers'.
Sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 36 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, are amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot paper'.
Sub-section (1) of section 37 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, is amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot paper' in clauses (c), (d), and (f).
Sub-section (3) of section 37 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, is amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot paper'.

Sub-section (2) of section 38 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, clause (j), is amended to include a new sub-clause (via) regarding the manner of giving and recording votes by voting machines.
A new section 38B is inserted into the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, stating that voting machines may be adopted in constituencies specified by the State Election Commission.
The heading of section 52 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, is amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot papers'.
Sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 52 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, are amended to include 'or voting machine' after 'ballot paper'.
Sub-section (1) of section 53 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, is amended to include 'voting machine' after 'ballot paper or' in clause (c), and after 'ballot paper' in clause (d).

Clause (f) of sub-section (1) of section 53 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, is amended to substitute 'ballot box, ballot papers or voting machine' for 'ballot box or ballot papers'.

Sub-section (2) of section 55 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, clause (h), is amended to include a new sub-clause (via) regarding the manner of giving and recording votes by voting machines.
A new section 55A is inserted into the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, stating that voting machines may be adopted in constituencies specified by the State Election Commission.
key_procedures: The State Election Commission, considering the circumstances of each case, can specify the constituency or constituencies where voting machines may be adopted for the giving and recording of votes. The manner of giving and recording votes by voting machines is also to be specified.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from May 28, 2009.
The Karnataka Municipalities and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (Karnataka Ordinance No. 1 of 2009) has been repealed.

title: THE KARNATAKA LOCAL AUTHORITIES (PROHIBITION OF DEFECTION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1987, to empower the Regional Commissioner to dispose of complaints regarding defection of members of Municipal Corporations, consequent to the redesignation of the post of Divisional Commissioner as Regional Commissioner.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1987, and applies to local authorities within Karnataka, specifically concerning the defection of members of Municipal Corporations.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) (Amendment) Act, 2010, and it comes into force at once.

This section amends Section 4 of the Karnataka Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1987. Specifically, in sub-section (2), clause (ii), it substitutes the words "to the Divisional Commissioner" with "to the Regional Commissioner".

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Regional Commissioner (amended from Divisional Commissioner)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Disposal of complaints referred regarding defection of members of Municipal Corporations.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment is a consequence of the redesignation of the post of Divisional Commissioner to Regional Commissioner.
The original Act being amended is The Karnataka Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1987 (Karnataka Act 20 of 1987).

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, to give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech of 2011-12, specifically by introducing or amending provisions for the levy and collection of cess on motor vehicles and public service vehicles for various infrastructure projects and funds.
scope: This act applies to motor vehicles registered under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and public service vehicles owned by fleet owners within the State of Karnataka. The amendments pertain to the levy of tax and cess as specified in sections 3A and 10A of the principal Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it shall come into force from the first day of April, 2011.

Amends section 3A of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1). It introduces a levy and collection of cess at eleven percentum of the tax levied under section 3 on registered motor vehicles. Ten percentum of this cess is allocated to various infrastructure projects across the State, equity in investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Manthri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi in a proportion of 57:28:15 respectively. One percentum is for the Urban Transport Fund.

Amends section 10A of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1). It introduces a levy and collection of cess at eleven percentum of the tax levied under section 10 on public service vehicles owned by fleet owners. Ten percentum of this cess is allocated to various infrastructure projects across the State, equity investment in Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Manthri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi in a proportion of 57:28:15 respectively. One percentum is for the Urban Transport Fund.

Empowers the State Government to make provisions by notification in the official Gazette to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the provisions of this Amendment Act. Such orders cannot be made after the expiry of two years from the commencement of the Amendment Act.

important_rules: A cess of eleven percentum of the tax levied under section 3 is to be collected on Motor Vehicles registered under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Of this, 10% is for infrastructure projects, Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Manthri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi (57:28:15 ratio), and 1% is for the Urban Transport Fund.

A cess of eleven percentum of the tax levied under section 10 is to be collected on public service vehicles owned by fleet owners. Of this, 10% is for infrastructure projects, Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, and Mukhya Manthri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi (57:28:15 ratio), and 1% is for the Urban Transport Fund.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (implied through the power to make notifications for removing difficulties and the general administration of taxation acts)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of cess as specified in the amended sections and through notifications issued by the State Government to resolve difficulties.

duties: Duty to pay the prescribed cess on registered motor vehicles.
Duty to pay the prescribed cess on public service vehicles owned by fleet owners.

key_procedures: Amendment of section 3A of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, by substituting sub-section (1) to introduce the levy of a new cess.
Amendment of section 10A of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, by substituting sub-section (1) to introduce the levy of a new cess.
State Government issuing notifications to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided such orders are made within two years of commencement.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka) is the issuing authority. The administration of the tax and cess levy would likely fall under the transport or finance department of the Karnataka State Government.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
The cess is levied at a rate of eleven percentum of the tax levied under sections 3 and 10.
The collected cess has specific allocations for infrastructure projects, Bangalore Mass Rapid Transit Limited, Mukhya Manthri Grameena Rasthe Abhivruddhi Nidhi, and the Urban Transport Fund.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, primarily to enhance the total number of wards in Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike to between two hundred and twenty-five and two hundred and fifty, to re-adjust geographical areas before holding elections, and to constitute a delimitation commission for recommending the manner of ward delimitation.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, with specific amendments relating to the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP). It concerns the number of councillors, the division of the city into wards, and the process of delimitation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Third Amendment) Act, 2020, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso. This proviso stipulates that the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike shall consist of not less than two hundred and twenty-five but not more than two hundred and fifty councillors, as determined by the Government through notification.

Amends section 21 of the principal Act in two parts. Sub-section (1) is amended to insert 'on the recommendation of delimitation commission' after 'Government shall'. A proviso is inserted stating that for the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike, the State Government shall divide the city into wards by notification, ensuring that ward areas are, as far as possible, within the jurisdiction of an Assembly constituency and no ward is divided between Assembly constituencies. Sub-section (2) is amended by inserting a new sub-section (2A) which empowers the State Government to constitute a delimitation commission to recommend the manner of delimitation of wards in each corporation.

important_rules: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike shall have between 225 and 250 councillors.
Wards in Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike should ideally align with Assembly constituency boundaries.
No ward in Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike should be divided between different Assembly constituencies.
A delimitation commission will be constituted to recommend ward delimitation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, potentially through the delimitation commission and relevant municipal authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications by the State Government regarding the number of councillors and ward delimitation, and through the recommendations of the constituted delimitation commission.

rights: Right of citizens to have wards aligned with Assembly constituencies as much as possible.
Right of citizens to have wards not divided between Assembly constituencies.
duties: Duty of the State Government to determine the number of councillors for BBMP by notification.
Duty of the State Government to divide the city into wards, considering Assembly constituencies.
Duty of the State Government to constitute a delimitation commission.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to implement the amendments to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government to determine the number of councillors for Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.
Constitution of a delimitation commission by the State Government.
Recommendation by the delimitation commission to the State Government regarding ward delimitation.
Division of the city into wards by the State Government through notification, adhering to specific criteria related to Assembly constituencies.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (for the act's enactment and notification). The day-to-day administration of the Municipal Corporations would fall under their respective authorities, guided by this amended Act.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
The increase in the number of wards is to address population growth and re-adjustment of geographical areas for elections.
The amendments are specifically focused on the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.

title: THE KARNATAKA KRISHNA BASIN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (REPEAL) ACT, 2021
purpose: To repeal the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 (Karnataka Act 12 of 1996) as the planning, investigation, estimation, education, operation, and maintenance of all Irrigation Projects in the Krishna basin are presently being undertaken by the Krishana Bhagya Jala Neeravari Nigama and Karnataka Neeravari Nigama.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically concerns the repeal of a previous act related to the development authority for the Krishna Basin.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority (Repeal) Act, 2021, and states that it comes into force at once.

This section repeals the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 (Karnataka Act 12 of 1996). It includes a proviso that the repeal will not affect the previous operation of the repealed act, any rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities acquired or incurred under it, any penalties or punishments incurred, or any ongoing investigations or legal proceedings. These will continue as if the repealing act had not been passed.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 is repealed.
Rule 2: The repeal does not affect past operations, accrued rights or liabilities, or existing legal proceedings under the repealed Act.

penalties: Any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed under the repealed Act will still be imposed as if this Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The text does not explicitly name a specific enforcement authority for this repeal act, but implies continuity of legal proceedings and enforcement of penalties from the repealed act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement relates to the continuation of legal proceedings and imposition of penalties for offenses committed under the repealed Act.

rights: Any right, privilege acquired, accrued or incurred under the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 remains unaffected.
duties: Any obligation acquired, accrued or incurred under the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 remains unaffected.
obligations: Any obligation acquired, accrued or incurred under the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 remains unaffected.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.

Procedure 2: Any legal proceedings, investigations, or remedies in respect of rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, or punishments incurred under the repealed Act may be instituted, continued, or enforced.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is involved in the publication and official communication of this act.
important_notes: The repeal of the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992 is effective from the date this Act comes into force.
The savings clause (Section 2(1)) is crucial for ensuring continuity and preventing the lapse of past actions, rights, and liabilities.

title: THE KARNATAKA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, to address specific fiscal conditions and targets for the financial year 2022-23, including raising the fiscal deficit limit, acknowledging potential revenue deficits due to economic recovery challenges, and accounting for increased total liabilities.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002. It specifically concerns the fiscal management and targets for the financial year 2022-23.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2022, and states that it comes into force from April 1, 2022.

Amends section 4 of the Karnataka Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2002, by inserting provisos that set the fiscal deficit limit at 3.5 percent of estimated Gross State Domestic Product, acknowledge a potential revenue deficit due to economic impacts of Covid and Omicron, and allow total liabilities to exceed twenty-five percent of the estimated Gross Domestic Product for the financial year 2022-23.

important_rules: The fiscal deficit during the financial year 2022-23 shall not exceed 3.5 percent of estimated Gross State Domestic Product.
During the financial year 2022-23, a State revenue deficit may arise due to slow economic recovery from the Covid and Omicron impact.
During the financial year 2022-23, the total liabilities would exceed twenty-five percent of the estimated Gross Domestic Product.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be related to fiscal management authorities within the Karnataka government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is made to address specific fiscal scenarios for the financial year 2022-23.
The Bill was introduced in the State Legislature under Clause (2) of Article 283 of the Constitution of India.
The act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on March 31, 2022.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Karnataka Road Tax Amendment Act, 2002, amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
Rule 2: It is deemed to have come into force on 6th September, 2002.
Rule 3: Various sections of the principal Act are amended or inserted to modify provisions related to taxation, penalties, and administration of motor vehicles.

penalties: Enhancement of penalty for certain offenses.
Penalties for non-compliance with provisions related to renewal of tax and other fees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, as amended by this Act, is enforced by the relevant authorities within the Karnataka government, likely the Transport Department and its subordinate offices.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves inspection of vehicles, assessment of taxes, levying penalties for non-compliance, and potentially prosecution for repeated offenses.

rights: The right for the government to exempt certain motor vehicles from tax.

duties: Duty to pay road tax as prescribed by the Act.

obligations: Obligation to renew tax within specified timeframes.
Obligation to pay penalties and fines as levied.

Procedure for the Government to issue exemptions from tax payment.
Procedures related to the enhancement of penalties and fines for violations.

important_notes: The Act makes extensive amendments to the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, suggesting significant changes in the taxation regime.

The 'Repeal and saving' section suggests that certain prior provisions are being replaced by the new amendments.
The retrospective nature of the commencement date (September 6, 2002) implies that the amendments are intended to have effect from that date, even though enacted later.

title: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority Act, 2002
purpose: To provide for the conservation of the cultural heritage of Hampi, its archeological remains and natural environs, to preserve its cultural identity, and to ensure sustainable development of the Hampi World Heritage Area by constituting the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority.
scope: The Act applies to the Hampi World Heritage Area, which comprises the Core Area Zone, Buffer Zone, and Peripheral Zones, excluding areas already protected under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958. It covers development activities, conservation of cultural heritage and natural environs, and coordination of various authorities. It also amends the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, and the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974.

key_definitions.Authority: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority established under section 3.
key_definitions.Heritage Area: The whole of the area comprising the Core Area Zone, Buffer Zone, and Peripheral Zones, but excluding the area referred to as a protected area under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958.
key_definitions.Cultural Heritage: Includes specific temples (Sri Virupaksheswara, Krishna, Achutaraya, Vittala, Hazararama), monolithic sculptures (Ganesh, Ugranarasimha, Veerabhadra), Jain temples, Mohammadan tombs, mosques, and other monuments conserved by the Archaeological Survey of India and the State Archaeology Department.
key_definitions.Development: Includes carrying out building, engineering, or other operations in or over or under any land, making any material change in any building or land or in the use of any building or land, and includes redevelopment and forming of layouts and sub-division of any land including amenities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification, with different dates possible for different provisions.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Advisory Committee', 'Amenity', 'Appointed day', 'Authority', 'Buffer Zone', 'Chairperson', 'Commissioner', 'Core Area Zone', 'Cultural Heritage', 'Development', 'Fund', 'Heritage Area', 'Local Authority', 'Land', 'Natural Environs', 'Peripheral Zone', and 'Schedule'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and Incorporation of the Authority
main_sections.description: Establishes the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue or be sued. It also lists the members of the Authority and specifies its headquarters.
Details the procedures for meetings of the Authority, including convening, frequency, quorum, presiding officers, voting, and abstention from discussions and votes on matters of personal interest.

Provides for the constitution and maintenance of an Authority Security Force for the protection of public property, prevention of encroachments, aiding in the detection of revenue leakage, and exercising other prescribed powers and functions. The State Government provides the force, and the Chairperson exercises superintendence and control.

Establishes a State Level Advisory Committee with specified members, including ministers and government officials, to coordinate and monitor the activities of the Authority and advise on matters concerning conservation of cultural heritage and natural environs. The committee meets at least once in six months.
States that the State Government shall appoint a Commissioner for the Authority, who should be an officer of the State Civil Service or a person familiar with historical and cultural development.

Outlines the duties of the Commissioner, who is the Chief Executive and Administrative Officer of the Authority. Responsibilities include all budgetary planning, enforcement, supervision, furnishing information, preparing annual reports, and submitting audited accounts.
Section title indicates the appointment of a Planning Officer.
Section title indicates the appointment of an Accounts Officer and other personnel.
Section title indicates the enumeration of the Authority's functions.
Section title indicates specific powers vested in the Chairperson.
Section title indicates the power of the Authority to delegate its functions.

main_sections.section_title: No other authority or person to undertake development without permission of the Authority
main_sections.description: Prohibits any other authority or person from undertaking development within the Heritage Area without the Authority's permission.
Section title indicates the Authority's power of entry into premises.
Section title indicates the Authority's power to levy fees.
Section title indicates the establishment and management of the Authority's fund.

main_sections.description: Section title indicates the provision of subventions and loans to the Authority.
Section title indicates the Authority's power to borrow funds.

Section title indicates the Authority's power to issue directions.

main_sections.description: Section title indicates penalties for violating the Act's provisions.
Section title indicates how offences committed by companies are handled.

main_sections.description: Section title indicates the Authority's ability to compromise claims.

main_sections.section_title: Fines realised to be credited to the Fund
main_sections.description: Section title indicates that fines realized are to be credited to the Authority's Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Members and officers to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members and officers of the Authority as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Control by the State Government etc
main_sections.description: Section title indicates the control exercised by the State Government over the Authority.
States that this Act shall prevail over other laws where there is an inconsistency.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for the Act.
Provides for the removal of difficulties in implementing the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Karnataka Town and Country Planning act, 1961
main_sections.description: Amends the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, as related to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of (Karnataka Act 32 of 1974) to Authority Premises
main_sections.description: Specifies the application of the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, to Authority premises.

important_rules: No development is to be undertaken by any other authority or person without the explicit permission of the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority.
The Authority Security Force is constituted for better protection of public property, prevention of encroachments, and aiding in investigations related to revenue leakage or offences under the Act.
The State Level Advisory Committee shall meet at least once in six months to coordinate and advise the Authority on matters of conservation and development.
All questions before the Authority's meetings are decided by a majority vote, with the Chairperson having a casting vote in case of a tie.
Members of the Authority must not participate in discussions or vote on matters where they have a direct or indirect interest.

penalties: Penalty for breach of the provisions of the Act (as indicated by Section 24 title).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority, its Commissioner, and potentially the Authority Security Force. The State Government also has oversight and rule-making powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Authority and its officers, including power of entry, imposition of penalties for breaches, and coordination with other authorities. Prosecution can be sanctioned by the State Government.

rights: Right to develop within the Heritage Area only with the Authority's permission.
Right to protection of public property within the Heritage Area by the Authority Security Force.
Right to consultation and advice from the State Level Advisory Committee.
duties: Duty to conserve the cultural heritage and natural environs of Hampi.
Duty to prevent uncontrolled development and commercial exploitation.
Duty to coordinate with various local and state authorities for development activities.
Duty to protect public property within the heritage area.
Duty to promote understanding and research into the values of the Hampi World Heritage site.
obligations: Obligation to obtain permission for any development from the Authority.
Obligation for members and officers to act as public servants.
Obligation to adhere to rules and regulations set forth by the Authority and the State Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for convening and conducting meetings of the Authority, including quorum and voting mechanisms.
Procedure for the appointment of the Commissioner, Planning Officer, and Accounts Officer.
Procedure for the preparation and submission of the Authority's budget, annual reports, and audited accounts.
Procedure for the State Government to make rules and the Authority to make regulations for the Act.
Procedure for sanctioning prosecution for offences under the Act.
administration: The Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority, with the Commissioner as the Chief Executive and Administrative Officer. The State Government exercises control and has the power to make rules. The State Level Advisory Committee also plays a crucial advisory and monitoring role.
important_notes: The Act specifically excludes areas already protected under the Ancient Monuments and Historical Sites and Remains Act, 1958, from the definition of 'Heritage Area'.
The Act requires the State Government to appoint an 'Appointed day' for its commencement, which can vary for different provisions.
The Act is intended to over-ride other laws in case of any conflict regarding the management and development of the Hampi World Heritage Area.
The State Government may, by notification, remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
