title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, specifically to empower Deputy Commissioners to grant exemptions to an extent not exceeding half hectare of land under section 109.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, concerning land reforms and exemptions related to land holdings.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2004, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section introduces an amendment to section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It provides a proviso allowing the Deputy Commissioner, subject to specified restrictions and manner, to exercise the power of the State Government to grant exemptions to an extent not exceeding half hectare of land.

important_rules: Rule 1: Deputy Commissioners may grant exemptions up to half hectare of land under section 109 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
Rule 2: The exercise of this exemption power by the Deputy Commissioner is subject to restrictions and manner specified in sub-section (1-A) of section 109.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner (for granting exemptions)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, as amended by this Act.

rights: Right of landowners to seek exemption for a portion of their land not exceeding half hectare.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for exemption to the Deputy Commissioner.
Procedure 2: Deputy Commissioner's decision on exemption based on specified restrictions and manner.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is responsible for the official publication and legislative aspects.
important_notes: The amendment specifically addresses the delegation of exemption granting power to the Deputy Commissioner.
The extent of exemption is strictly limited to half hectare of land.

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC PREMISES (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, to include all Universities established or deemed to have been established by or under any law of the State Legislature within the definition of 'public premises'. This aims to broaden the scope of the principal Act to cover a wider range of university premises for the purpose of evicting unauthorized occupants.
scope: This amendment applies to Universities established or deemed to have been established by or under any law of the State Legislature in Karnataka. It amends the definition of 'public premises' within the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974.

key_definitions.public premises: Includes any University established or deemed to have been established by or under any law of the State Legislature. This is an amendment to the original definition which was more specific about the universities covered.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it comes into force at once.

This section amends clause (e) of Section 2 of the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, by substituting sub-clause (vii) to redefine 'public premises' to include any University established or deemed to have been established by or under any law of the State Legislature.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment rectifies a situation where the Karnataka State Universities Act, 1976 (which was referenced in the original Act) was repealed and replaced by the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000. It also accommodates the establishment of new universities.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the Twenty Third day of May, 2005.

title: The Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1956, specifically Section 22-A, to streamline the recovery of loans sanctioned by the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Board by making them recoverable as arrears of land revenue, thereby addressing delays in loan recovery from defaulters.
scope: This Act applies to the recovery of sums payable to the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Board under any agreement, express or implied, by any person. It specifically deals with sums of rupees one lakh and above that remain unpaid after a demand notice has been served. The enforcement mechanisms involve the Deputy Commissioner of any district and officers authorized under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Board.
key_definitions.person: Any individual or entity liable to pay sums to the Board.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer of the Board or any other officer authorized by the Board.
key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: The Deputy Commissioner of any district in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it comes into force at once.
This section substitutes the existing Section 22-A of the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1956, with new provisions for the recovery of moneys due to the Board as arrears of land revenue.

important_rules: Rule 1: If any sum of rupees one lakh and above payable to the Board is not paid on or before the due date and remains in arrears for fifteen days after the service of a demand notice by the Chief Executive Officer or an authorized officer, it can be recovered in one or more specified ways.

Rule 2: The recovery can be effected as an arrear of land revenue upon the written application of the Chief Executive Officer or an authorized officer to the Deputy Commissioner, certifying the sum due.
Rule 3: Recovery can also be done by distraint and sale of the movable and immovable property of the defaulter by an officer authorized under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, and its rules.

penalties: The primary enforcement mechanism is the recovery of the due sum as arrears of land revenue or through distraint and sale of property. The 'penalty' is essentially the forced recovery of the outstanding amount.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Deputy Commissioner of any district and officers authorized under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through written application to the Deputy Commissioner for recovery as arrears of land revenue, or by distraint and sale of movable and immovable property by authorized revenue officers.

rights: The Board has the right to recover outstanding sums of one lakh rupees or more.
Individuals have the right to receive a demand notice before recovery proceedings commence.
duties: Persons liable to pay sums to the Board have a duty to pay on or before the due date.
The Chief Executive Officer or authorized officers have a duty to issue demand notices.
The Deputy Commissioner and authorized officers have a duty to facilitate recovery as per the Act.
obligations: Defaulters have an obligation to clear their dues to the Board, failing which their property is liable for distraint and sale.
The Board is obligated to follow the prescribed procedures for recovery.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Demand Notice - If a sum of Rs. 1 lakh or more payable to the Board is not paid by the due date, the Chief Executive Officer or an authorized officer serves a demand notice on the person liable.

Procedure 2: Arrears of Land Revenue Recovery - If the sum remains unpaid for fifteen days after the demand notice, the Chief Executive Officer or authorized officer applies in writing to the Deputy Commissioner, certifying the sum due. The Deputy Commissioner then initiates recovery as arrears of land revenue.

Procedure 3: Distraint and Sale of Property - Alternatively, or in addition, an officer authorized under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, can distrain and sell the movable and immovable property of the defaulter to recover the due amount.
administration: The Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Board, with enforcement actions involving the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation and revenue authorities.
important_notes: The amendment specifically targets sums of rupees one lakh and above for recovery as arrears of land revenue.
The recovery process is initiated only after a demand notice has been served and a grace period of fifteen days has elapsed.
The Act leverages the established mechanisms for land revenue recovery, implying the involvement of state revenue machinery.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and development) Act, 1966, by including provisions for defining 'insolvent' in relation to market functionaries, fixing the term of office for Chairman and Vice-chairman, specifying conditions for no-confidence motions, and empowering the State Government to hear appeals against orders passed by the Director.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) Act, 1966, and its scope is limited to the regulation and development of agricultural produce marketing within Karnataka. It specifically impacts market functionaries, the terms of office for Chairman and Vice-chairman of market committees, and the appeals process related to the Director's orders.

key_definitions.insolvent: A person who cannot pay his debts in respect of financial transactions pertaining to market functionaries in the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and development) (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends sub-section (15) of section 2 of the principal Act (Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966) to redefine 'insolvent'.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 42 of the principal Act to specify the term of office for the Chairman and Vice-chairman as twenty months or the term of the market committee, whichever is earlier.

Amends section 44 of the principal Act concerning no-confidence motions against the Chairman or Vice-Chairman. It modifies the required percentage of members to initiate the motion, adds a provision preventing no-confidence motions within six months of assuming office, and sets a two-thirds majority requirement for adopting the motion.

Amends section 74 of the principal Act to transfer the appellate authority for certain orders from the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal to the State Government. It also addresses the transfer of pending appeals to the State Government.

important_rules: The term of office for the Chairman and Vice-chairman of a market committee is now fixed at twenty months or the term of the market committee, whichever is earlier.
A motion of no-confidence against the Chairman or Vice-Chairman can only be moved by not less than fifty percent of the members.
A motion of no-confidence shall not be moved within a period of six months from the date of assuming office by the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
For a no-confidence motion to be carried, it requires a majority of not less than two-thirds of all the then members of the market committee.
Appeals against certain orders previously heard by the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal will now be heard by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for hearing appeals), Market Committees (for day-to-day regulation and development of agricultural produce marketing).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) Act, 1966, including the procedures for no-confidence motions and the new appellate process.

rights: The right of market committees to regulate and develop agricultural produce marketing.
The right of aggrieved parties to appeal certain orders to the State Government.
duties: Market functionaries have a duty to fulfill financial transactions pertaining to the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee to avoid being declared 'insolvent'.
Chairman and Vice-Chairman have a duty to serve their term, subject to no-confidence provisions.
Members of the market committee have a duty to participate in meetings and voting, including no-confidence motions.
obligations: Market functionaries are obligated to pay their debts related to financial transactions within the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee.
The State Government has an obligation to hear and decide appeals transferred from the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending the definition of 'insolvent' to include debt default in financial transactions with market functionaries.
Procedure for fixing the term of office for Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
Procedure for moving and passing a no-confidence motion against the Chairman or Vice-Chairman, including requirements for notice, number of members, and majority vote.
Procedure for hearing appeals against orders passed by the Director, now vested with the State Government.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for drafting and enactment), State Government (for administration of appeals), Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (for local regulation and development).
important_notes: The amendment comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
Appeals pending before the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal on the commencement date of this Act are transferred to the State Government for decision.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Development and Regulation) Act, 1966, to provide a provision to exempt payment of market fee in respect of new Food Processing Industries in respect of purchases of agricultural produce by such processing industries and existing Industries who take up extension or modernization in accordance with the New Industrial Policies in force in the state.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) Act, 1966. It applies to agricultural produce processing industries in Karnataka that are either new or existing ones undertaking expansion, modernization, or diversification. The geographical scope for exemption periods is defined by Zones 1, 2, and 3 as identified under the Karnataka New Industrial Policy 2009-2014.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section details the amendments made to section 65 of the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) Act, 1966. It introduces provisions for exemption from market fees for new and existing agricultural produce processing industries under specific conditions related to investment, production, and modernization.

important_rules: Existing processing industries undertaking expansion/modernization/diversification are exempted from market fee for five years from the commencement of the Amendment Act, subject to conditions like minimum investment, increased production, use of raw material for new products, replacement of old machinery with modern ones, and certification.

New agricultural produce processing industries and existing ones undertaking expansion/modernization/diversification are exempted from market fee for five years (Zone 1), four years (Zone 2), and three years (Zone 3) from the commencement of the Amendment Act, on purchases of specified agricultural produce directly from farmers, subject to similar conditions as above.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director of Industries and Commerce, Government of Karnataka or his nominee, for certification.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the certification process by the Director of Industries and Commerce or his nominee, confirming fulfillment of exemption conditions.

rights: Right to exemption from market fee for eligible new and existing agricultural produce processing industries.
Right to exemption for a specified period based on the zone and the type of industrial activity (new, expansion, modernization, diversification).
duties: Duty to make a minimum investment of fifty percent of earlier investment on fixed assets for expansion/modernization/diversification projects.
Duty to ensure increased production compared to the average of the previous three years for expansion programs.
Duty to use raw material for production of new products (other than existing ones) for diversification programs.
Duty for existing units to replace all old machineries with modern machineries for modernization programs.
Duty to obtain a certificate from the Director of Industries and Commerce or his nominee certifying fulfillment of conditions for exemption.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the specific conditions laid out for market fee exemption.
Obligation to adhere to the exemption periods defined for different zones and types of industrial activities.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining market fee exemption involves: undertaking expansion/modernization/diversification, meeting minimum investment criteria, achieving increased production (for expansion), using new raw materials (for diversification), or replacing old machinery (for modernization).

Procedure for certification involves: the eligible industry presenting evidence of fulfilling the above conditions to the Director of Industries and Commerce, Government of Karnataka, or his nominee, who then issues a certificate confirming eligibility for fee exemption.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act itself), and likely the Department of Industries and Commerce for administration of exemptions.
important_notes: Exemption is for a period of five years, four years, and three years for Zone-1, Zone-2, and Zone-3 respectively.
The agricultural produce purchased must be directly from farmers and specified in Sl. No.II, III, IV, VI, VII, IX and X of the Schedule appended to the Act.
The Karnataka New Industrial Policy 2009-2014 and Government Order No. CI/223/SPI/2008, dated 28.02.2009 are referenced for zone identification.

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION (No.3) ACT, 2020
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Services of the Financial year 2020-21.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the appropriation of funds for the financial year 2020-21. It covers various services and purposes as detailed in the schedule.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation (No.3) Act, 2020.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 400850.47 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2020-21
main_sections.description: This section authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees four thousand eight crores fifty lakhs and forty seven thousand only, from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for defraying charges during the Financial Year 2020-21.

This section states that the sums authorized to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

important_rules: Sums not exceeding those specified in the Schedule are authorized for payment and application from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
These sums are to be appropriated for the services and purposes detailed in the Schedule for the Financial Year 2020-21.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Governor of Karnataka and the Karnataka State Legislature are implicitly involved in the enactment and authorization process.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of enacting the act and subsequent financial management by the State Government.

rights: The right to authorize payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
duties: The duty to provide for the appropriation of funds for various services and purposes of the State.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Constitution of India (Article 205(1)(a)) for presenting supplementary demands for grants.
Obligation to adhere to the sums and services specified in the Schedule.

key_procedures: Presentation of a Bill to the Karnataka State Legislature to provide for appropriation of funds.
Authorization of payment and application of sums from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Appropriation of authorized sums for specific services and purposes as detailed in the Schedule.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs And Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The act is enacted in pursuance of Article 205(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.
The amounts are specified in lakhs and are for the Financial Year 2020-21.
The schedule provides a breakdown of the allocated sums for various services and purposes, including both 'Revenue' and 'Capital' expenditures.

title: THE KARNATAKA MARITIME BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Maritime Board Act, 2015, to provide for the inclusion of the Chief Minister as Chairman and the Minister in charge of ports and inland water transport as Vice-Chairman of the Karnataka Maritime Board, appointment of a custodian of cargo, increase the lease contract period from five to thirty years, and increase the limit for writing off losses.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Maritime Board Act, 2015. It applies to matters concerning the Karnataka Maritime Board, its composition, functions, and financial powers within the state of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Maritime Board (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it comes into force at once.
This section amends section 2 of the Principal Act by omitting specific words related to acting persons appointed under section 9.

This section significantly amends section 3 of the Principal Act by substituting sub-section (2) to redefine the composition of the Board, including the Chief Minister as Chairman and the Minister in charge of Ports and Inland Water Transport as Vice-Chairman, along with various ex-officio members and nominated members with specific expertise. It also substitutes sub-section (4) to allow the Board to co-opt other officers as invitees with the Chairman's approval and for the Government to appoint permanent invitees.

This section amends section 9 of the Principal Act, replacing the provision for appointment of a person to act as Chairman with a provision that the Additional Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary in charge of the Infrastructure Development, Ports and Inland Water Transport Department shall preside over the meeting.

This section amends section 10 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'any person chosen by the members present from amongst themselves' with 'Additional Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary to Government incharge of Infrastructure development, Port and Inland Water Transport' in sub-section (3).
This section amends section 12 of the Principal Act by substituting the word 'Deputy-Chairman' with 'Vice-Chairman' in the proviso.
This section makes a minor textual correction in section 16 of the Principal Act, substituting 'therefore' with 'thereof' in sub-section (3).
This section amends section 24 of the Principal Act by substituting 'five years' with 'thirty years' in clauses (a) and (b), thereby increasing the lease contract period.

This section inserts a new sub-section (5) into section 34 of the Principal Act, authorizing the Maritime Board to appoint a Custodian of Cargo for carrying out responsibilities under the Handling of Cargo in Customs Areas Regulations, 2009.

This section amends section 81 of the Principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'fifty thousand rupees' and 'one lakh rupees' with 'ten lakh rupees' in sub-section (2), thereby increasing the limit for writing off losses.

important_rules: The Chief Minister shall be the Chairman of the Karnataka Maritime Board.
The Minister in charge of Ports and Inland Water Transport shall be the Vice-Chairman of the Karnataka Maritime Board.

The Board shall consist of several ex-officio members including Additional Chief Secretary/Development Commissioner, Principal Secretaries from relevant departments (Infrastructure Development, Finance, Public Works Engineering, Industries and Commerce), Joint Secretary from Ministry of Shipping, Inspector General of Police (Internal Security), Director of Ports, Director of Fisheries, Naval Officer in charge INS Kadamba, Commander Coast Guard District, and Commissioner of Customs.

The Board shall also include nominated members with expertise in port development (Master Mariner, Harbour Engineering/Civil Engineering, Chamber of Commerce, Financial Management) and coastal engineering/marine engineering/sea erosion prevention.
The Member (Technical) and the Chief Executive Officer of the Board are also members.
The Board may co-opt other officers as invitees with the Chairman's approval.
The lease contract period for the Board is increased from five to thirty years.
The limit for writing off losses in a year is increased from ten thousand rupees to fifty thousand rupees and from one lakh rupees to ten lakh rupees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Karnataka Maritime Board (implied through its functions and amendments)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Maritime Board Act, 2015, as amended by this Act, including its powers related to cargo handling and financial management.

rights: The Board has the right to appoint a Custodian of Cargo.
The Board's lease contract period has been extended, granting it longer-term operational rights.
duties: The Board has a duty to manage maritime and inland water transport operations in Karnataka.
The Board has a duty to handle cargo responsibilities through appointed custodians.
The Board is responsible for financial management, including the writing off of losses within revised limits.

key_procedures: Amendment of the composition of the Karnataka Maritime Board to include specific high-ranking officials as Chairman and Vice-Chairman, and a comprehensive list of ex-officio and nominated members.
Procedure for co-opting invitees to Board meetings.
Appointment of a Custodian of Cargo by the Maritime Board for handling cargo responsibilities.
Financial procedures related to writing off losses, with increased monetary limits.
administration: Department of Ports and Inland Water Transport, Government of Karnataka (implied by the roles of Principal Secretary and Minister in charge).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Maritime Board Act, 2015 (Karnataka Act 41 of 2017).
The amendments are based on the constitutional entries relating to List II and List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor of Karnataka on the 5th day of April, 2021.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, to extend the period for payment of tax from fifteen days to one month and to provide for monthly payment of tax on a prorata basis for vehicles where quarterly tax exceeds Rupees Thirty Thousand.
scope: This act applies to motor vehicles within the state of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, specifically concerning the payment of motor vehicle tax.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the 'Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2022' and specifies its commencement date as April 1st, 2022.

Amends sub-section (1) of Section 4 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It changes the period for tax payment from 'fifteen days' to 'a month' and inserts a new proviso allowing monthly prorata tax payment for vehicles with quarterly tax of Rupees Thirty Thousand and above.

important_rules: The period for payment of motor vehicle tax is extended from fifteen days to one month.

Vehicles for which the quarterly tax amounts to Rupees Thirty Thousand or more can now be paid on a monthly prorata basis, before the expiry of the tax validity, subject to government-specified conditions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka (implied through 'subject to such condition as may be specified by the Government')
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and any rules or conditions specified by the Government.

duties: Taxpayers have the duty to pay motor vehicle tax.
obligations: Vehicles owners are obligated to pay tax according to the provisions of the act.

key_procedures: Procedure for tax payment extension: Taxpayers now have one month to pay tax instead of fifteen days.

Procedure for monthly prorata tax payment: For vehicles with quarterly tax of Rupees Thirty Thousand and above, tax can be paid monthly on a prorata basis before the expiry of the tax validity, following conditions specified by the Government.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as the issuing authority for the Governor's assent)
important_notes: The amendment comes into force on April 1st, 2022.
The provision for monthly prorata tax payment is applicable only for vehicles where the quarterly tax amounts to Rupees Thirty Thousand and above.

title: THE KARNATAKA ACT NO. 19 OF 2001 THE ROIERICH AND DEVIKARANI ROIERICH ESTAT (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER) ACT, 2001 (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. This amendment act aims to make a more adequate and effective machinery for the acquisition and transfer of the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996.
scope: The Act applies to the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate in Karnataka. It concerns the acquisition and transfer of this estate.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Amendment Act, 2001. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the sixteenth day of November, 1996.

After section 19 of the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996, the following section shall be inserted, namely:- '19A. Power to make provision for acquisition, transfer and other incidental matters for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the Act.'

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act aims to create a more adequate and effective machinery for the acquisition and transfer of the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate.
Rule 2: The amendment act allows for the insertion of a new section (19A) into the principal Act.
Rule 3: Section 19A grants the Government the power to make provisions for acquisition, transfer, and other incidental matters to carry out the Act's provisions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Karnataka State Government and its authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including acquisition, transfer, and potential penalties related to non-compliance or disputes.

obligations: Obligation to comply with the acquisition and transfer procedures outlined in the Act.
Obligation for the Government to establish a machinery for effective implementation.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Insertion of a new section 19A into the principal Act (Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996).
Procedure 2: Section 19A empowers the Government to make necessary provisions for acquisition, transfer, and related matters.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the relevant department of the Karnataka State Government responsible for land acquisition and estate matters.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act is an amendment to the Roierich and Devikarani Roierich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996.
Note 2: The commencement of this amendment act is retrospective, effective from November 16, 1996.
Note 3: Section 19A deals with the Government's power to facilitate the acquisition, transfer, and related financial matters.

title: THE BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, and the Mysore Act VI of 1948 to validate the levy and collection of property tax and to make provisions for repealing and savings, by addressing certain procedural and legal lacunae identified by the High Court.
scope: This act applies to the Bangalore Development Authority and its jurisdiction, and it amends existing laws related to property tax in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section likely provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into effect.
This section details amendments made to the Karnataka Act 12 of 1976, which is the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Mysore Act VI of 1948
main_sections.description: This section details amendments made to the Mysore Act VI of 1948.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of property tax
main_sections.description: This section addresses the validation of past property tax levies and collections.
This section deals with the repeal of any existing provisions that are inconsistent with this Act and provides for savings.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has been levying and collecting property tax on lands and buildings. A notification under Section 29 of the BDA Act, 1976, was issued for this purpose.
Rule 2: The BDA Act, 1976, does not grant the BDA the power to levy and collect such property tax.
Rule 3: The property tax levied and collected is not rendered by the BDA to the property owners.
Rule 4: The property tax is service-related and the property owner is liable to be refunded.

Rule 5: The High Court in Writ Appeal No. 5092-5290/1998 and Writ Petition No. 3597-3599/1999 had held that the BDA Act, 1976, was not amended prior to the incorporation of Sections 28A, 28B and 28C along with a validating provision.
Rule 6: The High Court further held that the BDA Act, 1956, was challenged before the High Court in Writ Petition No. 7559-7575/1995 by Shri B. Krishna Bhat.
Rule 7: The High Court has upheld the validation of Sections 28A to 28C of the BDA Act, 1976, which were incorporated by the 1951 Amendment Act.
Rule 8: The High Court's decision stated that the tax collected is liable to be refunded.
Rule 9: The Bangalore Development Authority has been discharging municipal functions in respect of its layouts till they are handed over to the respective Municipal Corporations.
Rule 10: In the circumstances, it is considered necessary to amend the BDA Act, 1976, to empower the BDA to levy and collect property tax for its layouts.
Rule 11: Further, it has also been held that the tax already collected is liable to be refunded.
Rule 12: The BDA has been providing most of the civic amenities provided by the local authority in the layouts formed by it.

Rule 13: In order to obviate the aforesaid situation, it is considered necessary to amend the BDA Act, 1976, to empower the BDA to levy property tax prior to the handing over of the layouts for the municipal corporations.
Rule 14: Such requisitions for refund of tax in accordance with the Supreme Court judgment would be impossible for the BDA.
Rule 15: The BDA has been discharging municipal functions in respect of its layouts till they are handed over to the respective Municipal Corporations.
Rule 16: In the circumstances, it is considered necessary to amend the BDA Act, 1976, to empower the BDA to levy and collect property tax for its layouts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bangalore Development Authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing acts and insertion of new sections to empower the BDA to levy and collect property tax.

rights: Right to claim refund of property tax if deemed improperly levied.
duties: Duty of the Bangalore Development Authority to levy and collect property tax for its layouts.
obligations: The BDA has an obligation to provide civic amenities in its layouts until they are handed over to municipal corporations.
The BDA has an obligation to comply with Supreme Court judgments regarding tax refunds.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, to insert new sections (28A, 28B, 28C) and a validating provision.
Procedure 2: Amendment of the Mysore Act VI of 1948.
Procedure 3: Validation of levy and collection of property tax by the BDA for its layouts.
Procedure 4: Issuance of notifications by the BDA for the levy and collection of property tax.
administration: Bangalore Development Authority
important_notes: The act aims to rectify the legal situation where the BDA was levying property tax without explicit legislative power, as identified by the High Court.
The High Court's judgments indicated that collected tax might be liable for refund, creating a need for legislative validation.
The BDA's role in providing civic amenities in its layouts until handover to municipal bodies is a key consideration for the BDA's tax collection powers.

title: THE KARNATAKA HOME GUARDS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, to provide for the procedure for selection and appointment of Commandants of Home Guards, their qualifications, conditions of service, and term of office, along with consequential amendments.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Home Guards organization and its administration within the state of Karnataka. It specifically amends provisions related to the selection, appointment, qualifications, service conditions, and tenure of Commandants of Home Guards.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Home Guards (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by substituting the State Government's general power to appoint Commandants with a process involving a selection committee. It introduces a committee for selecting Commandants, outlines its composition, the committee's role in preparing an eligibility list, and details regarding the Commandant's term of office and appointment conditions.
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act by replacing a reference to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Amends Section 12 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (aa) that specifies the qualification and selection procedure for Commandants under Section 3(2B) and the terms and conditions of their appointment.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government shall appoint Commandants from a list of eligible persons sent by a Committee. (Amended Section 3(2))

Rule 2: A Committee consisting of the Secretary to Government (Home and Transport Dept.), Commandant General (Home Guards and Civil Defence), and Deputy Commandant General (Home Guards and Civil Defence) will be formed for selecting Commandants. (Section 3(2A))
Rule 3: The Committee must follow a prescribed procedure to prepare a list of eligible persons for appointment as Commandants and submit it to the State Government. (Section 3(2B))
Rule 4: The term of office for Commandants will ordinarily be five years, subject to the State Government's pleasure, and may be extended for another five years. (Section 3(2C))
Rule 5: The terms and conditions of appointment for Commandants will be as prescribed. (Section 3(2D))

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and relevant authorities within the Home Guards organization.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administrative and legal framework established by the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, as amended by this Act, and by ensuring adherence to the prescribed procedures and conditions for Commandants.

rights: Right of eligible persons to be considered for appointment as Commandants based on prescribed qualifications and selection procedures.
duties: Duty of the selection committee to follow prescribed procedures and prepare an eligibility list.
Duty of the State Government to appoint Commandants based on the committee's list.
Duty of Commandants to serve for the prescribed term and adhere to appointment conditions.
obligations: Obligation to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure reference from 1898 to 1973.
Obligation to prescribe qualifications, selection procedures, and terms of appointment for Commandants.

key_procedures: Procedure for Selection and Appointment of Commandants: (1) A Committee is formed. (2) The Committee, following prescribed procedures, prepares a list of eligible persons. (3) The list is sent to the State Government. (4) The State Government appoints Commandants from this list. (Amended Section 3)
Procedure for updating legal references: Substituting the reference to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. (Section 3)
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for enactment), Home and Transport Department and Home Guards and Civil Defence (for operational administration of Commandants).
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The term of office for Commandants is a maximum of ten years (initial five years plus a possible extension of five years), subject to the State Government's pleasure.
Specific qualifications and detailed terms and conditions for Commandants are to be prescribed separately.

title: THE BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, specifically to empower the Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority, to sanction estimates up to rupees fifty lakhs, and to empower the Bangalore Development Authority for amounts exceeding fifty lakhs up to an amount specified by the State Government.
scope: This Act applies to the Bangalore Development Authority and its administrative functions related to sanctioning estimates. It amends the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Bangalore Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends Section 10 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976. It substitutes the words 'twenty lakhs' with 'fifty lakhs' in sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 10, thereby increasing the financial power for sanctioning estimates.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority, is empowered to sanction estimates up to rupees fifty lakhs.

Rule 2: The Bangalore Development Authority is empowered to sanction estimates where the amount exceeds rupees fifty lakhs but does not exceed such amount as may be specified by the State Government by notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bangalore Development Authority and its Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administrative and financial powers vested in the Commissioner and the Authority as amended by this Act.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is aimed at increasing the financial delegation for sanctioning estimates within the Bangalore Development Authority.
The specific financial limit for the Bangalore Development Authority, beyond fifty lakhs, is subject to future notification by the State Government.

title: THE BANGALORE WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To provide for making it mandatory to build rainwater harvesting structures by households to preserve groundwater by amending the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964.
scope: The Act applies to owners or occupiers of buildings in Bangalore with a sital area of 2400 square feet and above, and owners proposing to construct buildings on a sital area of 1200 square feet and above. It also applies to the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board.

key_definitions.sital area: Area of land on which a building is situated, specified as 2400 square feet and above for existing buildings and 1200 square feet and above for proposed buildings.
key_definitions.rain water harvesting structure: A structure designed to collect and store rainwater.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2009, and that it comes into force at once.
Inserts a new section (72A) into the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964, which mandates the provision of rainwater harvesting structures.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every owner or occupier of a building having a sital area of 2400 square feet and above shall provide for a rain water harvesting structure within nine months from the date of commencement of the Act.
Rule 2: Every owner who proposes to construct a building on a sital area of 1200 square feet and above shall provide for a rain water harvesting structure.
Rule 3: The rain water harvesting structure must be provided in such manner and with such conditions as may be provided in the regulations.

penalties: If an owner or occupier fails to provide a rain water harvesting structure, the Board may cause such structure to be provided and recover the cost from the owner or occupier as arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (the Board).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Board can directly construct the rainwater harvesting structure and recover the costs as arrears of land revenue.

rights: The right of the Board to undertake the construction of rainwater harvesting structures and recover costs.
duties: The duty of owners and occupiers to provide rainwater harvesting structures within stipulated timelines and according to regulations.
The duty of owners proposing to construct buildings to include rainwater harvesting structures.
obligations: Obligation to provide rain water harvesting structure for buildings with specified sital areas.
Obligation to comply with regulations regarding the manner and conditions of providing the structure.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: An owner or occupier must provide a rain water harvesting structure within nine months of the Act's commencement for existing buildings with a sital area of 2400 sq ft and above.
Procedure 2: An owner proposing to construct a building on a sital area of 1200 sq ft and above must include a rain water harvesting structure.
Procedure 3: In case of non-compliance, the Board may construct the structure and recover costs as arrears of land revenue.
administration: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 36 of 1964).
The specific manner and conditions for providing the rain water harvesting structure will be detailed in the regulations.

title: THE KARNATAKA EXCISE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend Section 67 of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, to extend the benefit of exemption of tax on liquor to diplomatic agents, in addition to members of the Armed Forces.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965. It applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the taxation of liquor sales.

key_definitions.diplomatic agents: Individuals holding diplomatic status, whose offices (consulates) are functioning within the State.
key_definitions.armed forces: Includes members of the Armed Forces (including Para-Military units) of the Union.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Karnataka Excise (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends clause (a) of Section 67 of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, by substituting sub-clause (i) to include 'diplomatic agents' along with 'members of the Armed Forces (including Para-Military units) of the Union' for whom excise dues on liquor can be exempted or reduced.

important_rules: Rule 1: Section 67(1)(i) of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, is amended to provide an enabling provision for the State Government to exempt or reduce excise dues on liquor for diplomatic agents.
Rule 2: The exemption or reduction of excise dues on liquor now applies to both members of the Armed Forces (including Para-Military units) of the Union and Diplomatic agents.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through its excise department, implied by the parent act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By virtue of the amendment, the State Government has the power to grant exemptions or reductions in excise dues.

rights: Right of the State Government to exempt or reduce excise dues on liquor for specified categories.
Right of Diplomatic agents to receive exemption of tax on liquor for their use or consumption.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government, in accordance with the amended Section 67(1)(i), can issue notifications to exempt or reduce excise dues on liquor for diplomatic agents.
Procedure 2: The amendment itself is the key procedural change, enabling the government to act upon the new provision.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the amendment process), and the Excise Department of the State Government (for administration of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965).
important_notes: The amendment is based on the privilege of the State Government to extend tax benefits on liquor to diplomats as a matter of honouring their dignity.
The amendment is made to the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965 (Karnataka Act 21 of 1966).

title: THE NATIONAL LAW SCHOOL OF INDIA (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the National Law School of India Act, 1986, to substitute the word 'Chancellor' with 'Visitor' and to provide that the Chief Justice of India or his nominee, who shall be a sitting Judge of the Supreme Court of India, shall be the 'Visitor' of the School.
scope: This act applies to the National Law School of India and its administration within the state of Karnataka.

key_definitions.visitor: The Visitor of the school, as defined in the amended section 2(13) of the Principal Act. It is further specified that the Chief Justice of India or his nominee, who is a sitting Judge of the Supreme Court, shall be the Visitor.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the National Law School of India (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it comes into force at once.
This section amends clause (13) of section 2 of the National Law School of India Act, 1986 (Principal Act), to define 'visitor' as 'the visitor of the school'.

This section substitutes sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Principal Act to declare that the Chief Justice of India or his nominee, who is a sitting Judge of the Supreme Court, shall be the Visitor of the School.
This section mandates the substitution of the word 'chancellor' with the word 'visitor' wherever it appears in the Principal Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Chief Justice of India or his nominee, who is a sitting Judge of the Supreme Court, shall be the Visitor of the National Law School of India.
Rule 2: The term 'Chancellor' in the National Law School of India Act, 1986, shall be replaced with the term 'Visitor'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the administrative bodies responsible for the National Law School of India and its governing legislation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and observance of the amended National Law School of India Act, 1986.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is a response to a request from the Chief Justice of India.
The amendment restores the title 'Visitor' to its pre-2004 status, with a specific designation for the role.
The Act is enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature.

title: THE KARNATAKA TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC PROCUREMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, to exempt construction works not exceeding Rs. 2 crores, entrusted by any procurement entity to the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited, from certain provisions of the Act, with consequential and incidental amendments.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999. The specific amendment pertains to construction works in rural and urban areas entrusted to the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited, where the value does not exceed Rupees Two Crores. It applies to procurement entities within Karnataka.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements (Amendment) Act, 2021' and specifies that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 4 of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, by inserting a new clause (e4). This new clause exempts construction works of all types in rural and urban areas, not exceeding Rupees Two Crores in value, when entrusted to the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited. It includes provisos regarding sub-letting through tendering and reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

important_rules: Construction works of all types in rural and urban areas, with a value not exceeding Rupees Two Crores, entrusted to the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited, are exempted from certain provisions of the Act.
The Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited shall execute the entrusted works by itself.
In case sub-letting of construction works is necessary, it must be done through tendering in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

When sub-letting construction works through tender, it shall be reserved in favour of persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in accordance with the provisos to Section 6 of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act itself does not specify a new enforcement authority; it amends the principal Act, which implies the existing enforcement mechanisms under the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, will apply.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would be through the mechanisms established by the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, which may include scrutiny of procurement processes and adherence to the stipulated rules.

rights: Right to tender for sub-letting of construction works for persons belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
duties: Duty of the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited to execute entrusted works by itself.
Duty to conduct tendering for sub-letting if necessary.
Duty to reserve sub-letting tenders in favour of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
obligations: Obligation for procurement entities to follow the amended provisions when entrusting construction works.
Obligation for the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited to adhere to the conditions of sub-letting and reservation.

key_procedures: Entrustment of construction works (under Rs. 2 crores) to Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited.
Execution of works by Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited.
Sub-letting of works through tendering, if necessary.
Reservation of sub-letting tenders for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is responsible for the legislative aspect. The administration of the principal Act and its amendments would generally fall under the purview of the departments responsible for public procurement and rural infrastructure development.
important_notes: The exemption applies only to construction works not exceeding Rs. 2 crores.
The Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited is designated as the entity to which these works can be entrusted.
The Act emphasizes execution by the entrusted entity itself, with strict conditions for sub-letting.
Specific provisions for reservation in favour of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes during sub-letting are included.

title: THE KARNATAKA RESERVATION OF APPOINTMENTS OF POSTS (IN THE CIVIL SERVICES OF THE STATE) FOR RURAL CANDIDATES ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for reservation of appointments of posts in the civil services of the State for rural candidates, and to provide for removal of difficulties. The act aims to ensure representation for rural candidates in civil services due to previous judgments by the High Court of Karnataka and the Supreme Court of India which deemed existing provisions inadequate.
scope: This Act applies to appointments of posts in the civil services of the State of Karnataka for rural candidates. It specifically addresses reservations in Group A and Group B civil services.

key_definitions.rural candidate: A person who has studied and passed the Second Standard onwards, where the educational institutions are situated in rural areas, having population of less than 25,000 as per the 1981 census. The definition was modified to be a person who has studied and passed the tenth standard in any of the schools situated in rural areas and Group A and Group B and the term 'rural candidate' was defined as a person, who has studied and passed the State of Karnataka, (i) from first standard to tenth standard.
key_definitions.civil services of the State: Includes appointments to posts in Group C and Group D civil services of the State.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'rural candidate' and 'civil services of the State'.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of appointments or posts for rural candidates
main_sections.description: Mandates the reservation of appointments or posts for rural candidates in the civil services of the State.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make orders to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Reservation of appointments for rural candidates in civil services of the State is to be implemented.
Rule 2: The government can make rules to effectively implement the provisions of this Act.
Rule 3: The government has the power to issue orders to resolve any difficulties encountered in the application of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka (implied through the power to make rules and remove difficulties).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of reservation policies and the issuance of rules and orders by the Government.

rights: Rural candidates have the right to be considered for reservation in civil service appointments.
duties: The State Government has a duty to implement the reservation for rural candidates.
The State Government has a duty to make rules and issue orders to facilitate the implementation of the Act.
obligations: The Government is obligated to ensure that rural candidates receive the intended benefits of the reservation policy.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Identification of eligible 'rural candidates' based on educational qualifications and area of study.
Procedure 2: Application of reservation percentages for the identified rural candidates in civil service recruitment processes.
Procedure 3: Government to issue orders to remove difficulties, ensuring smooth implementation of the Act.
administration: The Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to address the shortfall in reservation for rural candidates, as highlighted by judicial pronouncements.

The definition of 'rural candidate' was amended to include those who have studied from first standard to tenth standard in schools located in rural areas. Previous definition of 50% of population as rural was also revised.
The Act covers the period of reservation from 1991 to 2000 and also provides for further extension.

title: The Factories (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To amend the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act LXIII of 1948) in its application to the Karnataka State to make provisions for the appointment of a Welfare Officer, Medical Officer, and Female Supervisor in factories employing more than 200 workers.
scope: This act applies to factories within the State of Karnataka. It amends existing provisions related to the employment of workers and the appointment of specific roles within factories based on the number of employees.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the 'Factories (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2002'. It also states that the Act will come into force from a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
This section amends sub-section (4) of section 45 of the principal Act (Factories Act, 1948). It substitutes the word 'five hundred' with 'two hundred'.

This section amends section 49 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'five hundred' with 'two hundred' in sub-section (1). It also inserts a new sub-section (1A) which mandates the employment of female supervisors in every factory where two hundred or more women workers are ordinarily employed, with the number of supervisors to be prescribed.

important_rules: Rule: In factories where more than 200 workers are employed, the threshold for certain appointments or provisions has been reduced from 500 to 200.
Rule: In every factory where two hundred or more women workers are ordinarily employed, the occupier shall employ such number of female supervisors as may be prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notification for commencement and prescribing numbers of supervisors)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the State Government through notification and by ensuring compliance with the amended provisions of the Factories Act, 1948.

rights: Right to have Welfare Officers, Medical Officers, and Female Supervisors appointed in factories meeting the employment criteria.
duties: Duty of the occupier to appoint Welfare Officers, Medical Officers, and Female Supervisors in factories meeting the employment criteria.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the reduced worker threshold (200) for specific appointments.
Obligation to employ a prescribed number of female supervisors if 200 or more women workers are employed.

key_procedures: Procedure: The State Government may appoint a date by notification for the Act to come into force.
Procedure: Amendments to Section 45 and Section 49 of the Factories Act, 1948 are enacted, changing numerical thresholds and introducing requirements for female supervisors.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory M.R.HEGDE, Secretary)
important_notes: The Act is a Karnataka State amendment to the Central Factories Act, 1948.
The specific number of female supervisors to be employed will be determined by prescribed rules.

title: The Information Technology Investment Regions Act, 2010
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Information Technology Investment Regions (ITIRs) in the State of Karnataka and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the establishment and functioning of Information Technology Investment Regions within the state.

main_sections.description: Specifies the date on which the provisions of the Act shall come into force. The notification states this date is the 29th July 2010.

important_rules: All provisions of the Information Technology Investment Regions Act, 2010, shall come into force on 29th July 2010.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a commencement date for the Act's provisions.

key_procedures: The Government of Karnataka, in exercise of its powers, notifies the date on which the Act comes into force.
administration: Department of Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: This document is a notification bringing the Information Technology Investment Regions Act, 2010 into force.
The notification specifies that the Act comes into force on 29th July 2010, based on the powers conferred by Section 1(2) of the Act.

title: The Karnataka Advocates’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010
purpose: To bring into force all the provisions of The Karnataka Advocates’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010.
scope: The act applies to advocates within the state of Karnataka.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By appointing a date for the commencement of the Act's provisions.

key_procedures: The Government of Karnataka exercises powers conferred by sub-section (2) of Section 1 of the Act.
The Government appoints a specific date (6th August 2010) as the commencement date for all provisions of the Act.
administration: Department of Law, Justice & Human Rights, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: This notification specifically brings the Karnataka Advocates’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010 into effect. The details of the original Act and the amendments are not provided in this snippet.
The notification is issued by the Law, Justice & Human Rights Department of the Government of Karnataka.

title: THE KARNATAKA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Forest Act, 1963, to impose restrictions on the growing of Sandalwood trees in private lands and to provide for the amendment of the definition of 'Divisional Forest Officer' and to modify the penalties for forest offences.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and deals with forest offences, specifically concerning Sandalwood trees and their cultivation in private lands.

key_definitions.Divisional Forest Officer: The Deputy Conservator of Forests or officer designated as such.
key_definitions.Forest Officer: The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, the Chief Conservator of Forests, or any officer appointed under the Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Forest (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

In section 2 of the Karnataka Forest Act, 1963 (Karnataka Act 5 of 1964) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in clause (1), for the words "Deputy Conservator of Forests", the words "Deputy Conservator of Forests or officer designated as such" shall be substituted.
After section 51 of the principal Act, a new section 51A shall be inserted.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on the growing of Sandalwood trees
main_sections.description: No person shall grow Sandalwood trees in his land except with the permission of the Forest Officer, obtained in writing.
For section 56 of the principal Act, the following shall be substituted, namely: "56. Penalties for offences relating to Sandalwood trees.

All persons whether by the terms of their sannads, grants, or by judicial decision or otherwise, are legally entitled to the sandalwood trees in their lands shall not fell or sell such sandalwood trees or convert or transport or fell such sandalwood trees so obtained except in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
After section 83 of the principal Act, the following shall be inserted, namely: '83A. Certain acts to be punishable.

Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 51A shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. (2) On or after the commencement of the Karnataka Forest (Amendment) Act, 2001, whoever cultivates sandalwood trees shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

important_rules: Rule: No person shall grow Sandalwood trees in their land without obtaining prior written permission from the Forest Officer.
Rule: Individuals legally entitled to Sandalwood trees on their land must adhere to the Act's provisions for felling, selling, converting, or transporting these trees.
Rule: Cultivating Sandalwood trees without following the Act's regulations is a punishable offence.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both for contravening section 51A (restriction on growing Sandalwood trees).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both for cultivating Sandalwood trees after the commencement of the amendment act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Forest Officers, including the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, Chief Conservator of Forests, and officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves penalizing individuals who contravene the provisions related to Sandalwood cultivation and felling through imprisonment, fines, or both.

rights: Individuals legally entitled to Sandalwood trees on their land have the right to those trees, subject to the Act's regulations on felling and sale.
The right to obtain written permission from the Forest Officer to grow Sandalwood trees.
duties: Duty to obtain written permission from the Forest Officer before growing Sandalwood trees.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding the felling, sale, conversion, and transportation of Sandalwood trees.
Duty to ensure that any Sandalwood trees obtained or cultivated are done so in accordance with the Act.
obligations: Obligation to be punished as per the Act if Sandalwood trees are grown or cultivated without adhering to the stipulated rules.
Obligation to inform the State Government regarding any Sandalwood trees obtained or the right to fell such trees.

key_procedures: Procedure: Obtain written permission from the Forest Officer before growing Sandalwood trees on private land.
Procedure: Follow the rules outlined in the Act for felling, selling, converting, or transporting Sandalwood trees, even if legally entitled to them.
Procedure: Comply with the amended definition of Divisional Forest Officer and Forest Officer.
administration: The State Government and Forest Officers are responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
important_notes: The amendment aims to regulate the cultivation of Sandalwood trees in private lands to prevent illicit felling.
The definition of 'Divisional Forest Officer' has been amended to include designated officers.
The Act specifically addresses the situation of individuals who are legally entitled to Sandalwood trees on their land, ensuring they still operate within the legal framework.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE COMMISSION FOR THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND THE SCHEDULED TRIBES BILL, 2002
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Karnataka State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with the constitution and functioning of the Karnataka State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and when it comes into force.
Defines key terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Commission for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
main_sections.description: Establishes the State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.section_title: Terms of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Outlines the terms of office and service conditions for the Chairperson and Members of the Commission.
Deals with the appointment and functioning of staff for the Commission.
Details the various functions and responsibilities of the Commission.
Specifies the procedure for laying the Commission's report.
Grants powers to the Commission, such as summoning witnesses and examining documents.
Describes the financial support provided by the State Government to the Commission.
Covers the financial accounts and auditing procedures of the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Member and employee of the Commission to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Members, and employees of the Commission as public servants.
Grants the government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and saving provisions.

important_rules: The Commission shall consist of a Chairperson and such number of Members as the State Government may deem fit.
The Chairperson and Members shall be appointed by the State Government.
The Commission shall have the power to investigate and examine all matters relating to the constitutional and other legal safeguards for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The Commission shall submit an annual report to the State Government on the matters dealt with by it.
The State Government shall lay before the State Legislature the report submitted by the Commission and the action taken or proposed to be taken on the recommendation contained therein.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Commission itself.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, examinations, recommendations, and reporting to the State Legislature. The Act also declares Commission members as public servants, implying legal recourse for non-compliance.

rights: The right to investigate and examine matters concerning safeguards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The right to summon witnesses and examine documents.
The right to make recommendations to the State Government.
The right to have its annual reports laid before the State Legislature.
duties: To investigate and examine all matters relating to the constitutional and other legal safeguards for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
To monitor and evaluate the implementation of safeguards and policies for these communities.
To submit annual reports to the State Government.
To inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
obligations: To perform its functions and duties as outlined in the Act.
To conduct investigations and inquiries effectively.
To prepare and submit timely reports to the State Government.
To ensure accountability in its financial dealings.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission with a Chairperson and Members appointed by the State Government.
Investigation and examination of matters relating to safeguards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Submission of annual reports to the State Government.
Laying of these reports before the State Legislature by the State Government.
Inquiry into specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards.
administration: The State Government, through its relevant departments, and the Karnataka State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a dedicated statutory body for the welfare and protection of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Karnataka.
The Commission's recommendations are not binding but carry significant weight, and the State Government is obligated to report on actions taken.
The Act aims to facilitate the socio-economic and educational development of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, by allowing certain corporations to acquire agricultural land, and by empowering the Deputy Commissioner to grant exemptions for specific non-agricultural land uses.
scope: This act applies to lands within the State of Karnataka, amending the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It specifically addresses the acquisition of agricultural property by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd., and grants the Deputy Commissioner powers to exempt certain lands from specific provisions of the principal Act for industrial development, educational institutions, places of worship, housing projects, and horticulture/agro-based industries.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 81 of the principal Act to include the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation and the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited as entities in whose favour agricultural property can be acquired.

Amends section 109 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso that empowers the Deputy Commissioner to grant exemptions for land use for specific purposes, subject to prescribed restrictions and conditions. It also amends sub-section (2) to allow the Deputy Commissioner to exercise powers similar to the State Government in certain contexts.

important_rules: Agricultural property can be acquired by sale, gift, or mortgage in favour of the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited.

The Deputy Commissioner may grant exemptions under section 109 of the principal Act for land to be used for industrial development (up to ten units), educational institutions (up to two units), places of worship (up to one-fourth of a unit), housing projects (up to ten units), and horticulture/agro-based industries (up to ten units).
The exercise of exemption powers by the Deputy Commissioner is subject to the same restrictions and in the same manner as specified in section 109 of the principal Act.
