penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner and potentially other authorities under the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Deputy Commissioner and other relevant authorities under the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, including the granting or refusal of exemptions and adherence to stipulated restrictions.

rights: Right of Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited to acquire agricultural land under specified conditions.
Right of landowners to seek exemptions for certain land uses under section 109, as exercised by the Deputy Commissioner.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the restrictions and conditions set forth in the amended section 109 when seeking exemptions.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Application for exemption under section 109 by specifying the purpose of land use and extent, to be considered by the Deputy Commissioner.
Granting of exemptions by the Deputy Commissioner, subject to specified restrictions and manner.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the Deputy Commissioner.
important_notes: The exemptions granted by the Deputy Commissioner are subject to specific unit limits for each purpose.
The amendments are made to the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 (Karnataka Act 10 of 1962).

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC PREMISES (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, specifically to include the Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bangalore, in the definition of 'public premises' for the purpose of protecting its land from unauthorized occupation.
scope: This amendment applies to the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974. It specifically expands the definition of 'public premises' to include the land held by the Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bangalore. The geographical scope is within Karnataka. The subject matter scope is related to the eviction of unauthorized occupants from public premises.

key_definitions.public_premises: As defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, now including 'the Institute for social and economic change, Bangalore'.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it comes into force at once.

This section amends Section 2 of the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, by inserting 'the Institute for social and economic change, Bangalore' into clause (e) after item (iii), thereby expanding the definition of 'public premises'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in this amendment, but the original Act would specify the relevant authorities for eviction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in this amendment, but the original Act would specify the methods of enforcement.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment comes into force 'at once'.
The Institute for Social and Economic Change is a registered society under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and is funded by the Central and State Governments.
The land in question was granted to the Institute on a long-term lease by Bangalore University as per the direction of the Government of Karnataka.

title: THE KARNATAKA CO-OPERATIVE TEXTILE MILLS (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1986, to address issues related to land ownership and disbursement of amounts following the acquisition and transfer of co-operative textile mills, particularly in light of High Court directives.
scope: This Act applies to the co-operative textile mills in Karnataka that were subject to the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1986. It specifically addresses the rights and interests of lessors, lessees, and owners of land leased for the purpose of these mills.

key_definitions.principal_act: The Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1986 (Karnataka Act 29 of 1986).
key_definitions.owner_of_land: A person to whom the land specified in the annexure appended to this Act belonged and which is held on lease for the purpose of the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills, and includes any person who claims title to such land as his heir or legal representative.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills (Acquisition and Transfer) (Amendment) Act, 2004, and states that it is deemed to have come into force with effect from June 30, 1986.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting definitions for 'owner of land' and expanding the scope of land covered to include land belonging to the owner leased for the mills.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by inserting the term 'owner of land' alongside 'lessor and lessee'.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act to include 'owner of land' in provisions related to persons who are to be deemed to have been in possession or who have an interest in the property, and clarifies 'amount or other dues'.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by including 'owner of land' in the context of persons to whom payments may be made.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act by including 'owner of land' in the context of persons to whom payments may be made.
Amends section 16 of the principal Act by including 'owner of land' alongside 'other interested persons'.

Inserts a new section (22A) detailing the disbursement of amounts to lessors, lessees, and owners of land after meeting liabilities, and provisions for handling doubts or disputes regarding rightful entitlement by referring to the Court.

Inserts an Annexure after the Schedule of the principal Act, listing specific landed properties vested with the Government as per sections 4 and 5 of the principal Act, including their area, survey numbers, and boundaries.

important_rules: Rule: If, after meeting liabilities from the amount paid in relation to the Mills, a balance remains, the Commissioner shall disburse this balance to the lessor, lessee, and owner of land.

Rule: The Commissioner must satisfy himself about the right of the lessor, lessee, or owner of land to receive any part of the disbursed amount. In case of doubt or dispute, the matter shall be referred to the Court for decision.
Rule: The Court shall decide the apportionment of amounts among the lessor, lessee, or owner of land, considering the value of the property as of the appointed day.
Rule: Evidence is admissible to establish the right, title, and interest of the lessor, lessee, or owner of land in relation to the Mills before the Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner, as referred to in Section 22A, and the Court for dispute resolution.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of disbursement of amounts, investigation into claims of ownership, and court proceedings for dispute resolution.

rights: Right of owners of land to receive their share of any balance amount after liabilities are met.
Right to claim title to land leased for the mills as an heir or legal representative.
Right to have disputes regarding entitlement to disbursed amounts resolved by the Court.
Right to present evidence before the Court to establish title and interest in relation to the Mills.
duties: Duty of the Commissioner to disburse balance amounts to lessors, lessees, and owners of land.
Duty of the Commissioner to verify entitlement before disbursement.
Duty to refer disputes to the Court.
Duty of the Court to decide apportionment based on property value.
obligations: Obligation to establish title and interest to claim disbursed amounts.
Obligation to abide by court decisions regarding apportionment.

key_procedures: Procedure for Disbursement: The Commissioner identifies any balance amount after meeting liabilities of the Mills, verifies the rights of lessors, lessees, and owners of land, and disburses the balance accordingly. If there is doubt or dispute, the matter is referred to the Court.

Procedure for Dispute Resolution: In case of doubt or dispute regarding the right to receive the whole or any part of the amount, or its apportionment, the Commissioner shall refer the matter to the Court. The Court will then decide the apportionment, considering the value of the property and admitting evidence to establish rights, title, and interest.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is involved in the publication and enactment of the Act, and the Commissioner is responsible for administration of disbursements.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from June 30, 1986.

The Annexure lists specific landed properties vested with the Government but explicitly excludes properties sold by the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills Ltd. or acquired by other Government authorities before 1986.

title: THE KARNATAKA STAMP (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, specifically to reduce the stamp duty on sale transactions of all kinds of immovable properties, including agricultural land, from seven and a half percent to six percent, as announced in the Budget Speech for the year 2009-2010. This act also replaces the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. Its subject matter scope pertains to stamp duties on sale transactions of immovable properties.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Stamp (Second Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it is deemed to have come into force with effect from 4th June 2009.

Amends the Schedule of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. It modifies Article 20 by omitting a proviso and substituting the stamp duty for certain clauses. It also amends Article 41 by substituting the stamp duty for a specific clause.

Repeals the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009. It also provides that anything done or any action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the repealed ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Stamp duty on sale transactions of all kinds of immovable properties, including agricultural land, is reduced from seven and a half percent to six percent.
Rule: In Article 20 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, in clause (1), the proviso is omitted.
Rule: In Article 20 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, in clause (2), in column (3), the words ‘seven and a half percent’ are substituted with ‘the same duty as a conveyance under Article 20(1)’.

Rule: In Article 41 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, in clause (eb), in column 3, the words ‘seven rupees and fifty paise for every one hundred rupees or part thereof’ are substituted with ‘the same duty as a conveyance under Article 20(1)’.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but generally assumed to be the State Government or its designated authorities responsible for stamp duty collection.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but would involve the assessment and collection of stamp duties as per the amended Act.

duties: Duty to pay the reduced stamp duty as per the amended provisions.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the amended stamp duty rates for sale transactions of immovable properties.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of the Schedule of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, to reflect the reduced stamp duty rates for immovable property transactions.
Procedure: Repeal of the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009, and ensuring continuity of actions taken under it.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as per the signature of the Secretary to Government). The overall administration would likely involve the Revenue Department or its equivalent in Karnataka.
important_notes: Note: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from 4th June 2009.
Note: The Act replaces the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (Karnataka Ordinance No.5 of 2009).

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE CIVIL SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978, to dispense with the requirement of previous publication of rules specifying only the number and nature of posts created, and to update the reference to the Prevention of Corruption Act.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978, and applies to civil services in the state of Karnataka. It specifically deals with the creation of posts and references to corruption prevention legislation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka State Civil Services (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act (Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978) by inserting a proviso to sub-section (2). This proviso exempts rules specifying only the number and nature of posts from a certain requirement (implied to be previous publication).

Amends section 5 of the principal Act. It substitutes the reference to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, with the reference to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, in the explanation to sub-section (3).

important_rules: Rules specifying only the number and nature of posts created are exempt from a requirement of previous publication (as per the amendment to Section 3).
References to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, in relation to Section 5 of the principal Act are replaced with references to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly the relevant departments and authorities responsible for administering the Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978, and related rules.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory and the source of the Act). The overall administration would fall under the purview of the Karnataka government departments dealing with civil services.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 3rd day of May, 2010.
The Act was first published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on the 6th day of May, 2010.
The amendment to Section 5 updates the legal framework concerning corruption prevention, aligning it with the more recent central legislation.

title: THE KARNATAKA HOME GUARDS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, to provide for the extension of the office of the Commandant for a period of five years and further periods of two terms of five years each, and to fix the maximum age limit for the post of Commandants.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, and specifically amends Section 3 of that act concerning the term of office and age limit for Commandants. It is enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Home Guards (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 3 of the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962. It substitutes sub-section (2c) to state that the term of office of the Commandant shall ordinarily be for five years, extendable for two further terms of five years each, subject to the pleasure of the State Government. It also introduces a proviso that no person shall be eligible for appointment or hold the office of Commandant upon attaining the age of sixty years.

important_rules: The term of office of the Commandant shall ordinarily be for five years.
The term of office of the Commandant may be extended for a further period of two terms of five years each.
No person shall be eligible for appointment as Commandant or shall hold such office on their attaining the age of sixty years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, and administrative decisions regarding appointments and extensions of Commandants.

duties: Duty of the State Government to adhere to the provisions regarding the term and age limit for Commandants.
Duty of individuals seeking or holding the position of Commandant to comply with the age limit.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 3 of the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, by substitution of sub-section (2c).
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory). The administration of the Home Guards Act would typically fall under the Home Department.
important_notes: The extension of the Commandant's office is subject to the pleasure of the State Government.
The maximum age limit for holding the office of Commandant is sixty years.

title: VIDYASHILP UNIVERSITY ACT, 2020
purpose: To establish and incorporate in the State of Karnataka a University of unitary in nature in the private sector by the Vidyanidhi Education Trust to promote and undertake the advancement of applied University education in Sciences, all branches of Engineering, Arts, Management, Commerce and for the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the establishment and incorporation of the Vidyashilp University, a private university of unitary nature, by the Vidyanidhi Education Trust.

key_definitions.academic_council: The Academic Council of the University as specified in section 26.
key_definitions.agenda_matters: All matters and business to be designated in the Statutes, which can be included in the Agenda or taken up for discussion and decision at a meeting of the Board of Governors, Board of Management, Academic Council, or any other authority or Committee, only subject to the prior written approval of the Chancellor.
key_definitions.board_of_governors: The Board of Governors of the University as specified in section 24.
key_definitions.board_of_management: The Board of Management of the University as specified in section 25.
key_definitions.pro_vice_chancellor: The Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University.
key_definitions.campus: A campus established and maintained by the University, situated within the State.
key_definitions.committees: Committees formed under this Act or by the various functionaries of the University, including the Nomination Committee, the Finance Committee, and other committees.
key_definitions.constituent_college: A college or institution established and maintained by the University.
key_definitions.finance_committee: The Finance Committee of the University as specified in section 28.
key_definitions.national_accreditation_bodies: Bodies established by the Central Government for laying down norms and conditions for ensuring academic standards of higher education, such as University Grants Commission, All India Council of Technical Education, National Council of Teacher Education, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, Council of Architecture, and includes the Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.principal_in_relation_to_a_constituent_c: The head of the Constituent College, and includes the Vice-Principal or any other person for the time being appointed to act as Principal in the absence of the Principal.
key_definitions.regional_centre: A centre established or maintained by the University for coordinating and supervising the work of Study Centres in any region within the State and for performing other functions as conferred by the Board of Management.
key_definitions.statutes_and_regulations: The Statutes and Regulations of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.study_centre: A centre within the State established and maintained by the University for advising, counseling, or rendering other assistance required by students in the context of education.
key_definitions.teacher: Includes a Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, or other person appointed for imparting instruction, conducting or guiding research in the University or a Constituent College, and the Principal of a Constituent College, in conformity with UGC norms.
key_definitions.trust: Vidyanidhi Education Trust registered under the Indian Trust Act, 1882.
key_definitions.university_grants_commission: The Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
key_definitions.visitor: The visitor of the University as specified in section 13.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Vidyashilp University Act, 2020. It states that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification in the official Gazette. It also notes that the Act came into force w.e.f. 20.06.2022.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Agenda Matters', 'Board of Governors', 'Board of Management', 'Chancellor', 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Pro Vice-Chancellor', 'Campus', 'Committees', 'Constituent College', 'Finance Committee', 'Government', 'National Accreditation Bodies', 'Prescribed', 'Principal', 'Registrar', 'Regional Centre', 'Sponsoring Authority', 'State', 'Statutes', 'Regulations', 'Study Centre', 'Teacher', 'Trust', 'University', 'University Grants Commission', and 'Visitor'.

main_sections.section_title: Proposal for the establishment of the University
main_sections.description: This section outlines the process for proposing the establishment of the Vidyashilp University. It states that the Vidyanidhi Education Trust has the right to establish the University and must submit a proposal to the State Government containing detailed particulars about the objects, extent, status, land availability, programs, faculties, campus development, financial outlays, expenditure, sources of finance, resource mobilization, fee structure, experience and expertise of the Trust, student selection system, and fulfillment of other conditions. It also mentions the constitution of a Screening Committee by the State Government to examine these proposals.

This section details the conditions under which the State Government can accord sanction for the establishment of the Vidyashilp University. These include the Trust's ability to run a university with sufficient infrastructure, ownership of adequate land (specified acreage based on location), availability of adequate financial resources for statutory funds and university operations, and experience in running higher education institutions. It also covers the establishment of a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund, the headquarters of the University, its corporate status, and the vesting of properties acquired by the Trust in the University.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.
Rule 2: The Vidyashilp University shall be of a unitary nature and established in the private sector by the Vidyanidhi Education Trust.
Rule 3: The University shall be open to all classes, castes, creeds, genders, or nations, without discrimination.
Rule 4: The proposal for establishing the University must include detailed particulars regarding its objectives, financial viability, infrastructure, and academic plans.

Rule 5: The State Government may establish the University only after considering the recommendations of a Screening Committee and being satisfied with the Trust's ability to establish and run the university.

penalties: Section 57 mentions 'Penalties' but the specific details are not provided in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is responsible for sanctioning the establishment of the University and can issue directions. The Registrar is the point of contact for legal proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications by the State Government, establishment of a Screening Committee to review proposals, and potential legal actions where the Registrar is the designated party.

rights: The Vidyanidhi Education Trust has the right to establish the University.
The University has the right to sue and be sued in its name.
Right to appeal is mentioned in Section 41.
duties: The Trust must submit a detailed proposal for the establishment of the University.
The University must maintain funds, submit an Annual Report, and have its accounts audited.
The University must be open to all classes, castes, creeds, genders, or nations.
obligations: The Trust is obligated to establish a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund if directed by the Government.
The University must adhere to the norms specified by the University Grants Commission.
The University's land, building, and other properties shall not be used for commercial purposes (implied by the incomplete sentence).

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Proposal submission for University establishment (Section 3) - The Trust must submit a proposal with detailed particulars to the State Government. A Screening Committee will examine this proposal and make recommendations.

Procedure 2: Establishment of the University (Section 4) - The State Government, after considering the Screening Committee's recommendations and conducting inquiries, may accord sanction for the University's establishment, provided certain conditions are met. This includes the establishment of a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund.
Procedure 3: Making of Statutes (Section 34) - Statutes are to be made by the Board of Governors, subject to the approval of the State Government.
Procedure 4: Making of Regulations (Section 37) - Regulations are to be made by the Board of Management, subject to the approval of the Chancellor.
administration: The State Government plays a significant role in the establishment and oversight of the University. Various authorities within the University, such as the Board of Governors, Board of Management, Academic Council, Chancellor, and Vice-Chancellor, are responsible for its day-to-day administration.
important_notes: The Act specifies land requirements for the university based on its location within or outside the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike limits or Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority Area.

The headquarters of the University shall be at Bengaluru, with potential for campuses, regional centres, or study centres in other parts of Karnataka after five years, subject to State Government permission and UGC norms.
The Act mentions 'National Accreditation' in Section 10, indicating the importance of accreditation by recognized bodies.
The Act includes provisions for the establishment and maintenance of various funds, including a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund, University Endowment Fund, General Fund, and Development Fund.

title: THE KARNATAKA TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC PROCURMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, for the purpose of further strengthening the transparency in public procurements.
scope: This Act applies to all types of procurements of goods and services other than procurements done by the Government Departments, State Government Undertakings, Boards or Corporations established by or under any law, Municipal Corporations, City Municipal Councils, Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, Town Municipalities or Urban Development Authorities.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force at once.

In section 4 of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999 (Karnataka Act No. 27 of 1999) for the clauses (e), the following shall be substituted, namely:-(e) where the procurement is by the Government Departments, State Government Undertakings, Boards or Corporations established by or under any law, Municipal Corporations, City Municipal Councils, Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, Town Municipalities or Urban Development Authorities for the purpose of implementation of mini water supply schemes or construction of school rooms of the value not exceeding rupees five lakhs and in cases where the procurement is by the Government Departments, State Government Undertakings, Boards or Corporations established by or under any law, Municipal Corporations, City Municipal Councils, Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, Town Municipalities or Urban Development Authorities for the purpose of procurement of goods and services other than those for the construction work, of the value not exceeding rupees five lakhs.

important_rules: Rule 1: Clause (e) of Section 4 is amended to define the value limits for procurement of mini water supply schemes and construction of school rooms, not exceeding rupees five lakhs.

Rule 2: Clause (e) of Section 4 is also amended to define the value limits for procurement of goods and services (other than construction work) by government departments, undertakings, corporations, municipalities, etc., not exceeding rupees five lakhs.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government Departments, State Government Undertakings, Boards or Corporations, Municipal Corporations, City Municipal Councils, Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, Town Municipalities or Urban Development Authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to Section 4 of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, by defining value limits for specific types of procurements.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely administered by the relevant Government Departments and authorities listed under the scope.
important_notes: The amendment specifically targets Section 4 of the principal Act.
The amendment aims to set limits on procurement values for certain types of projects and services.

title: THE KARNATAKA SLUM AREAS (IMPROVEMENT AND CLEARANCE) AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1974, and the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, for further purposes of improvement, development, clearance or re-development of slum areas.
scope: This Act applies to the state of Karnataka. It amends existing acts related to slum areas improvement and clearance, and eviction of unauthorized occupants from public premises.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2002. It also specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force from the seventeenth day of November 2001.

This section details the amendments made to the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1974. It specifies that in section 2(i), after the words 'land acquired' the words 'or land transferred by the Government or any local authority' shall be inserted. It also modifies section 2(j) to include specific areas as 'slum areas'.

important_rules: Rule 1: The government or local authority may subject to such restrictions and conditions as it may impose, transfer to such... or vest in, the Board such land free of cost for the purpose of undertaking such measures as may be necessary for improvement, development, clearance or re-development of the land or buildings thereon.
Rule 2: The Board shall re-develop or re-allot sites free of cost for the purpose of improvement, development, clearance or re-development of the land or buildings thereon.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government or local authority, and the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of amending existing acts and empowering authorities to take measures for improvement, development, clearance, and re-development of slum areas.

rights: Right of the Government/Local Authority to impose restrictions and conditions for land transfer.
Right of the Board to re-develop or re-allot sites.
duties: Duty of the Government/Local Authority to transfer land for slum improvement purposes.
Duty of the Board to carry out development and allotment of sites.
Duty to undertake measures for improvement, development, clearance, or re-development of land and buildings.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that land is free of cost for the purpose of improvement and development.
Obligation to ensure that the Board undertakes development and allotment of sites.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of Section 2 of the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1974, to include new definitions and expand the scope of 'slum area'.
Procedure 2: The Government or local authority may transfer or vest land in the Board for the purpose of improvement, development, clearance, or re-development of slum areas.
Procedure 3: The Board is empowered to carry out development and allotment of sites.
administration: The Government of Karnataka and the Board (as defined under the amended Act).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from November 17, 2001.

The amendments aim to facilitate the development and clearance of slum areas more effectively by empowering the authorities with broader powers regarding land acquisition, transfer, and re-development.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REVENUE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, primarily by abolishing the posts of Divisional Commissioners, re-designating certain land records related posts, and entrusting appellate and revisional powers of the Divisional Commissioner to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964. It affects the administrative structure and designation of officials involved in land revenue administration within the state.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by modifying the heading related to division of the State into districts, omitting sub-section (1), and substituting 'The State' for 'Each division' in sub-section (2).
Omit the word 'division' wherever it occurs in section 6 of the principal Act.
Omits Section 7 of the principal Act.
Omit the words 'who shall be subordinate to the Divisional Commissioner' from sub-section (1) of section 8 of the principal Act.
Substitutes specific words in sub-section (3) of section 9 of the principal Act, removing the subordination of the Special Deputy Commissioner to the Divisional Commissioner.
Omit the words 'Divisional Commissioner, or the' from section 13 of the principal Act.
Omits sub-section (1) of section 14 of the principal Act.

Substitutes 'the State Government' for 'the Divisional Commissioner' in sub-section (1) of section 15 of the principal Act, making the Deputy Commissioner subject to the general orders of the State Government.
Omit the words 'and the Divisional Commissioner' from sub-section (1) of section 16 of the principal Act.
Substitutes specific job titles (e.g., Deputy Commissioner of Land Records to Joint Director of Land Records) in sub-section (1) of section 18 of the principal Act.

Substitutes 'Joint Director of Land Records' or 'Joint Director for Settlement' for 'Deputy Commissioner of Land records' or 'Deputy Commissioner for Settlement' in sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 22 of the principal Act.

Substitutes 'Joint Director of Land Records' or 'Joint Director for Settlement' for 'Deputy Commissioner of Land Records' or 'Deputy Commissioner for Settlement' in sub-section (1) of section 23 of the principal Act.
Omits sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 27 of the principal Act.
Substitutes 'a Secretary to Government' for 'a Divisional Commissioner' in clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 40 of the principal Act.
Omits clause (d) and substitutes new phrases in clauses (e), (f), and (g) of section 49 of the principal Act, reflecting the re-designation of land records posts.

Substitutes 'Assistant Director for Settlement' or 'Assistant Director of land Records' for 'Assistant Superintendent for Settlement' or 'Assistant Superintendent of Land Records' in clause (b-1), and 'Joint Director of Land Records' or 'Joint Director for Settlement' for 'Deputy Commissioner of Land Records' or 'Deputy Commissioner for Settlement' in clause (c) of section 50 of the principal Act.
Omit the words 'the Divisional Commissioner' from section 69 of the principal Act.
Substitutes 'the Tribunal' for 'the Divisional Commissioner' for appeals and decisions in sub-section (2) of section 122-B of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of the expressions "Deputy Commissioners of Land Records" etc.
main_sections.description: Provides a general substitution for various 'Deputy Commissioner' and 'Superintendent' titles related to land records with corresponding 'Director' titles throughout the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of Division and office of Divisional Commissioner and consequences to ensue on such abolition
main_sections.description: States that Divisions and the office of the Divisional Commissioner shall stand abolished on the commencement date. It details consequences including the transfer of appellate/revisional powers to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal or State Government, transfer of pending proceedings, transfer of officers and servants, and transfer of funds and properties.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to adapt laws
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make adaptations and modifications to existing laws to align them with the amended principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Orders bringing this Act into force
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make provisions for omissions, additions, adaptations, and modifications of rules, regulations, bye-laws, notifications, and orders for the effective commencement of the Act and the abolition of the Divisional Commissioner's office.
Authorizes the State Government to issue orders to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the amended principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Orders to be laid before the Houses of the State Legislature
main_sections.description: Mandates that any order made under sections 22, 23, and 24 must be laid before each House of the State Legislature for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

important_rules: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2002, shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
Upon the commencement of the Act, all Divisions and the office of the Divisional Commissioner shall stand abolished.

Appellate or revision powers previously held by the Divisional Commissioner under other enactments or rules shall be construed as reference to the State Government, and pending proceedings shall be transferred to the State Government.
Appeals, revisions, and other proceedings under the principal Act pending before the Divisional Commissioner shall be transferred to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal.
Other pending proceedings under the principal Act before the Divisional Commissioner shall be transferred to the concerned Deputy Commissioner.
Officers, servants, funds, and properties of the abolished Divisional Commissioner's office shall be transferred as directed by the State Government.
The State Government may issue orders to adapt existing laws to conform with the amended principal Act.
The State Government may issue orders to facilitate the commencement of the Act and the abolition of the Divisional Commissioner's office.
Any orders made by the State Government under sections 22, 23, and 24 must be presented to the State Legislature for review and potential modification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Karnataka Appellate Tribunal, Deputy Commissioners, and other relevant authorities under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the administrative and judicial mechanisms established by the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, and as amended by this Act. This includes the functioning of the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal for appeals and revisions.

rights: Right to appeal or revision to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal or State Government as per the transferred proceedings.
Right to have pending proceedings disposed of by the designated authorities (State Government, Tribunal, or Deputy Commissioner).
duties: Duty of the State Government to appoint commencement date and issue necessary notifications and orders.
Duty of the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal to dispose of transferred appeals and revisions.
Duty of Deputy Commissioners to dispose of transferred proceedings.
Duty of the State Government to adapt laws and provide for smooth transition.
Duty of the State Government to lay orders before the State Legislature.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the re-designated job titles and reporting structures within the land revenue administration.
Obligation to transfer personnel, funds, and properties as directed by the State Government following the abolition of the Divisional Commissioner's office.

key_procedures: Appointment of commencement date by the State Government via notification.
Transfer of pending appeals and revisions from the Divisional Commissioner to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal or State Government.
Transfer of other pending proceedings to the Deputy Commissioner.
Adaptation of existing laws by the State Government to align with the amended Act.
Laying of orders made by the State Government before the State Legislature for review.
administration: The primary administration of land revenue matters continues under the framework of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, with the State Government overseeing general policy and the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal handling appellate and revisional matters previously under the Divisional Commissioner. Various Directorate of Land Records officials are also involved.
important_notes: The Act signifies a significant administrative restructuring by abolishing the Divisional Commissioner level.

The 'Divisional Commissioner' in any other enactment or rules shall be construed as 'Deputy Commissioner', unless appellate/revision powers are involved, in which case it refers to the 'State Government'.
The Karnataka Appellate Tribunal plays a crucial role in absorbing the appellate and revisional functions of the erstwhile Divisional Commissioner.
The State Government has broad powers to issue orders to facilitate the transition and address any difficulties arising from the Act's implementation.

title: THE KARNATAKA SOUHARDA SAHAKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997, by incorporating definitions for 'Co-operative Bank', 'Deposit Insurance Corporation', 'National Bank', and 'Reserve Bank'; excluding Housing Co-operative Societies from the Act's purview; requiring Co-operative Societies engaged in banking to obtain prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India; ensuring Co-operative Banks operate in conformity with banking and credit policies laid down by the Reserve Bank of India and National Bank; safeguarding depositors' interests; making past members liable for their actions; fixing timelines for elections to the first board; providing enquiry reports to the Reserve Bank for supervision; protecting non-member depositors before winding up; vesting powers of supersession, liquidation, and inquiry with the Registrar; and allowing the Registrar or an appointed officer to function as an ex-officio director on the board of Federal Co-operatives. The amendment also makes consequential amendments.
scope: This Act applies to Co-operative Societies in Karnataka, with specific amendments affecting Co-operative Banks and their operations. Housing Co-operative Societies are excluded from its purview.

key_definitions.cooperative_bank: A Co-operative engaged in or having as one of its objects, the business of banking. 'Banking' has the meaning assigned in section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
key_definitions.deposit_insurance_corporation: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation established under section 3 of the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961.
key_definitions.director: An elected or co-opted member of the board.
key_definitions.insured_bank: A Co-operative Bank having the same meaning as assigned in clause (i) of section 2 of the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961.
key_definitions.national_bank: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development constituted under section 3 of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981.
key_definitions.reserve_bank: The Reserve Bank of India constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
key_definitions.secondary_cooperative: A Co-operative whose membership is also open to another Co-operative.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Souharda Sahakari (Amendment) Act, 2004, and it shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

This section amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new definitions for 'Co-operative Bank', 'Deposit Insurance Corporation', 'Insured Bank', 'National Bank', and 'Reserve Bank'. It also redefines 'Director' and makes other consequential amendments to existing clauses.

This section inserts a new sub-section (1) into section 4, stating that no co-operative shall be registered unless its main objects serve members' interests and its bye-laws promote members' betterment. It also adds provisos prohibiting the registration of economically unsound co-operatives or those adversely impacting the co-operative movement, and explicitly excludes Housing Co-operatives.

This section amends section 5 by inserting a clause requiring proposed co-operatives to comply with sound business requirements and have reasonable chances of success. It also adds a proviso stating that registration of a Co-operative Bank requires prior approval from the Reserve Bank.

This section amends section 10 to include the rights, privileges, duties, and liabilities of membership (including nominal and associate members). It also adds a sub-section stating that for co-operative banks, bye-laws concerning deposit acceptance, borrowing, reserves, profit appropriation, loans, interest rates, and other banking activities are subject to the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and directions from the Reserve Bank or National Bank.
This section amends section 11 to require a certificate from the President or Chairperson for amendments to bye-laws of a Co-operative Bank, stating conformity with sub-section (3) of section 10.
This section amends section 12 by adding a proviso that for a Co-operative Bank, no resolution under sub-section (1) or (2) can be passed without prior written sanction from the Reserve Bank.
This section amends section 14 by adding a proviso stating that a Co-operative Bank cannot enter into a partnership without prior written permission from the Reserve Bank.

This section amends section 15 by adding a proviso that a Co-operative Bank cannot promote a subsidiary, nor can a Co-operative promote a subsidiary dealing in banking business, without prior written permission from the Reserve Bank.
This section amends section 16 by adding a proviso that in the case of a Co-operative Bank, any collaboration must be entered into with prior written approval from the Reserve Bank.
This section amends section 17 by adding a further proviso stating that the first proviso of section 17 shall not apply to a Co-operative Bank.
This section amends section 18 by adding a proviso that in the case of a Co-operative Bank, investments must be made in accordance with the instructions and directives issued by the Reserve Bank.
This section amends section 21 by inserting a sub-section (4) making a past member liable for acts of commission or omission as such member, notwithstanding their removal.

This section inserts a new section 21A regarding 'Nominal and associate members'. It allows co-operatives to admit individuals, firms, companies, other co-operatives, or bodies as nominal or associate members for specific purposes. It clarifies their rights, privileges, and liabilities, stating they cannot be office-bearers and generally do not have voting rights or participate in management, unless specified in the bye-laws.

This section amends section 25 by replacing clause (d) to disqualify individuals convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude or an offence under this Act. It also inserts a new clause (e) to disqualify individuals who have defaulted on loan repayments or have been guarantors for such defaulters.

This section amends section 26 by substituting 'prescribed' for 'specified in the bye-laws' regarding the time for general meetings. It also inserts provisos that the first general meeting for a newly registered co-operative (excluding converted societies) must be held within one month, and for converted societies, within sixty days, to elect the board.

important_rules: Co-operatives must be registered with main objects serving members' interests and promoting their betterment through self-help and mutual aid.
Co-operatives likely to be economically unsound or adversely impact the co-operative movement will not be registered.
Housing Co-operative Societies are explicitly excluded from registration under this Act.
Co-operative Banks require prior approval from the Reserve Bank for registration.

Co-operative Banks' bye-laws regarding banking activities (deposits, loans, reserves, interest rates, etc.) must comply with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and directions from the Reserve Bank or National Bank.
Amendments to a Co-operative Bank's bye-laws require a certificate of conformity with section 10(3) and prior sanction from the Reserve Bank.
Co-operative Banks require prior written sanction from the Reserve Bank for certain resolutions and partnerships.
Co-operative Banks require prior written permission from the Reserve Bank to promote subsidiaries.
Co-operative Banks need prior written approval from the Reserve Bank for collaborations.
Co-operative Banks' investments must adhere to Reserve Bank instructions.
Past members remain liable for their actions as members, even after removal.
Nominal and associate members have limited rights, generally not including management, voting, or becoming office-bearers.
Individuals convicted of moral turpitude offences or this Act's offences, or loan defaulters, are disqualified from being members.
The first general meeting for electing the board must be held within one month (for new co-operatives) or sixty days (for converted societies) of registration.

penalties: A past member shall be liable to be proceeded against for acts of commission or omission as such member, even after removal.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar (as implied by the powers vested in them), and potentially the Reserve Bank of India for Co-operative Banks.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including removal of members, denial of registration, requiring prior approvals, and legal proceedings for acts of commission or omission.

rights: Members have rights related to their participation in the co-operative's activities as defined by bye-laws.
Nominal and associate members may have specific privileges and rights as specified in the bye-laws.
Depositors' interests are to be safeguarded.
duties: Co-operatives have a duty to serve the interests of their members and promote their economic and social betterment.
Co-operative Banks have a duty to operate in conformity with banking and credit policies.
Members have duties and liabilities as may be specified in the bye-laws.
Past members have liabilities for their actions as members.
obligations: Co-operative Banks have obligations to obtain prior approvals from the Reserve Bank for various activities.
Co-operatives have obligations to conduct elections and meetings within prescribed timelines.
Members have obligations to repay loans and fulfill surety responsibilities.

key_procedures: Registration of a Co-operative: Requires fulfilling specific objectives, bye-law provisions, and obtaining Reserve Bank approval for Co-operative Banks.
Amendment of Bye-laws: Requires a certificate of conformity and prior sanction from the Reserve Bank for Co-operative Banks.
Holding General Meetings: The first general meeting for electing the board must be held within prescribed timelines.
Enforcement Actions: The Registrar has powers of supersession and liquidation. Past members can be proceeded against for their actions.
administration: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Karnataka, and the Reserve Bank of India (for Co-operative Banks).
important_notes: Housing Co-operative Societies are excluded from the purview of this Act.
Co-operative Banks are subject to significantly more stringent regulations and require numerous prior approvals from the Reserve Bank of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA CIVIL COURTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964, to implement the recommendations of the First National Judicial Pay Commission regarding the terms 'Civil Judge (Junior Division)' and 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)'.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964, and applies to all laws, rules, notifications, orders, judgments, decrees, and other instruments in force within Karnataka, particularly those concerning the nomenclature of judicial officers and their courts.

key_definitions.senior_civil_judge: Replaces the term 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)' and 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)' in courts.
key_definitions.civil_judge: Replaces the term 'Civil Judge (Junior Division)' and 'Munsiff' in courts.
key_definitions.court_of_senior_civil_judge: Replaces 'Court of a Civil Judge (Senior Division)' and 'Civil Judges Court' or 'Court of Civil Judge (Senior Division)'.
key_definitions.court_of_civil_judge: Replaces 'Court of a Civil Judge (Junior Division)' and 'Munsiff’s Court'.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends various sections of the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964, by substituting 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)' with 'Senior Civil Judge' and 'Court of a Civil Judge (Senior Division)' with 'Court of a Senior Civil Judge'. It also substitutes 'Civil Judge (Junior Division)' with 'Civil Judge' and 'Court of a Civil Judge (Junior Division)' with 'Court of Civil Judge'.

Substitutes Sections 30-A and 30-B of the Principal Act. Section 30-A deals with the substitution of expressions in certain laws in force, aligning them with the new terminology. Section 30-B addresses the construction of references to the old terms in judgments, decrees, orders, or other instruments prior to the commencement of this amendment act.

important_rules: All references to 'Civil Judge (Senior Division)' shall be substituted with 'Senior Civil Judge'.
All references to 'Court of a Civil Judge (Senior Division)' shall be substituted with 'Court of a Senior Civil Judge'.
All references to 'Civil Judge (Junior Division)' shall be substituted with 'Civil Judge'.
All references to 'Munsiff' shall be construed as 'Civil Judge'.
All references to 'Munsiff's Court' shall be construed as 'Court of Civil Judge'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely the judiciary and relevant administrative departments within the Karnataka government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964, by judicial officers and administrative bodies.

key_procedures: The act itself is a procedure for amending an existing act.
Section 30-B outlines a procedural interpretation for existing legal documents to reflect the new terminology.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Karnataka Government (as indicated by the signature of the Secretary).
important_notes: The purpose of the amendment is to align with the recommendations of the First National Judicial Pay Commission.
The amendments are made to ensure consistency in nomenclature across various legal enactments and instruments.
The act clarifies how existing judgments, decrees, and orders should be interpreted after the commencement of the amendment.

title: THE KARNATAKA GOVERNMENT PARKS (PRESERVATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, to provide for the alienation of certain areas of Indira Gandhi Musical Foundation Park and Lalbagh to Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., respectively, for road widening and metro rail project construction. It also allows for the alienation of specific areas within Cubbon Park.
scope: This act applies to government parks in Karnataka, specifically amending the provisions related to alienation of park land for public infrastructure projects in Bangalore.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975 (Karnataka Act 23 of 1975).
key_definitions.alienate: To transfer ownership or grant rights to use park land for specific purposes.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2009. It also specifies the commencement dates for different clauses. Clauses 2 and 3 (except parts of section 5) are deemed to have come into force from November 22, 2008, while specific parts of section 5 commence immediately.

This section inserts a new section, Section 5, into the Principal Act. This new section allows the State Government to alienate areas of specific parks under certain conditions and restrictions. The specified areas include parts of Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park for road widening by BBMP, parts of Lalbagh for the construction of an elevated metro station, and specific areas of Cubbon Park for various purposes including road development and metro rail projects.

This section repeals the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (Karnataka Ordinance No. 4 of 2008). It also includes a savings clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the repealed ordinance will be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may, subject to conditions and restrictions, alienate specific areas of Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park (1223 sq. mtrs) to Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike for road widening.

Rule 2: The State Government may, subject to conditions and restrictions, alienate specific areas of Lalbagh gardens (1135.18 sq. mtrs) to Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited for the construction of an elevated metro station.

Rule 3: The State Government may, subject to conditions and restrictions, alienate specific areas of Cubbon Park (2126.71 sq. mtrs and 11,160 sq. mtrs) for purposes related to infrastructure development in proximity to Vidhana Soudha and the High Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, as amended by this Act, and any conditions and restrictions imposed by the State Government during alienation.

rights: The right of the State Government to permit alienation of park land for specific public purposes.
The right of Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike to receive alienated land for road widening.
The right of Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited to receive alienated land for metro rail projects.
duties: Duty of the State Government to impose conditions and restrictions on alienation.
Duty of the State Government to ensure the purposes for which land is alienated are met.
obligations: Obligation to repeal the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008.
Obligation to ensure actions taken under the ordinance are recognized under the new Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government identifies a need to alienate park land for specific public infrastructure projects (e.g., road widening, metro station construction).

Procedure 2: The State Government, through the provisions of the amended Act, may grant permission for such alienation, subject to imposing specific conditions and restrictions regarding construction, maintenance, management, and use of the alienated area.
Procedure 3: The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008, is repealed and replaced by this Act, with continuity of actions taken under the ordinance.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is responsible for the enactment and likely oversees the implementation through relevant departments.
important_notes: The amendment specifically permits alienation of land in Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park, Lalbagh, and Cubbon Park for public projects.
The commencement of certain provisions is retrospective, dating back to November 22, 2008, reflecting the urgency of the matter addressed by the ordinance.
The Act ensures that actions taken under the repealed ordinance are considered valid under the new Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA GOVERNMENT PARKS (PRESERVATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, to provide parking space for vehicles of Advocates and visitors in Cubbon Park without disturbing the standing trees.
scope: The act applies to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, and specifically concerns the allocation of space within Cubbon Park for parking.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section details the amendment to section 5 of the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975. It inserts a new clause (e) to allow for the allocation of 18028.35 Square meters of land between the High Court Building and Old KGID Building for parking vehicles of High Court Advocates and visitors. The boundaries of this allocated space are also precisely described.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, as indicated by the signature of the Secretary.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the enactment and amendment of legislative acts.

rights: Right for High Court Advocates and visitors to park vehicles in the designated area within Cubbon Park.

key_procedures: Insertion of a new clause (e) into section 5 of the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, specifying the location and area for vehicle parking.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is specifically to provide parking space in Cubbon Park without disturbing standing trees.
The allocated area for parking is 18028.35 Square meters.
The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975 (Karnataka Act 23 of 1975).

title: SRI JAGADHGURU MURUGARAJENDRA UNIVERSITY ACT, 2020
purpose: To establish and incorporate a unitary university in the private sector by the Sri JagadhguruMurugarajendraVidhyapeetha (R) Chitradurga to promote and undertake the advancement of University education in General, Technical, Health, Management, Law, Life Sciences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the establishment and functioning of the Sri JagadhguruMurugarajendra University, a private university.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University as specified in section 25.
key_definitions.Agenda Matters: Matters and business designated in the Statutes that can only be included in the Agenda or taken up for discussion and decision with the prior written approval of the Chancellor.
key_definitions.Board of Governors: The Board of Governors of the University as specified in section 23.
key_definitions.Board of Management: The Board of Management of the University as specified in section 24.
key_definitions.Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro Vice-Ch: The respective officers of the University.
key_definitions.Campus: A campus established and maintained by the University situated within the State.
key_definitions.Committees: Committees formed under this Act or by University functionaries, including the Nomination Committee, Finance Committee, and others.
key_definitions.Constituent College: A college or institution established and maintained by the University.
key_definitions.Finance Committee: The Finance Committee of the University as specified in section 27.
key_definitions.National accreditation bodies: Bodies established by the Central Government to ensure academic standards, such as UGC, AICTE, etc., and includes the Government.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.Principal (in relation to a Constituent: The head of the Constituent College, including acting principals.
key_definitions.Regional Centre: A center established or maintained by the University for coordinating and supervising Study Centres in a region.
key_definitions.Sponsoring Trust: Sri JagadguruMurugharajendraVidyapeetha, Chitradurga registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960.
key_definitions.Statutes and Regulations: The Statutes and Regulations of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.Study Centre: A center within the state established and maintained by the University for advising, counseling, or rendering assistance to students.
key_definitions.Teacher: Includes Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, Reader, Lecturer, or other persons appointed for instruction, research, or guidance, and the Principal of a Constituent College.
key_definitions.University: Sri JagadguruMurugharajendra University established and incorporated under this Act.
key_definitions.University Grants Commission: The Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Visitor: The visitor of the University as specified in section 13.

main_sections.description: Covers the short title, extent, commencement, and definitions for the Act.
Deals with the proposal for establishment, establishment process, grants, powers to establish constituent colleges, objects, powers of the University, inclusivity, and national accreditation.
Outlines the various officers of the University, including the Visitor, Pro-Visitor, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, and other officers.

Details the authorities of the University, such as the Board of Governors, Board of Management, Academic Council, Research and Innovation Council, Finance Committee, and other authorities, along with provisions for disqualification, vacancies, and agenda matters.
Governs the making, amendment, and fixation of fees related to Statutes and Regulations of the University.

Includes provisions on conditions of service for employees, right to appeal, provident/pension fund, disputes, committees, casual vacancies, protection of action taken in good faith, transitional provisions, endowment and general funds, annual report, accounts and audit, proof of records, directions from the State Government, penalties, inspection, dissolution of the University, removal of difficulties, and power to make rules.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act may be called the Sri JagadhguruMurugarajendra University Act, 2020.
Rule 2: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.
Rule 3: The Act shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

Rule 4: The Sponsoring Trust must submit a detailed proposal to the State Government for establishing the University, including objects, extent, land availability, programs, faculties, campus development, financial outlays, resource mobilization, fee structure, and experience.

Rule 5: The State Government, after considering the proposal and recommendations from a Screening Committee, can sanction the establishment of the University if satisfied with the Trust's ability, infrastructure, and land ownership as specified.

Rule 6: The University shall have its headquarters at Chitradurga and can establish Campuses or Regional Centres, Study Centres anywhere in Karnataka after five years with prior State Government permission and UGC norms.
Rule 7: The University shall be open to all classes, castes, creed, gender, or nation.
Rule 8: The University must obtain National Accreditation.
Rule 9: Statutes and Regulations are to be made and can be amended as per the provisions of the Act.
Rule 10: The State Government has the power to issue directions and make rules under the Act.

penalties: Section 56: Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and authorities constituted under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including powers of the State Government to issue directions, inspect, and impose penalties. Enforcement also involves the functioning of the University's authorities and adherence to Statutes and Regulations.

rights: Right of the Sponsoring Trust to establish the University.
Right to appeal under Section 40.
University's right to sue and be sued in its name.
Right of the University to acquire and hold property.
Right to establish constituent colleges, campuses, regional centres, or study centres.
duties: Duty of the Sponsoring Trust to submit a comprehensive proposal for establishment.
Duty of the University to promote and undertake advancement of University education.
Duty to maintain funds and prepare annual reports.
Duty to maintain academic standards and seek National Accreditation.
Duty to adhere to Statutes and Regulations.
Duty to be open to all classes, castes, creed, gender or nation.
obligations: Obligation to establish a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund as directed by the State Government.
Obligation to vest acquired properties in the University upon sanction.
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the State Government.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Proposal for Establishment: The Sponsoring Trust submits a detailed proposal to the State Government, which is then examined by a Screening Committee for recommendations.
Procedure 2: Sanction of Establishment: Based on the Screening Committee's recommendations and any necessary inquiry, the State Government may accord sanction for the establishment of the University.

Procedure 3: Making Statutes and Regulations: Statutes are to be made by the Board of Governors with the concurrence of the Chancellor, and Regulations are to be made by the Board of Management with the approval of the Chancellor.
Procedure 4: Audit and Reporting: The University's accounts are to be audited annually, and an Annual Report is to be submitted to the State Government.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka and the authorities of the Sri JagadhguruMurugarajendra University (including the Sponsoring Trust, Board of Governors, Board of Management, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, etc.).
important_notes: The Act came into force on 13.06.2022 by Notification No. ED 120 URC 2021.
The land specified for establishment must be a single block and in the name of the concerned Trust, institution, or university.
The University is of a unitary nature in the private sector.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for the registration of the tenants alongwith his living spouse as joint occupants and to remove the tenant's limitation for grant of land under section 77 A of the Act.
scope: This Act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint. (Though specific commencement date not explicitly stated in the provided text, it refers to the date of notification).

This section deals with the amendment of section 77 A of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 (Karnataka Act 10 of 1962). The amendment aims to remove the tenant's limitation for grant of land under section 77 A, specifically regarding joint occupation with the living spouse.

important_rules: Rule 1: Tenants can be registered jointly with their living spouse as occupants.
Rule 2: Tenant's limitation for land grant under section 77 A is removed.
Rule 3: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notifications and appointment of dates)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By bringing the amendments into force through notifications and enforcing the revised provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.

rights: Right of a tenant to have their living spouse registered as a joint occupant.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government issues a notification to bring the Act into force.
Procedure 2: Registration of tenants jointly with their living spouses as occupants is made possible by this amendment.
administration: Karnataka State Government
important_notes: The Act also refers to the Bill No. 52 of 2001 and the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary No. 53/56-A dated 25-8-2001 for publication.
It mentions an earlier amendment act, the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1997, and its subsequent effect.

title: THE KARNATAKA AMENDMENT ACT 2002
purpose: To amend the Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the State of Karnataka.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically amends the Registration Act, 1908.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the act and when it comes into force. Based on the text, it is referred to as "The Karnataka Amendment Act, 2002" and aims to amend the Registration Act, 1908.
This section details the amendment made to section 48C of the Registration Act, 1908. The amendment pertains to the notification of certain matters by the government.

This section details the amendment made to section 48D of the Registration Act, 1908. This amendment likely concerns matters related to the 'notification of the matters' as stated in the original text.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendment of section 48C of the Registration Act, 1908, as amended by the Karnataka Amendment Act, 1956. The amendment concerns the notification of certain matters.

Rule 2: Amendment of section 48D of the Registration Act, 1908. This amendment concerns the notification of matters as provided in clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k), (l), (m), (n), (o), (p), (q), (r), (s), (t), (u), (v), (w), (x), (y), (z), (aa), (bb), (cc), (dd), (ee), (ff), (gg), (hh), (ii), (jj), (kk), (ll), (mm), (nn), (oo), (pp), (qq), (rr), (ss), (tt), (uu), (vv), (ww), (xx), (yy), (zz), (aaa), (bbb), (ccc), (ddd), (eee), (fff), (ggg), (hhh), (iii), (jjj), (kkk), (lll), (mmm), (nnn), (ooo), (ppp), (qqq), (rrr), (sss), (ttt), (uuu), (vvv), (www), (xxx), (yyy), (zzz), (aaaa), (bbbb), (cccc), (dddd), (eeee), (ffff), (gggg), (hhhh), (iiii), (jjjj), (kkkk), (llll), (mmmm), (nnnn), (oooo), (pppp), (qqqq), (rrrr), (ssss), (tttt), (uuuu), (vvvv), (wwww), (xxxx), (yyyy), (zzzz) of that section. The amendment involves inserting new clauses and modifying existing ones to ensure the continuity and correct application of previous notifications and amendments.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the State Government of Karnataka or its designated authorities under the Registration Act, 1908.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms and authorities established by the Registration Act, 1908.

administration: Department of Stamps and Registration, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: This act aims to replace the Karnataka Amendment Act, 1956. It also seeks to continue all notifications and amendments made under the Registration Act, 1908, in their application to the State of Karnataka.

The act clarifies that any notifications, rules, or orders issued under the Registration Act, 1908, prior to the commencement of this amendment act, shall continue to be in force unless specifically superseded by the provisions of this act or by subsequent notifications, rules, or orders.

Specifically, Section 2 amends Section 48C, and Section 3 amends Section 48D of the Registration Act, 1908. The amendments involve inserting new clauses and modifying existing ones to ensure the continuity and correct application of previous notifications and amendments.

title: THE KARNATAKA VILLAGE OFFICES ABOLITION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961, specifically to extend the prohibition period for the transfer of re-granted land from fifteen years from the commencement of the 1978 amendment to fifteen years from the date of re-grant made on or after the commencement of this 2003 amendment, in order to safeguard the interests of farmers.
scope: This Act applies to land re-granted under the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961, within the state of Karnataka. It specifically amends sections relating to the prohibition of transfer of such re-granted land.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (3) of section 5 of the principal Act. It substitutes the existing wording regarding the prohibition period of re-granted land with a new period of fifteen years from the date of re-grant made on or after the commencement of the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition (Amendment) Act, 2003.

This section amends sub-section (1) of section 7A of the principal Act.
