It substitutes the existing wording regarding the prohibition period of re-granted land with a new period of fifteen years from the date of re-grant made on or after the commencement of the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition (Amendment) Act, 2003.

important_rules: Rule: Transfer of re-granted land is prohibited for a period of fifteen years from the date of re-grant, provided the re-grant is made on or after the commencement of the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition (Amendment) Act, 2003.
Rule: The amendment applies to sub-section (3) of section 5 and sub-section (1) of section 7A of the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The primary enforcement authority would be the relevant government departments and revenue authorities responsible for land administration in Karnataka, operating under the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would likely involve monitoring land transfers and taking action against violations of the prohibition period stipulated in the amended sections.

rights: Farmers who have been re-granted land have the right to hold that land without it being transferred within the specified prohibition period.
duties: Farmers are under a duty not to transfer re-granted land within fifteen years of the re-grant date, if the re-grant is made on or after the commencement of this Act.
obligations: The State Government has an obligation to administer and enforce the provisions of the Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961, as amended by this Act.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory to the Act) and ultimately the revenue and land administration departments of the Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is intended to prevent farmers from losing lands that were granted to them by the Government, by restricting their ability to sell these lands immediately after re-grant.

The 15-year prohibition period is renewed from the date of re-grant made on or after the commencement of this 2003 Act, effectively overriding or clarifying the previous prohibition periods that had expired.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, to provide for fixing of maximum quantity of agricultural produce or goods to be stocked by retail traders, rationalizing the levy of market fee to a single point once on the first sale, and to give impetus to the Agro Processing Sector by exempting processed and sold agricultural produce from further market fee levy.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with the regulation of agricultural produce marketing, specifically concerning retail sales, retail traders, market fee levy, and the agro-processing sector. It amends the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966.

key_definitions.Retail Sale: A sale of a quantity of notified agricultural produce, as determined by the market committee by-laws subject to prescribed maximum limits, on which market fee has already been levied and collected in the concerned market area, to a consumer for domestic consumption and not for subsequent sale or processing.
key_definitions.Retail Trader: A person engaged in the retail sale of any notified agricultural produce on which market fee has already been levied and collected in the concerned market area, and who holds in stock at a time not exceeding such quantity of notified agricultural produce as the State Government may specify by notification from time to time.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) (Amendment) Act, 2004' and specifies that it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by substituting clauses (37) and (37A), which define 'Retail Sale' and 'Retail Trader'.

Amends Section 65 of the principal Act by inserting a further proviso to sub-section (2). This proviso exempts agricultural produce from market fee levy if the fee has already been levied and collected in one market area within the State and the produce is subsequently processed and sold in another market area within the State or exported outside the State. Explanations clarify that this exemption does not apply to imported processed agricultural produce or agricultural produce imported for processing (except for domestic consumption).

important_rules: Retail sale is defined as a sale to a consumer for domestic consumption, not for resale or processing, with quantities determined by market committee by-laws within State Government-prescribed limits.
Retail traders are limited in the quantity of notified agricultural produce they can stock, as determined by State Government notifications.
Market fee will be levied at a single point, once, on the first sale of notified agricultural produce within any market committee area.

Agricultural produce on which market fee has already been levied and collected in a market area within the State is exempt from further market fee if it is processed and sold in another market area within the State or exported outside the State.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Market Committees and the State Government are involved in the enforcement through by-laws, notifications, and the principal Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the regulation of retail sales and stock limits by market committees, and by the State Government through notifications. Enforcement also occurs via the levy and collection of market fees and the application of exemptions.

rights: Consumers have the right to purchase commodities for domestic consumption.
Farmers are expected to benefit from better prices due to value addition in the agro-processing sector.
obligations: Market committees have the obligation to determine by-laws for retail sale quantities within prescribed limits.
Retail traders have the obligation to adhere to stock limits for notified agricultural produce.
Those involved in the trade of agricultural produce have an obligation to pay market fees at the first point of sale.

key_procedures: Market committees formulating by-laws to determine the quantity of agricultural produce for retail sale, subject to State Government prescribed maximum limits.
State Government issuing notifications to specify the maximum quantity of notified agricultural produce that retail traders can hold in stock.
Levying market fee at a single point on the first sale of notified agricultural produce within any market committee area.
Granting exemption from market fee for processed and sold agricultural produce that has already been subject to market fee levy in another market area within the State or exported.
administration: The Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation) Act, 1966, as amended by this Act, is administered by the relevant departments of the Karnataka State Government and the Market Committees established under the principal Act.
important_notes: The exemption for processed and sold agricultural produce does not apply to processed agricultural produce imported from outside the State and sold within the State.
The exemption does not apply to agricultural produce imported from outside the State for processing or manufacturing, unless it is for one's own domestic consumption.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to provide for enhancement of the maximum number of wards for a Corporation to 200, nomination of members equal to ten percent of the total number of members in the council from among the residents of the city to the Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, and substitution of certain expressions related to the Bangalore City Corporation.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and specifically to the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike. It governs the composition of the council and the terminology used for the municipal corporation in Bangalore.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it is deemed to have come into force from June 4, 2009.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting clause (a) to provide for elected councillors to be not less than thirty and not more than two hundred, as determined by the Government. It also amends clause (b) to state that the number of nominated members in the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike shall not exceed ten percent of the total number of Councillors, instead of a fixed number of ten persons for the Bangalore City Corporation.
Replaces the expressions 'Bangalore City Corporation' or 'Corporation of the City of Bangalore' with 'Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike' wherever they appear in the principal Act.

Repeals the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (Karnataka Ordinance No. 4 of 2009). It also states that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka (implied through notification powers for determining the number of councillors).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and government notifications.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government to determine the number of elected councillors (not less than thirty and not more than two hundred).
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the act's enactment). The administration of the Municipal Corporations would fall under the relevant municipal bodies as per the principal Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from June 4, 2009.
The amendment aims to facilitate smooth administration by creating smaller and more compact wards with an average population of 30,000 in the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike area.

title: THE KARNATAKA PART TIME JOB ORIENTED COURSE EMPLOYEES ABSORPTION ACT, 2011
purpose: To provide for the absorption of part-time Job Oriented Course employees working in the job oriented courses in Pre-university Education in the State of Karnataka, consequent upon the closure of Job Oriented Courses from the academic year 2011-12. It aims to absorb teaching and non-teaching staff who have worked for more than five years as part-time employees in Government or Private Aided JOC Institutions into vacant posts within Government Departments or other Private Aided JOC Institutions, respectively.
scope: This Act applies to part-time Job Oriented Course employees (teaching and non-teaching staff) who have completed five years of service and are working as such on the commencement date of the Act. It covers absorption into vacant posts within the Pre-university Education service, other Government Departments, or Private Aided JOC Institutions. The Act specifically addresses employees of Government JOC Institutions and Private Aided Institutions separately.

key_definitions.Part time Job Oriented Course employee: A person appointed as teaching staff, worker teacher, office assistant, or 'D' Group employee in job oriented courses by the head of Government or private aided Pre-university Colleges on a part-time or full-time basis, in accordance with specified Government Orders, who has worked for at least five years and is still employed as such on the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Part time Job Oriented Course Employees Absorption Act, 2011, and that it comes into force at once.
Defines terms used in the Act, most importantly 'Part time Job Oriented Course employee'.

main_sections.section_title: Absorption of the part time Job Oriented Course employee
main_sections.description: Outlines the process and conditions for absorbing part-time Job Oriented Course employees, excluding those in private aided institutions. It mandates following the State's reservation policy and considers absorption into equivalent vacant posts in Pre-university Education service or other Government departments if vacancies are insufficient. It also details conditions related to continuous service, qualifications, and reservation for Scheduled Castes/Tribes. For employees in private aided institutions, the Government may direct these institutions to absorb eligible persons.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for absorption of part time Job Oriented Course employee
main_sections.description: Establishes committees to recommend eligible employees for absorption. It details the process of recommendation, notification, and absorption by the Appointing Authority, including verification of antecedents and suitability. The process is to be completed within one year of the Act's commencement. Similar procedures are outlined for employees in private aided institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Pay fixation, seniority and leave of part time Job Oriented Course employee absorbed under these rules
main_sections.description: Specifies that the initial basic pay of an absorbed employee will be fixed at the minimum of the time scale of the absorbed post. Service rendered before absorption will not be counted for pay, seniority, leave, or pension purposes. Inter-se seniority is determined by the length of service after completing five years, with older individuals being senior in case of a tie.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of appointment of part time Job Oriented Course employee
main_sections.description: Prohibits the continuation or absorption of part-time Job Oriented Course employees who have not completed five years of service. It also prohibits new appointments or continuation of such employees after the absorption process is complete. Contravention of these provisions by individuals or appointing authorities is considered misconduct and liable for disciplinary action.

States that the Karnataka Civil Services Rules and other relevant service rules will apply to absorbed employees in Government service, provided they are not inconsistent with this Act. For employees absorbed in private aided institutions, applicable rules for aided institution employees will govern them.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for actions taken or omitted in good faith by Government officers under this Act.
Grants the Government the power to issue general or special orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, as long as these orders are not inconsistent with the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Part-time Job Oriented Course employees must have completed at least five years of continuous service without breaks attributable to them to be eligible for absorption.
Rule 2: Absorbed employees must possess the qualifications prescribed for the post on the date of their absorption.

Rule 3: Absorption into posts earmarked for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes is only permitted if eligible candidates from these classes are available among the part-time Job Oriented Course employees; otherwise, such posts become backlog vacancies.
Rule 4: The initial basic pay of an absorbed employee will be fixed at the minimum of the time scale of the new post, and prior service will not be counted for pay, seniority, leave, or pension.
Rule 5: Inter-se seniority among absorbed employees will be determined by the length of service after completing five years, with age as a tie-breaker.
Rule 6: No part-time Job Oriented Course employee who has not completed five years of service on the commencement date can be continued or absorbed.
Rule 7: No new appointments or continuation of part-time Job Oriented Course employees are allowed after the absorption process is completed.

penalties: Any person or Appointing Authority appointing or engaging any person on a part-time basis in contravention of sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 6 shall be liable for strict disciplinary action as misconduct.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka (specifically, the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation and other relevant departments involved in Pre-university Education and Government service administration).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution of committees to recommend eligible employees, notification of names, verification of antecedents and suitability by appointing authorities, and the application of service rules. The Government also has the power to issue directions to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to be considered for absorption into equivalent vacant posts in Government service or Private Aided Institutions if eligibility criteria are met.
Right to have pay fixed at the minimum of the time scale of the absorbed post.
Right to have seniority determined based on length of service and age.
Protection of actions taken in good faith by government officers.
duties: To discharge duties continuously for not less than five years without breaks attributable to the employee.
To possess the prescribed qualifications for the post on the date of absorption.
To abide by the reservation policy of the State.
To cooperate with the absorption process and verification procedures.
obligations: To accept absorption into a specified equivalent vacant post.
To be governed by the applicable service rules of the absorbed service or institution.
Not to engage in or appoint others in contravention of the prohibition of new part-time JOC employee appointments after the absorption process.

key_procedures: Formation of absorption recommendation committees by the State Government.
Determination of eligible candidates by the committee based on Act's conditions.
Recommendation of names by the committee to the State Government.
Notification of recommended names by the Government.
Verification of antecedents and suitability by the Appointing Authority.
Absorption of eligible employees into notified vacant posts according to relevant rules.
Direction to private aided institutions by the Government to absorb eligible persons in their vacant posts.
Removal of difficulties by the Government through general or special orders.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as per the signatory), and likely the Department of Pre-university Education.
important_notes: The absorption is a one-time measure.
The Act's provisions supersede any other law for the time being in force regarding absorption.
If sufficient vacant posts are not available in the Pre-university Education service, the Government must identify vacancies in other departments for absorption.
For private aided institutions, the Government may direct them to absorb eligible persons against available or future vacancies.

title: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, to reduce the time for calling public objections before extinguishing public rights on certain lands, and to extend the time limit for disposal of pending applications for regularization of unauthorized cultivation land.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically amends certain sections of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, pertaining to public rights extinguishment and regularization of unauthorized cultivation land.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2020, and states that it comes into force at once.

This section amends Section 68 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, by substituting 'one month' for 'ninety days' for the period of calling public objections before extinguishing public rights on public roads, streets, passages, or 'B' kharab land.

This section amends Section 94-B of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, by substituting 'within twenty two years' for 'within twenty years' in clause (iii) of sub-section (1). This amendment is deemed to have always been in effect and relates to the time limit for regularization of unauthorized cultivation land.

important_rules: Reduce the stipulated time for calling public objections from ninety days to one month before extinguishing public rights on public roads, streets, passages, or 'B' kharab land.

Extend the time limit for disposal of pending applications for regularization of unauthorized cultivation land by another two years (implicitly, by allowing amendments to the original act that had a deadline of 27.04.2020).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

rights: The right of the public to have objections considered for a period of one month before extinguishment of public rights on certain lands.
duties: Duty of authorities to adhere to the one-month period for calling objections.
Duty of authorities to dispose of pending applications for regularization of unauthorized cultivation land within the extended period.

key_procedures: Procedure for extinguishing public rights on public roads, streets, passages, or 'B' kharab land: A declaration is made, followed by a one-month period for public objections before the right is extinguished.
Procedure for regularization of unauthorized cultivation land: Applications are processed, and the time limit for disposal of pending applications has been extended.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory of the Act). The primary administration would fall under the revenue department responsible for land matters.
important_notes: The amendment to Section 94-B, extending the period from 'within twenty years' to 'within twenty two years', shall always be deemed to have been substituted, indicating retrospective application.
The original deadline for disposal of regularization applications was 27.04.2020, and the amendment extends this by two years.

title: THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974) to provide for the recording of evidence of witnesses by audio-video electronic means in the presence of the advocate of the accused person.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. It specifically relates to the recording of witness evidence in criminal proceedings within Karnataka.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2021, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section inserts a proviso after sub-section (1) of section 276 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. This proviso allows for the recording of a witness's evidence by audio-video electronic means in the presence of the advocate of the accused person, in such manner as may be prescribed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Evidence of a witness may be recorded by audio-video electronic means.
Rule 2: Such recording must be done in the presence of the advocate of the person accused of the offence.
Rule 3: The manner of recording evidence by audio-video electronic means shall be as prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the courts and relevant judicial authorities responsible for implementing the Code of Criminal Procedure.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended Section 276 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by courts during criminal proceedings.

rights: Right of the accused to have their advocate present during the recording of witness evidence by audio-video electronic means.
duties: Duty of the court or relevant authority to ensure that evidence is recorded in accordance with the provisions of the amended Act.
Duty to prescribe the manner in which audio-video electronic recording of evidence shall be carried out.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: When recording witness evidence by audio-video electronic means, it must be done in the presence of the advocate for the accused.
Procedure 2: The specific 'manner' in which this audio-video electronic recording is to be conducted will be prescribed by subsequent rules or regulations.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (indicated by the signatory to the Act).
important_notes: The amendment is made to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974).
The Act received the assent of the President on the 24th day of May, 2022.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on the 1st day of June, 2022.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for minimum representation of persons belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Municipal Councils and Town Panchayats, and to ensure representation of members of the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly in Municipalities and Town Panchayats.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It applies to Municipal Councils and Town Panchayats within Karnataka. The amendments specifically concern representation in these bodies.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the act as the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 2002, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.

Amends Section 11 of the principal Act by inserting provisos mandating reservation of at least one seat each for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in a municipal council. It also provides for filling a reserved seat by the other category if a person from the designated category is unavailable.

Amends Section 50 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso stating that if a meeting called for the election of President or Vice-President is adjourned for want of quorum, a quorum will not be necessary for the adjourned meeting.

Amends Section 352 of the principal Act concerning the composition of a Town Panchayat. It specifies the number of Councillors, allows for nominated members with special knowledge or social work experience (who do not have voting rights), and includes members of the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly whose constituencies lie within the transitional area. It also includes members of the Council of States and State Legislative Council registered as electors within the transitional area. Additionally, it inserts provisos for reservation of at least one seat each for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in a Town Panchayat, with a provision for filling seats if a person from a reserved category is unavailable.

important_rules: At least one seat shall be reserved in a municipal council for persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes and at least one seat for persons belonging to the Scheduled Tribes.
If no person belonging to the Scheduled Castes is available for a reserved seat, that seat shall be filled by a person belonging to the Scheduled Tribes, and vice versa.

A Town Panchayat shall consist of a specified number of Councillors, nominated members with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration or social workers, members of the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly representing the transitional area, and members of the Council of States and State Legislative Council registered as electors within the transitional area.
Nominated persons in a Town Panchayat shall not have the right to vote in its meetings.
If a meeting for the election of President or Vice-President is adjourned due to lack of quorum, the adjourned meeting will not require a quorum.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka and its designated authorities will be responsible for the implementation and enforcement of this act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, appointment of dates for commencement, and the administrative machinery responsible for municipal governance in Karnataka.

rights: Right to representation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Municipal Councils and Town Panchayats.
Right for members of the House of the People and State Legislative Assembly to participate in deliberations and vote in Municipalities (as per original Act, amended here for Town Panchayats).
Right for registered electors of the Council of States and State Legislative Council within the transitional area to be members of the Town Panchayat.
duties: Duty of the Government to notify the commencement date of the Act.
Duty of the Government to determine the number of Councillors in a Town Panchayat.
Duty to reserve seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
obligations: Obligation to reserve seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in municipal councils and town panchayats.
Obligation to include specific categories of members in the composition of Town Panchayats.
Obligation for nominated members of Town Panchayats to not have voting rights.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act through Government notification.
Procedure for reservation and filling of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in municipal bodies.
Procedure for the election of President and Vice-President, including rules for adjourned meetings.
Procedure for the composition of a Town Panchayat, including the number of councillors and nominated members.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation of the Government of Karnataka is involved in the enactment. The overall administration would fall under the Urban Development Department or equivalent responsible for municipal governance.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 10th November 2003.
The amendments are based on the 74th Constitutional Amendment's provisions for Urban Local Bodies.
Nominated members in Town Panchayats have special knowledge or experience in municipal administration, health, town planning, education, or are social workers, but do not have voting rights.

title: THE KARNATAKA TOWN AND COUNTRY PLANNING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1998
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, to provide for changes in definitions, empower the State Government to exempt certain bodies from fee payments, allow for additional Floor Area Ratio for land surrendered for road purposes and for starred hotels, clarify fee levies, introduce provisions for regularization of deviated buildings, and for the levy and collection of surcharge or cess for public amenities and transport systems, and to validate past collections of these levies.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. It applies to planning authorities, local authorities, owners of land and buildings within the jurisdiction of these authorities in Karnataka. It specifically addresses changes related to land use, development, fee structures, and the imposition of cess and surcharges for specific development purposes.

key_definitions.public_purpose: Includes widening of existing roads, formation of new roads, providing parks, playgrounds, open spaces, civic amenities, and maintaining or improving heritage buildings or precincts notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.development_right: The right to carry out development or to develop land or building or both.
key_definitions.infrastructure_project: Includes road, bridge, airport, port, inland waterways, rail system, water supply projects, irrigation projects, sanitation and sewerage systems, and tourism projects with significant investment, as notified by the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 1998, and that it comes into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by omitting 'Notified Area Committee, Sanitary Board' and substituting 'Town Panchayat or Grama Panchayat' for 'Mandal Panchayat'.

Inserts a new section 14B, titled 'Benefit of development rights', which allows Planning Authorities to permit additional floor area as development rights when land is surrendered free of cost for public purposes.

Amends Section 18 of the Principal Act. It substitutes sub-section (1) regarding prescribed fees for change of land use or development and inserts sub-section (3) empowering the State Government to exempt certain bodies and infrastructure projects from paying these fees.

Inserts a new section 18A, effective from 19th October 1992, titled 'Levy and collection of cess and surcharge'. This section empowers Planning Authorities to levy and collect cess and surcharge for water supply, ring roads, slum improvement, and mass rapid transport systems.

Substitutes Section 24 of the Principal Act to state that provisions of certain sections, including the newly inserted 14B and 18A, apply mutatis mutandis to the enforcement of the Comprehensive Development Plan.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of cess and surcharge for certain purpose
main_sections.description: Validates the levy, assessment, and collection of cess and surcharge for specific purposes (water supply, ring road, slum improvement, Mass Rapid Transport System) made since 19th October 1992, notwithstanding any court orders, and bars legal proceedings for refund.

important_rules: Development rights (additional floor area) can be granted equal to one and a half times the area of land surrendered free of cost for public purposes.
The granted development rights can be utilized on the remaining portion of the surrendered land or anywhere else in the local planning area, either by the owner or by transfer to another person.
A fee not exceeding one-third of the estimated increase in the value of land or building may be levied for permission for change of land use or development.
Cess and surcharge, not exceeding one-tenth of the market value of the land or building, may be levied for water supply schemes, ring roads, slum improvement, and mass rapid transport systems.
Buildings constructed in deviation of sanctioned plans can be regularized subject to payment of a penalty.

Buildings constructed in contravention of the plan or without permission may be forfeited to the State Government if demolition is not practicable and the owner does not agree to pay a penalty equivalent to twice the current value.

penalties: Penalty for buildings constructed deviating from the sanctioned plan: Not more than the market value of such deviated area.
Penalty for buildings constructed in contravention or without permission, where demolition is not practicable: An amount equivalent to two times the current value of such building or part thereof.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Planning Authority, local authority, and other authorities under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the enforcement of the Comprehensive Development Plan, application of amended sections relating to development rights, fees, cess, surcharges, and provisions for regularization and forfeiture of unauthorized constructions. Appeals against levy, assessment, and collection of cess or surcharge can be made to a prescribed authority.

rights: Right to obtain permission for change of land use or development of land or building.
Right to benefit from development rights (additional floor area) when land is surrendered for public purposes.
Right to appeal against the levy, assessment, and collection of cess or surcharge.
duties: Duty to obtain permission for change of land use or development of land or building.
Duty to pay prescribed fees for permission for change of land use or development.
Duty to pay cess and surcharge for specific public amenities and transport systems.
Duty to comply with sanctioned plans and building regulations.
Duty to regularize deviated buildings subject to penalty, or face forfeiture.
Duty to surrender land free of cost for public purposes when required by Planning Authorities.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, as amended.
Obligation to pay any prescribed penalties for deviations or unauthorized constructions.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission for change of land use or development, including payment of fees.
Procedure for surrendering land for public purposes and obtaining benefit of development rights.
Procedure for levying and collecting cess and surcharge by the Planning Authority.
Procedure for appealing against the levy, assessment, and collection of cess or surcharge.
Procedure for regularization of deviated buildings.
Procedure for forfeiture of unauthorized or deviated buildings in specific circumstances.
administration: Planning Authority, local authority, and the State Government (for exemptions and notifications).
important_notes: The Act clarifies that certain bodies (Notified Area Committee, Sanitary Board) no longer exist, and replaces 'Mandal Panchayat' with 'Town Panchayat or Grama Panchayat' to align with other legislation.
The State Government can exempt Boards, Authorities, Bodies owned or controlled by the State or Central Government, and approved infrastructure projects from paying fees, cess, or surcharge.
Levy and collection of cess and surcharge for certain purposes have been validated retrospectively from 19th October 1992.

title: THE KARNATAKA MINISTERS SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To enhance the salaries and allowances of the Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers by amending the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956, due to a considerable rise in living costs and relative depreciation of money value since the last revision in 2000.
scope: This act applies to the Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers of the Karnataka State Government. It amends the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956, and covers salaries and allowances as stipulated in that act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it comes into force at once.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary values for 'six thousand rupees' with 'twelve thousand rupees' and for 'rupees five thousand' with 'rupees ten thousand'.
Amends Section 4(1) of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 6A of the principal Act by substituting 'four thousand rupees' with 'eight thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 6B(1) of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by substituting 'three thousand five hundred rupees' with 'seven thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 8(1) of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.

Amends Section 12(2) of the principal Act: (i) substitutes 'eight rupees' with 'twelve rupees' in clause (b); and (ii) substitutes 'eight hundred rupees' with 'one thousand rupees' in clause (d), and 'one thousand rupees' with 'one thousand two hundred rupees' in the first proviso to clause (d).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as per the signatory of the order). The primary enforcement would likely involve the Finance Department or relevant administrative departments overseeing ministerial remuneration.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the revised salary and allowance structures as mandated by the amendments to the principal Act.

rights: Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers have the right to receive enhanced salaries and allowances as per the revised figures in the Act.
duties: The Government of Karnataka has a duty to implement the revised salary and allowance structures.

key_procedures: Upon assent by the Governor and publication in the Gazette, the Act comes into force immediately. The necessary administrative and financial adjustments are then made to implement the enhanced salaries and allowances for ministers, ministers of state, and deputy ministers according to the specified sections.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956 (Karnataka Act 5 of 1957).
The amendments relate to specific monetary figures for various salary and allowance components.
The rationale for the amendment is the increase in living costs since the last revision in 2000.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROFESSIONAL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (REGULATION OF ADMISSION AND FIXATION OF FEE) (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2011
purpose: To provide for the recognition of consensual arrangements or agreements entered into between the State Government and Private Unaided Educational Institutions offering Professional Educational Courses, and for other related matters, particularly concerning admissions and fee fixation for academic years 2008-09 to 2011-12.
scope: This Act applies to Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions in Karnataka offering Professional Educational Courses for the academic years 2008-09, 2009-10, 2010-11, and 2011-12. It governs the regulation of admissions and the fixation of fees in these institutions, particularly in relation to consensual agreements with the State Government and the P.A. Inamdar judgment.

key_definitions.common_entrance_test: The entrance test conducted for determining candidate merit, followed by centralized counseling for admission to professional educational courses through a single window procedure.
key_definitions.common_entrance_test_cell: The agency of the State Government responsible for conducting the common entrance test.
key_definitions.consensual_arrangement_or_agreement: Any agreement between the State Government and an association of unaided Private Professional Educational Institutions regarding admission and fee fixation in professional courses.
key_definitions.institution: Professional Educational Institutions offering Professional Educational Courses.
key_definitions.one_man_regulatory_committee: A committee constituted by the State Government under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.professional_educational_courses: Includes Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery, Bachelor of Dental Surgery, Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Technology, Bachelor of Architecture, and such other courses as notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.unaided_institution: A privately managed professional educational institution not receiving aid or grant-in-aid from the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its deemed commencement date (June 1, 2008), and its application, overriding the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006 for the specified academic years.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as Common Entrance Test, Consensual arrangement or agreement, Institution, One Man Regulatory Committee, Professional Educational Courses, and Unaided institution.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of One Man Regulatory Committee
main_sections.description: Establishes a One-Man Regulatory Committee, to be appointed by the State Government, consisting of a former Vice-Chancellor of a State University. This committee will oversee admissions and the implementation of consensual arrangements.

Empowers the State Government to fix fees for admissions to Unaided Private Professional Educational Institutions, in accordance with consensual arrangements, by notification. Different fee rates can be fixed for different student categories.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of admission and seat matrix
main_sections.description: Details the manner in which seats in Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions are to be filled for the academic years 2008-09 to 2011-12, specifying percentages for different courses and institution types (minority/non-minority). It also outlines the role of the Common Entrance Test Cell and the process for filling remaining seats.

main_sections.section_title: Invalidation of admissions made in violation of this Act
main_sections.description: Declares all admissions made in violation of the Act or consensual arrangements for the specified academic years as invalid. The State Government can direct universities to cancel such admissions or affiliations.
Grants the State Government the power to make orders, not inconsistent with the Act, to remove any difficulties in giving effect to its provisions.
Empowers the State Government to make rules, prospectively or retrospectively, for carrying out the purposes of the Act. These rules are subject to legislative scrutiny.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of admissions and collection of fee
main_sections.description: Validates all admissions made and fees collected from June 1, 2008, in accordance with consensual arrangements or the Act, notwithstanding any court judgments or orders. It prohibits suits or proceedings for refund of such fees and prevents enforcement of decrees for refunds.

important_rules: Seats in Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions must be filled as per the specified percentages for different courses and institution types (minority/non-minority) for academic years 2008-09, 2009-10, and 2010-11. For 2011-12, the number of seats will be as agreed upon in the consensual arrangement.
A significant portion of seats in Medical, Dental, and Engineering institutions (varying percentages for minority/non-minority institutions) must be filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell.
Remaining seats are to be filled through a Common Entrance Test conducted by associations of Private Professional Educational Institutions, followed by centralized counseling on a merit basis.
The State Government can, by notification, publish the seat matrix for different categories of students and institutions, subject to reservations and consensual arrangements.
All admissions made in violation of the Act or consensual arrangements for the academic years 2008-09 to 2011-12 are invalid and can lead to cancellation of admissions or affiliation.
Admissions made and fees collected from June 1, 2008, in accordance with consensual arrangements or the Act are validated, and no refund of such fees can be sought.

penalties: Invalidation of admissions made in violation of the Act or consensual arrangement.
Cancellation of admissions by the concerned university.
Cancellation of affiliation of the institution by the concerned university.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and concerned universities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the power to direct cancellation of admissions or affiliations, and by enacting specific provisions for validation and overriding previous judgments.

rights: Students have the right to admission based on merit as determined by the Common Entrance Test and centralized counseling.
The State Government has the right to enter into consensual arrangements with institutions regarding admissions and fees.
The State Government has the right to fix fees and publish seat matrices.
Institutions have the right to fill remaining seats through their own entrance tests and counseling, subject to merit and consensual agreements.
The State Government has the right to invalidate admissions made in contravention of the Act.
duties: Private Unaided Professional Educational Institutions have a duty to conduct admissions and collect fees in accordance with the Act and consensual arrangements.
The State Government has a duty to protect the interests of students of Karnataka domicile and backward classes through consensual arrangements.
The State Government has a duty to ensure admissions are regulated and fees are fixed appropriately.
The State Government has a duty to oversee the implementation of the Act through the One Man Regulatory Committee.
obligations: Institutions are obligated to adhere to the seat matrix and admission procedures prescribed by the Act and consensual arrangements.
The State Government is obligated to ensure transparency and fairness in the admission process.

key_procedures: Consensual arrangement or agreement: The State Government enters into an agreement with associations of unaided Private Professional Educational Institutions regarding admission and fee fixation.
Constitution of One Man Regulatory Committee: The State Government appoints a former Vice-Chancellor to oversee admissions and implementation of agreements.
Fixation of Fee: The State Government notifies the fees payable for admission based on consensual arrangements.

Seat Matrix Regulation: The State Government specifies the number and distribution of seats to be filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell and management, for different categories of students and institutions.

Admission Process: Seats are filled through the Common Entrance Test Cell (for a specified percentage of seats) and then through entrance tests conducted by institutions' associations, followed by centralized counseling based on merit.
Invalidation and Validation: Admissions violating the Act are invalidated, while those made in accordance with the Act and agreements are validated, overriding previous court orders.
administration: State Government (Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation is mentioned in the context of the Governor's order). The One Man Regulatory Committee is also a key administrative body.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from June 1, 2008.

The Act's provisions override the Karnataka Professional Educational Institutions (Regulation of Admission and Determination of Fee) Act, 2006, for the academic years 2008-09, 2009-10, 2010-11, and 2011-12.

Section 9 specifically validates all admissions and fee collections made from June 1, 2008, in accordance with consensual arrangements or the Act, irrespective of any prior court judgments, decrees, or orders, and prevents any proceedings for the refund of such fees.

title: THE KARNATAKA RACE COURSES LICENSING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952, to delegate powers to an officer authorised by the Government for better management of licensing, control and management of horse racing, and to enhance penalty amounts.
scope: This Act applies to the licensing, control, and management of horse racing within Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Race Courses Licensing (Amendment) Act, 2020, and states that it comes into force immediately.
Inserts the words 'or the officer authorised by the Government' after 'Government' in section 4 of the Principal Act.
Substitutes the words 'fifty thousand rupees' for 'five hundred rupees' in section 5 of the Principal Act.
Substitutes the words 'one lakh rupees' for 'one thousand rupees' in section 6 of the Principal Act.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 7 by inserting 'or the officer authorised by the Government' after 'Government' and substituting 'one lakh rupees' for 'one thousand rupees'. Amends sub-section (2) of section 7 similarly.
Inserts the words 'or the officer authorised by the Government' after 'Government' in section 8 of the Principal Act.
Inserts the words 'or the officer authorised by the Government' after 'Government' in sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Principal Act.

important_rules: Rule: Powers can be delegated by the Government to an authorised officer for the management of horse racing.
Rule: The penalty for an offence under section 5 of the Principal Act is enhanced from five hundred rupees to fifty thousand rupees.
Rule: The penalty for an offence under section 6 of the Principal Act is enhanced from one thousand rupees to one lakh rupees.
Rule: Penalties and delegation provisions under section 7 of the Principal Act are amended to reflect increased penalty amounts and delegation of powers.

penalties: For offences under section 5: Enhanced from five hundred rupees to fifty thousand rupees.
For offences under section 6: Enhanced from one thousand rupees to one lakh rupees.
For offences under section 7: Enhanced from one thousand rupees to one lakh rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and/or the officer authorised by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952, as amended by this Act, including the imposition of penalties.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of existing sections of the Karnataka Race Courses Licensing Act, 1952, to incorporate delegated powers and increased penalty amounts.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory for the notification). The act itself pertains to the licensing, control, and management of horse racing, implying oversight by relevant departments handling sports or licensing.
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon publication.
The amendments are made to enhance efficiency in management and to align penalty amounts with current monetary values.

title: THE NEW HORIZON UNIVERSITY ACT, 2021
purpose: To establish and incorporate in the State of Karnataka a University of unitary nature in the private sector by the New Horizon Educational and Cultural Trust to promote and undertake the advancement of applied university education in Sciences, all branches of Engineering, Arts, Management, Commerce, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Act aims to enhance the gross enrollment ratio in the higher education sector by spreading quality education.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the establishment and incorporation of The New Horizon University, a private university of unitary nature, and its operations within Karnataka.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University as specified in section 26.
key_definitions.Agenda Matters: Matters and business designated in the Statutes that can be included in the Agenda or taken up for discussion and decision at a meeting of the Board of Governors, Board of Management, Academic Council, or other University authority/Committees, subject to prior written approval of the Chancellor.
key_definitions.Board of Governors: The Board of Governors of the University as specified in section 24.
key_definitions.Board of Management: The Board of Management of the University as specified in section 25.
key_definitions.Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro Vice-Ch: The respective officers of the University.
key_definitions.Campus: A campus established and maintained by the University, situated within the State.
key_definitions.Sponsoring Authority or Sponsoring Body: The New Horizon Educational and Cultural Trust.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the provision for its commencement through a notification by the State Government.
Defines various terms and phrases used in the Act, including key authorities, bodies, and concepts related to the University.

main_sections.section_title: Proposal for the establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the sponsoring trust to propose the establishment of the University to the State Government, including the required particulars for the proposal.

Details the conditions under which the State Government can sanction the establishment of the University, including requirements for infrastructure, land, financial resources, and experience. It also covers the vesting of property in the University and its legal status.
Specifies the core objectives of the University, focusing on the advancement of applied university education.
Lists the various powers that the University is empowered to exercise under the Act.
Enumerates the different officers that the University will have.
Lists the various authorities that will govern the University.
Pertains to the Statutes of the University.
Pertains to the Regulations of the University.
Deals with the terms and conditions of service for the employees of the University.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to issue directions regarding the University.
Specifies the penalties that may be imposed for violations of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to give direction for dissolution of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the State Government's power to direct the dissolution of the University under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules by the State Government
main_sections.description: Confers the power on the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: A proposal to establish a University must include detailed particulars about its objects, extent, land availability, programs of study, faculties, campus development, financial outlays, resources, fee structure, student selection, and other conditions required by the State Government.

Rule: The State Government can sanction the establishment of a University only if the trust demonstrates sufficient infrastructure, owns the specified extent of land, has adequate financial resources for statutory funds and university affairs, and possesses experience in running higher education institutions.

Rule: The University headquarters shall be in Bengaluru, with the possibility of establishing campuses or regional/study centers elsewhere in Karnataka after five years, subject to prior State Government permission and UGC norms.
Rule: Agenda matters for meetings of University authorities require prior written approval from the Chancellor.
Rule: The State Government has the power to issue directions to the University and to direct its dissolution if deemed necessary.

penalties: Section 57 of the Act specifies that penalties may be imposed. Specific details of penalties are not elaborated in the provided text but are covered under this section.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Karnataka is the primary enforcement authority, with powers to issue directions, sanction establishment, and direct dissolution. The Registrar is the point of contact for legal proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement occurs through the State Government's power to issue notifications, conduct inquiries, require adherence to prescribed conditions (land, finance, experience), and through legal proceedings involving the Registrar. The State Government can also issue directions and make rules to ensure compliance.

rights: The Trust has the right to establish the University, subject to the Act's provisions.
The University has the right to sue and be sued in its name.
Employees have a right to appeal, as per Section 41.
duties: The Trust has a duty to submit a comprehensive proposal to the State Government.
The Trust must establish a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund if directed by the Government.
The University has a duty to promote and undertake advancement of applied university education.
The University must maintain funds and prepare annual reports and accounts for audit.
The University must ensure it is open to all classes, castes, creeds, genders, or nations.
obligations: The University must adhere to the conditions of service for its employees.
The University must maintain its funds (Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund, University Endowment Fund, General Fund, Development Fund) as specified.
The University must ensure compliance with norms set by the University Grants Commission and other National Accreditation Bodies.

key_procedures: Procedure for Establishment: The Trust submits a proposal to the State Government, which is examined by a Screening Committee. The Government then holds an inquiry and, if satisfied with the trust's ability, land ownership, financial resources, and experience, sanctions the establishment via notification after the Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund is established.
Procedure for making Statutes: Section 34 details how Statutes are made.
Procedure for making Regulations: Section 37 details how Regulations are made.
Procedure for Audit: Section 54 outlines the process for accounts and audit.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka is responsible for overall administration, sanctioning the establishment, issuing directions, and making rules. The University itself is administered by its officers and authorities (Board of Governors, Board of Management, Academic Council, etc.).
important_notes: Note: The University is of a 'unitary' nature.
Note: The University is in the 'private sector'.
Note: The headquarters of the University is at Bengaluru.
Note: Campus or Regional Centers can be established anywhere in Karnataka after five years of establishment, subject to prior permission of the State Government and UGC norms.
Note: The Act is enacted under Entry 25 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REVENUE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, specifically to extend the cut-off date for applying in Form-57 for the regularization of unauthorized cultivation of government lands by another one year. This amendment addresses the period from 17.03.2018 to 16.03.2019 for lands cultivated prior to 01.01.2005, extending the application window due to missed opportunities during election periods.
scope: This act amends Section 94A of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, and applies to the regularization of unauthorized cultivation of government lands within the State of Karnataka. It specifically addresses the period for applications related to lands cultivated prior to January 1, 2005, and extends the application deadline for Form-57.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2022, and it shall be deemed to have come into force from May 30, 2022.

Amends sub-section (4) of Section 94A of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964. It substitutes the phrase 'within a period of one year from the date of commencement of the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2018' with 'within a period of one year from the date of commencement of the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2022'.

Repeals the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022 (Karnataka Ordinance No 04 of 2022). It also includes a saving clause, stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The application period for regularization of unauthorized cultivation in government lands (using Form-57) is extended by one year, with the commencement date of the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2022, as the reference point for calculating this one-year period.
Rule 2: The amendment aims to regularize lands cultivated prior to January 1, 2005, for the period between March 17, 2018, and March 16, 2019.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the administrative mechanisms of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, which would include application processing and verification for regularization.

rights: Right to apply for regularization of unauthorized cultivation of government lands within the extended period.
duties: Duty to apply within the specified timeframe and according to the prescribed Form-57.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for regularization of unauthorized cultivation of government lands must be made in Form-57 within one year from the commencement date of the Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2022.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Government of Karnataka)
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force from May 30, 2022, irrespective of the publication date.
The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022, has been repealed and replaced by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act aims to amend the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959, to facilitate better development and efficient implementation of its provisions.
Rule 2: Definition of 'Assisted Society' is enlarged to include societies receiving assistance in the form of loan, grant, or guarantee for loan/interest repayment.
Rule 3: Section 2B, which is redundant, is omitted.
Rule 4: Provisions are made for the levy of fees for amendment of bye-laws of co-operative societies.
Rule 5: Self-help groups are allowed to be admitted as nominal members of a society.
Rule 6: Provisions are introduced to specify when a person ceases to be a member.
Rule 7: The Registrar's power to extend the time for convening the Annual General Body Meeting is restored, with a maximum extension of six months.
Rule 8: The term of office bearers is reduced from five years to three years.

Rule 9: Nominated members will not have the right to become bearers of a primary co-operative society, and other classes of co-operative societies can be specified by the Government. Nominated members will hold office at the pleasure of the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Registrar and other appointed authorities to enforce the provisions of the Act and ensure compliance by co-operative societies.

Right of self-help groups to be admitted as nominal members.
Right to convene Annual General Body Meetings within extended timeframes.
Right of members to hold office (subject to provisions).
duties: Duty to comply with amended provisions of the Act.
Duty to pay fees for amendment of bye-laws.
Duty to adhere to term limits for office bearers.
Duty for nominated members to hold office during the pleasure of the Government.

Societies must ensure that nominated members comply with their designated roles and limitations.

important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959.
Specific focus on co-operative society governance, membership, and financial assistance.
The term of office bearers has been reduced to three years.
Nominated members have specific restrictions on their roles.
The Act aims to improve the functioning and efficiency of co-operative societies in Karnataka.

title: The Karnataka Municipalities (Third Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to omit provisions related to specifying an Industrial Township from Section 3 and to insert a new Chapter XVI-A for specifying industrial townships, their authorities, powers, functions, and related matters.
scope: This Act applies to areas within Karnataka that are specified as Industrial Townships under the provisions of this Act. It amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, which governs municipalities within the state.

key_definitions.Industrial Township: An area specified by the Governor, having regard to factors like size, municipal services provided by industrial establishments, public infrastructure, industrial and residential buildings, and income from local administration, to be an Industrial Township.
key_definitions.Industrial Township Authority: A body corporate constituted for every Industrial Township, responsible for its administration and functions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by omitting the second proviso to sub-section (1) and sub-section (3), and inserting a new proviso to sub-section (2) regarding the status of municipal areas whose population reduces due to the specification of Industrial Township areas.
Inserts a new Chapter XVI-A after Section 364 of the principal Act, which deals with the specification of Industrial Townships and the constitution and functions of the Industrial Township Authority.

important_rules: Rule 1: Specification of an Industrial Township requires consideration of factors like area size, municipal services, public infrastructure, building types, and income from local administration and services.
Rule 2: An Industrial Township Authority will be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Rule 3: The Industrial Township Authority will consist of a Chairperson, elected members from industrial establishment owners, and nominated representatives from relevant government departments and local authorities.

Rule 4: The Industrial Township Authority is responsible for making adequate provision for various municipal services including building regulation, economic and social development planning, roads, water supply, public health, sanitation, environment protection, amenities, and more.
Rule 5: The Industrial Township Authority shall levy Property Tax on all buildings and lands within the township, with 30% of the collected tax remitted to the original local authority.
Rule 6: The Government can issue directions to the Industrial Township Authority to carry out the purposes of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka and the Industrial Township Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, as amended, and specific powers conferred upon the Industrial Township Authority, including the power to levy taxes and the power to appoint an Administrator if the Authority fails its duties.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property by the Industrial Township Authority.
Right to enter into contracts by the Industrial Township Authority.
Right of residents or affected persons to submit objections and suggestions during the notification process for an Industrial Township.
duties: Duty of the Industrial Township Authority to make adequate provision for specified municipal services and development matters.
Duty of the Industrial Township Authority to comply with directions issued by the Government.
Duty of the Industrial Township Authority to prepare and submit a budget for approval.
Duty of the Industrial Township Authority to maintain proper accounts and records.
Duty of the Industrial Township Authority to remit 30% of property tax to the original local authority.
obligations: Obligation to consult local authorities and publish draft notifications for public feedback before specifying an Industrial Township.
Obligation for the Industrial Township Authority to manage its funds and apply them for its expenses.
Obligation for the Chief Executive Officer and other officers of the Authority to perform their duties.

key_procedures: Procedure for specifying an Industrial Township: The Governor may issue a notification considering specified factors, after consulting the local authority and inviting public objections and suggestions.

Procedure for constitution of the Industrial Township Authority: The Authority is constituted with an elected Chairperson and elected/nominated members, with initial members of the first Authority being nominated by the Government.
Procedure for transaction of business: The Authority shall hold at least one meeting per month, with decisions taken by a simple majority. Quorum is five members.
Procedure for appointment of Chief Executive Officer: The Authority may appoint a Chief Executive Officer possessing qualifications notified by the Government.

Procedure for appointment of other officers and employees: The Authority may appoint officers and employees with the approval of the Government and determine their recruitment and service conditions by regulations.

Procedure for the Government to appoint an Administrator: If the Authority fails to perform its duties, the Government may appoint an Administrator after giving the Authority an opportunity to be heard.
administration: The Department of Urban Development and the Commerce and Industries Department of the Government of Karnataka, along with the Industrial Township Authority.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.
The provision for specifying an Industrial Township is now consolidated in Chapter XVI-A, replacing earlier provisions in Section 3.
The Government has the power to apply provisions of the Act, rules, and bye-laws to an Industrial Township with modifications.
The original local authority from which an Industrial Township area is carved out is entitled to receive 30% of the property tax collected by the Industrial Township Authority.

title: THE KARNATAKA SELECTION OF CANDIDATES FOR ADMISSION TO MEDICAL, DENTAL AND ENGINEERING COURSES (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2004
purpose: To make special provisions for the selection of candidates and admission to professional institutions in the State, in the light of principles laid down by the Constitution Bench in the TMA Pai's case and subsequent pronouncements, specifically for the academic year 2004-05.
scope: This Act applies to the selection of candidates for admission to Professional Institutions (Medical, Dental, and Engineering) in the State of Karnataka for the Academic year 2004-05. It covers aided, un-aided minority, and non-minority professional institutions.

key_definitions.professional institutions: Includes Medical, Dental, and Engineering colleges in the State.
key_definitions.government seats: Seats allocated to the government quota.
key_definitions.management seats: Seats allocated to the management quota in private institutions.
key_definitions.un-aided non-minority professional insti: Non-minority professional institutions not receiving aid.
key_definitions.un-aided minority professional instituti: Minority professional institutions not receiving aid.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it comes into force at once, and specifies its application to the selection of candidates for admission to Professional Institutions for the Academic year 2004-05.

States that words and expressions used in this Act shall have the same meaning as assigned to them in the Karnataka Educational Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee) Act, 1984, and the Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004.

main_sections.section_title: The sharing of seats in respect of Government seats and Management seats
main_sections.description: Details the seat sharing ratio between Government seats and Management seats for different types of professional institutions (Aided, Un-aided Non-minority, Un-aided Minority).

main_sections.section_title: Management seats shall be filled on merit
main_sections.description: Mandates that management seats in non-minority and minority institutions must be filled on merit through a Common Entrance Test (CET) conducted by the State CET Cell or the Association of Private Professional Colleges. Minority institutions may conduct their own CET, supervised by the Overseeing Committee.

Specifies that reservation of seats shall apply to all seats in the Government quota in accordance with rule 14 of the Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004.

main_sections.section_title: Fee fixed for Professional Course for the academic year 2004-05
main_sections.description: States that the fee payable for professional courses for the academic year 2004-05 shall not exceed the fee fixed by the Fee Determination Committee, including tentative fees for engineering courses.

main_sections.section_title: Invalidation of admissions made in violation of the Act
main_sections.description: Declares that all admissions made in violation of the Act for the academic year 2004-05, whether made before or after the commencement of the Act, shall be invalid.
Prescribes a penalty of fine up to five lakh rupees for contravening the provisions of this Act or the Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004.
Stipulates that no court shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a written complaint by an officer authorized by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith or intended to be done under this Act by any officer of the Government.
Empowers the Government to issue general or special orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act.

Grants the Government the power to make rules, by notification in the official Gazette, for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying these rules before the State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Applicability of Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004
main_sections.description: States that in respect of any matter not covered under this Act, the provisions contained in the Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004 shall apply.

important_rules: Rule: Seat Sharing Ratios - For Aided Institutions: 95% Government, 5% Management. For Un-aided Non-minority Institutions: 75% Government, 25% Management. For Un-aided Minority Institutions: 50% Government, 50% Management.
Rule: Filling of Management Seats - Must be on merit through a Common Entrance Test.
Rule: Fee Determination - Fees for 2004-05 shall not exceed the fee fixed by the Fee Determination Committee.
Rule: Invalidation of Admissions - Admissions made in violation of the Act are invalid.

penalties: Fine which may extend to five lakh rupees for contravention of the Act or associated Rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, through authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings initiated on complaint by an authorized officer; invalidation of admissions made in violation of the Act; and imposition of fines.

rights: Right of students to be admitted on merit basis for management seats.
