Right of institutions to conduct their own CET for minority institutions (subject to oversight).
duties: Duty of managements to fill management seats on merit.
Duty of the government to ensure fair admission processes.
Duty of the government to fix fees not exceeding those determined by the Fee Determination Committee.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the seat sharing ratios specified in the Act.
Obligation for all admissions to comply with the Act's provisions to be valid.

key_procedures: Admission Procedure: Candidates are selected for Government seats based on reservation rules and for Management seats through a merit-based Common Entrance Test. The seat sharing ratio is determined by the type of institution.
Rule Making Procedure: The Government can make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, which must be laid before the State Legislature for approval or modification.
administration: The Government of Karnataka is responsible for the administration of this Act, including issuing notifications, authorizing officers, and making rules.
important_notes: This Act is a special and temporary measure for the academic year 2004-05 only.
The principles laid down in the TMA Pai case and subsequent pronouncements by the Supreme Court are the basis for this Act.
In case of difficulties, the Government can issue orders not inconsistent with the Act to remove them.
For matters not covered by this Act, the Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Professional Institutions Rules, 2004 shall apply.

title: The Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, to enhance the salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to members and former members of the Karnataka Legislature due to a considerable rise in living costs and depreciation of money value since the last revision in 2000.
scope: This Act applies to members and former members of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, and amends the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956. Geographically, it applies within the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956 (Karnataka Act 2 of 1957).
key_definitions.member: Includes a person who prior to the 1st day of November 1956 represented any of the areas which with effect on and from the said date have become part of the new State of Karnataka, as a member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of the State of which the said areas were part. For nominated members, eligibility for pension requires permanent residence in an area forming part of Karnataka during their membership.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by increasing the monthly salary from six thousand rupees to twelve thousand rupees.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting the heading 'Chairman and Speaker' to 'Chairman, Speaker etc.', expanding the list of positions to include Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition, and Government Chief Whip, and increasing their remuneration from ten thousand rupees to twenty thousand rupees.
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act by increasing the daily allowance from ten rupees to twelve rupees.
Amends Section 10 of the principal Act by increasing the monthly allowance from four thousand rupees to eight thousand rupees.
Amends Section 10A of the principal Act by increasing the monthly allowance from five thousand five hundred rupees to ten thousand rupees for both sub-sections (1) and (2).
Removes Section 10B from the principal Act.
Amends Section 10D of the principal Act by substituting references to 'section 10B' with 'section 4' in both sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 10E of the principal Act by increasing the monthly allowance from five thousand rupees to ten thousand rupees.
Removes Section 10F from the principal Act.
Amends Section 10I of the principal Act by substituting references to 'section 10F' with 'section 4' in both sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 10J of the principal Act by increasing the monthly allowance from four thousand rupees to eight thousand rupees.
Removes Section 10K from the principal Act.
Amends Section 10N of the principal Act by substituting references to 'section 10K' with 'section 4' in both sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 11 of the principal Act by increasing the monthly allowance from four thousand rupees to eight thousand rupees.

Substantially amends Section 11A concerning pensions. It sets a base pension of five thousand rupees per mensem for those serving five years as a member (Assembly or Council, or both). An additional pension of five hundred rupees per mensem is provided for each subsequent completed year, up to a maximum of ten thousand rupees per mensem. Several provisos clarify how service is calculated, including for dissolution of assembly, termination by lots, pending election petitions, mid-term elections/nominations, and resignations after three years. The explanation for 'member' is also included, along with a provision for nominated members.
Amends Section 11B by substituting 'five hundred rupees' with 'fifty percent of the pension admissible to a member under section 11A'.

Makes several amendments to Section 12 concerning traveling and constituency allowances. It increases daily allowances for meetings, introduces a fixed traveling allowance option, increases allowances for deputy speaker and others, allows ex-members to receive constituency allowances, and significantly increases constituency traveling allowance from a yearly installment to a monthly amount. It also revises the allowance for telephone and cell phone expenses.

important_rules: Members of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council shall be paid a salary of twelve thousand rupees per month.
The Chairman, Speaker, Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition, and Government Chief Whip shall be paid twenty thousand rupees.
A person who has served for a period of five years as a member of the Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly shall be eligible for a pension of five thousand rupees per mensem for life.
Additional pension for members serving more than five years is five hundred rupees per mensem for each subsequent completed year, capped at ten thousand rupees per mensem.
Daily allowances for attending meetings are increased.
Traveling allowances for meetings can be a fixed sum of one thousand five hundred rupees per meeting in lieu of distance-based calculation.
Constituency traveling allowance is now five thousand rupees per month.
An allowance of seven thousand five hundred rupees per month is provided for telephone and cell phone expenses.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly detail penalties for violations. Enforcement would likely fall under the general administrative purview of the Karnataka Legislature and its Secretariat, and potentially judicial review.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the administration of the salaries, pensions, and allowances as stipulated in the amended Act by the relevant government departments.

rights: Right to receive enhanced salaries and allowances as a sitting member.
Right to receive pension after completing the prescribed years of service as a former member.
Right to receive traveling and constituency allowances.
Right to receive allowances for telephone and cell phone usage.
duties: Duty to serve as a member of the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council as per the Constitution and relevant laws.
Duty to adhere to conditions and requirements for claiming salaries, pensions, and allowances.
obligations: Obligation of the State Legislature to ensure timely payment of salaries, pensions, and allowances.
Obligation of members and former members to fulfill service and eligibility criteria for financial benefits.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections of the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, to reflect the revised financial entitlements.
Application of the amended provisions for calculating and disbursing salaries, pensions, and allowances to eligible individuals.
Process for determining pension eligibility based on years of service, with specific conditions for various scenarios (e.g., dissolution, bye-elections, nominations, resignations).
Procedure for claiming constituency traveling allowance on a monthly basis.
Procedure for claiming allowances for telephone and cell phone expenditure.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.
Specific deeming provisions exist for calculating pension eligibility in cases of premature termination of service or inability to complete a full term.
The definition of 'member' for pension purposes includes individuals who represented areas that later became part of Karnataka, as well as specific conditions for nominated members.
The Act explicitly omits certain sections (10B, 10F, 10K) from the principal Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Forest Act, 1963, to provide for the levy of interest on belated payments of Forest Development Tax, to ensure timely payment of government dues, and to maintain consistency in revenue flow to the State Exchequer. The levy of interest is intended to act as a deterrent against delayed payments.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Forest Act, 1963. It applies to the levy and collection of interest on Forest Development Tax within Karnataka. The scope is primarily financial and administrative concerning forest-related taxes.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Forest (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends Section 98A of the principal Karnataka Forest Act, 1963, by inserting a new sub-section (4). This new sub-section mandates the levy and collection of interest at the rate of eighteen percent per annum on all tax dues until the date of payment or recovery.

This section amends Section 98B of the principal Act by inserting the words 'and interest' after the word 'tax' in sub-section (2)(a). This ensures that interest, along with the tax, is accounted for in the relevant provisions of Section 98B.

important_rules: Rule: Interest at the rate of eighteen percent per annum shall be levied and collected on all Forest Development Tax dues that are belatedly paid or recovered, until the date of such payment or recovery. (Derived from Section 2 of the Act).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering the Karnataka Forest Act, 1963, and collecting Forest Development Tax.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of interest on belated tax payments, as stipulated in the amended sections of the principal Act.

rights: The right of the Government to collect interest on delayed Forest Development Tax payments.
duties: The duty to pay Forest Development Tax on time.
The duty to pay interest on belated payments of Forest Development Tax.
obligations: Obligation to pay interest at 18% per annum on all tax dues until payment or recovery.

key_procedures: Procedure: If Forest Development Tax is paid belatedly, interest at the rate of 18% per annum is to be calculated from the due date of the tax until the actual date of payment or recovery and collected by the relevant authorities. (Implied from Section 2).
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for enactment), and likely the Forest Department or Revenue Department for administration and collection of Forest Development Tax and associated interest.
important_notes: The amendment introduces interest as a component of Forest Development Tax dues, aligning with practices in Sales Tax and Income Tax departments.
The rate of interest is fixed at 18% per annum.
The amendment is in line with Entry 17A of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA PANCHAYATH RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Panchayath Raj Act, 1993, to define 'Panchayat Development Officer' and provide for their powers and functions, to introduce modern technology like electronic voting machines for timely and precise election results in Grama Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, and Zilla Panchayat elections, and to provide for fifty percent reservation for women in seats and offices across all three tiers of Panchayath Raj Institutions.
scope: This act applies to the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, and amends provisions related to Grama Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, and Zilla Panchayat elections and administration within the state of Karnataka.

key_definitions.Panchayath Development Officer: The Panchayat Development Officer of the Grama Panchayat.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force at once.
Inserts the definition of 'Panchayath Development Officer' into the principal Act.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a sub-section of Section 5.
Inserts provisions for the adoption of voting machines in Grama Panchayat elections.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a clause of Section 44.
Substitutes 'Panchayat Development Officer and Secretary' for 'Secretary' in a sub-section of Section 111.
Substitutes 'Panchayat Development Officer, Secretary and Accounts Assistant' for 'Secretary' in a sub-section of Section 112.
Substitutes 'Panchayat Development Officer' for 'Secretary' in sub-sections (2) and (4) of Section 113.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a sub-section of Section 123.
Inserts provisions for the adoption of voting machines in Taluk Panchayat elections.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a clause of Section 138.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a sub-section of Section 162.
Inserts provisions for the adoption of voting machines in Zilla Panchayat elections.
Substitutes 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in a clause of Section 177.
Substitutes 'Panchayat Development Officer' for 'Secretary' in a sub-section of Section 200.
Substitutes 'Panchayat Development Officer' for 'Secretary' in sub-sections (1) and (5) of Section 241.

important_rules: Reservation for women: Fifty percent reservation is to be provided for women in seats and offices in all three tiers of Panchayath Raj Institutions.

Use of voting machines: Voting machines may be adopted for Grama Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, and Zilla Panchayat elections as prescribed by the State Election Commission, considering the circumstances of each case.

Definition of Voting Machine: Any machine or apparatus, electronic or otherwise, used for giving or recording votes, and any reference to ballot boxes or ballot papers in the Act shall include such voting machines where used.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Election Commission (for election-related matters) and relevant authorities under the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, and by the prescribed authorities implementing the new provisions.

rights: Right to fifty percent reservation for women in Panchayath Raj Institutions.
Right to vote using electronic voting machines where adopted.
duties: Duty to implement the fifty percent reservation for women.
Duty to adopt and implement the use of electronic voting machines as prescribed.
Duty to define and empower the Panchayat Development Officer.

key_procedures: Insertion of definition for 'Panchayath Development Officer'.
Substitution of 'fifty percent' for 'one third' in various sections relating to reservations.

Insertion of provisions allowing the use of voting machines in elections for Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats, with specifications on how and where they can be adopted by the State Election Commission.

Substitution of 'Secretary' with 'Panchayat Development Officer' and in some cases 'Panchayat Development Officer and Secretary' or 'Panchayat Development Officer, Secretary and Accounts Assistant' in relation to various administrative roles.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the enactment process), and the relevant Panchayath Raj administration bodies and State Election Commission for implementation.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1993).
The amendments related to voting machines are subject to prescription by the State Election Commission and depend on the circumstances of each case.

title: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 to provide for the establishment of the Karnataka Property Tax Board, as recommended by the 13th Finance Commission of India, to assist urban local bodies in determining and collecting Property Tax, and to make provisions relating to audit reports to be placed before the State Legislature.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1977) and the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 22 of 1964). The scope is related to property tax determination and collection within municipalities (which include municipal corporations, city or town municipal councils, and town panchayats) in Karnataka.

key_definitions.Fund: The Karnataka Property Tax Board Fund.
key_definitions.Municipality: A municipal corporation established under section 3 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, or a city or a town municipal council incorporated under section 10 or a town panchayat constituted under section 351 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Municipal Corporations and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2011' and states that it shall come into force from such date as the State Government may appoint, allowing for different dates for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 14 of 1977
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Chapter IX-A titled 'Establishment of the Karnataka Property Tax Board' into the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. This chapter contains sections detailing definitions, overriding effect on other laws, establishment, composition, validation, functions, publication of draft valuation rates, appointment of staff, funds, grants, payments by municipalities, annual report, expenditure, budget, accounts, audit, delegation of powers, public servant status for board members, role of the Secretary, custody of records, control over establishment, and notice for suits.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Karnataka Act 22 of 1964
main_sections.description: This section is mentioned in the Arrangement of Sections but not detailed in the provided text. It implies an amendment to the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, likely to align with the provisions for the Property Tax Board.

important_rules: No municipality or corporation shall determine the rate of any zone, area, or any nature or class of building for taxation without consultation of the Board (Section 102B).

The Board shall perform functions including enumerating properties, reviewing the property tax system, suggesting bases for valuation, designing transparent procedures, recommending tax rates and modalities for periodic revision, assisting municipalities, ensuring transparency in valuation, publishing work plans, recommending market value guidelines, and providing training for officers (Section 102F).
After determination of valuation rates, the Board shall publish draft rates, consider suggestions, and recommend final rates to the municipality (Section 102G).
The Board's accounts shall be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the State Government (Section 102Q).
An annual report of the Board's activities shall be prepared and placed before the State Legislature (Section 102M).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Legislature, the State Government, and the Karnataka Property Tax Board itself, through its appointed authorities and staff.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing municipal laws, establishment of the Board with defined functions, consultation requirements for tax determination, and oversight by the State Government, including budget approval and auditor's report review. Enforcement also involves the Board's powers to recommend rates, assist municipalities, and conduct training.

rights: Municipalities have the right to receive assistance from the Board in determining property tax rates (Section 102F(f)).
The Board has the right to sue and be sued in its corporate name and to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 102C(2)).
The State Government has the right to approve the Board's budget and make modifications (Section 102O(2)).
The State Government has the right to issue directions after perusal of the auditor's report (Section 102Q(3)).
duties: Municipalities and other local authorities are obligated to pay a proportion of the expenditure incurred by the Board for performing its functions (Section 102L).
The Board is responsible for enumerating properties, developing a database, reviewing the tax system, and recommending tax rates (Section 102F).
The Board must ensure transparency in the capital valuation process and facilitate disclosure (Section 102F(g)).
The Board must prepare and submit an annual report to the State Legislature (Section 102M).
The Board must prepare a budget for the ensuing financial year and forward it to the State Government for approval (Section 102O(1)).
The Secretary is responsible for the custody of all records of the Board (Section 102U).
The Secretary shall carry on correspondence between the Board and the Government or other authorities (Section 102T).

key_procedures: Establishment of the Karnataka Property Tax Board by State Government notification (Section 102C).
The Board undertaking functions like enumeration of properties, developing databases, reviewing tax systems, and formulating transparent procedures for valuation (Section 102F).

Publication of draft valuation rates by the Board, allowing for a minimum of thirty days for suggestions, followed by consideration of these suggestions, and preparation of final valuation rates to be recommended to the municipality (Section 102G).
Preparation and submission of an annual budget by the Board to the State Government for approval (Section 102O).

Annual audit of the Board's accounts by an auditor appointed by the State Government, submission of audited accounts and auditor's report to the State Government, and compliance with State Government directions (Section 102Q).

Procedure for instituting suits against the Board or its officers, requiring a two-month written notice detailing the cause of action, relief sought, compensation claimed, and plaintiff's details, unless the suit is for an injunction where notice would defeat the object (Section 102W).
administration: The Karnataka Property Tax Board and the State Government (specifically, the department responsible for municipal administration, implied by the power to make rules and approve budgets).
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government, which can be different for different provisions.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

The Chairperson and members of the Board hold office for a period of five years and are not eligible for reappointment or for further appointment to any office of profit under the State Government or related entities.
No action of the Board shall be invalid due to a vacancy in the office of its members.

The Chairperson shall be an officer not below the rank of Secretary to the Government. Up to two members can have expertise in municipal administration, property valuation, accountancy, law, and urban planning.
The expenditure incurred by the Board for its operations, including salaries and contingencies, is defrayed from the State Property Tax Board Fund.
The Board has the same financial powers as a State Government department Secretary; matters beyond that require State Government decision.
Members, officers, and employees of the Board are deemed public servants under the Indian Penal Code.
Notice is required before instituting suits against the Board or its personnel, with exceptions for injunctions.
The State Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of Chapter IX-A, with a provision for previous publication, unless immediate action is required.

title: ST. JOSEPH’S UNIVERSITY ACT, 2021
purpose: To establish the St. Joseph’s University, a public private partnership University of unitary nature aided by State and Central Government in the State of Karnataka, focusing on advancement of applied university in various disciplines, fostering industry and market relevant studies, research and innovation, and providing opportunities to serve society and the nation.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to the establishment and functioning of St. Joseph's University.

key_definitions.University: St. Joseph's University, established and incorporated under this Act by upgrading St, Joseph's College (Autonomous), Bengaluru, under the provisions of RUSA 2.0 and as a public-private-partnership Unitary University.
key_definitions.Sponsoring Body: The Bangalore Jesuit Educational Society (BJES), registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960.
key_definitions.Public-Private partnership University: A University partially funded by the State and Central Government and administered by the Sponsoring Body.
key_definitions.Statutes or Regulation: The Statutes and Regulations of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.National Accreditation or Regulatory Bod: A body established by the Central Government for laying down norms and conditions for ensuring academic standards of higher education, including UGC, AICTE, CSIR, ICSSR, NAAC, NBA, NCTE, Distance Education Council, Council of Architecture, Rehabilitation Council of India and other statutory bodies.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as the St. Joseph's University Act, 2021, states its extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Board of Governors', 'Board of Management', 'Finance Committee', 'Chancellor', 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Registrar', 'Sponsoring Body', 'University', and 'Government'.

main_sections.section_title: Proposal for the establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Sponsoring Body to propose the establishment of the University to the State Government, detailing the particulars to be included in the proposal.
Details the process for the establishment of the University upon receiving the State Government's approval.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules and regulations made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules by the State Government
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: The Sponsoring Body shall have the right to establish a public-private partnership University, a non-affiliating Unitary University, in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

Rule: The proposal to establish a University shall be made to the State Government by the Sponsoring Body and must contain specific particulars regarding the University's objects, extent, programs, faculties, campus development, financial outlays, resource mobilization, and fund generation.
Rule: The University shall be open to all classes, castes, creeds, genders, or nations and shall not discriminate on any of these grounds.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules and regulations made thereunder are specified in Section 60.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, the Karnataka State Higher Education Council, and the various authorities of the University are involved in the enforcement and oversight of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the provisions of the Act, rules made by the State Government, Statutes and Regulations of the University, and periodical inspections by the Karnataka State Higher Education Council.

rights: Right of the Sponsoring Body to propose and establish the University.
Right to appeal as outlined in Section 43.
The University shall be open to all classes, castes, creeds, genders, or nations (Section 9).
duties: Duty of the University to promote and undertake advancement of applied university education.
Duty to foster industry and market relevant studies, research, and innovation.
Duty to maintain funds and prepare annual reports and accounts for audit.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act, Statutes, and Regulations.
Obligation to comply with guidelines from National Accreditation or Regulatory Bodies.
Obligation to ensure proper maintenance of funds, accounts, and audit.

key_procedures: Procedure for proposing the establishment of the University (Section 3).
Procedure for making Statutes (Section 36) and Regulations (Section 39).
Procedure for Audit of Accounts (Section 56).
administration: The Act establishes various authorities and officers for the administration of the University, including the Board of Governors, Board of Management, Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, and Finance Officer. The State Government also plays a role in administration through rule-making and issuing directions.
important_notes: Note: The Act has come into force w.e.f. 02.07.2022 by Notification No. ED/117/URC/2021 Dated: 02.07.2022.
Note: The University is established as a public-private partnership Unitary University of a unitary nature.
Note: The establishment of the University is in accordance with the guidelines provided under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) 2.0.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROTECTION OF INTEREST OF DEPOSITORS IN FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004, by making offences cognizable and non-bailable, providing for clubbing of multiple First Information Reports (FIRs) against the same accused or financial establishment, and empowering special courts to try other offences alongside offences under this Act during the same trial.
scope: This Act applies to financial establishments operating within Karnataka and depositors who have invested in them. It amends the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2022, and states that it is deemed to have come into force with effect from May 4, 2022.

Inserts a new section (9A) into the principal Act, making offences under the Act cognizable and non-bailable. It also empowers a prescribed officer to order the clubbing of multiple FIRs related to the same accused or financial establishment into a single case for common investigation and filing of a common final report before the Special Court where the earliest FIR was registered.

Amends Section 10 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (4). This amendment empowers the Special Court, while trying an offence under this Act, to also try any other offence with which the accused may be charged under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in the same trial.

Repeals the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022 (Karnataka Ordinance 01 of 2022). It also includes a savings clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Offences under this Act are cognizable and non-bailable.
Multiple FIRs against the same accused or financial establishment can be clubbed into a single case for common investigation and trial.
Special Courts can try offences under this Act along with other offences that the accused may be charged with under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in the same trial.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed officer for ordering clubbing of FIRs; Special Courts for trial.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation and prosecution by designated authorities, trial by Special Courts.

rights: Depositors have the right to protection of their interests in financial establishments.
Accused have the right to a fair trial.

key_procedures: Procedure for clubbing FIRs: A prescribed officer may order the clubbing of subsequent FIRs into the earliest case and order a common investigation. A common final report is to be filed before the Special Court where the earliest FIR was registered.

Procedure for joint trial: Special Courts, while trying an offence under this Act, may also try other offences with which the accused may be charged under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in the same trial.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory G. SRIDHAR, Secretary to Government).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from May 4, 2022.
The amendment is based on the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022, which has been repealed and replaced by this Act.

title: THE TUNGABHADRA SUGARS (DEVI SUGARS) LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ORDINANCE, 2001
purpose: To acquire and transfer the undertakings of The Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited in public interest and for the purpose of ensuring the more equitable distribution of income and wealth of the Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited, for the management of its affairs and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of The Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 2001. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of August 2001.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of the Karnataka Act 1 of 1997
main_sections.description: This section refers to the repeal of the Karnataka Act 1 of 1997. The Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1996 is hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government shall, on and from the appointed day, be deemed to have acquired the undertakings of the Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited.
Rule 2: The undertakings of the Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited shall stand transferred to and vest in the Government.

Rule 3: The acquisition and transfer of the undertaking is for the purpose of ensuring more equitable distribution of income and wealth, for the management of its affairs, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process and administrative actions as per the Act.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire the undertakings of the Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited.
duties: Duty of the Government to manage the acquired undertakings.
Duty to ensure equitable distribution of income and wealth.
obligations: Obligation to repeal the Karnataka Act 1 of 1997.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Deemed acquisition of the undertakings by the Government on the appointed day.
Procedure 2: Transfer and vesting of the undertakings in the Government.
administration: The Government of Karnataka
important_notes: Note 1: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 20th August 2001.
Note 2: The Ordinance supersedes the provisions of the Karnataka Act 1 of 1997 (The Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1996).
Note 3: The Tungabhadra Sugars (Devi Sugars) Limited Ordinance, 2001 published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on the 20th day of August 2001.

title: THE KARNATAKA COMMAND AREAS DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend section 24 of the Karnataka Command Areas Development Act, 1980, to provide for placing the audited accounts of the Command Area Development Authority before each House of the State Legislature along with the Annual Reports.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Command Areas Development Act, 1980. It applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with the development of command areas under irrigation projects.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Command Areas Development (Amendment) Act, 2003, and it comes into force at once.

Inserts a provision in sub-section (2) of section 24 of the Karnataka Command Areas Development Act, 1980, mandating that the audited accounts and the report shall be laid before each House of the State Legislature as soon as may be after it is received by the State Government.

important_rules: The audited accounts and the report of the Command Area Development Authority shall be laid before each House of the State Legislature as soon as may be after it is received by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the State Legislature, through the process of laying reports and accounts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ensuring that audited accounts and reports are presented to the legislature.

duties: The State Government has a duty to receive the audited accounts and report from the Authority.
The State Government has a duty to lay the audited accounts and report before each House of the State Legislature as soon as may be after its receipt.

key_procedures: Preparation of Annual Reports by the Authority.
Auditing and certification of CADA accounts by the Controller of State Accounts.
Receipt of audited accounts and report by the State Government.
Laying of audited accounts and report before each House of the State Legislature by the State Government.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (for publishing and enacting the act). The underlying act is related to Command Areas Development.
important_notes: The amendment is to address a lack of specific provision for placing audited CADA accounts before the State Legislature.
This amendment is in accordance with Entry 17 of List-II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA ENTERTAINMENTS TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To re-introduce the provision of collection of tax-free service charges by cinema theatre owners for the maintenance of the theatres, as requested by the film industry.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958. It applies to proprietors of cinema theatres in Karnataka that pay tax on cinematograph shows. It specifically allows for the collection of service charges on payments for admission to various classes of theatres.

key_definitions.proprietor of a cinema theatre: An entity or individual owning and operating a cinema theatre.
key_definitions.service charges: An amount collected by cinema theatre owners for the maintenance of the theatres, in addition to the payment for admission.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005, and specifies that it comes into force at once.
Introduces a new section, 4-AA, into the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958. This new section deals with the 'Collection of Service Charges'.

important_rules: Every proprietor of a cinema theatre paying tax on cinematograph shows may collect service charges.
The collection of service charges is subject to such rules as may be prescribed.
The amount collected as service charges shall not exceed the amount specified in the table.
For Air-conditioned and Air-cooled Theatres, the maximum service charge is one rupee and fifty paise on each payment for admission.
For Other Theatres (excluding Touring Talkies), the maximum service charge is one rupee on each payment for admission.
For theatres existing on the date this section comes into force, the collection of service charges shall be in addition to the payment for admission prevalent immediately before commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly, the authorities responsible for enforcing the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and mechanisms established by the Karnataka Entertainments Tax Act, 1958, and any prescribed rules.

rights: Right of cinema theatre proprietors to collect service charges, subject to limitations and rules.
Right of patrons to be admitted to cinema shows upon payment for admission and any applicable service charges.
duties: Duty of cinema theatre proprietors to ensure that service charges collected do not exceed the specified limits.
Duty of cinema theatre proprietors to comply with any prescribed rules regarding the collection of service charges.
obligations: Obligation for proprietors of existing theatres to collect service charges in addition to pre-existing admission payments.

key_procedures: Cinema theatre proprietors calculating and collecting service charges up to the specified maximum amounts per admission payment.
Cinema theatre proprietors ensuring that the collection of service charges is in accordance with any prescribed rules.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation ( Karnataka). The enforcement would likely fall under the tax administration department of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
The collection of service charges is a new provision being re-introduced for theatre maintenance.
The rates for service charges are capped and differ based on theatre classification.

title: The Karnataka Rajya Dr. Gangubai Hangal Sangeetha Mattu Pradarshaka Kalegala Vishwavidyalaya Act, 2009
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of the Karnataka Rajya Dr. Gangubai Hangal Sangeetha Mattu Pradarshaka Kalegala Vishwavidyalaya, exclusively for furthering the advancement of learning and prosecution of research, documentation, publishing of audio and video recording, and popularising all branches of music and performing arts.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Karnataka Rajya Dr. Gangubai Hangal Sangeetha Mattu Pradarshaka Kalegala Vishwavidyalaya. Its jurisdiction is primarily within Karnataka, with provisions for recognizing institutions outside India for specific purposes. The scope covers all branches of Music and performing arts, including dance, drama, Yakshagana, Harikatha, and other arts the university may decide upon.

key_definitions.Accompanists: Players of various instruments like Hormonium, Tabla, Violin, Mridangam, Ghatam, Khanjeera etc.
key_definitions.Appointed date: The date appointed for the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Hostel: A unit of residence for the students of the University maintained or recognised by the University in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.performing arts: Includes dance, drama, Yakshagana, Harikatha and such other performing arts as the university may decide.
key_definitions.Statutes: The statutes of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.Teachers: Professors, emeritus Professors, readers, lecturers and other like persons as may be declared by the statutes to be teachers.
key_definitions.University: The Karnataka Rajya Dr. Gangubai Hangal Sangeetha Mattu Pradarshaka Kalegala Vishwavidyalaya established under Section-3.
key_definitions.University Grants Commission: The Commission established under Section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956 (Central Act 3 of 1956).
key_definitions.University Library: A Library maintained by the University, whether instituted by it or not.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Accompanists', 'Appointed date', 'Government', 'Hostel', 'performing arts', 'Prescribed', 'Statutes', 'Teachers', 'University', 'University Grants Commission', and 'University Library'.

Establishes the Karnataka Rajya Dr. Gangubai Hangal Sangeetha Mattu Pradarshaka Kalegala Vishwavidyalaya, describes its corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, unitary and residential nature, jurisdiction (headquarters within Mysore District or within a 20 km radius), and powers related to property acquisition and contracts. It also outlines requirements for the approval of property transfers and the procedure for legal proceedings.

Outlines the comprehensive objectives of the University, including providing instruction and research in Music and performing arts, preserving traditional arts, promoting them, facilitating exchange of ideas, preparing and publishing works, regularizing study, fostering interdisciplinary studies, establishing museums and archives, digitizing manuscripts, establishing studios for audio-video recording, organizing events, establishing directorates for supportive education, distance and online education, a publication department, chairs for research, hobby classes, organizing cultural tours, experimenting with music and arts as therapy, and creating networks with similar institutions.

Details the powers of the University, including instituting and conferring degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions, conferring honorary degrees, supervising hostels and student welfare, prescribing conditions for withholding awards, cooperating with other institutions, establishing and maintaining libraries and research facilities, instituting research posts, and appointing personnel to these posts.

important_rules: The University must be of a unitary and residential type.
No institution affiliated with another university in the state shall be recognized without prior government and concerned university approval.
The University requires prior government approval to lease, sell, or otherwise transfer any immovable property.
All legal proceedings by or against the University must have their pleadings signed and verified by, and processes served on, the Registrar.

The University's objectives are to systematically study, research, preserve, promote, and disseminate knowledge of Music and performing arts, fostering a common platform for scholars and promoting traditional arts with an emphasis on Karnataka's forms.

rights: The right to establish and incorporate a university for Music and performing arts.
The right to provide instruction, research, and advancement of studies in Music and performing arts.
The right to preserve, foster, popularise, and promote traditional Indian Music and performing arts.
The right to confer degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.
The right to cooperate with other universities and bodies.
The right to establish and maintain libraries, research stations, museums, and publication bureaus.
The right to institute research posts and appoint persons to them.
duties: To systematize the study of Music and performing arts.
To make provision for research and advancement of studies in Music and performing arts.
To provide a common platform for scholars for exchange of ideas.
To preserve, foster, popularise and promote traditional Indian Music and performing arts.
To make Music and performing arts popular among all sections of society.
To regularize the study of all forms of Music and performing arts.
To establish and maintain University libraries, research stations, museums for research and publication bureau.
To supervise and control hostels and regulate discipline among students.
obligations: The University has an obligation to obtain prior approval from the Government and the concerned University before recognizing any affiliated institution.
The University has an obligation to obtain prior approval from the Government before leasing, selling, or otherwise transferring any immoveable property.
The University has an obligation to serve the purposes and objectives for which it is established.

key_procedures: The establishment of the University requires an Act of the Karnataka State Legislature.
The commencement of the Act is determined by a notification from the State Government.
The University shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Legal proceedings against the University are handled by the Registrar.
The conferment of degrees and diplomas requires research or study under prescribed conditions.
The establishment of chairs for research and hobby classes are within the University's purview.
The University can enter into contracts and do all other things necessary for its purposes, subject to government approval for immovable property transactions.
administration: The Karnataka State Legislature enacts the law, and the State Government plays a role in appointments, approvals, and notifications. Specific administrative bodies and officers of the University (Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate, Academic Council, Registrar, Finance Officer) are outlined in subsequent chapters.
important_notes: The Act has been amended by Act 39 of 2017 (enhancing Vice-Chancellor age limit and changing nomenclature) and Act 31 of 2020 (removing discriminatory provisions against persons suffering from leprosy).
The headquarters of the University shall be located within the limits of the Mysore District or in any place within a radius of twenty kilometers around those limits.
The University is of a unitary and residential type.

The University shall not recognize any institution affiliated to, or associated with, or maintained by any other University in the State without prior approval of the Government and the concerned University.

title: THE KARNATAKA LOKAYUKTA (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984 to enable the Karnataka Lokayukta to function more effectively by including certain categories of secretaries, conferring suo-motu investigation powers on the Lokayukta for actions of public servants with high remuneration, allowing Lokayukta and Upalokayukta to discharge each other's functions during vacancies, permitting legal heirs to file or pursue complaints, and clarifying the utilization of services of any person or agency.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984. It applies to public servants within Karnataka, specifically addressing actions of the Chief Minister, Ministers, members of the State Legislature, nominated authorities, and other public servants earning above a certain remuneration. It also pertains to the functioning of the Lokayukta and Upalokayukta within the state.

key_definitions.Secretary: Includes the Chief Secretary, Additional Chief Secretary, Principal Secretary, or Secretary-II to the Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by substituting the definition of 'Secretary' to include Chief Secretary, Additional Chief Secretary, Principal Secretary, or Secretary-II.

Amends Section 7 of the principal Act to allow the Lokayukta to investigate actions of public servants with fixed pay, salary, or remuneration of more than twenty thousand per month (with certain exceptions) upon recording an opinion in writing. It also allows the Lokayukta to discharge Upalokayukta functions during a vacancy and vice-versa, and clarifies the insertion of 'recorded in writing' for the Upalokayukta's opinion.

Amends Section 9 of the principal Act to allow legal representatives or authorized persons to file or prosecute a complaint if the aggrieved person is deceased or unable to act. It also specifies the inclusion of the Lokayukta's written opinion for suo-motu investigations when referring to complaints.
Amends Section 13 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'after giving an opportunity of being heard' in relation to accepting or rejecting a declaration.

Amends Section 15 of the principal Act to require prior concurrence of the Central Government and State Government for certain actions and to allow the utilization of services of 'any person or any other agency' (deemed to have been substituted retrospectively from August 1, 2006). It also inserts provisions for the Lokayukta to discharge Upalokayukta functions during a vacancy.

Validates any action taken by the Lokayukta under the Principal Act prior to the commencement of this Amendment Act, even if the Lokayukta lacked specific powers at the time, and prevents such actions from being invalidated or questioned in any court or authority.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Lokayukta may investigate actions taken by or with the approval of the Chief Minister, Ministers, members of the State Legislature, or nominated authorities, if a complaint involving a grievance or allegation is made.

Rule 2: The Lokayukta may investigate actions of other public servants earning more than twenty thousand per month if a complaint is made, or if the Lokayukta, in writing, considers the action to be the subject of a grievance or allegation.
Rule 3: In case of a grievance, if the aggrieved person is deceased or unable to act, their legal representatives or an authorized person can file or pursue the complaint.
Rule 4: The Lokayukta and Upalokayukta can discharge each other's functions when their respective offices are vacant.
Rule 5: The Lokayukta and Upalokayukta can utilize the services of any person or any other agency.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Lokayukta
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of complaints, suo-motu investigations, and recommendations made by the Lokayukta. The validation section also suggests that past actions are deemed valid, implying enforcement of the act's intent.

rights: Right of an aggrieved person to file a complaint.
Right of legal heirs or authorized persons to file or pursue a complaint if the aggrieved person is deceased or unable to act.
Right to have actions investigated by the Lokayukta under certain conditions.
duties: Duty of public servants to cooperate with investigations.
Duty of the Lokayukta to investigate actions of public servants as per the Act.
Duty of the State Government to appoint a date for the commencement of the Act by notification.
obligations: Obligation for Lokayukta to record opinion in writing for suo-motu investigations concerning specific public servants.
Obligation to provide an opportunity of being heard before accepting or rejecting a declaration (Section 13).

key_procedures: Procedure for filing a complaint: A complaint can be filed by an aggrieved person, or by their legal heirs/authorized representative if the aggrieved person is deceased or unable to act.
Procedure for investigation: The Lokayukta can investigate actions based on a complaint or suo-motu upon recording an opinion in writing.
Procedure for filling vacancies: The Lokayukta can discharge the functions of the Upalokayukta when the Upalokayukta's office is vacant, and vice-versa.
administration: The Karnataka Lokayukta and the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as evidenced by the Secretary's signature) are involved in the administration and implementation of this act.
important_notes: The definition of 'Secretary' has been expanded.
The Lokayukta's suo-motu investigative powers now extend to public servants earning over twenty thousand per month, with specific exclusions.
The ability of legal heirs to pursue complaints is a significant addition.
The validation clause retrospectively legalizes past actions of the Lokayukta taken under the principal act.
The amendment concerning the utilization of services of 'any person or any other agency' is retrospective from August 1, 2006.

title: THE KARNATAKA GROUND WATER (REGULATION AND CONTROL OF DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To regulate and control the development and management of ground water in the State of Karnataka and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, including controlling indiscriminate exploitation of ground water, especially in notified areas.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the development and management of groundwater, including extraction and use, and matters related to its regulation and control.

key_definitions.artificial_recharge_to_ground_water: The process by which Groundwater reservoir is augmented at a rate exceeding that under natural conditions of replenishment.
key_definitions.authority: The Karnataka Groundwater Authority established under section 3.
key_definitions.contravention: Defiance or violation of a rule, law or judicial order or a breach of a regulatory requirement or not fulfilling an obligation, promise or agreement.
key_definitions.digging_drilling: Includes digging, drilling or boring of new wells or in existing wells, deepening and modification of existing wells for extraction of groundwater.
key_definitions.drilling_agency: A person or an agency or an organization or an institution engaged in the business of drilling or digging of well for exploration of water resources or extraction of water.
key_definitions.defunct_well: Open wells or bore wells that are no longer yielding water or not in use.
key_definitions.failed_bore_wells: A bore well yielding less than one liter per second (or 791 GPH) at the time of installation.
key_definitions.groundwater: Water which exists below the ground surface in the zone of saturation and can be extracted through wells or any other means or emerges as springs and base flows in streams and rivers.
key_definitions.inferior_quality_work: Defects and faults occurred during the design stage that affect well maintenance.
key_definitions.local_authority: A City Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Town Panchayat, Zilla Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, Grama Panchayat, Industrial Township Authority, Bangalore Development Authority, Improvement Board, Urban Development Authority, Planning Authority, Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board, Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Sewerage Board, constituted under any law for the time being in force.
key_definitions.rain_water_harvesting: The technique of collection and use of rainwater at surface or in sub-surface aquifer.
key_definitions.registration: A certificate of registration granted under section 12 and section 13.
key_definitions.user_of_groundwater: Any person or group of persons or an institution including a company or an establishment, whether the Government or not who or which extract or use or sell groundwater for any purpose including domestic use made either on a personal or community basis.
key_definitions.well: A structure constructed for the search or extraction of groundwater by a person or persons for drinking/domestic/industrial/commercial/agriculture use except by the authorized officials of the State Government or the Central Government for carrying out scientific investigation, exploration, development, augmentation, conservation, protection or management of groundwater and shall include open well, bore well, dug cum bore well, tube well, filter point, collection well, infiltration gallery, recharge well, disposal well or any of their combinations or variations.
key_definitions.zone_of_saturation: A subsurface zone in which all the pores or the material are filled with ground water under phreatic condition.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent and commencement and application
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), commencement date (appointed by notification), and that its provisions are in addition to other laws relating to protection of public drinking water sources.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Artificial recharge to Ground Water, Authority, Contravention, Digging/drilling, Drilling Agency, Defunct well, Failed bore wells, Government, Groundwater, Inferior quality work, Local Authority, Notified area, Permit, Rain water harvesting, Registration, User of groundwater, Well, and Zone of saturation.

Establishes the Karnataka Groundwater Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered in Bangalore. It outlines the composition of the Authority, including ex-officio members and nominated representatives from various government departments, organizations, and farmers.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for the members of the authority
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a nominated non-official member of the Authority, including conviction for certain offences, unsound mind, insolvency, removal from service, or having a direct or indirect interest in contracts or employment with the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service
main_sections.description: Details the term of office for non-official members (three years, eligible for reappointment), their right to resign, and their entitlement to prescribed allowances.
Outlines the grounds for removal of a nominated non-official member by the Government, including becoming disqualified, refusing to act, continuous absence from meetings, or abusing their position.

Addresses the filling of casual vacancies by the Government through nomination and clarifies that vacancies or procedural defects do not invalidate the Authority's proceedings if they don't affect the merits of the case.

Specifies that the Authority shall meet at least once every three months, outlines rules for chairing meetings, representation by authorized persons, and decision-making by majority vote with a casting vote for the Chairperson in case of a tie. The quorum for a meeting is also mentioned.

main_sections.section_title: Power to notify areas to regulate and control the development and management of groundwater
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to notify specific areas for the regulation and control of groundwater development and management.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of permit to extract and use groundwater in the notified area
main_sections.description: Details the process for obtaining a permit to extract and use groundwater in areas notified under Section 10.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of existing users in the notified areas
main_sections.description: Mandates the registration of existing users of groundwater in notified areas.
Requires drilling agencies to register themselves.
Outlines the various powers vested in the Groundwater Authority, which would include the power to regulate, control, grant permits, and take other necessary actions for groundwater management.

main_sections.section_title: Rainwater harvesting for ground water recharge
main_sections.description: Deals with the promotion and implementation of rainwater harvesting for the purpose of groundwater recharge.
Specifies the actions that constitute offences under the Act and the corresponding penalties for such offences.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its own functioning.
Provides for the mechanism of appeals against orders passed under the Act.

important_rules: A permit is required to extract and use groundwater in notified areas (Section 11).
Existing users of groundwater in notified areas must register themselves (Section 12).
Drilling agencies must be registered (Section 13).
The Act aims to control indiscriminate exploitation of groundwater, especially in notified areas.
Rainwater harvesting is to be encouraged for groundwater recharge (Section 22).

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for offences committed under the Act (Section 32).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Groundwater Authority is established for the regulation and control of groundwater, implying it will be the primary enforcement body.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement likely involves monitoring, inspection, issuing permits and registrations, and taking action against contraventions as per the Act and prescribed rules/regulations. Recovery of dues can be made as arrears of land revenue (Section 25).

rights: Right to obtain a permit for groundwater extraction and use in notified areas (subject to conditions).
duties: Duty to register as an existing user of groundwater in notified areas (if applicable).
Duty for drilling agencies to register.
Duty of the public to provide information regarding contravention of the Act (Section 24).
Members and employees of the authority are public servants (Section 29).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, and regulations.
Obligation to obtain permits and registrations as required.
Obligation to participate in groundwater management and conservation efforts as mandated by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishing the Karnataka Groundwater Authority (Section 3).
Procedure for disqualification and removal of Authority members (Sections 4, 6).
Procedure for conducting meetings of the Authority (Section 8).
Procedure for notifying areas for groundwater regulation (Section 10).
Procedure for granting permits to extract and use groundwater (Section 11).
Procedure for registration of existing users and drilling agencies (Sections 12, 13).
Procedure for appealing against orders passed under the Act (Section 41).
administration: The Karnataka Groundwater Authority is the primary body established for the administration and management of groundwater. The Government also plays a role in establishing the Authority, making rules, and notifying areas.
important_notes: The Act commenced on 20.06.2011.
Different dates can be appointed for different areas and provisions.
The Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law for the time being in force relating to the protection of public sources of drinking water.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 30).
Civil Courts are barred from entertaining suits regarding matters under the Act (Section 35).

title: THE KARNATAKA GRAM SWARAJ AND PANCHAYAT RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, to provide for the constitution, functions, and powers of a Delimitation Commission for Panchayat Raj institutions, including the participation of experts, inviting public objections, and making consequential amendments. This amendment aims to address issues related to delimitation and reservation notifications challenging the arbitrariness and irrationality of previous processes.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, specifically concerning the delimitation of constituencies and reservations for Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2021, and it shall come into force at once.
This section amends section 5 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government' in various sub-sections.
This section amends section 121 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government'.
This section amends section 122 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government'.
This section amends section 123 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government'.
This section amends section 124 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government' and omitting specific words related to reserved constituencies.

This section amends section 161 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government based on the recommendation of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission'.
This section amends section 162 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government'.

This section amends section 163 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'State Election Commission' with 'Government on the recommendation of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission' and omitting specific words related to reserved constituencies.
This section amends section 308 of the Principal Act by omitting specific words related to the delimitation of territorial constituencies.
This section inserts new sections detailing the constitution, functions, powers, meetings, employees, directions, and protections of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission.
This section outlines transitory provisions, including the lapsing of existing delimitation and reservation notifications and the immediate steps for constituting the Delimitation Commission.

important_rules: The Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission shall be constituted by the State Government.

The Delimitation Commission shall perform functions including making recommendations for fixing the number of elected members, dividing areas into wards/constituencies, determining ward boundaries, ensuring equal population in wards, and making wards geographically compact areas.
The Delimitation Commission shall invite objections from the public and provide an opportunity for hearing before making recommendations.
The Delimitation Commission shall have the powers of a Civil Court in summoning witnesses, requiring document production, and requisitioning public records.
The Government may issue directions to the Delimitation Commission, which must be followed.
Proceedings of the Delimitation Commission shall not be invalidated by vacancies or absence of members.
No legal proceedings shall lie against the Government, Delimitation Commission, or its members/employees for actions taken in good faith.
The Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka and the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the constitution and functioning of the Delimitation Commission, the issuance of directions by the Government, and legal provisions for removing difficulties.

rights: Right of the public to be invited for objections and heard by the Delimitation Commission.
Protection of actions taken in good faith by the Government, Delimitation Commission, or its employees.
duties: Duty of the State Government to constitute the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission.
Duty of the Delimitation Commission to perform its functions as specified.
Duty of the Delimitation Commission to give effect to directions issued by the Government.
Duty of the State Government to take immediate steps to constitute the Delimitation Commission.
obligations: Obligation to amend the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, as per the provisions of this Act.
Obligation to adhere to the principles of population-based delimitation and geographical compactness for wards/constituencies.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission with specified members.
Performing functions of the Delimitation Commission including making recommendations on population, ward division, boundaries, and compactness.
Inviting public objections and providing an opportunity for hearing.
Exercising powers of a Civil Court for summoning witnesses, requiring documents, and requisitioning records.
Issuing directions by the Government to the Delimitation Commission.
Removing difficulties by issuing orders as required.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department.
important_notes: All previous delimitation and reservation notifications for Taluk Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats shall stand lapsed upon the commencement of this Act.

The Act is enacted based on the Supreme Court's decision in DravidaMunetraKazhagam (DMK) Vs Secretary, Governor’s Secretariat and others, emphasizing the need for research and proposals by a Delimitation Commission.
The headquarters of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Delimitation Commission is established in Bengaluru.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROTECTION OF RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF RELIGION ACT, 2022
purpose: To provide for the protection of the right to freedom of religion and to prohibit unlawful conversion from one religion to another through misrepresentation, force, undue influence, coercion, allurement, or any fraudulent means, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It governs acts of religious conversion and individuals involved in such conversions, including converters and those converted. It also applies to institutions facilitating conversions.

key_definitions.allurement: Offer of temptation in the form of gifts, gratification, easy money, material benefit, employment, free education, promise to marry, better lifestyle, divine displeasure, or portraying one religion detrimentally against another.
key_definitions.coercion: Compelling an individual against their will through psychological pressure or physical force causing bodily injury or threat thereof.
key_definitions.conversion: Renouncing one's own religion and adopting another religion.
key_definitions.force: Includes a show of force or a threat of injury to the person converted or sought to be converted, or to any other person or property.
key_definitions.fraudulent: Includes impersonation of any kind by false name, surname, religious symbol, or otherwise.
key_definitions.mass_conversion: Where two or more persons are converted.
key_definitions.minor: A person under eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.religion_convertor: A person of any religion who performs any act of conversion from one religion to another, regardless of their title (e.g., Father, Priest, Purohit, Pandit, Moulvi, Mulla).

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022, and states that it is deemed to have come into force with effect from May 17, 2022.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'Allurement', 'Coercion', 'Conversion', 'Force', 'Fraudulent', 'Institution', 'Mass Conversion', 'Minor', 'Original Religion', 'Religion', 'Religion Convertor', and 'Undue Influence'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of conversion from one religion to another religion by misrepresentation, force, fraud, undue influence, coercion, allurement or by promise of marriage
main_sections.description: Prohibits conversion or attempted conversion of any person from one religion to another through misrepresentation, force, undue influence, coercion, allurement, fraudulent means, or by promise of marriage. It also prohibits abetting or conspiring to such conversion. A proviso clarifies that reconversion to the immediate previous religion is not deemed a conversion under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for contravention of provisions of section 3
main_sections.description: Specifies the punishment for contravening Section 3. Standard punishment is imprisonment for three to five years and a fine of ₹25,000. Enhanced punishments apply for conversion of minors, persons of unsound mind, women, or persons belonging to Scheduled Castes/Tribes (three to ten years imprisonment and ₹50,000 fine), and for mass conversions (three to ten years imprisonment and ₹1 lakh fine). Repeat offenders face imprisonment of at least five years and a fine of ₹2 lakhs. Courts can also grant compensation up to ₹5 lakhs to the victim.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration before conversion of religion and pre-report about conversion
main_sections.description: Mandates a declaration in Form-I to be submitted to the District Magistrate at least thirty days before conversion. Religious converters must also give a thirty-day advance notice in Form-II. The District Magistrate will publish these notices for objections and conduct inquiries. Contravention of these provisions makes the conversion illegal and void, with penalties for both the person desiring conversion and the religious converter.

Requires the converted person to submit a declaration in Form-III to the District Magistrate within thirty days of conversion. This declaration includes personal details, religions involved, date and place of conversion, and process. The District Magistrate will publish this declaration for objections and may conduct inquiries. Failure to comply renders the conversion illegal and void. If no objections are received, the conversion is recorded, and concerned authorities are intimated for reclassification.

important_rules: No person shall convert or attempt to convert another person from one religion to another through misrepresentation, force, undue influence, coercion, allurement, fraudulent means, or promise of marriage. (Section 3)
Any marriage solely for unlawful conversion shall be declared null and void. (Section 6)
A person desiring to convert must declare their intention to the District Magistrate at least 30 days in advance. (Section 8(1))
A religious converter performing a conversion ceremony must give the District Magistrate 30 days' advance notice. (Section 8(2))
The converted person must submit a declaration post-conversion within 30 days and appear before the District Magistrate for identity confirmation. (Section 9(1), 9(4))

penalties: Contravention of Section 3: Imprisonment of 3-5 years and fine of ₹25,000.
Contravention of Section 3 (minor, person of unsound mind, woman, SC/ST): Imprisonment of 3-10 years and fine of ₹50,000.
Contravention of Section 3 (mass conversion): Imprisonment of 3-10 years and fine of ₹1 lakh.
