A person is disqualified from being or continuing as an Archak if they suffer from a virulent or contagious disease, are unable to recite Vedic mantras or Shlokas (unless not compulsory for the temple), or are involved in 'Sapta Vyasanas'.
Emoluments, pay, and allowances of Archaks and temple servants must be fair and reasonable, considering the income, usage, custom, and tradition of the institution.

Notified institutions are required to make contributions to the Rajya Dharmika Parishat based on their net annual income (10% for income exceeding ten lakhs, 5% for income exceeding five lakhs but not exceeding ten lakhs).
Members nominated to the Rajya Dharmika Parishat by the Government (except a retired district judge) hold office subject to the pleasure of the Government.
Members nominated to the Rajya Dharmika Parishat must have contributed to the Hindu Religious field and cannot be office bearers of any political party.

rights: Protection of hereditary rights of trustees.
Continuation of management of temples by hereditary trustees.
Protection of hereditary right of Archaks and temple servants, allowing legal heirs to continue in service.

administration: The administration of this Act falls under the purview of the Department/Ministry responsible for Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments in Karnataka. The Rajya Dharmika Parishat and Zilla Dharmika Parishats are established for administration and dispute settlement.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments Act, 1997.

The High Court of Karnataka had previously struck down the Karnataka Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments Act, 1997, but the Supreme Court of India stayed its operation, allowing enforcement except for section 25.
The Act introduces the concept of 'Composite Institution' for places of worship of Hindus and other religions jointly worshipped.
Provisions are made for the registration of private temples.
Prohibition of sharing in temple hundis and other income by temple servants.
Prohibition of collecting funds from the public in the name of temples by private individuals or organizations.
Establishment of a State Level Architectural Committee for development works in temples.
Establishment of a survey wing for temple land and site property to avoid encroachment.
The Rajya Dharmika Parishat and Zilla Dharmika Parishats are constituted with specific powers for administering temples and settling disputes.

title: THE KARNATAKA GRAM SWARAJ AND PANCHAYAT RAJ (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, specifically to revise the total number of elected members of the Zilla Panchayat in districts based on rural population and to comply with a High Court direction regarding election timelines for rural local bodies.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, and therefore applies to the rural local governance structure within the state of Karnataka, specifically concerning Zilla Panchayats and their elected members.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Second Amendment) Act, 2022, and specifies its deemed commencement date as August 22, 2022.
Amends Section 121 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'two lakhs' with 'two lakh thirty thousand' in clauses (i) and (ii).

Amends Section 160 of the principal Act by substituting 'not less than twenty persons' with 'not less than twenty five members' and inserting a further proviso regarding the number of elected members for districts with a specific rural population range.

Repeals the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022 (Karnataka Ordinance 06 of 2022) and provides for the continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance as if they were taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The number of elected members in Zilla Panchayats for districts with a rural population of more than seven lakhs but not more than nine lakhs fifty thousand shall be twenty-eight.
Rule 2: For other clauses of section 121, the population threshold for elected members is now 'two lakh thirty thousand' instead of 'two lakhs'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, and the Election Commission for conducting elections.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and subsequent implementation by the relevant authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of Section 121 of the principal Act to revise population thresholds related to elected members.
Procedure 2: Amendment of Section 160 of the principal Act to modify the minimum number of elected members and to introduce a specific provision for districts based on rural population.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from the 22nd day of August, 2022.
The amendment addresses the direction of the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No: 20426/2021 to conduct elections to rural local bodies within the time limit.
The Act replaces the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, for certain purposes.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It specifically relates to municipal properties, building constructions, and associated taxation within the state.

main_sections.description: States the short title as 'The Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 2001' and specifies the commencement date as the date of assent by the Governor of India.
Amends Section 2 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 142
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for Section 142 of the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964.

main_sections.section_title: Taxation of buildings or lands or both, etc.
main_sections.description: Deals with the taxation of buildings or lands or both, and the procedure for assessment and levy of property tax.

important_rules: Rule 1: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to simplify the procedure for assessment of property tax and to provide for the following, namely:-

Rule 2: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to introduce a system of assessment of property tax based on the estimated market value of the land and estimated cost of erection of the building.

Rule 3: To levy property tax at such percentage of the Capital Value fixed by the Municipalities with reference to location, type of construction of the building, area of the land and age of the building.

Rule 4: To levy property tax at such percentage of the Capital Value fixed by the Municipalities with reference to location, type of construction of the building, area of the land and age of the building.

Rule 5: To levy property tax at such percentage of the Capital Value fixed by the Municipalities with reference to location, type of construction of the building, area of the land and age of the building.
Rule 6: To impose a penalty at the rate of fifty percent of the tax in cases of failure to submit returns.
Rule 7: To collect service charges in respect of properties exempt from property tax.
Rule 8: To collect penalty equal to twice the property tax leviable in respect of unlawful buildings without prejudice to any proceedings or action to be taken.
Rule 9: To publish property tax register for public information.
Rule 10: To undertake survey of lands and buildings and preparation of property register.

penalties: Penalty of fifty percent of the tax in cases of failure to submit returns.
Penalty equal to twice the property tax leviable in respect of unlawful buildings without prejudice to any proceedings or action to be taken.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Karnataka State Government/Municipalities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and levy of property tax, imposition of penalties, and undertaking surveys of properties.

duties: Duty to submit returns.
Duty to pay property tax.
Duty to facilitate survey of lands and buildings and preparation of property register.
obligations: Obligation to pay property tax at rates determined by the Municipalities.
Obligation to adhere to building bylaws.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Assessment of property tax based on Capital Value (estimated market value of land + estimated cost of erection of building).
Procedure 2: Levy of property tax at a percentage of the Capital Value, considering location, type of construction, area, and age of the building.
Procedure 3: Publication of property tax register for public information.
Procedure 4: Undertaking survey of lands and buildings and preparation of property registers.
Procedure 5: Collection of service charges for properties exempt from property tax.
Procedure 6: Imposition of penalties for non-compliance, including failure to submit returns and unlawful constructions.
administration: Municipalities in Karnataka
important_notes: The amendment is effective from the date of assent by the Governor of India.
The Act aims to establish a more equitable and efficient property tax system.
Specific percentages for Capital Value and other details are to be determined by the Municipalities.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, to give effect to the proposals made in the Budget Speech 2004-05, primarily by revising the lifetime tax rates for certain categories of motor vehicles.
scope: This Act applies to motor vehicles registered in the State of Karnataka. Specifically, it amends the taxation rules for Motor Cars, Jeeps, Omni Buses, and Private Service Vehicles, by introducing new lifetime tax rates based on the cost of the vehicle and its age. The scope also includes provisions for vehicles registered prior to specific dates and those migrated to Karnataka.

key_definitions.Motor Cars, Jeeps, Omni Buses and Privat: These are the classes of vehicles to which the amended taxation rules apply. The tax structure is further differentiated based on the floor area and cost of these vehicles.
key_definitions.Lifetime Tax: A tax levied once on a vehicle for its entire life, as opposed to periodic taxes.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Second Amendment) Act, 2004, and specifies that it comes into force with effect from the first day of August, 2004.

This section details the amendments made to the Schedule of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It substitutes Part A5, which outlines the Lifetime Tax for Motor Cars, Jeeps, Omni Buses, and Private Service Vehicles. The amendment introduces revised tax percentages based on the cost of the vehicle (up to Rs. 5 Lakhs, between Rs. 5 Lakhs and Rs. 10 Lakhs, and exceeding Rs. 10 Lakhs) and also provides a structure for calculating the tax based on the age of vehicles for which lifetime tax was levied previously.

This section empowers the State Government to issue notifications to remove any difficulties encountered in giving effect to the provisions of this amending Act. Such orders must be made within two years from the date of commencement of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: For vehicles where lifetime tax was due before April 1, 2003, and not paid, the tax shall be collected at the rates applicable before that date, along with any applicable penalty.

Rule 2: For Motor Cars, Omni Buses, and Private service vehicles (with floor area up to 5 Sq.mtrs) registered in other States before April 1, 2003, and migrated to Karnataka after that date, tax shall be levied as per Part-A5 of the Act as it existed prior to April 1, 2003.
Rule 3: A purchase invoice must be produced for vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2003, for the purpose of levying tax under this part.
Rule 4: The rates specified in this part do not apply to vehicles owned by Central Government employees or defense personnel.

penalties: Applicable penalty for unpaid tax due prior to April 1, 2003, shall be collected along with the tax.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Karnataka, likely through its transport and taxation departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, as amended by this Act, which includes collection of taxes and penalties at the time of registration or as per the revised schedules. Section 3 also provides a mechanism for the State Government to issue orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to have tax levied according to the specified rates based on vehicle class, cost, and age.
Right to have difficulties in implementation addressed by the State Government.
duties: Duty to pay the specified lifetime tax on motor vehicles.
Duty to produce purchase invoices for vehicles registered on or after April 1, 2003.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the revised taxation structure for specified motor vehicles.
Obligation to pay taxes and penalties as prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure for calculating Lifetime Tax: At the time of registration, tax is calculated as a percentage of the vehicle's cost (9%, 10%, or 12% depending on cost thresholds). If the vehicle is already registered, the tax is a percentage of the initially levied lifetime tax, decreasing with the age of the vehicle.

Procedure for removing difficulties: The State Government can issue notifications to address any issues in implementing the Act, provided such orders are made within two years of the Act's commencement.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for drafting and enactment), and likely the Transport Department or Commercial Taxes Department for collection and administration of taxes.
important_notes: The Act came into force on August 1, 2004.
Specific provisions are made for vehicles registered or migrated before April 1, 2003, and for those registered on or after April 1, 2003.
Exemption is provided for vehicles owned by Central Government employees or defense personnel.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to a two-year period from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To avoid undue hardship to the owners of shops and commercial establishments in registering their establishments and renewing their registration certificates by providing for deemed registration or renewal of registration certificates if the Labour Inspector fails to act within thirty days.
scope: This act applies to shops and commercial establishments in Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the act as the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2005, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.
Details the amendments made to Section 4 of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961, introducing sub-sections (3A), (6), (7), and (8).

important_rules: Deemed Registration: If the Inspector does not communicate a decision for refusing to register an establishment within thirty days of receiving the application and fees, the establishment is deemed to have been registered.

Deemed Renewal: If the Inspector does not communicate a decision for refusing to renew a registration certificate within thirty days of receiving the renewal application and fees, the registration certificate is deemed to have been renewed.

Display of Self-Certification: If the registration or renewal certificate is not received within the specified period, the employer must display a self-certification statement sent by Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due, along with the acknowledgement.
Replacement of Self-Certification: Upon receiving the regular certificate of registration or renewal, the self-certification must be replaced.

penalties: Imprisonment of not less than six months and a fine up to five thousand rupees for falsely claiming the benefit of deemed registration and displaying a self-certificate.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspector (Labour Inspector)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Inspector's review of applications for registration and renewal, and potential prosecution for false claims of deemed registration.

rights: Right to deemed registration if the Inspector fails to act within 30 days.
Right to deemed renewal of registration if the Inspector fails to act within 30 days.
duties: Duty to apply for registration and renewal of registration certificates.
Duty to pay prescribed fees.
Duty to display a self-certification if the certificate is not received within the specified period.
Duty to replace self-certification with a regular certificate upon receipt.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the amended Act, including the penalties for false claims.

key_procedures: Application for Registration/Renewal: Employer submits application with fees to the Inspector.
Inspector's Review: Inspector decides on registration/renewal within 30 days.
Communication of Refusal: If refused, Inspector must communicate decision with reasons within 30 days.
Deemed Registration/Renewal: If no communication of refusal within 30 days, registration/renewal is deemed granted.
Self-Certification and Display: If certificate not received, employer displays self-certification.
Issuance of Regular Certificate: Inspector issues regular certificate upon approval.
Replacement of Self-Certification: Employer replaces self-certification with regular certificate.
administration: State Government (through the Labour Department and its Inspectors)
important_notes: The act further amends the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.
The provisions for deemed registration and renewal are intended to alleviate hardship.
False claims of deemed registration are subject to significant penalties.

title: THE KARNATAKA ADVOCATES’ WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Advocates’ Welfare Fund Act, 1983, to enhance retirement benefits for Advocates, provide for medical relief, and introduce other amendments.
scope: This Act applies to advocates enrolled on the roll of the Karnataka State Bar Council and persons holding pleadership certificates within the State of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Advocates’ Welfare Fund Act, 1983.

key_definitions.permanent_disability: Disability incurred by an advocate after becoming a member which renders him totally incapable of practicing as an advocate, certified by the District Surgeon of the District where the advocate is practicing.
key_definitions.schedule: Means the schedule appended to this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification, with different dates for different provisions.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting definitions for 'voluntary retirement' and 'permanent disability', and inserting a definition for 'schedule'.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting 'three years' for 'four years' in sub-sections (4) and (5).
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by substituting 'in accordance with this Act' for 'in accordance with section 16' in sub-section (2), clause (e).
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting specific requirements for association rules or bye-laws.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act concerning membership, admission fees, and annual fees. It includes provisions for members who have completed fifteen years of practice and those enrolled before forty years of age. It also clarifies consequences of non-payment of fees and allows lump sum payment for senior practitioners. It also introduces a proviso for deemed suspension for five years or more.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act concerning entitlement to receive amounts from the fund. It redefines entitlements based on cessation of practice (death or other reasons), introduces specific rates for certain categories of members, and details calculations for completed years of practice. It also includes provisions for exclusion of suspension periods due to misconduct and a special calculation for advocates enrolled before April 2, 1997. It also adds a sub-section regarding recovery of excess payments due to false claims.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 16 A and 16 B
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 16A and 16B. Section 16A provides for medical relief for serious ailments, specifying conditions, limits, and recovery mechanisms. Section 16B allows for part payment from the fund during financial hardship for members who have attained seventy years of age and completed specified years of practice and membership.
Omit section 26A of the principal Act.
Inserts a new schedule at the end of the principal Act, outlining the entitlement amounts from the fund based on completed years of practice.

Deals with pending claims for amounts from the fund made between June 1, 2005, and the commencement of this Amendment Act, where the member had defaulted in fee payment. It specifies a deduction rate for such defaults.

important_rules: Rule regarding voluntary retirement: An advocate can voluntarily retire upon attaining an age of seventy-five years or after completing fifty years of practice, whichever is earlier.
Rule for permanent disability: Permanent disability means an advocate becoming totally incapable of practicing, certified by the District Surgeon.
Annual fee payment: Members must pay an annual fee by December 31st. Failure to do so can result in deemed voluntary suspension of practice.
Lump sum payment option: Members who have completed fifteen years of practice can pay a lump sum of fifteen thousand rupees annually.

Medical relief conditions: Medical relief is available for prescribed serious ailments, limited to one lakh rupees or fifty percent of the amount under section 16, whichever is less. The member must have completed five years of practice, and the benefit is available only once in a lifetime.

Financial hardship part payment: Members aged seventy and above with twenty years of practice and twelve years of membership facing financial hardship may apply for a part payment up to fifty percent of their entitlement or one lakh rupees, whichever is less.

penalties: Non-payment of annual fees: Deemed voluntary suspension of practice, with a provision for delayed payment with a penalty of fifty rupees per month.
False or incorrect claims for fund amounts: The trustee committee may direct the refund of excess amounts paid, recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.
False statements or particulars for medical relief: The member may be required to refund the entire amount received with interest at twelve percent per annum, recoverable if not paid.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Trustee committee, Karnataka State Bar Council, and recovery as arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through claims processing, inquiries, directing refunds, and recovery as arrears of land revenue.

rights: Right to receive amounts from the fund upon cessation of practice (death or other reasons).
Right to receive medical relief for prescribed serious ailments.
Right to apply for part payment from the fund during financial hardship.
Nominees, dependents, or heirs have the right to receive benefits in case of the member's death.
duties: Duty to become a member of the fund.
Duty to pay admission fees and annual fees as prescribed.
Duty to provide truthful statements and particulars when applying for benefits.
obligations: Obligation to pay annual fees by the due date to avoid deemed suspension of practice.
Obligation to refund excess amounts paid due to false claims or statements.
Obligation to deduct amounts received from other schemes when claiming medical relief.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for medical relief: Member applies with prescribed documents for treatment of a serious ailment within three months of hospitalization (extendable). The trustee committee makes a decision after inquiry.

Procedure for applying for part payment during financial hardship: Member aged seventy and above with specified practice/membership years applies to the trustee committee, which may sanction payment with Bar Council approval.
Procedure for recovery of excess payments: If a claim is found false or incorrect, the trustee committee may direct refund after inquiry and hearing, with recovery as arrears of land revenue.
administration: The administration of the Act and the fund is overseen by the Trustee Committee and the Karnataka State Bar Council.
important_notes: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.
The amount payable for medical relief is subject to a maximum limit and a condition that it is available only once in a lifetime.

The number of applications considered for medical relief and financial hardship payments in a financial year is subject to determination by the trustee committee based on financial position and other factors.

title: THE KARNATAKA RENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Rent Act, 1999, to provide tenancy rights to a deserted wife of a tenant in occupation of the matrimonial home or tenanted premises, and to a divorced wife of a tenant who has a decree of divorce incorporating the right of residence.
scope: Applies to the Karnataka Rent Act, 1999, specifically amending Section 3 concerning tenancy rights. The geographical scope is Karnataka.

key_definitions.deserted wife: A deserted wife of a tenant who has been or is entitled to be in occupation of the matrimonial home or tenanted premises of her husband.
key_definitions.divorced wife: A divorced wife of a tenant who has a decree of divorce in which the right of residence in the matrimonial home or tenanted premises has been incorporated as one of the conditions of the decree.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Rent (Amendment) Act, 2008, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 3 of the Karnataka Rent Act, 1999, by inserting provisions for deserted and divorced wives of a tenant to be considered as tenants.

important_rules: A deserted wife of a tenant is granted tenancy rights if she is in or entitled to be in occupation of the matrimonial home or tenanted premises of her husband.
A divorced wife of a tenant is granted tenancy rights if her decree of divorce incorporates the right of residence in the matrimonial home or tenanted premises.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but generally would be the authorities responsible for enforcing rent control laws in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

rights: Tenancy right for a deserted wife of a tenant.
Tenancy right for a divorced wife of a tenant with a decree of divorce including right of residence.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The amendment is in view of observations of the Supreme Court in B.P. Achala Anand Vs.S. Appi Reddy and another.
The Act was first published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on the twenty-second day of June 2011.
The Act received the assent of the President on the tenth day of June, 2011.

title: THE KARNATAKA REGULATION OF STONE CRUSHERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Regulation of Stone Crushers Act, 2011, to provide clarity, facilitate transfer of licenses, extend license validity, and introduce provisions for compounding of offences.
scope: This Act applies to stone crushers within the state of Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka Regulation of Stone Crushers Act, 2011.

key_definitions.other_road: All roads excluding foot or cart roads, and roads approaching stone crushers.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date as March 30, 2020.
Inserts the definition of 'other road' into the principal Act.
Omitted sub-sections (2), (3), (4), (5), (6), and (7) of section 3 of the principal Act.
Inserts a proviso to section 4(1) allowing late applications for license renewal under certain conditions and with additional fees.
Inserts new sections allowing for the transfer of crusher licenses under specific conditions and outlining the status of a crusher license upon the death of the licensee.

Substitutes section 5 to extend the validity of crusher licenses to twenty years and provides for deemed extension of existing licenses, including those pending consideration or rejected for late renewal, subject to fees and penalties.

Amends section 6 to modify distance requirements from certain areas and adds an explanation that subsequent development of habitations, schools, temples, or roads will not affect the operation or continuance of a declared safer zone or license extension.
Inserts a provision for licensees to pay an annual regulation fee.
Substitutes section 16 to revise penalties for contravening provisions of section 3 and license conditions, including imprisonment and fines.
Substitutes 'Licensing Authority' with 'State Government' in section 17(1).
Inserts a new section allowing for the compounding of offences punishable under section 16(1A) by designated officers.
Repeals the Regulation of Stone Crushers (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020, and states that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the amended Act.

important_rules: License transfer requires a non-refundable application fee of ₹25,000, affidavits from the transferee regarding adherence to terms and tax compliance, and proof of consent from the landowner.
Transfers are subject to a survey demarcation by a Deputy Director or Senior Geologist at the licensee's expense.
Existing crusher licenses are deemed extended for twenty years from their original grant date upon payment of annual regulation fees.
Licensees must pay an annual regulation fee from the commencement date of the Amendment Act.
Contravention of section 3 provisions can lead to imprisonment up to two years, a fine of up to ₹2 lakh, or both, with additional daily fines for continuing contravention.
Contravention of license conditions can lead to imprisonment up to one year, a fine of ₹25,000, or both, with additional daily fines for continuing contravention.

penalties: Contravention of section 3: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to ₹2 lakh, or both. Continuing contravention: additional fine up to ₹5,000 per day.
Contravention of license conditions: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine of ₹25,000, or both. Continuing contravention: additional fine up to ₹500 per day.
Late renewal application submission (rejected solely on this ground but applied before expiry): Penalty of ₹2 lakh.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Authority, Deputy Director or Senior Geologist of the concerned District (for compounding offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prosecution for contraventions, compounding of offences upon payment of specified amounts.

rights: Right to apply for transfer of license.
Legal representatives are eligible for transfer of license upon the licensee's death, subject to prescribed conditions.
Right to have existing licenses deemed extended for twenty years.
Right to have renewal applications pending consideration or rejected solely for late filing but submitted before expiry, considered for extension.
duties: Licensees must adhere to all terms, conditions, and liabilities of the license.
Licensees must pay annual regulation fees.
Licensees must pay all dues payable to the State Government up to the date of application for transfer.
obligations: The transferee must abide by all terms, conditions, and liabilities of the license.
The transferee must have filed up-to-date income tax returns and paid assessed taxes.
The transferee must furnish proof of consent from the land owner or lease extension if applicable.

key_procedures: Procedure for Transfer of Crusher License: Application to Licensing Authority with fee, affidavits (transferee obligations, tax compliance), proof of land owner consent/lease, and payment of all dues. Requires survey demarcation at applicant's expense. A deed must be executed within six months.

Procedure for Compounding of Offences: Any offence under section 16(1A) can be compounded by the Deputy Director or Senior Geologist or designated officer upon payment of an amount not exceeding the specified penalty.
administration: Department of Mines and Geology (implied through the role of Senior Geologist).
important_notes: Habitations, schools, temples, or roads developing after a safer zone is declared will not affect the operation of stone crushers in that zone or the extension of their licenses.
Late renewal applications submitted before expiry but rejected solely for not filing three months prior to expiry can be renewed subject to a penalty of ₹2 lakh.

title: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (Amendment) Act, 2022
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, to change the nomenclature of the Board to Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board in line with the New Education Policy 2020, to conduct Pre-University Examinations in addition to SSLC and other public examinations, and to re-designate the post of Director Mass Education as Chairman of the Board.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966. It applies to the Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (formerly Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board) and covers matters related to secondary and pre-university examinations within Karnataka.

key_definitions.Director (Exams): Director for SSLC and other examinations.
key_definitions.Principal: Principal of Government Pre-university colleges and Composite Pre-university Colleges or Principal of recognised Pre-university Colleges.
key_definitions.Higher Secondary School: Government Pre-university colleges and Composite Pre-university Colleges including any recognised Pre-university Colleges.
key_definitions.Vice-chairman-1: Vice-chairman for SSLC and other examinations.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (Amendment) Act, 2022' and states that it comes into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of title and long title
main_sections.description: Amends the title and long title of the principal Act by substituting 'Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board' with 'Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board'.
Amends section 1 of the principal Act by substituting 'Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board' with 'Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board'.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act, making changes to definitions including the Board's name, 'Director', and introducing definitions for 'Principal' and 'Higher Secondary School'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act to reflect the change in the Board's name to 'Board of School Examination and Assessment'.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act concerning the appointment of the Chairman, the roles of special invitees, Directors, and the composition of the Board's members (ex-officio, elected, and nominated).
Amends section 15 of the principal Act by adding 'Pre-university examinations' and 'Diploma in Pre-School Education' to the functions of the Board.
Amends section 17 of the principal Act by inserting the word 'respective' in subsection (2) and adding 'as directed by the Chairman' in subsection (6).
Amends section 18 of the principal Act concerning the Board's Secretaries and the role of Directors in maintaining question paper confidentiality.
Amends section 24 of the principal Act by inserting a new subsection (3) allowing the Board to conduct internal audits of its accounts through a registered chartered accountant.
Omit section 29 of the principal Act.

important_rules: The Board's name is changed to Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board.
The Board will now conduct Pre-University Examinations in addition to SSLC and other public examinations.
The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed by the Government in the cadre of IAS (Selection Grade or Junior Administrative Grade).
The Commissioner for Public Instruction Department and Director, Pre-University Education Department shall be special invitees of the Board.
The Board shall have two Secretaries, one from the Department of Public Instruction and one from Pre-University Education, both not below the rank of Joint Director.
The preparation, distribution, and confidentiality of question papers is the prerogative of the Directors (Secretary) of the concerned examination and no authority shall interfere in this matter.
The Board may conduct internal audits of its accounts through a registered chartered accountant.

rights: The Board has the right to conduct examinations, including SSLC, Pre-University, and other public examinations.
The Board has the right to conduct internal audits of its accounts.
Directors (Secretary) have the prerogative over question paper preparation, distribution, and confidentiality.
duties: The Board has the duty to conduct examinations efficiently and confidentially.
The Board has the duty to maintain the confidentiality of question papers.
The Board has the duty to manage its accounts and may conduct audits.
obligations: The Board must comply with the provisions of the amended Act.
The Board must ensure that the functions are carried out in accordance with the New Education Policy 2020.
The Board must appoint Directors and Secretaries as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Appointment of Chairman: The Government shall appoint the Chairman of the Board in the cadre of IAS (Selection Grade or Junior Administrative Grade).

Appointment of Directors: Director-1 (Department of Public Instruction) and Director-2 (Pre-university Education) shall be appointed by the State Government, not below the rank of Joint Director, and shall hold office during the pleasure of the State Government.
Internal Audit: The Board may cause to conduct internal audit of its accounts through a registered chartered accountant and pay the required fee.
Question Paper Management: The preparation, distribution, and maintenance of confidentiality of question papers are the responsibility of the Directors (Secretary) of the concerned examination.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act), and the Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (for the functions of the Board).
important_notes: The amendment is in accordance with the New Education Policy 2020.
The Board now has expanded responsibilities to include Pre-University Examinations.
The amendment aims to streamline the governance and functions of the examination board.

title: THE KARNATAKA SPECIAL TAX ON ENTRY OF CERTAIN GOODS ACT, 2004
purpose: To provide for the levy of a special tax on the entry of certain goods into local areas within the State of Karnataka for consumption, use, or sale therein.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the entry of 'notified goods' into 'local areas' for consumption, use, or sale therein. The definition of 'person' includes various entities, and 'goods vehicle' is defined by reference to the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.

key_definitions.assessee: A person by whom tax is payable.
key_definitions.assessing authority: In the case of an importer who is a dealer, the authority specified under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act. For other importers, it's the officer-in-charge of the check post, or the officer intercepting goods vehicles, or the Assistant Commissioner of Commercial Tax with jurisdiction over the importer's residence.
key_definitions.dealer: A dealer as defined under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
key_definitions.entry of goods into a local area: Entry of notified goods into a local area from outside the State for consumption, use, or sale therein.
key_definitions.goods vehicle: A goods vehicle as defined in the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
key_definitions.importer: A person who brings or causes to be brought any notified goods into a local area from outside the State for consumption, use, or sale therein, or who owns the notified goods at the time of entry.
key_definitions.karnataka sales tax act: The Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act No.25 of 1957).
key_definitions.local area: An area within the limits of a local authority.
key_definitions.notified goods: Goods notified by the Government from time to time for the purpose of this Act.
key_definitions.person: Includes any company, association, body of individuals, firm, local authority, Hindu Undivided Family, society, club, individual, or the government of any other state or Union Territory.
key_definitions.value of the notified goods: The purchase value of the notified goods, including accessories, insurance, duties, taxes, transport fees, freight, and other incidental charges. If not ascertainable, it's the open market value of like goods.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the commencement date (to be appointed by the Government by notification).

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as Assessee, Assessing authority, Dealer, Entry of goods into a local area, Goods vehicle, Government, Importer, Karnataka Sales Tax Act, Local area, Notified Goods, Person, State, Tax, and Value of the notified goods. It also states that undefined terms take meaning from the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.

Establishes the levy and collection of tax on the entry of notified goods into a local area for consumption, use, or sale therein. The tax is levied on the value of the notified goods at the rate specified under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act and is payable by the importer.

Provides for the reduction of tax liability. For dealers, the liability under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act is reduced by the tax paid under this Act. For non-dealers using goods for their own consumption, the liability under this Act is reduced by any tax paid under General Sales Tax or Central Sales Tax laws of the originating state/union territory.

Grants the State Government the power to exempt, by notification, any specified class of importers or any class of notified goods from tax payment if it is in the public interest. Exemptions may be subject to restrictions and conditions, and can be cancelled or varied.

main_sections.section_title: Tax authorities, returns, assessments, payments, recovery, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act to assess, reassess, collect, and enforce payment of tax, interest, and penalty under this Act. It states that all provisions of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, including those related to returns, assessment, recovery, appeals, and offences (excluding specific sections on offences), apply accordingly. For importers who are not dealers, assessment and collection procedures will be as prescribed.

Places the burden of proof on the importer to show that notified goods brought into a local area are not liable to tax. It also specifies penalties for submitting false documents to support a claim of non-liability: three times the tax for the first detection and five times for subsequent detections.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to Government officers and servants for actions taken in good faith in the execution of their duties under the Act. No suit, prosecution, or other proceedings can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Government and must be filed within six months of the action complained of.

main_sections.section_title: Courts not to set aside or modify assessment, except, as provided in this Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits courts from setting aside or modifying any assessment made under this Act, except as expressly provided within the Act itself.

Outlines offences and penalties. Failing to pay tax or penalty, or wilfully contravening the Act/rules, is punishable with a fine up to two thousand rupees. Willfully submitting untrue returns, failing to submit returns, or fraudulently evading tax is punishable with a fine up to two thousand rupees for a first offense, and imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both for subsequent offenses. Making false statements or declarations carries imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees or both. Fraudulent evasion or abetment of evasion carries imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees or both.

States that if an offence is committed by a company, every person in charge of and responsible for the company's business will be liable, along with the company. However, such persons are not liable if they prove the offence was committed without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence. It also states that if an offence is committed with the consent or connivance of, or due to neglect by, a director, manager, secretary, or other officer, such officer shall also be liable.

important_rules: Tax is levied and collected on the entry of 'notified goods' into a 'local area' for consumption, use, or sale therein.
The tax is calculated on the 'value of the notified goods' at rates specified under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
The tax is payable by the 'importer'.
The liability under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act is reduced by the tax paid under this Act for dealers.
For non-dealers, tax liability under this Act can be reduced by taxes paid under similar laws in the originating state/union territory.
The State Government can exempt certain importers or goods from tax in the public interest.
Authorities under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act are empowered to administer this Act.
The burden of proof for non-liability to tax rests with the importer.
Penalties apply for submitting false documents to avoid tax.
Specific penalties are prescribed for various offences including non-payment, evasion, and false declarations.
Companies can be held liable for offences, with provisions for individual accountability of officers.

penalties: Failure to pay tax/penalty or wilful contravention: fine up to ₹2,000.

Wilfully submitting untrue returns, failure to submit returns, fraudulent tax evasion: first offence fine up to ₹2,000; second/subsequent offence imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹5,000 or both.
Making false statements/declarations: imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹2,000 or both.
Fraudulent evasion or abetment of evasion: imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to ₹2,000 or both.
Penalty for submitting false documents to support non-liability claim: three times the tax for the first detection, five times for subsequent detections.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorities empowered under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, reassessment, collection, and enforcement of tax, interest, and penalties, utilizing the powers and provisions of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act. This includes procedures for returns, provisional assessment, advance payment, recovery, appeals, and inspections.

rights: Right to an opportunity of being heard before penalty is imposed for submitting false documents (Section 7(2)).
Protection from legal proceedings for officers acting in good faith (Section 8).
duties: Duty to pay tax on the entry of notified goods into a local area (Section 3).
Duty to submit returns as required by the Act and rules (Section 10(2)(a)).
Duty not to submit untrue returns or fraudulently evade tax (Section 10(2)(b)).
Duty not to make false statements or declarations (Section 10(3)).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
obligations: Importers have an obligation to pay the specified tax.
Importers have an obligation to prove their non-liability to tax if challenged.
Persons are obligated to provide true and accurate information in returns and documents.
Companies and their responsible officers have an obligation to ensure compliance and prevent offences.

key_procedures: Assessment, reassessment, collection, and enforcement of tax, interest, and penalty by designated authorities, largely mirroring procedures under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
Submission of returns and payment of tax as prescribed.
Procedures for appeals, reviews, and revisions as provided under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act.
Procedures for recovery of tax, including from third parties.
Procedures for inspection of premises, goods vehicles, and seizure of documents or unaccounted goods.
Procedures for compounding of offences (as per Chapter IV).
administration: The Karnataka Sales Tax Act authorities are designated to administer this Act, with specific procedures for non-dealers to be prescribed.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to supplement revenue for the State Government and to address situations not covered by the Karnataka Entry Tax Act, 1979, by levying tax on goods brought in by persons other than dealers.
The Act came into force on 20th September 2004.
The definition of 'value of the notified goods' is comprehensive and aims to capture the full cost of goods upon entry.
The Act extensively leverages the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, for its procedural framework, making it crucial to refer to that Act for detailed operational aspects.

title: THE KARNATAKA IRRIGATION AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965 and the Karnataka Irrigation (Levy of Betterment Contribution and Water Rate) Act, 1957. Specifically, to provide for supply of water in bulk on a volumetric basis by the Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited to Water Users Co-operative Societies and to enable the Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Ltd. to levy and collect water rates for water supplied or made available from an irrigation network.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends two existing acts related to irrigation, water supply, and water rates within the state.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Irrigation and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2010, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends Section 62(A) and Section 62AA of the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965, by inserting provisions to include 'Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited or any other body or Corporation established by the State Government for this purpose' alongside existing mentions of 'Karnataka Neeravari Nigam'.

Amends Section 10, sub-section (1), in the proviso of the Karnataka Irrigation (Levy of Betterment Contribution and Water Rate) Act, 1957, by inserting 'Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited or any other body or Corporation established by the State Government for this purpose' after 'Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited'.

important_rules: Rule 1: Water supply in bulk on a volumetric basis by Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited to Water Users Co-operative Societies is to be provided.
Rule 2: Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Ltd. is empowered to levy and collect water rates for water supplied or made available from an irrigation network.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The act itself does not specify an enforcement authority; however, the amendments are to existing acts which likely have their own enforcement mechanisms. The Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited is empowered to levy and collect water rates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms provided by the amended Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965, and the Karnataka Irrigation (Levy of Betterment Contribution and Water Rate) Act, 1957.

rights: Right of Water Users Co-operative Societies to receive water in bulk on a volumetric basis.
Right of Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited to levy and collect water rates.
duties: Duty of Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited to supply water in bulk on a volumetric basis.

administration: The administration of the amended sections would fall under the purview of the relevant departments overseeing irrigation and water resources in Karnataka, specifically related to the functions of the Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited and the implementation of the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965 and the Karnataka Irrigation (Levy of Betterment Contribution and Water Rate) Act, 1957.
important_notes: The amendments aim to modernize water supply mechanisms and revenue collection for irrigation purposes.
The act is based on Entry 17 and 18 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAX ON LUXURIES ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of a tax on luxuries in the State of Karnataka.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with luxury taxes on various goods and services.

main_sections.description: Concerns the short title and commencement of the act.
Details the amendment of section 2 of the act.
Concerns the substitution of section 4B.
Details the insertion of a new section 17A.
Covers the repeal and savings provisions of the act.

important_rules: Levy of tax on goods: Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1997.  However, by an amendment to the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 2001, the rate of tax on goods not specified under the Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1997 was made applicable to the State. As the rate of the aforesaid cases is also applicable to the State, it is not possible to continue to levy tax.
The Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 2001 was promulgated.
This Bill seeks to replace the said Ordinance.

Section 17A (Special Important): Act, 1955 on tobacco (and also on tobacco products). The Additional Duty of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957 is on tobacco (and also on tobacco products).

The levy of sales tax on gutkha would entail an increase of rupee thirty-three crore per annum. It was considered necessary to increase the rate of luxury tax on gutkha from 4% to 20% by amendment the Karnataka Luxuries Tax Act, 1957.

The Karnataka Tax on Luxuries Act, 1957 has been held that gutkha is not liable for sales tax. As the ratio of the aforesaid case is also applicable to the State, it is not possible to continue to levy of sales tax.

penalties: Discontinuation of sales tax on gutkha would entail an revenue loss of about rupee thirty-three crore per annum.
It was considered necessary to increase the rate of luxury tax on gutkha from 4% to 20% by amendment the Karnataka Luxuries Tax Act, 1957.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Levy and collection of luxury taxes.

rights: Right to impose luxury tax on specified goods.
duties: Duty to pay luxury tax as per the provisions of the act.
Duty to levy and collect luxury taxes.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the rates of tax and procedures outlined in the act.

key_procedures: Amendment of sections of existing acts related to taxation.
Insertion of new sections to address specific tax provisions.
administration: State Government
important_notes: The act aims to replace the corresponding ordinance.
There is a provision for repeal and savings.
The act addresses the levy of sales tax on gutkha and the consequent revenue implications.
Judicial pronouncements (e.g., regarding gutkha and sales tax) influence the application of the act.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROHIBITION OF SMOKING AND PROTECTION OF HEALTH OF NON-SMOKERS ACT, 2001
purpose: To provide for prohibition of smoking in places of public work or use and in public service vehicles, and for the protection of health of non-smokers in the State of Karnataka, and to make provisions for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It covers places of public work or use, and public service vehicles. It prohibits smoking, advertisement, sale, and storage of smoking substances in specified locations and to minors.

key_definitions.advertisement: Any notice, circular, wallpaper, pamphlet, display on hoardings, or any visible representation made by means of any light, sound, smoke, gas or any other means which has the effect of promoting smoking.
key_definitions.place_of_public_work_or_use: A place visited by the general public, including auditoriums, hospital buildings, health institutions, amusement centers, restaurants, public offices, court buildings, educational institutions, libraries, places of worship, and other places notified by the State Government. It does not include any open place.
key_definitions.public_service_vehicle: A vehicle as defined under clause (35) of section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
key_definitions.smoking: Smoking of tobacco in any form, whether in the form of cigarette, cigar, beedis or otherwise with the aid of a pipe, wrapper or any other instrument.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force from such date as the State Government may appoint by notification, with different dates for different provisions.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'advertisement', 'Authorised Officer', 'Place of public work or use', 'Public Service Vehicle', and 'smoking'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of smoking, advertisement, sale and storage of smoking substances
main_sections.description: Prohibits smoking in designated places and public service vehicles. It also prohibits advertisements promoting smoking, selling smoking substances to persons below eighteen years, and storing or distributing smoking substances within premises of specific institutions like hospitals, schools, and places of worship.
Mandates the owner, manager, or person in charge of a place of public work or use to display a 'No smoking Zone' notice in Kannada and English at a conspicuous place.

Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act. Fines are prescribed for smoking in prohibited areas and for other violations, with increased penalties for subsequent offences, including imprisonment for certain violations.
Empowers the State Government to appoint Authorised Officers for the purposes of the Act and states that these officers are deemed public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of a person from the Place of an offence
main_sections.description: Allows for the removal of a person persisting in smoking after being asked to desist by an authorised officer or police officer from the place of the offense. No refund of payments for journey or admission is given to removed persons.

main_sections.section_title: Court Competent to try offences under this Act and take cognizance of offences
main_sections.description: Specifies that only Metropolitan Magistrates or Judicial Magistrates First-Class can try offences under the Act. Cognizance is taken based on a written complaint by an authorized officer or a report by a police officer.

main_sections.section_title: Certain offences to be cognizable and Bailable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under clauses (2), (3), and (4) of section 3 as cognizable and bailable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act to be tried summarily
main_sections.description: States that all offences under the Act shall be tried summarily as per the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Lays down provisions for holding companies and their officers liable for offences committed by the company, with provisions for exculpation if due diligence is proven.
Allows the State Government to delegate its powers under the Act to other officers by notification.
Grants the State Government or its authorized person the power to compound offences punishable under the Act.

Repeals the Karnataka Prohibition of Smoking in Show houses and Public halls Act, 1963, and makes consequential amendments to the Karnataka Police Act, 1964. Savings provisions under the Karnataka General Clauses Act are applied.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. Rules are subject to laying before the State Legislature and modification or annulment.

important_rules: No person shall engage in smoking in any place of public work or use where smoking is prohibited and such prohibition is displayed, or in any Public Service Vehicle.

No person shall advertise in any place of Public Work or use or in any Public Service Vehicle to promote smoking or the sale of cigarettes and beedies, with specific exceptions for advertisements on packages or at the entrance/inside warehouses/shops.
No person shall sell cigarettes, beedis or any other smoking substance to any person below the age of eighteen years.

No person shall store, sell or distribute cigarettes or beedis or any other smoking substance within the premises of any Hospital, Health Institution, Public Office, Court, Library, College, School or other Educational Institution and Place of worship.
Owners/managers of places of public work or use must display 'No smoking Zone' notices in Kannada and English.

penalties: Contravention of clause (1) of section 3 or section 4: Fine up to one hundred rupees; for second/subsequent offence, minimum fine of two hundred rupees, up to five hundred rupees.

Contravention of clauses (2), (3), (4) of section 3: Fine up to five hundred rupees; for second/subsequent offence, imprisonment up to three months, and a minimum fine of five hundred rupees, up to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officers appointed by the State Government, and Police Officers not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution in courts (Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First-Class), summary trials, removal of offenders from the place of offense, and compounding of offences.

rights: Right of non-smokers to be protected from passive smoking in public places and vehicles.
Right to have 'No smoking Zone' signage displayed in designated areas.
duties: Duty of persons to refrain from smoking in prohibited areas and public service vehicles.
Duty of owners/managers to display 'No smoking Zone' notices.
Duty of persons selling smoking substances not to sell to minors.
Duty of persons not to store/sell/distribute smoking substances in restricted institutional premises.
Duty of companies and their officers to prevent commission of offences.
Duty of offenders to desist from smoking when asked by authorized personnel.
obligations: Obligation to comply with prohibition of smoking, advertisement, sale, and storage rules.
Obligation to face penalties for contravention.
Obligation to cooperate with Authorised Officers and Police Officers.

key_procedures: Notification by State Government to bring the Act or its provisions into force.
Appointment of Authorised Officers by the State Government.
Display of 'No smoking Zone' notices by owners/managers.
Complaint in writing by an authorized officer or report by a police officer for cognizance of offences.
Summary trial of offences as per the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Removal of offenders from the place of offense.
Compounding of offences by authorized authorities.
Rule-making process by the State Government, including tabling before the State Legislature.
administration: State Government (through its departments, potentially including Health, Home, and Parliamentary Affairs)
important_notes: The Act aims to protect the health of non-smokers from passive smoking hazards.

Specific institutions like Hospitals, Health Institutions, Public Offices, Courts, Libraries, Colleges, Schools, and Places of worship have strict prohibitions on storage and sale of smoking substances.
The Act repeals the Karnataka Prohibition of Smoking in Show houses and Public halls Act, 1963.

title: THE KARNATAKA PANCHAYAT RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and its territories, specifically concerning matters related to the Karnataka Panchayat Raj system.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Karnataka Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2000, and states that it shall come into force at once. It also refers to a previous amendment act from 1999.

This section concerns the insertion of a new section 56A after section 56 of the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993. This new section deals with the duties of Grama Panchayats regarding the abolition of bonded labour system.

important_rules: Rule 1: Grama Panchayats shall be responsible for reporting cases of bonded labour. This reporting is to be done to the Deputy Commissioner or any other authority specified by the Government. Any failure to report such cases will be considered a default in the performance of duties.
Rule 2: The new section 56A details the duties of Grama Panchayats concerning the bonded labour system, aligning with the provisions of the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976.

penalties: Failure to report bonded labour cases will be considered a default in the performance of duties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner or any other authority specified by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through reporting mechanisms and potential actions for default in duties.

duties: Duty to report cases of bonded labour to the Deputy Commissioner or designated authority.
obligations: Obligation to report bonded labour cases in the prescribed form and within specified intervals.

key_procedures: Procedure: Reporting of bonded labour cases by Grama Panchayats to the Deputy Commissioner or other authorized authority in the manner and within the intervals specified.
administration: Deputy Commissioner or any other authority specified by the Government.
important_notes: The Act further amends the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993.
It specifically addresses the abolition of the bonded labour system by Grama Panchayats.

title: THE KARNATAKA SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, to revise sales tax rates on certain commodities and introduce a non-collectable additional tax of one per cent on certain commodities, in view of the deferment of Value Added Taxation System in the State.
scope: This Act applies to all registered dealers and dealers liable to get registered under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, within the State of Karnataka. It specifically amends tax rates and introduces an additional tax on certain commodities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2003, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the First day of June, 2003.
Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by substituting the words "twelve per cent" with "thirteen per cent" in sub-section (1).

Inserts a new Section 6-C, 'Levy of additional tax', which makes every registered dealer and every dealer liable to get registered liable to pay tax at the rate of one per cent of such portion of the total turnover which is liable to tax under sections 5, 5-B, 5-C or 6. It also provides for certain exceptions where this additional tax is not payable.

Amends Section 18 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (3) stating that no dealer liable to pay additional tax under Section 6-C shall collect any amount by way of such additional tax or purporting to be by way of such additional tax.

Amends the Second Schedule to the principal Act by revising the sales tax rates on various commodities in Parts A, B, and C, increasing some rates from twelve per cent to thirteen per cent, from fifteen per cent to sixteen per cent, and from four per cent to five per cent.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections but no details are provided in the provided text excerpt.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections but no details are provided in the provided text excerpt.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections but no details are provided in the provided text excerpt.

important_rules: Rule 1: Levy of additional tax at the rate of one per cent on the portion of total turnover liable to tax under sections 5, 5-B, 5-C, or 6, applicable to registered dealers and dealers liable for registration.

Rule 2: No additional tax shall be payable on turnover related to sales/purchases of goods in the Fifth Schedule, interstate trade, export/import, amounts collected as tax, freight charged separately, discounts allowed, goods returned, labour charges in works contracts, sale of business as a whole, or purchase/sale consideration of goods where tax is leviable at the point of sale/purchase respectively.
Rule 3: Dealers liable to pay additional tax under Section 6-C are prohibited from collecting any amount by way of such additional tax or purporting to be by way of such additional tax.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the sales tax authorities responsible for administering the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder apply to the assessment, collection, or refund of the additional tax, as they apply to other taxes under the Act.

duties: Duty to pay additional tax at the rate of one per cent on specified turnover.
Duty to comply with the assessment, collection, and refund procedures for the additional tax as per the principal Act.
obligations: Obligation for registered dealers and dealers liable for registration to pay the additional tax.
Obligation not to collect additional tax from customers.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Calculation of additional tax at one per cent on the turnover liable to tax under Section 5, 5-B, 5-C, or 6, with specified deductions.
Procedure 2: Assessment, collection, and refund of the additional tax are to be carried out according to the general provisions of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
administration: The administration of this Act is implied to be under the purview of the Karnataka State Legislature and the tax authorities responsible for the implementation of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
important_notes: The revised tax rates and additional tax measures are interim and will be dismantled upon the introduction of the Value Added Tax system.
The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from June 1, 2003.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROTECTION OF INTEREST OF DEPOSITORS IN FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS ACT, 2004
purpose: To provide for the protection of the interests of depositors in financial establishments and to regulate their activities, especially in cases of default or fraudulent practices.
scope: The Act applies to financial establishments operating within the State of Karnataka that accept deposits from the public, excluding those regulated by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, or other government-controlled entities. It covers the actions of these establishments, their promoters, directors, partners, and managers, as well as the properties acquired through deposits and any fraudulent transfers of such properties.

key_definitions.Competent Authority: The authority appointed under Section 5 of the Act.
key_definitions.Deposit: Includes any receipt of money or acceptance of a valuable commodity by a Financial Establishment to be returned after a specified period or otherwise, with or without benefits, but excludes amounts raised by way of share capital, debentures, bonds, amounts from scheduled banks, specific financial institutions, security deposits, dealership deposits, earnest money, advances against orders, amounts received from money lenders, and subscriptions to a Chit.
key_definitions.Depositor: A person who has made deposits with a Financial Establishment.
key_definitions.Financial Establishment: Any person or group of individuals accepting deposits under any scheme or arrangement, but excludes corporations or co-operative societies owned or controlled by any State or Central Government, or banking companies as defined under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
key_definitions.Special Court: A court established under Section 10 of the Act.
key_definitions.Market intelligence: The process of gathering and analyzing information about a financial establishment's financial position and market trends to identify fraudulent activities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Competent Authority, Deposit, Depositor, Financial Establishment, Government, Special Court, and Market intelligence.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of properties on default of return of deposits
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for attaching properties and money acquired by a financial establishment from deposits when it defaults in returning deposits, fails to pay interest, or provides promised services. It details the powers of investigation for the Government, District Magistrates, Police Authorities, and the Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, including civil court powers for summoning persons and documents. It also describes the conditions under which the Government can issue an ad-interim order for attachment and the subsequent notification process.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter premises and inspect certain documents
main_sections.description: Grants powers to the Competent Authority or any authorized officer to enter any premises and inspect documents related to the financial establishment's business.
Provides for the appointment of a Competent Authority by the Government to exercise control over the properties attached under the Act and to perform other duties and functions as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Duties and powers of Competent Authority
main_sections.description: Details the responsibilities and authorities vested in the Competent Authority, including taking possession of attached properties, managing them, and taking steps for their realization.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment of assets and deposit liabilities
main_sections.description: Requires the Competent Authority to assess the assets of the financial establishment and its total deposit liabilities.
Mandates the Competent Authority to submit a report to the Government after assessing the assets and liabilities.
Defines what constitutes a fraudulent default by a financial establishment, including intentional failure to return deposits or pay promised benefits.
Provides for the establishment of a Special Court by the State Government for the purpose of dealing with offenses and matters arising under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Special Court regarding realization of assets and payment to depositors
main_sections.description: Grants powers to the Special Court to realize attached assets and disburse them to the depositors in a fair and equitable manner.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Special Court regarding attachment
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the Special Court concerning the attachment and release of properties.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property of malafide transferees
main_sections.description: Allows for the attachment of property transferred by a financial establishment to another person in bad faith and without consideration.
Provides for furnishing security in place of attachment of property under certain circumstances.
Governs the administration and management of properties attached under the Act.
Specifies the procedure for filing an appeal against orders passed by the Special Court.
Provides for the appointment of a Special Public Prosecutor to conduct cases before the Special Court.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure and powers of Special Court regarding offences
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure and powers of the Special Court in relation to the trial of offenses under this Act.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Financial establishments are prohibited from defaulting on the return of deposits, payment of interest, or provision of promised services.

The Government, based on market intelligence or complaints, can order the attachment of properties acquired by financial establishments from deposits, including personal assets of promoters, directors, etc., if deposits are not returned or assured benefits are not paid.
Properties transferred by financial establishments in bad faith and without consideration can be attached.
The Competent Authority has the power to manage and realize attached properties for the benefit of depositors.
Special Courts are established to deal with cases under this Act, with powers to attach, realize assets, and distribute them to depositors.
Criminal proceedings can be instituted against those responsible for the management of financial establishments for contravention of the Act's provisions, with imprisonment up to ten years and fines.
The Act overrides other laws in cases of inconsistency.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

penalties: Imprisonment up to ten years and a fine up to one lakh rupees for fraudulent default by a Financial Establishment and for contravention of the provisions of the law.
The 2021 amendment enhances the term of imprisonment and penalty for fraudulent default to be on par with the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, District Magistrates, Police Authorities, Competent Authority, and Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of complaints, attachment of properties, appointment of a Competent Authority, establishment of Special Courts, prosecution of offenders, and realization and distribution of attached assets.

rights: Depositors have the right to have their deposits returned with promised interest or benefits.
