Depositors have the right to seek redressal through the mechanisms provided by the Act, including attachment of properties and proceedings in the Special Court.
The right to appeal against orders of the Special Court.
duties: Financial Establishments have a duty to return deposits and pay promised benefits as agreed.
Promoters, Directors, Partners, Managers, and other responsible persons of Financial Establishments have a duty to manage the establishment honestly and in compliance with the Act.
Persons summoned by authorities under the Act have a duty to attend and provide truthful information and produce documents.
obligations: Financial Establishments are obligated to comply with the provisions of the Act and any orders issued by the Government or Special Court.
Those involved in fraudulent activities are obligated to face legal consequences as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Upon receiving a complaint or based on market intelligence, the Government or District Magistrate can order an investigation into a financial transaction.
The Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, Competent Authority, or nominated authority can conduct investigations with civil court powers to summon persons and documents.
If the Government is satisfied that a financial establishment has defaulted or intends to defraud depositors, it can issue an ad-interim order attaching money or property acquired from deposits.
The attached properties are managed by the Competent Authority, and a report is submitted to the Government.
A Special Court is constituted to deal with all cases arising under the Act.
The Special Court has the power to confirm ad-interim attachments, realize attached assets, and disburse them to depositors.
Criminal proceedings are initiated against those responsible for fraudulent defaults.
Appeals can be filed against orders of the Special Court.
administration: The Revenue Department of the State Government, along with other nominated authorities and the Special Courts.
important_notes: The Act was amended by Act 06 of 2021 to enhance investigation powers, appointment of competent authorities, time limits for applications, asset valuation, penalty enhancements, and transfer of cases.
The Act aims to provide a robust legal framework to protect the interests of depositors from fraudulent financial establishments.
The definition of 'Deposit' is crucial, and specific exclusions are provided to define the scope of financial establishments covered.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, to establish new universities and redefine the jurisdiction of existing ones for expanding higher education facilities and promoting student convenience.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and specifically concerns the establishment and jurisdiction of state universities within Karnataka. It amends the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Act, 2010, and states that it shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by omitting certain district names from existing clauses and inserting provisions for the establishment of the Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University (Bellary) and the Ranichannamma University (Belgaum) with their respective territorial jurisdictions.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (5). This sub-section deals with the withdrawal of privileges enjoyed by colleges from Gulbarga University or Karnataka University, and their subsequent affiliation to the newly established Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University or Ranichannamma University, respectively.

Amends Section 14 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso after the fifth proviso in sub-section (4). This proviso states that the first Vice-Chancellors of the Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University and Ranichannamma University shall be appointed by the State Government.

Empowers a special officer appointed by the State Government to exercise specified powers and perform functions of the University and Vice-Chancellor until the first Vice-Chancellor is appointed, for the purpose of establishing the new universities.

Specifies the duty of the first Vice-Chancellor to make arrangements for constituting the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities of the new universities within six months (extendable to one year by the Chancellor).

Addresses transitional arrangements, allowing the first Vice-Chancellor to discharge University functions until authorities are constituted. It also states that existing Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Rules of Gulbarga or Karnataka University will apply to affiliated colleges of the new universities until they make their own.

Provides savings for students studying for degrees or for examinations already held or results published before the commencement of this Act, ensuring continuity in examinations and conferment of degrees.

Grants the State Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the amendment Act, publishable in the official gazette, within two years of commencement.

important_rules: Colleges previously affiliated with Gulbarga or Karnataka Universities in specific districts are now deemed affiliated to the newly established Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University or Ranichannamma University.
The first Vice-Chancellors of the new universities will be appointed by the State Government.
The first Vice-Chancellors are responsible for constituting the governing bodies of the new universities within six months to a year.
Existing university statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules will apply to affiliated colleges of the new universities until the new universities establish their own.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (specifically mentioned for appointment of Vice-Chancellors and removal of difficulties). The overall enforcement is implicitly by the State Legislature and the relevant university authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, appointment of university officials, and by the respective university authorities once established.

rights: Colleges and educational institutions have the right to be affiliated with the appropriate new university.
Students have the right to continue their studies and receive degrees/diplomas under existing examination frameworks until the new universities are fully operational.
duties: The State Government has the duty to establish the new universities and appoint their first Vice-Chancellors.
The first Vice-Chancellor has the duty to constitute the governing bodies of the new universities.
obligations: The State Government has an obligation to ensure the smooth transition and functioning of the new universities.
The new universities (and their authorities once formed) have an obligation to affiliate colleges and conduct examinations.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing University Act: The process involves legislative action to amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.
Establishment of New Universities: This involves defining their territorial jurisdiction and headquarters.
Affiliation of Colleges: A procedure for transferring affiliations from old universities to new ones is outlined.
Appointment of First Vice-Chancellors: The State Government directly appoints the first Vice-Chancellors of the new universities.
Constitution of University Authorities: The first Vice-Chancellor is tasked with forming the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other bodies.
Removal of Difficulties: The State Government can issue orders to resolve any issues arising from the implementation of the Act.
administration: The administration of the new universities will fall under the purview of the State Government and the respective university bodies (Syndicate, Academic Council, etc.) once constituted.
important_notes: The establishment of Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University and Ranichannamma University is aimed at improving access and convenience in higher education.
The act ensures a smooth transition for colleges and students affected by the jurisdictional changes.
The State Government has the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in implementing the act for a period of two years.
The governor's assent was received on July 24, 2010, and the act was first published on July 27, 2010.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, for the purposes of providing for the orderly introduction of self-assessment of property tax and to provide for the constitution of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal. The act aims to amend sections of the principal act to introduce a system of self-assessment of property tax and to provide for the constitution of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal.
scope: The act applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations and their administration, specifically concerning property tax assessment and related procedures.

main_sections.description: This section likely deals with the official name of the act and when it comes into effect.
Amends section 2 of the principal act. Specific details of the amendment are not provided in the excerpt.
Amends section 154 of the principal act. Specific details of the amendment are not provided in the excerpt.
Omission of section 156 of the principal act. Specific details are not provided.
Amends section 157 of the principal act. Specific details are not provided.
Deals with provisions for the transition to the new act.

main_sections.section_title: STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS (as appended to the Bill)
main_sections.description: This section details the rationale behind the act's introduction, including the necessity to amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to introduce self-assessment of property tax and to provide for the constitution of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal.

important_rules: Rule 1: The act aims to introduce a system of self-assessment of property tax and to provide for the constitution of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal.
Rule 2: It is considered necessary to amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to implement these changes.
Rule 3: The amendment aims to streamline the process of property tax assessment and collection.

Rule 4: The act concerns the imposition of property tax at such percentage of the capital value of the building as may be fixed by the Corporation with reference to the location, type of construction of the building, nature of use to which it is put, and the area of the building.
Rule 5: Payment of property tax and filing of returns by owners or occupiers.
Rule 6: An incentive at the rate of five percent of the tax for owners filing returns within the specified time.
Rule 7: To collect service charges in respect of properties exempted from property tax.
Rule 8: To collect penalty equal to twice the tax leviable in respect of unlaweful buildings without prejudice to any proceedings or action to be taken.
Rule 9: To publish property tax register for public information.
Rule 10: To undertake survey of lands and buildings and preparation of properties registered.

penalties: Penalty of five percent of the tax for owners filing returns within the specified time.
Penalty equal to twice the tax leviable in cases of unlawful buildings without prejudice to any proceedings or action to be taken.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations and the constituted Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal are implied enforcement authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and collection of property tax, filing of returns, and imposition of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to receive incentives for timely filing of returns.
Right to have property tax assessed based on location, construction type, use, and area.
duties: Duty to self-assess and pay property tax.
Duty to file returns within specified times.
Duty to cooperate with surveys of lands and buildings.
Duty to pay service charges for exempted properties.
Duty to pay penalties for unlawful buildings or failure to file returns.
Duty to pay property tax at such percentage of the capital value of the building as may be fixed by the Corporation.
obligations: Owners/occupiers are obligated to pay property tax and file returns.
Corporations are obligated to publish property tax registers for public information.

key_procedures: Self-assessment of property tax by owners/occupiers.
Filing of property tax returns within specified times.
Collection of property tax by the Corporation.
Conducting surveys of lands and buildings.
Preparation of property tax registers.
Constitution of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal for appeals.
Imposition of penalties for non-compliance.
administration: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations are responsible for the administration of this act.
important_notes: The amendment introduces a system of self-assessment for property tax.
A Karnataka Municipal Corporations Appellate Tribunal is constituted for appeals.
Incentives are provided for timely filing of returns.
Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, including for unlawful buildings and delayed filings.
The act amends The Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, Act No. 12 of 1977.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 (Karnataka Act 22 of 1964) to introduce provisions for specifying smaller urban areas with district headquarters as city municipal areas even with less than 50,000 population, modify requirements for no-confidence motions against Presidents/Vice-Presidents, dispense with government sanction for levying taxes, reduce property tax rates on vacant land, exempt certain places of public worship and charitable purposes from property tax, levy penalties on belated property tax payments, omit provisions for water cess, exempt certain vacant land around residential buildings from property tax, provide for delegation of powers, and validate past assessments.
scope: This Act applies to municipalities within the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It affects the classification of urban areas, the levy and assessment of property tax, and related procedures.

key_definitions.Director of Municipal Administration: The Director of Municipal Administration appointed under sub-section (1-A) of section 388.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the dates from which different provisions come into force, including retrospective application for certain clauses.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act to omit clause (5), insert the definition of 'Director of Municipal Administration', and modify definitions related to 'buildings or lands or both' and introduce 'Vacant land'.
Inserts a proviso to Section 3(2) allowing the Governor to specify a smaller urban area with a district headquarters as a city municipal area even if the population is less than fifty thousand.

Amends Section 42(9) to require a motion of no-confidence in the President or Vice-President to be passed by a majority of the total number of councillors having voting rights and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of those present and voting.

Amends Section 94 of the principal Act to omit certain clauses related to government sanction for taxes, revise the scope of property tax, and introduce exemptions for various types of buildings and vacant lands, including places of public worship, choultries, charitable institutions, ancient monuments, hospitals, and government lands.
Omit Section 94A of the principal Act.
Omit Sections 95 and 96 of the principal Act.

Substitutes Section 97 to outline the process for publishing resolutions for levying taxes, including notice board display and newspaper advertisements, and states that such publication is conclusive evidence of proper imposition.
Amends Section 99 by inserting 'and transitional area' after 'municipal area' in sub-section (1) and 'or Town Panchayat' after 'municipal council' in sub-section (3).
Omit Section 100 of the principal Act.

Amends Section 101 to modify the levy of property tax on buildings and vacant land, specifying percentage ranges for commercial buildings, residential buildings, and vacant lands of different sizes, and omitting explanations.
Provides for the validation of assessments and other related actions made under the principal Act.
Repeals the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003, and provides for savings.

important_rules: Property tax rates on vacant land are reduced compared to previous rates.

Property tax exemption is provided for places of public worship, choultries used for charitable purposes, orphanages, homes, schools for the deaf and dumb, asylums for the aged and fallen women, and similar philanthropic institutions.
A penalty of 2% per month is to be levied on belated payment of property tax due.
Water cess provisions are omitted to mitigate tax burden.
Vacant land up to a maximum of 50 square meters around a residential building on a site up to 225 square meters is exempt from property tax.

No tax is levied on specific types of advertisements, including those displayed within a building related to its trade, or those relating to the property itself, railway advertisements, state government activities, or public meetings.

penalties: A penalty of 2% per month on belated payment of property tax due.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Municipal Councils, Chief Officers, and potentially other designated authorities under the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy of property taxes, penalties for non-payment, and the established administrative and legal mechanisms of municipal governance in Karnataka.

rights: Right to have smaller urban areas with district headquarters classified as city municipal areas irrespective of population thresholds.
Right to exemption from property tax for specific categories of properties (e.g., public worship, charitable purposes, certain vacant lands).
Right to have tax resolutions published and to have such publication serve as conclusive evidence of proper imposition.
duties: Duty to pay property tax as levied by the municipal council.
Duty to comply with the provisions regarding no-confidence motions in Presidents/Vice-Presidents.
Duty to pay property tax on time to avoid penalties.
obligations: Municipal councils have the obligation to pass resolutions levying taxes and publish them.
Municipal councils have the obligation to implement exemptions and levy penalties as prescribed.
Government and designated officers have obligations related to delegation of powers.

key_procedures: Procedure for specifying a smaller urban area with a district headquarters as a city municipal area.
Procedure for passing a motion of no-confidence in the President or Vice-President.
Procedure for levying any tax, which involves passing a resolution at a general meeting, specifying liable classes and rates, and publishing the resolution with notice.
Procedure for obtaining exemptions from property tax for specified buildings and vacant lands.
Procedure for appealing or challenging assessments, though not explicitly detailed in the provided text, is implied within the framework of municipal tax administration.
administration: The Act amends the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, thus its administration falls under the purview of the Karnataka State Government, likely through the Urban Development Department or a similar body responsible for municipal affairs, and the respective municipal councils and officers.
important_notes: Certain provisions have retrospective effect, with specific dates mentioned for commencement.
The definition of 'buildings or lands or both' is expanded to include 'any land occupied by it or vacant land or both'.
The Act aims to mitigate tax burden by omitting provisions related to the levy of water cess.
A certificate issued by the Government or an authorized officer regarding the use of a building or land for government purposes is binding on the municipal council.

title: THE CHILD MARRIAGE RESTRAINT (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To provide for the prevention of child marriages by appointing a Child Marriage Prevention Officer and empowering the State Government to make rules for this purpose, by amending the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 (Central Act 19 of 1929) in its application to the State of Karnataka.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka. It amends the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, to introduce provisions for the prevention of child marriages within the state.

key_definitions.Child Marriage Prevention Officer: An officer appointed by the State Government to prevent marriages performed in contravention of the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, collect evidence for prosecutions, and discharge other assigned functions.
key_definitions.Public Servant: The Child Marriage Prevention Officer appointed under Section 13 is deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of Section 21 of the Penal Code, 1860.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Child Marriage Restraint (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2004, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Provides for the insertion of new sections, namely 13, 13A, 13B, and 14, after section 12 of the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929.

Empowers the State Government to appoint a Child Marriage Prevention Officer, defines their duties which include preventing child marriages, collecting evidence, and performing other functions assigned by the State Government. It also allows the State Government to invest the officer with powers of a Police Officer and to associate them with a non-official advisory body of social workers.

main_sections.section_title: Child Marriage Prevention Officer appointed under the Act to be public servant
main_sections.description: Declares that the Child Marriage Prevention Officer appointed under section 13 shall be deemed to be a public servant under the Penal Code, 1860.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit or legal proceedings shall lie against a Child Marriage Prevention Officer for any action taken in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including providing for matters expressly required or allowed by the Act to be prescribed. It also includes provisions for laying down such rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Child Marriage Prevention Officer's duty is to prevent marriages contravening the Act, collect evidence for prosecution, and perform other assigned functions.
Rule 2: The Child Marriage Prevention Officer is to be considered a public servant.
Rule 3: No legal proceedings can be initiated against the Child Marriage Prevention Officer for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Rule 4: The State Government has the power to make rules for the effective implementation of the Act, and these rules are subject to legislative scrutiny.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Child Marriage Prevention Officer, appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the actions of the Child Marriage Prevention Officer, which may include collecting evidence for prosecution and, if empowered, exercising powers of a Police Officer. The State Government also makes rules for enforcement.

rights: Right to protection from child marriage.
Right to have a Child Marriage Prevention Officer appointed to prevent contraventions of the Act.
Right to have a non-official advisory body assist the Child Marriage Prevention Officer.
duties: Duty of the Child Marriage Prevention Officer to prevent child marriages and collect evidence.
Duty of the State Government to appoint officers and make rules.

key_procedures: Appointment of a Child Marriage Prevention Officer by the State Government via notification.
The Child Marriage Prevention Officer takes action to prevent child marriages and collects evidence.
The State Government can invest the Child Marriage Prevention Officer with Police Officer powers.
The State Government can form an advisory body to assist the Child Marriage Prevention Officer.
The State Government can make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to legislative approval.
administration: State Government of Karnataka, through the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory of the document).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Central Act 19 of 1929 (The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929).
The Act comes into force on a date to be notified by the State Government.
The Child Marriage Prevention Officer is deemed a public servant.
Actions taken in good faith by the Child Marriage Prevention Officer are protected from legal proceedings.

title: THE KARNATAKA HIGHWAYS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964, to provide an enabling provision to levy and collect fees from users for services or benefits rendered by highways, to meet the expenditure involved in the improvement of State highways/major district roads constructed, developed, and maintained under Public Private Partnership on an annuity basis.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964. It applies to users of highways in Karnataka that are constructed, developed, or maintained under Public Private Partnership on an annuity basis, or through loans. The scope is geographical to Karnataka and subject matter to the levying and collection of fees for highway services and benefits.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Highways (Amendment) Act, 2010, and that it comes into force at once.

This section amends section 19A of the principal Act. It inserts a new sub-section (3A) allowing the Government to levy and collect fees from highway users for services or benefits rendered, with rates notified in the official Gazette. It also makes an amendment to sub-section (4) of section 19A, inserting 'or State Government'.

This section amends section 19B of the principal Act by substituting 'in sub-section (1) of section 19A' with 'in sub-section (1) and sub-section (3A) of section 19A', thereby extending the scope of section 19B to include the newly inserted sub-section (3A).

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government may levy and collect fees from users of highways for services or benefits rendered by it.
Rule 2: Such fees shall be at rates notified by the Government in the official Gazette. Different rates may be notified for different highways over different periods.

Rule 3: The notification of fee rates should consider the expenditure involved in land acquisition, construction, development, and maintenance of highways developed under public-private partnership on an annuity basis, or by raising loans.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levying and collection of fees as notified in the official Gazette.

rights: The right of the Government to levy and collect fees from highway users for services and benefits rendered.
duties: The duty of the Government to notify fee rates and considerations for their determination.
obligations: Obligation of highway users to pay the levied fees.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Government notifies the rate of fee to be levied and collected from highway users for services or benefits rendered, potentially with different rates for different highways and periods, considering expenditure on land acquisition, construction, development, and maintenance of PPP annuity basis highways or loan-funded highways.
Procedure 2: The Government enforces the collection of these notified fees from the users of the specified highways.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory)
important_notes: The amendment allows for fee collection notwithstanding anything contained in section 48A of the principal Act.
The fees are intended to meet the expenditure involved in the improvement of State highways/major district roads.

title: THE KARNATAKA PROFESSIONAL CIVIL ENGINEERS ACT, 2024
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council, for the registration of Professional Civil Engineers, to set standards of professional conduct and etiquette, and a code of ethics for professional civil engineers, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to civil engineers and matters related to their professional practice and registration.

key_definitions.Certificate of Practice: A certificate issued by the Council to a Professional Civil Engineer.
key_definitions.Certificate of Registration: A certificate issued to a Civil Engineer whose name is entered into the register maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.Civil Engineer: A person who has obtained a Diploma in Civil Engineering or Bachelors Degree in Civil Engineering/ Masters Degree in any discipline of Civil Engineering as defined in National Building Code – 2016.
key_definitions.Council: The Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers established under section 3.
key_definitions.Disciplinary Committee: A committee constituted under section 31 of the Act.
key_definitions.Engineering Designs: Civil, Structural, Geo-technical, Environmental Engineering Designs/Drawings and also encompassing Conceptual Plans, Master Plans, Layout Plans, other design & drawings etc., for buildings & infrastructure.
key_definitions.Professional Civil Engineer: A registered civil engineer who has obtained a Certificate of Practice from the Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers (KCPCE).
key_definitions.Recognised Engineering Institution: Any college/institution/university established by law in India or other institution in India or outside India which imparts education in civil engineering and confers a degree or diploma in civil engineering.
key_definitions.Register: The register of Professional Civil Engineers maintained under section 23.
key_definitions.Registered Civil Engineer: A person who has enrolled with the Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers.
key_definitions.Regulations: Regulations made under section 46 by the Council.
key_definitions.Rules: Rules made under section 45 by the State Government.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Act, 2024, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of Karnataka, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Certificate of Practice', 'Civil Engineer', 'Council', 'Engineering Designs', 'Professional Civil Engineer', 'Register', etc.

Establishes the 'Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers' as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It details the composition of the Governing Council, including elected, ex-officio, nominated, and co-opted members, totaling eighteen members.
Outlines the election of the President and Vice-President of the Council from amongst its members, their term of office (three years), eligibility for re-election, and resignation provisions.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, indicating it will detail the specific duties and responsibilities of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Registration to practice as Civil Engineer
main_sections.description: This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, suggesting it deals with the process or requirements for registering to practice as a Civil Engineer.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, implying it specifies the educational and/or experience criteria required for registration.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, indicating it will define what constitutes professional misconduct for Civil Engineers.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, suggesting it outlines the penalties for individuals practicing without being registered.

main_sections.section_title: Authority not to permit construction unless engineering design is certified by Professional Civil Engineer
main_sections.description: This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, indicating a provision that construction authorities must ensure engineering designs are certified by a Professional Civil Engineer.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, indicating the State Government's authority to make rules under the Act.
This section is listed in the arrangement of sections, indicating the Council's authority to make regulations under the Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint the date on which the Act shall come into force.
Rule 2: The Council shall meet at least once in every three months at such time and place and shall observe rules of procedure.
Rule 3: Elections of the President and Vice-President shall be conducted in a manner prescribed by Rules.
Rule 4: The State Government can nominate members to the first Council if the register is not yet prepared, with specific experience requirements and a tenure of two years.
Rule 5: Any casual vacancy in the Council shall be filled by fresh election, nomination, or co-option, with the new member serving for the remainder of the term.

penalties: Penalty for non-registration (Section 33)
Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered (Section 34)
Penalty for failure to surrender certificates of registration and practice (Section 37)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers and potentially other relevant authorities as mandated by specific sections (e.g., authorities permitting construction).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for registration, disciplinary proceedings, penalties for misconduct and non-compliance, and the requirement for certification of engineering designs by registered professional civil engineers.

rights: Right to practice as a Civil Engineer upon registration and obtaining a Certificate of Practice.
Right to have one's name entered in the register.
Right to challenge election disputes through a tribunal.
duties: Duty to register as a Civil Engineer to practice.
Duty to adhere to professional conduct and ethics.
Duty to surrender certificates as required by the Act.
Duty of the Council to prepare and maintain the register.
Duty of the Council to conduct elections and meetings.
Duty of the Special Committee (if constituted) to hold elections within six months.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a Certificate of Practice to be a 'Professional Civil Engineer'.
Obligation for authorities to ensure engineering designs are certified by a Professional Civil Engineer before permitting construction.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment and composition of the Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers, including elections and nominations.
Procedure for the election of the President and Vice-President of the Council.
Procedure for filling casual vacancies in the Council.
Procedure for registration of Civil Engineers and obtaining a Certificate of Practice.
Procedure for inquiries relating to misconduct of registered engineers.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of a Special Committee if elections fail.
Procedure for the resolution of election disputes through a Tribunal.
administration: The Karnataka Council of Professional Civil Engineers, established under the Act. The State Government also plays a role in rule-making, notifications, and oversight.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
The first Council may be nominated by the State Government pending preparation of the register, with specific experience requirements and a limited tenure.
No act or proceeding of the Council is invalid due to vacancies, defects in constitution, or procedural irregularities that do not affect the merits of the case.
Members of the Council, officers, and employees are considered public servants.
The State Government has the power to remove difficulties and to supersede the Council under certain circumstances.

title: Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Act, 2024
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council and to provide for the registration and regulation of the profession of Civil Engineers in the State of Karnataka.
scope: This act applies to the entire State of Karnataka and regulates the profession of Civil Engineers within the state.

key_definitions.act: The Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Act, 2024
key_definitions.certificate of practice: A certificate granted by the Council under section 22 of this Act.
key_definitions.registration certificate: A certificate granted to a Civil Engineer registered in the register maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.civil engineer: A person who has obtained a Diploma or a Post Graduate Degree in Civil Engineering or a Post Graduate Degree in any branch of Civil Engineering as specified in the National Building Code/2016 (NBC 2016).
key_definitions.council: The Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council established under section 3.
key_definitions.disciplinary proceedings committee: A committee constituted under section 31 of the Act.
key_definitions.engineering drawings: Includes drawings, schematics, plans, conceptual plans, master plans, layout plans, and other engineering drawings for buildings and infrastructure, civil, geo-technical, structural engineering.
key_definitions.professional civil engineer: A Civil Engineer registered with the Council and holding a certificate of practice.
key_definitions.recognised engineering institution: Any college/institute/university established by the central government or state government or any institution outside India or institution outside India, which offers Civil Engineering education and awards a degree or diploma in Civil Engineering.
key_definitions.register: The register of Professional Civil Engineers maintained under section 23.
key_definitions.registered civil engineer: A person whose name is registered in the Council of Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Council under section 46.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the State Government under section 45.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the act, states its extent to the whole of Karnataka, and specifies its commencement upon notification by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and constitution of the Council
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It outlines the Council's perpetual succession, common seal, power to contract and sue/be sued. The head office is to be in Bengaluru. It specifies the composition of the Council including elected members from different divisions and nominated members from various government departments and educational institutions.

main_sections.section_title: President and Vice-President of the Council
main_sections.description: Deals with the election of the President and Vice-President of the Council by its members, as per the procedure laid down in Section 5. It also mentions interim arrangements and the tenure of the elected President and Vice-President.

Lays down the procedure for the election of the President and Vice-President, as may be prescribed by rules. It also provides for the establishment of an authority to decide any dispute arising out of such elections.

Specifies the term of elected, nominated, or ex-officio members of the Council as three years. It also details resignation, vacation of seats due to absence from meetings, ceasing to be a Civil Engineer, or disciplinary action, and the procedure for filling casual vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: Holding of elections of the Council
main_sections.description: Mandates that the ordinary election of the Council shall be held within one month before the expiry of the term of the existing members.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of special committee in case of failure to hold election
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a special committee, comprising the senior-most member (President) and a nominated member from the list of registered Civil Engineers, to perform the functions of the Council in case of failure to hold elections within the stipulated time. This committee will function until a new Council is constituted.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of proceedings not to be affected by vacancies or technicalities
main_sections.description: Ensures that the proceedings of the Council are not invalidated due to any vacancy in its membership, any defect in its constitution, or any technical irregularity in its procedure.
Lists disqualifications for becoming a member of the Council, including being declared insolvent, convicted of certain offenses, or declared of unsound mind.
States that the Council shall meet at least once in three months, at such times and places as may be prescribed by regulations. It also refers to quorum for meetings.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including penalties for unregistered practice and disciplinary actions.

rights: Right to practice as a Civil Engineer after registration and obtaining a certificate of practice.
duties: Duty to register with the Council.
Duty to adhere to the code of conduct.
Duty to obtain a certificate of practice.
Duty to maintain professional standards.
obligations: Obligation to follow the regulations and rules made under the Act.
Obligation to cooperate with the Council and its inquiries.

key_procedures: Procedure for election of President and Vice-President (Section 5).
Procedure for filling casual vacancies in the Council (Section 6).
Procedure for holding ordinary elections of the Council (Section 7).
Procedure for constituting a special committee if elections fail (Section 8).
Procedure for registration and obtaining certificate of practice (implied through definitions and structure of the Act).
administration: Karnataka State Government, and the Karnataka Professional Civil Engineers Council.
important_notes: The Act has provisions for penalties for practising without registration and for professional misconduct.
The Act establishes a Disciplinary Proceedings Committee to inquire into cases of professional misconduct.

title: THE KARNATAKA RE-REGISTRATION OF MOTOR VEHICLES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To amend the Registration of Motor Vehicles Act, 1956, for further matters relating to the re-registration of motor vehicles and to make amendments to the Registration Act, 1956, in its application to the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the re-registration of motor vehicles, including electronic and other devices used for such purposes.

key_definitions.registration: The process of registering motor vehicles by means of electronic or other devices.
key_definitions.re-registration: The act of re-registering motor vehicles.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Karnataka Re-registration of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2001. It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 6 of the Registration Act, 1956 (Central Act XXVI of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in its application to the State of Karnataka.
In section 12 of the principal Act, after the word 'whom', the words 'the Inspector General of Registration or' shall be inserted.
This part shall apply only to the areas in respect of which a notification is issued by the State Government under section 50C.

In this part, 'process of Re-registration of documents by means of electronic or other devices' shall mean and include scanning and preservation of documents with the help of computers, scanners, microfilming and any other device used for the purpose of storage and retrieval when required.

main_sections.section_title: Process of re-registration of documents by means of electronic or other devices
main_sections.description: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, authorize the Inspector General of Registration, or any other officer, to computerise the process of re-registration of documents by means of electronic or other devices in such areas as may be notified by the State Government.

important_rules: Documents can be re-registered using electronic or other devices, including scanning, microfilming, and computerization.
The State Government may authorize the Inspector General of Registration or other officers to computerize re-registration processes in specified areas.
Electronic or scanned documents are considered valid for storage and retrieval.

penalties: Section 55 (4) (a): Application of this part is mandatory for the areas specified.
Section 55 (4) (b): Definition of the process of re-registration of documents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Inspector General of Registration, and other authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notifications to specify areas where computerization of re-registration is mandatory and by authorizing officers to carry out these processes.

rights: Right to re-register documents using electronic or other devices.
Right to store and retrieve documents through computerized processes.
duties: Duty to apply this part to notified areas.
Duty to carry out re-registration processes as specified by the State Government.
obligations: Obligation to ensure the validity of electronic or scanned documents.
Obligation for the State Government to issue notifications for the implementation of the Act.

key_procedures: Notification by the State Government to specify areas for compulsory re-registration using electronic or other devices.
Authorization of officers by the State Government to computerize the re-registration process.
Application of electronic or other devices for scanning, preservation, storage, and retrieval of documents.
administration: Inspector General of Registration and other officers authorized by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on dates notified by the State Government.
The Act makes reference to other acts, such as the Registration Act, 1956 (Central Act XXVI of 1956).

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to rationalize provisions relating to inspections, dispense with government sanction before imposing tax, reduce property tax on vacant land, increase currency of trade licenses, levy penalty on belated property tax payment, omit water cess levy, enhance tax on commercial buildings, exempt certain vacant land around residential buildings, and validate assessments.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, and its provisions are applicable to Municipal Corporations established under that Act within the state of Karnataka. It primarily deals with property tax, trade licenses, and administrative powers related to municipal corporations.

key_definitions.building or land or both: Amended to 'vacant land or building' or 'building including any land occupied by it or vacant land or both' to specifically include vacant land in tax assessments.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different provisions, some of which are retrospective.
Amends definitions in Section 2 of the principal Act, particularly concerning 'land or building' to include 'vacant land' and defines 'vacant land'.
Substitutes 'Deputy Commissioner of the district' for 'Divisional Commissioner of the revenue division' in Section 71(1) of the principal Act.
Replaces Section 106 of the principal Act concerning the publication of resolutions with notice for levying taxes.

Amends Section 108 of the principal Act to redefine the rates of property tax for commercial buildings, residential buildings, and vacant land, and introduces an exemption for vacant land around residential buildings.
Inserts a new sub-section (4) into Section 112 of the principal Act to introduce a penalty of 2% per month for belated payment of tax.
Replaces Section 146 of the principal Act with a provision empowering the Government to require a corporation to impose taxes by notification.
Indicates the insertion of a new section 443-A into the principal Act, the content of which is not detailed in the provided text.
This section deals with the validation of assessments made under the principal Act.
This section likely deals with the repeal of any conflicting provisions and savings clauses for actions taken under previous enactments.

important_rules: Property tax on commercial buildings shall be levied at a rate not less than 0.5% and not more than 1.5% of the taxable capital value.
Property tax on residential buildings and other non-commercial buildings shall be levied at a rate not less than 0.3% and not more than 0.6% of the taxable capital value.
Property tax on vacant land shall be levied at varying rates based on its measurement, with lower rates for larger areas.
Vacant land up to 50 square meters around residential buildings on sites up to 225 square meters is exempt from property tax.
A penalty of 2% per month is levied on belated payment of property tax.
Trade licenses shall have a currency of five years.
Government officers authorized can inspect corporation properties, works, and documents and require written replies to objections.
Corporations must afford authorized government officers access to premises and records for inspection.

penalties: Penalty at the rate of two per cent per month on the amount of property tax remaining unpaid after the specified period.
Penalty at the rate of two per cent per month of the amount of property tax assessed and due in case of failure to pay and submit a return.
One hundred rupees in case of failure to submit a return after payment of property tax in full.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner or authorized officer of the Municipal Corporation, and officers of the Government authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, requiring written replies, imposition of penalties for non-compliance or delayed payments, and validation of assessments.

rights: Right of authorized government officers to inspect corporation properties, works, and records.
Right to exemption from property tax on a specified extent of vacant land around residential buildings.
Right to have trade licenses with a currency of five years.
duties: Duty of corporations and municipal authorities to afford access to authorized government officers.
Duty of taxpayers to pay property tax on time.
Duty to submit returns related to property tax.
Duty to publish resolutions for tax imposition in local newspapers.
obligations: Obligation of the corporation to pass a resolution at a general meeting to levy any tax.
Obligation to follow the rates prescribed for property tax on different types of properties.
Obligation to provide written replies to government officers regarding objections to proposed actions.

key_procedures: Levying a tax: A corporation shall pass a resolution at a general meeting, specify liable classes/properties and rates, publish a notice of the resolution, which serves as conclusive evidence of imposition.
Inspection by government officers: Authorized officers can enter, inspect properties, call for documents, and require written replies from corporations regarding objections or necessary actions.

Property tax assessment and payment: Tax is levied based on capital value, with specific rates for commercial buildings, residential buildings, and vacant land. Penalties apply for delayed payment. Exemptions are provided for certain vacant lands.
Transfer of property tax responsibility: Upon transfer of property, the transferee's name is entered in the property tax register if the Commissioner or authorized officer is informed.
administration: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, administered by Municipal Corporations within Karnataka, with oversight and directive powers from the State Government.
important_notes: Some provisions of the Act are retrospective, with specific commencement dates from November 19, 2001, and June 16, 2003.
The amendment aims to mitigate tax burden by omitting water cess.
The amendment seeks to avoid hardship to small traders by increasing the currency of trade licenses.
Validation of assessments made prior to the amendment is included.

title: THE BANGALORE WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To amend the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964, to empower the State Government to direct the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board to levy and collect beneficiary capital contribution through Local Bodies for water supply and sanitation projects, and to validate the collection of such contributions made from January 1, 2003.
scope: Applies to the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board, Local Bodies within the Bangalore Metropolitan Area, and beneficiaries of water supply and sanitation projects in the region. It specifically addresses the collection of capital contributions for projects sanctioned for seven City Municipal Councils and one Town Municipal Council of the Bangalore Metropolitan Area.

key_definitions.capital contribution: Capital contribution collected from the beneficiaries of any project, or through a Local Authority, for making funding arrangements for water supply and sanitation projects.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2010, and that it comes into force at once.

Inserts a new section 89A into the principal Act (Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1964), empowering the State Government to direct the Board to collect capital contribution from beneficiaries or through Local Authorities, or to borrow loans for funding water supply and sanitation projects. This insertion is deemed to have effect from January 1, 2003.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of assessment and collection of capital contribution
main_sections.description: Declares that notwithstanding any court judgment or order, any direction issued by the State Government to collect capital contribution, and any assessment or collection of such contribution made from January 1, 2003, in accordance with such directions, are valid. It also prevents suits or proceedings for the refund of such contributions and prohibits courts from enforcing orders directing refunds.

important_rules: Rule 1: The State Government may issue directions to the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board to collect capital contribution from beneficiaries or through Local Authorities for water supply and sanitation projects.
Rule 2: Such capital contribution can be collected for funding arrangements of these projects.
Rule 3: Any assessment or collection of capital contribution made from January 1, 2003, in accordance with State Government directions is deemed valid and effective.
Rule 4: No proceedings can be maintained for the refund of capital contributions collected under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued by the State Government to the Board, and by the Board and Local Authorities in assessing and collecting capital contributions. The Act also enforces its provisions by invalidating any legal challenges to past collections and preventing future refund claims.

rights: Right of the State Government to issue directions for funding arrangements and collection of capital contribution.
Right of the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board to collect capital contribution as directed.
Right of Local Authorities to collect capital contribution on behalf of the Board.
Right of beneficiaries to have their capital contributions applied to water supply and sanitation projects.
duties: Duty of the State Government to issue necessary directions.
Duty of the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board to make funding arrangements and collect capital contribution.
Duty of Local Authorities to collect capital contribution as per directions.
Duty of beneficiaries to pay the assessed capital contribution.
obligations: Obligation to comply with State Government directions regarding capital contribution.
Obligation to ensure that collected capital contributions are used for water supply and sanitation projects.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: State Government issues directions to the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board for funding arrangements, including the collection of capital contribution from beneficiaries or through Local Authorities.
Procedure 2: The Board or Local Authority assesses and collects the capital contribution as per the State Government's directions.
Procedure 3: Validation of all actions, assessments, and collections of capital contribution made from January 1, 2003, in accordance with the said directions.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (as indicated by the signatory and the legislative context), and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board for operational aspects.
important_notes: The insertion of section 89A and the validation of capital contribution collection are deemed to have effect from January 1, 2003.
The Act nullifies any previous court judgments, decrees, or orders that were contrary to the collection of capital contribution.
No suit or other proceedings can be maintained or continued in any Court or Tribunal or before any authority for the refund of any capital contribution collected under this Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE SALARIES, PENSIONS AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To enhance the salaries and allowances of parliamentary functionaries and legislators, and certain other benefits by amending the Karnataka Legislature Salaries Act, 1956.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances Act, 1956, and therefore applies to the salaries, pensions, and allowances of legislators and parliamentary functionaries in Karnataka.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Legislature Salaries, Pensions and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it comes into force at once.
Amends sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 3 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'twelve thousand rupees' with 'thirty thousand rupees'.

Amends sub-section (1) of Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting 'twenty thousand rupees' with 'forty thousand rupees', and sub-section (2) by substituting 'five thousand rupees' with 'ten thousand rupees'.
Amends sub-section (2) of Section 5 of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres of petrol' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres of petrol'.
Amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres of petrol' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres of petrol'.

Amends sub-section (2) of Section 8 of the principal Act by substituting various amounts and multipliers, including 'twelve rupees' to 'twenty rupees', 'one and one fifth times' to 'one and one fourth times', and 'one thousand rupees' to 'two thousand rupees'.

Amends sub-section (1) of Section 10 of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees', and sub-section (2) by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'Seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends sub-section (1) and (2) of Section 10A of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of Section 10D of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends Section 10E of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends sub-section (2) of Section 10G of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of Section 10I of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends Section 10J of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 10K of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends sub-section (2) of Section 10L of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends sub-section (2) of Section 10M of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of Section 10N of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred litres' with 'seven hundred and fifty litres'.
Amends sub-section (1) of Section 11 of the principal Act by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 12 of the principal Act in various clauses, including substituting monetary values and multipliers related to allowances and salaries.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is responsible for the administration and likely enforcement of this act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and amendment of the provisions of the principal Act (The Karnataka Legislature Salaries Act, 1956) as outlined in this amendment act.

key_procedures: The primary procedure involves the substitution of specific monetary values and quantities within the principal Act, as detailed in each amendment section. This effectively changes the financial entitlements and allowances for legislators and parliamentary functionaries.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The act came into force immediately upon enactment.
The amendments are to the Karnataka Legislature Salaries Act, 1956 (Karnataka Act 2 of 1957).

The act was enacted during the Sixty-second year of the Republic of India and received the assent of the Governor on July 1, 2011. It was first published in the Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary on July 4, 2011.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, primarily to establish a Women's University at Bijapur to promote higher education among women in northern Karnataka and to facilitate its establishment and functioning.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000. It applies to the establishment of a Women's University with headquarters at Bijapur and its territorial jurisdiction over women's colleges and educational institutions in the state. The territorial jurisdiction for affiliation purposes specifically covers districts like Bagalkot, Belgaum, Bellary, Bidar, Bijapur, Dharward, Gadag, Gulbarga, Haveri, Koppal, Raichur, and Uttara Kannada.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and deems it to have come into force on June 21, 2003.

Inserts a new sub-section (1A) to establish a Women's University at Bijapur with specific territorial jurisdiction for women's educational institutions. It also amends sub-section (2) of section 3 of the principal Act.

Re-numbers section 5 as sub-section (1) and inserts a new sub-section (2). This sub-section deals with the transfer of privileges and affiliations for women's colleges and institutions from Gulbarga University or Karnataka University to the newly established Women's University.

Inserts a proviso to sub-section (1) of section 6, stating that the Women's University shall be open to all women irrespective of race, creed, caste, or class, and prohibiting any religious tests for admission or holding office.

Inserts further provisos to sub-section (4) of section 14. One proviso states that the Vice Chancellor of the Women's University shall, as far as practicable, be a woman. Another proviso states that the First Vice Chancellor shall be appointed by the State Government.

Inserts a proviso to sub-section (1) of section 28. For the Women's University, it mandates the inclusion of the Secretary in charge of the Women and Child Development Department (or their nominee not below the rank of Deputy Secretary) as an additional member of the Syndicate.

Inserts a proviso to sub-section (1) of section 30. For the Women's University, it mandates the inclusion of the Director, Women and Child Development, as an additional member of the Academic Council.

Inserts a proviso to sub-section (1) of section 32. For the Women's University, it mandates the inclusion of the Secretary in charge of the Women and Child Development Department (or their nominee not below the rank of Deputy Secretary) as an additional member of the Finance Committee.
Defines the powers and functions of a Special Officer appointed by the State Government for establishing the Women's University until the first Vice Chancellor is appointed.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of the First Vice Chancellor
main_sections.description: Outlines the duty of the first Vice Chancellor to make arrangements for constituting the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities within six months (or an extended period up to one year) and specifies when these authorities commence their functions.

Contains provisions for the functioning of the Women's University during its transitional phase, including the powers of the first Vice Chancellor and the continuation of statutes, ordinances, and rules from other universities until the Women's University makes its own.

Provides for the continuation of examinations and conferment of degrees/diplomas for students studying under Gulbarga University or Karnataka University, even after the commencement of the amendment act, until the Women's University makes its own provisions.
Empowers the State Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the amendment act, within a period of two years from its commencement.
Repeals the Karnataka State Universities (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003, and states that anything done or actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been done or taken under the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, appointment of officials, and by-laws/ordinances of the Universities.

rights: Women's colleges and educational institutions have the right to be affiliated to and admitted to the privileges of the Women's University.
Women have the right to be admitted as teachers or students to the Women's University without any religious test.
duties: Duty of the first Vice Chancellor to constitute University authorities.
Duty of the State Government to establish the Women's University and appoint officials.
obligations: Obligation to amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.
Obligation to integrate women's educational institutions into the Women's University framework.

key_procedures: Establishment of a Women's University at Bijapur.
Transfer of affiliations and privileges of women's colleges from existing universities to the Women's University.
Appointment of the First Vice Chancellor by the State Government.
Constitution of the Syndicate, Academic Council, and Finance Committee for the Women's University, including representation from the Women and Child Development Department.
Procedure for the Special Officer to exercise powers until the first Vice Chancellor is appointed.
Procedure for the first Vice Chancellor to constitute University authorities.
Procedure for the State Government to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act's enactment), and the administrative bodies of the Karnataka State Universities, particularly the newly established Women's University and the Women and Child Development Department.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on June 21, 2003.
The territorial jurisdiction for affiliation purposes is specific to certain districts.
The Vice Chancellor of the Women's University shall, as far as practicable, be a woman.
Transitory provisions are in place to ensure smooth functioning during the initial phase.

title: THE KARNATAKA PRIVATE MEDICAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007, to provide for the extension of time prescribed for the registration of existing Private Medical Establishments and the reconstitution of the District Level Registration Authority.
scope: This Act applies to Private Medical Establishments within the state of Karnataka, amending the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007 (Karnataka Act 21 of 2007).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2010, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting the words "Integrated medicine," after the word and comma "Yoga," in clause (l).

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. In the proviso, it substitutes the words "within three months from the date of the commencement of the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2010" for the words "within ninety days from the appointed day".

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. In clause (b), it substitutes "Member Secretary" for "Member". It also inserts new clauses (d) and (e) to include the District AYUSH officer and the President/Secretary of the AYUSH Federation of India of the concerned district as Members of the District Level Registration Authority.

important_rules: Rule 1: Existing Private Medical Establishments have an extended period of three months from the commencement of this Act for registration.

Rule 2: The District Level Registration Authority is reconstituted, with the inclusion of the District AYUSH officer and the President/Secretary of the AYUSH Federation of India of the concerned district as members.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Level Registration Authority (reconstituted)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amendments made to the principal Act regarding registration and the composition of the registration authority.

rights: Right of existing Private Medical Establishments to have an extended period for registration.
duties: Duty of Private Medical Establishments to register within the extended period.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Obtaining registration for existing Private Medical Establishments within three months from the commencement of the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2010.
Procedure 2: The functioning and composition of the District Level Registration Authority as amended by this Act.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (responsible for publishing the Act)
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007.
The amendment includes 'Integrated medicine' in the scope of covered medical establishments.
The amendment extends the registration deadline for existing establishments.

title: THE KARNATAKA MINISTERS SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To revise the salaries, house rent allowances, conveyance allowances, and the rates of Traveling Allowance and Dearness Allowance for the Chief Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers due to a considerable increase in the cost of living. The Act amends the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956.
scope: This Act applies to the Chief Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers in the State of Karnataka. It specifically amends provisions within the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2011, and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act (Karnataka Act 5 of 1957) by substituting the old monetary figures with revised ones for salary or allowances.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures in sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (2).
Amends Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (1), clause (a).
Amends Section 6A of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures.
Amends Section 6B of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures in sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 6C of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (2).
Amends Section 6D of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (1), clause (a).
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures.
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures in sub-sections (1) and (2).
Amends Section 9 of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (2).
Amends Section 10 of the principal Act by substituting the quantity of fuel (litres) in sub-section (1), clause (a).
Amends Section 12 of the principal Act by substituting monetary figures in sub-section (2), clauses (b) and (d), and the first proviso to clause (d).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be governmental authorities responsible for implementing and overseeing the salaries and allowances of ministers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956.

key_procedures: The Act mandates the substitution of specific monetary amounts and quantities within various sections of the Principal Act (Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956) to reflect revised allowances and salaries for ministers.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Ministers Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956 (Karnataka Act 5 of 1957).
The amendments are made to reflect the increase in the cost of living.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the first day of July, 2011, and was first published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on the fourth day of July, 2011.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, specifically to modify the provisions for the grant of surplus land to landless persons, other persons residing in villages within the same Panchayat area, and ex-military personnel, by revising the gross annual income limits for eligibility.
scope: This act applies to the state of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It specifically concerns the eligibility criteria for the grant of surplus land based on income and category of beneficiaries (landless persons, residents of the same Panchayat area, and ex-military personnel).

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

This section details the amendments to sub-section (1) of section 77 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It substitutes clause (iv) with new provisions regarding income limits for landless persons, other persons residing in villages in the same Panchayat area, and ex-military personnel, and omits clause (vi).

important_rules: Rule 1: Grant of surplus land to landless persons or other persons residing in villages in the same Panchayat area whose gross annual income does not exceed rupees twenty thousand.
Rule 2: Grant of surplus land to ex-military personnel whose gross annual income does not exceed rupees twenty-two thousand.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notifications for commencement and potentially other administrative actions related to land reforms).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through administrative action and implementation of the amended provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.

rights: Right to be considered for grant of surplus land for eligible landless persons, residents of the same Panchayat area, and ex-military personnel meeting the specified income criteria.
duties: Duty of the State Government to appoint a commencement date for the Act.
Duty of relevant authorities to implement the amended provisions of Section 77 of the Principal Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government, by notification, appoints a date on which this Act comes into force.

Procedure 2: Amendment of Section 77(1) of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, by substituting the existing clause (iv) and omitting clause (vi) to reflect the revised income criteria for land grants.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for drafting and enactment), and the relevant revenue/land reforms department for implementation.
important_notes: The Act has come into force on 1st day of November 2003, vide Notification No. RD 8 LRA 2001 (Part) dated 30.10.2003.
The amendment specifically revises the income thresholds for eligibility for surplus land grants, aiming to provide a consolidated and updated framework.

title: THE ALLIANCE UNIVERSITY ACT, 2010
purpose: To establish and incorporate in the State of Karnataka a University of Global Standards in the private sector that would be comparable to any in the world in so far as education, research and community service activities are concerned. It aims to bring about value knowledge by rendering quality education accessible to all and to set new benchmarks in an era of increasing globalization.
