scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the establishment of Alliance University, a private university, and its operations, including its campuses, regional centres, and study centres, which can be located anywhere in India or overseas with the permission of the concerned government.

key_definitions.University: The Alliance University established and incorporated under section 4.
key_definitions.Sponsoring Authority or Sponsoring Body: The Company, which is Alliance Business School Private Limited.
key_definitions.Company: Alliance Business School Private Limited, a company registered under section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956, or any other company formed and registered by the Promoters under section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.Constituent College: A college or institution maintained by the University.
key_definitions.Teacher: Includes a Distinguished Professor, Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, or Research Associate or such other person as may be appointed for imparting instruction or conducting or guiding research in the University or in a Constituent College, and includes the Principal of the Constituent College in conformity with the norms prescribed by the University Grants Commission.
key_definitions.National Accreditation Bodies: A body established by the Central Government for laying down norms and conditions for ensuring academic standards of higher education, such as University Grants Commission, All India Council of Technical Education, Medical Council of India, Pharmaceutical Council of India, Indian Council of Agriculture Research, National Assessment and Accreditation Council, National Council of Teacher Education, Distance Education Council, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, and includes the Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the 'Alliance University Act, 2010', its territorial extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and its commencement date to be appointed by the State Government by notification in the official Gazette.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Agenda Matters', 'Board of Governors', 'Board of Management', 'Chancellor', 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Pro Vice-Chancellor', 'Campus', 'Committees', 'Company', 'Constituent College', 'Distance Education', 'Distance Education Committee', 'Finance Committee', 'Government', 'National Accreditation Bodies', 'Prescribed', 'Principal', 'Registrar', 'Regional Centre', 'Sponsoring Authority' or 'Sponsoring Body', 'State', 'Statutes' and 'Regulations', 'Study Centre', 'Teacher', 'University Grants Commission', 'University', and 'Visitor' and 'Pro-Visitor'.

main_sections.section_title: Proposal for the establishment of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for proposing the establishment of the University, which must be done by the Company (promoters belonging to the Scheduled Tribe community) to the State Government. It details the required particulars for the proposal, including objects, extent, programmes, faculties, campus development, financial outlays, funding sources, fee structure, experience of the company, student selection system, and other conditions.

Describes the procedure for establishing the University. After the State Government is satisfied with the proposal and the company's ability to run a university, it directs the company to establish the Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund. Upon establishment of this fund, the State Government accords sanction for the establishment of the University by name 'Alliance University'. It also specifies the location of the headquarters, the possibility of campuses/regional/study centres, and that the University becomes a body corporate.

States that the University shall be self-financing and not entitled to any maintenance, grant-in-aid, or financial assistance from the State or state-controlled bodies. However, the State may provide financial support for research, development, specific research programs, or for the benefit of similar universities.
Grants the University the power to establish Constituent Colleges, Regional Centres, and Study Centres at such places in the State as it deems fit.

Details the objectives of the University, focusing on spreading quality education, teaching, training in Business, Education, and Management, and enhancing the gross enrolment ratio in higher education.

important_rules: The Company shall have the right to establish the University subject to and in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
The proposal to establish a University shall be made to the State Government by the Company (the promoters belong to the Scheduled Tribe community).

The University shall be self-financing and shall neither make a demand nor be entitled to any maintenance, grant-in-aid or any other financial assistance from the State or any other body or corporation owned or controlled by the State, with specific exceptions for research and development support.
The University may have Constituent Colleges, Regional Centres, and Study Centres at such places in the State as it deems fit.

rights: The Company has the right to establish the University.
The University has the power to establish constituent colleges, regional centres, and study centres.
The University as a body corporate can sue and be sued in its name.
Right to appeal (Section 40).
duties: The University must be established in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
The University must be self-financing.
The University's land, buildings, and other properties shall not be used for any other purpose.
The Registrar is responsible for signing and verifying pleadings and for service of process in suits and legal proceedings involving the University.
obligations: The Company must submit a detailed proposal to the State Government.
The Company must establish a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund before the University can be officially established.
The University must operate within its stated objects and powers.

key_procedures: Proposal for establishment: The Company submits a detailed proposal to the State Government, including specific particulars related to the university's objectives, finances, programs, and infrastructure.

Screening and Approval: A Screening Committee examines the proposal and makes recommendations to the State Government. The State Government, after inquiry, may direct the company to establish the Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund if satisfied.
Establishment of University: Upon establishment of the endowment fund, the State Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette sanctioning the establishment of Alliance University.
Incorporation: The Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, members of the Board of Governors, Board of Management, and Academic Council constitute a body corporate upon establishment.
Vesting of Property: All movable and immovable properties acquired by the University vest in the University upon its establishment.
administration: The State Government plays a key role in the establishment process and has the power to make rules. The University itself is administered by its own officers and authorities as outlined in Chapters III and IV of the Act.
important_notes: The university is promoted by an institution managed by a Scheduled Tribe Community.
The Act emphasizes the establishment of a private university focused on quality education, teaching, and training in Business, Education, and Management.
The university is intended to help increase the gross enrolment ratio in higher education in Karnataka.
The university is expected to be of 'Global Standards' and comparable to international institutions.
The Act provides for the establishment of a Permanent Statutory Endowment Fund.

The University's headquarters are decided by the Sponsoring Body, and it can have Campuses or Regional Centres and Study Centres anywhere in India or overseas, subject to the permission of the concerned government.

title: THE KARNATAKA PANCHAYATH RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Panchayath Raj Act, 1993, to give effect to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Krishnamurthy and others Vs Union of India, to give effect to the 13th Central Finance Commissions recommendations, and to make certain other consequential amendments.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Panchayath Raj Act, 1993. It applies to the Panchayath Raj Institutions in Karnataka, including Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats.

key_definitions.Panchayat Ombudsman: The Panchayat Ombudsman appointed by the State Government under section 296A, responsible for hearing grievances and complaints against elected members, officers, and officials of the Panchayat Raj Institutions.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Karnataka Panchayath Raj (Amendment) Act, 2011, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 4, 2010.
Inserts the definition of 'Panchayat Ombudsman' into section 2 of the principal Act.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in a Grama Panchayat does not exceed fifty percent of the total seats.

Amends section 44 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of offices of Adhyakshas and Upadhyakshas reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in Grama Panchayaths does not exceed fifty percent of the total offices in the State.
Amends section 111 of the principal Act, changing the designation of 'Secretary' to 'Panchayat Development Officer and other officers' and clarifying their appointment, salary, and allowances.

Amends section 123 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in a Taluk Panchayat does not exceed fifty percent of the total seats.

Amends section 138 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in Taluk Panchayaths does not exceed fifty percent of the total offices in the State.
Amends the proviso to section 160 of the principal Act to specify the population ratio for members in Uttara Kannada, Chickmagalur, Bangalore Urban, and Kodagu districts.

Amends section 162 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in a Zilla Panchayat does not exceed fifty percent of the total seats.

Amends section 177 of the principal Act to ensure that the total number of offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Backward Classes in Zilla Panchayaths does not exceed fifty percent of the total offices in the State.

Amends section 246 of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) clarifies the role of the Comptroller and Auditor General in auditing Grama Panchayat accounts. A new sub-section (12) is inserted, requiring the Controller of State Accounts Department to submit a consolidated Annual Report to the Government, which will be laid before the State Legislature.
Amends section 267 of the principal Act to substitute 'The Government shall' with 'The Governor shall' in sub-section (1).
Inserts new sections related to the Panchayat Ombudsman, defining its appointment, powers, functions, procedures for complaints and investigations, and matters not subject to investigation.
This section typically deals with the repeal of previous enactments and provisions for saving existing rights and actions. Specific details are not provided in the excerpt.

important_rules: Reservation of seats for Backward Classes in Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats, when combined with reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, shall not exceed fifty percent of the total seats.

Reservation of offices of Adhyakshas and Upadhyakshas for Backward Classes, when combined with reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, shall not exceed fifty percent of the total offices in Grama Panchayaths and Taluk Panchayaths.
The Panchayat Ombudsman has the power to investigate allegations against elected members, officers, and officials of Panchayat Raj Institutions.

Complaints to the Panchayat Ombudsman can involve omissions in duty, failures in service, negligence, improper performance, nepotism, favouritism, delays in disposal of applications, payments, meetings, selection of beneficiaries, and discharge of statutory functions.
The Panchayat Ombudsman has the powers of a civil court for investigation, including summoning witnesses, examining on oath, requiring production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Panchayat Ombudsman (for grievances and complaints against elected members, officers, and officials), State Government (for overall administration and reporting), The Governor (as substituted in section 267).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation by Panchayat Ombudsman, submission of reports to the Government, laying of consolidated annual reports before the State Legislature.

rights: Right of any person to make a complaint to the Panchayat Ombudsman against elected members, officers, or officials of Panchayat Raj Institutions.
Right to have grievances and complaints heard and investigated by the Panchayat Ombudsman.
duties: Duty of Panchayat Development Officer and Secretary to discharge their duties.
Duty of the Comptroller and Auditor General to provide technical guidance and supervision for audit of accounts.
Duty of the Controller of State Accounts Department to submit a consolidated Annual Report.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that reserved seats and offices do not exceed fifty percent of the total.
Obligation to assist the Panchayat Development Officer by the Secretary and other officials.
Obligation to not prejudice the affairs of the State or national security when disclosing information during investigations.

key_procedures: Appointment of Panchayat Ombudsman by the State Government.
Investigation of allegations and actions by Panchayat Ombudsman.
Submission of complaints involving grievances and allegations to the Panchayat Ombudsman.
Procedure for investigation by Panchayat Ombudsman, including requiring information and documents, summoning persons, and taking evidence.
Submission of reports by the Panchayat Ombudsman to the Government.
administration: State Government, with specific roles for Panchayat Development Officers, the Controller of State Accounts Department, and the Comptroller and Auditor General.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 4, 2010.

Certain provisions related to reservation of seats and offices for Backward Classes are subject to a fifty percent overall limit when combined with reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Disclosure of information that might prejudice the affairs of the State, national security, or Cabinet proceedings is not required during Ombudsman investigations.
Matters being investigated by the Lokayukta or Upa-lokayukta, or by a competent authority under other enactments, are not subject to investigation by the Panchayat Ombudsman.

title: The Karnataka Prison Development Board Act, 2021
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the 'Karnataka Prison Development Board' for strengthening of Prisons and Correctional administration, particularly correctional interventions, skill improvement, welfare of Prisoners and Prison Staff, and expanding Prison industries. It also aims to develop modern prison industries, formulate job-oriented technical programs, improve coordination between justice administration, police, probation, after-care, and prison administration, and modernize prison industries to prepare prisoners for life after release.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It governs the establishment and functioning of the Karnataka Prison Development Board, its powers, functions, and financial management, with the objective of improving prison conditions, correctional programs, and the welfare of prisoners and staff.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Prison Development Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Building: Includes a house, dormitory, barrack, cell, latrine, godown, factory shed, hut, wall or any other structure made of any material.
key_definitions.Commissioner: Commissioner of the Board, appointed as Director General of Prison.
key_definitions.Land: Includes rights in or over land and benefits arising from land, as well as buildings and structures attached to the earth.
key_definitions.Prison: Any prison or jail, including all appurtenant lands and buildings, used for the detention of prisoners, whether Central Prison, District Prison, Taluka Prison, Revenue Prison, Open Prison, Women Prison, or any other prison notified by the Government.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the official Gazette of the Government of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Prison Development Board Act, 2021, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Building', 'Chairperson', 'Commissioner', 'Government', 'Land', 'Prison', and 'Notification'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of the Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Prison Development Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition, including the Chairperson (Minister in-charge of Prison), Vice Chairperson (Additional Chief Secretary, Home Department), ex-officio members from various departments, and a Member-Secretary (Director General, Prisons and Correctional Services).

Details the functions of the Board, which include examining prisoner living conditions, improving coordination among criminal justice agencies, framing policies for prison products marketing, planning and implementing skill development and welfare programs, organizing prison industries on a commercial basis, improving the skills and welfare of prison staff, and undertaking programs for prisoner reform and re-assimilation into society.

Establishes the 'Prisons Development Fund' to be maintained by the Board, detailing the sources of funds (grants, loans, earnings from prison industries, disposal of property, donations, etc.) and its application towards the administration of the Act and other prescribed purposes.

Mandates the Board to maintain proper accounts and relevant records, prepare an Annual Statement of Accounts in a prescribed form, and specifies that the financial year of the Board is the same as the financial year of the Government.

important_rules: The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract.
The Board shall ordinarily meet at least once every three months.
The Commissioner shall be the Chief Controlling Authority of the Board in all matters connected with the administration of the Act.
The Board shall prepare a Budget and an Annual Report, and submit them to the Government.
The Board shall maintain proper accounts and prepare an Annual Statement of accounts for audit.
The Government may make grants, advances, and loans to the Board for the performance of its functions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka and the Karnataka Prison Development Board through its Commissioner and appointed staff.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functions and powers vested in the Board and its Commissioner as detailed in the Act, including the management of the Prison Development Fund, acquisition and disposal of property, and implementation of correctional and development programs. Section 21 provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

rights: Prisoners have the right to improved living conditions and correctional programs designed for re-assimilation into society.
Prison staff have the right to improved skills and welfare programs.
The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to contract.
The Board has the right to borrow funds and receive grants, advances, and loans from the Government.
duties: The Board has the duty to examine and improve prisoner living conditions.
The Board has the duty to suggest ways to improve coordination between criminal justice agencies.
The Board has the duty to plan, implement, and coordinate skill development and welfare programs for prisoners.
The Board has the duty to organize prison industries on a business-cum-commercial basis.
The Board has the duty to improve the skills and competency of prison officers and employees and ensure their welfare.
The Board has the duty to provide an enabling environment for prisoners to lead productive lives after release.
The Board has the duty to maintain proper accounts and prepare an annual report.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to establish the Board and may provide grants, advances, and loans.
The Commissioner has an obligation to act as the Chief Controlling Authority of the Board.
The Board is obligated to apply its funds towards the administration of the Act and other prescribed purposes.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Karnataka Prison Development Board by the Government through notification.
Convening meetings of the Board by the Member Secretary with the Chairperson's approval.
Preparation of an annual budget and an annual report by the Board, to be submitted to the Government.
Maintenance of proper accounts and preparation of an Annual Statement of accounts by the Board.
administration: The Government of Karnataka, with the Karnataka Prison Development Board acting as the primary administrative body. The Commissioner (Director General of Prison) is the Chief Controlling Authority.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.
No act or proceedings of the Board shall be invalidated due to vacancies or defects in its constitution or appointment of members.
The Board may delegate powers to the Commissioner.
The Government has the power to make rules and give directions to the Board.
The Act has overriding effects as specified in Section 23.

title: THE KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: To amend the Electricity Act, 1910, in its application to the State of Karnataka, to provide for the "The Eletrcitiy (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2001", and to amend the Eletrcitiy Act, 1910 (Central Act 9 of 1910) in its application to the State of Karnataka.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Electricity Act, 1910.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Eletrcitiy (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2001. It extends to the State of Karnataka. It came into effect on the eleventh day of December, 2001.
Inserts new sections 49B to 49I to the Electricity Act, 1910.
This section details the insertion of new sections into the principal Act concerning penalties and compounding of offences.

important_rules: Rule 1: Penalties for offences committed under the Act. Penalties include imprisonment and fines.

Rule 2: If any person commits an offence and is convicted for an offence punishable under this Act, it is debarred from getting any supply of energy for a term not less than three months and with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
Rule 3: If any person commits an offence and is convicted for an offence punishable under this Act, and with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

Rule 4: The person who commits an offence and is convicted for an offence punishable under this Act, shall not be less than three months and with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
Rule 5: For the compounding of offence by the specially empowered officer of the electricity utility for the first offence only.
Rule 6: For the compounding of offence by the specially empowered officer of the electricity utility for the first offence only.
Rule 7: For the compounding of offence by the specially empowered officer of the electricity utility for the first offence only.
Rule 8: For the compounding of offence by the specially empowered officer of the electricity utility for the first offence only.
Rule 9: For the compounding of offence by the specially empowered officer of the electricity utility for the first offence only.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than three months.
Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Specially empowered officer of the electricity utility.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act provides for penalties and compounding of offences. Offences can lead to imprisonment and fines. Compounding is allowed for the first offence.

rights: Right to receive energy supply from the electricity utility (subject to conditions).
duties: Duty to avoid electricity theft.
Duty to pay for energy consumed.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the amended Act.
Obligation to pay any compounded amount as per the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: If a person commits an offence, they may be subject to imprisonment and/or a fine.
Procedure 2: For a first offence, it may be compounded by a specially empowered officer of the electricity utility.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be related to the electricity sector and government departments responsible for electricity regulation in Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act amends the Electricity Act, 1910 (Central Act 9 of 1910).
The amendments are made applicable to the State of Karnataka.
The Act came into force on 11th December 2001.
Specific sections inserted include 49B to 49I.

title: THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND THE SCHEDULED TRIBES (PREVENTION OF ATTROCITIES) (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, in its application to the State of Karnataka, to authorize Courts of Sessions to take cognizance of offenses under this Act as a court of original jurisdiction for speedy trial and disposal of cases.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (Central Act 33 of 1989). It specifically deals with the jurisdiction of special courts for trying offenses under the Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2002, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

This section amends section 14 of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. It substitutes the words 'to try offences under this Act' with 'to take cognizance of offences under this Act as a court of original jurisdiction and to try such offences'.

important_rules: Rule 1: Special Courts under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, are authorized to take cognizance of offenses under the Act as a court of original jurisdiction.
Rule 2: Special Courts are empowered to try such offenses.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, through the appointment of Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By empowering Courts of Sessions to act as special courts with original jurisdiction for speedy trial of offenses under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The State Government issues a notification in the Official Gazette to appoint the date on which this Act comes into force.

Procedure 2: Courts of Sessions, designated as Special Courts, take cognizance of offenses under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, as courts of original jurisdiction.
Procedure 3: These Special Courts then try such offenses.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the signatory). The overall administration of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, would fall under relevant government departments responsible for law and social justice.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 30th September 2003, as per Notification No. HD 247 PCR 2000(P) dated 30.9.2003.
The amendment addresses a legal issue highlighted by the Supreme Court regarding the cognizance of cases by Courts of Session without commitment by a Magistrate, aiming for speedy trial.

title: THE KARNATAKA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, specifically to enable landowners to raise loans by mortgaging their lands for the higher studies of their children.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It applies to landowners in Karnataka who wish to mortgage their land for educational loans for their children's higher studies.

key_definitions.Higher studies: For the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 61, 'Higher studies' means further studies after Pre-university Examination or 12th Standard Examination conducted by CBSE or ICSE or any Diploma courses.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 61 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961. It inserts provisions to allow landowners to mortgage their land for raising educational loans for their children's higher studies and defines 'Higher studies'.

important_rules: Landowners can raise loans by mortgaging or creating a charge on their interest in the land for the higher studies of their children.
Higher studies are defined as further studies after Pre-university Examination or 12th Standard Examination (CBSE/ICSE) or any Diploma courses.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, and its amendments are enforced by the relevant state authorities responsible for land revenue and land reforms in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, which includes registration of mortgages and charges, and adherence to the conditions for raising loans.

rights: Right of landowners to mortgage their land for educational loans for their children's higher studies.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, when mortgaging land for loans.
Duty to ensure that loans raised are for the specified purpose (higher studies of children).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the definition of 'Higher studies' as defined in the act.
Obligation to fulfill any conditions stipulated by financial institutions for granting loans against land mortgage.

key_procedures: Mortgaging of land by landowners for raising educational loans.
Raising of educational loans by landowners for their children's higher studies.
Enforcement of the amended provisions of Section 61 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Karnataka), and likely the Department of Revenue, Government of Karnataka for the implementation of land reforms.
important_notes: This amendment specifically expands the purpose for which a landowner can mortgage their land, previously limited to land development and improvement of agricultural practices.
The definition of 'Higher studies' is crucial for determining the eligibility of the loan purpose.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE MINORITIES COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994, to provide for nomination of members with a minimum degree from a recognized University, ensure representation from Christian, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh communities, change the payment to members from salary and allowances to allowances only, and add the function of recommending implementation of the Prime Minister's new 15 Point Programme.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994. It applies to the Karnataka State Minorities Commission and its members. The subject matter scope includes the composition, nomination, and functions of the Commission.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994 (Karnataka Act 31 of 1994).
key_definitions.minority community: Refers to communities designated as minorities within the state.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka State Minorities Commission (Amendment) Act, 2011, and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act to redefine the composition of the Commission. It specifies that the Chairman must be from a minority community, and eight other members must hold a degree from a recognized university, with at least one member each from Christian, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh communities. It also defines the Secretary as a government officer not below the rank of Deputy Secretary.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act concerning the payment to members. It substitutes provisions to state that the Chairman shall receive salary and allowances, while other members shall receive only allowances as prescribed. It also clarifies that 'other members' in sub-section (4) refers to 'allowances payable to other members'.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (bb) which adds the function to the Commission of making recommendations for implementing the Prime Minister's new 15 Point Programme.

Amends section 17 of the principal Act by substituting clause (b) of sub-section (2). This amendment specifies that the rules made by the government may provide for the salary, allowances, and other emoluments payable to the Chairman, and the allowances payable to other members of the Commission, along with other conditions of service.

important_rules: Rule 1: Members of the Commission, excluding the Chairman, must possess a minimum degree from a recognized University.
Rule 2: The Commission must have at least one member each from the Christian, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh communities among the eight other members.
Rule 3: The Chairman shall receive salary and allowances, while other members shall only receive allowances as prescribed.
Rule 4: The Commission is empowered to make recommendations for implementing the Prime Minister's new 15 Point Programme.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Karnataka and the Karnataka State Minorities Commission itself, through its functions and recommendations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994, including the Commission's ability to make recommendations and the Government's role in prescribing rules regarding salaries, allowances, and conditions of service.

rights: Members (including the Chairman) have a right to receive prescribed allowances (and salary for the Chairman).
Minority communities have a right to representation on the Commission.
The Commission has the right to make recommendations for implementing the Prime Minister's new 15 Point Programme.
duties: The Government has the duty to appoint the Secretary to the Commission.
The Commission has a duty to perform its functions, including making recommendations.
Members of the Commission have a duty to fulfill their roles as members.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to prescribe the salary, allowances, and other conditions of service for the Chairman and other members.
The Government has an obligation to ensure the Commission has appropriate representation from minority communities.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Nomination of Commission Members - The Chairman must be a person of a minority community, and eight other members must hold a degree from a recognized university, with specific representation from Christian, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh communities.
Procedure 2: Payment to Members - The Chairman receives salary and allowances, while other members receive only allowances as prescribed by the Government.
Procedure 3: Additional Function - The Commission can make recommendations for implementing the Prime Minister's new 15 Point Programme.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (Government of Karnataka), and the Karnataka State Minorities Commission.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994.
The amendment focuses on enhancing the representation and scope of functions of the Commission.
The provisions for salary and allowances are subject to prescription by the Government.

title: THE KARNATAKA IRRIGATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965, specifically to introduce restrictions on the alienation of certain lands that benefit from irrigation projects to ensure that the benefits accrue to the original landholder.
scope: This act applies to lands in Karnataka that are irrigated from major or medium irrigation projects. It restricts the transfer of such lands by sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, or otherwise without prior permission from the Irrigation Officer, for a period not exceeding ten years from a date specified by the Chief Engineer. The scope is also subject to the conditions outlined in the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Act, 2003, and states that it is deemed to have come into force from June 6, 2003.

Inserts a new section, 27A, into the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965. This new section imposes restrictions on the alienation of certain lands after the commencement of construction of any irrigation work for such lands.

Repeals the Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 (Karnataka Ordinance 2 of 2003) and clarifies that any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: No owner of land benefiting from a major or medium irrigation project shall transfer their land by way of sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange, or otherwise for a period not exceeding ten years from a date to be specified, without prior permission of the Irrigation Officer.
Rule: The Irrigation Officer may grant permission for transfer of land based on guidelines issued by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Irrigation Officer (for granting permission for land transfer)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By requiring prior permission from the Irrigation Officer for any transfer of land that falls under the purview of Section 27A.

rights: Right of original landholders to benefit from irrigation projects.
Right to seek permission from the Irrigation Officer for land transfer.
duties: Duty of landowners to obtain prior permission before transferring land that benefits from irrigation projects.
obligations: Obligation not to transfer land by sale, mortgage, lease, gift, exchange or otherwise without prior permission for a period not exceeding ten years, after the commencement of construction of any irrigation work to irrigate the land.

key_procedures: Procedure: A landowner seeking to transfer land that benefits from an irrigation project must first apply for and obtain permission from the Irrigation Officer.
Procedure: The Irrigation Officer will consider issuing permission based on State Government guidelines.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act itself), Irrigation Officer and Chief Engineer (for implementation and enforcement related to irrigation works and land transfer).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force with effect from June 6, 2003.
The restriction on land transfer is for a period not exceeding ten years from a date to be specified by notification.
This amendment is a replacement of the Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, primarily to enhance the number of standing committees for the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and to define their functions.
scope: This act applies to the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and other Municipal Corporations in Karnataka, as it amends the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. It specifically deals with the structure and functions of Standing Committees within these corporations.

key_definitions.Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike: The Greater Bangalore Municipal Corporation, formed by increasing the number of wards.
key_definitions.Principal Act: The Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1977).

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2010, and it shall come into force at once.

This section amends section 11 of the principal Act to substitute the existing sub-sections (1-A) and (2). It specifies the composition and number of Standing Committees for the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike (twelve committees) and for other Corporations (seven Councillors each). It also details the election process for these committees and includes a proviso for representation of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in specific committees.

This section amends section 61A of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1). It outlines the specific functions to be performed by each of the twelve Standing Committees of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike.
This section amends section 88 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'or establishment and administrative reforms' after 'taxation, finance and appeals' in sub-section (1).

important_rules: For the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, there shall be twelve specific Standing Committees listed in section 2(1-A).
Each Standing Committee for Corporations other than Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike shall consist of seven Councillors.
Each Standing Committee for Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike shall consist of eleven Councillors, elected by proportional representation with the single transferable vote.
The Standing Committees for public health, education, and social justice (or social justice alone) must include at least two Councillors from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Specific functions are assigned to each of the twelve Standing Committees of the Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike as detailed in section 3.
Section 88 is amended to include 'establishment and administrative reforms' in the scope of taxation, finance, and appeals committees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the relevant authorities within the Municipal Corporations established under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

duties: Standing Committees are responsible for performing their assigned functions as detailed in section 3.
Councillors have a duty to elect Standing Committee members according to the principles of proportionate representation.

key_procedures: Election of Standing Committees: Elected at the first meeting of the corporation after general elections and at the first meeting in the same month each succeeding year, using the principle of proportionate representation by means of the single transferable vote.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is responsible for the enactment and promulgation of this Act.
important_notes: The amendment is necessitated by the reconstitution of the Bangalore Maha Nagara Palike as Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike with an increased number of wards.
The Act is enacted based on Entry 5 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.

title: THE KARNATAKA REPEALING (REGIONAL LAWS) ACT, 2011
purpose: To repeal certain regional laws in force in various areas of the State of Karnataka and to amend certain other laws in force in the State, based on the recommendations of a One Man Committee to repeal obsolete regional acts.
scope: The Act applies to regional laws that were in force in the former States of Bombay, Coorg, Hyderabad, Madras, and Mysore immediately before November 1, 1956, and continued in force in the respective areas now part of Karnataka. It repeals specific laws listed in the Schedule.

key_definitions.regional_laws: Laws in force in the former States of Bombay, Coorg, Hyderabad, Madras and Mysore immediately before 1st November 1956, and continued in force under section 119 of the States Reorganization Act 1956 in the respective Areas of those States which are now part of Karnataka State.
key_definitions.schedule: A schedule annexed to this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Repealing (Regional Laws) Act, 2011, and states that it comes into force at once.
Defines 'regional laws' and 'Schedule' for the purposes of the Act.
States that the regional laws specified in the Schedule, as in force in the respective Areas of the State, are hereby repealed.

Provides for various savings and clarifications regarding the effect of the repeal, including that it does not affect other laws, things already done, acquired rights or liabilities, existing principles of law, or proceedings initiated under the repealed laws. It also clarifies the effect on amendments and validations made by the repealed laws and states that Sections 6, 8, and 24 of the Karnataka General Clauses Act, 1899 shall be applicable.

important_rules: The repeal of any regional law shall not affect any other law in which the repealed law has been applied, incorporated, or referred to.

The repeal shall not affect the validity, invalidity, effect, or consequences of anything already done or suffered, or any right, title, obligation, or liability already acquired, accrued, or incurred.
The repeal shall not affect any proceedings initiated or to be initiated under a repealed law before any court or other authority to challenge or enforce rights conferred by that law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned for the repeal act itself, but enforcement would have pertained to the original laws that are now repealed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not applicable as the act's primary function is repeal.

rights: Continuance of rights, titles, obligations, or liabilities already acquired, accrued, or incurred prior to the repeal.
Continuation of proceedings to enforce rights conferred by repealed laws.
obligations: Continuance of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred prior to the repeal.

key_procedures: Identification and recommendation of obsolete regional laws by a One Man Committee.
Enactment of the Repealing Act to repeal the identified laws.
Application of savings provisions to ensure continuity of certain legal effects and proceedings.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The Act repeals numerous regional laws from various historical areas of Karnataka, including Belgaum, Coorg, Gulbarga, Mangalore, Kollegal, and Mysore.
The Savings section (Section 4) is extensive and aims to prevent unintended consequences of repealing these historical laws.

title: THE KARNATAKA PANCHAYAT RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, to introduce Ward Sabhas and Grama Sabhas with enhanced responsibilities, to provide for disqualification for failure to lodge election expenses, to ensure representation of women in meetings, to require disclosure of pecuniary interests, to make the Adhyaksha of Grama Panchayat an executive head, to redefine the powers of the Secretary of Grama Panchayat, to pool state civil services for Grama Panchayats, to transfer powers related to delimitation and reservations to the State Election Commission, to require asset declarations from Taluk and Zilla Panchayat members, to provide for the Chairman of the Social Justice Standing Committee to act in vacant Adhyaksha/Upadhyaksha positions, and to facilitate maintenance and lodging of election expenses accounts.
scope: This Act amends the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, and applies to all Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats within the state of Karnataka. It covers aspects of their functioning, composition, and the roles and responsibilities of their members and the electorate.

key_definitions.Ward Sabha: A body consisting of persons registered in the voters list of each Grama Panchayat constituency.
key_definitions.Grama Sabha: A body comprising all the registered voters in a Grama Panchayat area, with specific meeting and quorum requirements and delegated powers and functions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date notified by the Government, with different provisions potentially having different commencement dates.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting 'voters list of a Gramapanchayat' for 'electoral roll relating to a village comprised within the area of Grama panchayat' in clause (16) and inserting a new clause (42A) defining 'Ward Sabha'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of Chapter II and section 3
main_sections.description: Substitutes the entire Chapter II and section 3 of the principal Act with provisions establishing Ward Sabha and Grama Sabha, detailing their meeting schedules, quorum, representation of women and Scheduled Castes/Tribes, and their respective powers and functions.

important_rules: Ward Sabhas must meet at least once every six months. The quorum is one-tenth of total members or twenty members, whichever is less, with at least thirty percent women attendees. Scheduled Castes and Tribes should be represented proportionally.

Grama Sabhas must meet at least once every six months. A special meeting can be convened upon a request from at least ten percent of members with specified agenda items. The quorum is one-tenth of total members or one hundred members, whichever is less, with at least ten members from each Ward Sabha and at least thirty percent women attendees. Scheduled Castes and Tribes should be represented proportionally.
Members of Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats are required to disclose any pecuniary interest they have in any matter coming before a meeting of these bodies.
Members of Taluk Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats must declare their assets, with provisions for cessation of membership for filing false or incorrect declarations.
Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Zilla Panchayats must strive to have at least one-third women members attending their meetings.

rights: Right to participate in Ward Sabha and Grama Sabha meetings.
Right to information from Grama Panchayat officers regarding services and proposed works.
Right to information on the rationale of Grama Panchayat decisions concerning their area.
Right to information on follow-up actions taken on Ward Sabha decisions.
duties: Duty to generate proposals and determine priorities for development schemes.
Duty to identify eligible beneficiaries for welfare schemes.
Duty to verify eligibility for welfare assistance.
Duty to provide and mobilize voluntary labour and contributions for development work.
Duty to supervise development works through volunteer teams.
Duty to make efforts to ensure members pay taxes and repay loans.
Duty to suggest locations for public amenities.
Duty to identify deficiencies in public amenities and suggest remedial measures.
Duty to impart awareness on matters of public interest (cleanliness, environment, pollution).
Duty to assist Grama Panchayat employees in sanitation and garbage removal.
Duty to promote adult education programs.
Duty to assist public health centers, especially in disease prevention and family welfare.
Duty to create arrangements for reporting epidemics and natural calamities.
Duty to promote harmony and unity among groups.
Duty to arrange cultural festivals and sports meets.
Duty to conserve and maintain public properties.
Duty to take action to prevent discrimination.
Duty to direct Grama Panchayaths not to grant licenses for certain prejudicial activities.
Duty to identify child labourers and take action.
obligations: Obligation to register in the voters list for Ward Sabha.
Obligation to attend Ward Sabha and Grama Sabha meetings (as per quorum requirements).
Obligation to pay taxes and repay loans to the Grama Panchayat (persuaded by Ward Sabha/Grama Sabha).
Obligation for members of Taluk and Zilla Panchayats to declare assets.

key_procedures: Convening and conducting meetings of Ward Sabha as prescribed.
Generating proposals and determining priority of schemes at the Ward Sabha level and forwarding them to Grama Sabha.
Identifying and preparing lists of eligible beneficiaries for schemes at the Ward Sabha level and forwarding them to Grama Panchayat.
Disseminating information on development and welfare programmes at the Grama Sabha level.
Approving the annual plan prepared by the Grama Panchayat at the Grama Sabha level.
Selecting eligible beneficiaries for schemes at the Grama Sabha level based on criteria and priority lists from Ward Sabhas.
Reporting the incidence of epidemics and natural calamities quickly.
administration: The administration of the Act would fall under the purview of the Panchayati Raj Department of the Karnataka State Government, with the State Election Commission also playing a role in specific electoral matters.
important_notes: The Act aims to make people's participation at the village level more meaningful and intense.
Disqualification for failure to lodge election expenses is for a period of three years.
The Act seeks to ensure that women constitute at least one-third of the attendees in Grama Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, and Zilla Panchayat meetings.
The State Election Commission is entrusted with powers related to determining elected members, reservation of seats, and delimitation of territorial constituencies for Taluk and Zilla Panchayats.

title: The Karnataka Information Technology Investment Regions Act, 2010
purpose: To provide for the establishment of information technology investment regions in the State of Karnataka to promote investment and to augment exports and generate employment in the Information Technology (IT), Information Technology enabled services (ITES), and Electronic Hardware manufacturing (EHM) units.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It specifically concerns the declaration and development of Information Technology Investment Regions (ITIRs) which are planned areas for IT/ITES and EHM units, including associated services, infrastructure, residential, commercial, and social facilities.

key_definitions.Authority: The Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board, Karnataka Housing Board, or any other authority empowered to acquire land.
key_definitions.Board: The Management Board constituted under section 8 of the Act.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer of the Management Board.
key_definitions.Developer or Co-developer: A Developer or Co-developer selected by the State Government through a transparent mechanism.
key_definitions.Feasibility report: A report prepared for the declaration of ITIRs, including area demarcation, infrastructure needs, land use patterns, master plan, and cost estimates.
key_definitions.High Powered Committee: The High Powered Committee constituted by the Government of India for ITIRs.
key_definitions.Information Technology Investment Region: Regions declared under section 3 of the Act for promoting investment in IT/ITES and EHM units.
key_definitions.Nodal Department: The Department of Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology of the State Government.
key_definitions.Policy Resolution: The policy resolution for setting up ITIRs issued by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, Government of India on 28th May 2008.
key_definitions.State Level Empowered Committee: The committee constituted under Section 12 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Karnataka Information Technology Investment Regions Act, 2010' and states it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Authority, Board, Chief Executive Officer, Developer, Feasibility report, High Powered Committee, ITIRs, Nodal Department, Policy Resolution, and State Level Empowered Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of Information Technology Investment Regions
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for declaring ITIRs, including identification of suitable locations, preparation of project proposals with feasibility reports (including area demarcation, infrastructure needs, land use, master plan, and cost estimates), obtaining approval from the Central Government, and subsequent notification by the State Government. It specifies the characteristics of ITIRs, such as minimum area, composition of processing and non-processing areas, and the possibility of including SEZs or industrial parks. It also details the role of Developers/Co-developers in infrastructure development and the State Government's responsibility for external linkages and public amenities.

main_sections.section_title: Infrastructure Facilities to be provided by the State Government
main_sections.description: Specifies the infrastructure facilities the State Government shall provide within ITIRs, including power, water, road and mass transit connectivity, sewerage, effluent treatment, and facilities for health, safety, environment, residential, educational, commercial, recreational, and socio-cultural needs. It also mentions adherence to Ministry of Environment and Forest norms and the role of the Developer and Central Government in providing these facilities.
Empowers the State Government to notify additional incentive packages for the development of ITIRs and for units established within them.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of Land for Information Technology Investment Regions
main_sections.description: Details the process for acquiring land for ITIRs, either by the State Government under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, or through an Authority, with acquisition expenses potentially borne by the Developer/Co-developer. The acquired land is transferred to and vests with the Management Board.

main_sections.section_title: Allotment of Land by the Management Board
main_sections.description: States that the Management Board shall transfer land to Developers for development purposes as per the master plan, subject to prescribed terms and conditions. Developers are then required to sell at least seventy-five percent of the developed land to entrepreneurs within a prescribed time.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Management Board and its Functions
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Management Board for each ITIR, with the Minister in-charge of Information Technology and Bio Technology as Chairman, and includes Principal Secretaries from various departments as members. The section also outlines the functions of this Board.
Deals with the establishment and management of the Board's Fund.
Specifies penalties for contraventions of the Act or its rules.

main_sections.section_title: Resumption of the possession of premises including the residential tenements on breach of terms or conditions of lease or holding without authority
main_sections.description: Details provisions for the resumption of possession of premises in case of breach of lease terms or unauthorized holding.
States that this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws in certain circumstances.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Management Board the power to make regulations for the efficient administration of the Act.

important_rules: Rule: ITIRs must have a minimum area of forty square kilometers.
Rule: A minimum of forty percent of the total designated area of an ITIR must be a processing area.
Rule: Developers must sell at least seventy-five percent of the developed land to entrepreneurs within a prescribed time.
Rule: The State Government shall provide essential infrastructure and public amenities within ITIRs.
Rule: Land acquired for ITIRs vests with the Management Board.

penalties: Penalties are specified in Chapter VI of the Act.
Resumption of possession of premises for breach of lease terms or unauthorized holding.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Management Board and the State Government are the primary authorities for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties, resumption of premises, and other legal measures as prescribed by the Act and rules made thereunder.

rights: Right of entrepreneurs to acquire developed land from developers.
Right to use common infrastructure and support services within ITIRs, subject to payment.
Benefits available under relevant Acts for SEZs, Industrial Parks, etc., forming part of ITIRs shall continue.
duties: Duty of the State Government to provide infrastructure and facilities.
Duty of the Developer to develop land according to the master plan and sell to entrepreneurs.
Duty of users to pay for the use of infrastructure.
Duty to adhere to norms and standards prescribed by the Ministry of Environment and Forest.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to obtain Central Government approval for ITIR proposals.
Obligation of the Developer to select through a transparent mechanism.
Obligation to ensure proper implementation of the Master Plan for declared land.

key_procedures: Procedure: Declaration of ITIRs involving identification of location, techno-economic survey, feasibility report preparation, proposal submission to Central Government, and notification by State Government.
Procedure: Acquisition of land for ITIRs by the State Government or Authority and subsequent transfer to the Management Board.
Procedure: Allotment of developed land by the Management Board to Developers and subsequent sale by Developers to entrepreneurs.
Procedure: Constitution of the Management Board with specified members.
administration: The Nodal Department is the Department of Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology of the State Government. The Management Board is constituted for each ITIR.
important_notes: Note: The first phase of development in an ITIR shall not exceed twenty percent of the notified area.
Note: ITIRs can include existing settlements, industries, and estates, benefiting from and complementing the region.
Note: The Act has an overriding effect, implying its provisions will prevail over other laws in case of conflict.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, to provide for a provision to extend the benefit of tax concession to Central Government employees, defence personnel, employees of Central Government undertakings including nationalised banks, who bring their vehicles to the State of Karnataka on transfer, provided they have already paid life time tax or quarterly or annual tax in other States or Union territories.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and applies to motor vehicles brought into the State of Karnataka by certain categories of employees on transfer. It specifically concerns the taxation of these vehicles.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Second Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting provisions to extend tax concessions to vehicles brought into Karnataka by Central Government employees, defence personnel, and employees of Central Government undertakings including nationalised banks, if lifetime, quarterly, or annual tax has already been paid in other states or union territories.

Substitutes a proviso in section 4(1) of the principal Act concerning tax rates for specific types of three-wheelers, motor cycles, motor cars, omni buses, and private service vehicles. It reiterates the tax concession for vehicles brought by Central Government employees, defence personnel, and employees of Central Government undertakings including nationalised banks, where tax was already paid elsewhere. It also specifies the period for which tax is paid and the timeframe for paying subsequent taxes.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act, specifically in Part-A, items No. 1 and 14. It inserts wording to extend the tax concession benefits to vehicles brought into the State of Karnataka on transfer by Central Government employees, defence personnel, and employees of Central Government undertakings including nationalised banks, for which tax has already been paid in other states or union territories.

important_rules: Rule 1: For vehicles brought to the State of Karnataka on transfer by Central Government employees, defence personnel, and employees of Central Government undertakings (including nationalised banks), if lifetime, quarterly, or annual tax has already been paid in other states or union territories, the tax concession benefit is extended.

Rule 2: Tax for certain categories of vehicles (three-wheelers, motor cycles, motor cars, omni buses, private service vehicles) will be levied after the expiry of the period for which tax was previously paid, and the new tax must be paid within one month of the expiry date.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the relevant motor vehicles taxation authorities in Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but enforcement would typically involve verification of tax payments and compliance with the amended provisions.

rights: Right to claim tax concession on bringing a vehicle to Karnataka on transfer if taxes were paid in another state/union territory (for eligible employees).
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicles tax in Karnataka as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty to pay the renewed tax within one month of the expiry of the previously paid tax period for certain vehicle categories.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Claiming tax concession: Eligible employees bringing vehicles on transfer to Karnataka need to demonstrate proof of payment of lifetime, quarterly, or annual tax in other states or union territories.
Procedure 2: Renewal of tax: For specified vehicle categories, tax is levied after the expiry of the existing tax period and must be paid within one month of that expiry.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for drafting and enactment), and the relevant motor vehicles taxation department in Karnataka (for administration and enforcement).
important_notes: The amendment applies to vehicles brought to Karnataka on transfer by Central Government employees, defence personnel, and employees of Central Government undertakings including nationalised banks.
The tax concession is contingent upon the motor vehicle tax having been paid in another state or union territory.
The act clarifies tax provisions for specific vehicle types including three-wheelers, motorcycles, motor cars, omni buses, and private service vehicles.

title: THE KARNATAKA EXCISE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, with the objectives of removing ambiguity in definitions, providing for interim custody of seized property upon bank guarantee, and allowing for acceptance of money or imposition of penalty in lieu of license cancellation or suspension for contraventions.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965. It specifically addresses matters related to toddy, excise trees, seized property under Section 43A, and contraventions of license conditions or rules made under the Act.

key_definitions.toddy: The definition of 'toddy' in Section 2 of the Principal Act is amended by omitting the words 'of which contains alcohol and' from the definition of 'excise tree'.
key_definitions.excise_tree: The definition of 'excise tree' in Section 2 of the Principal Act is amended by omitting the words 'of which contains alcohol and'.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Excise (Amendment) Act, 2003' and states that it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, by omitting the words 'of which contains alcohol and' from clause (11A) (definition of excise tree).

Inserts a proviso to Section 43A of the Principal Act, allowing the authorized officer to release seized property (except excisable articles) to the owner on production of a Bank Guarantee equal to its value, pending final disposal of proceedings. Excisable articles can be released to owners with a valid license under similar conditions.

Inserts a new section 45B into the Principal Act, titled 'Special provision to accept money or to impose penalty in lieu of cancellation or suspension of licence'. This section allows the Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or specially empowered Excise Officer to accept money or impose a penalty in lieu of canceling or suspending a license for contravention of conditions or rules, provided the holder is given notice and an opportunity to be heard.

important_rules: Rule 1: Owners of seized property (except excisable articles) can get interim custody by providing a Bank Guarantee equal to the property's value, and executing a bond for its production if required.
Rule 2: Owners of seized excisable articles can get interim custody if they possess a valid license under the Act, by providing a Bank Guarantee and executing a bond.
Rule 3: A license holder, whose license is liable for cancellation or suspension due to contravention, can apply to have money accepted or a penalty imposed in lieu of such action.
Rule 4: No order imposing a penalty under Section 45B can be made without giving the license holder written notice of the grounds and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
Rule 5: A person from whom money is accepted or on whom a penalty is imposed under Section 45B is not liable for prosecution for the same facts under the Act.

penalties: A sum of money may be accepted by the Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or specially empowered Excise Officer from a license holder in lieu of cancellation or suspension of the license.

A penalty may be imposed by the Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or specially empowered Excise Officer in lieu of cancellation or suspension of the license, not exceeding the amount or penalty provided in the relevant rule or license conditions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or any Excise Officer specially empowered in this behalf.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through acceptance of money or imposition of penalties in lieu of license cancellation or suspension for contravention of license conditions or rules. Enforcement also involves the interim release of seized property upon Bank Guarantee and the requirement for license holders to be heard before penalties are imposed.

rights: Right to apply for acceptance of money or imposition of penalty in lieu of license cancellation or suspension.
Right to be given written notice of the grounds for proposed penalty and a reasonable opportunity of being heard before a penalty is imposed.
Right to obtain interim custody of seized property (except excisable articles) by providing a Bank Guarantee and executing a bond.
Right to obtain interim custody of seized excisable articles if a license is possessed, by providing a Bank Guarantee and executing a bond.
duties: Duty to comply with the conditions of the license and any rules made under the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965.
Duty to produce seized property or excisable articles if and when required by the authorized officer, after obtaining interim custody.
Duty to provide a Bank Guarantee from a Scheduled Bank for a sum equal to the value of the seized property, as estimated by the authorized officer, for its interim release.
Duty to execute a bond for the production of seized property or excisable articles.
obligations: Obligation to pay a sum of money or penalty in lieu of license cancellation or suspension when applicable.
Obligation to ensure that seized property is available for final disposal proceedings when interim custody is granted.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: When a license holder or employee contravenes license conditions or rules, and the license is liable for cancellation/suspension: The license holder can apply to accept money. In other cases, the Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or empowered officer can impose a penalty, not exceeding prescribed limits, after giving notice and an opportunity to be heard.

Procedure 2: For seized property (including excisable articles): The authorized officer may release the seized property (except excisable articles) to the owner upon production of a Bank Guarantee equal to the value of the property and execution of a bond for its production. Excisable articles can be released to owners possessing a license under similar conditions (Bank Guarantee and bond).
administration: The Excise Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or any Excise Officer specially empowered in this behalf are involved in the administration and enforcement of the provisions related to penalties and license contraventions. The 'authorised officer' is responsible for the release of seized property.
important_notes: The amendment aims to provide flexibility in dealing with minor contraventions of excise laws by allowing for financial settlements instead of drastic actions like license cancellation or suspension.
The provision for releasing seized property upon Bank Guarantee is intended to ease the burden on property owners while ensuring the property remains available for legal proceedings.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To reduce the lifetime tax for construction equipment vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators from ten percent to six percent of the cost of the vehicle and to provide for the payment of this tax in two equal installments.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It specifically applies to construction equipment vehicles (as defined in the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989) and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators operating within Karnataka.

key_definitions.construction equipment vehicles: Vehicles as defined in clause (ca) of rule 2 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Second Amendment) Act, 2010, and deems it to have come into force from April 1, 2010.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso allowing lifetime tax for construction equipment vehicles and vehicles with air compressors/generators to be paid in two equal installments: half at the time of tax due or registration, and the balance within six months of the first installment.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act, stating that registered owners who have paid tax in part under the new provision in Section 4 are not entitled to a refund unless the tax is paid in full.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by substituting the lifetime tax rate for specific vehicles in Part A7, Sl. No. A, from '10 percent of cost of the vehicle' to '6 percent of the cost of the vehicle'.

important_rules: Rule 1: Lifetime tax for construction equipment vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators can be paid in two equal installments. The first installment is half the tax amount, payable at the time of tax due or registration. The second installment is the remaining balance, payable within six months of the first installment.
Rule 2: No refund of tax will be granted if the tax has been paid in part, unless the full tax amount has been paid.
Rule 3: The lifetime tax rate for the specified vehicles has been reduced from 10% to 6% of the cost of the vehicle.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement is implicitly handled by the authorities responsible for motor vehicles taxation in Karnataka, as governed by the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection and monitoring of motor vehicle taxes as per the provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, and its amendments.

rights: Right to pay lifetime tax in two equal installments for specified vehicles.
duties: Duty to pay the first installment of lifetime tax at the time of tax due or registration.
Duty to pay the second installment of lifetime tax within six months of the first installment.
Duty to ensure the full tax is paid to be eligible for any potential refunds (though the act focuses on preventing partial refunds).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the amended tax rates and payment schedules for construction equipment vehicles and vehicles fitted with air compressors and generators.

key_procedures: Procedure for payment of lifetime tax: 1. Determine the applicable lifetime tax rate (now 6% of the vehicle cost). 2. Pay 50% of the determined tax at the time of tax due or registration. 3. Pay the remaining 50% within six months from the date of the first installment payment.
administration: Department of Finance, Government of Karnataka (as responsible for taxation matters).
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2010.
Refunds are not permissible if the tax is paid in part; full payment is required.

title: THE KARNATAKA SOCIETIES REGISTRATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, to provide a time limit for the Registrar to accept or reject amendments to the rules and regulations submitted by a society, and to allow for condonation of delay in submission of resolutions.
scope: This act applies to societies registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, within the state of Karnataka. It specifically amends provisions related to the registration of amendments to the rules and regulations of these societies.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Societies Registration (Amendment) Act, 2011, and that it shall come into force at once.
