Amends section 10 of the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, by substituting sub-section (2). The amended sub-section (2) stipulates that every amendment made under sub-section (1) shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days. If the Registrar is satisfied that the amendment is in accordance with the Act and rules, he shall register it, and it will have effect from the date of the resolution. It also includes a proviso allowing the Registrar to condone delays not exceeding one year for sufficient cause.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendments to the rules and regulations of a society must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the resolution being passed.
Rule 2: The Registrar must be satisfied that the amendment is in accordance with the provisions of the Act and its rules before registering it.
Rule 3: Amendments, once registered, will have effect from the date the resolution was passed.
Rule 4: The Registrar has the power to condone delays in filing the resolution, provided there is sufficient cause and the delay does not exceed one year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Societies
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By registering or rejecting amendments to the rules and regulations of societies and by enforcing the time limits for submission and potential condonation of delays.

rights: Societies have the right to amend their rules and regulations.
Societies have the right to have their amendments registered by the Registrar if they comply with the Act and rules.
Societies have the right to have delays in submission of resolutions condoned by the Registrar under specific circumstances.
duties: Societies have a duty to file amendments to their rules and regulations with the Registrar within thirty days of passing the resolution.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A society passes a resolution to amend its rules and regulations.
Procedure 2: The society files the resolution with the Registrar within thirty days of passing it.
Procedure 3: The Registrar reviews the resolution to ensure it complies with the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and its rules.
Procedure 4: If satisfied, the Registrar registers the amendment, which takes effect from the date of the resolution.

Procedure 5: If the resolution is not filed within thirty days, the society can request the Registrar to condone the delay, providing sufficient cause. The Registrar may condone the delay for a period not exceeding one year.
administration: Department of Registrar of Societies (implied by the role of the Registrar)
important_notes: The amendment is intended to provide clarity and efficiency in the process of amending society rules and regulations.
The original Act being amended is the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960 (Karnataka Act 17 of 1960).

title: THE KARNATAKA APPROPRIATION (No.3) ACT, 2021
purpose: To authorize payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Services of the Financial Year 2021-22.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and concerns the financial year 2021-22. It covers various government services and purposes as detailed in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Appropriation (No.3) Act, 2021.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rupees 1026533.15 Lakhs out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Karnataka for the Financial year 2021-22
main_sections.description: Authorizes payment and application of sums not exceeding those specified in the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to Rupees Ten thousand two hundred and sixty five crores Thirty three lakhs fifteen thousand only, towards defraying charges for services in the Financial Year 2021-22.
States that the sums authorized to be paid and applied shall be appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

important_rules: Sums not exceeding those specified in column 5 of the Schedule are authorized for payment and application.
The total aggregate sum authorized is Rupees 10,26,533.15 Lakhs.
The appropriated sums are for specific services and purposes listed in the Schedule for the Financial Year 2021-22.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the administrative departments responsible for the services listed in the schedule, overseen by the Governor and the State Legislature.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of authorizing and appropriating funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

rights: The right of the State Government to disburse funds for specified services.
duties: Duty to ensure that expenditures are within the authorized limits.
Duty to appropriate funds for the specified services and purposes.
obligations: Obligation to follow the provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically Article 205 (1) (a).

key_procedures: Legislative approval for payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund.
Specification of services and purposes in a Schedule.
Publication in the Official Gazette.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is based on the provisions of Article 205 (1) (a) of the Constitution of India.
The total amount authorized is Rupees 10,26,533.15 Lakhs (Ten thousand two hundred and sixty five crores Thirty three lakhs fifteen thousand only).

The Schedule details the appropriation for various government services and purposes for the Financial Year 2021-22, differentiating between amounts voted by the Legislative Assembly and amounts charged on the Consolidated Fund.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, to insert a new provision providing for disqualification for failure to lodge accounts of election expenses for candidates contesting elections to urban local bodies.
scope: Applies to candidates contesting elections to urban local bodies governed by the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976. Geographically it applies within Karnataka.

key_definitions.candidate: A person contesting an election under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976.
key_definitions.election expenses: All expenditure in connection with an election incurred or authorised by a candidate or their election agent between the date of nomination and the date of declaration of results.
key_definitions.political party: Has the same meaning as in the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Inserts a new sub-section (1B) into section 26 of the principal Act, stating that a person disqualified under section 26C shall be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a Councillor. This disqualification ceases to operate after three years from the date of the order made under section 26C.
Inserts new sections 26A, 26B, and 26C into the principal Act, dealing with the account of election expenses, lodging of accounts, and consequences of failure to lodge accounts, respectively.

important_rules: Every candidate must keep a separate and correct account of all election expenditure incurred or authorised between nomination and declaration of results.

Expenditure incurred by a political party, association, body, or individual (other than the candidate or election agent) is not deemed to be the candidate's expenditure for the purpose of this section.
The account of election expenses must contain prescribed particulars.
The total election expenditure shall not exceed a prescribed amount.
Every contesting candidate must lodge a true copy of their election expense account with the Returning Officer within thirty days from the date of election of the returned candidate.

penalties: Disqualification for a period of three years from the date of the order, if the State Election Commission is satisfied that a person has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the required time and manner, and has no good reason for the failure.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Election Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing an order, published in the official Gazette, declaring the person disqualified.

duties: Duty of every candidate to keep a separate and correct account of election expenses.
Duty of every contesting candidate to lodge their election expense account with the Returning Officer within the prescribed time.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the maximum prescribed amount for election expenditure.
Obligation to provide a true copy of the election expense account.

key_procedures: Candidates must maintain a detailed account of election expenditure from nomination to result declaration.
Candidates must submit this account to the Returning Officer within 30 days of the election result.
The State Election Commission reviews the lodged accounts and can disqualify candidates for failure to comply without good reason.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (mentioned as the department of the Secretary to Government who signed the act), with the State Election Commission as the enforcing authority.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 16-01-2004.
Expenditure by political parties or others not acting on behalf of the candidate is excluded from the candidate's account.
Explanations clarify the meaning of 'political party' and exclude certain expenditure related to official duties.

title: THE KARNATAKA TAX ON ENTRY OF GOODS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979, to address constitutional validity issues raised regarding the levy of tax on the entry of motor vehicles into local areas and to validate past assessments and collections.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically deals with the levy and collection of tax on the purchase value of motor vehicles entering a local area within the State for use or sale therein, and it amends the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods (Amendment) Act, 2000'. It also specifies the commencement dates: clauses 2 and 3 are deemed to have come into force from April 1, 1995, and clause 4 comes into force at once.

This section substitutes the existing Section 4B of the principal Act with a new section that levies tax on the purchase value of a motor vehicle entering a local area for use or sale, provided it's liable for registration or re-registration in Karnataka. It also includes provisions for rate fixation, a condition for non-levy of tax on previously registered vehicles, and the procedure for tax payment.

This section inserts a further proviso into Section 4C of the principal Act, specifying that in the case of a dealer in motor vehicles, tax under this Act shall be payable at the time tax is payable under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, on the sale of such motor vehicle.

This section retrospectively validates all actions, assessments, and collections made under the principal Act prior to the commencement of this Amendment Act, notwithstanding any court judgments or orders. It also clarifies that this validation does not prevent persons from questioning levies or claiming refunds under the amended Act.

important_rules: Rule: Tax is levied on the purchase value of a motor vehicle entering a local area for use or sale, if it requires registration or re-registration in Karnataka.
Rule: The tax rate shall be fixed by the State Government but shall not exceed the rates specified for motor vehicles under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957.
Rule: No tax is levied on a motor vehicle registered in another State or Union Territory for at least fifteen months prior to its new registration in Karnataka.
Rule: Tax paid under this Act shall be adjusted against the liability under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, 1957, and vice versa, subject to conditions and proof.
Rule: Dealers in motor vehicles must pay entry tax when the sales tax is payable on the sale of the motor vehicle.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and its designated authorities, as per the principal Act and its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy, assessment, re-assessment, and collection of tax and penalties as prescribed under the Act. Section 4 also validates past enforcement actions.

rights: Right to claim refund of tax paid in excess of the amount due under the amended Act.
Right to question levies, assessments, or collections under the amended Act.
duties: Duty to pay tax on the purchase value of a motor vehicle entering a local area for use or sale in Karnataka, if liable.
Duty for dealers to pay entry tax at the time of sales tax payment.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax by the importer in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed time.
Obligation to provide proof for tax adjustment claims.

key_procedures: Procedure for levying and collecting tax on motor vehicles entering local areas for use or sale.
Procedure for adjusting entry tax liability against sales tax liability and vice versa.
Procedure for payment of entry tax by dealers at the time of sales tax payment.
Procedure for validation of past assessments and collections.
administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, as indicated by the signatory to the Act. The actual administration of tax collection would typically fall under the State's tax department.
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Tax on Entry of Goods Act, 1979.
Clauses 2 and 3 have retrospective effect from April 1, 1995.
Section 4 validates all prior actions, irrespective of court judgments, which may impact any pending litigation or past tax disputes.
The Act aims to resolve constitutional challenges related to discrimination between imported and locally manufactured goods and to ensure tax neutrality.

title: THE KARNATAKA MUNICIPALITIES (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964, to insert provisions for disqualification of candidates in urban local body elections for failure to lodge accounts of election expenses, thereby curbing corrupt practices related to excessive spending on campaigning.
scope: This Act applies to elections to urban local bodies governed by the Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964. It specifically addresses the conduct of candidates and their accountability for election expenses.

key_definitions.election expenses: Expenditure incurred or authorised by a candidate or their election agent in connection with an election, between the date of nomination and the date of declaration of the result, both inclusive. Certain expenditures by political parties, associations, or individuals are not deemed to be the candidate's expenditure.
key_definitions.political party: Has the same meaning as in the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Inserts a new sub-section (1B) into section 16 of the principal Act, stating that a person is disqualified from being or becoming a Councillor if disqualified under section 16C. This disqualification ceases after three years from the date of the order made under section 16C.

Introduces three new sections into the principal Act. Section 16A deals with the requirement for candidates to keep a correct account of election expenses and specifies the maximum expenditure. Section 16B mandates the lodging of this account with the Returning Officer. Section 16C outlines the consequences of failing to lodge the account.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every candidate must keep a separate and correct account of all election expenditure incurred or authorised by them or their election agent between nomination and result declaration.

Rule 2: Expenditure incurred by political parties, associations, or individuals (other than the candidate or their agent) is not considered the candidate's expenditure for the purpose of sub-section (1) of section 16A.
Rule 3: The account of election expenses must contain prescribed particulars and the total expenditure must not exceed the prescribed amount.

Rule 4: A contesting candidate must lodge a true copy of their election expense account with the Returning Officer within thirty days from the date of election of the returned candidate (or the later date if multiple returned candidates).

Rule 5: The State Election Commission can disqualify a person for a period of three years if they fail to lodge the account of election expenses within the required time and manner and have no good reason for the failure.

penalties: Disqualification for a period of three years from the date of the order made by the State Election Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Election Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The State Election Commission, upon being satisfied that a person has failed to lodge election expense accounts without good reason, will issue an order of disqualification published in the official gazette.

rights: Right to contest elections to urban local bodies (subject to compliance with this Act).
duties: Duty of every candidate to keep a correct and separate account of election expenses.
Duty of every candidate to lodge their account of election expenses with the Returning Officer within the stipulated time and in the prescribed manner.
Duty to ensure that total election expenditure does not exceed the prescribed limit.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the prescribed particulars for the account of election expenses.
Obligation to provide a true copy of the kept account to the Returning Officer.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Candidate nominates themselves and, between nomination and result declaration, maintains a detailed record of all election-related expenditure incurred or authorised by them or their election agent.

Procedure 2: After the election result, the candidate lodges a true copy of their detailed election expense account with the Returning Officer within thirty days of the returned candidate's election date.

Procedure 3: If a candidate fails to lodge the account as required and provides no valid justification, the State Election Commission reviews the case and, if satisfied, issues an order disqualifying the candidate for three years, published in the official gazette.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation (for the Act's enactment), and the State Election Commission (for enforcement and disqualification).
important_notes: The Act came into force on 10th November 2003.
Expenditure incurred by political parties or others, not directly authorised by the candidate or their agent, is generally not counted towards the candidate's expenses.
Expenditure related to official duties of government or municipal council servants for a candidate, with their consent, is also excluded from the candidate's expenses.

title: THE KARNATAKA LOCAL FUND AUTHORITIES FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY ACT, 2003
purpose: To provide for the responsibility of Local Fund Authorities to ensure best practice of financial management of local funds, enhance the scope for improving social and physical infrastructure and human development by achieving sufficient revenue surplus, ensuring prudent management of public fiscal operations of the Local Funds and use of a medium term fiscal framework, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to such Local Fund Authorities as may be notified by the State Government from time to time. It applies to the revenue administered by bodies which by any law or rule having the force of law are under the control of the State Government regarding their budgets, creation or filling of posts, specific appointments, or encashment of leave, pension, or similar matters.

key_definitions.local_fund: The revenue administered by bodies which by any law or rule having the force of law are under the control of State Government whether in regard to the proceeding generally or to specific matters such as sanctioning of their budget, sanction to the creation or filling up of post or particular appointments or encashment of leave, pension or similar matters.
key_definitions.local_fund_authority: Any body which administers the local fund.
key_definitions.accounting_standard: Such accounting standards in respect of local fund authorities, as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.annual_budget: The budget placed before the concerned local fund authority as per the relevant Acts or the rules made thereunder.
key_definitions.budget_variance: The difference between the budgeted amount and the actuals for the financial year.
key_definitions.controlling_authority: Any officer appointed as controlling authority by the State Government for the purpose of this Act and different controlling authorities may be appointed in respect of different local fund authorities.
key_definitions.current_year: The year preceding the year for which budget and Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) are being presented.
key_definitions.fiscal_indicators: Such measures as may be prescribed, for evaluation of fiscal position of local fund authority.
key_definitions.previous_year: The year preceding the current year.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Local Fund Authorities Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003'. It also defines the territorial extent of the Act, which is applicable to Local Fund Authorities notified by the State Government, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'local fund', 'local fund authority', 'accounting standard', 'annual budget', 'budget variance', 'Controlling Authority', 'Current Year', 'fiscal indicators', and 'Previous Year'.

This section mandates the preparation of a Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) annually along with the annual budget for every local fund authority. The MTFP is a four-year rolling plan that includes fiscal objectives, mission, objectives, goals, evaluation of previous and current year performance, future prospects, strategic priorities, policies on expenditure, borrowings, investments, conformity with financial management principles, linkage of physical and financial targets, and key performance areas and indicators. It also serves as the source document for the annual budget and should address citizen needs and functional aspects like accounting systems and transparent budgeting.

This section outlines the financial management principles that every local fund authority must follow. These include transparency, performance-linked budgeting, effective fiscal monitoring, robust financial management, maintaining prudent debt levels, prudent management of guarantees and contingent liabilities, considering financial implications on future generations, adopting accrual accounting, using borrowings for productive purposes, predictability in fund flow, pursuing cost-effective and equitable tax and fiscal policies, providing impetus for economic growth and human welfare, proper maintenance of physical assets, disclosing sufficient information for public scrutiny, ensuring best value for money, managing expenditure consistent with revenue, realistic and objective budgeting, expeditious collection of dues, timely discharge of liabilities, and adopting appropriate cost measurement techniques.

This section requires local fund authorities to ensure greater transparency in their fiscal operations. This includes minimizing secrecy in budget preparation, holding at least two annual meetings with citizen forums during budget preparation and finalization, and making provisions for meetings to review operations and finances. At the time of budget presentation, authorities must disclose significant changes in accounting standards and policies, and contingent and actual liabilities.

main_sections.section_title: Measure to enforce compliance to this Act
main_sections.description: The State Accounts Department is responsible for enforcing compliance with the Act and its rules. They may oversee compliance and require periodical review reports. Local fund authorities must comply with budget-related Acts and rules, ensure their budgets align with the MTFP, and explain any variations. They must also prepare budget variance reports and financial statements. Audit of accounts is conducted by auditors appointed under relevant Acts, and follow-up action on audit reports is the responsibility of Controlling Authorities, who report any slackness to the State Government. The State Government may also constitute a Local Fund Audit Overseeing Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of financial document and annual report
main_sections.description: This section mandates the publication of financial documents and annual reports. (Note: Specific details are not fully provided in the extract).
This section grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act. (Note: Specific details are not fully provided in the extract).

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section provides protection for actions taken in good faith by individuals acting under the provisions of this Act. (Note: Specific details are not fully provided in the extract).
This section clarifies the applicability of other laws in conjunction with this Act. (Note: Specific details are not fully provided in the extract).
This section empowers the State Government to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act. (Note: Specific details are not fully provided in the extract).

important_rules: Rule 1: Every local fund authority must prepare a Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) annually along with its annual budget. The MTFP should be a four-year rolling plan that includes fiscal objectives, evaluation of performance, strategic priorities, and policies for expenditure, borrowings, and investments.

Rule 2: Local fund authorities must be guided by specific financial management principles, including transparency, performance-linked budgeting, prudent debt management, and ensuring borrowings are used for productive purposes.
Rule 3: Local fund authorities must ensure transparency in their fiscal operations, including minimizing secrecy in budget preparation and holding meetings with citizen forums.

Rule 4: The State Accounts Department is responsible for enforcing compliance with the Act. Local fund authorities must submit budget variance reports and financial statements and ensure their budgets align with the approved MTFP.
Rule 5: Audit reports of local fund authorities must be followed up strictly by Controlling Authorities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Accounts Department is responsible for enforcing compliance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. The Controlling Authorities are responsible to ensure strict follow-up action on audit reports.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The State Accounts Department oversees compliance and may require periodical review reports. Local fund authorities are required to prepare budget variance reports, receipts and payments accounts, income and expenditure accounts, and balance sheets. Slackness in follow-up action on audit reports is to be reported to the State Government for appropriate action against the defaulting local fund authority.

duties: Local fund authorities have a duty to prepare and adhere to a Medium Term Fiscal Plan and an annual budget.
Local fund authorities have a duty to ensure transparency in their fiscal operations and engage with citizen forums.
Local fund authorities have a duty to manage their finances according to the outlined financial management principles.
Local fund authorities have a duty to ensure proper maintenance of physical assets.
Local fund authorities have a duty to ensure expeditious collection of dues and timely discharge of current liabilities.
obligations: Obligation to prepare a Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) in each financial year along with the annual budget.
Obligation to adhere to financial management principles as laid down in Section 4.
Obligation to ensure transparency in fiscal operations and conduct meetings with citizen forums.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules, including budget preparation and variance reporting.
Obligation to ensure strict follow-up action on audit reports.

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of a Medium Term Fiscal Plan (MTFP) along with the annual budget.
Conducting at least two meetings with citizen forums during budget preparation and finalization.
Disclosure of significant changes in accounting standards and policies, and contingent liabilities at the time of budget presentation.
Preparation and submission of a budget variance report by the local fund authority to the Controlling Authority.
Preparation of receipts and payments account, income and expenditure account, and a balance sheet.
Audit of accounts by appointed auditors and submission of audit reports to concerned authorities.
Follow-up action on audit reports by Controlling Authorities.
administration: The State Accounts Department is responsible for enforcing compliance. The State Government may also notify Controlling Authorities and constitute a Local Fund Audit Overseeing Authority.
important_notes: The Act extends only to Local Fund Authorities notified by the State Government.
The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.
The State Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: THE KARNATAKA GOVERNMENT PARKS (PRESERVATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, specifically to empower the State Government to notify the Central Jail premises as a park for the purpose of the said Act, following the relocation of the Central Jail and the decision to develop its land and building as a park to preserve lung space in the heart of the city.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka. It specifically amends the definition of 'park' in the principal Act to include any land with or without a building earmarked by the State Government for development and preservation as parks.

key_definitions.park: Includes any land with or without building earmarked by the State Government for development and preservation as parks.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, by inserting a new definition for 'park' to include land earmarked by the State Government for development and preservation as parks.

administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975 (Karnataka Act 23 of 1975).
The amendment was necessitated by the decision to develop the land and building of the Central Jail in Bangalore as a park.

title: THE KARNATAKA RELIGIOUS STRUCTURES (PROTECTION) ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for the protection of religious structures on public places constructed before the date of commencement of this Act, in order to protect communal harmony and not to hurt the religious sentiments of the public, and to restrict unauthorized religious structures and constructions on public places in the future.
scope: This Act applies to religious structures constructed on public places within the State of Karnataka. It covers structures existing before the commencement of the Act and prohibits new unauthorized constructions in the future. The scope is limited to religious structures on public places.

key_definitions.Local Authority: Means the local self-government constituted by the State Government under relevant Laws and includes all Government-owned, managed or controlled, statutory or non-statutory Boards, Corporations, companies, committees, etc.
key_definitions.Public Place: Means a place belonging to the Government and includes any premises belonging to a Local Authority, a Government company, or a Board or Corporation or any statutory or non-statutory body of the State Government.
key_definitions.Religious structure: Means religious structures such as temple, church, mosque, Gurudwara, Bodh vihar, Majar etc., constructed on a public place without the authority of law.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Religious Structures (Protection) Act, 2021, and that it shall come into force at once.
Defines 'Local Authority', 'Public Place', and 'Religious structure' as used in the Act.

Mandates the Government to protect religious structures existing on the date of commencement of the Act, subject to prescribed conditions. However, no protection is granted if a case relating to their removal is pending in any court of law or in other prescribed circumstances.
Prohibits the State Government or any Local Authority from allowing any religious structure and construction on a public place in the future without proper permission.
Empowers the District Administration to allow religious activity in protected structures, subject to custom, law, usage, and conditions laid down by the State Government.
Provides exemption from legal proceedings against the State Government or its officers/employees for anything done or intended to be done under the Act or its rules.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, after previous publication and notification in the Official Gazette. Such rules are subject to modification or annulment by the State Legislature.

Empowers the Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within two years of its commencement. These orders must also be laid before both Houses of the State Legislature.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Local Authorities, and District Administration.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the power to grant protection, prohibit new constructions without permission, allow religious activities under specific conditions, and make rules to facilitate enforcement. The power to remove difficulties also aids in enforcement.

rights: Right to have existing religious structures on public places protected, subject to conditions and pending legal cases.
Right to conduct religious activities in protected structures, subject to custom, law, usage, and government conditions.
duties: Duty of the State Government and Local Authorities to protect existing religious structures.
Duty of the State Government and Local Authorities to not allow new religious structures or constructions on public places without proper permission.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to custom, law, and usage when allowing religious activities.
Obligation to comply with conditions prescribed by the State Government for protection and activity.

key_procedures: Protection of existing religious structures: The Government shall protect such structures subject to prescribed conditions and provided no removal case is pending in court.
Making of rules: The State Government can make rules after previous publication and notification, which are then laid before the State Legislature for approval or modification.
Removal of difficulties: The Government can issue orders to resolve difficulties, which are also laid before the State Legislature.
administration: The State Government, through its various departments and Local Authorities, along with the District Administration for religious activities.
important_notes: No protection will be granted to religious structures if a case relating to their removal is pending in any court of law.
The power to remove difficulties is time-bound, valid only for two years from the commencement of the Act.
Rules made under the Act are subject to review and modification by the State Legislature.

title: The Karnataka Medical Registration (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Medical Registration Act, 1961, to define 'teachers' and 'teachers of University' for election to the Medical Council, to modify the nomination of State Government members, to prevent elections for short-term vacancies, to enable fixing of fees by rules, to include negligence, incompetence, and violation of medical ethics as grounds for removal, to empower the council to inspect medical institutions, and to require Continuing Medical Education (CME) for registration renewal.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Medical Registration Act, 1961, and applies to registered medical practitioners in Karnataka, medical institutions, and the Karnataka Medical Council.

key_definitions.teachers: As defined in clause (m) of section 2 of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences Act, 1994.
key_definitions.teachers of the University: As defined in clause (n) of section 2 of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences Act, 1994.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification, with different dates possible for different provisions.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act concerning the composition of the Medical Council. It modifies the election of members from 'teachers' and 'teachers of the University', the nomination of members by the State Government, and the rotation of nominees from other health councils.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act to exclude a member nominated under clause (d) of sub-section (2) of section 3 from certain provisions related to members of the Medical Council.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso that no election shall be held to fill a vacancy in the office of an elected member if the remaining period of the term is less than six months.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by modifying the grounds for a member ceasing to be a member of the Council.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso that a member nominated under clause (d) of sub-section (2) of section 3 shall participate in meetings but shall not have a right to vote.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act regarding fees for registration and references to the Code of Criminal Procedure, updating the fee description and replacing the 1898 Code with the 1973 Code.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act by expanding the grounds for removal of a medical practitioner from 'misconduct' to include 'misconduct, negligence, incompetence or violation of code of Medical ethics' and updating the reference to the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act by empowering the Medical Council to inspect various medical institutions, with a proviso that inspection of private or government hospitals or teaching hospitals requires a written complaint.
Amends section 18 of the principal Act to allow the Medical Council to take the assistance of an assessor in inquiries.

Amends section 19 of the principal Act regarding renewal of registration. It replaces the fixed renewal fee with a 'prescribed fee' and inserts a proviso requiring a certificate of attendance at a Continuing Medical Education (CME) program of at least 100 hours for renewal.
Amends section 23 of the principal Act by updating the reference to the Code of Criminal Procedure from 1898 to 1973.
Amends section 26 of the principal Act concerning the publication of notices, changing the requirement from the 'official Gazette' to the 'notice board in the office of the Medical Council'.

important_rules: Rule 1: Medical practitioners seeking renewal of registration must produce a certificate for having attended a Continuing Medical Education (CME) program of not less than one hundred hours, conducted by a recognized organization or institution.
Rule 2: No election shall be held to fill a vacancy in the office of an elected member if the remaining period of the term is less than six months.
Rule 3: A member nominated by the State Government from other health councils shall attend meetings of the Medical Council but shall not have the right to vote.

penalties: Removal of a medical practitioner from the register on grounds of misconduct, negligence, incompetence, or violation of the code of Medical ethics (as amended in Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Medical Council
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, disciplinary actions, and the process of registration and renewal of medical practitioners, including the inspection of medical institutions.

rights: Right of registered medical practitioners to practice medicine, subject to registration and renewal requirements.
Right of the Medical Council to inspect medical institutions.
duties: Duty of medical practitioners to maintain professional conduct, including adhering to the code of Medical ethics.
Duty of medical practitioners to undergo Continuing Medical Education (CME) for registration renewal.
Duty of the State Government to nominate members to the Medical Council as per the Act.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Medical Registration Act, 1961, as amended.
Obligation for the Medical Council to conduct its affairs according to the Act and rules.
Obligation for nominated members from other health councils to participate in meetings without voting rights.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending the Karnataka Medical Registration Act, 1961, involving legislative processes and gubernatorial assent.
Procedure for the composition of the Medical Council, including elections and nominations.
Procedure for filling vacancies in the Medical Council, with specific rules for short-term remaining periods.
Procedure for holding inquiries into the conduct of medical practitioners, including the possibility of appointing an assessor.
Procedure for renewal of registration, which now includes a CME requirement.
Procedure for inspection of medical institutions, requiring a written complaint for private/government/teaching hospitals.
administration: The Karnataka Medical Council, and relevant government departments for notification and oversight, particularly the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Karnataka Medical Registration Act, 1961.
The commencement date is to be notified by the State Government.
Inspections of private or government hospitals or teaching hospitals require a written complaint.
Nominated members from other health councils have no voting rights in the Medical Council.

title: THE KARNATAKA GROUND WATER (REGULATION FOR PROTECTION OF SOURCES OF DRINKING WATER) ACT, 1999
purpose: To regulate the exploitation of ground water for the protection of public sources of drinking water and matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the regulation of ground water extraction and the protection of public drinking water sources.

key_definitions.appropriate authority: The Deputy Commissioner and includes any officer, not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner, as the Government may by notification appoint for the purposes of this Act. Different officers may be appointed for different local areas of the State.
key_definitions.drinking water purpose: Consumption or use of water by the human population for drinking and for other domestic purposes; and includes consumption of water for similar such relevant purposes for livestock. Domestic purposes include cooking, bathing, washing, cleansing, and other day-to-day activities.
key_definitions.ground water: Water existing in an aquifer below the surface of the ground at any particular location regardless of the geological structure in which it is stationary or moving and includes all ground water reservoirs.
key_definitions.over exploited watershed: A water shed where the estimated annual ground water extraction is more than eighty-five percent of the estimated average annual ground water recharge, calculated in the prescribed manner, and declared as such under section 6.
key_definitions.public source of drinking water: A well from which the Government or a local authority or such authority as the Government may, by notification specify, provides water to the public and includes such point or any other drinking water sources as may be notified by the appropriate Authority.
key_definitions.sink: In relation to a well, includes any drilling, boring or digging of a new well or deepening carried out to an existing well.
key_definitions.well: A well sunk for the search or extraction of ground water by a person or persons except by the authorised officials of the State or Central Governments for carrying out scientific investigations, exploration, development, augmentation, conservation, protection, or management works and shall include open well, dug well, borewell, dug-cum-borewell, tubewell, filter points, collector well and infiltration gallery or any of their combinations or variations.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and outlines the commencement provision where the State Government may appoint the date by notification.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appropriate authority', 'drinking water purpose', 'Government', 'Ground water', 'Local Authority', 'Over exploited Water Shed', 'Public source of drinking water', 'public water supply systems', 'requisite quantity of water', 'Sink', 'Technical officer', 'Water scarcity area', and 'Watershed'.

Prohibits sinking of a well within five hundred metres of a public source of drinking water without permission from the appropriate authority. Outlines the application process, factors for granting permission (considering public interest in drinking water supply and advice of Technical Officer), and conditions for permission including potential prohibition or restriction of extraction.

Empowers the appropriate authority, on the advice of the Technical Officer and considering rainfall patterns, to declare an area as a 'water scarcity area' if public drinking water sources are likely to be adversely affected. Such declarations are for a period not exceeding one year at a time.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of extraction of water from wells in water scarcity area
main_sections.description: Upon declaration of a water scarcity area, the appropriate authority may regulate extraction from any well within that area by restricting or prohibiting it, especially if the well is within 500 meters of a public drinking water source. Details the procedure for serving orders for such restrictions or prohibitions.

Allows the appropriate authority, on the advice of the Technical Officer, to declare a watershed as 'over exploited'. It also provides for cancelling such a declaration if groundwater availability improves.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition for sinking wells in over-exploited watershed
main_sections.description: Prohibits sinking of wells in an over-exploited watershed without permission from the appropriate authority. Similar to Section 3, it details the application process and conditions for granting or rejecting permission, with considerations for drinking water requirements and public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of extraction of water from an existing well for certain period
main_sections.description: If an existing well in an over-exploited watershed is adversely affecting a public drinking water source, the appropriate authority may, after giving the owner an opportunity to be heard, prohibit extraction from that well for a specific period (February 1st to July 31st) each year.

If a well in an over-exploited watershed is adversely affecting a public drinking water source and cannot be adequately protected by other measures, the appropriate authority may, after giving the owner an opportunity to be heard, order the closure or sealing of the well, temporarily or permanently.

main_sections.section_title: Power of entry upon any land for obtaining information
main_sections.description: Grants the appropriate authority or its authorized officer the power to enter any land to make inquiries or examinations related to the protection of public drinking water sources or public water supply systems.

main_sections.section_title: Power to stop contravention of the provisions of section 3, 5, 7, 8 or 9
main_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate authority to stop any contravention of specific sections of the Act related to sinking wells, regulating extraction in scarcity areas, and prohibitions in over-exploited areas.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders made by the appropriate authority under this Act.
Specifies the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act.
States that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws in force concerning the matters dealt with in this Act.
Confers power upon the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall sink a well within 500 meters of a public drinking water source without permission from the appropriate authority.

In times of water scarcity, the appropriate authority can declare an area as a 'water scarcity area' and regulate or prohibit water extraction from wells within 500 meters of public drinking water sources.
The appropriate authority can declare a watershed as 'over-exploited' if groundwater extraction exceeds 85% of recharge.
Sinking of wells is prohibited in over-exploited watersheds without permission.
Extraction from existing wells in over-exploited watersheds affecting public drinking water sources can be prohibited from February to July annually.
Existing wells in over-exploited watersheds adversely affecting public drinking water sources may be ordered to be closed or sealed if other actions are insufficient.

penalties: Details of specific penalties are not fully provided in the extract, but Section 16 mentions 'Penalty' and Section 17 covers 'Offences by companies'.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'appropriate authority', which includes the Deputy Commissioner and officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders for prohibition, restriction, or regulation of water extraction, closure of wells, power of entry for information, and imposition of penalties for contraventions.

rights: Right to apply for permission to sink a well (subject to conditions).
Right to be heard before an order is made to prohibit extraction or close a well.
Right to appeal against orders of the appropriate authority.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before sinking a well near a public drinking water source.
Duty to comply with regulations on water extraction in water scarcity areas.
Duty to comply with prohibitions on sinking wells or extracting water in over-exploited watersheds.
Duty to allow appropriate authorities entry for obtaining information.
Duty to comply with orders for closure or sealing of wells.
obligations: To ensure the protection of public sources of drinking water.
To regulate ground water exploitation in a manner that does not adversely affect drinking water sources.

key_procedures: Application for permission to sink a well (Sections 3 & 7): Applicant submits an application in the prescribed form with fees to the appropriate authority.
Declaration of Water Scarcity Area (Section 4): Appropriate authority, on technical advice and consideration of rainfall, may declare an area as a water scarcity area.
Regulation of extraction in scarcity areas (Section 5): Appropriate authority issues orders for restriction or prohibition of extraction, with specific service procedures.
Declaration of Over-exploited Watershed (Section 6): Appropriate authority, on technical advice, declares a watershed as over-exploited.
Order to prohibit extraction from existing wells (Section 8): Appropriate authority, on technical advice and after hearing the owner, may issue an order prohibiting extraction for a specific period.
Order to close down an existing well (Section 9): Appropriate authority, after hearing the owner, may order closure/sealing if other measures are insufficient.
Appeals (Section 14): Procedures for filing appeals against orders.
administration: The Act is administered by the 'appropriate authority' (Deputy Commissioner and appointed officers) and the State Government, which has the power to make rules and appoint officers.
important_notes: Exemptions exist for sinking wells on behalf of the Government or a local authority for public drinking water sources.
The Act aims to protect public drinking water sources, especially in rural areas, as urged by the Central Government.
The Act can be brought into force on different dates for different local areas or provisions.

title: THE KARNATAKA INDUSTRIES (FACILITATION) ACT, 2002
purpose: To provide for the promotion of industrial development and facilitation of new investments, to simplify the regulatory framework by reducing procedural requirements and rationalizing documents, and to provide for an investor-friendly environment in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act applies to industrial and other projects to be set up in the State of Karnataka. It covers the establishment of various committees for clearance, appointment of nodal agencies, combined application forms, self-certification, rationalization of inspections, deemed approvals, appeals, and penalties.

key_definitions.Appellate Authority: An appellate authority referred to in section 18.
key_definitions.Applicable Acts: Includes the Factories Act, 1948, the Boilers Act, 1923, the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, the Employees State Insurance Act, 1948, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, Gratuity Act, 1972, the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, and the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.
key_definitions.Authority: Includes a local authority or any statutory Board, Corporation or other authority established by the State Government and which are entrusted with the powers or responsibility to grant or issue clearances.
key_definitions.Clearances: Grant or issue of no-objection certificate, allotments consents, approvals, permissions, registration, enrolments, licences and the like, by any Authority or authorities in connection with setting up an industrial undertaking in the State.
key_definitions.Department: A department of the State Government.
key_definitions.Entrepreneur: A person or body of persons or a company, having majority investment or controlling interest in an industrial or undertaking.
key_definitions.Industrial undertaking: An undertaking engaged in manufacturing or processing or both or providing service or doing any other business or commercial activity as may be specified by the State Government.
key_definitions.Nodal Agency: The Nodal Agency at the State level or at the district level constituted under section 12.
key_definitions.State High Level Clearance Committee: The State High Level Clearance Committee constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.State Level Single Window Clearance Comm: The State Level Single Window Clearance Committee constituted under section 6.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Appellate Authority', 'Applicable Acts', 'Authority', 'Clearances', 'Department', 'District Level Single Window Clearance Committee', 'Entrepreneur', 'Industrial undertaking', 'Nodal Agency', 'State High Level Clearance Committee', and 'State Level Single Window Clearance Committee'.
Provides for the constitution of a State High Level Clearance Committee to examine and consider proposals for industrial and other projects with an investment of rupees fifty crores and above.
Outlines the functions of the State High Level Clearance Committee, including meeting schedules, procedures, examination of proposals, and communication of decisions.

States that the State High Level Clearance Committee is the final authority in granting approvals for projects placed before it, and its decisions are binding on all concerned departments and authorities.

main_sections.section_title: State Level Single Window Clearance Committee
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a State Level Single Window Clearance Committee to examine and consider proposals for industrial and other projects with an investment of more than three crores rupees and less than fifty crores rupees.
Outlines the functions of the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee, including meeting schedules, procedures, examination of proposals, and communication of decisions within one week.

States that the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee is the final authority in granting approvals for projects placed before it, and its decisions are binding on concerned departments and authorities.

main_sections.section_title: District level Single Window Clearance Committee
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a District Level Single Window Clearance Committee to examine and consider proposals for industrial projects with an investment of up to rupees three crores.
Outlines the functions of the District Level Single Window Clearance Committee, including meeting schedules, procedures, examination of proposals, and communication of decisions.

States that the District Level Single Window Clearance Committee is the final authority in granting approvals for projects placed before it, and its decisions are binding on concerned departments and authorities.
Provides for the appointment of Karnataka Udyoga Mitra as the State Nodal Agency and District Industries Centres as District Nodal Agencies.

Details the functions of the Nodal Agency, including investment promotion, guidance to entrepreneurs, issuing and receiving combined application forms, providing secretarial support, promoting environmentally friendly practices, and preparing an entrepreneurs' guide.
Allows for the prescription of a Combined Application Form in lieu of existing forms for obtaining clearances, except for factory licensing under the Factories Act, 1948.
Requires entrepreneurs to furnish a 'Self Certification' undertaking to comply with applicable Acts and rules, which will be accepted by departments and authorities for issuing clearances.
Mandates joint inspections by different levels of authorities with the Office of the Labour Commissioner and Chief Inspector.
Provides for deemed approval by departments or authorities in case of delay (details not fully present in the provided text).
Provides for an appeal process against decisions made under the Act (details not fully present in the provided text).
Specifies penalties for entrepreneurs who fail to comply with the conditions of undertaking in their self-certification (details not fully present in the provided text).
Deals with offences committed by companies and other entities (details not fully present in the provided text).
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (details not fully present in the provided text).

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith by persons acting under the Act (details not fully present in the provided text).
Grants the State Government the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act (details not fully present in the provided text).

important_rules: Any proposal with an investment of fifty crores and above is to be considered by the State High Level Clearance Committee.
Proposals with an investment of more than three crores and less than fifty crores are to be considered by the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee.
Proposals with an investment of up to three crores are to be considered by the District Level Single Window Clearance Committee.
The Nodal Agency is responsible for carrying out investment promotional activities, guiding entrepreneurs, and arranging required clearances.
Entrepreneurs must furnish a 'Self Certification' undertaking to comply with relevant Acts and rules.
Inspections by different authorities shall be conducted jointly.

penalties: Penalty for entrepreneurs who fail to comply with the conditions of undertaking in the self-certification (specifics not detailed in the provided text).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various departments and authorities concerned with granting clearances, as well as the Nodal Agencies and the constituted Committees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the review and approval processes by the Clearance Committees, the issuance of clearances by departments and authorities, and the enforcement of self-certification undertakings. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.

rights: Right to receive guidance and assistance from Nodal Agencies.
Right to submit a Combined Application Form for clearances.
Right to deemed approval in case of delays by authorities (as per section 17, details not fully present).
duties: Duty of entrepreneurs to furnish Self Certification and comply with applicable Acts and rules.
Duty of departments and authorities to issue required clearances within stipulated time.
Duty of members of Committees to attend meetings personally or depute a senior officer with authorization.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to constitute Committees and appoint Nodal Agencies.
Obligation of entrepreneurs to comply with the provisions of the Act and applicable laws.
Obligation of concerned departments and authorities to accept the Combined Application Form and act upon approvals given by the Committees.

key_procedures: Submission of proposals to the appropriate Clearance Committee based on investment amount.
Examination and decision-making by the Clearance Committees.
Communication of decisions by the Committees to entrepreneurs and concerned departments/authorities.
Submission of Combined Application Form by entrepreneurs.
Furnishing of Self Certification by entrepreneurs.
Issuance of clearances by departments and authorities based on Committee approvals and self-certification.
administration: The State Government, through its departments and the constituted Committees and Nodal Agencies.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 22.12.2003.
The Combined Application Form does not replace the application for Licensing of a Factory as provided in section 41-A of the Factories Act, 1948.
Decisions of the Clearance Committees are binding on all concerned departments and authorities.

title: THE KARNATAKA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To give effect to the proposals made in the budget speech and further amend the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, for the purposes specified therein.
scope: This act amends the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957. It applies to motor vehicles registered in Karnataka. The amendments primarily relate to the imposition of taxes and fees on various categories of motor vehicles, including the introduction of a 'green tax'.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2002, and specifies that it comes into force from April 1, 2002.
Amends sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Principal Act by substituting '1500 kgs.' for '1000 kgs.' in clause (a) of the fourth proviso.
Amends Section 3A of the Principal Act by substituting 'six years' for 'four years'.

Inserts a new section 3B, titled 'Levy of Green Tax', which introduces a cess called 'green tax' on motor vehicles to control air pollution. It specifies rates for non-transport and transport vehicles based on their age.
Amends Section 4 of the Principal Act by substituting '1500 Kgs' for '1000 Kgs' in the third proviso.

Introduces extensive amendments to various parts of the Schedule of the Principal Act, primarily altering tax rates and classifications for different types of motor vehicles, including goods vehicles, three-wheelers, omni buses, private service vehicles, and fire engines. It also details changes to the refund table for three-wheelers.
Empowers the State Government to make provisions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, for a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

important_rules: Introduction of 'green tax' on motor vehicles that have completed 15 years (non-transport) or 7 years (transport) from the date of registration for the purpose of controlling air pollution.
The levy, assessment, and collection of 'green tax' will follow the procedures applicable to the motor vehicles tax under the Act and its rules, excluding those related to refund of tax.
Revised tax rates and classifications for various motor vehicle categories, including increased rates for goods vehicles, motor cars, and passenger vehicles.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (implied, for general enforcement and removal of difficulties)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, which governs the assessment and collection of motor vehicle taxes.

rights: Right to claim refund of tax under specific conditions as per the refund table for three-wheelers.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicle tax as per the rates specified in the amended schedule.
Duty to pay 'green tax' on eligible vehicles.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1957, as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Renewal of certificate of registration for non-transport vehicles subject to green tax.
Renewal of fitness certificate for transport vehicles subject to green tax.
Application of existing rules for levy, assessment, and collection of green tax.
administration: State Government (as indicated by the 'Power to remove difficulty' section and the nature of motor vehicle taxation)
important_notes: The amendments come into effect from April 1, 2002.
The 'green tax' is levied in addition to the existing motor vehicle tax.
The power to remove difficulties by the State Government is limited to a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KARNATAKA TRANSPARENCY IN PUBLIC PROCUREMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, specifically to extend the period of exemption for certain government departments, public sector undertakings, boards, corporations, and other institutions.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and amends the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999. It specifically addresses the scope of exemptions provided under Section 4 of the principal Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements (Amendment) Act, 2003, and that it comes into force at once.

This section amends clause (d) of section 4 of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999. It substitutes the words 'two years' with 'three years', effectively extending the period of exemption.

important_rules: Rule: The period of exemption from the applicability of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, for Government Departments, Public Sector Undertakings, Boards, Corporations, and other specified Institutions, is extended from two years to three years from the date of commencement of the principal Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The principal Act, Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999, would be enforced by the relevant authorities responsible for public procurements in Karnataka. This amendment itself does not introduce new enforcement mechanisms but modifies an existing provision regarding exemptions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By extending the exemption period, the scope of the principal Act's application during that extended period is narrowed.

administration: The Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation, Government of Karnataka, is indicated as the administrative department responsible for legislation.
important_notes: The amendment 'shall be deemed always to have been substituted', implying that the change to 'three years' has retrospective effect.
The Governor of Karnataka assented to the Act on the twenty-seventh day of March, 2003.
The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette on the twenty-seventh day of March, 2003.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE UNIVERSITIES AND CERTAIN OTHER LAW (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 and the Karnataka Janapada Vishwavidyalaya Act, 2011 to provide for establishment of Nrupatunga University, registration of universities for income tax exemption, barring certain universities from offering Open and Distance Learning, appointment of first Vice-Chancellors for specific universities, appointment of Special Officers, change of nomenclature of 'Bengaluru Central University' and 'Controller of State Accounts Department', and other consequential amendments.
scope: The act amends the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 (Karnataka Act 29 of 2001) and the Karnataka Janapada Vishwavidyalaya Act, 2011 (Karnataka Act 11 of 2012). It applies to universities governed by these acts within the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.Assessment Year: The year following the year in which the income of a financial year is assessed or taxed.
key_definitions.Financial Year: A period of twelve consecutive months commencing on 1st day of April every year.
key_definitions.New university: A university established by the State Government by an amendment of the Principal Act.
key_definitions.Person having a substantial interest in: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to this expression in explanation 3 below sub-section (9) of section 13 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
key_definitions.Previous university: The university from which a new university is carved out and established.
key_definitions.Previous Year: The financial year immediately preceding the assessment year.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its various provisions. Some provisions are deemed to have come into force from September 12, 2001, while others came into force from June 19, 2020.

Details the amendments made to the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, including insertion of new definitions, modification of section 3 regarding university establishment and jurisdiction, insertion of provisions for Special Officers, and amendments to sections 4, 5, 11, 14, 17, and 19 concerning university functions, powers, appointments, and financial administration.
This section number is listed in the initial table of sections but not detailed in the provided text excerpt. Based on the title, it would amend the Karnataka Janapada Vishwavidyalaya Act, 2011.
This section number is listed in the initial table of sections but not detailed in the provided text excerpt.
This section number is listed in the initial table of sections but not detailed in the provided text excerpt.

important_rules: Rule 1: Universities governed by the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 (except Karnataka State Open University) are barred from offering Open and Distance Learning (ODL) courses due to the statewide jurisdiction of the Karnataka State Open University.
Rule 2: The first Vice-Chancellors of Maharani Cluster University, Bengaluru and Mandya University, Mandya shall be appointed by the State Government.

Rule 3: The State Government may appoint a Special Officer (not below the rank of Group A officer of senior scale) to take steps to establish a new university, and this officer shall exercise specified powers until the first Vice-Chancellor is appointed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing university acts, appointment of officers, and administrative directives.

rights: Students studying for a degree in a previous university may continue to be admitted to examinations by the previous university until examinations are provided by the new university.
Privileges enjoyed by Government Science College (Autonomous), Bengaluru from Bengaluru Central University are deemed to be withdrawn and transferred to Nrupatunga University, Bengaluru.
duties: The first Vice-Chancellor of a newly established university has the duty to make arrangements for constituting the Syndicate, Academic Council, and other authorities within six months (or longer as directed by the Chancellor).
obligations: Nrupatunga University is established as a non-profit making institution and shall not transfer its income or property.
Statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules made by a previous university shall be deemed to be those of the new university until the new university makes its own.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Establishment of Nrupatunga University by separating Government Science College (Autonomous), Bengaluru from Bangalore Central University.
Procedure 2: Appointment of first Vice-Chancellors for Maharani Cluster University, Bengaluru and Mandya University, Mandya by the State Government.
Procedure 3: Appointment of Special Officers for new universities to oversee establishment steps.
Procedure 4: Registration of universities governed by the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000 to avail income tax exemptions under Section 12A of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
administration: State Government
important_notes: The change of nomenclature of 'Bengaluru Central University' to 'Bengaluru City University' is made.
The change of nomenclature of 'Controller of State Accounts Department' to 'Principal Director, Karnataka State Audit and Accounts Department' is made in relevant acts.
The Nrupatunga University, Bengaluru is exempt from certain provisions related to affiliation and correspondence instruction.
Existing examination results and degrees for students of previous universities shall be honored.

title: THE KARNATAKA PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARIES SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS (REPEAL) ACT, 2020
purpose: To repeal the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963 (Karnataka Act 15 of 1963). This repeal is necessitated by a High Court ruling that struck down the 1963 Act as void.
scope: This act applies to the State of Karnataka. It specifically targets the repeal of the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act can be called the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions (Repeal) Act, 2020, and that it comes into force immediately upon enactment.

This section formally repeals the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963. It includes a proviso that the repeal does not affect past operations, rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, penalties, forfeitures, punishments, investigations, legal proceedings, or remedies that were established under the repealed Act.

important_rules: Rule: The Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963 is hereby repealed.

Rule: The repeal shall not affect the previous operation of the repealed Act, anything duly done or suffered under it, any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred, or any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of offenses committed under the repealed Act. Any such matters may be pursued as if the repealing act had not been passed.

penalties: Any penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed under the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963, shall still be imposed as if this act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the relevant authorities for legal proceedings and enforcement of existing rights/obligations from the repealed act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through existing legal proceedings and remedies, as well as the imposition of penalties incurred under the repealed act.

rights: Any right, privilege acquired, accrued, or incurred under the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963.
obligations: Any obligation, liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963 is repealed and shall come into force at once.
Procedure: For any legal proceedings, investigations, or remedies related to the repealed Act, they may be instituted, continued, or enforced as if the repealing Act had not been passed.
administration: Department of Parliamentary Affairs And Legislation, Government of Karnataka
important_notes: The repeal is based on a High Court of Karnataka judgment (W.P.No. 2073 of 2019) which declared the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963, void ab initio.
The Supreme Court judgment Bimolangshu Roy Vs State of Assam (2018) 14 SCC 408 was relied upon by the High Court in its decision.

title: THE KARNATAKA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETING (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Agricultural Produce Marketing (Regulation and Development) Act, 1966, specifically to provide for the Market Committee to regulate the marketing of notified agricultural produce only in the designated market yards and sub-yards, and to make consequential amendments.
scope: This Act applies to the regulation of marketing of notified agricultural produce within Karnataka, specifically within market yards, market sub-yards, and sub-market yards. It amends the principal Act of 1966.
