Lists grounds for disqualification from being a member, including conviction for an offense involving moral turpitude, unsound mind, undischarged insolvency, dismissal from government service, having a share or interest in contracts or employment with the Board, or being a paid legal practitioner for or against the Board. It also provides an exception for having an interest in a newspaper that publishes Board advertisements.

Details grounds for removal of a Chairman or member by the State Government: becoming subject to disqualification (with a proviso for representation in case of interest in contracts), refusing to act, becoming incapable, absence from three consecutive meetings without leave, or abuse of position detrimental to public interest (also with a proviso for representation).

Outlines the Secretary's remuneration and leave. The Secretary is the chief executive responsible for implementing approved schemes, operating the Board's fund, maintaining accounts, and performing other functions assigned by law.

Governs the convening and conduct of Board meetings. Meetings are convened by the Chairman or Secretary (with Chairman's approval) at places within the Board's jurisdiction or the State Headquarters. The Board must meet at least once every three months. A quorum of twenty members is required. The Chairman presides, or another member if the Chairman is absent or the office is vacant. An amendment allows the Secretary to convene urgent meetings when the Chairman's post is vacant.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings presumed to be good and valid
main_sections.description: States that any disqualification or defect in the appointment of a Chairman or member does not invalidate the Board's acts or proceedings if they are otherwise in accordance with the Act.

Establishes an Implementation Committee comprising the Secretary (as Chairman), Deputy Commissioners of districts in Bayaluseeme, Chief Executive Officers of Zilla Panchayats, Directors of Horticulture, Agriculture, Sericulture, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Sciences, Director of Development Programme (State Watershed), Chief Engineer (Minor Irrigation), Chief Engineers with jurisdiction in Bayaluseeme, Chief Conservator of Forests with jurisdiction in Bayaluseeme, and Vice Chancellors of Agricultural Universities. The State Government may appoint other officers.

Defines the powers of the Implementation Committee, stating it can exercise powers delegated to it by the Board. It must meet at least once a month and follow procedural rules provided by regulations.

Enumerates the primary objectives of the Board: promoting development and conservation of water resources, adopting soil and water conservation measures in rainfed agriculture, promoting forest development, promoting horticulture development, promoting and supporting activities in agriculture and allied sectors, and promoting animal husbandry in Bayaluseeme.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation of plan and approval of schemes
main_sections.description: Mandates the Board to prepare an annual plan for the development of Bayaluseeme and obtain approval for schemes within the plan.

important_rules: The Board must meet at least once every three months (Section 8(2)).
The Implementation Committee must meet at least once a month (Section 11(2)).
The Board prepares an annual plan for the development of Bayaluseeme (Section 13(1)).
The Board's administrative expenses, including salaries and allowances, are defrayed out of the Board's Fund (Section 3(7)).
Allowances for the Chairman and members are prescribed and defrayed out of the Board's Fund (Section 4(4)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bayaluseeme Development Board and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board to prepare plans, supervise implementation, coordinate departments, and through the State Government's powers to appoint the Chairman and Secretary, make rules, and direct the Board.

rights: Right of the Board to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (Section 3(2)).
Right of the Board to contract, sue, and be sued (Section 3(2)).
Right of members to receive prescribed allowances (Section 4(3)).
duties: Duty of the Secretary to implement approved schemes, operate the fund, maintain accounts, and discharge other functions (Section 7(3)).
Duty of the Board to prepare an annual plan for development (Section 13(1)).
Duty of the Board to supervise the implementation of schemes under the plan (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
Duty of the Board to coordinate functioning of all departments and organizations in Bayaluseeme (Statement of Objects and Reasons).
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to appoint a Chairman and Secretary (Section 3(4), 3(5)).
Obligation of the State Government to provide necessary officers and employees to the Board (Section 3(6)).
Obligation of the Board to observe rules of procedure for meetings as provided by regulations (Section 8(4), 11(3)).

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board: The Board is established upon commencement of the Act, with its composition defined by statute (Section 3).
Appointment and Removal of Members: Members are appointed by the State Government, with specific grounds for disqualification and removal (Sections 4, 5, 6).
Meeting Procedures: Rules for convening, presiding over, and quorum for Board and Implementation Committee meetings are outlined (Section 8, 11).
Plan Preparation and Scheme Approval: The Board prepares an annual plan and seeks approval for schemes (Section 13).
Financial Management: Procedures for the Board's fund, application of funds, grants, borrowing, accounts, audit, budget, and reporting are detailed (Sections 19-26).
administration: The Bayaluseeme Development Board, with overall oversight and rule-making powers vested in the State Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended by Act 16 of 2000 to revise the schedule of taluks and authorize the Secretary to convene meetings when the Chairman's post is vacant.
The Act came into force w.e.f. 26.1.1995, as notified by the State Government.
The headquarters of the Board is at Chitradurga (Section 3(1)).

title: THE HYDERABAD-KARNATAKA AREA DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1991
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Development Board for the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area to prepare an annual plan containing programmes and projects for the development of the area, supervise the implementation of projects and programmes, and monitor and evaluate the implementation of its plan.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area, which comprises the revenue districts of Bellary, Bidar, Gulbarga, Raichur, and Koppal, and Harapanahalli taluk of Davanagere revenue district. It applies to the development of this specific geographical region.

key_definitions.Board: The Hyderabad-Karnataka Area Development Board, constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Development Department: All departments of the State Government functioning in Hyderabad-Karnataka Area, including any body or corporation established by the State Government by or under any law, having jurisdiction over the area, but excluding Police and Judicial departments.
key_definitions.Implementation Committee: The Implementation Committee constituted under section 10.
key_definitions.Hyderabad-Karnataka Area: The area comprising the revenue districts of Bellary, Bidar, Gulbarga, Raichur, and Koppal, and Harapanahalli taluk of Davanagere revenue district.
key_definitions.plan: The annual plan prepared by the Board for the development of Hyderabad-Karnataka Area, excluding the district plan of the Zilla Parishads and the plan of various development departments.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area Development Board Act, 1991. It specifies that the Act extends to the whole of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area and shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Development Department', 'Implementation Committee', 'Hyderabad-Karnataka Area', 'member', 'plan', and 'Secretary'.

This section details the establishment of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area Development Board with its headquarters at Gulbarga. It describes the Board as a body corporate and specifies its composition, including Members of Parliament and State Legislature, Adhyakshas of Zilla Parishads, nominated members, and the Secretary. It also covers the appointment of the Chairman and the provision of other officers and employees.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service
main_sections.description: This section outlines the term of office for the Chairman and other appointed members (three years), conditions for resignation, prescribed allowances, and states that no act or proceeding of the Board shall be invalid due to vacancy or defect in constitution.

This section lists the grounds on which a person can be disqualified from being appointed as or for being a member of the Board. These include conviction for certain offenses, being of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, dismissal from government service, having an interest in works or contracts with the Board, and being employed as a paid legal practitioner for or against the Board. It also provides an exception for having a share in a newspaper where Board advertisements are published.

This section details the grounds for removal of the Chairman or a member by the State Government. These include becoming subject to disqualifications (with provisions for representation), refusal to act or incapacity, absence from three consecutive meetings without leave, or abuse of position detrimental to public interest (also with provisions for representation).

This section defines the role of the Secretary, stating that they will receive salary and allowances as determined by the State Government. The Secretary is the Chief Executive of the Board and is responsible for implementing schemes, operating the fund, maintaining accounts, and discharging other functions conferred by the Act.

This section specifies that meetings of the Board can be convened by the Chairman or Secretary (with Chairman's approval) and can be held within the Board's jurisdiction or at the State Headquarters. It mandates at least one meeting every three months, outlines rules for transaction of business as per regulations, and states that the Chairman presides over meetings, with a quorum of twenty members.

This section establishes an Implementation Committee and lists its members, including the Secretary of the Board (who is the Chairman), Chief Secretaries of Zilla Parishads of the relevant districts, Administrators of specific Command Area Development Authorities, Directors of various departments (Agriculture, Collegiate Education, Animal Husbandry, Health and Family Welfare Services, Social Welfare), Chief Engineers, and the Commissioner for Public Instruction.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation of plan and approval of scheme
main_sections.description: This section outlines the process by which the Board prepares a plan for the development of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area and gets it approved.
This section deals with the procedures and responsibilities for implementing the development schemes approved by the Board.
This section describes the constitution and management of the Fund of the Board, which will be used to defray its administrative expenses and implement its functions.
This section mandates the maintenance of accounts by the Board and their audit.
This section empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Board to make regulations for the transaction of business at its meetings and other matters as provided by the Act.

important_rules: The Board shall meet at least once in every three months (Section 8(2)).
The Board must prepare an annual plan for the development of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area and supervise its implementation (Preamble & Section 12).
The Secretary is the Chief Executive of the Board and is responsible for implementing schemes, operating the fund, and maintaining accounts (Section 7(3)).

Members can be disqualified on grounds of criminal conviction, unsound mind, insolvency, dismissal from service, financial interest in Board works/contracts, or acting as a legal practitioner for/against the Board (Section 5).
The State Government can issue directions to the Board in the public interest to carry out the purpose of the Act (as per Amending Act 23 of 1993, mentioned in Statement of Objects and Reasons).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area Development Board, through its Chairman and Secretary.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board to prepare plans, supervise implementation, monitor progress, and through the State Government's power to make rules and issue directions. Enforcement also implicitly involves the disqualification and removal of members who fail to adhere to the Act's provisions.

rights: Members have the right to represent against proposed disqualification or removal (Section 5(2), Section 6(a) & (d) Provisos).
The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and to contract (Section 3(2)).
The Board has the power to borrow money (Section 22).
duties: The Board has the duty to prepare an annual plan for the development of the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area (Preamble).
The Board has the duty to supervise the implementation of projects and programmes and monitor and evaluate their implementation (Preamble).
The Secretary has the duty to implement approved schemes, operate the fund, and maintain accounts (Section 7(3)).
Zilla Parishads and Development Departments are expected to cooperate by providing information (Section 16) and their Chief Secretaries are part of the Implementation Committee (Section 10).
The Board has a duty to coordinate the functioning of development departments and Zilla Parishads in the area (Statement of Objects and Reasons (i)).
obligations: Members appointed by the State Government hold office subject to the pleasure of the State Government (Section 4(1)).
The Board is obligated to follow procedures for transaction of business at meetings as provided by regulations (Section 8(4)).

key_procedures: Preparation and approval of an annual development plan for the Hyderabad-Karnataka Area by the Board (Section 12).
Convening and conducting meetings of the Board, including maintaining quorum and presiding over meetings (Section 8).
Process for removal of a member, including providing an opportunity for representation (Section 6).
Process for disqualification of a member, with specific provisions for financial interests (Section 5).
Appointment of Chairman and Secretary by the State Government (Section 3(4), 3(5)).
administration: The Hyderabad-Karnataka Area Development Board, with the State Government having oversight and rule-making powers.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 10.3.1992 (as per footnote in Section 1(3)).
The definition of Hyderabad-Karnataka Area has been amended by Act 33 of 1998 to include Koppal and Harapanahalli taluk of Davanagere district.
The Secretary of the Board is now a Divisional Commissioner, as amended by Act 23 of 1993.
The Act recognizes non-Governmental Organizations for formulation of schemes (as per Statement of Objects and Reasons for Amending Act 23 of 1993).

title: The Kannada Development Authority Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Kannada Development Authority for the development of Kannada, to supervise the implementation of projects and programmes relating to the development of Kannada, and to monitor and evaluate the implementation of Kannada as the official language and its projects and programmes.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and covers all departments of the State Government, public undertakings, institutions, local bodies, and organizations receiving financial aid from the State Government, in relation to the development and implementation of the Kannada language.

key_definitions.authority: The Kannada Development Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.department: All departments of the State Government, including any body or corporation established by the State Government by or under any law or any institution or body of organizations receiving financial aid from the State Government.
key_definitions.projects_and_programmes: The annual projects and programmes prepared by the Authority for the development of Kannada in various departments.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Authority', 'Chairman', 'department', 'Member', 'Projects and programmes', 'Secretary', and 'Regulation'.

Establishes the Kannada Development Authority with its headquarters in Bangalore. It is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. Details the composition of the Authority, including the Chairman, nominated members, ex-officio members, and the Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairman and nominated members (three years), and conditions for ex-officio members. It also covers resignation, filling of casual vacancies, and allowances.

Outlines grounds for disqualification from being a member of the Authority, including conviction for certain offences, unsound mind, insolvency, removal from government service, and having a direct or indirect interest in contracts or employment with the Authority.
Details the grounds on which the State Government may remove a Chairman or member, such as becoming disqualified, refusing to act, prolonged absence from meetings, or abusing their position.

Deals with the appointment of the Secretary, their rank, salary, and allowances. It also outlines the Secretary's responsibilities as the Chief Executive, including implementing projects, operating the fund, maintaining accounts, and performing other functions.

main_sections.section_title: Officers of the Authority and conditions of service
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government or its authorized officer to appoint or depute officers and employees for the efficient discharge of the Authority's functions, and specifies that recruitment and service conditions will be prescribed by rules.
Governs the convening and conduct of Authority meetings, including frequency (at least once every two months), quorum (eight members), and presiding over meetings.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings presumed to be good and valid
main_sections.description: States that any act or proceeding of the Authority will not be invalidated due to a disqualification or defect in the appointment of a Chairman or member, provided the act or proceeding is otherwise in accordance with the Act.

Allows the Authority to constitute sub-committees for specific purposes, consisting of not more than five members, with the Chairman of the Authority also serving as the Chairman of the sub-committee.

Defines the powers and duties of sub-committees, which are delegated by the Authority. It also specifies meeting frequency for sub-committees (at least once a month) and their role in reviewing urgent matters and suggesting actions.
Grants the Authority the power to obtain the services or assistance of experts for carrying out the purposes of the Act, and outlines the provision for honorarium and allowances to these experts.
Requires the Authority to prepare annual projects and programmes for the development of Kannada and submit them to the State Government for approval, which may be with or without modifications.

Enumerate the primary functions of the Authority, including reviewing actions of departments and institutions for official language policy implementation, suggesting measures for the Sarojini Mahishi Report recommendations, identifying and solving hurdles in the implementation of Kannada as an administrative language, and securing priority and promotion for Kannada in education and cultural activities.
Confers power on the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made thereunder, for the transaction of its business.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kannada Development Authority, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the review and monitoring of implementation of Kannada as the official language and its development projects, identification of hurdles and suggesting solutions, and by exercising powers delegated to sub-committees. The State Government also has powers to make rules for enforcement.

rights: Right to have a dedicated Authority for Kannada development and official language implementation.
Right to propose measures and seek solutions for the promotion of Kannada.
Right to receive allowances and prescribed conditions of service for members and staff.
duties: Duty of the Authority to prepare and implement projects and programmes for Kannada development.
Duty to monitor and evaluate the implementation of Kannada as the official language.
Duty to identify and resolve challenges in the administrative use of Kannada.
Duty to review and suggest improvements for Kannada examinations and syllabus.
Duty of officers and employees to efficiently discharge their functions.
obligations: Obligation of government departments, public undertakings, and aided institutions to comply with the official language policy.
Obligation of members to avoid conflicts of interest.
Obligation to adhere to the rules and regulations set forth in the Act.

key_procedures: Annual preparation and submission of projects and programmes for Kannada development to the State Government for approval.
Convening of Authority meetings at least once every two months, with special meetings convened as needed.
Constitution and functioning of sub-committees to review urgent matters and suggest actions.
Obtaining services of experts for carrying out the Act's purposes.
The process for appointment, disqualification, and removal of members of the Authority.
administration: The Kannada Development Authority, with the State Government holding powers for rule-making, appointment, and oversight.
important_notes: The Act came into force by notification w.e.f. 1.11.1995.

The Act has been amended by Act 26 of 1997, which inserted provisions for the Director of Translation to be a member and empowered the Authority to secure priority for Kannada in education and cultural activities.
The composition of the Authority has been modified by amendments.

title: KANNADA UNIVERSITY ACT, 1991
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of Kannada University at Hampi, with the objective of furthering the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in the Kannada language, literature, and allied fields, recognizing its hoary and glorious literary and cultural tradition and heritage.
scope: Applies to the establishment, incorporation, and functioning of the Kannada University. Geographically, it is established at Hampi, Karnataka. Subject matter scope covers advancement of learning, research, and preservation of Kannada language, literature, art, culture, history, and related fields.

key_definitions.appointed_date: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.hostel: A unit of residence for students maintained or recognised by the University.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by this Act and the statutes.
key_definitions.statutes: Statutes of the University made under this Act.
key_definitions.teachers: Professors, emeritus professors, readers, lecturers, and other persons declared as teachers by the statutes.
key_definitions.university: The Kannada University established under section 3.
key_definitions.university_grants_commission: The Commission established under section 4 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
key_definitions.university_library: A library maintained by the University.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kannada University Act, 1991, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed date', 'Government', 'hostel', 'prescribed', 'statutes', 'teachers', 'University', 'University Grants Commission', and 'University library'.

Establishes 'The Kannada University' for furthering learning and research in Kannada. It is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, of a unitary and residential type. It specifies conditions for recognition of affiliated institutions and the location of its headquarters.

Outlines the numerous objects of the University, including functioning as a research center, imparting training, facilitating advanced study and research in various art, culture, and science fields related to Kannada, translating books, preserving manuscripts, compiling epigraphs, documenting culture and monuments, and developing Kannada as a medium of instruction.

Details the powers of the University, such as instituting and conferring degrees, supervising hostels, prescribing conditions for awards, co-operating with other bodies, establishing libraries and research stations, instituting research posts, awarding fellowships, maintaining hostels and staff accommodation, fixing fees, managing endowments, and borrowing money.

States that the University is open to all persons, subject to the Act and statutes. However, it can refuse admission or retain students who do not meet academic qualifications, whose academic record is below the minimum standard, or whose conduct is prejudicial to the University's interests.

Lists disqualifications for election or nomination to University authorities, including being of unsound mind, an insolvent, or having been sentenced for an offense involving moral turpitude. The Executive Council decides on disqualification disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for nomination to Governing Council and Executive Council in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that a person who has served a total of six years on the Governing Council or Executive Council (or both) is disqualified for nomination to these bodies.

important_rules: Rule: The University shall function as a high-level research center for Kannada language and literature.
Rule: The University shall provide training for individuals within and beyond India who wish to study Kannada language and literature.

Rule: The University shall facilitate and regulate advanced study and research in fields like Art, Culture, Music, Stage-plays, Painting, Sculpture, Folk Arts, Archaeology, Architecture, Literature, Grammar, Linguistics, History, Religion, Philosophy, Geography, Soil Sciences, Astronomy, Navigation and Shipping, Astrology, Siddha Medicine, Engineering Science, and Handicrafts, as developed based on the Kannada language and literature.
Rule: The University shall translate books from other languages into Kannada and vice-versa.
Rule: The University shall preserve and publish palm leaf manuscripts and rare ancient books.
Rule: The University shall search for, compile, and publish epigraphs related to Kannada language, literature, culture, and the history of Kannadigas.
Rule: The University shall compile and publish Kannada words, expressions, colloquial terms, and industry/agriculture-specific words used by Kannadigas.
Rule: The University shall conduct research on Kannada language and literature in ancient times with a view to future scientific developments.
Rule: The University shall research and determine procedures for the development of Kannada language and literature, incorporating educational fields and evolving suitable approaches.
Rule: The University shall institute studies in Kannada language and literature in relation to other Indian cultures.
Rule: The University shall organize advanced studies and research programs based on an in-depth understanding of trends in Kannada language and literature.
Rule: The University shall promote archaeology to resurrect and re-discover ancient Kannada culture.
Rule: The University shall document monuments in the State to facilitate future research.

Rule: The University shall project Kannada culture as expressed through art, architecture, sculptures, paintings, iconography, epigraphy, theatre, dance, music, tribal-art, religion, philosophy of life, and social movements.
Rule: The University shall document, analyze, and preserve traditional, tribal folk-art forms and performing arts.
Rule: The University shall develop Kannada as a medium of instruction in relation to modern advances in science and technology.
Rule: The University shall foster comparative studies of Kannada with other Dravidian and Aryan languages.
Rule: The University shall build a museum to store classic objects and artifacts of Karnataka.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, the Executive Council, and other authorities of the University as defined within the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the exercise of powers by the University authorities, determination of disputes by the Executive Council, and the potential for amendment or removal of difficulties by the State Government.

rights: Right to admission for all persons, subject to prescribed qualifications and conduct.
Right to institute and confer degrees, diplomas, and academic distinctions.
Right to co-operate with other bodies for similar objectives.
Right to establish and maintain libraries, research stations, and museums.
Right to fix and demand fees.
Right to hold and manage endowments and properties.
Right to borrow money on security of University property with Government approval.
duties: Duty to further the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in Kannada.
Duty to function as a high-level research center and impart training.
Duty to preserve and publish manuscripts and rare books.
Duty to compile and publish epigraphs and Kannada words.
Duty to promote archaeology and document monuments.
Duty to project Kannada culture.
Duty to document and preserve traditional arts.
Duty to develop Kannada as a medium of instruction.
Duty to foster comparative studies of Kannada.
Duty to build a museum.
Duty to supervise and control hostels and regulate discipline among students.
Duty to make arrangements for student health and welfare.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the Act and statutes for admission and retention of students.
Obligation to obtain prior approval from the Government and concerned University before recognizing institutions affiliated with other Universities.
Obligation to comply with conditions for award of degrees and diplomas.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for conferring honorary degrees.
Obligation to manage endowments and properties for the University's purposes.
Obligation to secure Government approval for borrowing money.

key_procedures: Procedure for Commencement: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
Procedure for Admission: The University is open to all, but admission and retention are subject to prescribed academic qualifications, minimum standards, and conduct requirements.

Procedure for Disqualification Disputes: In case of doubt or dispute regarding disqualification for membership of University authorities, the Executive Council shall determine the matter, and its decision is final.
Procedure for Making Statutes: Statutes are made in the manner prescribed by the Act, likely involving proposals from University authorities and approval mechanisms.
Procedure for Filling Casual Vacancies: Vacancies in University authorities and bodies are to be filled in accordance with the Act's provisions.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the State Government (for notifications, approvals, and removing difficulties), the University Grants Commission (for grants and setting standards), and the various authorities of the Kannada University (Chancellor, Pro-chancellor, Vice-chancellor, Governing Council, Executive Council, Faculties, Boards of Studies, Finance Committee, Registrar, and Finance Officer).
important_notes: The Act came into force on 8.11.1991.
Amendments have been made by Act 10 of 1992 and Act 19 of 1999.
The 1999 amendment makes the Governor the Chancellor of the University and establishes a Search Committee for Vice-Chancellor appointments, to facilitate grants from the University Grants Commission.
The University is of a unitary and residential type.

No institution affiliated with, associated with, or maintained by another University in the State can be recognized by this University without prior approval from the Government and the concerned University.

title: THE KARNATAKA KORAGAS (PROHIBITION OF AJALU PRACTICE) ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for the prevention of the use of services of Koragas for Ajalu practice in certain parts of the State of Karnataka, as such practices amount to exploitation, treating them as slaves, and offend human dignity.
scope: The Act extends to the whole State of Karnataka. It specifically addresses the 'Ajalu practice' involving the Koraga community.

key_definitions.ajalu_practice: The performance of any act or ceremony that differentiates between Koragas and persons belonging to other communities by paying no wages or lesser wages for their service; treating Koragas as inferior human beings; mixing hair, nails, or any other inedible or obnoxious substance in food and asking Koragas to eat it; or driving Koragas to run like buffaloes before the beginning of Kambala.
key_definitions.koraga: An Adivasi Tribal person belonging to the Koraga Community of any age.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Koragas (Prohibition of Ajalu Practice) Act, 2000, extends to the whole State of Karnataka, and is deemed to have come into force from August 17, 2000.
Provides definitions for 'Ajalu practice', 'Kambala', and 'Koraga'.
Prohibits any person from using the services of a Koraga for Ajalu practice, with or without their consent, notwithstanding any law, custom, usage, or practice.

Prescribes punishment for anyone who uses or abets the use of a Koraga's services for Ajalu practice, with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but extending up to five years, and a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: States that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to legislative approval and modification.

Repeals the Karnataka Koragas (Prohibition of Ajalu practice) Ordinance, 2000, and states that anything done or action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule under Section 6: The State Government can make rules for the implementation of the Act. These rules are subject to prior publication and must be laid before both Houses of the State Legislature for a specified period, during which they can be modified or annulled.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend up to five years.
A fine not exceeding five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and any person acting in good faith under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through conviction for the offense of using or abetting the use of Koraga services for Ajalu practice, and through rules made by the State Government.

rights: The right of Koragas not to be subjected to Ajalu practice, even if consent is implied or given under duress.
The right of Koragas to be treated as equal human beings.
duties: The duty of all persons not to engage in Ajalu practice involving Koragas.
The duty of the State Government to implement and enforce the Act and make necessary rules.
obligations: The obligation on any person to refrain from differentiating wages, treating Koragas as inferior, forcing them to consume inedible substances, or making them run like buffaloes as part of Ajalu practice.

key_procedures: Procedure for making rules: The State Government makes rules after previous publication. These rules are placed before the State Legislature. If both Houses agree on modifications or annulment, the rules take effect accordingly. (Section 6)
Procedure for prosecution and penalties: Any person found guilty of violating Section 3 (Prohibition of Ajalu Practice) shall be convicted and punished as per Section 4. (Section 4)
administration: The State Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from August 17, 2000.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
The Act repeals the Karnataka Koragas (Prohibition of Ajalu practice) Ordinance, 2000, but actions taken under the Ordinance are considered valid under the Act.

title: The Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority Act, 1992
purpose: To provide for the constitution of an Authority for the expeditious utilization of the State's share of waters of the Krishna River and its tributaries, to facilitate speedy execution and maintenance of Irrigation, Power, and other projects and works relating thereto in the Krishna Basin Area, and to promote Agricultural and General Economic Development of the Krishna Basin Area. It aims to expedite decisions and resolve problems like Land Acquisition and Contractual Disputes to ensure timely completion of Irrigation Projects.
scope: The Act applies to the Krishna Basin Area within the territories of the State of Karnataka. The Authority's functions and powers are primarily within the Krishna Basin, but the State Government can extend its area of operation to other specified areas for carrying out additional functions and exercising additional powers.

key_definitions.Authority: The Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority.
key_definitions.Chief Executive: The Chief Executive of the Authority appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.Code: In relation to scheduled disputes, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908; in relation to scheduled offences, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
key_definitions.Krishna Basin: The basin area of the Krishna River and its tributaries lying within the territories of the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.land: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
key_definitions.person interested: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
key_definitions.Special Court: A Special Court constituted under section 31.
key_definitions.Special Land Acquisition Officer: Land Acquisition Officer of the Authority appointed under section 29.
key_definitions.Special Government Pleader-cum-Public Pr: Special Government pleader-cum-Public Prosecutor of the Authority appointed under section 36.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Authority, Chairman, Chief Executive, Code, Krishna Basin, land, person interested, Member, Regulations, Rules, Special Court, Scheduled disputes, Scheduled Offences, Special Land Acquisition Officer, and Special Government Pleader-cum-Public Prosecutor.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and Incorporation of the Authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority by the State Government and describes it as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire, hold, dispose of property, and contract, and to sue or be sued.

main_sections.section_title: Limits of Krishna Basin and area of operation
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to specify the limits of the Krishna Basin by notification. The Authority operates within the Krishna Basin, but its area of operation can be extended by the State Government to other areas for additional functions and powers.

Specifies the members of the Authority, including the Chief Minister (Chairman), Minister in charge of Major and Medium Irrigation (Vice-Chairman), and other Ministers and Secretaries related to Irrigation, Agriculture, Revenue, Energy, Finance Commissioner, Secretary, Irrigation, Secretary, Agriculture, Secretary, Planning, Chairman of Karnataka Electricity Board, Managing Director of Karnataka Power Corporation, and the Chief Executive (Member Secretary).

Lays down the procedure for meetings of the Authority, including times, places, and conduct of proceedings as per regulations. It also outlines the presiding officer in case of absence of the Chairman or Vice-Chairman, decision-making by majority votes, casting vote, and the quorum (six members).

Details the functions of the Authority, which include planning, investigation, execution, operation, and maintenance of irrigation projects; promoting irrigation water supply and drainage schemes; controlling navigation; formulating and executing comprehensive development schemes for the Krishna Basin; undertaking resettlement and rehabilitation of affected people; constructing drainage systems; preventing water logging and salinity; undertaking environmental protection measures; and performing other functions for efficient water utilization entrusted by the State Government.

Grants the Authority general powers to do anything necessary or expedient for carrying out its functions. This includes acquiring property, constructing dams, reservoirs, power structures, irrigation canals, etc.; preventing water pollution; stocking reservoirs with fish and regulating fishing; undertaking rehabilitation and resettlement of displaced populations; aiding co-operative societies; and compounding claims and demands.

main_sections.section_title: Rates for supply of water for irrigation, industrial and domestic purposes
main_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to levy and collect water charges for irrigation, industrial, and domestic purposes at rates specified by regulations, and to fix the minimum quantity of water to be supplied.

main_sections.section_title: Supply of water where supply has been stopped or reduced
main_sections.description: Mandates the Authority to arrange for the supply of water on the same terms as before if it stops or reduces supply to a person who was enjoying it by prescriptive right, for the purpose of operating its schemes.

Allows the Authority to issue directions to the Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board, Karnataka Electricity Board, and other connected bodies for carrying out the Act's purposes, providing funds for compliance, and recovering expenses upon failure. Disputes between the Authority and these bodies are decided by the Government. It also grants the Authority power to direct Command Areas Development Authorities.

Permits the Authority to delegate its powers (except the power to make regulations) to the Chief Executive or other whole-time members/officers through notification, subject to restrictions and conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Exercise of the powers under the Command Areas Development Act, 1980
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything in the Command Areas Development Act, 1980, the powers of the State Government under that Act shall be exercised by the Authority.
Provides for the appointment of a Chief Executive and Administrative Officer for the Authority by the State Government. It also mentions their salary and allowances as determined by the Authority.
This section likely deals with the Authority's power to acquire land.
Provides for the constitution of Special Courts to deal with scheduled disputes and offences.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Authority to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations for the transaction of its business, including the conduct of meetings, and other matters specified in the Act.
Likely grants the Authority or its officers the power to enter premises for inspection or other purposes related to the Act.
Indicates that this Act may amend another Karnataka Act (Act 34 of 1987).

important_rules: Rules for the conduct of meetings of the Authority are to be provided by regulations. (Section 6(1))
The Authority shall levy and collect water charges for irrigation, industrial, and domestic purposes at rates specified by regulations. (Section 9)

The Authority shall arrange for the supply of water on the same terms as before if it has stopped or reduced supply due to operating its schemes, to a person enjoying it by prescriptive right. (Section 10)
Directions issued by the Authority to certain boards and bodies must be complied with, and expenses incurred on failure can be recovered. (Section 11(2))
The State Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. (Section 41)
The Authority has the power to make regulations for its business and other specified matters. (Section 42)

penalties: The Act specifies 'Scheduled Offences' in Schedule II, implying penalties are associated with them.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Authority, and potentially Special Courts constituted under the Act for scheduled disputes and offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the exercise of powers granted to the Authority, directions issued to other bodies, and through the jurisdiction of Special Courts for scheduled disputes and offences.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, lease, sell or otherwise transfer movable and immovable property (Section 8(2)(i)).
Right to construct dams, reservoirs, power structures, canals, etc. (Section 8(2)(ii)).
Right to prevent pollution of water under its control (Section 8(2)(iii)).
Right to stock reservoirs with fish and regulate fishing (Section 8(2)(iv)).
Right to levy and collect water charges (Section 9).
Right to issue directions to other bodies (Section 11).
Right to exercise powers under the Command Areas Development Act, 1980 (Section 13).
duties: To undertake planning, investigation, execution, operation, and maintenance of irrigation projects (Section 7(a)).
To promote and operate schemes for irrigation water supply and drainage (Section 7(b)).
To promote and control navigation (Section 7(c)).
To formulate and execute comprehensive development schemes for the Krishna Basin (Section 7(d)).
To undertake resettlement and rehabilitation of affected people (Section 7(e)).
To construct drainage systems and prevent water logging and salinity (Section 7(f)).
To undertake measures for environmental protection (Section 7(g)).
To arrange water supply on the same terms if stopped or reduced to persons with prescriptive rights (Section 10).
obligations: Obligation to comply with State Government's directions if its area of operation is extended (Section 4(3)).
Obligation to comply with directions issued by the Authority by other designated bodies (Section 11(2)).
Obligation to have its actions (as public servants) protected under the Act (Section 37, 38).

key_procedures: Constitution of the Authority: State Government issues a notification to constitute the Authority. (Section 3(1))
Defining Operational Area: State Government specifies the limits of the Krishna Basin and can direct the Authority to operate in additional areas. (Section 4)
Holding Meetings: Meetings are held at specified times and places, with proceedings conducted as per regulations. Decisions are by majority vote. (Section 6)
Issuing Directions: The Authority can issue directions to specific boards and bodies, with the State Government resolving disputes arising from these directions. (Section 11)
Delegation of Powers: The Authority can delegate its powers to the Chief Executive or other officers through notification. (Section 12)
Land Acquisition: The Act provides for land acquisition procedures, potentially involving Special Land Acquisition Officers. (Sections 25-30)
Dispute Resolution: Constitution of Special Courts to handle scheduled disputes and offences. (Sections 31-35)
administration: The Karnataka Krishna Basin Development Authority itself, with administrative support from the Chief Executive and other officers appointed under the Act. The State Government has oversight and rulemaking powers.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary on March 31, 1992, but it was first published as Act 12 of 1996 on July 19, 1996, and received Presidential assent on September 7, 1994. It was not yet brought into force at the time of the documentation referenced. (Section 1(2) and footnote)
The Authority's general powers include the ability to construct various infrastructure like dams, reservoirs, power structures, and irrigation canals. (Section 8(2)(ii))
The Authority can compound or compromise claims arising from contracts or legal actions. (Section 8(2)(vii))
The Authority can direct Command Areas Development Authorities. (Section 11(4))
Officers and servants of the Authority are deemed to be public servants. (Section 37)
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected. (Section 38)
The Act has an overriding effect over other laws in case of conflict. (Section 39)

title: The Karnataka Land (Restriction on Transfer) Act, 1991
purpose: To impose certain restrictions on the transfer of land that has been acquired by the Government or in respect of which acquisition proceedings have been initiated, with the aim of preventing large-scale purported transfers and protecting unwary buyers, thereby facilitating planned urban development and speedy formation and distribution of sites.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It specifically covers lands acquired by the Government or in relation to which acquisition proceedings have been initiated for development schemes under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 or the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, 1987. The scope is limited to 'urban areas' as defined in these Acts.

key_definitions.competent_authority: Any person or authority not below the rank of a Deputy Commissioner of the district, authorized by the Government by notification to perform the functions of a competent authority under the Act for specified areas.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under the Act.
key_definitions.scheme: A development scheme drawn up under section 15 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 or the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, 1987, and sanctioned by the Government.
key_definitions.urban_area: Includes the Bangalore metropolitan area and any urban area for which an Urban Development Authority is constituted under the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, 1987.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of Karnataka, and outlines that it comes into force on a date specified by the Government, potentially different dates for different urban areas.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority', 'Government', 'prescribed', 'scheme', and 'urban area'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on transfer of lands acquired by Government
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from transferring, by sale, mortgage, gift, lease, or otherwise, any land situated in an urban area that has already been acquired by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of transfer of lands in relation to which acquisition proceedings have been initiated
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transfer of land situated in an urban area, which is proposed to be acquired for a scheme, without the previous written permission of the competent authority.

main_sections.section_title: Application for grant of permission of transfer under section 4
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for permission to transfer land under section 4, the powers of the competent authority to grant or refuse permission (with specific grounds for refusal), the requirement to record reasons for refusal, and a deemed permission clause if no refusal is communicated within thirty days.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals against orders of competent authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the right to appeal against an order of the competent authority under section 5 to a prescribed authority within thirty days, and states that the appellate authority's order is final.

main_sections.section_title: Period of operation of orders of refusal to grant permission to transfer land
main_sections.description: Specifies that an order refusing permission to transfer land operates for three years from the date of the order. After this period, and subject to section 3, the land can be transferred. It also allows for the exclusion of periods where acquisition proceedings were stayed by a court.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on registration of transfer of land
main_sections.description: Mandates that registering officers shall not register documents purporting to transfer land referred to in section 4 unless the transferor provides written permission from the competent authority.
Prescribes punishment for contravention of sections 3 or 4, which may include imprisonment up to three years, a fine, or both.

Deals with offenses committed by companies, making individuals in charge responsible, and also holding directors or officers liable if the offense was committed with their consent, connivance, or due to their neglect.

Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including specifying application particulars, appeal procedures, and any other prescribed matters. It also includes a provision for laying rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

important_rules: No person shall transfer any land situated in an urban area that has already been acquired by the Government (Section 3).
No person shall transfer land in an urban area, proposed for acquisition for a scheme, without prior written permission from the competent authority (Section 4).

Permission to transfer land proposed for acquisition can only be refused on specific grounds related to the implementation of the scheme or the objectives of urban development authorities (Section 5(3)).
Registration of documents for transfer of land under Section 4 is prohibited unless the transferor provides permission from the competent authority (Section 8).
Orders refusing permission to transfer land are generally valid for three years (Section 7).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, for contravening provisions of section 3 or section 4.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority, prescribed authority (for appeals), and registering officers (for registration of documents).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the competent authority's power to grant or refuse permission for transfers, the appellate authority's review of these decisions, restrictions on registration of sale deeds by registering officers, and penalties for violations.

rights: Right to apply for permission to transfer land proposed for acquisition (Section 5(1)).
Right to appeal against the competent authority's order of refusal to grant permission (Section 6(1)).
Right to transfer land after a period of three years if permission was refused, subject to section 3 (Section 7).
duties: Duty of individuals not to transfer lands already acquired by the Government (Section 3).
Duty to obtain prior written permission from the competent authority before transferring land proposed for acquisition (Section 4).
Duty of the competent authority to inquire and make a written order on applications for permission (Section 5(2)).
Duty of the competent authority to record reasons for refusal and communicate them to the applicant (Section 5(4)).
Duty of the appellate authority to give the appellant an opportunity of being heard (Section 6(2)).
Duty of registering officers to not register documents without the required permission (Section 8).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the restrictions on transfer of acquired or proposed acquisition lands.
Obligation for companies to ensure their directors, managers, and officers are aware of and comply with the Act's provisions.

key_procedures: Application for permission to transfer land proposed for acquisition: A person desirous of transferring such land must submit a written application with prescribed particulars to the competent authority. The authority will then inquire and pass a written order to grant or refuse permission. Reasons must be recorded for refusal.

Appeal against refusal of permission: Any person aggrieved by the competent authority's order can file an appeal to the prescribed authority within thirty days. The appellate authority will hear the appellant and dispose of the appeal expeditiously. The appellate order is final.

Registration of transfer: Registering officers are prohibited from registering any document for the transfer of land under Section 4 unless the transferor produces written permission from the competent authority.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, which appoints the 'competent authority' and 'prescribed authority' through notifications. The Housing and Urban Development Department is mentioned as the department in charge of issuing such notifications.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st August 1992 in 22 specified urban areas in Karnataka.
The explanation to Section 7 clarifies that periods during which acquisition proceedings were stayed by a court are excluded when computing the three-year period of operation for refusal orders.
Section 10 regarding offenses by companies defines 'company' broadly to include any body corporate, firm, or association of individuals, and 'director' in relation to a firm as a partner.

title: The Karnataka Prohibition of Admission of Students to the Un-recognised and Un-affiliated Educational Institutions Act, 1992
purpose: To prohibit the admission of students to un-recognised and un-affiliated educational institutions in the State of Karnataka and to provide for matters relating thereto, curbing the practice in public interest and maintaining educational standards.
scope: The Act applies to all educational institutions within the State of Karnataka, encompassing various types of education including general, professional, medical, and technical education. It prohibits admission to institutions that are not recognized or affiliated with a competent authority or university.

key_definitions.commerce_education: Education in Shorthand and Typewriting, Bookkeeping and Accountancy, Commerce, Office Practice and Procedure, Salesmanship and Marketing, Banking Practice, Insurance Practice, and other subjects notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.commerce_institution: Any institution imparting commerce education and presenting students for examinations conducted by the Karnataka State Secondary Education Examination Board.
key_definitions.competent_authority: Any person, officer, or authority authorized by the State Government to perform functions and discharge duties under the Act for a specified area, purpose, or class of institutions.
key_definitions.educational_institution: Any institution, by whatever name called (other than a Commerce Institution), managed by Government, Private body, Local Authority, Society, Trust, University, or any other person, imparting education in General Education, Professional Education, Medical Education, Technical Education, leading to a degree or diploma conferred by a University established under the Karnataka State Universities Act, 1976, or grant of Diploma or Certificate by any Authority, or any other class of institution as specified by the State Government.
key_definitions.general_education: Every branch of education other than religious, professional, medical, technical, or special education.
key_definitions.medical_education: Includes education in modern scientific medicine, Pharmacy, Dental Education, Ayurvedic System of Medicine, Indigenous Medicine, Naturopathy, Siddha, or Homeopathy.
key_definitions.special_education: Education for the handicapped, education in music, dance, drama, fine arts, physical education (including sports and games), and other types of education as specified by the State Government.
key_definitions.society: Includes a society registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, or the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959, or a trust registered under the Bombay Public Trust Act, 1950, or any association of individuals whether registered or not.
key_definitions.technical_education: Any course of study in Engineering, Technology, Architecture, Ceramics, Industrial Training, Mining, or other subjects as specified by the State Government.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Prohibition of Admission of Students to the Un-Recognised and Un-affiliated Educational Institutions Act, 1992, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on May 28, 1992.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'commerce education', 'commerce institution', 'competent authority', 'educational institution', 'general education', 'medical education', 'special education', 'society', and 'technical education'.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of admission of students to un-recognised and un-affiliated educational institutions
main_sections.description: Prohibits the admission of students to any educational institution unless it has been granted permission or recognition by the State Government, University, Board, or other competent authority, and is affiliated to a University established under the Karnataka State Universities Act, 1976, for a specific course of study.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of admission of students in excess of intake
main_sections.description: Prohibits educational institutions from admitting students in excess of the intake capacity fixed by the University, State Government, Board, or other authority. Admissions made in excess of the intake are deemed invalid. Students admitted in contravention of this section or Section 3 are not eligible to appear for any examination.

Empowers the State Government to issue directions to examination boards or universities to conduct examinations for students admitted to new colleges or courses, or in excess of intake, where affiliation was not granted or where such students were not allowed to appear for examinations in the academic year 1991-92, to protect their interests.

Prescribes penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder. Penalties include imprisonment for a term not less than one year but not exceeding three years, a fine up to three thousand rupees, and a daily fine not exceeding two hundred and fifty rupees for continuing offences.

Deals with offences committed by companies, making the company and persons responsible for its business liable. It also covers offences committed with the consent or connivance of or due to neglect by directors, managers, secretaries, or other officers.
States that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under the Act except on a complaint made by the competent authority or an officer authorized by it.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of act done in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings against the Government or any officer, authority, or person empowered to exercise powers under the Act for anything done or intended to be done in good faith.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with a provision for laying such rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act through orders, provided such orders are made within two years from the commencement of the Act.

Repeals the Karnataka Prohibition of Admission of Students to the Un-Recognised and Un-affiliated Educational Institutions (No.2) Ordinance, 1992, and states that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: No student shall be admitted to an educational institution unless it is recognized/permitted by a competent authority and affiliated to a University under the Karnataka State Universities Act, 1976.
No educational institution shall admit students in excess of the prescribed intake capacity. Admissions in excess are invalid.
Students admitted in contravention of Sections 3 or 4 are ineligible to appear for any examination.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than one year but not exceeding three years.
Fine which may extend to three thousand rupees.
Daily fine not exceeding two hundred and fifty rupees for continuing offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Competent Authority, or an officer authorized by the Competent Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings initiated by the Competent Authority or its authorized officer, based on complaints. The State Government also has the power to issue directions to educational bodies and authorities.

duties: Duty of the Board, authority, or University to comply with directions issued by the State Government under Section 5.
Duty of educational institutions to adhere to recognition, affiliation, and intake limits.
obligations: Educational institutions have an obligation to ensure they are recognized, affiliated, and do not exceed intake limits before admitting students.
Companies and their responsible individuals have an obligation to ensure compliance with the Act, with provisions for accountability in case of offences.

key_procedures: Procedure for admission: Students can only be admitted to institutions that are recognized/permitted and affiliated. Intake limits must be adhered to.
Procedure for handling contraventions: Offences are to be taken up by the Competent Authority, leading to court cognizance based on their complaint.
Procedure for rule-making: The Government can make rules, which are then laid before the State Legislature for potential modification or annulment.
Procedure for removing difficulties: The Government can issue orders to resolve difficulties in implementing the Act within a specified period.
administration: The State Government, through the 'Competent Authority' appointed by notification, administers the Act. Various Boards, Universities, and authorities are involved in enforcement and compliance.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from May 28, 1992.
The Act overrides any inconsistent provisions in other existing laws.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
A specific provision allows the State Government to issue directions to facilitate examinations for students affected by admissions in the academic year 1991-92.

title: The Karnataka State Minorities Commission Act, 1994
purpose: To constitute a State Commission for minorities and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, aiming to safeguard the social, educational, and economic interests of minorities in Karnataka.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and concerns the constitution, functions, and administration of the Karnataka State Minorities Commission.

key_definitions.Commission: The Karnataka State Minorities Commission constituted under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.minorities: Persons belonging to minority communities residing in the State of Karnataka whom the Government has recognised as minorities.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and that it comes into force at once.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Government', 'member', and 'minorities'.

Details the establishment of the Karnataka State Minorities Commission by the Government, its headquarters in Bangalore, and its composition (Chairman and six other members, with a specific provision for minority community representation, and a Secretary).

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of the Chairman and members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairman and members (three years), resignation procedures, remuneration, and provisions for casual vacancies.

Outlines grounds for disqualification for appointment or continuation as Chairman or member, including conviction for certain offences, unsound mind, insolvency, dismissal from service, refusal to act, habitual absence from meetings, and abuse of position.

Enumerate the wide-ranging functions of the Commission, including examining safeguards for minorities, making recommendations for their effective implementation, monitoring policies and schemes, conducting studies on discrimination, assessing representation in services, promoting communal harmony, reporting to the Government, considering grievances, and looking into specific complaints. It also clarifies that if the National Commission for Minorities takes up a matter, the State Commission's jurisdiction ceases.

main_sections.section_title: Budget of the Commission and grants by the Government
main_sections.description: Deals with the financial provisions, requiring the Commission to prepare budget estimates, and the Government to provide grants for the Commission's functioning, subject to appropriation by the State Legislature.
Covers the maintenance of accounts, preparation of annual statements, annual audit by an auditor appointed by the Government, and the submission of reports to the Government.
Mandates the Commission to prepare and submit an annual report on its activities to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before the State Legislature
main_sections.description: Requires the Government to lay the annual report and audit report, along with a memorandum of action taken, before the State Legislature.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including rules regarding the status of the Chairman, salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service, and other matters necessary for implementation. These rules are subject to laying before the State Legislature.

important_rules: The Commission shall meet at least once in three months. (Section 8(1))
All orders and decisions of the Commission shall be authenticated by the Secretary or an authorized officer. (Section 8(3))
The Government shall lay the Commission's recommendations before the State Legislature with an explanation of action taken or proposed. (Section 10(2))
The Chairman and members of the Commission are deemed public servants under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code. (Section 16)

penalties: While specific penalties for contravention of the Act are not detailed in the provided text, Section 5 outlines disqualifications that can lead to removal from office.
Section 11 provides protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Government is responsible for constituting the Commission, appointing its members and Secretary, providing grants, and overseeing its functioning. The Commission itself enforces its mandate through its functions. The State Legislature plays a role in reviewing the Commission's reports and approving budgets.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the Commission's functions of monitoring, recommending, investigating grievances, and reporting. The Government's role in acting upon recommendations and laying reports before the Legislature also contributes to enforcement. The power to make rules and remove difficulties also aids in enforcement.

rights: Minorities have the right to have their social, educational, and economic interests safeguarded.
Minorities have the right to have their grievances considered and appropriate solutions suggested by the Commission.
Minorities have the right to have their specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards looked into by the Commission.
duties: The Government has a duty to constitute the Commission, provide it with funds, and act upon its recommendations.
The Commission has a duty to examine safeguards, make recommendations, monitor policies, conduct studies, and report its findings.
The Commission's Chairman, members, and authorized officers have a duty to act as public servants.
obligations: The Government is obligated to cause the annual report and audit report to be laid before the State Legislature.
The Commission is obligated to comply with directions given by the Government after perusal of the auditor's report.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission: Government constitutes the Commission comprising a Chairman, six members (with a majority from minority communities), and a Secretary. (Section 3)
Term of Office and Resignation: Chairman and members serve for three years, can resign in writing, and casual vacancies are filled for the unexpired term. (Section 4)
Functioning of the Commission: The Commission meets as needed (at least quarterly), regulates its own procedure, and its decisions are authenticated by the Secretary. (Section 8)
Reporting to Government: The Commission submits periodical reports and an annual report to the Government. (Sections 10(1)(g), 14)
Legislative Review: The Government lays the Commission's annual report and audit report before the State Legislature with explanations for action taken on recommendations. (Section 15)
Rule Making: The Government can make rules for the Act's implementation, which are then laid before the State Legislature for approval or modification. (Section 17)
administration: The Government of Karnataka is responsible for the overall administration and oversight of the Karnataka State Minorities Commission. The Secretary of the Commission acts as its Chief Executive.
important_notes: The Act provides for the conferment of statutory status on the State Minorities Commission. (Statement of Objects and Reasons)
If a matter is undertaken by the National Commission for Minorities, the State Commission ceases to have jurisdiction over it. (Section 10(1) proviso)
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith by the Commission or its members. (Section 11)
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the State Legislature and are subject to modifications or annulment by the Legislature. (Section 17(3))

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE OPEN UNIVERSITY ACT, 1992
purpose: To establish and incorporate an Open University at the State level for the introduction and promotion of Open University and distance education systems in the educational pattern of the State and for the co-ordination and determination of standards of such systems.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the establishment and functioning of the Karnataka State Open University, its officers, authorities, and the distance education system within the state.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.Board of Management: The Board of Management of the University.
key_definitions.Distance Education System: The system of imparting education through any means of communication such as broadcasting, telecasting, instruction media or print media, seminars, contact programmes or the combination of any two or more of such means.
key_definitions.employee: Any person appointed by the University and includes academic and administrative staff of the University.
key_definitions.University: The Karnataka State Open University established under section 3 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the provision for its commencement by notification in the Official Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Board of Management', 'Distance Education System', 'employee', 'University', 'Vice-Chancellor', and 'Registrar'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka State Open University, specifies its headquarters, its power to establish/maintain/recognize colleges, Regional Centres, and study centres. It also constitutes the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, and grants it the power to acquire and hold property and enter into contracts.

Outlines the primary objectives of the University, which include advancing and disseminating learning and knowledge through various means (including communication technology), providing opportunities for higher education to a larger population, promoting educational well-being, encouraging the distance education system, and coordinating standards.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction, planning courses, holding examinations, conferring degrees, establishing professorships, instituting scholarships, establishing Regional Centres and Study Centres, preparing instructional materials, organizing refresher courses, recognizing institutions, creating posts, receiving donations, borrowing money, entering contracts, and maintaining discipline. It also emphasizes the duty to promote open university and distance education systems.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds
main_sections.description: States that the University shall be open to all persons irrespective of sex, race, creed, caste, or class.

important_rules: Rule 1: The University shall be open to persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class.
Rule 2: The University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and shall sue and be sued by its name.
