Rule 3: The University shall be competent to acquire and hold property, both movable and immovable, and to manage it for its purposes.
Rule 4: The University shall have the power to provide for admission and instruction in various branches of knowledge, including technology and vocations, and to make provision for research.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the authorities of the University as established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, the powers vested in the University's authorities, and potential actions by the State Government as outlined in specific sections (e.g., power to remove difficulties).

rights: Right to establish and operate an Open University.
Right to provide higher education through distance learning.
Right to confer degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
Right to acquire and hold property.
Right to enter into contracts and agreements.
Right to admit students of all backgrounds.
duties: To advance and disseminate learning and knowledge.
To provide opportunities for higher education to a larger segment of the population.
To promote the educational well-being of the community.
To encourage the Open University distance education system.
To co-ordinate and determine the standards of distance education systems.
To take all steps for the promotion of open university and distance education systems.
To maintain discipline among students and employees.
obligations: To function in accordance with the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
To adhere to the objectives specified in the First Schedule.
To ensure admission and instruction are open to all classes, castes, and creeds.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University: To be established by the State Government via notification, with its headquarters specified. The University is constituted as a body corporate.

Conferment of Degrees/Diplomas: Achieved by holding examinations and conferring degrees, diplomas, certificates, or other academic distinctions/recognitions to persons who have pursued a course of study or conducted research as laid down by Statutes and Ordinances.
Establishment of Centres: The University can establish, maintain, or recognize colleges, Regional Centres, and Study Centres as it deems fit.
administration: The administration of the Act is primarily through the authorities of the Karnataka State Open University itself, with oversight and certain powers retained by the State Government (e.g., notification for commencement, specifying headquarters, power to remove difficulties).
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1.6.1996.
The Act has been amended by Act 16 of 2003 to provide for the continuation of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations of Mysore University and to validate actions taken.
The University has specific powers regarding distance education systems, including the use of communication technology, planning courses, and organizing instruction and evaluation.

title: The Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for ensuring transparency in public procurement of goods and services by streamlining the procedure in inviting, processing and acceptance of tenders by Procurement Entities, and for matters related thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the procurement of goods and services by Procurement Entities within the State of Karnataka. Procurement Entities include Government Departments, State Government Undertakings, Local Authorities, Boards, Bodies or Corporations established by or under any law and owned or controlled by the Government, and any other body or authority owned or controlled by the Government. Certain exceptions and limitations to applicability are outlined in Section 4.

key_definitions.Construction Works: Means putting up, demolishing, repairs or renovation of buildings, roads, bridges or other structures including fabrication of steel structures and all other civil works.
key_definitions.Goods: Means Machinery, Motor Vehicles, Equipment, Furniture, Articles of Stationary, textiles raw materials, drugs, scientific instruments, chemicals, food grains, oil and oil seeds or other commodity required for consumption, use or distribution by a Procurement Entity in discharge of its public duties.
key_definitions.Procurement Entity: Means any Government Department, a State Government Undertaking, Local Authority or Board, Body or Corporation established by or under any law and owned or controlled by the Government, and any other body or authority owned or controlled by the Government and as may be specified by it.
key_definitions.Public Procurement or procurement: Means purchase of goods, obtaining of services or undertaking of construction works by the procurement entities.
key_definitions.Services: Means the action of serving, attending upon, helping or benefiting a Procurement Entity in the course of discharging its public duties and includes construction works.
key_definitions.Specified goods or Services: Means the goods or services as the case may be specified in a tender and identified in the contract resulting from acceptance of a tender on account of a procurement entity.
key_definitions.Tender: Means the formal offer made for supply of goods or services in response to an invitation for tender published in a Tender Bulletin.
key_definitions.Tender Accepting Authority: Means an officer or a Committee appointed to accept tenders.
key_definitions.Tender Inviting Authority: Means an officer or a Committee appointed to invite tenders.
key_definitions.Tender Bulletin: Means a bulletin published for the State as a whole or for any district or districts within the State containing the details of invitation, processing and acceptance of Tenders.
key_definitions.Tender Bulletin Officer: Means a State Tender Bulletin Officer or a Tender Bulletin Officer referred to in section 7.
key_definitions.Tender Document: Means the set of papers detailing the schedule of works, calendar of events, requirement of goods and services, technical specifications, procurement criteria and such other particulars, as may be prescribed for evaluation and comparison of tenders.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act, 1999' and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from October 4, 2000.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Construction Works', 'Goods', 'Government', 'Procurement Entity', 'Public Procurement', 'Services', 'Specified goods or Services', 'Tender', 'Tender Accepting Authority', 'Tender Inviting Authority', 'Tender Bulletin', 'Tender Bulletin Officer', and 'Tender Document'.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions not to apply to certain Projects
main_sections.description: Specifies that the provisions of this Act will not apply to procurement of goods or services for projects funded by International Financial Agencies or covered under International Agreements, if those provisions are inconsistent with the specified procedures for such projects.

Lists various exceptions to the applicability of Chapter II of the Act, including procurement during natural calamities or emergencies, single-source procurements, procurements for standardization and compatibility, procurements from certain government entities for a specified period, procurements below certain monetary thresholds by specific government and local authorities, procurements under rate contracts, and specific procurements notified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Procurement other than by Tender Prohibited
main_sections.description: States that no Procurement Entity shall procure goods or services except by inviting Tenders for supply from the date of commencement of the Act.
Mandates that no tender shall be invited, processed, or accepted by a Procurement Entity except in accordance with the procedure laid down in the Act or the rules made thereunder.

Empowers the Government to appoint a State Tender Bulletin Officer for departments whose procurement covers more than one district. It also designates the Deputy Commissioner of the District as the District Bulletin Officer.

Outlines the responsibility of the Tender Bulletin Officer to publish the State or District Tender Bulletin upon receiving intimations regarding tender invitations, acceptances, or rejections. It also specifies that the Tender Bulletin shall be made available for sale.

main_sections.section_title: Tender Inviting Authority and Tender Accepting Authority
main_sections.description: Empowers Procurement Entities to appoint one or more officers or a committee of officers to be the Tender Inviting Authority and the Tender Accepting Authority for specified areas, procurements, or classes of goods or services.
Provides a mechanism for appeal against decisions made under the Act. (Specific details of the appeal process are not fully elaborated in the provided text snippet).

Specifies that a person contravening any provision of the Act or the rules made thereunder shall be punishable with a fine. (The exact penalty amount or further details are not fully elaborated in the provided text snippet).
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Procurement of goods or services must be done by inviting Tenders for supply (Section 5).
All tender processes (invitation, processing, acceptance) must adhere to the procedures laid down in the Act and its rules (Section 6).
Tender Bulletins must be published to provide details of tender invitations, acceptances, and rejections (Section 8).

Specific monetary thresholds apply for certain exemptions to Chapter II of the Act, particularly for construction works and other goods/services procured by various government and local authorities (Section 4(e) and 4(ee)).
Procurement during natural calamities or emergencies is exempted from Chapter II applicability (Section 4(a)).
Procurements from a single source or where exclusive rights exist are exempted from Chapter II applicability, subject to examination by an expert committee (Section 4(b)).

penalties: Contravention of any provision of the Act or the rules made thereunder shall be punishable with a fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act does not explicitly name a single enforcement authority in the provided text. Enforcement would likely involve the Procurement Entities, Tender Bulletin Officers, Tender Inviting Authorities, Tender Accepting Authorities, and potentially judicial or administrative bodies for appeals and penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is primarily through the adherence to prescribed procedures for tendering, publication of information via Tender Bulletins, and the imposition of penalties for contravention. Appeals mechanisms are also part of the enforcement framework.

rights: The right to participate in public procurement through submitting tenders.
The right to appeal decisions made under the Act.
duties: Procurement Entities have the duty to conduct procurements transparently by inviting tenders.
Procurement Entities have the duty to follow the prescribed procedures for inviting, processing, and accepting tenders.
Tender Bulletin Officers have the duty to publish Tender Bulletins.
Procurement Entities have the duty to provide accurate information related to tenders.
Officers involved in the procurement process are deemed to be Public Servants (Section 19).
obligations: Obligation to invite tenders for procurement of goods and services (Section 5).
Obligation to follow the laid down procedure in the Act and rules (Section 6).
Obligation to ensure transparency in the evaluation and acceptance of tenders (implied by the purpose of the Act).
Obligation to provide information and records when called for by designated authorities (Section 17, 18).

key_procedures: Invitation of Tenders: Procurement Entities must invite tenders for the supply of goods or services (Section 5).
Tender Bulletin Publication: Tender Bulletin Officers are responsible for publishing details of tender invitations, acceptances, and rejections in the Tender Bulletin (Section 8).
Appointment of Authorities: Procurement Entities are to appoint Tender Inviting Authorities and Tender Accepting Authorities (Section 9).
Procurement Process: Tenders are to be processed and accepted in accordance with the procedures laid down in the Act and its rules (Section 6).
Exceptions and Exemptions: Specific procedures and conditions apply for various exceptions to the general applicability of Chapter II, as outlined in Section 4.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Karnataka. Specific departments or bodies responsible for different aspects of administration (like appointing Tender Bulletin Officers) are mentioned.
important_notes: The Act aims to prevent irregularities in tender processing such as inadequate publicity, restricted supply of tender documents, and lack of transparency in evaluation and acceptance.
Chapter II, concerning the regulation of procurement, has several exceptions, particularly based on the type of procurement, value, or specific circumstances like natural calamities.
The Act was amended by Act 21 of 2001 and Act 4 of 2003, primarily to adjust monetary thresholds for exemptions and extend exemption periods.
Officers involved in the procurement process under this Act are deemed to be Public Servants (Section 19).
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 20).
The jurisdiction of Civil Courts is barred in certain matters (Section 21).
This Act overrides other laws where inconsistent (Section 22).

title: THE KARNATAKA URBAN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITIES ACT, 1987
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Urban Development Authorities for the planned development of major and important urban areas in the State and the areas adjacent thereto, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka, except for the Bangalore Metropolitan Area. It applies to urban areas and areas adjacent to them for the purpose of planned development.

key_definitions.authority: The Urban Development Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.amenity: Includes road, street, lighting, drainage, public works and such other conveniences as the Government may, by notification, specify.
key_definitions.betterment_tax: The tax payable under sections 20 and 21 in respect of an increase in the value of land resulting from the execution of a development scheme.
key_definitions.development: Carrying out of building, engineering or other operations in or over or under land or making of any material change in any building or land, and includes planning and redevelopment.
key_definitions.urban_area: Any local area within the jurisdiction of a local authority and includes such other area adjacent to the limits of the local authority as the Government may, from time to time, by notification specify.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka except Bangalore Metropolitan Area), and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Authority', 'amenity', 'betterment tax', 'development', and 'urban area'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and incorporation of the Authority
main_sections.description: Details the process of constituting an Urban Development Authority by the Government, its corporate status, and its members.
Outlines the primary objectives and functions that the Urban Development Authority is established to pursue.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Authority to undertake works and incur expenditure for development etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to undertake various works and incur necessary expenditure for the purpose of development.
Introduces the provision for levying a betterment tax on properties that benefit from a development scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to have power to acquire land by agreement
main_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to acquire land through mutual agreement.
Grants the Authority the power to borrow funds for its operations.
Confers upon the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have an overriding effect over other laws where there is an inconsistency.

important_rules: The Government may, by notification, constitute an Authority for any urban area for its development.
The Authority shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal, with power to acquire, hold, dispose of property and to contract.

The Authority shall consist of a Chairman, a town planner, an engineer, elected representatives, representatives of various boards, ex-officio members like the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner of Police, and other appointed members.
The Authority has the power to undertake works and incur expenditure for development schemes.
A betterment tax is leviable on lands whose value increases due to development schemes.
The Authority can acquire land by agreement or other statutory procedures.
The Authority has the power to borrow money for its functions.
The Act has overriding effect on other laws where there is inconsistency.
The Government has the power to make rules, and the Authority can make regulations and by-laws.

penalties: Penalty for breach of the provisions of the Act (Section 75).
Offences by companies (Section 55).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Urban Development Authority and its officers, with oversight and direction from the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Authority for development, acquisition, finance, and regulatory actions. Enforcement also involves penalties for breaches of the Act and prosecution of offences. The Government can also issue directions and review resolutions.

rights: Right to acquire land for development.
Right to levy betterment tax.
Right to borrow funds.
Right to sue and be sued.
duties: To undertake planned development of urban areas.
To execute development schemes.
To manage its finances and accounts.
To ensure adherence to rules and regulations.
To report its activities to the Government.
obligations: To act in accordance with the provisions of the Act and any rules or regulations made thereunder.
To ensure that areas reserved for parks, playgrounds, and civic amenities are not used for other purposes.
To submit annual estimates of income and expenditure for sanction.
To maintain accounts and get them audited.

key_procedures: Constitution and incorporation of an Urban Development Authority by the Government.
Formulation and sanction of development schemes by the Authority.
Acquisition of land for development schemes.
Levy, assessment, and recovery of betterment tax.
Preparation, submission, and sanction of annual estimates of income and expenditure.
Appointment of officers and servants.
Making of rules, regulations, and by-laws.
administration: The Act is administered by the Urban Development Authorities constituted under it, with overall supervision and direction from the State Government of Karnataka. The Department of Urban Development, Government of Karnataka, would typically be the nodal department.
important_notes: The Act has been amended by subsequent Acts, including Acts 17 of 1991, 14 of 1992, and 12 of 1996, indicating subsequent legislative changes and incorporations.
The Act specifically excludes the Bangalore Metropolitan Area, implying a separate regulatory framework for that region.
The commencement of the Act was notified on different dates for different urban areas and provisions, indicating a phased implementation.
Section 76 states that this Act overrides other laws in case of inconsistency, highlighting its supremacy in its domain.

title: THE KARNATAKA CEILING ON GOVERNMENT GUARANTEES ACT, 1999
purpose: To provide for ceiling on Government guarantees issued on behalf of Government Departments, Public Sector Undertakings, Local Authorities, Statutory Boards and Corporations, and Co-operative Institutions, and for promoting fiscal discipline in the State.
scope: This Act applies to the State Government of Karnataka and its government departments, public sector undertakings, local authorities, statutory boards and corporations, and co-operative institutions operating within Karnataka. It regulates the issuance of government guarantees.

key_definitions.Government Guarantee: Includes the guarantee given by the State Government on behalf of Departmental Undertakings, Public Sector Undertakings, Local Authorities, Statutory Boards and Corporations, and Co-operative Institutions.
key_definitions.Performance Guarantee: Includes documents such as letters of comfort, power purchase agreements, state support agreements, concession agreements for infrastructure projects, and other agreements guaranteed in certain performance on behalf of Government, Local Authorities, Statutory Boards and Corporations, and Co-operative Institutions, as well as Public Sector Undertakings.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 1999' and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Government', 'Government Guarantee', and 'Performance Guarantee'.

This section sets a limit on the total outstanding Government guarantees. It states that as of April 1st of any year, the total outstanding Government guarantees shall not exceed eighty percent of the State's revenue receipts of the second preceding year, as recorded by the Accountant General of Karnataka. A proviso exempts additional borrowing for the implementation of the Upper Krishna Project for utilizing water resources as per the Bachawath Award.

This section prohibits the issuance of Government guarantees under certain conditions: (1) no guarantee shall be given for a loan of any private individual, institution, or company; (2) no guarantee shall be extended to the Co-operation sector unless the share capital contribution from non-Government sources is at least ten percent of the total equity proposed.

This section mandates that the Government shall charge a minimum of one percent as guarantee commission, which cannot be waived. It includes a proviso (inserted by Act 15 of 2002) exempting this commission for guarantees extended during April 1, 2001, to March 31, 2002, for agricultural loans from specific cooperative banks, provided these banks reduce their lending interest rate by one percent for agricultural loans disbursed during that period. It also allows the Government to specify enhanced commission rates based on default risk.

This section addresses performance guarantees. It states that the Government may continue to provide performance guarantees for infrastructure projects. The Government is required to place a comprehensive report before both Houses of the State Legislature detailing potential future liabilities arising from failure to meet contractual obligations in performance guarantees, within six months of issuing such a guarantee.

important_rules: The total outstanding Government guarantees as on April 1st of any year must not exceed eighty percent of the State's revenue receipts of the second preceding year.
Government guarantees cannot be issued for loans of private individuals, institutions, or companies.
For guarantees to the Co-operation sector, non-Government sources must contribute at least ten percent of the total proposed equity.

A minimum guarantee commission of one percent must be charged and cannot be waived (with a specific exemption for agricultural loans from certain cooperative banks between April 1, 2001, and March 31, 2002).
The Government must submit a report on potential liabilities from performance guarantees to the State Legislature within six months of issuing them.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is responsible for enforcing this Act, including appointing notifications for commencement and specifying commission rates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves setting limits on guarantees, prohibiting certain types of guarantees, charging commissions, and requiring reporting to the legislature.

duties: The Government has the duty to set a ceiling on its guarantees.
The Government has the duty to charge a minimum guarantee commission (with exceptions).
The Government has the duty to report to the State Legislature on performance guarantee liabilities.
Specific cooperative banks have a duty to reduce interest rates if they benefit from the commission exemption.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the eighty percent revenue receipt ceiling for guarantees.
Obligation to comply with prohibitions on guaranteeing private loans and to ensure minimum non-Government equity for cooperative sector guarantees.
Obligation to charge and report guarantee commissions.
Obligation to submit performance guarantee reports to the Legislature.

key_procedures: Appointment of commencement date: The Government may, by notification, appoint the date on which the Act shall come into force.
Specification of enhanced commission rates: The Government may, by notification, specify an enhanced commission rate based on the default risk of a project.

Reporting on performance guarantees: The Government shall place a comprehensive report on potential liabilities arising from performance guarantees before both Houses of the State Legislature within six months of giving such a guarantee.
administration: The State Government is responsible for the administration of this Act, as indicated by its power to issue notifications and collect guarantee commissions.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 29.4.1999.
An amendment by Act 15 of 2002 modified Section 5(1) regarding guarantee commission for agricultural loans from specific cooperative banks between April 1, 2001, and March 31, 2002.

title: THE KARNATAKA CO-OPERATIVE TEXTILE MILLS (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER) ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills, Dharwar in public interest, to secure its proper management, and to ensure the continued manufacture, production, and distribution of yarn and cloth, which are essential to the country's economy, thereby also addressing unemployment.
scope: This Act applies to the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills, Dharwar, including its movable and immovable properties, and concerns the acquisition and transfer of these assets. It also covers the rights and liabilities of the lessor, lessee, and owners of land leased for the mill's purpose.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date on which the Act or any of its provisions comes into force.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of Payment appointed under Section 15.
key_definitions.company: The Karnataka State Textile Mills Private Limited, a company registered under the Companies Act, 1959.
key_definitions.karnataka_cooperative_textile_mills: The composite textile mill formerly run as New Karnataka Cotton Mills, Hubli, purchased by Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills Ltd., Dharwar, and leased to M/s. G. Mahadevappa & Sons (operating as Mahadev Textile Mills, Hubli). It includes all associated movable and immovable properties, as well as land leased for the mill's purpose.
key_definitions.lessee: The partnership firm M/s. Mahadevappa & Sons.
key_definitions.lessor: The Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills Ltd., Dharwar, a co-operative society.
key_definitions.owner_of_land: A person to whom land specified in the annexure belonged and was leased for the mill's purpose, including their heirs or legal representatives (inserted by Act 20 of 2005).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification in the Official Gazette, with different dates applicable to different provisions.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'Government', 'Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills', 'lessee', 'lessor', 'owner of land', 'present management', 'Schedule', and 'specified date'.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration under Article 31C of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of the Act are for implementing the State's policy to secure the principles laid down in clauses (a) and (b) of Article 39 of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of the Mills in the Government
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills, along with the rights, title, and interest of the lessor, lessee, and owner of land, shall be transferred to and vest absolutely in the Government.

Details that the vesting includes all assets, rights, leaseholds, powers, properties (movable and immovable), cash, investments, book debts, and other interests. It also clarifies that vested properties are freed from trusts, mortgages, leases, charges, liens, encumbrances, attachments, or injunctions.

main_sections.section_title: Lessor or lessee to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Specifies the liability of the lessor or lessee for certain liabilities incurred prior to the vesting.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Government to recover back wages, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the right to recover back wages, gratuity, and other amounts payable to employees.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to direct vesting of the mills in the company
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to direct the vesting of the mills in the designated company (Karnataka State Textile Corporation Private Limited).

main_sections.section_title: Amount to be given to lessor, lessee and other interested persons
main_sections.description: Outlines the amount to be paid to the lessor, lessee, and other interested parties.
Deals with the payment of any further amounts that may be due.
Concerns the management of the mills after acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of persons in-charge of management of the mills
main_sections.description: Defines the duties of those in charge of the mills' management.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons to account for assets, etc., in their possession
main_sections.description: Requires individuals in possession of assets or property related to the mills to account for them.
Covers the maintenance of accounts and their audit.
Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payment.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by the Government to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Deals with payments made by the Government to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Certain powers of the Government and the company
main_sections.description: Outlines specific powers of the Government and the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Specifies that claims against the acquired mills must be made to the Commissioner.
Establishes the order of priority for the payment of claims.
Describes the process for examining claims submitted to the Commissioner.
Details the procedure for admitting or rejecting claims.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of the amount by the Commissioner to the claimants
main_sections.description: Covers the disbursement of amounts by the Commissioner to the claimants.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of amount of the Lessor etc.
main_sections.description: Specifically addresses the disbursement of amounts related to the Lessor (inserted by Act 20 of 2005).

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amount to be deposited to the General Revenue Account
main_sections.description: Deals with the deposit of any undisbursed or unclaimed amounts into the General Revenue Account.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of officers or other employees of the Mills
main_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of service of officers and employees of the Mills.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of provident fund, welfare fund, etc.
main_sections.description: Covers the transfer of provident fund, welfare fund, and similar amounts.
States that this Act supersedes other laws in case of conflict.

main_sections.section_title: Contract to cease to have effect unless ratified by company
main_sections.description: Specifies that existing contracts will cease to have effect unless ratified by the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Deals with offences committed by companies.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing provisions and savings related to the Act.

important_rules: All movable and immovable properties of the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills, along with rights, title, and interests of the lessor, lessee, and owner of land, shall vest in the Government on the appointed day.
Vested properties shall be free from all encumbrances, including trusts, mortgages, leases, charges, and liens.
Mortgagees and persons with other interests in the property must provide intimation to the Commissioner of Payment.
Claims against the acquired mills must be submitted to the Commissioner of Payment.
The Act has an overriding effect over other laws.
Existing contracts will cease unless ratified by the Company.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

penalties: Section 29 specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions. (Specific details of penalties are not provided in the extract).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, and potentially the Commissioner of Payment and the Company.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of a Commissioner of Payment, examination and disbursement of claims, and penalties for non-compliance. The Government also has the power to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire and vest the mills.
Right of the Government to recover back wages, etc.
Right of mortgagees and other interested persons to claim payment out of the specified amount.
duties: Duty of persons in-charge of management to account for assets.
Duty of mortgagees and persons with other interests to provide intimation to the Commissioner.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to pay compensation to interested parties.
Obligation to manage the mills for public interest and continued production.
Obligation to ensure continued employment for workers.

key_procedures: Acquisition and vesting of the mills in the Government on the appointed day.
Appointment of a Commissioner of Payment to receive and process claims.
Examination, admission, or rejection of claims by the Commissioner.
Disbursement of amounts by the Commissioner to eligible claimants.
Transfer of service of employees of the mills.
Transfer of provident fund and welfare fund.
administration: The State Government, and through it, the Karnataka State Textile Corporation Private Limited (Company) and the Commissioner of Payment.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to replace the Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills (Acquisition and Transfer) Ordinance, 1986.
The Act was amended by Act 20 of 2005, effective from 30.06.1986, to include the 'owner of land' in the definition of Karnataka Co-operative Textile Mills and other relevant sections.
The primary objective is to acquire the sick mill for public interest, ensure its proper management, and continue the production of essential goods, while also safeguarding employment.

title: THE KARNATAKA CONTROL OF ORGANIZED CRIMES ACT, 2000
purpose: To make special provisions for the prevention and control of, and for coping with, criminal activity by organized crime syndicates or gangs, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and deals with organized crimes and activities of organized crime syndicates.

key_definitions.abet: Includes communication or association with a person known or believed to be engaged in assisting an organized crime syndicate, passing on information likely to assist an organized crime syndicate, or rendering any assistance to an organized crime syndicate.
key_definitions.continuing_unlawful_activity: An activity prohibited by law which is a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment of three years or more, undertaken by a member of or on behalf of an organized crime syndicate, with more than one charge-sheet filed in the preceding ten years and cognizance taken by a court.
key_definitions.organized_crime: Any continuing unlawful activity by an individual, singly or jointly, as a member of or on behalf of an organized crime syndicate, using violence, threat of violence, intimidation, coercion, or other unlawful means, with the objective of gaining pecuniary benefits, undue economic or other advantages, or promoting insurgency.
key_definitions.organized_crime_syndicate: A group of two or more persons who, acting either singly or collectively as a syndicate or gang, indulge in activities of organized crime.
key_definitions.special_court: A Special Court constituted under section 5 of the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'abet', 'continuing unlawful activity', 'organized crime', and 'organized crime syndicate'.
Specifies punishments for committing organized crime, conspiracy, abetment, harbouring members of syndicates, membership in a syndicate, and holding property derived from organized crime.
Empowers the State Government to constitute one or more Special Courts for specific areas or cases, and outlines the appointment and qualifications of judges for these courts.
Mandates that offences punishable under this Act shall be triable only by the Special Court within whose local jurisdiction the offence was committed.
Allows the State Government to appoint an officer, not below the rank of Secretary to Government in the Home Department, as the Competent Authority.
Deals with the provisions related to the forfeiture and attachment of property derived from or connected with organized crime.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.

important_rules: Punishment for organized crime includes imprisonment for life or death if it results in death, and imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment in other cases.
Membership in an organized crime syndicate is punishable with imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment.
Special Courts are constituted to try offences under this Act, with their jurisdiction being exclusive.
The Act allows for the forfeiture and attachment of property connected to organized crime.

penalties: Death or imprisonment for life and a fine of not less than one lakh rupees for organized crime resulting in death.
Imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment and a fine of not less than five lakh rupees for other organized crimes.
Imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment and a fine of not less than five lakh rupees for conspiracy, attempt, abetment, or facilitation of organized crime.
Imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment and a fine of not less than five lakh rupees for harboring or concealing syndicate members.
Imprisonment for not less than five years but up to life imprisonment and a fine of not less than five lakh rupees for being a member of an organized crime syndicate.
Imprisonment for not less than three years but up to life imprisonment and a fine of not less than two lakh rupees for holding property derived from organized crime.
Imprisonment for not less than three years but up to ten years and a fine of not less than one lakh rupees for possessing unaccountable wealth on behalf of a syndicate member.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, through police authorities and Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by designated authorities, trial by Special Courts, and application of special rules of evidence and procedures.

rights: Right to appeal against judgments, sentences, or orders of a Special Court to the High Court within thirty days.
Protection of witnesses.

key_procedures: Special Courts can take cognizance of offences upon receiving a complaint or police report.
Special Courts can try offences summarily under certain conditions, with provisions for re-hearing if necessary.
Special Courts can tender a pardon to an accused person for their full and true disclosure.
Trials by Special Courts have precedence over other cases involving the accused.
Special Courts have the power to transfer cases to regular courts if the offence is found not to be triable by it.
administration: The State Government, through the Home Department, is responsible for the administration of the Act, including the appointment of Special Courts, Public Prosecutors, and Competent Authorities.
important_notes: The Act has overriding effects, meaning its provisions prevail over any inconsistent laws.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
There are special rules of evidence and provisions regarding confessions made to police officers.

title: The Karnataka Fishing Harbour Terminals Authority Act, 1986
purpose: To provide for the constitution, systematic development and conservancy of Fishing Harbour Terminals in the State of Karnataka, and to manage and supervise fishing activities within these terminals, including levying and collection of port dues and other charges.
scope: The Act applies to fishing harbour terminals within the State of Karnataka, excluding areas within the limits of a major port as defined in the Ports Act, 1908. It governs the development, conservation, regulation, and control of these terminals, as well as fishing activities within them.

key_definitions.Authority: The Karnataka Fishing Harbour Terminals Authority constituted under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.fish: Includes all aquatic animals and plants of sea and estuary.
key_definitions.fishing harbour terminal: Any area notified as a fishing harbour terminal by the State Government, excluding areas within the limits of a major port.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint. Different dates can be appointed for different areas.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Authority', 'Chairman', 'fish', and 'fishing harbour terminal'.

States that the State Government may, by notification, constitute an Authority for the whole of Karnataka to develop, conserve, and administer fishing harbour terminals. The Authority is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

Details the members of the Authority, including the Minister in charge of fisheries (Chairman), Director of Fisheries, a nominee from the Ministry of Agriculture (Government of India), Director of Ports and Inland Water Transport, an officer from the Finance Department, Deputy Secretary (Fisheries), Chairmen of various fisheries corporations and federations, and nominated members from deep sea fishing vessel operators, fish merchants, fisher women's co-operative societies, the Navy, Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, and others connected with fishing interests. The Managing Director is the Secretary.

Outlines the functions of the Authority, including developing, conserving, regulating and controlling fishing harbour terminals; maintaining and supervising their functions; acquiring land and equipment; providing safety measures; ensuring hygienic handling of fish; executing works; preventing unauthorized use of explosives; promoting processing and storage facilities; levying and collecting fees; collecting statistics; and performing other functions assigned by the State Government.

Specifies the sources of funds for the Authority, including loans, grants, and advances from the State and Central Governments, loans from financial agencies, receipts from fees, rents, charges, and fines, and other sums from any other source.
Deals with penalties for offenses under the Act.
Empowers the Authority to make regulations, subject to the control of the State Government, for the transaction of business at its meetings and other matters.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: The Authority shall have a common seal and can acquire, hold, dispose of property and contract in its name.
The Minister in charge of fisheries in Karnataka shall be the Chairman of the Authority.
Nominated members of the Authority shall hold office for three years and be eligible for re-nomination, and they hold office during the pleasure of the State Government.
A member can be removed if they become subject to disqualifications, refuse or are incapable of discharging duties, are absent from three consecutive meetings without leave, or abuse their position.
The Authority shall meet at least once in three months.
All questions at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes, with the Chairman having a casting vote in case of a tie.
The quorum for a meeting shall be seven members.
The State Government shall appoint a Managing Director for the Authority.
The Authority shall maintain a separate fund for its financial operations.
The Authority shall prepare an annual budget.
The Authority's accounts shall be audited annually.
The Authority shall submit an annual report to the State Government.

penalties: Penalties for offenses under the Act (details not fully provided in the excerpt).
Abetment of offences is also punishable.
Punishment under other laws is not barred.
Provision for composition of offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Authority, and by extension the State Government and its appointed officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties, powers to remove and take into custody persons committing offenses in the fishing harbour terminal, and the general administrative and regulatory functions of the Authority.

rights: The Authority has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Authority has the right to sue and be sued.
The Authority has the right to levy and collect fees for facilities provided.
Members of the Authority and its staff are considered public servants.
duties: The Authority has the duty to develop, conserve, regulate and control fishing harbour terminals.
The Authority has the duty to maintain and supervise fishing harbour terminals.
The Authority has the duty to provide for safety measures.
The Authority has the duty to arrange quick and hygienic handling of fish.
The Authority has the duty to prevent unauthorized use of explosive materials.
The Authority has the duty to promote processing and storage facilities.
The Authority has the duty to collect statistics related to fishing.
The Authority has the duty to do other functions necessary for efficient discharge of its responsibilities.
The State Government has the duty to appoint a Managing Director and potentially other officers.
obligations: Members of the Authority and its staff have obligations as public servants.
The Authority has an obligation to prepare a budget and maintain accounts.
The Authority has an obligation to submit an annual report.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Authority by notification by the State Government.
Nomination of members to the Authority.
Conduct of meetings of the Authority, including quorum and voting procedures.
Preparation and submission of an annual budget.
Auditing of accounts.
Submission of an annual report.
Appeals to the Deputy Commissioner.
Revision processes.
administration: The Karnataka Fishing Harbour Terminals Authority, under the overall supervision and control of the State Government.
important_notes: The Act excludes the control of any Major Port in the State from its purview.
A representative from the Navy is to be included in the composition of the Authority.
The Head Office of the Authority is located at Malpe.

Members are subject to disqualification on grounds such as conviction involving moral turpitude, unsound mind, insolvency, dismissal from service, or having an interest in works or contracts of the Authority.
The State Government can make rules for the effective implementation of the Act.
The Authority can make regulations for its procedures and functioning.

title: The Karnataka Inland Fisheries (Conservation, Development and Regulation) Act, 1996
purpose: To provide for the conservation, development, and regulation of inland fisheries in the State of Karnataka, and to repeal existing acts that do not adequately cover these aspects. The Act aims to prevent the extinction of rare fish species and to manage inland fisheries scientifically.
scope: This Act applies to inland fisheries within the State of Karnataka. It explicitly excludes fishing and fishery in areas covered by the Karnataka Marine Fishing (Regulations) Act, 1986, national parks and sanctuaries declared under the Wild Life Protection Act, 1973, and areas beyond territorial waters.

key_definitions.Appellate Authority: An authority constituted by the State Government by notification to hear appeals.
key_definitions.Authorised officer: An officer not below the rank of Assistant Director of Fisheries, authorized by the State Government to exercise powers and discharge duties under the Act.
key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Inland Fisheries Advisory Board constituted under Section 8.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of Fisheries appointed by the State Government.
key_definitions.Fish: Includes shrimp, prawn, crab, lobster, molluscs, and their young ones.
key_definitions.Fish culture: Any activity related to breeding and rearing of fish through artificial processes.
key_definitions.Fishery: Any activity or occupation related to the conservation, development, and propagation of fish in any water area.
key_definitions.Fishing: Any act or activity connected with catching fish from any water.
key_definitions.Fishery products: All products derived from fish or their parts.
key_definitions.Fish Sanctuary: Any water area declared as such under Section 7 for protecting, propagating, or developing fisheries.
key_definitions.Fish seed: Spawn, fry, and fingerlings at their early stages.
key_definitions.Private water: Water that is the exclusive property of a person or in which a person has exclusive fishing rights.
key_definitions.Water: Means any water other than private water.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, the procedure for commencement through notification by the State Government, and specifies exclusions from the Act's application (Marine Fishing Act areas, Wildlife Sanctuaries, territorial waters).

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as Appellate Authority, Authorised officer, Board, Director, Fish, Fish culture, Fishery, Fishing, Fishery products, Fish Sanctuary, Fish seed, Private water, and Water.

Prohibits fishing in any water without a license granted under the Act. It allows for exemptions by the State Government and provides a grace period for existing fishers. It details the application process for licenses, grounds for refusal, license conditions, suspension/cancellation of licenses, and the appeal process.

Requires registration for anyone breeding fish for the sale of fish seeds. It outlines the application process, conditions for registration, and the possibility of cancellation with a right to be heard.

Empowers the authorized officer or other empowered officers to lease fishery rights in prescribed manners. It specifies the execution of lease deeds and provides an appeal mechanism for aggrieved persons.

Prohibits fishing using chemicals, explosives, poisons, poisonous weapons, or noxious materials. It also prohibits the capture, killing, or destruction of spawn, fry, fingerlings, juveniles, or breeding fish without authorization.

Authorizes the State Government to declare any water area as a 'fish sanctuary' for protection, propagation, or development of fisheries. Fishing or any activity detrimental to fish is prohibited in declared sanctuaries.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Inland Fisheries Advisory Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the Karnataka Inland Fisheries Advisory Board, specifying its maximum number of members (13) and their composition, including official members (Minister in charge, Secretaries from relevant departments, Director of Fisheries) and nominated members (legislators, persons from SC/ST, women, cooperative societies, fishermen community). It also outlines the duties of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for the membership of the Board
main_sections.description: Lists grounds for disqualification from being a member of the Board, including conviction for an offense involving moral turpitude, unsound mind, undischarged insolvency, previous dismissal from government service, having a share or interest in contracts with the Board, or acting as a legal practitioner for or against the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of nominated members
main_sections.description: Specifies that nominated members hold office for three years, subject to the State Government's pleasure and provisions for removal. It also details the resignation process for nominated members.

Outlines the conditions under which the State Government shall remove a nominated member, including becoming disqualified, refusing to act, being incapable of acting, or being absent from three consecutive meetings without leave of absence.

main_sections.section_title: Power of entry, search, seizure and detention
main_sections.description: Grants powers to authorized officers to enter, search, seize, and detain any vessel, net, gear, or any other appliance used in contravention of the Act's provisions.
Specifies penalties for contraventions of the Act's provisions. Fines are prescribed, which can increase for subsequent offenses.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters related to licenses, registration, lease of fishery rights, and other prescribed procedures.
Provides for the repeal of existing laws related to fisheries in the state and savings for actions taken or proceedings commenced under the repealed laws.

important_rules: No person shall fish in any water without a valid license granted under the Act (Section 3(1)).
No person shall breed fish for sale of fish seeds unless registered under the Act (Section 4(1)).
Fishing using chemicals, explosives, poisons, poisonous weapons, or noxious materials is prohibited (Section 6(a)).
Capture, killing, or destruction of spawn, fry, fingerlings, juveniles, or breeding fish is prohibited (Section 6(b)).
Fishing is strictly prohibited in any area declared as a fish sanctuary (Section 7(2)).
Nominated members of the Advisory Board hold office for a period of three years (Section 10(1)).

penalties: First offense: Fine up to one thousand rupees (Section 15).
Subsequent offenses: Fine up to two thousand rupees (Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, search, seizure, and detention; prosecution for offenses; and compounding of offenses.

rights: Right to apply for a fishing license (Section 3(2)).
Right to appeal against refusal, suspension, or cancellation of a license (Section 3(6)).
Right to apply for registration for fish breeding (Section 4(2)).
Right to appeal against orders related to leasing of fishery rights (Section 5(3)).
Right to be heard before license suspension or cancellation (Section 3(5)) or cancellation of registration (Section 4(4)).
Nominated members have the right to resign (Section 10(2)) and receive allowances (Section 8(5)).
duties: Duty of the Board to advise the State Government on conservation, development, and regulation of inland fisheries; assist in fisherman welfare; encourage fishery development; collect production statistics; and establish training institutions (Section 8(6)).
Duty of licensed persons to adhere to license terms and conditions.
Duty of registered persons to adhere to registration terms and conditions.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a fishing license before fishing (Section 3(1)).
Obligation to register for fish breeding for sale of fish seeds (Section 4(1)).
Obligation to comply with the terms and conditions of licenses and registrations.
Obligation to execute a lease deed in the prescribed form within the prescribed period upon obtaining fishery rights (Section 5(2)).

key_procedures: Application for a fishing license: Apply to the authorized officer in the prescribed form with the prescribed fee. The officer may grant or refuse based on inquiry and conservation considerations (Section 3(2), 3(3)).

Application for fish breeding registration: Apply to the authorized officer in the prescribed form with the prescribed fee. The officer may grant a certificate subject to prescribed terms and conditions (Section 4(2), 4(3)).
Leasing of fishery rights: Authorized officers or empowered officers lease fishery rights in the prescribed manner. Lease deeds must be executed as prescribed (Section 5(1), 5(2)).
Declaration of a fish sanctuary: The State Government issues a notification to declare an area as a fish sanctuary (Section 7(1)).

Appeal process: Appeals against orders related to licenses or fishery rights are made to the Appellate Authority within specified time limits, with provisions for condonation of delay (Section 3(6), 5(3)).
Board meetings: The Board convenes for meetings, with provisions for deputation of officers if official members cannot attend (Section 8(4), 13).
administration: The State Government, through its various departments including Fisheries, Irrigation, and Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, administers this Act. The Director of Fisheries and Authorised Officers play key roles in implementation.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 1st October 2003, as per a notification in the Karnataka Gazette (Footnote 1, page 2).

The Act is enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature under Entry 21 of List-II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, relating to fisheries (excluding fishing and fisheries beyond territorial waters).

The Act does not apply to fishing and fishery in areas specified under the Karnataka Marine Fishing (Regulations) Act, 1986, or in National Parks and Sanctuaries declared under the Wild Life Protection Act, 1973, or beyond territorial waters (Section 1(3)).

Existing fishers and breeders have a grace period of three months from the commencement of the Act to continue their activities and apply for licenses/registration (Section 3(1) proviso, Section 4(1) proviso).

title: The National Law School of India Act, 1986
purpose: To establish and incorporate the National Law School of India University at Bangalore with the objectives of advancing and disseminating learning and knowledge of law and legal processes, developing a sense of responsibility in students and scholars to serve society in the field of law, organizing activities to promote legal knowledge, and making law and legal processes efficient instruments of social development. The Act aims to encourage the establishment of a national-level institution in Karnataka for legal education.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the National Law School of India University located in Bangalore, Karnataka. It covers its incorporation, objects, powers, functions, authorities, officers, finances, and student admission and conduct.

key_definitions.Academic Council: The Academic Council of the School.
key_definitions.Bar Council of India: The Bar Council of India constituted under the Advocates Act, 1961.
key_definitions.Bar Council of India Trust: A public charitable trust created by the Bar Council of India.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the General Council.
key_definitions.Vice Chancellor: The Vice Chancellor of the School (formerly Director).
key_definitions.Executive Council: The Executive Council of the School.
key_definitions.General Council: The General Council of the School.
key_definitions.Regulations: Regulations of the School made under clause 31.
key_definitions.School: The National Law School of India University established under section 3.
key_definitions.Schedule: The Schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.Society: The National Law School of India Society registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960.
key_definitions.Chancellor: The Chancellor of the School (formerly Visitor).

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the National Law School of India Act, 1986, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on January 9, 1986.

This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'Bar Council of India', 'Bar Council of India Trust', 'Chairman', 'Vice Chancellor', 'Executive Council', 'General Council', 'Registrar', 'Regulations', 'School', 'Schedule', 'Society', and 'Chancellor'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and Incorporation of the National Law School of India University
main_sections.description: This section establishes the National Law School of India University in Karnataka, which is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It details the university's composition, powers to acquire property and contract, and the process for legal proceedings. The headquarters are located in Bangalore.

main_sections.section_title: The Objects of the School etc.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the primary objects of the School, which include advancing legal learning, developing a sense of responsibility in students, promoting legal knowledge through various activities, and making law an instrument of social development. It also states that the School is open to all individuals regardless of their background and prohibits religious tests for admission or employment.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the School
main_sections.description: This section details the extensive powers and functions of the School, including administering and managing the institution, providing instruction and research in law, organizing extra-mural teaching, granting degrees and diplomas, conferring honorary degrees, fixing fees, establishing hostels, creating and filling academic, administrative, and other posts, regulating employee discipline, instituting professorships and research posts, appointing teachers and researchers, awarding fellowships and scholarships, publishing research, cooperating with other organizations for legal education and research, and managing its finances and properties.

rights: Right to acquire and hold property.
Right to contract.
Right to sue and be sued.
Right to receive grants, subventions, subscriptions, donations, and gifts.
Right to purchase, lease, or accept land or buildings.
Right to construct, alter, and maintain buildings.
Right to sell, exchange, lease, or dispose of properties.
duties: Duty to advance and disseminate learning and knowledge of law and legal processes.
Duty to develop in students and research scholars a sense of responsibility to serve society in the field of law.
Duty to make law and legal processes efficient instruments of social development.
Duty to administer and manage the School and its centers for research, education, and instruction.
Duty to supervise and control the residence and regulate the discipline of students.
Duty to make arrangements for promoting the health of students.
Duty to regulate and enforce discipline among employees.
Duty to manage the accounts of the School.
Duty to provide for printing, reproduction, and publication of research and other works.
Duty to cooperate with other organizations in education, training, and research in law.

key_procedures: Establishment of the University: The State Government appoints a date for the establishment of the National Law School of India University. (Section 3(1))
Incorporation and Corporate Status: The School becomes a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with the power to acquire property and contract. (Section 3(2))
Legal Proceedings: All suits and legal proceedings involving the School are handled through the Vice-Chancellor, who signs and verifies pleadings and receives service of processes. (Section 3(3))
Admission of Students: The School is open to all persons of either sex irrespective of race, creed, caste, or class, and no religious test can be imposed for admission or employment. (Section 4(2))

Granting and Withdrawal of Degrees: The School has the power to hold examinations and grant diplomas, certificates, degrees, and other academic distinctions, subject to its conditions, and can withdraw them for good cause. (Section 5(iv))
Conferral of Honorary Degrees: The School can confer honorary degrees or other distinctions in the manner laid down in the regulations. (Section 5(v))
Appointment of School Review Commission: The State Government may appoint a School Review Commission to assess the working of the School. (Section 14)
Removal of Difficulties: Provisions are made for the State Government to remove difficulties at the commencement of the Act. (Section 16)
Transitory Provisions: Provisions are made for the transition to the Act. (Section 17)
administration: The Act itself establishes the National Law School of India University as the administrative body. Specific departments or agencies administering the act are not explicitly detailed in the provided text beyond the university's own structure (General Council, Executive Council, Academic Council, Officers). The State Government has a role in appointing the commencement date and potentially removing difficulties.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1993 to redefine the General Council's role as a chief advisory body and modify its powers, as suggested by the University Grants Commission.
The Act was further amended in 2004 to change the nomenclature of 'Director' to 'Vice-Chancellor' and 'Visitor' to 'Chancellor' to align with other Universities.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over other laws in case of conflict.
The Act includes provisions for repeal and savings, indicating that previous laws or enactments related to the School might be superseded.
The Act is effective from January 9, 1986.

title: THE KARNATAKA PAYMENT OF SUBSISTENCE ALLOWANCE ACT, 1988
purpose: To provide for the payment of subsistence allowance to employees during the period of suspension.
scope: The Act applies to employees and employers within establishments in Karnataka. It excludes offices or departments of the Central or State Government, railway administration, mines or oil fields, major ports, and public sector undertakings of the Central Government.

key_definitions.employee: Any person employed in an establishment doing skilled, semi-skilled, unskilled, manual, supervisory, technical, clerical, or any other kind of work for hire or reward, excluding those employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, or supervisory staff drawing wages exceeding five hundred rupees per month or exercising mainly managerial functions.
key_definitions.employer: The owner of an establishment, including any person entrusted with the supervision and control of employees in such establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Any place where any industry, trade, business, undertaking, manufacture, occupation, or service is carried on, within the executive power of the State, excluding government offices, railway administration, mines/oil fields, major ports, and central government public sector undertakings.
key_definitions.suspension: An interim decision by an employer barring an employee from attending to their work and performing functions in the establishment because an enquiry into grave charges is contemplated or pending, or a criminal offense complaint is under investigation or trial, and no final order has been passed.
key_definitions.wages: Has the same meaning as in clause (rr) of section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'employee', 'employer', 'establishment', 'Government', 'industry', 'suspension', and 'wages'.

Specifies the amount of subsistence allowance payable to a suspended employee (50% for the first 90 days, 75% for days 91-180, 90% thereafter), conditions for reduction, and when it is not payable. It also states that the allowance shall be paid on dates wages would have been payable.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of money due from an employer
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for an employee or their representative to apply to the Government for recovery of money due under the Act, with a time limit of one year for applications, extendable for sufficient cause.

main_sections.section_title: Savings of certain rights and privileges
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not affect any existing rights or privileges of an employee that are more favorable than those conferred by the Act.
Empowers the Government to exempt, by notification and subject to conditions, any class of establishments from the operation of all or any provisions of the Act, in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of powers of the Government
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to delegate its powers to subordinate authorities or officers, with provisions for withdrawal, restrictions, and control/revision.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder, including protection for the Government.
Prescribes penalties for contravening any provision of the Act or rules, including imprisonment and/or fine.

main_sections.section_title: Exemption of occupier or manager from liability in certain cases
main_sections.description: Allows an occupier or manager charged with an offense to bring the actual offender before the court, and if they prove due diligence and lack of knowledge/consent/connivance, the actual offender will be convicted, and the occupier/manager discharged from liability.
Stipulates that no court shall take cognizance of an offense except on a complaint by an authorized officer, and specifies the minimum court jurisdiction for trying offenses.

Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects of subsistence allowance payment, delegation of powers, and other prescribed matters. Rules are to be laid before the State Legislature.

important_rules: An employee under suspension is entitled to subsistence allowance: 50% of wages for the first 90 days, 75% for days 91-180, and 90% for periods exceeding 180 days.
Subsistence allowance for periods exceeding 90 days can be reduced to 50% if the delay in enquiry or criminal proceedings is directly attributable to the employee.
An employee is not entitled to subsistence allowance if they accept other employment during suspension.
Subsistence allowance paid shall be adjusted against full wages if the employee is exonerated.
Subsistence allowance must be paid on the dates wages would have normally been payable.
Applications for recovery of money due must be made within one year, with provision for extension for sufficient cause.

penalties: Contravention of any provision of the Act or rules is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or a fine not less than one thousand rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (State Government), or authorities/officers delegated powers by the Government. Enforcement of recovery of money due is done by the Deputy Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penal provisions for contraventions, and through a prescribed recovery process via the Deputy Commissioner for monetary dues. Complaints for offenses must be made by authorized officers.

rights: Right to receive subsistence allowance during suspension.
Right to have subsistence allowance adjusted against full wages upon exoneration.
Right to more favorable rights and privileges under existing laws, contracts, custom, or usage.
duties: Duty of the employer to pay subsistence allowance.
Duty of the employer to ensure due diligence in enforcing the Act (for Section 10).
obligations: Obligation of the employee to not accept other employment during suspension to be eligible for allowance.
Obligation for the occupier/manager to provide notice and bring the actual offender to court if claiming exemption from liability.

key_procedures: Payment of subsistence allowance: Employer pays the employee at prescribed rates during suspension.
Recovery of money due: Employee or representative applies to the Government, which issues a certificate to the Deputy Commissioner for recovery as arrears of land revenue.
Exemption of occupier/manager: The occupier/manager must give notice and bring the actual offender to court, proving due diligence and lack of knowledge/consent/connivance.
Cognizance of offenses: Complaint in writing by an authorized officer.
Rule-making procedure: Rules made by the Government are laid before the State Legislature for a total of thirty days.
administration: The State Government (referred to as 'Government' in the Act) and authorities/officers to whom powers may be delegated.
important_notes: The definition of 'employee' has specific exclusions for managerial/administrative staff and certain supervisory staff.
The definition of 'establishment' has specific exclusions for government bodies, railway administration, mines/oil fields, major ports, and central government public sector undertakings.
The Act is an enactment of the Karnataka State Legislature.
The Act received the assent of the President on December 24, 1988, and was first published on July 15, 1992.

title: THE KARNATAKA PREVENTION OF DANGEROUS ACTIVITIES OF BOOTLEGGERS, DRUG-OFFENDERS, GAMBLERS, GOONDAS, IMMORAL TRAFFIC OFFENDERS AND SLUM-GRABBERS ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the preventive detention of bootleggers, drug-offenders, gamblers, goondas, immoral traffic offenders, and slum-grabbers to prevent their dangerous activities that are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Karnataka and deals with specific categories of anti-social elements whose activities adversely affect public order. It covers bootleggers, drug offenders, gamblers, goondas, immoral traffic offenders, and slum-grabbers.

key_definitions.acting_in_any_manner_prejudicial_to_the_: This means engaging or preparing to engage in activities as a bootlegger, drug-offender, gambler, goonda, immoral traffic offender, or slum-grabber that adversely affect, or are likely to adversely affect, the maintenance of public order. Public order is deemed affected if the activities cause or are calculated to cause harm, danger, alarm, or a feeling of insecurity among the general public or any section thereof, or a grave or widespread danger to life or public health.
key_definitions.bootlegger: A person who distills, manufactures, stores, transports, imports, exports, sells, or distributes liquor, intoxicating drugs, or intoxicants in contravention of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, or any other law, or knowingly supports such activities, or abets them.
key_definitions.drug_offender: A person who manufactures, stocks, imports, exports, sells, or distributes drugs, cultivates plants, or does anything in contravention of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, or the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930, or any other law, or knowingly supports such activities, or abets them.
key_definitions.gambler: A person who commits or abets the commission of any offence punishable under Chapter VII of the Karnataka Police Act, 1963, including gambling related to 'matka'.
key_definitions.goonda: A person who, individually or as part of a gang, habitually commits, attempts to commit, or abets offences punishable under Chapters VIII, XV, XVI, XVII, or XXII of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
key_definitions.immoral_traffic_offender: A person who commits or abets the commission of any offence under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956.
key_definitions.slum_grabber: A person who illegally takes possession of land, enters into illegal tenancies/agreements, constructs unauthorized structures for sale/hire, gives such lands for unauthorized construction/use, provides financial aid for illegal possession/construction, collects rent/compensation through criminal intimidation, evicts occupiers by force without lawful procedure, or abets such acts.
key_definitions.unauthorised_structure: Any structure constructed without express written permission from the appropriate authority under the relevant law.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it is deemed to have come into force on December 15, 1984.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order', 'bootlegger', 'detention order', 'detenue', 'drug-offender', 'gambler', 'goonda', 'immoral traffic offender', 'slum-grabber', and 'unauthorised structure'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to issue detention orders against bootleggers, drug-offenders, gamblers, goondas, immoral traffic offenders, or slum-grabbers if satisfied that it is necessary to prevent them from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. It also allows District Magistrates or Commissioners of Police to exercise this power under certain conditions and for limited periods.
Specifies that detention orders can be executed at any place within the State in the same manner as warrants of arrest under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention
