main_sections.description: States that a person under a detention order is liable to be detained in a place and under conditions specified by the State Government, and can be removed from one detention place to another within the State.

main_sections.section_title: Detention orders not to be invalid or inoperative on certain grounds
main_sections.description: Ensures that detention orders are not invalidated simply because the person detained is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the issuing officer or the place of detention is outside those limits, provided both are within the State.

Provides that if a detention order is based on multiple grounds, it will not be invalid if one or more grounds are vague, non-existent, irrelevant, not connected, or otherwise invalid, as long as at least one ground remains valid.

main_sections.section_title: Powers in relation to absconding persons
main_sections.description: Details the powers the authorities have concerning persons who abscond or attempt to evade the execution of a detention order.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to persons affected by the order
main_sections.description: Mandates that the grounds on which a detention order has been made must be disclosed to the person affected by the order.
Provides for the constitution of an Advisory Board to consider detention orders.
Specifies the procedure for referring detention orders to the Advisory Board.
Outlines the procedural rules that the Advisory Board must follow.

main_sections.section_title: Action upon report of Advisory Board
main_sections.description: Describes the actions that the State Government must take based on the report submitted by the Advisory Board.
Prescribes the maximum duration for which a person can be detained under this Act.
Empowers the State Government to revoke or cancel a detention order.
Allows for the temporary release of persons who are under detention orders.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for any act done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Detention order against any bootlegger, drug-offender, gambler, goonda, immoraltraffic offender or slum-grabber to be made under this Act and not under National Security Act
main_sections.description: Clarifies that detention orders for the specified categories of offenders must be made under this Act and not under the National Security Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous provisions and savings related to the Act.

important_rules: Detention orders can only be made against individuals identified as bootleggers, drug offenders, gamblers, goondas, immoral traffic offenders, or slum-grabbers, who are acting or preparing to act in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
The grounds for detention must be communicated to the detained person.
Detention orders are subject to review by an Advisory Board.
The State Government has the power to regulate the place and conditions of detention, as well as to grant temporary release.
Detention orders will not be invalidated by minor technical defects in the grounds of detention, provided at least one valid ground exists.

penalties: The primary penalty is preventive detention as per Section 3.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, District Magistrates, Commissioners of Police, and their subordinates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance and execution of detention orders, regulation of detention places and conditions, and referral to an Advisory Board for review. Enforcement also involves actions against absconding persons.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds of detention (Section 8).
Right to have one's case considered by an Advisory Board.
duties: Duty of the State Government to ensure detention orders are made only when necessary to prevent acts prejudicial to public order.
Duty of detaining authorities to report detention orders and grounds to the State Government.
Duty of the State Government to act upon the report of the Advisory Board.
obligations: Detained persons are obligated to comply with the conditions of detention.
Authorities are obligated to follow the procedures laid out in the Act, including consulting the Advisory Board.

key_procedures: Issuance of a detention order by the State Government or authorized officers (Section 3).
Execution of the detention order as per CrPC warrants (Section 4).
Regulation of detention place and conditions (Section 5).
Reporting of detention order to the State Government by subordinate officers (Section 3(3)).
Disclosure of grounds to the detained person (Section 8).
Reference of the detention order to the Advisory Board (Section 10).
Consideration of the case by the Advisory Board (Section 11).
Action by the State Government based on the Advisory Board's report (Section 12).
Potential revocation of the detention order (Section 14).
Possibility of temporary release (Section 15).
administration: The State Government, along with District Magistrates and Commissioners of Police, are responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1987 to address procedural difficulties and technical grounds for challenging detention orders (Amending Act 22 of 1987).

The Act was further amended in 2001 to include persons engaged in committing or abetting offences against public tranquility under Chapter VIII and religious offences under Chapter XV of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Amending Act 16 of 2001).
The Act aims to provide a mechanism for preventive detention that is distinct from the National Security Act for the specified categories of offenders.

title: THE KARNATAKA REGULARISATION OF UNAUTHORISED CONSTRUCTIONS IN URBAN AREAS ACT, 1991
purpose: To provide for the regularisation of certain unauthorised constructions in urban areas in Karnataka, acknowledging the difficulty faced by local bodies in meeting the demand for sites due to a high number of such constructions and the impracticality and potential issues arising from wholesale demolition.
scope: This Act applies to unauthorised constructions within 'urban areas' as defined in the Act, which includes areas under City/Town Municipalities, Improvement Boards, Bangalore Metropolitan area, and areas defined under the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, 1987, plus any other adjacent areas notified by the State Government. It covers constructions made prior to January 1, 1995, subject to specific exclusions.

key_definitions.authority: Includes the Bangalore Development Authority, Urban Development Authorities constituted under the Karnataka Urban Development Authorities Act, 1987, and Improvement Boards established under the Karnataka Improvement Boards Act, 1976.
key_definitions.competent_authority: An officer appointed by the State Government, not below the rank of K.A.S. Group-A Senior Scale, responsible for scrutinizing applications for regularisation.
key_definitions.family: An individual, their spouse, and their unmarried minor children.
key_definitions.permanent_structure: Any building made of masonry, bricks, wood, mud, metal, or any other material.
key_definitions.revenue_site: A site formed without approval under town and country planning law or on land not diverted as per the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
key_definitions.unauthorised_construction: Any construction made without a building license, or with a license issued in violation of town and country planning or building erection laws. It includes appurtenant land up to a prescribed maximum extent.
key_definitions.urban_area: Areas within City/Town Municipalities, Improvement Boards, Bangalore Metropolitan area, Karnataka Urban Development Authorities, and other areas notified by the State Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government notification. The Act came into force on 1.8.1992.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Authority', 'Competent Authority', 'construction', 'family', 'permanent structure', 'revenue site', 'unauthorised construction', and 'urban area'.
Outlines the conditions under which unauthorised constructions made prior to January 1, 1995, in urban areas, can be regularised upon application. Excludes constructions mentioned in Section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Unauthorised constructions which shall not be regularised
main_sections.description: Lists specific types of unauthorised constructions that are explicitly excluded from regularisation, including those obstructing roads, in forest land or tank beds, on another person's land without title, in violation of the Urban (Land Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, on State/Central Government land, on land belonging to an Authority, or on land reserved for parks, play-grounds, or civic amenities.

Specifies conditions for eligibility, such as the applicant or their family not owning another building or site in the urban area and not seeking regularisation for more than one unauthorised construction.

Details the appointment of a Competent Authority by the State Government to scrutinize applications, conduct inquiries, and make provisional orders for regularisation, including provisional orders for the grant of appurtenant land on State Government property. It places the burden of proof for construction date on the applicant.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of amount and grant of land
main_sections.description: Requires the applicant to pay a prescribed amount within two months of receiving a provisional order. Upon payment, a final order is made, and for State Government land, a sale deed is executed. In other cases, the construction is regularised.

main_sections.section_title: Unauthorised constructions not regularised to be demolished
main_sections.description: Mandates the demolition of unauthorised constructions that are not regularised under the Act.

Provides for revision of orders passed or proceedings recorded by the Screening Committees (note: this section refers to Screening Committees, which were replaced by Competent Authorities by Act 27 of 1995, implying a potential for overlap or a transitional provision).
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Grants the State Government the power to make orders not inconsistent with the Act's provisions to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act.

important_rules: Regularisation is subject to rules prescribed by the State Government.
Unauthorised constructions made prior to January 1, 1995, are eligible for regularisation, provided they are not excluded by Section 4.
Applications for regularisation must be made before December 31, 1995.
The applicant or their family must not own any other building or site in the concerned urban area to be eligible for regularisation.
No person can seek regularisation for more than one unauthorised construction.
A prescribed amount must be paid by the applicant within two months of receiving a provisional order of regularisation.
Unauthorised constructions not regularised under the Act are liable for demolition.

penalties: Unauthorised constructions not regularised are to be demolished (Section 8).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the scrutiny of applications, holding inquiries, making provisional and final orders for regularisation, and ordering demolition of non-regularised constructions.

rights: Right to apply for regularisation of eligible unauthorised constructions.
Right to receive a provisional order for regularisation upon meeting initial criteria.
Right to obtain a sale deed for appurtenant land on State Government property upon payment and final order.
duties: Duty to apply for regularisation within the prescribed timeframe.
Duty to pay the prescribed amount for regularisation.
Duty to provide proof of construction date if seeking regularisation.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to ensure constructions comply with basic civic facilities and do not obstruct essential infrastructure.
Obligation to adhere to conditions set by the Competent Authority for regularisation.
Obligation to face demolition if the construction is not regularised.

key_procedures: Application for regularisation by the owner of an unauthorised construction.
Scrutiny of the application by the Competent Authority.
Holding of an inquiry by the Competent Authority.
Issuance of a provisional order of regularisation by the Competent Authority.
Payment of the prescribed amount by the applicant within two months.
Issuance of a final order of regularisation by the Competent Authority.
Execution of a sale deed for appurtenant land on State Government property, if applicable.
Demolition of constructions not regularised.
administration: The State Government has the overall administrative control, appointing Competent Authorities and making rules. The Competent Authority is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of regularisation processes.
important_notes: The Act has been amended multiple times, notably by Acts 9 of 1994, 29 of 1994, and 27 of 1995, which have expanded the scope of regularisation (e.g., including commercial constructions, constructions in green belt areas, more floors) and adjusted deadlines.
Section 8A mentions 'Screening Committees', but Section 6 was substituted by Act 27 of 1995 to appoint 'Competent Authority', suggesting a shift in the designated body.

The Act aims to regularise constructions made on State Government land, revenue sites, and certain other categories, but explicitly excludes numerous types of constructions that would be detrimental to urban planning and public interest.

title: THE KARNATAKA RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT, 2000
purpose: To provide for the right of access to information to the citizens of the State, promoting openness, transparency, and accountability in administration, and ensuring effective participation of people in the administration, making democracy meaningful.
scope: The Act applies to all public authorities in the State of Karnataka. This includes offices of the State Government, local authorities, authorities constituted by State Legislature acts, and companies, corporations, trusts, societies, statutory or other authorities, cooperative societies, or organizations funded, owned, or controlled by the State Government. It excludes offices of the Central Government, establishments of armed forces or Central Para Military forces, and bodies or corporations owned or controlled by the Central Government.

key_definitions.competent_authority: Head of the office or any officer or person notified by the State Government for the purpose of this Act. If an application is transferred, the officer or person to whom it is transferred is also deemed the Competent Authority.
key_definitions.information: Information relating to any matter concerning the affairs of the administration or decisions of a public authority.
key_definitions.public_authority: Includes all offices of the State Government (including Karnataka Public Service Commission), local authorities, authorities constituted by State Legislature acts, and companies, corporations, trusts, societies, statutory or other authorities, cooperative societies, or organizations funded, owned, or controlled by the State Government. Excludes Central Government offices and entities.
key_definitions.right_to_information: The right of access to information from any public authority, obtainable by certified copies of records, diskettes, floppies, electronic modes, print-outs, or other prescribed methods.
key_definitions.record: Includes documents, manuscripts, files, microfilm, microfiche, facsimile copies, reproductions of images, and any material produced by a computer or other device.
key_definitions.trade_secret: Information contained in a formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, product, method, technique, or process that is not generally known and may have economic value.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification. Different dates can be appointed for different provisions.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Competent authority', 'Information', 'Public authority', 'Right to Information', 'record', and 'Trade secret'.

Mandates public authorities to maintain records in a catalogued and indexed manner, and to publish specific information such as their organization, functions, duties, powers of officers, decision-making procedures, norms, facilities for information access, and relevant facts concerning important decisions and policies affecting the public.

Establishes the right to information for every citizen, subject to certain exemptions. These exemptions include information that could prejudicially affect India's sovereignty, security, strategic interests, international relations, public safety, fair trial, Cabinet papers (with exceptions for decisions and reasons), internal discussions, tax assessment, parliamentary privilege, trade secrets, economic interests, and information related to legal custody or impeding investigations.

Outlines the procedure for applying for information, including making an application in the prescribed manner with a fee. The competent authority must respond within fifteen working days, either granting or refusing the request with reasons. If the authority doesn't have the information, they must transfer the application to the relevant officer within fifteen days.

main_sections.section_title: Grounds for refusal to supply information in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies additional grounds for refusal, such as requests that are too general, relate to information required to be published at a specific time, or are contained in published material. It also includes refusal for disclosure of personal information without public interest, with an exception for government servants' asset and liability returns.

Provides a two-tier appeal process. A person aggrieved by an order of the competent authority or by non-receipt of information within the stipulated period can appeal to a prescribed appellate authority within thirty days. A second appeal can be preferred to the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal against the order of the appellate authority. Appeals must be disposed of within thirty days.
Empowers the State Government to make provisions to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, provided such provisions are not inconsistent with the Act.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions. The provided text does not detail the penalty amounts or specific contraventions.

States that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit, application, or other proceedings in respect of any order made by the competent authority or appellate authority under this Act.
Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which will be laid before the State Legislature.
Provides for the repeal of the Karnataka Right to Information Ordinance, 2000, and includes savings provisions.

important_rules: Public authorities must maintain records in a catalogued and indexed manner (Section 3(a)).
Public authorities must publish information regarding their organization, functions, duties, powers of officers, decision-making processes, norms, and facilities for citizens (Section 3(b)).
Public authorities must publish facts concerning important decisions and policies that affect the public (Section 3(c)).
Before sanctioning or initiating projects/schemes, public authorities must publish relevant facts to the public (Section 3(d)).
Citizens have the right to information, subject to specific exemptions outlined in Section 4 (Section 4(1)).
Applications for information must be made in the prescribed manner with a fee, not exceeding the actual cost of supply (Section 5(1)).
The competent authority must respond to information requests within fifteen working days (Section 5(2)).
If a request is rejected, the competent authority must communicate the reasons, appeal period, and appellate authority details in writing (Section 5(3)).
Appeals against orders or non-receipt of information must be filed within thirty days (Section 7(1)).
Appeals must be disposed of within thirty days (Section 7(4)).

penalties: The Statement of Objects and Reasons mentions a penalty on the competent authority up to two thousand rupees for failure to give information without reasonable cause (Statement of Objects and Reasons, point (v)). Specific details of penalties are not fully elaborated in the provided text of Section 9.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The primary enforcement is through the 'Competent authority' within each public authority, and the appellate authorities (prescribed authority and the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is achieved through the application process outlined in Section 5, the appeal process in Section 7, and potential penalties for non-compliance. The overarching effect of the Act is ensured by Section 11 (overriding effect) and the bar of jurisdiction of civil courts (Section 10).

rights: Every citizen has the right to access information from any public authority (Section 4(1)).
The right to information includes obtaining certified copies, electronic copies, and print-outs (Section 2(d)).
The right to appeal against rejection of information requests or non-receipt of information (Section 7(1)).
duties: Public authorities have a duty to maintain records in a catalogued and indexed manner (Section 3(a)).
Public authorities have a duty to proactively publish specific information (Section 3(b), (c), (d), (e)).
The competent authority has a duty to consider applications, provide information or reasons for refusal within fifteen working days (Section 5(2), (3)).
The competent authority has a duty to assist in reframing requests if rejected on grounds of being too general (Section 6(a)).
obligations: Public authorities are obligated to make information available, subject to exemptions.
Citizens are obligated to make applications for information in the prescribed manner and pay the prescribed fee (Section 5(1)).
The State Government has an obligation to appoint competent authorities and appellate authorities, and make rules for the Act's implementation (Sections 2(a), 7(1), 12).

key_procedures: Requesting Information: A person applies to the competent authority in the prescribed manner with a fee. The authority must respond within 15 working days, either granting the request or providing reasons for refusal and appeal details. If the authority lacks the information, they must transfer the application to the correct officer within 15 days and inform the applicant.

Appealing a Decision: A person aggrieved by an order of the competent authority or non-receipt of information within 15 working days can appeal to a prescribed appellate authority within 30 days. A second appeal can be filed with the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal. Appeals are to be disposed of within 30 days.
administration: The State Government is responsible for appointing competent authorities, prescribing procedures and fees, and making rules for the implementation of the Act. The Karnataka Appellate Tribunal serves as the second appellate authority.
important_notes: The Act came into force on different dates for different provisions (Section 1(2)). Sections 1 and 12 were effective from 12.10.2001, while Sections 2 to 11 and 13 (except 3(c) and 3(d)) were effective from 18.07.2002.
Information disclosure is subject to exemptions listed in Section 4, which are crucial for maintaining national security, public order, and efficient administration.
Information regarding Cabinet decisions and the reasons leading to them shall be made available, as will be government orders based on these decisions with explanations (Section 4(2)(c) proviso).

Internal discussions and advice are exempt, but records of advice, opinions, or recommendations related to executive decisions or policy formulations must be made available after the decision or formulation (Section 4(2)(d) proviso).
Returns of assets and liabilities filed by any Government servant are to be made available to the public, even if they are considered personal information (Section 6(d) proviso).

title: The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment etc) Act, 1990
purpose: To provide for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of members of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in the State Civil Services, establishments in the public sector, and in admission to universities and educational institutions established, maintained, or aided by the State Government, ensuring their adequate representation.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and covers reservation of appointments or posts in State Civil Services, establishments in the public sector (including co-operative societies, educational institutions, government companies, local authorities, statutory bodies, corporations, and universities), and admission to universities and educational institutions established, maintained, or aided by the State Government. It also includes provisions for issuing and verifying caste certificates.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date notified by the State Government under sub-section (2) of Section 1.
key_definitions.appointing_authority: The authority empowered to make appointments to a particular service or post.
key_definitions.establishments_in_public_sector: Includes co-operative societies, educational institutions, government companies, local authorities, statutory bodies, corporations, and universities as defined in the Act.
key_definitions.other_backward_classes: Communities, castes, and tribes notified by the State Government under Article 15(4) and 16(4) of the Constitution.
key_definitions.scheduled_castes: Scheduled Castes specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, as amended.
key_definitions.scheduled_tribes: Scheduled Tribes specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, as amended.
key_definitions.service_or_post: A civil service or civil post under the State of Karnataka, including services or posts in public sector establishments.
key_definitions.unfilled_vacancies: Includes backlog in direct recruitment, vacancies not filled by SC/ST due to regularization of daily wage employees, and shortfalls in representation of SC/ST in direct recruitment vacancies to reach prescribed percentages.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointments, etc.,) Act, 1990' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'appointing authority', 'establishments in public sector', 'other backward Classes', 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes', 'service or post', and 'unfilled vacancies'.

Specifies certain categories of posts to which the Act does not apply, such as posts for research, scientific posts, tenure posts, posts filled by contract, and posts requiring specific qualifications not covered by reservation.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of appointments or posts etc.
main_sections.description: This section, though not fully detailed in the provided text, is implied to be the core provision for mandating reservation of appointments or posts in favor of SC, ST, and OBC.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Caste Certificate and income and caste certificate
main_sections.description: Details the authority competent to issue Caste Certificates to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and Caste-cum-income Certificates to Other Backward Classes, and the procedure for such issuance. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997)
Provides for an appeal against an order passed by the authority competent to issue Caste Certificates or Caste-cum-income Certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997)

main_sections.section_title: Verification of caste certificate and Income and caste certificate
main_sections.description: Concerns the verification of caste certificates and caste-cum-income certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997)
Provides for appeals against decisions related to the verification of caste certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997)
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Details the procedures for taking cognizance of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of records and submission of annual report etc.
main_sections.description: Requires the maintenance of records and submission of annual reports related to reservation.
Provides for the constitution of a Standing Committee.
Specifies the functions to be performed by the Standing Committee.
Relates to the submission and content of the annual report.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Empowers the State Government to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. (Amended by Act 7 of 2004 to provide for laying rules before the State Legislature).

important_rules: The Act mandates reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes in appointments/posts and admissions to educational institutions.
Caste Certificates and Caste-cum-income Certificates are to be issued by competent authorities as specified by the Act and subsequent amendments.
Provisions exist for appeals against orders related to the issuance and verification of caste certificates.
Unfilled vacancies for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are addressed through special recruitment measures as defined in the Act.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of the State Legislature.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the provisions of the Act (Section 5).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, appointing authorities, and designated authorities for issuing and verifying certificates are responsible for enforcement. The exact enforcement mechanism and specific authorities for different sections are elaborated within the Act and its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the mandatory implementation of reservation policies, adherence to procedures for issuing and verifying certificates, and penalties for non-compliance. The Act also provides for appeals to ensure fairness.

rights: Members of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes have the right to benefit from reservations in appointments, posts, and educational admissions.
Individuals have the right to obtain Caste Certificates and Caste-cum-income Certificates.
Individuals have the right to appeal against decisions concerning their caste status and related certificates.
duties: Appointing authorities have a duty to implement reservation policies as prescribed.
Institutions and government bodies have a duty to maintain records and submit annual reports related to reservation.
The State Government has a duty to notify backward classes and frame rules to implement the Act.
obligations: Obligation to ensure adequate representation of SC, ST, and OBC in services and educational institutions.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for the issuance and verification of caste certificates.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding unfilled vacancies.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining Caste Certificates and Caste-cum-income Certificates (Section 4A).
Procedure for appeal against orders of certificate issuing authorities (Section 4B).
Procedure for verification of caste certificates (Section 4C).
Procedure for appeal against verification decisions (Section 4D).
Procedure for filling unfilled vacancies (implied by definition of 'unfilled vacancies').
Procedure for laying rules before the State Legislature (amendment to Section 13).
administration: The Social Welfare Department is mentioned as a nodal department in the context of special recruitment rules (Statement of Objects and Reasons IV). The overall administration and rule-making power rests with the State Government.
important_notes: The Act has been amended multiple times (by Acts 27 of 1997, 7 of 2004, and 8 of 2004) to address specific issues like certificate issuance, appeals, verification, and filling backlog vacancies.
The Act does not apply to certain categories of posts, including those for research, scientific posts, tenure posts, and contract-based positions.
The definition of 'unfilled vacancies' is crucial for understanding the Act's provisions related to backlog recruitment.
The Act ensures that actions taken in good faith are protected.

title: THE KARNATAKA SCHEDULED CASTES, SCHEDULED TRIBES AND OTHER BACKWARD CLASSES (RESERVATION OF APPOINTMENT ETC) ACT, 1990
purpose: To provide for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of members of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in State Civil Services, establishments in the public sector, and in admissions to universities and educational institutions established or maintained or aided by the State Government, as these groups are not adequately represented.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka, specifically to: State Civil Services, establishments in the public sector (including cooperative societies, educational institutions, government companies, local authorities, statutory bodies, corporations, and universities), and admissions to universities and educational institutions established, maintained, or aided by the State Government. It aims to ensure adequate representation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date notified by the State Government under sub-section (2) of section 1 when the Act comes into force.
key_definitions.appointing_authority: The authority empowered to make appointments to a specific service or post.
key_definitions.establishments_in_public_sector: Includes cooperative societies, state-aided educational institutions, government companies, local authorities, statutory bodies/corporations owned/controlled by the State Government, and universities established by state law.
key_definitions.other_backward_classes: Communities, castes, and tribes notified by the State Government under Article 15(4) and 16(4) of the Constitution.
key_definitions.scheduled_castes: As specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, made under Article 341 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.scheduled_tribes: As specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, made under Article 342 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.service_or_post: A civil service of or a civil post under the State of Karnataka, including those in establishments in the public sector.
key_definitions.unfilled_vacancies: Includes backlog in direct recruitment, vacancies not filled by SC/ST in direct recruitment while regularizing daily wage employees, and shortfalls in direct recruitment vacancies to reach 15% for SC and 3% for ST representation as of the commencement of the Second Amendment Act, 2004.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on a date notified by the State Government. The Act came into force on 1.6.1992.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'appointing authority', 'establishments in public sector', 'other backward Classes', 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes', 'service or post', and 'unfilled vacancies'.
Specifies exemptions from the Act's provisions, including posts for research, scientific posts, tenure posts, posts filled by contract, and a list of other excluded categories.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of appointments or posts etc.

main_sections.description: Deals with the authority and procedure for issuing caste certificates and caste-cum-income certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997).
Provides for an appeal mechanism against orders issued under section 4A concerning caste and income certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997).

main_sections.section_title: Verification of caste certificate and Income and caste certificate
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for verifying caste certificates and caste-cum-income certificates. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997).
Provides for an appeal against the orders of the verification committee. (Introduced by Amending Act 27 of 1997).

Requires the submission of an annual report to the State Legislature. (Content not fully available in provided text).

main_sections.description: Protects individuals acting in good faith under the provisions of the Act from legal proceedings. (Content not fully available in provided text).

rights: Right to reservation in appointments/posts and educational admissions for members of SC, ST, and OBC.
Right to obtain Caste Certificates and Caste-cum-Income Certificates.
Right to appeal against orders related to certificate issuance and verification.
duties: Duty of the State Government to ensure adequate representation of SC, ST, and OBC.
Duty of appointing authorities to implement reservation policies.

Obligation to adhere to the notified classifications and reservations for OBC.

The Act provides for reservations in both appointments/posts and educational admissions.

title: THE KARNATAKA STATE COMMISSION FOR BACKWARD CLASSES ACT, 1995
purpose: To constitute a Commission for Backward Classes of citizens other than the Scheduled Castes and Schedule Tribes in the State of Karnataka to ensure their social and economic development, examine requests for inclusion/exclusion from backward classes lists, survey their social and educational conditions, and supervise the implementation of welfare schemes.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka. It concerns the identification and welfare of Backward Classes of citizens, excluding Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.Backward Classes: Such class or classes of citizens other than the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as may be notified by the State Government in the list from time to time.
key_definitions.Commission: The Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes constituted under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.Lists: Lists prepared by the State Government for making provisions for reservation in favour of Backward Classes of citizens under Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification. (Act came into force on 1.12.1997).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Backward Classes', 'Commission', 'Lists', and 'member'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Karnataka Commission for Backward Classes
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes with its headquarters in Bangalore. It details the composition of the Commission, including the Chairman, members, and Member Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairman and Members
main_sections.description: Prescribes the term of office (three years), resignation procedures, and grounds for removal of the Chairman and members. It also mentions that vacancies will be filled by fresh nomination and that salaries, allowances, and terms of service will be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission
main_sections.description: States that the State Government shall provide necessary officers and employees for the Commission and that their terms and conditions of service will be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries and allowances to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: Specifies that salaries and allowances for the Chairman, members, and employees are to be paid out of the grants referred to in section 12(1).

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that the proceedings of the Commission are not invalidated due to any vacancy or defect in its constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to meet as necessary, regulate its own procedure, and mandates that its orders and decisions be authenticated by the Member-Secretary or an authorized officer.

Outlines the primary functions of the Commission: examining requests for inclusion/exclusion of classes in Backward Classes lists, making surveys of social and educational conditions, and supervising the implementation of welfare schemes. It also states that the Commission's advice shall ordinarily be binding on the Government.

Grants the Commission the powers of a civil court trying a suit, including summoning persons, examining on oath, requiring production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, issuing commissions, and other prescribed matters.

main_sections.section_title: Periodic revision of lists by the State Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to revise the lists of Backward Classes every ten years to include new backward classes or exclude those who are no longer backward, requiring consultation with the Commission.
Details the provision of grants by the State Government to the Commission for its purposes and allows the Commission to spend these grants for performing its functions.

Lays down provisions for the keeping of accounts, preparation of annual statements of accounts, annual audit by a government-appointed auditor, and submission of audit reports to the State Government.
Requires the Commission to prepare and submit an annual report on its activities to the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before the State Legislature
main_sections.description: Mandates that the State Government lay the annual report and audit report, along with a memorandum of action taken, before each House of the State Legislature. It also allows the Commission to submit special reports.

main_sections.section_title: Chairman, members and employees of the Commission to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairman, members, and employees of the Commission as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, which will be laid before the State Legislature.
Grants the State Government powers to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functions and powers vested in the Commission, including its advisory role, and through the State Government's power to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Right to have social and economic development for Backward Classes.
Right to have requests for inclusion/exclusion from Backward Classes lists examined.
Right to have welfare schemes supervised.
Right to be heard if facing removal from office (for Chairman/members).
duties: Duty of the Commission to examine requests, conduct surveys, and supervise schemes.
Duty of the State Government to constitute the Commission, provide staff, make grants, and consult the Commission during list revisions.
Duty of the Commission to regulate its procedure and authenticate its decisions.
Duty of the Commission to prepare annual reports and accounts.
Duty of the State Government to lay reports before the Legislature.
obligations: The Commission's advice is ordinarily binding on the Government.
The Commission must comply with directions from the State Government after perusal of audit reports.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the State Legislature.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission: The State Government constitutes the Commission with a Chairman, members, and a Member Secretary.
Term of Office and Removal: Chairman and members serve for three years and can resign. Removal is subject to specific grounds and a prior hearing.
Functions Execution: The Commission performs its functions by examining requests, conducting surveys, and supervising schemes, with its advice being ordinarily binding.
Powers of Civil Court: The Commission exercises powers similar to a civil court for its functions.
List Revision: The State Government undertakes periodic revision of Backward Classes lists in consultation with the Commission.
Finance and Audit: The Commission receives grants from the State Government, maintains accounts, and undergoes annual audits.
Reporting: The Commission prepares and submits annual reports to the State Government, which are then laid before the State Legislature.
Rule Making: The State Government can make rules for the Act, which are then presented to the State Legislature.
administration: The State Government and the Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes.
important_notes: The Act excludes Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes from its purview of 'Backward Classes'.
The Commission's advice is ordinarily binding on the Government.
The Act came into force on 1st December 1997.
Amendments were made by Act 24 of 1997, notably regarding the eligibility criteria for the Chairman and the number of members.

title: THE KARNATAKA ANATOMY ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the supply of unclaimed bodies of deceased persons or donated bodies or any part thereof of deceased persons to hospitals and medical and teaching institutions for the purpose of anatomical examination and dissection and other similar purposes.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. Applies to unclaimed bodies in hospitals, prisons, and public places, and to donated bodies or parts thereof for anatomical examination and dissection.

key_definitions.approved institution: A hospital or a medical college or an allied institution declared by the State Government as such for the purposes of the Act.
key_definitions.authorised officer: An officer authorised by the State Government under section 3.
key_definitions.hospital: Any hospital established or maintained by the State Government or by a local authority, and any other hospital declared as such by the State Government.
key_definitions.person interested: A near relative or any other person interested in the disposal of the deceased person's body according to religious usage or social custom. 'Near relative' includes wife, husband, parent, son, daughter, brother, sister, and other specified relatives by consanguinity or marriage.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under the Act.
key_definitions.unclaimed body: The body of a person who dies in a hospital, prison, or public place, and which is not claimed by any person interested within the prescribed time.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Anatomy Act, 1957. It extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and specifies its commencement in different areas.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'approved institution', 'authorised officer', 'hospital', 'person interested', 'prescribed', and 'unclaimed body'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to authorise officers to act under section 4
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to authorize officers to act under section 4 and declares these officers as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Unclaimed dead bodies in hospitals, prisons and public places how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for dealing with unclaimed bodies in hospitals, prisons, and public places, including reporting to the authorized officer and handing over to approved institutions for anatomical examination and dissection.

main_sections.section_title: Donation of bodies or any part thereof of deceased persons for anatomical examination etc.
main_sections.description: Introduces provisions for the donation of bodies or parts thereof by individuals before their death for anatomical examination, subject to certain conditions and consents.

main_sections.section_title: Doubt or dispute as to near relative to be referred to Magistrate of the First Class
main_sections.description: Mandates that any doubt or dispute regarding a 'person interested' be referred to a Magistrate of the First Class, whose decision shall be final.
Specifies penalties for the improper disposal of unclaimed bodies or obstruction of authorized personnel.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Police and other officers to assist in obtaining possession of unclaimed bodies
main_sections.description: Obligates Police, Medical, Public Health Departments, local authority staff, and village officers to assist authorized officers in their duties.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for anything done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals certain previous Anatomy Acts in force in specific areas and provides for the continuity of actions taken under those repealed Acts.

important_rules: Unclaimed bodies in hospitals, prisons, or public places must be reported to the authorized officer and, if required, handed over to approved institutions for anatomical examination and dissection.
The body or part of a body donated for anatomical examination cannot be removed within forty-eight hours of death or until twenty-four hours' notice is given to the Executive Magistrate.
A certificate from a registered medical practitioner stating the manner and cause of death is required before the removal of a donated body or part thereof.
If an inquest or postmortem is likely to be required, the removal of a donated body or part thereof needs the consent of the authority empowered to hold such proceedings.

penalties: Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for disposing of, or abetting the disposal of, an unclaimed body otherwise than as provided by the Act.
Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for obstructing authorized personnel from handing over, taking possession of, removing, or using dead bodies for the purposes specified in section 4.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers appointed by the State Government, along with Police and other relevant departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through reporting procedures, possession of unclaimed bodies, handing over to approved institutions, and legal proceedings for violations of the Act.

rights: Right of 'persons interested' to claim bodies according to religious usage or social custom (subject to the Act's provisions).
duties: Duty of authorities in charge of hospitals and prisons, and police officers, to report unclaimed bodies.
Duty of Police and other officers to assist authorized officers in obtaining possession of unclaimed bodies.
Duty to obtain consent of relevant authorities if an inquest or postmortem is likely to be required before removing a donated body.
obligations: Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for the handling and disposal of unclaimed and donated bodies.
Obligation to ensure that donations of bodies are made with informed consent and without subsequent revocation.

key_procedures: Reporting of unclaimed bodies by hospital, prison, or police authorities to the authorized officer.
Authorized officer taking possession of unclaimed bodies and handing them over to approved institutions for anatomical examination.

Procedure for donation of bodies: expressing intention in writing, obtaining consent of interested persons (unless objection is known), and adhering to conditions regarding time of removal, notice to Magistrate, and medical certification.
Referral of doubts or disputes regarding 'persons interested' to a Magistrate of the First Class.
administration: The State Government, through authorized officers and rules made under the Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to standardize the law relating to anatomy across the State of Karnataka.
The Act was amended in 1999 to include provisions for the donation of bodies or parts thereof by individuals before death.
Actions taken under repealed Acts are deemed to have been taken under this Act unless superseded.

title: The Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Transfer of Staff of Department of Collegiate Education) Act, 2012
purpose: To provide for the regulation of transfer of Principals, teaching or non-teaching staff of the Department of Collegiate Education to ensure transparency and availability of such staff in Government First Grade Colleges throughout the State.
scope: Applies to teaching or non-teaching staff of the Department of Collegiate Education, excluding the posts of Director, Additional Director, Joint Director, and Deputy Director, within the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.appointment: Means appointment by direct recruitment, by posting or by promotion.
key_definitions.appointing_authority: Means the concerned authority competent to make appointment to any post in the Karnataka Collegiate Education Department Service.
key_definitions.competent_authority: Means the authority competent to make orders of transfer or appointment of staff of the Department of Collegiate Education. The Government is the competent authority for Principals, and the Commissioner of Collegiate Education for other teaching or non-teaching staff.
key_definitions.deputation: Means deployment of the services of staff, fully or partially, from one Office/Government First Grade College of the Department of Collegiate Education to another Office or Government First Grade College without shifting the lien.
key_definitions.government_first_grade_college: Means all First Grade Colleges belonging to the State Government, whatever name they are called.
key_definitions.non_teaching_staff: Means a person appointed to any category of non-teaching posts of Group-A, Group-B, Group-C or Group-D in various offices or Government First Grade College or Department of Collegiate Education belonging to the State Civil Services and such other posts as specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.principal: Means a person appointed to a category of post of a Principal Grade-1 (U.G.) or Principal Grade-II (P.G) in a Government First Grade College belonging to the Department of Collegiate Education specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.process_of_counseling: Means the process of computerized counseling by giving opportunity to a person considered for appointment or a Government servant considered for transfer to opt a place or post on priority which is being given based on the length of the service put in by him in the place where he is working and such other criteria as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.staff_of_department_of_collegiate_educat: Means Principal, teaching staff or non-teaching staff of the Department of Collegiate Education.
key_definitions.schedule: Means Schedule appended to this Act.
key_definitions.teaching_staff: Includes persons appointed to teaching posts such as professor, Associate Professor/Assistant Professor, Librarian, and Physical Culture Instructor in Government First Grade Colleges belonging to the Department of Collegiate Education Services, as specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.transfer: Means posting of a staff from one post or office to another post or office from one place of working to a post in another place of working and includes transfer within or outside the same Zone or cadre.
key_definitions.unit_of_seniority: For Principals, teaching and non-teaching staff (except Group-D), it's the State. For Group-D posts, it's the district.
key_definitions.zone: Specific areas classified for staff transfer: Zone-A (Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and Bangalore Development Authority limits, City Corporations, District Headquarters and City Municipal Councils/City Municipalities), Zone-B (Taluk Headquarters and Town Municipalities excluding Zone-A areas), and Zone-C (areas outside Zone-A and Zone-B).

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its applicability to teaching and non-teaching staff of the Department of Collegiate Education (excluding certain higher posts), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including appointment, appointing authority, competent authority, deputation, Government First Grade College, non-teaching staff, principal, process of counseling, staff of Department of Collegiate Education, Schedule, teaching staff, transfer, unit of seniority, and zones (Zone-A, Zone-B, Zone-C).

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory appointment of a Principal, teaching or non-teaching staff to Zone-C
main_sections.description: Mandates that vacancies in Zone-C be filled first during initial appointments. It also details the process for creating vacancies in Zone-C by transferring staff from Zone-C to Zone-B and Zone-B to Zone-A, and outlines conditions for transferring staff with penalties or criminal charges to Zone-C.
States that transfers under this Act will be conducted through a counseling process. It specifies that Group-D staff can be transferred within a district, or to another district only on request.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of Principal, teaching or non-teaching staff (excluding Group-D) in the interest of public service
main_sections.description: Requires transfer of staff who have served continuously for more than the prescribed number of years in the same place in Zone-C, to another zone in the public interest. It also includes a proviso that staff with less than two years to superannuation will not be transferred outside Zone-A unless they request it.

Limits the total number of transfers in a unit of seniority to eight percent of the sanctioned strength of the respective cadre. It also allows for a prescribed percentage of transfers under special categories.

Allows for shifting of teaching posts within the same Zone or to another Zone (from C to B, and B to A) if there is insufficient workload in a subject in a particular college and sufficient workload elsewhere.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of Teaching Staff/Non –Teaching Staff working in a shifted post
main_sections.description: States that staff working in shifted posts will be transferred within the same zone according to the provisions of Sections 3, 4, and 5.

Provides exceptions to the minimum period of stay in a place or zone, including cases where both spouses are government employees and working in different zones, or where the staff is a widow or physically challenged.
Concerns the regulation of deputation of staff.
Deals with penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Specifies how offences under the Act will be taken cognizance of.
States that this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Grants the State Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the State Government to amend the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Gives the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Provides for transitional arrangements.

important_rules: Vacancies in Zone-C must be filled first during initial appointments.
Transfers under this Act will be conducted through a counseling process.
Staff serving in Zone-C for more than the prescribed period may be transferred to another zone in public interest.
The total number of transfers in a unit of seniority shall not exceed eight percent of the sanctioned strength.
Teaching posts can be shifted if workload is insufficient, first within the same Zone, then to Zone-B or Zone-A if necessary.
Exceptions to minimum tenure include cases of spouse transfers for government employees, widows, and physically challenged individuals.

penalties: Section 11 outlines penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and its appointed authorities, including the Commissioner of Collegiate Education.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the stipulated transfer processes, counseling, and adherence to the rules and regulations laid out in the Act and associated rules.

rights: Right to opt for a place or post based on priority during counseling.
Right to request transfer to another district for Group-D staff (on request).
Right to continue in Zone-C or Zone-B if eligible for transfer to Zone-B or Zone-A respectively, but desires to continue (under certain conditions).
Exceptions to tenure for spouses working in different zones, widows, and physically challenged individuals.
duties: Duty of appointing authorities to ensure Zone-C vacancies are filled first.
Duty to follow the prescribed counseling process for transfers.
Duty to comply with transfer orders issued in public interest.
Duty to adhere to restrictions on the percentage of transfers.
obligations: Obligation to serve in designated zones according to the Act's provisions.
Obligation to undergo transfer if deemed necessary in public interest or due to post shifting.
Obligation for staff with disciplinary or criminal proceedings to be transferred to Zone-C if applicable.

key_procedures: Initial appointment and transfer to ensure Zone-C vacancies are filled first.
Transfer through a computerized counseling process where staff can opt for places/posts based on priority.
Creation of vacancies in Zone-C by transferring staff from Zone-C to Zone-B and Zone-B to Zone-A.
Shifting of posts due to workload disparities.
Application of exceptions to the minimum tenure rules in specific personal circumstances.
administration: Department of Collegiate Education, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act came into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
The Karnataka State Civil Services Act, 1978 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1990) applies to words and expressions not defined in this Act.
Staff with less than two years of service for superannuation will not be transferred outside Zone-A unless on their request.

title: THE KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY (TAXATION ON CONSUMPTION) ACT, 1959
purpose: To provide for the levy of tax on the consumption of electrical energy in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the levy and collection of tax on the consumption of electrical energy by consumers.

key_definitions.consumer: Includes a local authority, company or other person to whom energy is supplied by a licensee on payment of charges or otherwise, and a licensee or other person who consumes energy generated by himself. It excludes a licensee to whom energy is supplied by the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation for supply to others, unless that licensee consumes any part of the energy himself. The word 'consume' with its grammatical variations is construed accordingly.
key_definitions.licensee: Means: (a) Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation incorporated as a transmission company under the Companies Act, 1956 (this expression is deemed to include the Karnataka Electricity Board for energy supplied prior to the effective date of transfer of property, interest, rights, and liabilities under the Karnataka Electricity Reform Act, 1999); (b) any person licensed under Part II of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, to supply energy, and includes any person who has obtained the sanction of the State Government under section 28 of the said Act; and (c) the State Government when it is engaged in the business of supplying energy.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Electricity (Taxation on Consumption) Act, 1959. It specifies that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It also details the commencement date, with most provisions deemed to have come into force on July 1, 1959, except for section 13.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'consumer', 'energy', 'licensee', 'notification', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of tax on electricity charges
main_sections.description: Specifies the levy of an ad valorem tax (electricity tax) at five percent on the electricity charges payable by all consumers, excluding consumers under agricultural (irrigation pump sets up to and inclusive of Ten Horse Power), Bhagya jyothi, and Kutira jyothi categories.

Mandates that every licensee shall collect and pay the electricity tax to the State Government at the prescribed time and manner, based on electricity charges included in the bill issued to the consumer. The tax is a first charge on amounts recoverable by the supplier. It also outlines provisions for rebates to licensees for the cost of collection, not exceeding two percent of the collected tax. It further states that any person who consumes energy not supplied by a licensee is liable to pay tax as prescribed.

Requires licensees to keep books of account, registers, and documents in the prescribed form, and to produce them for inspection by authorized officers. It also mandates maintaining separate accounts for energy consumed and supplied, and tax collected and paid.
Empowers the State Government to appoint officers to inspect the books of account, registers, and other documents of any licensee or consumer for the purposes of the Act.
Details the procedure for the recovery of any tax or penalty due under the Act, which can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to notify exemptions and reductions of tax
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to notify exemptions from or reductions in the electricity tax payable under the Act, either generally or for specified classes of consumers or areas, and for specified periods.

main_sections.section_title: Dispensing with the performance of certain contracts
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to direct that, for a specified period, no licensee shall be required to perform any contract which requires him to reimburse or indemnify any consumer for any tax levied or increased under this Act. This provision aims to prevent unjust enrichment of industries at the expense of consumers and conserve state resources.
Specifies penalties for various offenses under the Act, including failure to collect or pay tax, making false statements, or obstructing inspection. Penalties can include fines or imprisonment.

Confers power on the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, including rules for prescribing forms, time and manner of payment, collection of tax, and other incidental matters.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and Notifications to be laid before State Legislature
main_sections.description: Requires all rules and notifications made or issued under this Act to be laid before the State Legislature for a prescribed period, allowing for their modification or annulment.
Repeals any existing law relating to the levy of tax on electricity consumption, subject to savings provisions for actions taken or rights accrued under the repealed law.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No. 2 of 1959 and savings
main_sections.description: Repeals the Karnataka Ordinance No. 2 of 1959, with savings provisions for actions taken or rights accrued under the Ordinance.
Grants the State Government the power to make orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Every licensee shall collect and pay the electricity tax to the State Government at the prescribed time and manner, based on electricity charges included in the bill issued to the consumer. The tax is a first charge on amounts recoverable by the supplier. (Section 4(1))
Rule: A rebate may be granted to licensees for the cost of collection, not exceeding two percent of the electricity tax collected. (Section 4(2))

Rule: Licensees must keep books of account, registers, and documents in the prescribed form and produce them for inspection. Separate accounts for energy consumed and supplied, and tax collected and paid, must be maintained. (Section 5)
Rule: The State Government can exempt or reduce the electricity tax for certain classes of consumers or areas. (Section 8)

penalties: Failure to collect or pay tax: Fine which may extend to twice the amount of tax due, or imprisonment, or both.
Making false statements: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine, or both.
Obstructing inspection: Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting Officers appointed by the State Government, and the State Government itself.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of accounts, recovery of tax as arrears of land revenue, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Right of licensees to collect electricity tax from consumers.
Right of the State Government to receive the collected electricity tax.
Right of licensees to be granted a rebate for the cost of collection (up to 2%).
Right of consumers to be billed correctly for electricity charges and applicable tax.
duties: Duty of every licensee to collect and pay the electricity tax to the State Government.
Duty of licensees to maintain proper books of account and registers.
Duty of consumers to pay the electricity charges and the electricity tax levied.
Duty of consumers to cooperate with inspecting officers.
obligations: Licensees are obligated to remit the tax collected to the State Government.
Licensees are obligated to provide energy at the prescribed tariffs.
All persons consuming energy are obligated to pay the applicable tax.

key_procedures: Collection and Payment of Tax: Licensees collect tax from consumers as part of their electricity bills and pay it to the State Government at prescribed times and in the prescribed manner. (Section 4(1))
Inspection of Accounts: Authorized officers can inspect the books of account, registers, and documents of licensees and consumers to verify compliance with the Act. (Section 6)
Recovery of Arrears: Any tax or penalty due under the Act can be recovered as arrears of land revenue. (Section 7)
Application for Exemption/Reduction: Consumers or licensees may seek exemptions or reductions in tax, which the State Government may grant through notifications. (Section 8)
administration: The State Government, through its appointed officers and departments, administers this Act. The Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation and other licensed entities are responsible for collection and remittance.
important_notes: The Act has been amended several times to enhance tax rates, adjust limits for exemptions, and align with changes in electricity sector legislation.
Section 8A allows the State Government to dispense with certain contractual obligations related to tax reimbursement to prevent unjust enrichment and conserve state resources.
The Act's provisions related to the levy and collection of tax apply to the entire State of Karnataka.
Specific categories like agricultural consumers with small pump sets, Bhagya Jyothi, and Kutira Jyothi are exempted from the tax as per Section 3.

title: The Karnataka Existing Laws (Construction of References to Values) Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the construction of references in existing laws to values expressed in annas, pice and pies, in relation to new coins (Naye Paise).
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka. It covers existing laws, including Acts, Ordinances, regulations, notifications, rules, orders, bye-laws, and schemes that have the force of law within the State, except for those to which sub-section (3) of section 14 of the Indian Coinage Act, 1906, is already applicable.

key_definitions.existing_law: Means any Act, Ordinance or regulation having the force of law in the whole or any part of the State of Karnataka relating to any matter with respect to which the Karnataka State Legislature has power to make laws or any notification, rule, order, bye-law, scheme or other instrument issued or made thereunder, other than any enactment, notification, rule or order to which the provisions of sub-section (3) of section 14 of the Indian Coinage Act, 1906 (Central Act III of 1906), are applicable.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Existing Laws (Construction of References to Values) Act, 1957, and that it shall come into force on the first day of April, 1957.
Defines 'existing law' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to certain values in existing laws
main_sections.description: Mandates that all references to values expressed in annas, pice, and pies in any existing law shall be construed as references to those values expressed in new coins (Naye Paise), converted at the rate specified in sub-section (2) of section 14 of the Indian Coinage Act, 1906.

important_rules: Rule 1: All references to values in annas, pice, and pies in existing laws must be interpreted in terms of Naye Paise, using the conversion rates from the Indian Coinage Act, 1906.
Rule 2: The Act's provisions apply to 'existing laws' as defined, excluding specific enactments covered by the Indian Coinage Act, 1906.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be authorities responsible for the application of laws within the State of Karnataka.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the interpretation and application of existing laws by courts and administrative bodies according to the provisions of this Act.

duties: Duty 1: To construe references to annas, pice, and pies in existing laws as references to Naye Paise at the prescribed conversion rates.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but the Act is administered by the State Legislature of Karnataka and its judicial and executive branches.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act was enacted in response to the introduction of new coins (Naye Paise) under the Indian Coinage Act, 1906.
Note 2: The Act is adapted by the Karnataka Adaptations of Laws Order, 1973.

title: The Karnataka Habitual Offenders Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the treatment and training of habitual offenders.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. Applies to habitual offenders as defined in the Act, and addresses registration, movement restrictions, corrective training, penalties, and miscellaneous provisions related to such offenders.

key_definitions.corrective settlement: Any place established, approved or certified as a corrective settlement under section 13.
key_definitions.District: The territorial division constituting a district for the purpose of the Code and includes the City of Bangalore.
key_definitions.District Magistrate: The Deputy Commissioner of the District.
key_definitions.habitual offender: A person who, during any continuous period of five years, has been sentenced on conviction on not less than three occasions, since attaining the age of eighteen years, to a substantive term of imprisonment for any one or more of the scheduled offences, committed on different occasions. The period spent in jail under sentence or detention is not counted.  The sentence must not have been reversed in appeal or revision.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered offender: A habitual offender whose name and other particulars are entered in a Register made under a direction issued under section 3 or who is re-registered under section 9.
key_definitions.scheduled offence: An offence specified in Schedule A or an offence analogous thereto.
key_definitions.Superintendent of Police: The Superintendent of Police having jurisdiction over the area.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act (The Karnataka Habitual Offenders Act, 1961), its territorial extent (the whole of the State of Karnataka), and its commencement date, which is appointed by the Government through a notification in the Official Gazette.

Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Code', 'corrective settlement', 'District', 'District Magistrate', 'habitual offender', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'registered offender', 'scheduled offence', and 'Superintendent of Police'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to direct registration of habitual offenders.
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to direct the District Magistrate to create and maintain a Register of habitual offenders within their district, including their names, previous convictions, and other prescribed particulars.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of notice to habitual offenders and enquiry regarding entries to be made in the Register.
main_sections.description: After a notification under section 3, the District Magistrate or an appointed officer must issue a notice to every habitual offender, requiring them to appear, provide information, and allow finger and palm impressions, footprints, and photographs to be taken. Entries are made only after affording the offender an opportunity to show cause and after verifying previous convictions.

main_sections.section_title: Charge of register and alterations therein.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Register of habitual offenders will be kept by the Superintendent of Police, who will report necessary alterations to the District Magistrate. No fresh entries or cancellations can be made except by or under the written order of the District Magistrate.
