main_sections.section_title: Power to take finger impressions, etc., at any time.
main_sections.description: Grants the District Magistrate or an appointed officer the authority to order the taking of finger and palm impressions, footprints, and photographs of any registered offender at any time.

main_sections.section_title: Registered offenders to notify every change of residence and to report themselves.
main_sections.description: Mandates registered offenders to notify any change or intended change of ordinary residence to the prescribed authority. They may also be directed by the District Magistrate to report themselves periodically and notify any absence from their ordinary residence.

main_sections.section_title: Action to be taken when a registered offender changes his ordinary residence.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure when a registered offender moves to another district, involving the informing of the District Magistrate of the new district, registration there, and cancellation of the entry in the original district's Register. Similar provisions apply if the offender moves outside the state, with a request for information on actions taken in the other district.

main_sections.section_title: Duration of registration, cancellation thereof and re-registration of habitual offenders.
main_sections.description: States that registration ceases after five years unless cancelled earlier. A habitual offender can be re-registered if convicted of scheduled offences after cancellation or expiry. Registration duration can be extended by five years from release from imprisonment if convicted during the registration period.

main_sections.section_title: Right to make representations against registration and re-registration, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants any person aggrieved by registration, re-registration, or certain orders the right to make a representation to the State Government within a prescribed period. The State Government will consider the representation, offer a hearing, and either confirm or cancel the action, recording reasons for confirmation.

main_sections.section_title: Power to restrict movement of a registered offender.
main_sections.description: Allows the State Government to order restrictions on a registered offender's movement to a specified 'restriction area' for a period not exceeding three years, if deemed necessary in the public interest. Before issuing such an order, the Government must consider the nature of past offences, the offender's lawful occupation, the suitability of the area, and other relevant factors.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would likely deal with the establishment and management of corrective settlements for habitual offenders.

main_sections.section_title: Power to direct habitual offender to receive corrective training.
main_sections.description: This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would likely grant the authority to direct habitual offenders to undergo corrective training.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with certain provisions of the Act.
main_sections.description: This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would define penalties for non-compliance with specific provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Arrest of persons found outside restriction area or corrective settlement.
main_sections.description: This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would detail the provisions for the arrest of individuals found outside their designated restriction areas or corrective settlements.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would likely specify limitations on the jurisdiction of certain courts or authorities regarding matters covered by this Act.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would likely outline limitations or bars on initiating legal proceedings against certain actions taken under the Act.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would likely grant the power to delegate certain functions or powers under the Act to other authorities.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would empower the appropriate authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
This section, indicated by its presence in the arrangement of sections, would address the repeal of any previous laws on the subject and include provisions for savings.

important_rules: Registered offenders must notify any change of residence to the prescribed authority.
Registered offenders may be directed to report themselves periodically to a specified authority.
Entries in the Register of habitual offenders cannot be made or cancelled without the written order of the District Magistrate.
A habitual offender's registration ceases after five years unless cancelled earlier or extended due to subsequent convictions.
State Government may restrict the movement of registered offenders to a specific area for up to three years.
The Act consolidates and provides a uniform law for the treatment and training of habitual offenders across the state, replacing previous regional laws.

penalties: Penalty for failure to comply with certain provisions of the Act (details to be found in Section 16, which is not fully provided).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the registration of habitual offenders, monitoring their movements, imposing restrictions, directing corrective training, and enforcing penalties for non-compliance. The process involves notifications, notices, enquiries, and the maintenance of a register.

rights: Right to be afforded a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against registration.
Right to make a representation to the State Government against registration, re-registration, or certain orders.
Right to an opportunity of being heard by the State Government during the consideration of a representation.
duties: Duty of registered offenders to notify any change of ordinary residence.
Duty of registered offenders to report themselves if directed by the District Magistrate.
Duty of the Superintendent of Police to maintain the Register and report alterations to the District Magistrate.
obligations: Habitual offenders have an obligation to appear before the District Magistrate when notified.
Habitual offenders have an obligation to furnish information and allow biometric data collection when required.
District Magistrates have an obligation to verify previous convictions before making entries in the Register.

key_procedures: Registration of Habitual Offenders: State Government directs District Magistrate to create a register. Offenders are notified, required to appear, provide information, and allow biometric data collection after an opportunity to show cause and verification of past convictions.
Change of Residence: Registered offenders must notify changes. If moving to another district, information is exchanged between District Magistrates for registration and cancellation of entries.
Representation against Registration: Aggrieved persons can represent to the State Government, which will hear the matter and decide on confirmation or cancellation of the registration/order.
Restriction of Movement: State Government considers various factors before ordering restrictions on an offender's movement to a specific area for a defined period.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, with key roles played by the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police. The State Government also handles representations and issues orders for movement restrictions and corrective training.
important_notes: The Act aims to create a uniform law across Karnataka, consolidating previous separate laws from different regions (Mysore, Madras, Bombay, Hyderabad).
The definition of 'habitual offender' is specific, requiring multiple convictions for scheduled offences over a five-year period, with jail time excluded from this period.
Corrective training and settlements are part of the Act's provisions for the treatment and rehabilitation of habitual offenders.

title: THE KARNATAKA HEALTH CESS ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the levy of health cess on certain items of revenue in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the levy of health cess on land revenue, specific items of State revenues, and taxes levied by local authorities.

key_definitions.local_authority: A municipal corporation, a municipal committee, a town committee, a municipal council, a borough municipal council, a sanitary or town board, a notified area committee, a taluk development board, a village panchayat or any authority established for the purpose of local self-government or village administration.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the date of commencement (deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1962).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'local authority' and 'notification'.

Provides for the levy and collection of health cess at a specified rate (15 paise in the rupee) on land revenue, State revenues mentioned in Schedule A, and taxes levied by local authorities as mentioned in Schedule B.
States that the health cess is to be levied, assessed, and recovered along with the items of revenue or tax on which it is levied, and the provisions of the relevant laws and rules will apply.

main_sections.section_title: Local authorities entitled to cost of collection of health cess
main_sections.description: Allows local authorities recovering health cess to deduct ten percent of the amount recovered as cost of collection, with the balance to be paid to the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Cess to be collected to the nearest paisa
main_sections.description: Specifies the rounding rules for calculating the health cess amount, disregarding fractions less than half a paisa and treating half a paisa or more as one paisa.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of cess under other Acts not affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the levy of health cess under this Act is in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other duty or cess levied under any other law.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, with a provision for laying such rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.
Repeals the Mysore Health Cess Act, 1951.

important_rules: Health cess is levied at the rate of fifteen paise in the rupee.
Fractions of a paisa less than half a paisa are disregarded; fractions of a paisa equal to or exceeding half a paisa are treated as one paisa.
The health cess is levied on land revenue, specified State revenues (Schedule A), and specified local authority taxes (Schedule B).
Local authorities recovering health cess are entitled to deduct 10% as collection costs.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and local authorities, as per the recovery provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the existing mechanisms for levy, assessment, and recovery of land revenue, State revenue, or taxes, as specified in Section 4.

rights: Local authorities have the right to deduct 10% of collected health cess as collection costs (Section 4A).
duties: The State Government has the duty to levy and collect health cess.
Local authorities have the duty to collect health cess and pay the balance to the State Government.
obligations: Obligation to pay health cess on specified revenue items.
Obligation to adhere to the rounding rules for cess calculation.

key_procedures: Levy, assessment, and recovery of health cess along with the primary revenue/tax it is attached to, using the procedures of the respective laws (Section 4).
Deduction of collection costs by local authorities (Section 4A).
Rounding of cess amounts to the nearest paisa (Section 5).
Rule-making procedure by the State Government, including laying rules before the State Legislature (Section 7).
administration: The State Government, with provisions for local authorities to collect and remit the cess.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1968 and 1976 to adjust rates and clarify certain provisions, including the omission of item 2 from Schedule A and re-numbering of item 3 in Schedule B.
The Act is a successor to the Mysore Health Cess Act, 1951, which was repealed.
The levy of health cess is in addition to any other duties or cesses that may be levied under other laws.

title: The Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a volunteer organisation, the Home Guards, in the State of Karnataka for use in emergencies and for other purposes, specifically for the protection of persons, security of property, and preservation of public order and tranquility.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to individuals appointed as Home Guards and their employers.

key_definitions.Home Guard: A person who is appointed as a Home Guard under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Home Guards Act, 1962, and states that it extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, specifically 'Home Guard' and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Home Guards and appointment of Commandant General and Commandants
main_sections.description: This section outlines the constitution of the Home Guards as a volunteer body. It also details the appointment of Commandants for specific jurisdictions and a Commandant General for overall supervision and control.

This section describes the process of appointing members to the Home Guards, with approval from the Commandant General. It also covers the appointment of members to offices of command and the issuance of certificates of appointment, which confer powers, privileges, and duties.

This section empowers the Commandant General, Commandants, Deputy Commissioner, or Superintendent of Police to call out members of the Home Guards for training or to discharge assigned functions and duties.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of employer to permit Home Guards to join Duty
main_sections.description: This section mandates employers to permit Home Guards to join their duty and pay them for the period of duty (not exceeding sixty days in a year), treating it as if they were on regular duty. It also prohibits employers from taking prejudicial action against employees for being Home Guards.

This section grants Home Guard members, when called out, the same powers, privileges, and protection as police officers. It also requires prior sanction from the Commandant General for any prosecution against a Home Guard member for actions taken in their official capacity.

main_sections.section_title: Control by officers of police force
main_sections.description: This section states that Home Guards, when called out in aid of the police force, will be under the control of police officers as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate, arms, etc., to be delivered up by person ceasing to be a member
main_sections.description: This section requires members ceasing to be Home Guards to deliver up their appointment certificates, arms, clothing, and other issued articles. It also provides for search and seizure of undelivered items.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment of members for neglect of duty, etc.
main_sections.description: This section details the disciplinary powers of the Commandant and Commandant General, including suspension, reduction, dismissal, or imposition of fines for neglect of duty, misconduct, or disobedience. It also provides for appeals against these orders and the right to discharge members whose services are no longer required.

This section specifies punishments for Home Guard members who, without reasonable excuse, neglect or refuse to obey orders or discharge their duties when called out. It also covers the punishment for wilfully neglecting to deliver up certificates or articles.

main_sections.section_title: Disciplinary action against Commandant or the Commandant General
main_sections.description: This section is listed in the arrangement but not detailed in the provided text.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section grants the State Government the power to make rules for the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Members of the Home Guards to be public servants
main_sections.description: This section declares members of the Home Guards to be public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Members of the Home Guards not disqualified from being members of local authorities
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that being a member of the Home Guards does not disqualify a person from being a member of local authorities.
This section pertains to the amendment of another Karnataka Act, not detailed in the provided text.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of certain Acts and savings
main_sections.description: This section deals with the repeal of specific Acts and includes provisions for savings.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No. 4 of 1962
main_sections.description: This section specifically repeals the Karnataka Ordinance No. 4 of 1962.

important_rules: Employers must permit Home Guards to join duty and pay them for up to sixty days a year as if they were on regular duty.
Employers cannot dismiss, remove, suspend, or prejudice an employee for being a member of the Home Guards.
Members of the Home Guards, when called out, have the same powers, privileges, and protection as police officers.
Prosecution against a Home Guard member requires the previous sanction of the Commandant General.
Members ceasing to be Home Guards must return issued certificates, arms, and clothing.
Home Guards are considered public servants.

penalties: Contravention of employer obligations (Section 5A(1) or 5A(2)) is punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees.
Neglect or refusal to obey orders or discharge duties when called out (Section 10(1)) is punishable with simple imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees, or both.
Wilful neglect or refusal to deliver up certificates or articles (Section 10(2)) has penalties specified.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commandant, Commandant General, State Government, Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, and Police Officers are involved in the enforcement of this Act and its rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes calling out members for duty, disciplinary actions (suspension, dismissal, fines), prosecution for neglect of duty, search and seizure of undelivered items, and appeals against disciplinary orders.

rights: Members of the Home Guards have the same powers, privileges, and protection as police officers when called out.
Members are entitled to pay and allowances from their employers for up to sixty days of Home Guard duty per year.
Members have the right to appeal disciplinary orders against them.
duties: To discharge functions and duties related to the protection of persons, security of property, and preservation of public order and tranquility.
To obey lawful orders and directions given for the performance of their duties.
To deliver up certificates, arms, and other issued articles upon ceasing to be a member.
To attend training when called out.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to permit Home Guards to join duty and pay them for such duty.
Employers have an obligation not to prejudice employees for being Home Guards.

key_procedures: Appointment of Home Guard members through Commandants, with Commandant General approval.
Calling out members for training or duty by the Commandant General, Commandants, Deputy Commissioners, or Superintendents of Police.
Disciplinary proceedings against members, including opportunities to be heard and appeals.
Procedure for members ceasing to be Home Guards, including returning issued items.
Appeals against disciplinary orders to the Commandant General or the State Government.
administration: The State Government, through the Commandant General and Commandants, administers the Home Guards organization. Police officers also have control over Home Guards when they are called out in aid of the police force.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to provide a uniform law for the Home Guards organization across the entire State of Karnataka.
Section 5A was inserted by an Amending Act in 1977 to address the difficulties faced by Home Guards whose employers did not treat their absence on duty favourably.
The Act also deals with the repeal of certain previous ordinances and acts.

title: The Karnataka Homœopathic Practitioners Act, 1961
purpose: To regulate the qualifications and practice of homœopathic medicine and to provide for the registration of practitioners of the homœopathic system of medicine in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to the practice and education of the Homœopathic system of medicine.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Board of Homœopathic System of Medicine established under section 3.
key_definitions.Court: The Court of Examiners constituted under section 16.
key_definitions.homoeopathy: The system of medicine founded by Dr. Hahnemann and includes the allied branches of Biochemistry founded by Dr. Schussler.
key_definitions.practitioner: A person who practises the homœopathic system of medicine as his principal occupation.
key_definitions.registered practitioner: A practitioner whose name is for the time being entered in the register.
key_definitions.qualifying examination: An examination in homœopathic system of medicine specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: States the short title as 'The Karnataka Homœopathic Practitioners Act, 1961', its territorial extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and the commencement dates for different chapters.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Court', 'homoeopathy', 'Inspector', 'member', 'notification', 'practitioner', 'prescribed', 'President', 'qualifying examination', 'register', 'registered practitioner', 'Registrar', 'regulations', and 'rules'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment, constitution and incorporation of Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Board of Homœopathic System of Medicine as a body corporate and outlines its constitution, including the number of members (President and eleven members), nomination, and election processes.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board, which are elaborated further in other sections of the Act.
Concerns the preparation of the initial register of practitioners.
Specifies the qualifications required for practitioners to be registered after the initial registration.
Outlines the conditions and procedures for removing a practitioner's name from the register.

main_sections.section_title: Course of studies and qualifying examinations
main_sections.description: Deals with the prescribed course of studies and the qualifying examinations for homœopathic practitioners.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations for its internal functioning and administration.
Defines the supervisory control of the State Government over the Board and its activities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Board of Homœopathic System of Medicine and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Board for registration, examination, and regulation, and through the State Government's oversight and rule-making powers.

rights: Right to practice homœopathic medicine upon registration.
Right to be represented on the Board (for registered practitioners).
duties: Practitioners have a duty to be registered to practice homœopathy.
Registered practitioners must adhere to the rules and regulations governing their practice.
obligations: Obligation to meet prescribed qualifications for registration.
Obligation to pay renewal fees for registration.
Obligation to undergo qualifying examinations if applicable.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment and constitution of the Karnataka Board of Homœopathic System of Medicine.
Procedure for the election and nomination of Board members.
Procedure for the preparation and maintenance of the register of homœopathic practitioners.
Procedure for the registration of qualified practitioners.
Procedure for the removal of names from the register.
Procedure for the recognition of institutions for holding qualifying examinations.
Procedure for the removal of institutions authorized to hold qualifying examinations.
administration: The Karnataka Board of Homœopathic System of Medicine, under the overall control of the State Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended multiple times to address issues like election procedures, the composition of the Board, and fees.
Certain provisions (Chapters I, IV, and VI) came into force immediately, while others required a specific notification from the State Government.
The definition of homoeopathy includes allied branches like Biochemistry.

title: THE KARNATAKA INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (NATIONAL AND FESTIVAL HOLIDAYS) ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the grant of national and festival holidays to persons employed in industrial establishments in the State of Karnataka, ensuring uniform practice and paid holidays for specified national days and festivals.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to industrial establishments as defined within the Act, including shops, commercial establishments, factories, plantations, and any other establishment declared as such by the State Government. It covers employees working in these establishments.

key_definitions.day: A period of twenty-four hours beginning at midnight.
key_definitions.employee: Any person employed in an industrial establishment to do skilled or unskilled, manual, supervisory, technical, or clerical work for hire or reward, including apprentices, and any other person declared as such by the State Government.
key_definitions.employer: The person with ultimate control over the affairs of an industrial establishment, or their entrusted representative.
key_definitions.industrial_establishment: Includes shops and commercial establishments, factories, plantations, and any other establishment declared as such by the State Government.
key_definitions.inspector: An Inspector appointed under sub-section (1) of section 6 of the Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration capable of being expressed in terms of money, payable to an employee for their employment, including allowances and the value of amenities, but excluding bonuses, pension/provident fund contributions, gratuity, special expense reimbursements, and travelling concessions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent to the whole of Karnataka, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'day', 'employee', 'employer', 'industrial establishment', 'Inspector', 'notification', and 'wages'.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of National and festival Holidays.
main_sections.description: Mandates that every employee be allowed holidays on 26th January, 15th August, and 2nd October. It also allows for five other festival holidays to be specified by the employer from a list in consultation with trade unions or employees. For establishments not owned/controlled by the Government of India, seven other holidays are provided, including May 1st and November 1st. It outlines a procedure for resolving disagreements on festival holidays.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of Holidays on the polling day, for House of the People or to the State Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Obligates employers to grant a paid holiday on the polling day for general elections to the House of the People or State Legislative Assembly to employees whose names are on the electoral roll of the constituency, except for employees in establishments owned or controlled by the Government of India.

main_sections.section_title: Employer to send statement to Inspector.
main_sections.description: Requires employers to submit and display a statement of allowed holidays to the Inspector and within the establishment, in a prescribed form and manner.

Stipulates that employees are entitled to wages for allowed holidays. If an employee works on a holiday, they are entitled to double wages or wages plus a substituted holiday. Special provisions are made for daily wage or piece-rate workers. A proviso clarifies eligibility for wages for certain holidays based on service duration.
Empowers the State Government to appoint Inspectors for the purposes of the Act, with specified local limits or for particular industrial establishments.
Details the powers of Inspectors, including entry, inspection, examination of records, and taking statements, to ensure compliance with the Act.
Outlines penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Specifies penalties for obstructing an Inspector in the performance of their duties.
Defines the procedure for taking cognizance of offenses under the Act, generally requiring a complaint by an Inspector and action by a First Class Magistrate.
Grants the State Government the power to exempt any industrial establishment or class of establishments from any provisions of the Act, subject to certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Rights and privileges under other laws, etc., not affected.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect any rights or privileges that employees may have under any other law or agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to amend the Schedule.
main_sections.description: Confers power upon the State Government to amend the Schedule appended to the Act.
Authorizes the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and notifications to be laid before the State Legislature.
main_sections.description: Requires that all rules and notifications made under the Act be laid before the State Legislature for its consideration.

important_rules: Every employee is entitled to holidays on January 26th, August 15th, and October 2nd each calendar year.
Employers must grant at least five additional festival holidays, chosen from the Schedule, in consultation with trade unions or employees.
Establishments not owned or controlled by the Government of India must provide seven additional holidays, including May 1st and November 1st.
Employees are entitled to wages for all granted holidays.
If an employee works on a holiday, they are entitled to twice their wages or wages plus a substituted holiday.

Employees must have completed a total period of thirty days of service within a continuous ninety days preceding a holiday (excluding Jan 26, Aug 15, Oct 2, and polling day holidays) to be eligible for wages, with exceptions for weekly holidays or authorized leave.
Employers must inform the Inspector and display a statement of holidays allowed in their establishment.
A paid holiday must be granted on the polling day for general elections to parliamentary or assembly constituencies for eligible employees.
The State Government can exempt establishments from certain provisions of the Act.

penalties: Fine for contravention of Act provisions or rules.
Penalty for obstructing Inspectors.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act, and ultimately the State Government and courts (Magistrate of the First Class for cognizance of offenses).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections by appointed Inspectors, submission of statements by employers, complaints filed by Inspectors, and prosecution of offenders in court.

rights: Right to be granted national and festival holidays with wages.
Right to receive wages for holidays or double wages/wages plus substituted holiday if working on a holiday.
Right to a paid holiday on polling day for elections if eligible.
Right to have their holiday disputes resolved by the Inspector.
Rights and privileges under other laws are not affected.
duties: Duty of the employer to grant specified national and festival holidays with wages.
Duty of the employer to inform and display holiday statements.
Duty of the employer to grant a paid holiday on polling day for elections.
Duty of the employer to consult trade unions or employees regarding festival holidays.
Duty of the employee to be employed for a minimum period to be eligible for wages for certain holidays.
obligations: Employers are obligated to adhere to the mandated holidays and wage payments.
Employees are obligated to be in service for a qualifying period for wage eligibility on certain holidays.

key_procedures: Annual declaration and display of holidays by employers.
Dispute resolution for festival holidays via referral to the Inspector.
Grant of paid holiday on polling day upon notification of elections.
Inspection of establishments by Inspectors to ensure compliance.
Prosecution of employers for non-compliance.
administration: The State Government, through its appointed Inspectors and potentially labor departments, administers this Act. The State Legislature is also involved in approving rules and notifications.
important_notes: The Act's provisions regarding additional holidays and their number may differ for industrial establishments owned or controlled by the Government of India.
Eligibility for wages for certain holidays is conditional on completing a minimum period of service within a specified timeframe immediately preceding the holiday.

title: The Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the organizing, developing and regulating of Khadi and Village Industries in the State of Karnataka and to constitute a Board to carry out these objects.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to Khadi and Village Industries within the state.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka State Khadi and Village Industries Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.khadi: Any cloth woven on handlooms in India from cotton, silk or woollen yarn handspun in India, or from a mixture of any two or all of such yarns.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.village industry: The Khadi Industry and any industry specified in the Schedule to this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and repeal
main_sections.description: This section defines the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1956. It specifies the extent of the Act to the whole of the State of Karnataka, the commencement as notified by the State Government, and the repeal of certain Acts (Bombay Village Industries Act, 1954 and Hyderabad Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1955) upon the commencement of this Act in specific areas.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'khadi', 'prescribed', 'Regulations', and 'village industry'.

This section establishes the Karnataka State Khadi and Village Industries Board with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowering it to sue and be sued, acquire and hold property, contract, and perform all necessary actions for the purposes of the Act.

This section details the composition of the Board, including members appointed from each district, ex-officio members from government departments, a nominee from the Finance Department, a nominee from the Department of Commerce and Industries, the State Director of Khadi and Village Industries Commission, the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer, and the Chief Executive Officer. It also specifies the appointment of a Chairman from among the members.
This section outlines the primary functions of the Board, which include organizing, developing, and regulating Khadi and Village Industries in the State.
This section enumerates the general powers vested in the Board to carry out its functions, such as undertaking schemes, providing financial assistance, and promoting the Khadi and Village Industries.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of moneys due to the Board as arrears of Land Revenue
main_sections.description: This section, inserted by an amendment, provides a mechanism for recovering moneys due to the Board as arrears of Land Revenue, ensuring financial security for funds advanced by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.
This section, also inserted by an amendment, provides for the dissolution of the Board under specific circumstances, likely related to ensuring the security of funds advanced by the Commission.
This section empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. An amendment also introduced a provision for laying these rules before the State Legislature.
This section empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made thereunder.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka State Khadi and Village Industries Board is established to carry out the objectives of the Act. The State Government plays a role in appointing members, approving programs, and making rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act outlines various provisions for the functioning and powers of the Board, including financial management and program submission. The enforcement likely involves the Board's operational activities, adherence to rules and regulations, and potentially legal recourse for recovery of dues as per Section 22A.

rights: The Board has the right to acquire and hold property, contract, and perform all things necessary for the purposes of the Act.
The Board has the right to sue and be sued in its corporate name.
Members of the Board have the right to receive prescribed allowances.
duties: The Board has the duty to organize, develop, and regulate Khadi and Village Industries in the State of Karnataka.
The Board has the duty to prepare and submit annual programs for approval.
The Board has the duty to maintain accounts and prepare an annual report.
obligations: Members of the Board and staff are considered public servants.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of annual programs by the Board for sanction by the State Government (Sections 15-17).
Preparation of budgets, their sanction, and supplementary budgets (Sections 23-25).
Preparation and submission of an annual report and other statistics/returns by the Board (Sections 26-27).
Maintenance of accounts and audit by the Board (Section 28).
administration: The Karnataka State Khadi and Village Industries Board, established under the Act, is responsible for its administration. The State Government also plays a significant role through rule-making, approvals, and nominations.
important_notes: The Act has been amended multiple times, including by Acts 25 of 1958, 9 of 1973, 16 of 1978, 21 of 1983, and 8 of 1985, to incorporate changes like the reference to the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, provisions for financial advisers and recovery of dues, and modifications to the Board's constitution and service conditions.
The Act ensures the security of funds advanced by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission by providing mechanisms for recovery and potentially dissolution of the Board if necessary.
Provisions exist for the laying of rules before the State Legislature, ensuring transparency and oversight.
The Act provides for the appointment of a Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer from officers of either the Central or State Government.

title: THE KARNATAKA LABOUR WELFARE FUND ACT, 1965
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund for financing and conducting activities to promote welfare of labour in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to employees and employers in various establishments including factories, motor omnibus services, societies, charitable trusts, plantations, and workshops, excluding establishments (not being a factory) of the Central or any State Government.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Labour Welfare Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.contribution: The sum of money comprising the employer's contribution, employee's contribution, and State Government's contribution payable to the Board in accordance with the provisions of section 7A.
key_definitions.employee: Any person who is employed for wages to do any work skilled or unskilled, manual or clerical, in an establishment.
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs one or more employees in an establishment, including managers in factories and persons responsible for supervision and control of employees or payment of wages.
key_definitions.establishment: Includes a factory, motor omnibus service, certain societies and trusts carrying on business employing more than fifty persons, and plantations or workshops. Excludes Central or State Government establishments (unless they are factories).
key_definitions.factory: As defined in section 2(m) of the Factories Act, 1948.
key_definitions.Fund: The Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.unpaid accumulations: All payments due to employees but not made within three years from the date they became due, excluding provident fund contributions.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration expressible in terms of money payable for employment or work done, excluding certain benefits like house accommodation, light, water, medical attendance, travelling allowance, expenses for special employment, and gratuity payable on discharge.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the commencement date which can be appointed by the State Government by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as Board, employee, employer, establishment, factory, Fund, independent member, Inspector, prescribed, unpaid accumulations, wages, and Welfare Commissioner.

Establishes the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund and details its constituents, which include fines realised from employees, unpaid accumulations, contributions, penal interest, voluntary donations, transferred funds, and borrowed sums.

Provides for the constitution of the Karnataka Labour Welfare Board by the State Government for administering the Fund and other assigned functions. It specifies the composition of the Board with representatives of employers and employees, independent members, and the election of a Chairman. The Board is a body corporate.
Outlines the conditions that disqualify a person from being a member of the Board and the grounds on which the State Government can remove a member from office.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation of office by member and filling up of casual vacancies
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for a member to resign and how casual vacancies in the Board are to be filled.

Deals with unpaid accumulations, stating they are deemed abandoned property. It outlines how employers are discharged of liability upon payment to the Board and the process for inviting claims from employees through notices.
Introduced by an amendment, this section likely deals with the levying of contributions from employees, employers, and the State Government to augment the fund's resources.

main_sections.section_title: Interest on unpaid accumulations or fines after notice of demand
main_sections.description: Also introduced by an amendment, this section probably pertains to penal interest on unpaid accumulations or fines after a demand notice.
Governs how the Fund vests and how it is to be applied for the welfare of labour.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of Welfare Commissioner
main_sections.description: Details the appointment and powers of the Welfare Commissioner, who plays a key role in the administration of the Act.
Provides for the appointment of Inspectors to carry out functions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for obstructing Inspector in the discharge of his duties or for failure to produce documents, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for obstructing Inspectors or failing to produce required documents.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of any provisions of the Act
main_sections.description: Defines penalties for general contraventions of the Act's provisions.
Empowers the State Government to supersede the Board in certain circumstances.
Enables the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Allows the State Government to grant exemptions from the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous legislation and savings provisions.

important_rules: Contributions by employees, employers, and the State Government are levied to augment the Welfare Fund (as per Statement of Objects and Reasons for Act 73 of 1976 and Act 10 of 1994).
Unpaid accumulations are deemed abandoned property and are transferred to the Fund, with a discharge of employer liability to the extent of the payment made to the Board.
The Board must publish notices regarding unpaid accumulations to invite claims from employees.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire property and contract.
Members of the Board must have equal representation for employers and employees.
Rules can be made by the State Government for the collection, maintenance, and audit of the Fund accounts, as well as for other procedural matters.

penalties: Penalty for obstructing an Inspector in the discharge of their duties.
Penalty for failure to produce documents required by an Inspector.
Penalty for contravention of any provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, through Welfare Commissioners and Inspectors appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appointment of Welfare Commissioners and Inspectors, powers to call for records, imposition of penalties for contraventions, and legal proceedings for recovery of sums payable into the Fund.

rights: Employees have the right to claim unpaid accumulations due to them.
Employees have the right to benefit from welfare activities funded by the Act.
duties: Employers have a duty to pay fines realised from employees into the Fund.
Employers have a duty to transfer unpaid accumulations to the Fund.
Employers have a duty to pay contributions as stipulated by the Act.
The Board has a duty to administer the Fund and carry out welfare activities.
The Board has a duty to maintain accounts and get them audited.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to constitute the Fund and the Board.
Obligation of the Board to invest the Fund appropriately.
Obligation of members of the Board, Welfare Commissioner, and officers to be public servants.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Karnataka Labour Welfare Board by the State Government.
Collection of fines, unpaid accumulations, contributions, and other sums into the Karnataka Labour Welfare Fund.
Notification and publication of unpaid accumulations to invite claims from employees.
Decision of claims for unpaid accumulations.
Investment of the Fund by the Board.
Appointment and powers of Welfare Commissioner and Inspectors.
Procedure for supersession of the Board by the State Government.
administration: The Karnataka Labour Welfare Board, under the overall direction and oversight of the State Government.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1976 to introduce contributions from employees, employers, and the State Government to augment the Fund's resources, as initial sources (fines and voluntary donations) were found to be insufficient.
Further amendments in 1994 enhanced the contribution rates.
The Act aims for uniform law across the entire State of Karnataka for labour welfare activities.
The Board is intended to take over Labour Welfare Centres previously under the control of the Government.

title: THE KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE (PREVENTION OF DISQUALIFICATION) ACT, 1956
purpose: To declare certain offices of profit not to disqualify their holders for being chosen as, or for being, members of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and the Karnataka Legislative Council, and to remove certain disqualifications.
scope: Applies to members of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and the Karnataka Legislative Council. It specifically addresses the disqualification of members due to holding certain offices of profit under the State Government or Central Government.

key_definitions.committee: Any Committee, Commission, Council, Board or any other body of one or more persons whether statutory or not, set up by the Government of India or the Government of any State.
key_definitions.compensatory_allowance: Sum of money determined by the Central Government or State Government, payable to the Chairman or any other member of a Committee by way of travelling allowance, daily allowance, sitting fee, conveyance allowance or house rent allowance to recoup expenditure incurred in attending meetings or performing functions as a member.
key_definitions.statutory_body: Any corporation, board, company, society or any other body of one or more persons, whether incorporated or not, established, registered or formed by or under any Central Law or the law of any State for the time being in force or exercising powers and functions under any such law.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Legislature (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1956.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Committee', 'Compensatory allowance', and 'Statutory body'.

This section declares that certain specified offices shall not disqualify, and shall be deemed never to have disqualified, the holders thereof for being chosen as, or for being, members of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly or the Karnataka Legislative Council. This section has been amended multiple times to include various offices.

important_rules: Rule: Offices of Deputy Minister, Parliamentary Secretary, Leaders of the Opposition, and Government Chief Whips shall not disqualify members.
Rule: Offices held in the National Cadet Corps, Territorial Army, and Auxiliary Air Forces shall not disqualify members.
Rule: Offices of Chairman or Member of a Committee shall not disqualify members, provided the holder is not in receipt of remuneration other than compensatory allowance.
Rule: Offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha of Zilla Parishads and Pradhana and Upa-Pradhana of Mandal Panchayats shall not disqualify members.

Rule (post-amendment): Offices of Chairman, Speaker, Deputy Chairman, Deputy Speaker, Minister of State, Deputy Minister, Parliamentary Secretary, Leaders of the Opposition, or Government Chief Whip in the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council shall not disqualify members.

Rule (post-amendment): Offices of President and Vice-President of a Municipal Council, Mayor or Deputy Mayor of a Municipal Corporation, and Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha of Zilla Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats, and Grama Panchayats shall not disqualify members.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be handled through legislative and constitutional processes concerning disqualification of members.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the declaration of certain offices as not disqualifying, thereby preventing members from being disqualified on those grounds.

rights: Right of individuals holding specified offices to not be disqualified from being a member of the State Legislature.
Right of the State Legislature to declare certain offices as non-disqualifying.
duties: Duty of the State Legislature to enact laws to prevent disqualification based on holding certain offices.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding disqualification.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the disqualification provisions outlined in the Constitution of India, unless exempted by this Act.
Obligation for members to not hold offices that would lead to disqualification, unless specifically exempted by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Enactment of the Act to declare certain offices as non-disqualifying.
Procedure: Amendment of the Act to include or exclude specific offices from the list of non-disqualifying offices.
Procedure: Consideration of offices of profit and their impact on legislative membership, as guided by the Constitution and this Act.
administration: The Act is administered by the Karnataka State Legislature and related government departments responsible for legislative affairs.
important_notes: The Act has been amended several times to include new categories of offices and to remove others, reflecting changes in governance structures and policies.
The Act aims to prevent unnecessary expenditure and financial burdens on the State exchequer by avoiding frequent disqualifications of members.
The amendments to Section 3 of the Act show a trend towards including elected positions in local self-governing bodies within the scope of non-disqualifying offices.

title: The Karnataka Legislature (Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership) Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the vacation by a person who is chosen a member of both Houses of the Legislature of the State of Karnataka of his seat in one House or the other, in accordance with Article 190 of the Constitution of India.
scope: This act applies to persons who are elected as members of both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.Assembly: Means the Legislative Assembly of the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.Council: Means the Legislative Council of the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.House: Means the Assembly or the Council.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Legislature (Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership) Act, 1956.
This section defines the terms 'Assembly', 'Council', and 'House' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Vacation of seat by persons when elected as members of both the Assembly and the Council
main_sections.description: This section outlines the procedure for a person elected to both the Assembly and the Council to choose which seat to vacate. It specifies a time limit for intimation and the consequence of default.

main_sections.section_title: Vacation of seats by persons already members of one House on election to the other House
main_sections.description: This section deals with a person who is already a member of one House and is subsequently elected to the other. It states that their seat in the original House becomes vacant upon publication of the declaration of their election to the other House.

important_rules: Rule 1: A person elected to both the Assembly and the Council must intimate in writing which House they wish to serve in within ten days of the gazette publication of their election. Their seat in the other House will then become vacant.
Rule 2: If no intimation is given within the stipulated period, the seat in the Council shall automatically become vacant.
Rule 3: Any intimation given by the person to choose their seat is final and cannot be revoked.
Rule 4: If a person is already a member of the Assembly and is elected to the Council, their Assembly seat becomes vacant upon the gazette publication of their election to the Council.
Rule 5: If a person is already a member of the Council and is elected to the Assembly, their Council seat becomes vacant upon the gazette publication of their election to the Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act's enforcement relies on the constitutional provisions and the procedures laid out for legislative bodies. The Governor's authorized person is mentioned for receiving notices.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the process of vacating seats as specified in the Act and as per Article 190 of the Constitution. This involves gazette notifications and the member's own intimation or default.

rights: Right to choose which House to serve in, if elected to both, within a specified period.
duties: Duty to vacate one of the seats if elected to both Houses.
Duty to intimate the choice of House within the prescribed time limit.
obligations: Obligation to abide by Article 190 of the Constitution of India.
Obligation to ensure simultaneous membership is avoided as per the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For a person elected to both Houses (and not having taken a seat in either): Deliver a written notice to the Secretary of each House (or authorized person) within 10 days of the gazette notification of election, stating the preferred House. The seat in the non-preferred House becomes vacant.
Procedure 2: For a person elected to both Houses who defaults in intimating their choice: Their seat in the Council automatically becomes vacant after the 10-day period.

Procedure 3: For a person already a member of the Assembly and elected to the Council: Their Assembly seat becomes vacant upon publication in the Karnataka Gazette of the declaration that they have been elected to the Council.

Procedure 4: For a person already a member of the Council and elected to the Assembly: Their Council seat becomes vacant upon publication in the Karnataka Gazette of the declaration that they have been elected to the Assembly.
administration: The administration of this Act is linked to the functioning of the Karnataka Legislature, with the Secretary of the respective Houses and potentially an authorized person by the Governor playing a role in procedural aspects.
important_notes: The Act is a consequence of Article 190(1) of the Constitution of India, which mandates that no person shall be a member of both Houses of the State Legislature.

The Act was enacted to address the situation arising after the formation of the new State and to implement the constitutional requirement, as the previous Mysore Legislature Act did not apply to the new State.
Adaptations by the Karnataka Adaptations of Laws Order 1973 have updated references to 'State of Mysore'/'Mysore Legislature' to 'State of Karnataka'/'Karnataka Legislature'.

title: The Karnataka Lifts Act, 1974
purpose: To provide for the regulation of the construction, maintenance and safe working of certain classes of lifts and all machinery and apparatus pertaining thereto in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. Covers the regulation of construction, maintenance, and safe working of lifts (defined as power-operated hoisting mechanisms with cars moving vertically for passengers or goods), including associated machinery and apparatus. Excludes lifts to which the Factories Act, 1948 applies.

key_definitions.inspector_of_lifts: An officer appointed as such by the Government.
key_definitions.lift: A hoisting mechanism equipped with a car which moves in a substantially vertical direction, is worked by power and is designed to carry passengers or goods or both.
key_definitions.lift_car: The cage or car of a lift used for the conveyance of passengers or goods or both, including its components, but excluding hoists or lifts covered by the Factories Act, 1948.
key_definitions.lift_installation: Includes the lift car, lift way, lift way enclosure, operating mechanism, and all directly connected ropes, cables, wires, and plant.
key_definitions.lift_way: The shaft in which the lift car travels.
key_definitions.lift_way_enclosure: Any permanent substantial structure surrounding or enclosing the lift way.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.power: Any form of energy not generated by human or animal agency.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its extent to the whole of Karnataka, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Government, Inspector of Lifts, licence, lift, lift car, lift installation, lift way, lift way enclosure, notification, power, and prescribed.

Requires owners intending to install a new lift to apply for permission from an authorized officer, providing specific details about the lift's type, capacity, dimensions, and construction. Permission is valid for twelve months, extendable by up to six months upon recommendation.

Owners permitted to install a lift must notify completion and apply for a licence to operate it within one month. The application requires specific forms and a fee. The Government may grant or refuse the licence.

main_sections.section_title: Application for licence in case of existing lifts
main_sections.description: Owners of lifts installed before the Act's commencement must apply for a licence within two months of the Act's commencement. Sub-sections (2) to (4) of Section 4 apply to these applications.

main_sections.section_title: Lift not to be operated without a licence
main_sections.description: Prohibits the operation of any lift except under and in conformity with the terms of its licence. Existing lifts have a grace period of two months, or until their licence application is disposed of.

main_sections.section_title: Additions and alterations to the lift installation
main_sections.description: Requires prior written permission from a government-authorized officer for any additions or alterations to a lift installation, except those mandated by Section 8(2).

main_sections.section_title: Right to enter any building for inspection of lifts and lift installation
main_sections.description: Authorizes government-appointed officers to enter buildings to inspect lifts. If a lift is found unsafe, the officer can issue orders for repairs or discontinuance of use, subject to appeal. Orders to discontinue use must be complied with unless reversed by an appellate authority.

main_sections.section_title: Owner to give facilities for inspection
main_sections.description: Requires the owner or their agent to provide reasonable facilities for inspection and to procure the attendance of competent personnel for the inspection at their own cost.

Mandates reporting of accidents causing or likely to cause injury to any person to the Inspector of Lifts and relevant authorities. The lift installation must not be interfered with, and operation must not resume without official permission.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers (except rule-making) to authorized officers through official gazette notification, subject to specified conditions.
Requires every lift to be inspected at least once every three months by an authorized officer. An annual fee is charged for such inspection.
States that all fees payable under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the Act's purposes, covering aspects like lift specifications, application procedures, testing, licence conditions, accident reporting, and notice forms. Rules must be laid before the State Legislature.
This section likely outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, though the specific details are not provided in the extracted text.
This section likely deals with how offenses committed by companies are to be handled under the Act.
This section likely specifies the requirement for sanction before prosecuting an offender under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Service of notices, orders or documents
main_sections.description: This section likely details the procedures for serving notices, orders, or other documents related to the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: This section likely provides protection to individuals acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act's provisions.
This section likely contains provisions that save certain actions or rights from the purview of the Act.
This section likely deals with the repeal of any previous enactment that is inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: No lift shall be operated except under and in conformity with the terms of its licence (Section 6).
Owners must apply for permission to erect a new lift and subsequently for a licence to use it (Sections 3 & 4).
Existing lifts must be licensed within two months of the Act's commencement (Section 5).
No additions or alterations to a lift installation are permitted without prior written consent from an authorized officer (Section 7).
Accidents causing or likely to cause injury must be reported immediately to designated authorities, and operations must not resume without permission (Section 10).
Every lift must be inspected at least once every three months (Section 12).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions are outlined in Section 15, though specific details are not in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers authorized by the Government, including Inspectors of Lifts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, issuance of permissions and licences, orders for repairs or discontinuance of use, and prosecution for violations.

rights: Right to appeal against an order to repair or discontinue lift use (Section 8(3)).
Right to operate a lift under a valid licence.
duties: Duty of the owner to apply for permission to erect a lift (Section 3).
Duty of the owner to apply for a licence to use a lift (Sections 4 & 5).
Duty of the owner to comply with repair or discontinuance orders (Section 8(2)).
Duty of the owner to provide facilities for inspection (Section 9).
Duty to report accidents promptly (Section 10).
Duty to pay inspection fees (Section 12).
obligations: Obligation to ensure safe construction, maintenance, and working of lifts.
Obligation to operate lifts only under a valid licence.
Obligation to facilitate inspections and comply with authorized officer's directives.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to erect a lift: Owner applies with detailed specifications to an authorized officer, who forwards it with remarks to the Government for approval/refusal.

Procedure for obtaining a licence to use a lift: After completion, owner notifies the authorized officer and applies for a licence, accompanied by a fee. The officer forwards the application with remarks to the Government for grant/refusal.
Procedure for reporting accidents: Owner/agent must promptly notify the Inspector of Lifts and other specified authorities. Operations cannot resume without written permission.
Procedure for appealing inspection orders: A person aggrieved by an officer's order under Section 8(2) can appeal to the Appellate Authority within thirty days.
administration: The State Government, which delegates powers to authorized officers and Inspectors of Lifts.
important_notes: The Bombay Lifts Act, 1939 was previously in force only in the Bombay Area.
The Act was amended in 1993 to extend the permission period for lift erection from six to twelve months, with possibility of further extension, and to increase inspection fees.
Section 1(3) states the Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification (came into force on 1.8.1976).

title: The Karnataka Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the improvement of live-stock in the State of Karnataka, specifically by regulating the keeping of bulls and promoting the castration of scrub bulls.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the keeping and licensing of bulls that have attained a prescribed age, the inspection of bulls, and the castration of bulls considered unsuitable for breeding.

key_definitions.cow: Includes a buffalo cow and a heifer.
key_definitions.Director: The officer appointed by the State Government as the Director of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services in Karnataka, and includes any other person on whom powers or duties are conferred under section 3.
key_definitions.Licensing Officer: The Director or any other officer authorized to grant licences under section 4.
key_definitions.notification: Notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.keep a bull: To own the bull or have it in possession or custody.
key_definitions.castrated: Rendered incapable of propagating its species.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent to the whole of Karnataka, and its commencement provisions, allowing for different commencement dates in different areas.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'bull', 'cow', 'Director', 'licence', 'Licensing Officer', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'keep a bull', and 'castrated'.

main_sections.section_title: Bulls which have attained a certain age to be licensed
main_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall keep a bull of a prescribed age without a licence. It specifies that a separate licence is required for each bull and outlines who can grant licences, the form, period, and conditions, with no fee charged for the licence.

Details the grounds on which a Licensing Officer may refuse to grant a licence (defective conformation, disease, undesirable breed) or revoke an existing licence (breach of conditions, improper grant). It also includes provisions for notice, opportunity to show cause, appeal against orders, and finality of appeal orders.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order castration of bulls
main_sections.description: Empowers the Licensing Officer to order the castration of bulls that have attained the prescribed age and are not licensed, specifying a timeframe and approved methods. Castration is free unless the owner makes their own arrangements.

Specifies penalties for contravening the Act's provisions, including keeping bulls without a licence, failing to submit for inspection, failing to comply with castration orders, or failing to produce a licence. Fines are prescribed, with higher fines for subsequent offences.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Licensing Officer to castrate bulls
main_sections.description: Grants the Licensing Officer the power to direct the castration of bulls if the owner fails to do so as required. It also covers the seizure, castration, marking, and subsequent sale or placement of stray bulls, and provisions for owners to reclaim seized bulls.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Licensing Officer, etc., to inspect or mark bull and to enter premises
main_sections.description: Grants Licensing Officers and authorized officers the power to inspect and mark bulls, and to enter premises where bulls are believed to be kept, for the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Repeals existing enactments related to livestock improvement and provides for savings, ensuring continuity.

important_rules: No person shall keep a bull that has attained the prescribed age without a valid licence (Section 4(1)).
A separate licence is required for each bull kept (Section 4(1) Explanation).
Licences can be refused if the bull is of defective conformation, suffers from incurable disease, or is of an undesirable breed (Section 5(1)).
Licences can be revoked for breach of conditions or if granted under improper circumstances (Section 5(2)).
A licence must be surrendered if it expires, is revoked, or the bull dies or is effectively castrated (Section 6).
Persons keeping licensed bulls must produce the licence on demand by authorized officers or the person in charge of a cow before service (Section 10).
Bulls not licensed or in respect of which no licence is in force and which have attained the prescribed age must be effectively castrated within thirty days of notice (Section 9(1)).
The Licensing Officer can order the castration and marking of bulls if the owner fails to comply with a castration notice, and can seize and castrate stray bulls (Section 13).

penalties: Fine up to twenty-five rupees for initial offences.
Fine up to fifty rupees for subsequent offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Officers, the Director, and officers authorized by the Director. Village officers and servants, and officers of Animal Husbandry, Agriculture, Community Development, and Revenue Departments also have reporting and prevention duties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, demand for production of licences, orders for castration, seizure of bulls, imposition of fines for contraventions, and composition of offences.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of refusal or revocation of a licence (Section 5(4)).
Right for owners to claim proceeds from the sale of seized and castrated bulls after deduction of costs (Section 13(2)(c)(i)).
Right for owners to reclaim seized bulls on payment of maintenance costs (Section 13(2)(c)(ii)).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for keeping a bull of a prescribed age (Section 4(1)).
Duty to surrender a licence under specified circumstances (Section 6).
Duty to submit a bull for inspection when required (Section 8).
Duty to have a bull effectively castrated when ordered (Section 9(1)).
Duty to produce a licence on demand (Section 10).
Duty of specified officers to report offences and prevent their commission (Section 15).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the conditions of a licence.
Obligation to comply with notices served under the Act, including orders for castration.
Obligation to provide reasonable assistance during inspections.

key_procedures: Licensing Procedure: Application for a licence for a bull of prescribed age; assessment by Licensing Officer; grant or refusal based on prescribed conditions; issuance of licence in prescribed form.

Revocation Procedure: Notice to the licensee of grounds for revocation; opportunity for the licensee to show cause; order of revocation by Licensing Officer or superior authority; communication of order with grounds.

Castration Procedure: Notice to the keeper of an unlicensed bull of prescribed age to get it castrated; option for owner to make own arrangements or have it done by Licensing Officer free of charge; if no compliance, Licensing Officer can direct castration and marking.

Seizure and Disposal Procedure (for stray/unidentified bulls): Seizure by Licensing Officer if ownership cannot be ascertained; castration and marking; sale by public auction or sending to recognized institutions; provisions for owners to claim proceeds or the bull upon payment of costs.
administration: The Act is administered by the Director of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services in Karnataka, Licensing Officers (who can be the Director or other authorized officers), and other officers appointed or authorized by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to unify livestock improvement laws across Karnataka.
The State Government has the power to notify specific areas for different commencement dates of the Act.
A bull dedicated to a religious purpose is exempt from licensing requirements (Section 21).
No fee is charged for the grant of a licence for a bull (Section 4(2)).

title: THE KARNATAKA LOCAL AUTHORITIES (OFFICIAL LANGUAGE) ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the adoption of Kannada as the language to be used for official purposes by all the local authorities within the State of Karnataka.
scope: The act applies to all local authorities within the State of Karnataka. This includes statutory corporations established by or under a law made by the State Legislature, and co-operative societies registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959.

key_definitions.local authority: Includes a statutory corporation established by or under a law made by the State Legislature with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, and a co-operative society registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Local Authorities (Official Language) Act, 1981.

main_sections.section_title: Kannada to be the official language of all the local authorities.
main_sections.description: This section declares Kannada as the official language of all local authorities in the State of Karnataka. It also includes provisos allowing the use of English in specific communication scenarios and provisions for linguistic minorities.

important_rules: Rule 1: Kannada shall be the official language of all local authorities in Karnataka.
Rule 2: The English language may be used in communications addressed to the Central Government offices, offices of other State Governments, and the Accountant General.
Rule 3: The English language may be used in communications relating to orders made under any law which are subject to appeal or revision by any authority.
Rule 4: The English language may be used in communications addressed to courts other than village courts.
Rule 5: The English language may be used where it cannot be dispensed with due to administrative reasons or where communications are purely technical and scientific in nature.

Rule 6: If the population of a linguistic minority within the area of operation of a local authority is not less than fifteen percent, petitions shall be accepted in the language of such minority and replies shall be given in that language as far as possible.
Rule 7: Hand-outs and publicity material shall also be given in the language of such minority.
Rule 8: Notices of the local authorities shall also be published in the language of such minority.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

rights: Right of linguistic minorities to have petitions accepted and replied to in their language (if population is >= 15%).
Right of linguistic minorities to receive hand-outs and publicity material in their language.
Right of linguistic minorities to have local authority notices published in their language.
duties: Duty of local authorities to use Kannada as their official language.
