Duty of local authorities to accept petitions in minority languages and reply in those languages where applicable.
Duty of local authorities to provide hand-outs and publicity material in minority languages where applicable.
Duty of local authorities to publish notices in minority languages where applicable.
obligations: Obligation to use Kannada for official purposes by all local authorities.
Obligation to consider the use of English in specific circumstances as outlined in the provisos.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining if a linguistic minority population is not less than fifteen percent in the area of operation of a local authority to trigger provisions for their language use.
Procedure for accepting and replying to petitions in minority languages.
Procedure for providing publicity material and notices in minority languages.
administration: The Act is enacted by the Karnataka State Legislature. The administration would likely fall under the State Government, possibly through departments dealing with local self-government and language.
important_notes: The English language is permitted for specific types of communications, including those to Central Government, other State Governments, the Accountant General, and in legal appeals/revisions.
English may also be used in communications to courts (excluding village courts) and where it is administratively essential or technically/scientifically required.
The provisions for linguistic minorities are triggered only if their population within the local authority's area is at least fifteen percent.

title: THE KARNATAKA LOKAYUKTA ACT, 1984
purpose: To make provision for the appointment and functions of certain authorities for making enquiries into administrative action relatable to matters specified in List II or List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, taken by or on behalf of the Government of Karnataka or certain public authorities in the State of Karnataka (including any omission or commission in connection with or arising out of such action) in certain cases and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto. The Act aims to improve public administration by looking into complaints against administrative actions, including cases of corruption, favouritism, and official indiscipline.
scope: The Act applies to administrative actions taken by or on behalf of the Government of Karnataka or certain public authorities in the State of Karnataka. It covers 'public servants' which includes the Chief Minister, Ministers, members of the State Legislature, all officers of the State Government, Chairmen/Vice-Chairmen of Local Authorities, statutory bodies, corporations, co-operative societies, universities, and persons in the service or pay of these entities.

key_definitions.action: Administrative action taken by way of decision, recommendation, or finding, or in any other manner, including wilful failure or omission to act.
key_definitions.allegation: An affirmation that a public servant has abused their position, been actuated by personal interest or improper motives, is guilty of corruption, favoritism, nepotism, lack of integrity, or has failed to act according to norms of integrity and conduct.
key_definitions.grievance: A claim by a person that they sustained injustice or undue hardship in consequence of maladministration.
key_definitions.maladministration: Action taken or purporting to have been taken in the exercise of administrative functions where such action, or the procedure governing it, is unreasonable, unjust, oppressive, improperly discriminatory, or involves wilful negligence or undue delay.
key_definitions.public servant: A broad category including Chief Minister, Ministers, Members of the State Legislature, Government Servants, Chairmen/Members of local authorities, statutory bodies, corporations, government companies, societies, co-operative societies, and universities, and persons in their service or pay.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provisions for its commencement.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'action', 'allegation', 'grievance', 'maladministration', 'public servant', etc.

Details the appointment process for the Lokayukta and Upalokayuktas. The Lokayukta must have held the office of a Judge of the Supreme Court or Chief Justice of a High Court, and an Upalokayukta must have held the office of a Judge of a High Court. Appointments are made on the advice of the Chief Minister in consultation with specified dignitaries.

main_sections.section_title: Matters which may be investigated by the Lokayukta and an Upalokayukta
main_sections.description: Outlines the types of complaints and grievances that the Lokayukta and Upalokayukta can investigate, relating to administrative actions of public servants.
Specifies matters that are excluded from the purview of investigation by the Lokayukta and Upalokayukta.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions relating to complaints and investigations
main_sections.description: Covers the procedures for filing complaints and conducting investigations by the Lokayukta and Upalokayukta.
Deals with the reporting mechanism of the Lokayukta and Upalokayukta after conducting investigations.

main_sections.section_title: Public servant to vacate office if directed by Lokayukta, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the consequences for a public servant if the Lokayukta finds the allegation against them to be prima facie true and directs them to vacate office.
Empowers the Lokayukta to initiate prosecution against a public servant if satisfied that a criminal offence has been committed, with prior sanction requirements deemed granted.

main_sections.section_title: Public servants to submit property statements
main_sections.description: Requires public servants to submit statements of their properties and assets.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and savings provisions in relation to this Act.

important_rules: Public servants, if found guilty of administrative misconduct or corruption, may be directed by the Lokayukta to resign or may be deemed to have vacated office or been placed under suspension.
The Lokayukta can initiate prosecution for criminal offences committed by public servants, with any prior sanction requirements deemed to be granted.
Public servants are required to submit property statements.

Complaints can be investigated if they relate to allegations of abuse of position, personal interest, corruption, favoritism, nepotism, lack of integrity, or failure to act according to norms of conduct.

penalties: Public servant to resign office if directed by Lokayukta.
Public servant to be deemed to have vacated office if directed by Lokayukta.
Public servant to be deemed to have been kept under suspension if directed by Lokayukta.
Prosecution for false complaints (Section 20).
Punishment for contempt of Lokayukta or Upalokayukta (Section 17A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Lokayukta and Upalokayukta
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations into complaints and grievances, submission of reports to the competent authority, initiation of prosecution, and direction for public servants to vacate office or be suspended.

rights: Right of citizens to complain about maladministration and corruption of public servants.
Right to fair investigation into grievances.
duties: Duty of public servants to act with integrity and in accordance with norms of conduct.
Duty of public servants to submit property statements.
obligations: Obligation of the State Government to appoint Lokayukta and Upalokayuktas.
Obligation of the competent authority to act upon the recommendations and directions of the Lokayukta.

key_procedures: Complaint Filing: A person aggrieved by maladministration or the conduct of a public servant can file a complaint with the Lokayukta or Upalokayukta.
Investigation: Upon receiving a complaint, the Lokayukta or Upalokayukta conducts an investigation, which may involve gathering evidence, examining documents, and interviewing persons.
Report Generation: After the investigation, the Lokayukta or Upalokayukta prepares a report detailing their findings and recommendations.

Action on Report: The report is submitted to the competent authority, who is then required to take action based on the recommendations. This may include directing a public servant to resign or be suspended.
Prosecution Initiation: If the Lokayukta is satisfied that a criminal offence has been committed, they can initiate prosecution.
administration: The Act establishes the institution of the Lokayukta and Upalokayuktas for its administration and enforcement. The State Government is responsible for appointing these authorities and making rules under the Act.
important_notes: The Act came into force on January 15, 1986.
The Vigilance Commission was abolished and its pending inquiries and investigations were transferred to the Lokayukta.
The Act has been amended by subsequent amending acts, including those related to the pay of Lokayukta and Upalokayukta, and the power to punish for contempt.

title: THE KARNATAKA MEDICAL REGISTRATION ACT, 1961
purpose: To consolidate the laws for the registration of medical practitioners of modern scientific system of medicine, surgery and obstetrics, other than veterinary medicine and surgery, in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to practitioners of the modern scientific system of medicine, surgery and obstetrics.

key_definitions.Council: The Karnataka Medical Council established under this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.registered practitioner: Any person registered under the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Council' or 'Medical Council', 'notification', 'registered practitioner', 'regulations', and 'rules'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment, incorporation and constitution of Council
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Medical Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It details the composition of the Council, which consists of fifteen members: six elected by registered medical practitioners, two elected by members of Faculties of Medicine of Universities, two elected by staff of medical colleges who are registered practitioners, and five nominated by the State Government. It also states that the President and Vice-President shall be elected by the members.

Mandates the Registrar to maintain a register of medical practitioners in a prescribed form. The Registrar's duties include keeping the register correct, updating addresses, entering additional qualifications, and striking off names of deceased registered persons.

Outlines the process for registration of medical practitioners. Persons holding medical qualifications included in the Schedules to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, can apply for registration by submitting their qualifications and paying a fee. It also includes a provision for registering practitioners registered under repealed enactments. The Council may refuse registration to persons convicted of cognizable offenses or found guilty of infamous conduct.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of Medical Practitioner's name from Register for misconduct
main_sections.description: Empowers the Medical Council to take action against a medical practitioner found guilty of misconduct after due inquiry, which may include issuing a letter of warning.

important_rules: Rule for election of President, Vice-President, and other members of the Medical Council.
Rules for the time and place of meetings of the Medical Council and the procedure at such meetings.
Rules for the maintenance and form of the register of medical practitioners.
Rules for appeals against the decisions of the Registrar regarding registration.

penalties: Section 28 lists penalties for offenses under the Act. Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided text excerpt, but it indicates that penalties exist.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Medical Council and the State Government are the primary authorities for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries into misconduct, removal of names from the register, and legal penalties as prescribed by the Act.

rights: Right to be registered if holding prescribed medical qualifications.
Right to appeal against the Registrar's decisions.
Right for registered practitioners to vote in Council elections.
Exemption from serving on inquests, etc. (Section 23).
duties: Duty of the Registrar to maintain the register.
Duty of registered practitioners to comply with the Act and Council regulations.
Duty of medical practitioners to notify their death (Section 22).
obligations: Obligation to hold prescribed medical qualifications for registration.
Obligation to pay prescribed fees for registration and other services.
Obligation for medical colleges and universities to participate in the election of Council members.
Obligation for the State Government to establish and oversee the Medical Council.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment, incorporation, and constitution of the Karnataka Medical Council.
Procedure for nomination of members in case of default in election.
Procedure for the election of the President and Vice-President.
Procedure for handling vacancies in the Council.
Procedure for registration of medical practitioners, including application and fee payment.
Procedure for appeals against the Registrar's decisions.
Procedure for removal of a medical practitioner's name from the register for misconduct, involving due inquiry.
Procedure for renewal of registration (Section 19).
Procedure for publication of the list of practitioners (Section 26).
administration: The Karnataka Medical Council and the State Government administer the Act. The Registrar is appointed by the Council and acts under its orders.
important_notes: The Act consolidates existing laws for medical registration in the state, addressing the need for a single Medical Register following the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
The State Government has the power to make rules (Section 31) and the Council can make regulations (Section 32).
The State Government has control over the Council (Section 33).
The Act includes provisions for removing difficulties and for protection of actions taken in good faith (Section 29).
The jurisdiction of Civil Courts is limited regarding matters under this Act (Section 30).

title: THE KARNATAKA MINISTERS SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the salaries, residences, conveyances, and other allowances of the Chief Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers in the State of Karnataka.
scope: This Act applies to the Chief Minister, Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers of the State of Karnataka. It governs their remuneration, housing, transport, and other associated benefits.

key_definitions.Minister: Includes the Chief Minister, a Minister of State, and a Deputy Minister.
key_definitions.Minister of State: Refers to a Minister of State appointed in the State Government.
key_definitions.Deputy Minister: Refers to a Deputy Minister appointed in the State Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Minister', 'Minister of State', and 'Deputy Minister'.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries of Chief Minister and Ministers
main_sections.description: Specifies the salaries payable to the Chief Minister and other Ministers.
Deals with the provision of residential accommodation for Ministers.
Outlines the provisions for conveyances to be provided to Ministers.
Specifies the salaries payable to Ministers of State.
Deals with the provision of residential accommodation for Ministers of State.
Outlines the provisions for conveyances to be provided to Ministers of State.
Specifies the salaries payable to Deputy Ministers.
Deals with the provision of residential accommodation for Deputy Ministers.
Outlines the provisions for conveyances to be provided to Deputy Ministers.

main_sections.section_title: Use of helicopter and aircraft by Ministers etc
main_sections.description: Regulates the use of helicopters and aircraft by Ministers and other specified officials.

main_sections.section_title: State Government to bear electricity and water charges in certain other cases
main_sections.description: Specifies circumstances under which the State Government will bear electricity and water charges.

main_sections.section_title: Deductions in respect of house rent etc.
main_sections.description: Details deductions to be made for house rent and other similar charges.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling Allowances of a Minister, a Minister of State or a Deputy Minister on assuming or relinquishing office
main_sections.description: Specifies the travelling allowances admissible to Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers when assuming or relinquishing office.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and other allowances on tours
main_sections.description: Lays down the rules for travelling and other allowances for Ministers when on tours.
Provides for medical attendance for Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.

main_sections.section_title: Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers not to practise profession, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers from practicing professions or engaging in certain other activities.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No. 2 of 1956 and savings
main_sections.description: Repeals the Karnataka Ordinance No. 2 of 1956 and provides for savings.

important_rules: Ministers are entitled to specific salaries as prescribed in the Act.
Official residences are provided to Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
Conveyances are made available for official duties.
Travelling and daily allowances are admissible for official tours, both within and outside the State.
Medical attendance is provided to eligible officials.
Certain allowances like sumptuary allowance, house rent allowance, and conveyance allowance are provided.
Provisions exist for the use of helicopters and aircraft by Ministers for official purposes.
Deductions are made for house rent and other charges.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is primarily through the provisions outlined in the Act regarding salaries, allowances, residences, and conveyances. The State Government also has the power to make rules to further the Act's implementation.

rights: Right to receive prescribed salaries and allowances.
Right to be provided with official residences and conveyances.
Right to medical attendance.
Right to travelling and daily allowances for official tours.
Right to use State-owned helicopter and aircraft under specified conditions.
duties: Duty to adhere to the provisions of the Act regarding salaries and allowances.
Duty not to practice any profession or engage in other prohibited activities.
Duty to comply with rules made by the State Government under the Act.
obligations: Ministers are obligated to use provided facilities for official purposes.
Deductions for house rent and other charges must be met.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming travelling and daily allowances on tours.
Procedure for assuming or relinquishing office and related allowances.
Procedure for making rules by the State Government.
Procedure for medical attendance.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka is responsible for administering this Act. Specific departments or ministries would handle the day-to-day implementation.
important_notes: The Act has been amended multiple times since its enactment to revise salaries, allowances, and introduce new benefits in response to economic changes and evolving needs.
Provisions for Ministers of State were introduced via amendments.
The Act includes provisions for pension for Ministers who have served for a minimum period.
The cost of living and travel expenses have been a significant factor in the amendments, leading to increases in various allowances.

title: The Karnataka Money-Lenders Act, 1961
purpose: To regulate and control transactions of money-lending in the State of Karnataka, affording protection to innocent debtors and restricting usurious practices.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. Applies to individuals, undivided Hindu families, companies, and unincorporated bodies engaged in the business of money-lending within the state, with certain exclusions.

key_definitions.bank: Includes various scheduled banks, subsidiary banks, regional rural banks, financial institutions like IDBI, NABARD, EXIM Bank, SFCs, and certain other specified financial entities.
key_definitions.business_of_money_lending: The business of advancing loans, irrespective of whether it is in conjunction with or in addition to any other business.
key_definitions.loan: An advance at interest, whether of money or in kind, including transactions that in substance amount to such an advance. Excludes deposits with government banks, co-operative societies, loans by government/local authorities, provident fund advances, loans to/by insurance companies and banks, certain advances based on negotiable instruments, and loans to traders/licensed money-lenders/tenants under specific conditions.
key_definitions.money_lender: An individual, undivided Hindu family, company, or unincorporated body that carries on the business of money-lending in the State or has its principal place of business in the State. Excludes banks and other financial institutions specified by the State Government.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Money-lenders Act, 1961, specifies its extension to the whole of Karnataka, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'bank', 'business of money-lending', 'capital', 'company', 'co-operative society', 'interest', 'licence', 'licence fee', 'loan', 'money-lender', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'principal', and 'Provident Fund'.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Registrar General, Registrars and Assistant Registrars
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Registrar General, Registrars, and Assistant Registrars for the purposes of the Act.
Mandates the maintenance of a register of money-lenders by the Registrar.
Requires every money-lender to obtain a licence to carry on the business of money-lending.
Outlines the procedure for applying for a money-lender's licence.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of licence and entry in register
main_sections.description: Details the process of granting a licence and its subsequent entry in the register of money-lenders.
Specifies the conditions that may be attached to a licence.
Deals with the forfeiture of security deposited by a money-lender.
Lays down the grounds on which the issue of a licence may be refused.
Grants the Registrar the power to cancel a money-lender's licence.

main_sections.section_title: Suits by money-lenders not holding licence
main_sections.description: Prohibits money-lenders from instituting suits for recovery of loans if they do not hold a valid licence.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of money-lender to keep accounts and furnish copies
main_sections.description: Mandates money-lenders to maintain proper accounts and provide copies to debtors.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of court in suits regarding loans
main_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for courts in suits related to loans.
Imposes limitations on the rates of interest that can be charged.
Provides general provisions relating to penalties for contraventions of the Act.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of existing laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Money-lenders must obtain a licence to conduct their business (Section 5).
Money-lenders must maintain proper accounts and furnish copies to debtors (Section 20).
There are limitations on the rates of interest that can be charged (Section 28).
Money-lenders must exhibit their names over their shops (Section 36).
Loans advanced by banks, co-operative societies, government, and certain other entities are excluded from the Act's purview (Section 2(9)).

penalties: Penalties for carrying on business without a licence.
Penalties for contravening provisions of the Act, including fines and imprisonment (enhanced by amendments).
Specific offences like entry of wrong sums in bonds or molestation of debtors carry penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar General, Registrars, Assistant Registrars, and authorised officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, registration, inspection of premises, seizure of documents, court proceedings for recovery of loans, and imposition of penalties. Authorised officers have powers of entry, inspection, and seizure (Section 15).

rights: Debtors are not bound to admit the correctness of accounts presented by money-lenders (Section 23).
Courts have the power to limit interest recoverable in certain cases (Section 26).
Courts can direct payment of decretal amounts by installments (Section 27).
Right to obtain a licence for legitimate money-lending business.
Right to appeal against certain orders of the Registrar.
Right to receive copies of accounts from the money-lender.
duties: Duty of money-lenders to obtain a licence.
Duty to maintain accounts and furnish statements.
Duty to display name over the shop.
Duty to inform debtors of the terms of the loan.
Duty to comply with licence conditions.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to interest rate limitations.
Obligation to allow inspection of accounts and premises by authorised officers.
Obligation to pay licence fees and security deposits.
Obligation to repay security deposit in case of licence cancellation.

key_procedures: Licensing of money-lenders: Application, scrutiny, grant/refusal of licence, and registration (Sections 6, 7, 8).
Maintaining and furnishing accounts: Money-lenders must keep accounts and provide statements to debtors (Sections 20, 21).

Court procedures in loan suits: Specific procedures to be followed by courts when dealing with suits for recovery of loans, including powers to limit interest and order installment payments (Sections 24, 26, 27).
Cancellation/Suspension of Licences: Procedures for cancellation by the Registrar or Court (Sections 9, 13, 16).
Enforcement actions: Powers of authorised officers to enter, inspect, and seize documents (Section 15).
administration: The State Government through the Registrar General, Registrars, and Assistant Registrars appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act was amended to enhance licence periods and fees, introduce security deposits for money-lenders dealing with pledged ornaments, and specify accounts to be kept in Kannada or English.
Certain institutions like banks and co-operative societies are excluded from the definition of 'money-lender' and thus from the purview of the Act.
The Act aims to curb usurious practices and protect debtors.
Penalties have been enhanced over time through amendments.

title: THE KARNATAKA NURSES, MIDWIVES AND HEALTH VISITORS ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the registration of nurses, midwives, and health visitors in the State of Karnataka and to ensure uniformity in law and control over the nursing profession.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to persons practicing as nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, and health visitors. Certain provisions have specific commencement dates and may apply to particular classes of persons or in specified areas.

key_definitions.affiliated_institution: An institution for nursing of the sick, maternity, or child welfare, affiliated to the Council.
key_definitions.auxiliary_nurse_midwife: A person who has passed the prescribed examination for this category.
key_definitions.council: The Karnataka Nursing Council constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.health_visitor: A person holding a Health Visitors’ Certificate from a Council-recognized institution.
key_definitions.institution: Includes any association that maintains or controls a nurses' establishment.
key_definitions.licensing_authority: In a municipal area, the municipal corporation, council, or other municipal authority; in other areas, the taluk development board. The State Government can specify other authorities.
key_definitions.list: A list of nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, and health visitors maintained under section 17.
key_definitions.midwife: A person holding a certificate in midwifery from a Council-recognized institution.
key_definitions.nurse: A person holding a certificate in nursing from a Council-recognized institution.
key_definitions.nurses_establishment: An establishment, whether for gain or not, providing or intending to provide services of nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, or health visitors.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), commencement dates for different parts, and application.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'affiliated institution', 'auxiliary nurse-midwife', 'Council', 'health visitor', 'institution', 'licensing authority', 'list', 'midwife', 'nurse', 'nurses establishment', 'prescribed', 'register', 'registered medical practitioner', and 'rule'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment, incorporation and constitution of Council
main_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Karnataka Nursing Council as a body corporate, its perpetual succession, common seal, power to acquire property, contract, sue, and be sued. It also outlines the composition of the Council, including ex-officio, elected, and nominated members, and the election of the President and Vice-President.
Pertains to the maintenance of a register for nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, and health visitors.
Specifies the qualifications and criteria for individuals to be registered under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal of registration and removal and re-entry of names
main_sections.description: Covers the grounds and procedures for refusing registration, removing names from the register, and re-entering them.

main_sections.section_title: Persons not registered or included in the list not to practise as nurse, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits individuals who are not registered or included in the list from practicing as nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, or health visitors.
Provides for the regulation of nurses' establishments.
Deals with the recognition and regulation of training institutions for nurses, midwives, and health visitors.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for dishonest use of certificate
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for the dishonest use of certificates related to nursing practice.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for unlawful assumption of title of registered nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife or health visitor
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for falsely assuming the title of a registered nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife, or health visitor.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Council to make bye-laws
main_sections.description: Empowers the Council to make bye-laws for its functioning and for the purposes of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for dishonest use of certificate (Section 26).
Penalty for unlawful assumption of title of registered nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife or health visitor (Section 27).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Nursing Council, Licensing Authorities, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration processes, maintenance of registers and lists, regulation of establishments and training institutions, and by imposing penalties for violations.

rights: Right to practice as a registered nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife, or health visitor upon fulfilling registration requirements.
Right to appeal against orders of refusal of registration or removal from the register.
Right to have names retained on the register/list if conditions are met.
duties: Duty to obtain registration or be included in the list before practicing.
Duty to notify licensing authority before commencing practice (Section 21).
Duty to adhere to regulations for nurses' establishments (Section 22).
Duty to undergo training in recognized institutions for qualification.
Duty to pay renewal fees for registration.
obligations: Obligation to be registered or listed to practice legally.
Obligation to comply with the rules and bye-laws made under the Act.
Obligation to maintain professional standards as prescribed.

key_procedures: Establishment and constitution of the Karnataka Nursing Council (Section 3).
Registration of nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, and health visitors (Sections 12, 13).
Refusal of registration, removal from register, and re-entry of names (Section 14).
Appeals against registration-related orders (Section 15).
Renewal of registration (Section 16).
Maintenance of a list of practicing professionals (Section 17).
Regulation of nurses' establishments (Section 22).
Recognition of training institutions (Section 23).
Making of rules by the State Government (Section 29).
Making of bye-laws by the Council (Section 30).
administration: The Karnataka Nursing Council and the State Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to create a uniform law for the nursing profession across the state, replacing separate enactments from Bombay, Hyderabad, and Madras areas.
The Act was amended in 1981 to increase the renewal fee for registration from one rupee to five rupees.
Specific parts of the Act came into force at different times, with Part IV having a delayed commencement and selective application.
The Council has the power to affiliate institutions for nursing education and welfare.

title: THE KARNATAKA OFFICIAL LANGUAGE ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the adoption of Kannada as the language to be used for official purposes of the State of Karnataka and for the continuance of the use of English for the transaction of business of the State Legislature, and to declare authorised Kannada translations of Central and State Acts and other legal instruments.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to official purposes of the State, the transaction of business in the State Legislature, and the authoritative translation of Central and State Acts and other legal instruments into Kannada.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Karnataka Official Language Act, 1963, and it extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.section_title: Kannada to be the official language of the State.
main_sections.description: Declares Kannada as the official language of the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.section_title: English to be continued to be used for official purposes until the Government otherwise directs.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding Section 2, English shall continue to be used for all official purposes of the State for which it was used before the commencement of the Act, until the State Government directs otherwise by notification under Section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Government’s power to notify the official purposes for which Kannada to be used.
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to direct, by notification in the Official Gazette, that Kannada shall be used for specified official purposes and in specified areas.

main_sections.section_title: Language to be used in the legislature etc.
main_sections.description: Allows for the continued use of English, in addition to Kannada and Hindi, for transacting business in the State Legislature. It also permits the use of Kannada in Bills, amendments, Acts, Ordinances, orders, rules, regulations, or bye-laws issued by the State Government or the Governor.

main_sections.section_title: Authorised Kannada translation of Central and State Acts.
main_sections.description: Provides that an authorised Kannada translation of Central Acts, State Acts, Ordinances, rules, regulations, or bye-laws, published under the authority of the Governor, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in the Kannada language.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications issued under section 4 to be placed before the Legislature.
main_sections.description: Mandates that every notification issued under Section 4 must be laid before each House of the State Legislature. Both Houses can agree to modify or annul the notification.

important_rules: Kannada is the official language of the State of Karnataka.
English may continue to be used for official purposes until the Government directs otherwise.
The State Government can specify official purposes and areas where Kannada must be used.
English, Kannada, and Hindi can be used for the transaction of business in the State Legislature.
Kannada can be used in legislative bills, ordinances, and administrative rules.
Authorised Kannada translations of legal texts are deemed authoritative.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (specifically mentioned for issuing notifications and directing the use of languages). The Legislature has oversight over notifications issued under Section 4.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the State Government, and through legislative review of such notifications.

rights: Right to use English for official purposes until otherwise directed.
Right to use Kannada as the official language of the State.
Right to use English, Kannada, and Hindi in the State Legislature.
Right for authorised Kannada translations of legal texts to be considered authoritative.
duties: Duty of the State Government to notify official purposes for Kannada usage.
Duty to place notifications before the Legislature for review.
Duty to ensure authorised Kannada translations are published.
obligations: Obligation to adopt Kannada as the official language.
Obligation to continue English usage for certain purposes until directed otherwise.
Obligation to abide by legislative review of notifications.

key_procedures: The State Government may issue notifications to specify official purposes and areas for the use of Kannada.
Notifications issued under Section 4 must be laid before the State Legislature for a period of thirty days.
The State Legislature can modify or annul notifications issued under Section 4.
The State Government may appoint a date for the commencement of the provisions related to authorised Kannada translations via notification.
administration: General Administration Department (as indicated by the signatory of the notification for the Amendment Act of 1974).
important_notes: The Act has been amended by Act 27 of 1974 and Act 6 of 1982.
The provisions of Article 345 of the Constitution of India are referenced.
The Act acknowledges the constitutional provision (Article 210(2)) regarding the use of English in State Legislatures after a certain period.
The 'Karnataka Adaptations of Laws Order 1973' has adapted certain provisions of the Act.
Section 5A regarding authorised Kannada translations became effective from 1st February 1975, as notified.

title: THE KARNATAKA OPEN PLACES (PREVENTION OF DISFIGUREMENT) ACT, 1981
purpose: To prevent disfigurement, by unauthorised advertisements of places open to public view in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act applies to places open to public view within the State of Karnataka. This includes public places and private places or buildings, monuments, statues, posts, walls, fences, trees, or contrivances visible from a public place. The Act has come into force in specific cities and municipalities, with the State Government having the power to extend its application to other areas. It also excludes ancient and historical monuments declared to be of national importance.

key_definitions.advertisement: Any printed, cyclostyled, typed or written, notice, document, paper or any other thing containing any letter, word, picture sign or visible representation.
key_definitions.place open to public view: Includes any private place or building monument, statue, post, wall, fence, tree or contrivance visible to a person being in, or passing along, any public place.
key_definitions.public place: Means any place (including a road, street or way, whether a thoroughfare or not and a landing place) to which the public are granted access or have a right to resort or over which they have a right to pass.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act and outlines its commencement. It specifies the initial date of enforcement in certain cities and allows the State Government to appoint future dates for other areas.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'advertisement', 'place open to public view', and 'public place'.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for unauthorised disfigurement by advertisement.
main_sections.description: This section defines the offence of disfiguring a place open to public view with an unauthorized advertisement and prescribes the punishment. It also includes a proviso detailing exceptions to this rule.

main_sections.section_title: Burden of proof in certain cases.
main_sections.description: In cases prosecuted under Section 3, this section places the burden of proving the existence of written permission from the local authority on the accused person.
This section specifies that individuals who abet the commission of an offence under Section 3 will be punished with the same penalty as the principal offender.

This section deals with offences committed by companies, making them and responsible individuals within the company liable. It includes provisions for when an offence is committed with consent, connivance, or gross negligence.
This section provides indemnity to the State Government, local authorities, or any person for actions taken in good faith or intended to be taken under the Act.
This section declares offences punishable under this Act to be cognizable offences under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
This section clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and do not derogate from, any other existing laws.
This section grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying these rules before the State Legislature.

This section repeals the Karnataka Open Places (Prevention of Disfigurement) Ordinance, 1981, and states that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall affix to, or erect, inscribe or exhibit on, any place open to public view any advertisement without the written permission of the local authority having jurisdiction over such area. (Section 3)
Rule 2: If a person is prosecuted for an offence under section 3, the burden of proving that they had the required written permission shall be on them. (Section 4)
Rule 3: Whoever causes, procures, counsels, aids, abets or is accessory to the commission of an offence under section 3 shall be punished with the prescribed punishment. (Section 5)

Rule 4: If a company commits an offence under this Act, every person in charge of and responsible to the company for its business, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty. (Section 6(1))

Rule 5: If an offence by a company is proved to have been committed with the consent, connivance, or gross negligence of a director, manager, secretary or other officer, that individual shall also be deemed guilty. (Section 6(2))

Rule 6: No suit, prosecution, or legal proceeding shall lie against the State Government, any local authority or person for anything done in good faith or intended to be done under this Act. (Section 7)
Rule 7: Offences under this Act are to be treated as cognizable offences. (Section 8)

penalties: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months.
Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authority having jurisdiction over the area (for issuing permissions and presumably for initial enforcement), State Government (for making rules and appointing commencement dates). Offences are cognizable, implying police involvement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for unauthorized disfigurement by advertisements. The act specifies penalties and makes offences cognizable, allowing for police action. The burden of proof for permission rests with the accused. Offences by companies are also addressed.

rights: Right to seek written permission from the local authority for displaying advertisements in places open to public view.
duties: Duty to obtain written permission from the local authority before affixing, erecting, inscribing, or exhibiting any advertisement on any place open to public view.
Duty for individuals in charge of companies to ensure no offences under the act are committed, or to prove their lack of knowledge and due diligence.
obligations: Obligation to not disfigure places open to public view with unauthorized advertisements.
Obligation for companies and their responsible officers to adhere to the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Obtaining written permission from the local authority before displaying advertisements in places open to public view. (Implicit in Section 3)
Procedure 2: Prosecution of offenders under Section 3, with the burden of proof for permission resting on the accused. (Section 4)
Procedure 3: Investigation and prosecution of abettors and offences committed by companies. (Sections 5 & 6)
Procedure 4: Making rules by the State Government and laying them before the State Legislature for modification or annulment. (Section 10)
administration: State Government (for making rules and appointing commencement dates). Local authorities are responsible for granting permissions and likely for initial enforcement. Police are involved in enforcing cognizable offences.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1984 to exclude ancient and historical monuments declared to be of national importance from its purview.
The Act's commencement date varies, with specific cities having an earlier date of enforcement and other areas determined by State Government notification.
The provisions of this Act are supplementary to, not a replacement for, other existing laws.
The Act was preceded by an Ordinance which has since been repealed but actions taken under it are validated.

title: The Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963
purpose: To provide for the salary, allowances, and miscellaneous provisions for Parliamentary Secretaries of the State of Karnataka, ensuring they have adequate facilities to attend to their duties.
scope: This Act applies to Parliamentary Secretaries appointed by the Chief Minister of the State of Karnataka. It covers their salary, allowances, duties, and conduct during their tenure.

key_definitions.Parliamentary Secretary: A member of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly or the Karnataka Legislative Council appointed as a Parliamentary Secretary by the Chief Minister.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Parliamentary Secretaries Salary, Allowances and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1963, and that it shall come into force at once.
Defines 'Parliamentary Secretary' and 'prescribed' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Salary and allowances of Parliamentary Secretary
main_sections.description: Entitles a Parliamentary Secretary to salaries and allowances as are admissible to a Minister, Minister of State, or Deputy Minister under the Karnataka Minister's Salaries and Allowances Act, 1956, as specified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Parliamentary Secretary not to draw salaries and allowances as member
main_sections.description: Stipulates that a Parliamentary Secretary shall not, while drawing salary and allowances for their office, be entitled to any salary and allowances as a member of the legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Functions and duties of Parliamentary Secretary
main_sections.description: Specifies that the functions and duties of a Parliamentary Secretary shall be as determined by the Chief Minister or a Minister to whom they are assigned.

main_sections.section_title: Oath of Office and of Secrecy
main_sections.description: Requires a Parliamentary Secretary to take an oath of office and secrecy, administered by the Chief Minister, in a form specified by the Government before entering office.

main_sections.section_title: Parliamentary Secretary not to practise profession, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits a Parliamentary Secretary, during their tenure, from practising any profession, engaging in any trade, or undertaking any remunerative employment other than their duties as a Parliamentary Secretary.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, which must be laid before both Houses of the State Legislature for a specified period.

important_rules: A Parliamentary Secretary is entitled to salaries and allowances equivalent to those of a Minister, Minister of State, or Deputy Minister, as specified by the Government.
A Parliamentary Secretary cannot draw both their office's salary and allowances and those as a member of the legislature.
The functions and duties of a Parliamentary Secretary are determined by the Chief Minister or the Minister to whom they are assigned.
Parliamentary Secretaries must take an oath of office and secrecy before assuming their role.
Parliamentary Secretaries are prohibited from engaging in any profession, trade, or paid employment outside their official duties during their tenure.
The State Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act, subject to legislative oversight.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, through the Chief Minister and relevant ministers, and the State Legislature for rule-making oversight.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of Parliamentary Secretaries, the specification of their duties, the administration of oaths, and the promulgation of rules by the State Government. The State Legislature reviews rules made under the Act.

rights: Right to receive salaries and allowances as specified.
duties: To perform functions and duties assigned by the Chief Minister or a Minister.
To take Oath of Office and Secrecy.
obligations: To not practice any profession or engage in any trade or undertake remunerative employment other than their duties as Parliamentary Secretary during their tenure.

key_procedures: Appointment of Parliamentary Secretary by the Chief Minister.
Administration of Oath of Office and Secrecy by the Chief Minister.
Specification of functions and duties by the Chief Minister or a Minister.
Laying of rules made by the State Government before the State Legislature for approval/modification.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka, specifically the Chief Minister's Office and potentially other departments involved in ministerial affairs.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1999 (Act 7 of 1999) to include provisions regarding appointment, duties, functions, oath of office, and salary, which were not originally present.
The Act's name was adapted to include 'Salary' and 'Miscellaneous Provisions' by the 1999 amendment.

The original Statement of Objects and Reasons indicates provisions for free furnished residence or house rent allowance, travelling and daily allowances, and free medical aid, though the current text focuses on salary and allowances being admissible to Ministers.

title: THE KARNATAKA PAWNBROKERS ACT, 1961
purpose: To regulate and control the business of pawnbrokers in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to all persons carrying on the business of pawnbrokers.

key_definitions.company: A company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.cooperative_society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959.
key_definitions.interest: Includes any amount, by whatsoever name called, in excess of the principal, paid or payable to a pawnbroker in consideration of or otherwise in respect of a loan, but does not include any sum lawfully charged for or on account of charges.
key_definitions.licence: A licence granted under this Act.
key_definitions.loan: An advance at interest whether of money or in kind and includes any transaction which the Court finds in substance to amount to such an advance, but excludes certain specific types of deposits and advances made by specified institutions and individuals.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.pawn_broker: A person who carries on the business of taking goods and chattels in pawn for a loan. This also includes any person who keeps a shop for the purchase or sale of goods or chattels and who purchases goods or chattels and pays or advances thereon any sum of money, with or under an agreement or understanding expressed or implied that the goods or chattels may be afterwards repurchased on any terms.
key_definitions.pawner: A person delivering an article for pawn to a pawnbroker.
key_definitions.pledge: An article pawned with a pawnbroker.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.principal: In relation to a loan, the amount actually lent to the pawner.
key_definitions.year: The year commencing on the first day of April.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of the State of Karnataka), and commencement dates for different areas.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'company', 'co-operative society', 'interest', 'licence', 'loan', 'notification', 'pawn-broker', 'pawner', 'pledge', 'prescribed', 'principal', and 'year'.

Mandates that no person can carry on business as a pawnbroker without obtaining a licence under the Act. It also specifies that a separate licence is required for each place of business. Licences are valid for five years and may be renewed.

Details the process for applying for and renewing a pawnbroker's licence. It outlines grounds for refusal (bad character of applicant, frequented by bad characters, not holding a Money-Lenders Act licence), the appeal process, licence form and conditions, and the prescribed fees.

Specifies that an applicant for a licence must pay a security deposit at the time of application or renewal. The amount of the security deposit is based on the amount invested in the business and varies according to different investment slabs. This security deposit does not carry any interest.

main_sections.section_title: Pawnbrokers to exhibit their names over shops, etc.
main_sections.description: Requires pawnbrokers to display their names prominently over their shops or places of business.

main_sections.section_title: Interest and charges allowed to pawnbrokers.
main_sections.description: Prescribes the maximum rates of interest and charges that pawnbrokers are allowed to levy on loans.

main_sections.section_title: Pawn-ticket to be given to pawner.
main_sections.description: Mandates that a pawnbroker must give a pawn-ticket to the pawner for every pledge made.

main_sections.section_title: Person producing pawn-ticket presumed to be entitled to redeem the pledge.
main_sections.description: States that any person who produces a pawn-ticket is presumed to be entitled to redeem the pledge, unless the pawnbroker has received notice of loss or theft of the ticket or knows that the person is not entitled.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of owners and of pawners not having pawn-tickets.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for owners whose goods have been pawned without their consent and for pawners who have lost their pawn-tickets.

main_sections.section_title: Pawnbrokers to keep books, give receipts, etc.
main_sections.description: Obliges pawnbrokers to maintain proper books of account, give receipts for all transactions, and provide details of the pledge.
Outlines the conditions and timeframes within which a pawner can redeem their pledge.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of pledge and inspection of sale book.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the sale of unredeemed pledges and allows pawners to inspect the sale book.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of pawnbroker in case of fire.
main_sections.description: Defines the liability of a pawnbroker in case of damage or loss of a pledge due to fire.
Deals with compensation payable by a pawnbroker for the depreciation of a pledge.

main_sections.section_title: Pawn-broker advancing smaller amount or receiving higher interest than that specified in accounts to be punishable.
main_sections.description: Punishes pawnbrokers who advance a smaller amount than specified in their accounts or receive higher interest than legally allowed.

main_sections.section_title: Certain other acts of pawn-brokers to be punishable.
main_sections.description: Specifies other acts by pawnbrokers that are considered punishable offenses under the Act.
This section likely details obligations or procedures for pawnbrokers regarding the redemption of pledges, although the exact content isn't fully visible in the provided text.

main_sections.section_title: Certain acts of pawners to be punishable.
main_sections.description: Outlines acts committed by pawners that are punishable under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: General penalty for contravention of Act, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides a general penalty for any contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Specifies the courts that have the jurisdiction to try offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by Hindu undivided Family, Companies etc.
main_sections.description: Addresses how offenses committed by Hindu undivided families, companies, and other entities are to be dealt with.
Identifies certain offenses under the Act as cognizable, meaning police can arrest without a warrant.

main_sections.section_title: Contract of pawn to be void in certain cases and not to be void in certain other cases.
main_sections.description: States under what circumstances a contract of pawn becomes void and under what circumstances it remains valid.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Contains provisions that save certain existing rights or liabilities from the operation of the Act.
Repeals any previous laws that are inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: Pawnbrokers must obtain a licence to conduct their business.
Licences are valid for five years and can be renewed.
Pawnbrokers must display their names prominently over their shops.
Pawnbrokers must issue a pawn-ticket for every pledge.
Pawnbrokers must maintain proper books of accounts and give receipts for all transactions.
Pledges can be redeemed within a specified period.
Unredeemed pledges can be sold according to a prescribed procedure.
Pawnbrokers are subject to specified maximum interest rates and charges.
Pawnbrokers must pay a security deposit as a condition of their licence.

penalties: Penalty for carrying on business without a licence.
Penalty for advancing a smaller amount or receiving higher interest than specified in accounts.
Penalty for other punishable acts by pawnbrokers.
Penalty for punishable acts by pawners.
General penalty for contravention of the Act or rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and prescribed licensing authorities, along with judicial authorities for trying offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, regulation of interest rates and charges, maintenance of records, procedures for redemption and sale of pledges, and prosecution of offenders by courts.

rights: Pawners have the right to redeem their pledges within the prescribed period.
Pawners have the right to receive a pawn-ticket and a receipt.
Pawners have the right to protection if their goods are pawned without their consent.
Pawners have the right to inspect the sale book of the pawnbroker.
Licensees have the right to appeal against refusal to grant or renew a licence.
duties: Pawnbrokers have a duty to obtain a licence.
Pawnbrokers have a duty to exhibit their names.
Pawnbrokers have a duty to issue pawn-tickets and receipts.
Pawnbrokers have a duty to maintain proper books of account.
Pawnbrokers have a duty to adhere to prescribed interest rates and charges.
Pawnbrokers have a duty to pay security deposits.
Pawners have a duty to redeem pledges within the stipulated time or face sale.
Pawners have a duty to not commit any punishable acts.
obligations: Pawnbrokers are obligated to provide a pawn-ticket for each pledge.
Pawnbrokers are obligated to keep records of all pawn transactions.
Pawnbrokers are obligated to follow the rules regarding the sale of unredeemed pledges.
Pawnbrokers are obligated to not charge interest exceeding the prescribed rates.
Pawnbrokers are obligated to maintain the security deposit.

key_procedures: Application for and grant/renewal of a pawnbroker's licence, including payment of fees and security deposits.
Issuance of pawn-tickets and receipts by pawnbrokers.
Redemption of pledges by pawners within the prescribed time.
Sale of unredeemed pledges by pawnbrokers, including inspection of sale books.
Appeals against orders refusing licence grant or renewal.
Reporting and prosecution of offenses under the Act.
administration: The State Government, through designated licensing authorities and prescribed authorities for appeals, administers the Act. The Karnataka High Court is mentioned in the context of a legal challenge regarding security deposit interest.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to regulate and control the business of pawnbrokers, recognizing that provisions for pawnbrokers differ from those for money-lenders.
Amendments have been made over time to address issues like pawnbrokers pledging articles with commercial banks, increasing license fees, introducing security deposits, and enhancing licence duration.
Specific categories of institutions and individuals are excluded from the definition of 'loan' for the purpose of this Act.

title: The Karnataka Ports (Landing and Shipping Fees) Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the levy of fees on landing, shipping and storage of goods, and on passengers embarking and disembarking within the ports of the State of Karnataka, and for related administrative and financial purposes.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to all ports within the State, excluding major ports. It covers fees on passengers, goods (landed, shipped, stored), animals and vehicles, and various port services.

key_definitions.drift: Includes timber or other floating matter, whether under possession or control of any person or not.
key_definitions.goods: Includes wares and merchandise of every description, and also vehicles, animals, packages, and other articles.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.owner: When used in relation to goods or drift, includes any consignor, consignee, shipper, or agent for the sale, custody, landing, or shipping of such goods or drift.
key_definitions.passenger: Means any person not below the age of three years carried in a vessel, other than the master and crew, the owner, his family, and his servants.
key_definitions.port: Means the area included within the limits of a port to which all or any of the provisions of the Indian Ports Act, 1908 (Central Act XV of 1908) are for the time being applicable, other than a major port.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.vessel: Includes anything made for the conveyance mainly by water of human beings or property.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), mentions that commencement is on a date appointed by the State Government, and specifies its application to all ports in the State (excluding those where the relevant provisions of the Indian Ports Act, 1908 are not applicable and major ports).
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'drift', 'goods', 'notification', 'owner', 'passenger', 'port', 'prescribed', and 'vessel'.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of fees on goods Shipped, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the types of fees that can be levied at prescribed rates and conditions, including on passengers embarking/disembarking, goods landed/shipped, goods stored, animals/vehicles, transhipping, landing/shipping from vessels to port facilities, cranage/porterage, use of port property/places, and any other service related to vessels, passengers, or goods. It also includes provisions for exemptions and penalties for evasion, with a special provision for differential fees for Mangalore port. Fees and penalties are payable in addition to other lawful tolls or charges.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties under this Act by whom to be exercised and performed
main_sections.description: States that the levy of fees and penalties, and the exercise of other powers and performance of duties under the Act and its rules, shall be carried out by such officers and persons as the State Government may direct.

main_sections.section_title: Detention of goods until payment of fees made
main_sections.description: Empowers officers to detain goods until lawful fees and penalties are paid. If dues are not paid within specified periods (30 days from becoming payable or 14 days from notice), the goods can be sold by public auction after deducting expenses, fees, penalties, and fine. Any surplus is to be paid to the owner. Perishable goods can be sold sooner. A notice in writing must be given to the owner/consignee.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of owner causing damage to pier, jetty, etc.
main_sections.description: Holds the owner or master of a vessel, or the owner of drift, liable for damage caused to a pier, jetty, wharf, or quay. Any person causing such damage is also liable. The amount of damage can be ascertained and recovered by seizure and sale of the vessel, drift, or any property thereon, or by other prescribed means.

main_sections.section_title: Expenditure of fees received under this Act
main_sections.description: Lists the purposes for which fees and other amounts received under the Act may be expended, including improvement of facilities for storage and handling of cargo and passengers, administration expenses, and generally for essential works and services for efficient port functioning.

Mandates a separate 'Port Fees Fund Account' for each port, which merges the existing Port Fund Account and General Account from the Indian Ports Act, 1908. All moneys received under this Act, the Indian Ports Act, 1908, or any other law/otherwise concerning a port, shall be credited to this account. The account shall be maintained as prescribed.

Allows the State Government to direct that a group of ports be treated as a single port for the purposes of Section 8. This creates a common 'Karnataka Ports Funds Account' for the payment of expenses for any port in the group. The State Government can make rules for expenditure within the group and exercise authority collectively or separately over the ports.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with offenses committed by companies, specifying liability for directors, managers, and other officers, as well as the company itself.
Clarifies the impact and enforceability of the Act.
Provides protection to officers and persons acting in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder for anything done or intended to be done in execution of their duty.
Repeals previous legislation and provides savings for actions taken or things done under the repealed provisions.

important_rules: Prescribed fees at prescribed rates and conditions are levied on passengers, goods, animals, vehicles, and for port services.
Evasion of fees incurs a penalty not exceeding twice the payable fees.
Fees and penalties are payable in addition to any other lawful tolls or charges.
Goods can be detained until fees and penalties are paid. Unpaid goods can be sold by public auction after a specified period.
Owners of vessels or drifts causing damage to port infrastructure are liable for the repair costs.
Fees collected are to be expended for port improvements, passenger facilities, administration, and general efficient functioning of the port.
All receipts are to be credited to a 'Port Fees Fund Account' for each port, or a common 'Karnataka Ports Funds Account' if ports are grouped.
State Government can group ports for fund management and administrative purposes.
State Government may exempt certain classes of goods, passengers, vessels, animals, or vehicles from fees.
Different fees and conditions may be prescribed for the port of Mangalore.

penalties: Penalty not exceeding twice the fees payable for evading or attempting to evade payment of fees.
Liability for the amount of damage caused to any pier, jetty, wharf, or quay, recoverable by seizure and sale of vessel/drift or other prescribed means.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Such officers and persons as the State Government may direct.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy of fees and penalties, detention and sale of goods, and recovery of damages by seizure and sale of vessels/drifts.

rights: Right to claim surplus proceeds from the sale of detained goods within six months of sale.
Right to use port facilities upon payment of prescribed fees.
Right to receive services for which fees are levied.
duties: Duty to pay prescribed fees on passengers, goods, animals, vehicles, and for port services.
Duty to not evade or attempt to evade fee payment.
Duty to compensate for damages caused to port infrastructure.
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act.
Obligation to allow detention and sale of goods in case of non-payment of fees and penalties.
Obligation to pay fees and penalties in addition to any other lawful tolls or charges.

key_procedures: Levy of fees by designated officers and persons as directed by the State Government.
Detention of goods for non-payment of fees, followed by a written notice to the owner/consignee.
Public auction of detained goods if dues are not paid within the specified period, with surplus proceeds returned to the owner.
Ascertainment and recovery of damages caused to port infrastructure by seizure and sale of vessels/drifts or other prescribed methods.
Crediting of all receipts to the Port Fees Fund Account or Karnataka Ports Funds Account.
Grouping of ports by the State Government for unified fund management and administration.
administration: State Government (through designated officers and persons), Directorate of Ports and Inland Water Transport (implied by amending act context).
important_notes: The Act was amended by Act 8 of 1980, which introduced significant changes, including expanded fee categories and special provisions for Mangalore port. The amendment also repealed the Mangalore Port Trust Act, 1953, transferring the administration of the old Mangalore Port to the State Government.
The Act aims to standardize the levy and collection of port fees across the state for administrative convenience and better utilization of revenue.
The 'Port Fees Fund Account' concept merges revenue streams for comprehensive port development and maintenance.

title: The Karnataka Prevention of Cow Slaughter and Cattle Preservation Act, 1964
purpose: To provide for the prevention of slaughter of cows, calves of cows and calves of she-buffaloes and for the preservation of other cattle in the State.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It regulates the slaughter of cows, calves of cows, calves of she-buffaloes, and other cattle.

key_definitions.animal: Means bull, bullock, buffalo-male or female, or calf of she-buffalo whether male or female.
key_definitions.competent authority: Means a person or a body of persons appointed to perform the functions of a competent authority under this Act.
key_definitions.cow: Includes calf of a cow, whether male or female.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Prevention of Cow Slaughter and Cattle Preservation Act, 1964. It extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and comes into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'animal', 'competent authority', 'cow', 'notification', and 'prescribed'.
Empowers the State Government to appoint a competent authority for specific local areas through a notification.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of slaughter of cow or calf of she-buffalo
main_sections.description: Prohibits the slaughter, intentional killing, or offering for slaughter/killing of any cow or calf of a she-buffalo, notwithstanding any law, custom, or usage to the contrary.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against slaughter of animals without certificate from competent authority
main_sections.description: Prohibits the slaughter of any animal (other than a calf of she-buffalo) without a written certificate from the competent authority. The certificate is granted if the animal is over twelve years old or permanently incapacitated for breeding, draught, or milk, and not suffering from a disease that makes its meat unwholesome.

Grants the State Government the power to call for and examine records of orders passed by the competent authority regarding certificates and to pass appropriate orders. Orders passed by the competent authority or the State Government are final and not subject to court challenge.

main_sections.section_title: Slaughter to be in places specified
main_sections.description: Mandates that animals for which a certificate has been granted under section 5 shall only be slaughtered in places specified by an authority or officer appointed by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on transport of animal or cow for slaughter
main_sections.description: Prohibits the transport of any animal or cow from within the State to any place outside the State for the purpose of slaughter in contravention of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of sale, purchase or disposal of cow or calf of she-buffalo for slaughter
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale, purchase, or disposal (or offering for sale/purchase/disposal) of cows or calves of she-buffaloes for slaughter, or knowing or believing that they will be slaughtered.

Empowers the competent authority or an authorized person to enter and inspect any premises where an offense under the Act is believed to have been committed or is likely to be committed. Occupiers of premises must provide access and answer questions.
Specifies penalties for contravening any provision of the Act, including imprisonment up to six months, a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act to be cognizable
main_sections.description: Declares all offenses under the Act to be cognizable.
Punishes abetment of or attempts to commit any offense under the Act with the same punishment as for the offense itself.

main_sections.section_title: Persons exercising powers under the Act deemed to be public servants
main_sections.description: States that all persons exercising powers under the Act are deemed to be public servants under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder.

Lists exemptions to the Act, including animals used for vaccine lymph, serum, experimental, or research purposes at recognized institutions, animals certified by a Veterinary Officer to be necessary for public health, animals suffering from contagious diseases dangerous to other animals, and animals suffering from incurable disease or injury (with specific provisions for Central Government/Ministry of Defence animals).
Allows the State Government to delegate its powers and functions under Section 3 to local authorities and powers under sub-section (1) of Section 6 to any officer of the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of institutions for taking care of cows or other animals
main_sections.description: Enables the State Government to establish or direct local authorities, societies, or associations to establish institutions for the care of cows or other animals. Rules may be made for their management and admission criteria. Fees may be levied for maintenance.

Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters related to competent authority powers, certificate forms and fees, exemptions, and management of care institutions.
Provides for the repeal of any conflicting laws.

important_rules: No person shall slaughter any cow or calf of a she-buffalo.
