No animal (other than a calf of she-buffalo) shall be slaughtered without a certificate from the competent authority, certifying that the animal is over twelve years old or permanently incapacitated, and not suffering from a disease making its meat unwholesome.
Slaughter of certified animals must occur only in specified places.
Transport of animals from within the State to outside for slaughter in contravention of the Act is prohibited.
Sale, purchase, or disposal of cows or calves of she-buffaloes for slaughter is prohibited.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months.
Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority appointed by the State Government, and any person authorized by the competent authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, requiring certificates for slaughter, and prosecution for violations. Offenses are cognizable.

rights: Right to obtain a certificate for slaughter of eligible animals.
Right to have actions taken by authorities reviewed by the State Government (under specific conditions).
duties: Duty not to slaughter cows or calves of she-buffaloes.
Duty to obtain a certificate before slaughtering other eligible animals.
Duty to comply with specified slaughter locations.
Duty not to transport animals for illicit slaughter.
Duty not to engage in the sale/purchase of cows or calves of she-buffaloes for slaughter.
Duty to allow entry and inspection by authorized personnel.
Duty to answer questions truthfully to competent authorities or authorized persons.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that the slaughter of animals occurs only in designated places.
Obligation to adhere to the conditions for obtaining a slaughter certificate.

key_procedures: Application for a certificate for slaughter of an animal (other than a calf of she-buffalo) to the competent authority.
Inspection and certification by the competent authority based on age or incapacitation, and absence of unwholesome disease.
Issuance or refusal of the certificate, with reasons to be recorded.
Appeal/Revision process available to the State Government regarding orders of the competent authority.
Slaughter only in a specified place after obtaining the certificate.
Inspection of premises by competent authority or authorized person.
Application of rules made by the State Government for management of institutions and fees.
administration: The State Government is the primary administrative body, with powers to appoint competent authorities, make rules, delegate powers, and oversee the establishment of animal care institutions.
important_notes: The Act was amended by Karnataka Acts 24 of 1966 and 26 of 1975.
Exemptions are provided for specific purposes like research, public health, and incurable diseases/injuries, under specified conditions and certifications by authorized Veterinary Officers.
The definition of 'cow' in the context of the Act may be broader than common understanding.
Orders passed by the competent authority and the State Government under Section 6 are final and not subject to challenge in any court.

title: THE KARNATAKA PRISONERS ACT, 1963
purpose: To make certain provisions relating to prisoners confined by order of a court in the State of Karnataka.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to prisoners confined by order of a court.

key_definitions.court: Includes any officer lawfully exercising civil, criminal or revenue jurisdiction.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prison: Includes any place declared by the State Government, by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its territorial extent to the whole of Karnataka, and allows for its commencement by notification of the State Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'court', 'notification', and 'prison'. It also specifies that references to prisons or imprisonment in sections 5 to 9 include reformatories and similar institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Officers in charge of prisons to detain persons duly committed to their custody.
main_sections.description: Mandates that officers in charge of prisons must receive and detain all persons lawfully committed to their custody by any court, until discharged or removed according to law.

main_sections.section_title: Officers in charge of prisons to return writs, etc., after execution or discharge.
main_sections.description: Requires officers in charge of prisons to return writs, warrants, or orders to the issuing court after their execution or discharge of the committed person, with an endorsement showing how it was executed or why discharge occurred.

main_sections.section_title: Power of officers in-charge of prisons to give effect to sentences of certain courts.
main_sections.description: Grants officers in charge of prisons the power to give effect to sentences, warrants, or orders for detention issued by any court or tribunal acting under the authority of the Central or State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Warrant of officer of such court to be sufficient authority.
main_sections.description: States that a warrant signed by an officer of a court or tribunal as referred to in Section 5 is sufficient authority for confinement or for sending a person for imprisonment for life.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where officer in-charge of prison doubts the legality of warrant sent to him for execution.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure when an officer in charge of a prison doubts the legality of a warrant or the competency of the issuing officer. The matter is to be referred to the State Government for orders, with the prisoner detained as specified in the warrant pending a decision.

Empowers the State Government to provide for the removal of prisoners (under sentence of death, imprisonment for life, in default of fine, or for security) to other prisons within the State. The Inspector-General of Prisons can also provide for such removals under the State Government's control.

main_sections.section_title: Lunatic prisoners how to be dealt with.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for dealing with prisoners found to be of unsound mind. The State Government can order their removal to a mental hospital for treatment, with provisions for their continued detention if necessary for safety after their sentence expires. It also incorporates provisions of the Indian Lunacy Act, 1912, and allows for removal to mental hospitals in other states by agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of places for confinement of persons under sentence of imprisonment for life and removal thereto.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to appoint specific places within Karnataka for persons sentenced to imprisonment for life and to order their removal, unless they are already serving a life sentence. It also allows for the appointment of such places in other states by agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Release on recognizance by order of High Court, of prisoner recommended for pardon.
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to permit a prisoner, for whom it has recommended a free pardon, to be at liberty on their own recognizance.

Repeals specific earlier Acts relating to prisoners in different areas of the integrated State of Karnataka, while providing for the application of the Karnataka General Clauses Act, 1899, to such repeal.

important_rules: Officers in charge of prisons must detain all persons duly committed to their custody by any court.
Warrants or orders for detention must be returned to the issuing court with an endorsement after execution or discharge.
Warrants of officers of specified courts or tribunals are sufficient authority for confinement.
If an officer in charge of a prison doubts the legality of a warrant, they must refer it to the State Government.
The State Government can provide for the removal of prisoners to other prisons within the State, including those under sentence of death, life imprisonment, or in default of fine.
Lunatic prisoners can be removed to mental hospitals for treatment, with provisions for their continued detention if necessary.
The State Government can appoint specific places for persons sentenced to life imprisonment and order their removal.
The High Court can release a prisoner recommended for pardon on their recognizance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and Officers in charge of prisons.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the detention, removal, and management of prisoners as per the Act's provisions and orders issued by the State Government.

rights: Right to be detained according to due course of law.
Right to be dealt with according to orders of the State Government in case of doubt regarding warrant legality.
Right to be transferred to a mental hospital for treatment if found to be of unsound mind.
Right to be discharged or remanded according to law after treatment for unsoundness of mind.
Right to be released on recognizance by the High Court if recommended for pardon.
duties: Duty of officers in charge of prisons to detain persons duly committed.
Duty of officers in charge of prisons to return writs and warrants.
Duty to comply with orders of the State Government regarding prisoner detention and removal.
Duty to treat lunatic prisoners appropriately.
Duty to remove prisoners to appointed places for life imprisonment.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the specific provisions of the Act concerning prisoner confinement and management.
Obligation to follow the directives issued by the State Government or authorized officers.

key_procedures: Procedure for detaining prisoners: Officer in charge must receive and detain persons committed by court.
Procedure for returning writs: After execution or discharge, return writ to court with endorsement.
Procedure for doubting warrant legality: Refer to State Government for orders, prisoner detained as per warrant pending decision.
Procedure for removal of prisoners: State Government or Inspector-General of Prisons may order removal to another prison.
Procedure for lunatic prisoners: State Government may order removal to a mental hospital; provisions for sound mind and continued detention.
Procedure for appointment of places for life imprisonment: State Government to appoint places and order removal.
administration: State Government and Inspector-General of Prisons.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and provides uniform law for the execution of punishments in the integrated areas of Karnataka, replacing earlier fragmented laws.
The Act came into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification, which is not available in the provided text.
Provisions relating to reformatories, Borstal institutions, and certified schools are included within the scope of 'prisons' for certain sections.

title: THE KARNATAKA PRISONS ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for a uniform law for the regulation of prisons in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the regulation and management of prisons and prisoners within the state. It covers various aspects including maintenance and officers of prisons, duties of officers, admission, removal and discharge of prisoners, discipline, food, clothing, bedding, employment, health, visitors, offenses in relation to prisons, prison offenses, temporary release, and miscellaneous provisions. However, it explicitly excludes places exclusively in police custody, places appointed under Section 541 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and subsidiary jails declared by the State Government.

key_definitions.civil prisoner: Any prisoner who is not a criminal prisoner.
key_definitions.convicted criminal prisoner: Any criminal prisoner under sentence of a Court or Court Martial, and includes a person detained in prison under the provisions of Chapter VIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
key_definitions.criminal prisoner: Any prisoner duly committed to custody under a writ, warrant or order of any Court or authority exercising criminal jurisdiction or by order of a Court Martial.
key_definitions.furlough system: A system of releasing prisoners in jails on furlough in accordance with the rules made under section 63.
key_definitions.history ticket: The ticket exhibiting such information as is required in respect of each prisoner by this Act or the rules made thereunder.
key_definitions.medical subordinate: An Assistant Surgeon appointed as medical subordinate under section 4.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prison: Any jail or place used permanently or temporarily under the general or special orders of the State Government for the detention of prisoners, and includes all lands and buildings appurtenant thereto, but does not include certain specified places.
key_definitions.prohibited article: An article the introduction or removal of which into or out of a prison is prohibited by any rule made under this Act.
key_definitions.remission system: The system of regulating the award of marks to, and the consequence of shortening of sentences of prisoners in jail in accordance with the rules for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Karnataka Prisons Act, 1963, extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'civil prisoner', 'convicted criminal prisoner', 'criminal prisoner', 'furlough system', 'history ticket', 'Inspector-General', 'medical subordinate', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'prison', 'prohibited article', and 'remission system'.
The State Government shall appoint an Inspector-General who shall, subject to the orders of the State Government, exercise the general control and superintendence of all prisons in the State.

For every prison, there shall be a Superintendent, a Medical Officer, a Medical Subordinate, a Jailer, and other officers as deemed necessary by the State Government. The State Government may allow the Jailer's office to be held by the Superintendent.
The State Government shall provide accommodation in prisons that are constructed and regulated to comply with the Act's requirements regarding the separation of prisoners.

If a prison is overcrowded, or due to an epidemic or other reasons, the Inspector-General can arrange for temporary accommodation for prisoners in temporary prisons, as directed by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Control and duties of officers of prisons.
main_sections.description: All prison officers must obey the Superintendent's directions. Subordinate officers to the Jailer must perform duties prescribed or imposed by the Jailer with the Superintendent's sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Officers not to have business dealings with prisoners.
main_sections.description: No prison officer or person acting for them can sell, let, or benefit from selling or letting any article to a prisoner, nor have any direct or indirect business dealings with a prisoner.

main_sections.section_title: Officers not to be interested in prison contracts.
main_sections.description: No prison officer or person acting for them can have any interest in contracts for supplying articles to the prison or benefit from the sale or purchase of articles on behalf of the prison or belonging to a prisoner.

The Superintendent manages the prison in all matters of welfare, discipline, labour, expenditure, punishment, and control, subject to the Inspector-General's orders. For prisons other than Central Prisons, the Superintendent must also obey orders from the District Magistrate, reporting them to the Inspector-General, who must ratify them.

main_sections.section_title: Records to be kept by Superintendent.
main_sections.description: The Superintendent must maintain records including a prisoner admission register, release schedule, punishment book, visitors' book, record of prisoners' effects, and other prescribed records.
The Medical Officer is in charge of the sanitary and health administration of the prison, subject to the Superintendent's control, and performs prescribed duties.

main_sections.section_title: Medical Officer to report in certain cases.
main_sections.description: If the Medical Officer believes a prisoner's mind is being injuriously affected by discipline or treatment, they must report it in writing to the Superintendent, who forwards it with his orders to the Inspector-General.

main_sections.section_title: Report on the death of prisoner.
main_sections.description: On a prisoner's death, the Medical Officer must record particulars such as the day of illness, labour, diet, and other relevant information.

main_sections.section_title: Prisoners to be examined on admission.
main_sections.description: Prisoners must be examined upon admission to the prison.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited articles, into or from prisons and communication with prisoners.
main_sections.description: This section outlines penalties for introducing or removing prohibited articles from prisons, or communicating with prisoners in contravention of the Act or rules.
This section defines what constitutes a 'prison offence'.
This section details the punishments that can be awarded for prison offences listed in section 45.

main_sections.section_title: Power to release certain prisoners temporarily.
main_sections.description: This section grants the power to release certain prisoners temporarily.
This section addresses the release of prisoners on parole.
This section empowers the State Government to make rules for the regulation of prisons.
This section deals with the repeal of previous enactments and any savings arising from them.

important_rules: Officers of prisons shall obey the directions of the Superintendent.
No officer of a prison shall have any business dealings, directly or indirectly, with any prisoner.
No officer of a prison shall have any interest, direct or indirect, in any contract for the supply of any article to the prison.
Prisoners must be examined upon admission.
The introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prisons, and communication with prisoners, is subject to penalties.

penalties: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prisons and for communication with prisoners (Section 42).
Penalty for failure to surrender after temporary release or parole (Section 58).
Punishments for prison offences as defined and detailed in Sections 45, 46, 47, and 48.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and its appointed authorities, including the Inspector-General of Prisons, Superintendents, and Jailers, are responsible for the enforcement of the Act. Courts also play a role in sentencing and dealing with offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the appointment of officials, the establishment of prison regulations, the imposition of punishments for prison offences, the power to arrest for certain offences, and the administrative oversight by the Inspector-General and the State Government. Rules made under the Act are also crucial for enforcement.

rights: Prisoners have rights to be housed in properly constructed and regulated accommodation.
Prisoners may have rights related to their health and medical care.
Prisoners might have rights concerning their food, clothing, and bedding as prescribed.
Certain prisoners have the right to temporary release or parole under specific conditions.
duties: Officers of prisons have a duty to obey the Superintendent and perform their prescribed duties.
Superintendents have duties to manage the prison, maintain records, and ensure discipline.
Medical Officers have duties related to the health and sanitary administration of the prison.
Prisoners have a duty to abide by prison discipline and rules.
Prisoners released temporarily or on parole have a duty to surrender themselves at the expiry of their period.
obligations: The State Government has an obligation to provide accommodation for prisoners.
The State Government has an obligation to appoint an Inspector-General and other prison officers.
Prison officers have an obligation not to engage in business dealings with prisoners or be interested in prison contracts.
Prisoners are obligated to surrender themselves upon the expiry of their temporary release or parole period.

key_procedures: Admission of prisoners: Prisoners are examined upon admission (Section 23).
Reporting of prisoner's death: Medical Officer records details of a prisoner's death (Section 14).
Reporting of prisoner's mental health issues: Medical Officer reports to the Superintendent if a prisoner's mental state is affected (Section 13).
Management of prison offenses: Procedures for dealing with and punishing prison offences, including medical certification for fitness for punishment (Sections 45-54).
Temporary release and parole: Procedures for releasing prisoners temporarily or on parole (Sections 55-58).
Rule-making and notification: The State Government can make rules under Section 63, and rules and notifications are to be laid before the State Legislature (Section 64).
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government of Karnataka, with the Inspector-General of Prisons having general control and superintendence of all prisons. Superintendents manage individual prisons, and other officers assist in the administration.
important_notes: The Act aims to unify prison laws previously in force in different regions of Karnataka.
The definition of 'prison' excludes certain types of confinement facilities, such as those exclusively for police custody or subsidiary jails.
The Act was amended by Act 13 of 1965 to address the separation of judicial and executive functions.

title: THE KARNATAKA PRIVATE NURSING HOMES (REGULATION) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the regulation and control of private nursing homes in the State, ensuring maintenance of standards, proper treatment, and fair charges for patients.
scope: This Act applies to all private nursing homes operating within the State of Karnataka. It covers their establishment, running, maintenance, staffing, facilities, and fees charged for medical treatment.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date specified in sub-section (2) of section 1, which is November 4, 1976.
key_definitions.competent_authority: Any person, persons, or authority appointed by the State Government to perform the functions of the competent authority under this Act. Different authorities can be appointed for different functions.
key_definitions.licence: A licence granted under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.manager: The person, by whatever name or designation called, who is in charge of, or is entrusted with, the running of a private nursing home.
key_definitions.medical_treatment: Treatment in modern medicine or in any other system of medicine like Ayurvedic, Unani, Homeopathic, and Naturopathic.
key_definitions.modern_medicine: Western methods of allopathic medicine, obstetrics, and surgery.
key_definitions.nursing_home: A hospital, clinic, or any other place where human diseases are given preventive and/or curative medical treatment.
key_definitions.private_nursing_home: A nursing home that is not owned or sponsored by the State or the Central Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Private Nursing Homes (Regulation) Act, 1976, and that it is deemed to have come into force on November 4, 1976.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'competent authority', 'licence', 'manager', 'medical treatment', 'modern medicine', 'nursing home', and 'private nursing home'.

main_sections.section_title: Private Nursing Home to be licensed
main_sections.description: Mandates that no private nursing home can be established, run, or maintained in the State without a licence. Existing nursing homes were required to apply for a licence within a specified period (initially two months, later extended to eight months).
Requires every private nursing home to conform to prescribed standards regarding operation theatres, nursing and other staff (including qualifications), facilities for patients, and maintenance.

Prohibits private nursing homes from charging fees for medical treatment in excess of prescribed scales. Prescribed fees are to consider the nature of the disease, treatment, and other relevant factors.

Details the process for applying for a licence to establish, run, maintain, or continue running a private nursing home, requiring an application to the competent authority in the prescribed form and with the prescribed fee.

Outlines the procedure for the competent authority to grant or refuse a licence after an enquiry, requiring reasons for refusal to be provided. It also specifies a deemed refusal if no communication is issued within ninety days.

main_sections.section_title: Factors to be taken into account in disposing of applications
main_sections.description: Lists the factors the competent authority must consider when disposing of licence applications, including the suitability and hygiene of the premises, adequacy of qualified staff, and other prescribed factors.

Empowers the competent authority to inspect private nursing homes to ensure compliance with the Act and licence conditions. If defects are found, the authority can direct the manager to remedy them within a specified time.

States that if a private nursing home defaults in observing licence conditions, fails to comply with directions, or contravenes the Act, the competent authority may revoke the licence after giving the concerned parties an opportunity to be heard.
Provides for appeals against refusal of a licence or any other order made under the Act to a prescribed appellate authority within thirty days. The appellate authority's order is final.
Specifies that contravening any provision of the Act or licence conditions can lead to imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to five thousand rupees upon conviction.
States that no offence under the Act can be taken cognizance of except on a complaint preferred by the competent authority.
Indemnifies the State Government and its officers against suits or legal proceedings for anything done in good faith under this Act.
Authorizes the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing standards, application forms, licence conditions, fees, and other relevant matters.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be placed before the State Legislature
main_sections.description: Mandates that all rules made under the Act must be laid before each House of the State Legislature for a specified period, allowing for modifications or annulment.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No. 25 of 1976
main_sections.description: Repeals the Karnataka Private Nursing Homes (Regulation) Ordinance, 1976, and states that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the Act, and applications made under the Ordinance are treated as applications under the Act.

important_rules: No private nursing home shall be established, run, or maintained without a licence from the competent authority.
All private nursing homes must conform to prescribed standards regarding facilities, staff, and hygiene.
Fees charged for medical treatment must not exceed the prescribed scales.
Existing private nursing homes must apply for a licence within the stipulated period (initially two months, later extended to eight months).
Managers of private nursing homes must comply with directions issued by the competent authority following inspections.
Contravention of the Act or licence conditions can lead to penalties including imprisonment and/or fine.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to six months.
Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
Revocation of the licence for defaults or contraventions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Competent Authority appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, issuing directions for remedial actions, processing licence applications, revoking licences for defaults, and initiating legal proceedings for contraventions.

rights: Right to prefer an appeal to the prescribed appellate authority against refusal of licence or other orders.
Right to be given an opportunity of making representations before licence revocation.
duties: Duty of private nursing homes to obtain and comply with the terms of a licence.
Duty to conform to prescribed standards.
Duty to charge fees within prescribed scales.
Duty of the manager to comply with directions issued by the competent authority after inspections.
obligations: Establishment, running, or maintenance of a private nursing home requires a licence.
Existing nursing homes have an obligation to apply for a licence within the specified period.
Compliance with all provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Application for a licence: A person desiring to establish or run a private nursing home must apply to the competent authority in the prescribed form and fee.

Disposal of application: The competent authority will conduct an enquiry and grant or refuse the licence, providing reasons for refusal. A deemed refusal occurs if no order is communicated within 90 days.
Inspection and rectification: The competent authority can inspect nursing homes and direct the manager to remedy any defects found within a specified time.
Revocation of licence: The competent authority can revoke a licence for non-compliance or contraventions, after giving the concerned parties an opportunity to respond.
Appeals: A person aggrieved by an order can prefer an appeal to the prescribed appellate authority within 30 days.
administration: The State Government, through the 'competent authority' it appoints.
important_notes: The Act was amended by Act 9 of 1977, which extended the time limit for existing nursing homes to apply for a licence from two months to eight months.
Anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance (Karnataka Ordinance No. 25 of 1976) is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
The Act provides indemnity to the State Government and its officers for actions taken in good faith.

title: The Karnataka Prohibition Act, 1961
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to the promotion and enforcement of and carrying out the policy of prohibition of consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and drugs, and to provide for certain other purposes.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It initially came into force in areas where certain other Prohibition Acts were in force and could be extended to other areas by notification by the State Government. Provisions can also cease to be in force in specified areas, with the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, then extending to those areas.

key_definitions.alcohol: Ethyl alcohol of any strength and purity having the chemical composition C2H5CH:
key_definitions.authorisation: An authorisation granted for the use, or for manufacture for use, of liquor for sacramental purposes.
key_definitions.bottling: The transfer of any article from a cask or other vessel to a bottle, jar, flask, pot or similar receptacle for the purpose of sale, whether any process of manufacture be employed or not; and includes rebottling.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Prohibition Commissioner appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.committee: Any of the committees appointed by the State Government under section 8.
key_definitions.country liquor: Includes all liquor produced or manufactured in India.
key_definitions.cultivation: Includes the tending or protecting of a plant and does not necessarily imply raising it from seed.
key_definitions.denatured: Subjected to a process prescribed for the purpose of rendering it unfit for human consumption as a beverage.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and commencement provisions, including different dates for different sections and areas.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'alcohol', 'authorisation', 'bottling', 'Commissioner', 'Committee', 'country liquor', 'cultivation', and 'denatured'.
Provides for the appointment of a Prohibition Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of the manufacture of, traffic in and consumption of liquors and intoxicating drugs.
main_sections.description: Establishes the core prohibition on manufacturing, selling, and consuming liquors and intoxicating drugs.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for illegal import, etc., of intoxicants or hemp.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for illegal import, transport, or possession of intoxicants or hemp.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable
main_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable and non-bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings provisions.

important_rules: Prohibition of manufacture, traffic in, and consumption of liquors and intoxicating drugs (Section 12).
Prohibition of advertisements relating to intoxicants (Section 15).
Licensing and regulation for possession of denatured spirit, rectified spirit, and alcohol for industrial or medicinal purposes (Section 22).
Issuance of various permits for specific purposes like medicinal, emergency, and tourist use (Sections 32, 33, 37).
Rules regarding excise duties, their levy, exemption, remission, and refund (Chapter V).
Specific penalties for various offences including illegal import, manufacture, sale, consumption, and related activities (Chapter VI).

penalties: Penalty for illegal import, transport, sale, or possession of intoxicants or hemp.
Penalty for alteration or attempt to alter denatured spirit.
Penalty for illegal cultivation and collection of hemp.
Penalty for printing or publishing advertisements relating to intoxicants.
Penalty for inciting or encouraging certain acts related to intoxicants.
Penalty for being drunk and for disorderly behaviour.
Penalties for various contraventions of licence, permit, or other provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prohibition Commissioner, Deputy Commissioners, subordinate officers, and other officers invested with powers under the Act by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, inspection, search, seizure, arrest, investigation, and prosecution, as well as through licensing and permit systems. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable. The Act also outlines special rules of evidence and procedure for trails.

rights: Right to appeal and revision against orders passed under the Act (Chapter IX).
Right to compensation or refund for cancellation or suspension of licence is generally not entitled (Section 46).
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, including prohibitions and licensing requirements.
Duty of landlords and others to give information about offences (Section 113).
Duty of persons admitted on bail to appear before a Prohibition Officer if required (Section 120).
obligations: Obligation to obtain necessary licences and permits for activities related to intoxicants.
Obligation to not possess, manufacture, sell, or consume intoxicants except as permitted by the Act.
Obligation to not publish or circulate advertisements related to intoxicants.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining licences and permits for various purposes related to intoxicants, including specific applications for medicinal, industrial, sacramental, and other uses.
Procedure for confiscation of intoxicants, implements, and things used in the commission of offences, including rights of bona fide owners and procedures for sale or destruction (Sections 94-97).
Procedure for search, seizure, and arrest by officers, including powers of entry, inspection, and requiring production of documents (Chapter VIII).
Procedure for compounding of offences (Section 89).
Procedure for demanding security for abstaining from commission of certain offences or for good behaviour (Sections 91-92).
administration: The Act is administered by the Prohibition Commissioner, with the State Government having overall powers to make rules and regulations, and to notify exemptions and the commencement of provisions.
important_notes: The Act consolidates previous Prohibition Acts in force in different areas of Karnataka to ensure uniform implementation.
The State Government has the power to exclude areas from the operation of the Act and extend the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965, in their place.
The Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, and Section 562 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, do not apply to persons convicted under this Act (Section 90).
The Act does not apply to import or export across a customs frontier (Section 127).

title: THE KARNATAKA PROHIBITION OF BEGGARY ACT, 1975
purpose: To prohibit persons from resorting to begging and to provide for the detention, training and employment of beggars, for the custody, trial and punishment of beggar offenders and for the relief and rehabilitation of such persons in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It came into force in certain areas on 1.4.1976 and in the rest of the areas on 6.11.1997. The Act covers persons who resort to begging.

key_definitions.alms: Anything given gratuitously to a beggar, such as money, cooked or un-cooked food, grains or clothing, or any other thing of value.
key_definitions.beggar: Any person other than a child who solicits or receives alms in a public place, enters private premises for soliciting alms, exposes sores/wounds for alms, wanders in public with no visible means of subsistence making it likely they exist by soliciting alms, or allows themselves to be used as an exhibit for soliciting alms. Exceptions include licensed religious mendicants, those collecting alms for religious vows without causing nuisance, those permitted by the Central Relief Committee for public institutions or objects, and students collecting for studies.
key_definitions.child: A boy who has not attained the age of sixteen years, or a girl who has not attained the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.institution: Includes a receiving centre, a relief centre, colony, settlement area or any other institution declared to be such by the Government.
key_definitions.public place: Any place intended for the use of or accessible to the public and includes any public conveyance.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and commencement provisions, allowing for different dates for different areas and requiring suitable relief facilities.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'alms', 'beggar', 'child', 'Central Relief Committee', 'Government', 'institution', 'local area', 'local committee', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'public place', 'receiving centre', and 'Relief centre'.
Makes begging illegal in areas where the Act is in force.

Provides for the constitution of a Central Relief Committee by the Government, its composition (official and non-official members), appointment of Chairman and Secretary, term of office, filling of vacancies, remuneration for non-official members, and meeting frequency. The Committee has supervision, direction, and control over relief administration.

Outlines the procedure for arresting persons contravening Section 3 (begging), informing them of the grounds for arrest, and removing them to a receiving centre. It details the enquiry by the receiving centre's officer-in-charge, potential release with or without surety, and production before a Magistrate within 24 hours. It also specifies the Magistrate's role in holding an enquiry and releasing the person on furnishing a bond.

main_sections.section_title: Magistrate to send beggar to the relief centre
main_sections.description: Empowers the Magistrate to send a beggar to a relief centre. Provisions amended in 2003 specify that the period of detention may extend to three years with a minimum of one year, replacing the previous twelve months.

main_sections.section_title: Infirm, disabled and decrepit beggars and persons suffering from any incurable disease to be arrested and sent to receiving centres
main_sections.description: Details the process for dealing with infirm, disabled, decrepit beggars, and those with incurable diseases, involving arrest and sending them to receiving centres. Similar to Section 12, amendments in 2003 extend the detention period to a maximum of three years with a minimum of one year.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal of a beggar to go to an institution or to a Magistrate punishable with imprisonment or fine or both
main_sections.description: Specifies that refusal by a beggar to go to an institution or comply with a Magistrate's order is punishable by imprisonment, fine, or both.

important_rules: No person shall beg in the areas where this Act is in force (Section 3).
Begging is prohibited by any person other than a child. Children (boys under 16, girls under 18) are treated differently.
Persons found begging are to be arrested and taken to a receiving centre for enquiry. If not released, they are produced before a Magistrate.
Magistrates can release beggars on furnishing a bond not to beg again. For repeated offenders or specific categories, detention in a relief centre is mandated.
Infirm, disabled, decrepit beggars, and those with incurable diseases are to be sent to receiving centres for further management.

Religious mendicants licensed by the Central Relief Committee, those collecting alms for religious vows without nuisance, those permitted by the Committee for public institutions, and students collecting for studies are not considered beggars under the Act.
Discipline, including manual labour and hard labour, can be enforced in institutions (Section 9(2) explanation).

penalties: Imprisonment or fine or both for abetting begging (Section 17).
Imprisonment or fine or both for refusing to go to an institution or to a Magistrate (Section 18).
Fines (general provision - Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers or other officers authorized by the Government, and the Central Relief Committee with its subordinate committees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, enquiry, production before Magistrates, detention in receiving and relief centres, enforcement of discipline, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds for arrest (Section 11(1)).
Right to be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (Section 11(3)).
Right to be released on furnishing a bond if the Magistrate is satisfied that the person will not commit the offence of begging again (Section 11(4)).
Right to be discharged from an institution on completion of the period of detention or on permission (Section 15).
Right to temporary release and unconditional release under prescribed conditions (Sections 20, 21).
duties: Duty of arrested persons to cooperate with the arrest and enquiry process.
Duty of officers to inform arrested persons of grounds of arrest and produce them before the appropriate authority.
Duty of the Central Relief Committee to provide for proper management of institutions and care of inmates.
Duty of inmates in institutions to adhere to prescribed rules of discipline.
obligations: Obligation of every person to refrain from begging in the notified areas (Section 3).
Obligation to furnish a bond when released by a Magistrate after committing the offence of begging (Section 11(4), 11(5)).
Obligation for beggars sent to relief centres to undergo detention, training, and rehabilitation.
Obligation for non-official members of the Central Relief Committee to attend meetings and inform of absence.

key_procedures: Arrest of persons found begging by authorized officers.
Enquiry by the officer-in-charge of a receiving centre.
Production of arrested persons before a Magistrate within 24 hours.
Magistrate's enquiry and potential release on bond or detention in a relief centre.
Detention, training, and rehabilitation of beggars in relief centres.
Transfer of beggars between institutions within the state and to other states.
Release of beggars on discharge, permission, or unconditionally.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, the Central Relief Committee, and Local Committees. Specific departments like the Social Welfare and Labour Department are involved.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1982 to enhance the period of detention from six months to one year.
Amendments in 1988 provided powers to the Chairman of the Central Relief Committee for inter-institutional and inter-state transfers of beggars.

Amendments in 2003 significantly increased the period of detention in relief centres to a minimum of one year and a maximum of three years for certain categories of beggars, and also specified bond amounts for release.

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC LIBRARIES ACT, 1965
purpose: To provide for the establishment and maintenance of public libraries and the organization of a comprehensive rural and urban library service in the State of Karnataka, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to the establishment, maintenance, and organization of public libraries and library services within the state.

key_definitions.academic_library: A library maintained by a university, college, school, or research institution.
key_definitions.aided_library: A library declared by the Director of Public Libraries to be eligible for aid from the Government in accordance with the rules.
key_definitions.book: Includes every volume, part or division of a volume, and pamphlet, in any language; every sheet of music, map, chart or plan separately printed or lithographed; and newspapers, periodicals and other such materials.
key_definitions.chief_librarian: The Librarian appointed to be in charge of a City Central Library or a District Central Library and other Libraries and the library service under the control of a City Library Authority or a District Library Authority.
key_definitions.city_library_authority: A Library Authority constituted for a city or other urban area under sections 16 and 17.
key_definitions.state_owned_library: A library maintained by a Department of the State Government, the State Legislature, the High Court or any other court or any authority of the State.
key_definitions.district_library_authority: A Library Authority constituted for a district under sections 16 and 18.
key_definitions.local_library_authority: A City Library Authority or a District Library Authority.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.outlier_library: Any library other than a public library.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public_library: A library established or maintained by a Local Library Authority, including branches and delivery stations; a library established or maintained by the State Government and declared open to the public; a library established or maintained by any local authority and declared open to the public; a library declared to be eligible for aid and receiving aid from the State Government; and any other library notified by the State Government as a public library.
key_definitions.state_central_library: The library declared to be the State Central Library under Chapter VI.
key_definitions.director_of_public_libraries: The Director of Public Libraries appointed under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Public Libraries Act, 1965, states its extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'academic library', 'aided library', 'book', 'chief librarian', 'city library authority', 'state-owned library', 'district', 'district library authority', 'library cess', 'local library authority', 'notification', 'outlier library', 'prescribed', 'public library', 'state central library', 'director of public libraries', 'state library authority', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of the State Library Authority
main_sections.description: Establishes the State Library Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It outlines its composition, including ex-officio members like the Minister in charge of Public Libraries, elected members from the Legislative Assembly and Council, representatives from universities and the Karnataka Library Association, and nominated experts.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the State Library Authority
main_sections.description: Details the functions of the State Library Authority, which include advising the State Government on matters related to the Act, managing the State Central Library, and exercising other powers and duties conferred by the Act or prescribed by rules.
Provides for the constitution of Local Library Authorities for cities and districts.
Introduces the concept of a library cess, which is a levy to fund library services.
Specifies offences and the penalties associated with them under the Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding the nomination of members to the State Library Authority in case of default in election.
Rules related to the term of office, vacancies, and disqualifications for members of the State Library Authority and Local Library Authorities.
Rules concerning the meetings and procedures of the State Library Authority and Local Library Authorities.
Rules for the levy and collection of Library Cess.
Rules for the management of City and District Library Funds and the State Library Fund.
Rules for the submission of reports, returns, and inspection of libraries.
Rules for the creation and management of public libraries, including the State Central Library and libraries under Local Library Authorities.

penalties: Penalties for offences committed under the Act, as detailed in Section 43.
Liability of members for loss, waste, or misapplication of funds or property, as per Section 45.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, the State Library Authority, and the Local Library Authorities, with the Director of Public Libraries playing a key role.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including penalties for offences, powers of control by the Government over Local Library Authorities, and the enforcement of rules and bye-laws made under the Act.

rights: Right to access public libraries and library services as established and maintained under the Act.
Right to receive aid from the Government for eligible libraries (aided libraries).
duties: Duty of the State Library Authority to advise the State Government on library matters and manage the State Central Library.
Duty of Local Library Authorities to establish and maintain public libraries and organize library services within their jurisdiction.
Duty to levy and collect library cess.
Duty of members and employees of Library Authorities to be public servants.
obligations: Obligations of universities, colleges, schools, and research institutions to maintain academic libraries.
Obligations of the State Government to ensure the establishment and maintenance of a comprehensive library service.
Obligations related to the vesting of the Bangalore Public Library in the State Library Authority.
Obligations related to the transfer of certain libraries.

key_procedures: Procedure for the constitution and composition of the State Library Authority, including election and nomination of members.
Procedure for the constitution and composition of Local Library Authorities (City and District).
Procedure for the levy and collection of Library Cess.
Procedure for the establishment and management of City and District Library Funds and the State Library Fund.
Procedure for the submission of annual reports and returns by libraries.
Procedure for the inspection of libraries.
Procedure for making rules and bye-laws under the Act.
Procedure for handling offences and penalties.
Procedure for the removal of difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Procedure for the transfer of certain libraries.
Procedure for the amendment of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867, in its application to Karnataka.
administration: The State Government, the State Library Authority, the Department of Public Libraries, and the Local Library Authorities are responsible for the administration of this Act. The Director of Public Libraries plays a significant administrative role.
important_notes: The Act was a consolidation effort to bring uniformity to public library law in Karnataka, replacing existing acts in different regions of the state.

Amendments have been made over time to adjust the ex-officio President of the State Library Authority, the percentage of cess collection for local authorities, the designation of the head of the Department of Libraries, and the grant percentage from land revenue for District Library Authorities.
The Act provides for the establishment of a State Central Library, by vesting the Bangalore Public Library in the State Library Authority.

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC MONEYS (RECOVERY OF DUES) ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for the speedy recovery of certain classes of dues, particularly those related to financial assistance provided by the State Government, Corporations, Government Companies, and banking companies under state-sponsored or socially desirable schemes, as arrears of land revenue.
scope: This Act applies to dues arising from financial assistance provided by the State Government, the Corporation (Karnataka State Financial Corporation), Government Companies, and banking companies. It covers loans, advances, grants, credit, and hire-purchase of goods given under State-sponsored schemes or socially desirable schemes. The recovery process is to be conducted within Karnataka.

key_definitions.banking_company: Includes various entities like those defined in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, corresponding new banks, Regional Rural Banks, Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation, and Agricultural Finance Corporation Limited.
key_definitions.corporation: Refers to the Karnataka State Financial Corporation and any other corporation owned or controlled by the Central or State Government that the State Government may specify by notification.
key_definitions.financial_assistance: Encompasses financial aid for establishing, expanding, modernizing, renovating, or running industrial undertakings; vocational training; development of agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, or agro-industry; any other planned development; or relief against distress.
key_definitions.government_company: As defined in Section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.industrial_concern: Has the meaning assigned in the State Financial Corporation Act, 1951.
key_definitions.industrial_undertaking: Includes undertakings for manufacturing, preservation, storage, or processing of goods, mining, hotel industry, transport of passengers or goods, generation or distribution of electricity or other power, or development of land as an industrial estate.
key_definitions.state_sponsored_scheme: A scheme sponsored by the State Government where the government advances money to a banking company or Government company for disbursing loans/grants/credit or for sale of goods on credit/hire purchase, or guarantees such repayment.
key_definitions.socially_desirable_scheme: A scheme notified by the State Government under which a banking company advances money to any person by way of loan.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1979. Section 6 came into force immediately, while other sections are deemed to have come into force on June 15, 1976.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'banking company', 'Corporation', 'financial assistance', 'Government company', 'industrial concern', 'Industrial undertaking', 'person', 'State sponsored scheme', and 'socially desirable scheme'.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of certain dues as arrears of land revenue
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for recovering specific dues as arrears of land revenue. This applies to defaults in payment of loans, grants, or credit under agreements related to financial assistance from the State Government or Corporation, or under State-sponsored schemes by banking companies or Government companies. It also covers defaults in compliance with agreement terms. It specifies the authorities who can send a certificate for recovery and the process the Deputy Commissioner must follow.

Clarifies that the Act does not affect existing interests in property created by mortgage, charge, pledge, or encumbrance. It also preserves rights and remedies against persons other than those referred to in Section 3. It details the procedure for recovering dues when the property is subject to a pledge, hypothecation, mortgage, or charge, prioritizing the sale of pledged goods or immovable property.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, subject to previous publication and laying before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

Repeals the Karnataka Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1976. It also includes a validation clause, making valid anything done or action taken under the repealed Act, notwithstanding any court judgment or order.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any person who defaults in payment of a loan, advance, grant, or fails to comply with the terms of an agreement related to financial assistance under a State-sponsored scheme or direct recovery, shall be subject to recovery as arrears of land revenue.

Rule 2: The Managing Director of a Corporation or Government Company, or the local agent of a banking company, or an authorized officer of the State Government, can issue a certificate to the Deputy Commissioner for recovery of outstanding dues.
Rule 3: The Deputy Commissioner, upon receiving a certificate, must proceed to recover the specified amount as an arrear of land revenue.

Rule 4: For loans given under a socially desirable scheme, a banking company can apply to a prescribed officer for a certificate of the sum due, after which the certificate becomes final and is sent to the Deputy Commissioner for recovery as arrears of land revenue.

Rule 5: No suit for recovery of dues shall lie in a civil court if proceedings are pending before the Deputy Commissioner, but periods of such bar shall be excluded from the limitation period for court recovery.

Rule 6: In cases of pledge or hypothecation of goods, the goods must first be sold. If proceeds are insufficient, the balance is recovered as arrears of land revenue. The State Government may direct recovery as arrears before or at the same time as the sale of goods in certain circumstances.

Rule 7: In cases of mortgage, charge, or encumbrance on immovable property, the property must first be sold for recovery as arrears of land revenue. Other proceedings can only be taken if the Deputy Commissioner certifies no prospect of full realization within a reasonable time.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner, authorized officers of the State Government, Managing Directors of Corporations/Government Companies, and local agents of banking companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue, which involves the powers and procedures associated with land revenue collection, including seizure and sale of property.

rights: The right of the State Government, Corporation, Government Company, or banking company to recover specified dues as arrears of land revenue.
The right to recover interest at the agreed rate and costs of proceedings.
The right to proceed for recovery of the balance if the sale of pledged goods is insufficient.
The right to take further proceedings if recovery from immovable property as arrears of land revenue is not fully realized within a reasonable time.
duties: The duty of the Deputy Commissioner to proceed with the recovery upon receiving a certificate.
The duty to first sell pledged goods or encumbered immovable property.
The duty to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the person from whom dues are to be recovered (in the case of socially desirable schemes).
obligations: Obligation to pay loans, advances, grants, or credit as per agreement terms.
Obligation to refund grants or portions thereof as per conditions.
Obligation to comply with the terms of agreements for financial assistance or goods sold on credit/hire purchase.

key_procedures: Initiation of Recovery: An authorized officer (State Govt.), Managing Director (Corporation/Govt. Co.), or local agent (Banking Co.) sends a certificate to the Deputy Commissioner specifying the sum due, including costs and future interest, for recovery as arrears of land revenue.
Deputy Commissioner's Action: Upon receiving the certificate, the Deputy Commissioner proceeds to recover the amount as arrears of land revenue.

Recovery for Socially Desirable Schemes: A banking company applies to a prescribed officer with a statement of accounts. The officer may conduct an enquiry, give a hearing, and grant a certificate. This certificate is then sent to the Deputy Commissioner for recovery as arrears of land revenue.

Handling of Encumbered Property: For pledged/hypothecated goods, the goods are sold first. For mortgaged/charged/encumbered immovable property, it is sold first as an arrear of land revenue. Further proceedings are taken only if the Deputy Commissioner certifies lack of prospects for full recovery.
administration: The State Government, through its authorized officers and the Deputy Commissioner, administers the recovery process. The State Legislature is also involved in the rule-making process.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect, with Section 6 coming into force immediately and other sections deemed to have come into force on June 15, 1976.
The Act validates actions taken under the repealed Karnataka Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1976.
Interest rates for recovery are to be at the agreed rate within the limits prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India and other relevant institutions.
The scope of 'banking company' is broad, including various financial institutions.
The Act aims to provide a faster mechanism than traditional civil suits for recovery of specified dues.

title: THE KARNATAKA PUBLIC PREMISES (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) ACT, 1974
purpose: To provide a speedy remedy for the eviction of unauthorised occupants from public premises and for the recovery of rent or damages in respect thereof.
scope: The Act applies to public premises in the State of Karnataka. Public premises are defined to include premises belonging to or taken on lease by the State Government, local authorities, companies in which the State Government has a prescribed share, and various other entities as amended over time (e.g., Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, Universities, Improvement Boards, Zilla Paris hads, Mandal Panchayats, Bangalore Development Authority, Urban Development Authorities, Market Committees, Wakf Institutions, and certain charitable endowments and Hindu religious institutions).

key_definitions.public_premises: Premises of any of the descriptions specified in the First Schedule. This definition has been expanded over time to include premises of various government-controlled entities, corporations, universities, and religious/charitable institutions.
key_definitions.unauthorised_occupant: A person who is in possession of any public premises, but who has not been duly authorised to occupy the same, and includes any person who continues to occupy any public premises after the expiry or termination of his authorisation to occupy the same.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (State of Karnataka), and the date from which it comes into force.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'public premises' and 'unauthorised occupant'.
Empowers the State Government to appoint officers (initially not below Class I, later amended to include Group 'B' Officers) as competent officers for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of notice to show cause against order of eviction.
main_sections.description: Mandates that a notice must be issued to any unauthorised occupant requiring them to show cause why an order of eviction should not be made against them.
Details the procedure for evicting unauthorised occupants after issuing a show cause notice and considering any cause shown.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of property left on public premises by unauthorised occupants.
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of the competent officer to deal with property left behind by unauthorised occupants after eviction.

main_sections.section_title: Power to recover rent or damages in respect of public premises as arrears of land revenue.
main_sections.description: Grants the competent officer the power to recover rent or damages for unauthorised occupation as arrears of land revenue.
Confers various powers on competent officers, including entering premises, inspecting, and summoning persons.
Provides for an appeal against orders passed by the competent officer to a designated appellate authority.
Defines offences related to obstructing officers or contravening the Act and prescribes penalties.
Ousts the jurisdiction of civil courts from entertaining any suit or proceeding in respect of the eviction of persons from public premises or recovery of arrears of rent or damages.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals the previous Mysore Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1961, and makes provisions for savings.

important_rules: A show cause notice must be issued before an eviction order is passed (Section 4).
The eviction order must be in writing and specify the grounds (Section 5).
Appeals against eviction orders must be filed within a prescribed time limit (Section 10).
Civil courts are barred from entertaining suits related to eviction or recovery of damages/rent from public premises (Section 16).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both, for obstructing an officer or contravening the Act (Section 12).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Officers appointed by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of show cause notices, eviction orders, recovery of rent/damages as arrears of land revenue, and by imposing penalties for non-compliance.

rights: The right to be issued a notice to show cause before eviction.
The right to appeal against an eviction order.
The right to present a defense against eviction proceedings.
duties: The duty of unauthorised occupants to vacate public premises upon receiving a valid eviction order.
The duty to pay rent or damages for unauthorised occupation.
The duty to cooperate with competent officers during inspections and inquiries.
obligations: Obligation to cease unauthorized occupation upon determination of authorization.
Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Issuance of a show cause notice to the unauthorised occupant, stating the grounds for eviction.
Consideration of any cause shown by the occupant in response to the notice.
If no sufficient cause is shown, passing of a written order of eviction.
Execution of the eviction order by the competent officer.
Filing of an appeal against the eviction order to the appellate authority within the prescribed time.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government of Karnataka, which appoints competent officers and makes rules for its implementation. Various departments may be involved depending on the nature of the public premises.
important_notes: The Act has been amended multiple times to extend its scope to various entities and to address practical difficulties.
The Act aims to provide a faster alternative to traditional civil court proceedings for eviction.
The Act's validity has been challenged in courts in the past, leading to amendments to ensure constitutional compliance.

title: The Karnataka Public Service Commission (Conduct of Business and Additional Functions) Act, 1959
purpose: To prescribe the procedure to be followed by the Karnataka Public Service Commission for the performance of its functions and to provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Commission.
scope: Applies to the Karnataka Public Service Commission and its functions concerning the services of the State, as well as services of local authorities, other bodies corporate constituted by law, and public institutions. It also covers the conduct of service examinations for government servants and, under certain conditions, employees of local authorities and statutory bodies.

key_definitions.Assistant Secretary: The Assistant Secretary to the Commission, or in his absence, such other person discharging the duties of the Assistant Secretary for the time being.
key_definitions.Member: A Member of the Commission and includes the Chairman thereof.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Secretary: The Secretary to the Commission, or in his absence, such other person discharging the duties of the Secretary for the time being.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different provisions. Section 2 and Chapter II came into force at once, while other provisions were to come into force on a date appointed by the State Government.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Assistant Secretary', 'Commission', 'Government', 'Member', 'prescribed', and 'Secretary'.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for performance of functions of the Commission
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of Chapter II are applicable for the performance of the Commission's functions under the Constitution or any other law.

Outlines that all questions for decision by the Commission are to be decided either at a meeting or by circulation among Members, with provisions for requiring a meeting and handling cases of Members on leave.
Specifies that the Secretary shall prepare the agenda and convene meetings after giving notice to all Members.
Determines that questions at a meeting are decided by a majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote in case of an equal division.
Details the procedure when the Chairman is unable to attend a meeting, with the senior-most Member acting on his behalf and provisions for informing the Chairman and reconsidering decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings
main_sections.description: States that proceedings of the Commission are not invalidated by any vacancy or absence of a Member.
Specifies the quorum for a meeting of the Commission, which was revised to four members.
Requires all decisions to be recorded by the Secretary, allowing dissenting Members to record their dissent and reasons.

main_sections.section_title: Communications to be signed by the Secretary or the Assistant Secretary
main_sections.description: Mandates that communications from the Commission are to be signed by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary, with restrictions on communicating dissent unless directed.
Allows the Commission to depute Members to associated committees or boards dealing with recruitment or promotion, with provisions for forwarding recommendations for advice.
States that interviews for appointments may be conducted by two or more authorized Members, with results presented to the Commission for decision.
Empowers the Chairman, or in his absence the next senior Member, to deal with urgent matters requiring immediate action, to be reported to the Commission.
Allows the Government to make rules for matters not covered by Chapter II, in consultation with the Commission, and for the Commission to regulate its proceedings subject to such rules.
Empowers the Commission to conduct service examinations for State government servants and, if notified by the Government, for employees of local authorities and other bodies corporate.

main_sections.section_title: Functions in respect of services of local authorities
main_sections.description: Details the Commission's functions concerning the services of local authorities, including conducting examinations for appointments, consultation on recruitment methods, promotions, disciplinary matters, legal defense costs, and pension claims.

main_sections.section_title: Commission to furnish returns, etc., to Government
main_sections.description: Requires the Commission to furnish returns, records, and information to the Government as may be required.
Empowers the Government to make rules, in consultation with the Commission, to carry out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Decisions of the Commission are to be made either at a meeting or by circulation among Members. (Section 4)
The Secretary is responsible for preparing the agenda and convening meetings. (Section 5)
Decisions at meetings are made by a majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote. (Section 6)
Communications from the Commission must be signed by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary. (Section 11)
The Commission is responsible for conducting service examinations for government servants and, under certain conditions, for employees of local authorities and other bodies corporate. (Section 16)
The Commission must be consulted on various matters relating to the services of local authorities, including recruitment, promotions, and disciplinary actions. (Section 17)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Public Service Commission, and the State Government for making rules and appointing commencement dates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures outlined in the Act, including meetings, decision-making processes, and the issuance of communications. The Government enforces the Act through the rules it prescribes.

rights: Members have the right to record dissent and their reasons for it. (Section 10)
The Chairman has a second or casting vote in case of an equal division of votes. (Section 6)
duties: The Commission has a duty to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of local authorities. (Section 17(a))
The Commission has a duty to advise on matters relating to the services of local authorities when referred by the Government. (Section 17(b))
The Secretary has a duty to prepare the agenda and convene meetings. (Section 5)
The Secretary has a duty to record all decisions of the Commission. (Section 10)
obligations: Local authorities and other bodies corporate are subject to the Commission's oversight regarding recruitment, promotions, and disciplinary matters for their employees, as specified in the Act. (Section 17)

key_procedures: Decision making: Questions are decided either at a meeting or by circulation among members. If a member desires a meeting, the question is considered there. (Section 4)
Meeting procedure: Meetings are convened by the Secretary with an agenda. Decisions are by majority vote, with the Chairman having a casting vote. The quorum is four members. (Sections 5, 6, 9)

Communication of decisions: Opinions or decisions of the Commission are communicated in writing, signed by the Secretary or Assistant Secretary. Dissent is not communicated unless directed. (Section 11)
Conducting examinations: The Commission conducts service examinations for government servants and, as notified by the Government, for employees of local authorities and other bodies. (Section 16)
administration: The Karnataka Public Service Commission, overseen by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act has been amended over time to reflect changes in the State's name (Mysore to Karnataka) and to adjust provisions like the quorum and the scope of service examinations.
Chapter III, dealing with additional functions, came into force on October 1, 1960, as per notification No. GAD 15 OSR 60 dated August 30, 1960.

title: The Karnataka Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1977
purpose: To make temporary provisions in respect of industrial undertakings whose running is considered essential for preventing or providing relief against unemployment.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to 'State industrial undertakings' and 'relief undertakings'.

key_definitions.government company: Has the same meaning assigned to it in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.industry: Means any business, trade, undertaking, manufacture or calling of employers and includes any calling, service, employment, handicraft or industrial occupation or avocation of workmen.
key_definitions.relief undertaking: Means a State industrial undertaking declared as such under section 3.
key_definitions.state industrial undertaking: An industrial undertaking that is started or whose management is acquired or taken over by the State Government or a Government company and is run or proposed to be run by or under the authority of the State Government or a Government company; or to which any loan advanced or grant has been given or in respect of which a guarantee has been given by the State Government or a Government company or a Corporation owned or controlled by the State Government.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Government company', 'industry', 'relief undertaking', and 'State industrial undertaking'.
