Empowers the State Government to declare a State industrial undertaking as a relief undertaking by notification, if satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest to provide relief against unemployment. Specifies initial and extended periods for such declarations, with an aggregate limit.

main_sections.section_title: Power to specify industrial relations and other facilities temporarily
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to direct, by notification, that certain enactments specified in the Schedule shall not apply or shall apply with modifications to a relief undertaking. It also allows for the suspension or modification of contracts, agreements, and liabilities of the undertaking.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension or modification of certain remedies, etc.
main_sections.description: Details the effect of suspension or modification of remedies for rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities under section 4(1)(b). It states that suspended or modified rights revive upon the notification ceasing to have effect, and stayed proceedings can be continued.

Mandates the exclusion of the period during which a right, privilege, obligation, or liability or the remedy for its enforcement was suspended, when computing the period of limitation for its enforcement.
Empowers the State Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act and outlines the procedure for laying these rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

important_rules: A State industrial undertaking can be declared a relief undertaking for a period not exceeding two years initially, extendable by one year at a time, with an aggregate limit of twelve years (as amended).
The State Government can direct by notification that specific enactments (listed in the Schedule) will not apply or will apply with modifications to a relief undertaking.
Contracts, agreements, and liabilities of a relief undertaking can be suspended or modified by notification.
The period of limitation for enforcing rights or liabilities that were suspended under the Act will exclude the suspension period.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the State Legislature for a specified period for potential modification or annulment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through notifications and rule-making power).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the State Government, and by making and enforcing rules under the Act.

rights: The right to declare a State industrial undertaking as a relief undertaking.
The right to suspend or modify enactments, contracts, agreements, and liabilities.
The right to revive suspended rights/liabilities and continue stayed proceedings after a notification ceases to have effect.
The right to exclude suspension periods from limitation periods.
The right to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.
obligations: Obligation to enforce the Act through notifications and rules.
Obligation to lay rules before the State Legislature.
Obligations arising from the original contracts or statutes that are suspended or modified are subject to such suspension or modification.

key_procedures: Declaration of a relief undertaking: State Government, if satisfied of public interest and necessity for unemployment relief, issues a notification specifying the undertaking, date, and period.

Application of enactments and modification/suspension of contracts: State Government issues a notification directing non-application or modified application of scheduled enactments, or suspension/modification of existing contracts and liabilities.
Rule making: State Government makes rules, which are then subject to legislative scrutiny.
Revival of rights and continuation of proceedings: After a notification ceases to have effect, suspended rights/liabilities revive, and stayed proceedings continue as per existing laws.
administration: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka (as indicated by the notification and signatory).
important_notes: The Act was amended by the Karnataka Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) (Amendment) Act, 1989, which increased the aggregate period for a relief undertaking from ten years to twelve years.
The Act has an overriding effect, as notifications issued under section 4 override anything to the contrary in other laws, agreements, or court orders.

The Schedule lists specific central and state acts that can be exempted or modified for relief undertakings, including the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, and the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961.

title: The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1978
purpose: To provide for the prohibition of transfer and for the restoration of lands granted by the Government to persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State, as the existing non-alienation clauses in Land Grant Rules were found insufficient to protect these grantees from exploitation by affluent sections.
scope: This Act applies to lands granted by the Government to persons belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes within the State of Karnataka. It covers transactions related to such granted lands, including sales, gifts, exchanges, mortgages, leases, and other agreements, aiming to prevent their alienation and ensure their restoration to the original grantees or their heirs.

key_definitions.bank: Includes co-operative societies, RBI, banking companies, State Bank of India, subsidiary banks, corresponding new banks, Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation, Karnataka State Agro-Industries Corporation, Agricultural Finance Corporation Limited, and other notified financial institutions owned or controlled by the Government.
key_definitions.granted land: Any land granted by the Government to a person belonging to any of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes, including land allotted or granted under agrarian reforms, land ceiling, or abolition of inams laws, excluding those related to hereditary offices or rights.
key_definitions.scheduled castes: Shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Constitution.
key_definitions.scheduled tribes: Shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Constitution.
key_definitions.transfer: Means a sale, gift, exchange, mortgage (with or without possession), lease, or any other transaction not being a partition among members of a family or a testamentary disposition. It also includes the creation of a charge or an agreement to sell, exchange, mortgage, lease, or enter into any other transaction.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1978' and states that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration under article 31C of the Constitution
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act are for giving effect to the policy of the State towards securing the principles laid down in article 46 of the Constitution, which pertains to the promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'bank', 'granted land', 'Government', 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes', and 'transfer'. It also specifies that undefined words and expressions will have the meaning assigned in the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of transfer of granted lands
main_sections.description: Prohibits any transfer of granted land, whether before or after the commencement of the Act, if it contravenes the terms of the grant or the law providing for the grant. Such transfers are declared null and void. It also prohibits the transfer or acquisition of granted land after the commencement of the Act without the previous permission of the Government. This prohibition extends to sales in execution of court decrees or orders of other authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Resumption and restitution of granted lands
main_sections.description: Empowers the Assistant Commissioner, upon application, information, or suo-motu, to take possession of a granted land if a transfer is found to be null and void. The land is to be restored to the original grantee or their legal heir. If restoration is not practicable, the land vests in the Government and may be regranted to persons belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes. Orders passed under this section are final, subject to appeals.

Provides for an appeal to the Deputy Commissioner against orders passed by the Assistant Commissioner regarding the resumption, restitution, or a declaration that a transfer is not null and void. Appeals are to be filed within three months, with provisions for condonation of delay.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of registration of transfer of granted lands
main_sections.description: Prohibits registering officers from accepting documents for registration related to the transfer of or creation of any interest in granted lands, unless such transfer is in accordance with the Act or the terms of the grant.
Exempts transfers of granted lands in favour of the Government, the Central Government, a local authority, or a bank, whether before or after the commencement of the Act.
Prescribes penalties for acquiring granted land in contravention of the Act, including imprisonment, fine, or both. Offences are made cognizable.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder, for officers and the Government.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act. Such rules must be laid before each House of the State Legislature for modification or annulment.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Empowers the Government to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Any transfer of granted land made either before or after the commencement of the Act, in contravention of the terms of the grant or the law providing for such grant, shall be null and void. (Section 4(1))
Rule: No person shall, after the commencement of this Act, transfer or acquire by transfer any granted land without the previous permission of the Government. (Section 4(2))
Rule: Sales of granted land in execution of a civil court decree or order of any other authority are also prohibited if they contravene the provisions of Section 4. (Section 4(3))

Rule: The Assistant Commissioner shall, after enquiry, restore a fraudulently transferred granted land to the original grantee or their legal heir. If restoration is not practicable, the land vests with the Government for regrant. (Section 5(1))
Rule: No registering officer shall accept for registration any document relating to the transfer of granted land unless it complies with the Act or the terms of the grant. (Section 6)

penalties: Acquiring granted land in contravention of Section 4(2) is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both. (Section 8(1))
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assistant Commissioner (for resumption and restitution), Deputy Commissioner (for appeals), and Registering Officers (for registration of documents). The Government also has powers to grant permission for transfers and make rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through enquiries by the Assistant Commissioner, orders for resumption and restitution, appeals to the Deputy Commissioner, prohibition of registration by registering officers, and prosecution for contraventions.

rights: Right of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes grantees to retain their granted lands without alienation.
Right of original grantees or their legal heirs to have alienated lands restored to them.
Right to appeal against orders of the Assistant Commissioner to the Deputy Commissioner.
duties: Duty of persons not to transfer granted lands without Government permission.
Duty of registering officers to prohibit registration of unauthorized transfers of granted lands.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to restore granted lands to original grantees or their heirs.
Obligation of the Government to enact rules and enforce the provisions of the Act.
Obligation of individuals to adhere to the non-alienation clause of granted lands.

key_procedures: Procedure for Resumption and Restoration: An interested person can apply, or the Assistant Commissioner can act suo motu, upon information. After enquiry, if the transfer is void, the Assistant Commissioner orders possession and restores the land to the grantee or heir. If not practicable, it vests with the Government for regrant. (Section 5(1))

Procedure for Appeal: A person aggrieved by an order of the Assistant Commissioner can prefer an appeal to the Deputy Commissioner within three months, with provisions for condonation of delay and special admission for pending court cases. The Deputy Commissioner disposes of the appeal in a prescribed manner, and their order is final. (Section 5A)
administration: The primary administration of the Act involves the Assistant Commissioner for initial orders and the Deputy Commissioner for appeals. The Government (specifically, the Government of Karnataka) has the power to make rules and grant exemptions.
important_notes: The Act is based on the policy to protect the interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as enshrined in Article 46 of the Constitution.
The Act aims to undo exploitative transfers and restore lands to their intended beneficiaries.
Section 11 states that this Act overrides other laws if there is an inconsistency, highlighting its special purpose.

title: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Secondary Education Examination Board for the State of Karnataka for the purpose of holding and conducting certain public examinations, ensuring efficient conduct, timely declaration of results, and expeditious disposal of matters related to these examinations.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to secondary education examinations.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.bye-laws: Bye-laws made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.examination: An examination conducted by the Board.
key_definitions.Examiner: Includes the Chief Examiner, the Joint Chief Examiner, the Deputy Chief Examiner, and a Paper-setter.
key_definitions.Head Master/Head Mistress: The head of the teaching staff of a recognised High School, by whatever name designated.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the State Government under this Act.
key_definitions.recognised High School: A High School, a Higher Secondary School, a Composite Junior College, a Multi-purpose High School, or a Junior Technical School recognised by the Director of Public Instruction in Karnataka or an officer authorised by him.
key_definitions.regulations: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the State Government under this Act.
key_definitions.Supervisor: Includes Chief Superintendent, Block Superintendent, Assistant Superintendent, Room Superintendent, and Custodian.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board Act, 1966, its territorial extent to the whole of the State of Karnataka, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Board, bye-laws, Chairman, Director, examination, Examiner, Head Master/Head Mistress, notification, prescribed, recognised High School, regulations, rules, Secretary, Supervisor, and Vice-Chairman.

Deals with the establishment of the Board of Secondary Education Examination by the State Government through notification. It states that the Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to sue and be sued, acquire and hold property, and perform necessary actions for the purposes of the Act.

Outlines the composition of the Board, including the ex-officio Chairman (Commissioner for Public Instruction), the ex-officio Vice-Chairman (the Director), and various ex-officio, elected, and nominated members representing different educational authorities, institutions, and expertise.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Board
main_sections.description: Specifies the powers and duties vested in the Board, which likely involve conducting examinations, setting syllabi, appointing examiners, and generally managing secondary education examinations.
Details the establishment and management of the Board's fund, which would be used for its operations and expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the authority to make regulations concerning its functions and administration, subject to approval by the State Government.
Encompasses the powers of the State Government in relation to the Act, which may include making rules, approving regulations, appointing officials, and overseeing the Board's activities.
Confers upon the State Government the authority to frame rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any previous enactment that might be inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: The Act outlines the establishment and functioning of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board.
The Board is a body corporate responsible for conducting public examinations.
The constitution of the Board includes ex-officio, elected, and nominated members.
The Board has the power to make regulations and the State Government has the power to make rules.
Audited reports of the Board are to be laid before each house of the legislature (as per Amendment Act 9 of 2006).

penalties: Section 37 provides a bar of suits, etc., for acts done in good faith, implying that actions taken in good faith under the Act will not lead to legal action.
Section 38 requires previous notice for suits, etc., indicating a procedural safeguard before legal action can be taken against the Board or its officials.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framing of rules and regulations, appointment of officials, conduct of examinations, and legal provisions safeguarding actions taken in good faith.

rights: The Board has the right to sue and be sued and to acquire and hold property.
The Board has the right to conduct examinations and make regulations.
The State Government has the right to make rules and approve regulations.
duties: The Board has a duty to conduct public examinations efficiently and ensure timely declaration of results.
The Board has a duty to manage its fund and prepare annual accounts and financial estimates.
The Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and members have responsibilities as public servants (Section 35 and 36).
obligations: The Board is obligated to be established by the State Government.
The Board is obligated to comply with rules and regulations made by the State Government.
The Board is obligated to submit audited reports to the legislature.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Board by State Government notification.
Constitution of the Board with specified ex-officio, elected, and nominated members.
Making of regulations by the Board and their approval by the State Government.
Making of rules by the State Government.
Submission of audited reports to the legislature.
administration: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board and the State Government (Department of Public Instruction is implied as the administrative department).
important_notes: The Act has been amended several times to update its provisions, including changes to the definition of recognized high school, the composition of the Board, and financial provisions.
The definition of 'year' for accounting purposes was amended to align with the official government year (from August 1st to March 31st).
The provision for paying the State Government for staff salaries and allowances out of the Board fund was omitted as staff are considered Government servants paid from the State's consolidated fund.

title: THE KARNATAKA SERVICE EXAMINATIONS ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for service examinations and connected matters, resolving uncertainties and confusion regarding the validity of departmental examinations for government servants and the promotions based on them, particularly concerning retrospective promotions and payment of arrears.
scope: The Act applies to persons serving in connection with the affairs of the State of Karnataka, including those allotted or deemed to be allotted to the New State of Mysore under Section 115 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It specifically addresses service examinations and promotions during defined periods.

key_definitions.service_examinations: Shall have the same meaning as the 'prescribed examinations' in the Karnataka Civil Services (Service and Kannada Language Examinations) Rules, 1974, issued under the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.government_servant: Means a person serving in connection with the affairs of the State of Karnataka and includes a person allotted or deemed to be allotted to the New State of Mysore in pursuance of Section 115 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement dates. Section 1 and all other sections except section 8 came into force on November 1, 1956. Section 8 came into force on April 11, 1974.
Provides definitions for 'service examinations' and 'Government Servant' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: No service examination for the period from 1st November 1956 to 9th January 1974.
main_sections.description: Declares that no service examination was validly prescribed for Government servants for promotion eligibility during the period from November 1, 1956, to January 9, 1974. It mandates promotions for those not promoted solely due to not passing an examination, provided they are otherwise eligible, with such promotions being prospective only from January 10, 1974. It also outlines provisions for initial pay entitlement and revision of pension/gratuity for retired individuals.

main_sections.section_title: Service Examinations for the period from 10th January 1974.
main_sections.description: Establishes that from January 10, 1974, service examinations are the same as those provided in the Karnataka Civil Services (Service and Kannada Language Examinations) Rules, 1974. It makes passing these examinations mandatory for all Government servants, including those promoted under section 3, with failure entailing specified consequences.

Requires a review of promotions made between November 1, 1956, and January 9, 1974, to facilitate promotions under section 3. It specifies that promoted persons may yield place to juniors and be reverted if necessary. It also states that the rank of a promoted person in the seniority list shall be fixed as if they had been promoted on their eligibility date.

Makes the provisions of the Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Promotion, Pay and Pension) Act, 1973 (Karnataka Act 11 of 1974), as amended by section 8, applicable to matters not expressly provided for in this Act, provided they are not inconsistent.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with a provision for laying such rules before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

Amends the Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Promotion, Pay and Pension) Act, 1973 (Karnataka Act 11 of 1974) by substituting 'Mysore' with 'Karnataka' and modifying section 3(1)(a) to restrict retrospective promotions. It also inserts a new section 9A related to rule-making powers.

important_rules: Rule for determining promotions from November 1, 1956, to January 9, 1974: No service examination was deemed prescribed during this period. Those not promoted solely due to not passing an examination are to be promoted if otherwise eligible. Such promotions are prospective from January 10, 1974.

Entitlement to initial pay for prospective promotions: Persons promoted under section 3 are entitled to initial pay as if they were promoted from their eligibility date, but without any arrears for the period prior to actual promotion.

Revision of pension and gratuity for retired personnel: If a person eligible for promotion under section 3 retired before January 10, 1974, they are deemed promoted from their eligibility date, and their pension and gratuity shall be revised accordingly.

Service examinations from January 10, 1974: Service examinations are defined as those in the Karnataka Civil Services (Service and Kannada Language Examinations) Rules, 1974. Passing these examinations is mandatory for all Government servants.
Review of past promotions: Promotions made between November 1, 1956, and January 9, 1974, are to be reviewed. Juniors to those promoted under section 3 may be reverted to lower posts.
Fixation of seniority: The rank of a promoted person in the seniority list shall be fixed as if they had been promoted on their eligibility date.
Application of Karnataka Act 11 of 1974: Provisions of the Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Promotion, Pay and Pension) Act, 1973, are applicable where not inconsistent with this Act.
Amendment to Karnataka Act 11 of 1974: Replaces 'Mysore' with 'Karnataka' and restricts retrospective promotions, allowing them only to the extent specified in rules.

penalties: Failure to pass service examinations from January 10, 1974, shall entail consequences specified in the Karnataka Civil Services (Service and Kannada Language Examinations) Rules, 1974.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, through its relevant departments responsible for civil services.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the Act's provisions, including review of promotions, prospective promotions, and mandatory adherence to service examinations. Rules made under the Act are also subject to legislative oversight.

rights: Right to promotion for those eligible and previously not promoted solely due to not passing a service examination (for the period up to Jan 9, 1974).
Right to receive initial pay on the date of actual promotion as if promoted from the eligibility date (without arrears).
Right to revised pension and gratuity for retired individuals who would have been promoted.
Right to have seniority fixed as if promoted on the eligibility date.
duties: Duty of Government servants to pass prescribed service examinations from January 10, 1974.
Duty of the State Government to conduct reviews of past promotions and implement the Act's provisions.
Duty of the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to make promotions prospective from January 10, 1974.
Obligation to refrain from making retrospective promotions except as specified in the rules.
Obligation to yield place and be reverted where necessary, if promoted persons are juniors to those promoted under Section 3.

key_procedures: Procedure for promotion for the period November 1, 1956, to January 9, 1974: Review of promotions, identification of eligible individuals not promoted solely due to examination failure, prospective promotion from January 10, 1974, entitlement to initial pay as if promoted from eligibility date (no arrears), and revision of pension/gratuity for retirees.

Procedure for service examinations from January 10, 1974: Passing of Karnataka Civil Services (Service and Kannada Language Examinations) Rules, 1974, as a mandatory requirement for all government servants. Consequences for failure are outlined in these rules.

Procedure for rule making: The State Government may make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, which are then laid before the State Legislature for a period of thirty days for potential modification or annulment.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka, likely through its Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms (DPAR) or a similar body responsible for service matters.
important_notes: The Act aims to resolve past legal disputes and uncertainties regarding service examinations and promotions.
Retrospective promotions are generally disallowed after January 10, 1974, with exceptions only as specified by rules.
The Act has been amended by the Karnataka Act 25 of 1982.

title: The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the regulation of conditions of work and employment in shops and commercial establishments and other incidental matters.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It initially applied to areas specified in the Schedule and areas where previous related acts were in force, with provisions for extension to other areas via notification. It applies to shops and commercial establishments.

key_definitions.adult: A person who has completed their eighteenth year.
key_definitions.apprentice: A person aged not less than fourteen years, employed for training in any trade, craft, or employment in any establishment, whether paid or not.
key_definitions.banking company: Includes the Reserve Bank of India, banks defined under the Banking Regulations Act, 1949, the State Bank of India, Subsidiary Banks, and corresponding new banks constituted under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: This section outlines the name of the Act, its geographical extent (State of Karnataka), commencement date, and how it applies to different areas.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'adult', 'apprentice', and 'banking company'.
Details provisions for exempting certain establishments or categories of employees from the Act's provisions.
Mandates the registration of shops and commercial establishments and outlines the process.
Specifies the maximum daily and weekly hours of work for employees in establishments covered by the Act.
Deals with the payment of additional wages for any work performed beyond the prescribed daily or weekly hours.
Ensures that every employee is entitled to a weekly holiday.
Governs the entitlement of employees to annual leave with wages.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of women and young persons during night
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of women and young persons during night hours, with provisions for exemptions.
Provides for the appointment of Inspectors to enforce the provisions of the Act.
Details the powers and responsibilities of Inspectors in carrying out their duties under the Act.
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to frame rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Establishments must be registered under the Act.
Daily and weekly working hours are regulated.
Overtime work must be compensated at extra wages.
Employees are entitled to intervals for rest during work.
There are specified opening and closing hours for establishments.
Employees are entitled to a weekly holiday.
Employees are entitled to annual leave with wages.
Employment of children is prohibited.
Employment of women and young persons during night is prohibited, with exceptions.
Employers must maintain registers and records and display notices as prescribed.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions, including fines.
Specific penalties for obstructing Inspectors.
Penalties for false claims of deemed registration.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act, and potentially other authorities designated by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of establishments, examination of registers and records, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right to regulated working hours.
Right to extra wages for overtime.
Right to intervals for rest.
Right to weekly holidays.
Right to annual leave with wages.
Protection against employment during prohibited hours (children, women, young persons at night).
Right to be issued an appointment order in writing (introduced later).
duties: Duty to register the establishment.
Duty to inform the Inspector of changes or closure.
Duty to comply with daily and weekly working hour regulations.
Duty to pay extra wages for overtime.
Duty to provide intervals for rest.
Duty to observe opening and closing hours.
Duty to grant weekly holidays.
Duty to grant annual leave with wages.
Duty to not employ children and women/young persons during prohibited hours.
Duty to maintain registers and records.
Duty to issue appointment orders in writing.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of employment as regulated by the Act.
Obligation to facilitate inspections by appointed authorities.
Obligation to pay wages and compensation as per the Act and related laws (e.g., Payment of Wages Act, Workmen's Compensation Act).

key_procedures: Registration of an establishment: An employer must apply for registration and obtain a certificate from the Inspector.
Reporting changes/closure: Employers must communicate any changes in the establishment or its closure to the Inspector.
Claiming annual leave: Employees are entitled to annual leave with wages based on their service period.
Enforcement and penalties: Inspectors can take action against establishments violating the Act, leading to penalties or prosecution.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government of Karnataka, with the Labour Department likely playing a key role, and Inspectors appointed under the Act responsible for day-to-day enforcement.
important_notes: The Act has undergone several amendments to adapt to changing economic and social conditions, including provisions for IT establishments and changes in renewal periods.
Certain establishments or categories of employees may be exempted from specific provisions of the Act.
The Act integrates provisions of other labor laws like the Payment of Wages Act and the Workmen's Compensation Act.

title: The Karnataka Silkworm Seed, Cocoon and Silk Yarn (Regulation of Production, Supply, Distribution and Sale) Act, 1959
purpose: To consolidate the laws providing for the regulation of the production, supply, distribution, and sale of silkworm seed, cocoon, and silk yarn in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to the production, supply, distribution, and sale of silkworm seed, cocoons, and silk yarn. Specific provisions may come into force in different areas of the state at different times as notified by the government.

key_definitions.cocoon: Cocoon produced by mulberry, tassar, muga, and eri silkworms, either green or stifled, dried or in any other state or condition, excluding pierced cocoons. A pierced cocoon is one from which a moth has cut out.
key_definitions.cocoon_market: A market established under section 10 for the sale or purchase of cocoons of all kinds intended for reeling.
key_definitions.cross-breed_cocoons: Cocoons produced by rearing silkworm seeds resulting from the cross-breeding of two different races of silkworms.
key_definitions.dupion_silk_yarn: Silk yarn reeled out of double cocoons or inferior cocoons.
key_definitions.dyer: A person in charge of an establishment where silk yarn is dyed.
key_definitions.licensing_authority: An officer appointed by the Director of Sericulture in Karnataka for specific areas and purposes.
key_definitions.licenced_dealer: A person who carries on the business of buying and selling silk yarn, whether brought from outside the State, purchased in a silk exchange, or from a licensed trader or another licensed dealer.
key_definitions.licensed_trader: A person who is licensed to purchase silk yarn in a silk exchange.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.rearer: A person engaged in rearing silkworms for the production of silkworm cocoons, whether for reproduction or reeling. Rearing includes all operations from incubation and brushing to cocoon harvesting.
key_definitions.reeler: A person in charge of a reeling establishment and engaged in the business of reeling cocoons.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, specifies its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and outlines the commencement dates for different sections and areas within the state.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'cocoon', 'cocoon market', 'cross-breed cocoons', 'dupion silk yarn', 'dyer', 'Government', 'Licensing Authority', 'Licenced dealer', 'licensed trader', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'rearer', and 'reeler'.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of production, etc., of silkworm seed
main_sections.description: Deals with the regulation of the production, supply, and distribution of silkworm seed.
Concerns the regulation of silkworm rearing activities.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of possession of silkworm seed
main_sections.description: Regulates the possession of silkworm seed.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of Possession of Silk Yarn
main_sections.description: Regulates the possession of silk yarn. This section was added to include regulation of silk yarn possession, even for dyers.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of disposal of silkworm cocoons
main_sections.description: Governs the disposal of silkworm cocoons.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of sale or purchase of silkworm cocoons for reeling
main_sections.description: Regulates the sale and purchase of silkworm cocoons specifically for reeling purposes.
Deals with the regulation of the reeling process of cocoons.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of Sale and Purchase of Silk Yarn, etc.
main_sections.description: Regulates the sale and purchase of silk yarn. Amendments have been made to clarify the position of twisters and to exclude them from bringing twisted silk yarn back to the Silk Exchange for sale.
Provides for the establishment of Silk Exchanges, particularly to regulate the sale and purchase of silk yarn and protect the interests of reelers.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require information and powers of entry, inspection, seizure, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants powers to authorities to require information, and conduct entry, inspection, and seizure of relevant items.
Outlines the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including rules related to market fees.
Deals with the repeal of previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Licensing of production of silkworm seeds.
Regulation of rearing, possession, disposal, sale, or purchase of silkworms and silkworm cocoons.
Licensing of reeling establishments.
Control of cocoon markets.
Prohibition of the sale or purchase of silkworm cocoons except in established cocoon markets (amendment 29 of 1969).
Requirement for licensed dealers to furnish a declaration of silk yarn possessed in excess of the prescribed quantity (amendment 12 of 1997).
Compulsory sale or agreement to sell silk yarn purchased or brought from outside the State only in the Silk Exchange by licensed dealers (amendment 12 of 1997).

penalties: Penalties for contravention of provisions of sections 3, 7, 8, and 8A.
Enhanced penalties for certain offenses (amendments 29 of 1969, 30 of 1994, 12 of 1997).
Suspension or cancellation of licence, forfeiture of property.
Penalties for offenses (detailed in Section 12 and further enhanced by amendments).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director of Sericulture and officers appointed by them (Licensing Authority).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, inspection, seizure, imposing penalties, suspension or cancellation of licences, and recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue.

rights: Right to be issued a license for relevant activities (if criteria are met).
Right to sell or purchase cocoons/silk yarn in designated markets/exchanges.
Protection of persons acting under the Act (Section 16).
duties: Duty to comply with regulations regarding production, supply, distribution, and sale of silkworm seed, cocoons, and silk yarn.
Duty to obtain necessary licenses.
Duty to possess silkworm seed and silk yarn according to regulations.
Duty to dispose of silkworm cocoons as per regulations.
Duty to sell or purchase cocoons for reeling in regulated markets.
Duty to adhere to regulations for reeling.
Duty for licensed dealers to furnish declarations and sell in Silk Exchange (as per amendment 12 of 1997).
obligations: Obligation to adhere to licensing requirements.
Obligation to participate in regulated markets and exchanges for transactions.
Obligation to provide information when required by authorities.
Obligation to allow inspection and seizure by authorized personnel.

key_procedures: Application for a license (Section 9).
Regulation and distribution of silkworm seed (Section 10).
Establishment of Silk Exchanges (Section 10A).
Procedures for entry, inspection, and seizure by authorized officers (Section 11).
Process for suspension or cancellation of a license and forfeiture of property (Section 13).
Procedure for composition of offenses (Section 14).
Recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue (Section 16A).
administration: Directorate of Sericulture, Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to consolidate existing laws in different areas of the Mysore State after reorganisation.
Various amendments have been made over the years to include silk yarn, enhance penalties, and refine regulations, particularly concerning Silk Exchanges and licensed dealers.
Market fees on the sale and purchase of silk yarn in silk exchanges are regulated under the Act, with specific provisions for their levy and collection.

Some provisions, including those related to the establishment of Silk Exchanges and repeal/savings, came into force immediately upon enactment, while others became effective at later dates or in specific areas.
The Act provides for a Development and Price Stabilisation Fund (Section 17A).

title: The Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1973
purpose: To provide for the improvement and clearance of slums in the State of Karnataka, addressing issues of public health, sanitation, congestion, and inadequate basic needs, and for the acquisition of land for improving, developing, or redeveloping slum areas, clearing slums, and rehabilitating slum dwellers.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to slum areas, which are defined and can be declared as such. It covers building regulations within slum areas, improvement works, slum clearance, redevelopment, acquisition of land, protection of tenants, and the establishment and functions of the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Slum Clearance Board established under section 33.
key_definitions.building: Includes a house, out-house, stable, latrine, shed, hut, wall and any other such structure, whether of masonry, bricks, wood, mud, metal or any other materials whatsoever, but does not include plant or machinery comprised in a building.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1973. It specifies the extent as the whole of the State of Karnataka and mentions that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Board' and 'building'.
Empowers the prescribed authority to declare any area to be a slum area.
Specifies the application of Chapter III A, which deals with the prohibition of unauthorized constructions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of prescribed authority to order demolition of building unfit for human habitation
main_sections.description: Grants the prescribed authority the power to order the demolition of any building found unfit for human habitation.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare any slum area to be slum clearance area
main_sections.description: Allows the prescribed authority to declare any slum area as a slum clearance area.
Grants the Government the power to acquire land for the purposes of the Act.
Lays down the provisions for the amount payable for acquired land.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings for eviction of tenants not to be taken without permission of the prescribed authority
main_sections.description: Prohibits eviction proceedings against tenants in slum areas without the permission of the prescribed authority.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board.
Outlines the various functions and responsibilities of the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board.
Details the procedure for serving notices and orders issued under the Act.
Specifies the penalties for various offenses under the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule related to the registration of buildings in slum areas (Section 4).
Rule related to restrictions on building, etc., in slum areas (Section 5).
Rule regarding prohibition of construction of buildings without previous permission (Section 5B).
Rule regarding demolition of unlawfully commenced, carried on or completed buildings (Section 5C).
Rules for the execution of works of improvement in slum areas (Sections 6 and 7).
Rules for the recovery of expenses for maintenance of improvement works (Section 8).
Rules for the demolition of buildings unfit for human habitation (Sections 9 and 10).
Rules for slum clearance and redevelopment, including the obligation to clear areas and demolish buildings (Sections 11-16).
Rules regarding the acquisition of land and the amount payable (Sections 17-27B).
Rules for the protection of tenants from eviction and rent regulation (Sections 28-32).
Rules related to the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board, its constitution, functions, finance, accounts and audit (Sections 33-48).
Rules for miscellaneous provisions including service of notices, powers of entry and inspection, eviction, penalties, and appeals (Sections 49-73).

penalties: Penalties for offenses specified in Section 62, which include imprisonment and fines for violations of the Act's provisions.
Penalties for unauthorized construction, demolition of unlawfully commenced buildings, and offenses by companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority and the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board are the primary enforcement bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves issuing notices, orders for demolition or improvement, acquisition of land, eviction proceedings, and prosecution for offenses. The Act also provides for appeals against orders.

rights: Right to receive compensation for acquired land (Section 19).
Right to appeal against orders fixing the amount of compensation (Section 21).
Right to appeal to the High Court against certain decisions (Section 25).
Right to appeal against orders refusing permission for eviction (Section 29).
Rights of previous occupants to be considered for transfer of property after redevelopment (Section 16).
duties: Duty to obtain permission before commencing construction in slum areas (Section 5B).
Duty to comply with orders for execution of works of improvement (Section 6).
Duty to vacate premises when demolition orders are made (Section 10).
Duty to clear slum clearance areas and demolish buildings as per orders (Section 12).
Duty to cooperate with the Board and authorities in slum improvement and clearance activities.
obligations: Obligation to demolish buildings unfit for human habitation when ordered (Section 9).
Obligation to clear areas declared as slum clearance areas (Section 12).
Obligation for owners to re-develop slum clearance areas (Section 14).
Obligation for the Board to implement schemes for improvement and clearance (Section 40).
Obligation to comply with directions of the Government (Section 44).

key_procedures: Procedure for declaration of Slum Areas: The prescribed authority can declare an area as a slum area based on its conditions (Section 3).
Procedure for obtaining permission for construction: Construction of buildings in slum areas requires previous permission (Section 5B).
Procedure for demolition of unfit buildings: If a building is unfit for human habitation, the prescribed authority can order its demolition after following a procedure (Sections 9, 10).
Procedure for slum clearance and redevelopment: Declaring an area as a slum clearance area, clearing it, and redeveloping it (Sections 11-16).
Procedure for acquisition of land: The government can acquire land for slum improvement and clearance purposes, with provisions for compensation and appeals (Sections 17-27B).
Procedure for eviction of tenants: Eviction requires permission from the prescribed authority, with appeal provisions (Sections 28-30).
Procedure for establishing and functioning of the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board: Includes constitution, powers, duties, and financial management (Sections 33-48).
Procedure for serving notices and orders: Proper service of official communications is mandated (Section 50).
Procedure for appeals: Various sections provide for appeals against orders made under the Act (e.g., Sections 21, 25, 29, 59).
Procedure for disposal of materials from demolished buildings and recovery of expenses (Section 61).
administration: The Karnataka Slum Clearance Board is the primary administrative body, alongside the prescribed authority appointed by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act was necessitated due to the inadequacy of previous laws in effectively checking the growth of slums and clearing those unfit for human habitation, as well as the need to implement schemes with financial assistance from the Government of India.

Amendments have been made over time to rename the state from Mysore to Karnataka, to prohibit unauthorized constructions, to enhance penalties for encroachments, to increase compensation rates for acquired land, to empower the Board to acquire land by agreement, and to streamline the Board's functions regarding land transfer, development, and recovery of dues.
Chapter III A, dealing with the prohibition of unauthorized constructions, was extended to the whole State.
The Act overrides other laws in case of inconsistency (Section 70).

title: The Karnataka Small Cause Courts Act, 1964
purpose: To provide for a uniform law relating to Courts of Small Causes in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It establishes and governs Courts of Small Causes, defining their constitution, jurisdiction, practice, and procedure for the trial of suits of a civil nature within their pecuniary limits.

key_definitions.City of Bangalore: Has the meaning assigned to it in the Bangalore City Civil Court Act, 1979.
key_definitions.Code: Means the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908).
key_definitions.Court of Small Causes: Means a Court of Small Causes constituted or deemed to have been constituted under this Act and includes any person exercising jurisdiction under this Act in any such Court.
key_definitions.High Court: Means the High Court of the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.Judge: Means a Judge of the Court of Small Causes and in the City of Bangalore the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes.
key_definitions.judicial service: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (b) of Article 236 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the official Gazette.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Small Cause Courts Act, 1964. It specifies that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and shall come into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'City of Bangalore', 'Code', 'Court of Small Causes', 'High Court', 'Judge', 'judicial service', and 'notification'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, to establish a Court of Small Causes at any place and define its local limits of jurisdiction by notification.

States that upon the establishment of a Court of Small Causes, the High Court shall appoint a Civil Judge as its Judge by notification. It also provides for the appointment of a District Judge as the Chief Judge in the City of Bangalore.

Allows the High Court to appoint one or more Civil Judges as additional Judges. These Additional Judges can discharge functions assigned by the Judge and exercise the same powers. In the absence of the Judge, the Additional Judge or Senior Additional Judge can perform the Judge's functions.

Details the appointment of a Registrar to a Court of Small Causes by the High Court. The Registrar acts as the chief ministerial officer. The High Court can also confer upon a Registrar (if in judicial service) the jurisdiction of a Judge for trying suits up to a certain value (initially fifty rupees). The Registrar tries suits as directed by the Judge.

Requires ministerial officers of a Court of Small Causes to perform duties assigned by the Judge, in addition to those prescribed by law. The High Court can make rules to confer powers and duties on these officers.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of suits by Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: This section outlines which suits are cognizable by Courts of Small Causes. The pecuniary jurisdiction has been subject to amendments, with the original Act specifying limits that were later increased.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusive jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Defines the exclusive jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes within their local limits for suits of a civil nature cognizable by them.
States that the procedure, save as otherwise provided by this Act, shall be in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Details the circumstances under which a Registrar can try suits, as directed by the Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Admission, return and rejection of plaints by Registrar
main_sections.description: Grants the Registrar the power to admit, return, and reject plaints in suits cognizable by the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Passing of decrees by Registrar on admission
main_sections.description: Allows the Registrar to pass decrees in suits where the defendant admits the claim.
Empowers the Registrar to execute decrees passed by the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Adjournment of cases by chief ministerial officers
main_sections.description: Permits chief ministerial officers to adjourn cases in the absence of the Judge or Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: Return of Plaint In Suits Involving question of title
main_sections.description: Provides for the return of plaints in suits where a question of title is involved, to be presented in the proper court.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal from certain orders of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Specifies that an appeal shall lie from certain orders passed by a Court of Small Causes, as prescribed by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Revision of decrees and orders of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power of revision over decrees and orders made by Courts of Small Causes.
Declares that subject to the provisions of this Act, decrees and orders passed by a Court of Small Causes shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Subordination of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Places Courts of Small Causes under the subordination of the District Court and the High Court.
Deals with the vacation periods for Courts of Small Causes, which have been subject to amendments aiming to reduce litigation delays and harmonize with other civil courts.
Prescribes that every Court of Small Causes shall have a seal for its process.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Provides the State Government with the power to abolish any Court of Small Causes by notification.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of power to appoint Judge of Court of Small Causes to other office
main_sections.description: Saves the power to appoint a Judge of a Court of Small Causes to any other office.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to Courts invested with jurisdiction of Court of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Makes provisions for the application of this Act to courts invested with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act and Code to Courts so invested as to two Courts
main_sections.description: Deals with the application of the Act and the Code to courts invested with small cause jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of Code as so applied
main_sections.description: Allows for modifications to the Code of Civil Procedure as applied to courts invested with small cause jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of proceedings of abolished Courts
main_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of proceedings of abolished Courts of Small Causes.
Repeals previous enactments and provides savings clauses to ensure smooth transition and continuity of legal provisions.

important_rules: Rules regarding the admission, return, and rejection of plaints by the Registrar (Section 12).
Rules for the passing of decrees by the Registrar on admission of the claim (Section 13).
Rules for the execution of decrees by the Registrar (Section 14).
Rules for the adjournment of cases by chief ministerial officers (Section 15).
Rules for the return of plaints in suits involving questions of title (Section 16).
Rules regarding the vacation periods for Courts of Small Causes (Section 21).
Rules for the application of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, with modifications, to the proceedings in Courts of Small Causes (Section 10, 26, 27).

rights: Right to have suits of a civil nature within the pecuniary jurisdiction heard by a Court of Small Causes.
Right to appeal from certain orders of Courts of Small Causes (Section 17).
Right to seek revision of decrees and orders of Courts of Small Causes by the High Court (Section 18).
duties: Duty of the State Government to establish Courts of Small Causes in consultation with the High Court.
Duty of the High Court to appoint Judges and Registrar.
Duty of the Judge to assign functions to Additional Judges.
Duty of ministerial officers to perform duties as directed by the Judge and High Court.
Duty of parties to adhere to the procedures prescribed by the Act and the Code of Civil Procedure.
obligations: Obligation of the High Court to supervise the functioning of Courts of Small Causes.
Obligation of the Registrar to perform duties assigned by the Judge and High Court.
Obligation to present suits within the pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction of the respective Courts of Small Causes.

key_procedures: Establishment of Courts of Small Causes by the State Government.
Appointment of Judges and Registrar by the High Court.
Trial of suits by the Judge, Additional Judges, or Registrar as per their jurisdiction and directions.
Admission, return, or rejection of plaints by the Registrar.
Passing of decrees by the Registrar on admission.
Execution of decrees by the Registrar.
Appeals from certain orders to the appropriate court.
Revision of decrees and orders by the High Court.
administration: The High Court of Karnataka is responsible for the administration and supervision of the Courts of Small Causes, including the appointment of Judges and Registrar, and making rules for their functioning. The State Government is responsible for the establishment of these courts and their abolition.
important_notes: The pecuniary jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes has been significantly enhanced through various amendments (e.g., from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 25,000 by Act 13 of 1989).
The Act aims to provide a uniform law across the State, replacing disparate enactments.
The Act was amended to abolish vacation in civil courts and later to restore it, reflecting evolving needs and judicial practices.
The establishment of a City Civil Court for Bangalore led to amendments defining 'City of Bangalore' and adjusting roles like the Chief Judge.
The Act is a key piece of legislation for the expeditious disposal of smaller civil claims.

title: THE KARNATAKA SOCIETIES REGISTRATION ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the registration of literary, scientific, charitable and other societies in the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to societies established for the promotion of charity, education, science, literature, fine arts, sports, diffusion of knowledge relating to commerce or industry, diffusion of political education, foundation or maintenance of libraries, reading rooms, public museums and galleries, collection of natural history, mechanical and philosophical inventions, instruments or designs, and promotion of conservation and proper use of natural resources and scarce infrastructural facilities. Societies must intend to apply their profits or income in promoting their objects and prohibit the payment of any dividend or distribution of income or profits among their members.

key_definitions.governing body: The governors, council, directors, committee, trustees or other body to whom by the rules and regulations of the society, the management of its affairs is entrusted.
key_definitions.member: A person who, having been admitted to membership of a society in accordance with the rules and regulations thereof, has paid their subscription and signed the roll or list of members, and has not resigned. However, in proceedings under this Act, a person whose subscription is in arrear for more than three months is not entitled to vote or be counted as a member.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar: Such officer as the State Government may, by notification, appoint to perform the duties and functions of the Registrar under this Act in a specified area. Where no such officer is appointed, it refers to the Inspector General of Registration in Karnataka.
key_definitions.year: The year ending on the 31st day of December, or in the case of societies whose accounts are made up to another date with the Registrar's sanction, the year ending with that date.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka State), and the commencement date which is to be appointed by the State Government through a notification in the official Gazette. The Act came into force on 15.6.1961.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'governing body', 'member', 'prescribed', 'registered society', 'Registrar', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Societies to which the Act applies
main_sections.description: This section lists the types of societies that can be registered under the Act, covering a broad range of charitable, educational, scientific, artistic, and socio-political objectives, as well as the promotion of conservation and proper use of natural resources. It also specifies that these societies must apply their profits or income to their objects and prohibit dividend distribution to members.
This section mandates that a society must consist of at least seven persons above the age of eighteen years to be registered under the Act, unless the State Government is a member of that society.

This section outlines the process for forming a society. It requires seven or more persons, each above eighteen years of age, associated for a purpose specified in section 3, to subscribe their names to a memorandum of association and comply with the Act's requirements for registration.

This section details the contents of the memorandum of association, which must include the society's name, objects, names, addresses, and occupations of the governing body members responsible for management, and the location of the registered office. It also requires the registration of the society's rules and regulations, which must cover member admission, general meetings, voting procedures, the governing body, and its meetings. No rule can exclude a member from voting rights.

This section provides for the appointment of an Administrator to manage the affairs of a society temporarily when it has not held its general body meeting, a new governing body cannot be elected, or the State Government deems it necessary in the public interest. The Administrator's term is limited, and they are required to take steps to convene a meeting and hold elections.
This section deals with offenses committed under the Act and the penalties associated with them.
This section empowers the State Government to make rules under the Act.
This section addresses the repeal of previous laws and any savings provisions.

penalties: Penalties are described under Section 28. Specific details of penalties are not provided in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Societies is the primary authority for enforcement and oversight, as indicated by sections concerning inquiries and the appointment of an Administrator.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes inquiries into the activities of societies, the cancellation of registration, the appointment of administrators, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Members have the right to vote and participate in general meetings (subject to rules and regulations, and provided subscriptions are not in arrears for over three months).
duties: Members have a duty to pay subscriptions.
Societies have a duty to apply profits or income in promoting their objects.
Societies must prohibit the payment of any dividend or distribution of any income or profits among their members.
Societies must hold general meetings.
Societies must maintain accounts and file balance sheets and annual lists of the governing body with the Registrar.
obligations: Societies are obligated to register their memorandum of association and rules and regulations.
Societies must comply with the requirements regarding their memorandum of association and rules and regulations.
Societies must ensure their name is not undesirable.
Societies must provide for the vesting of property.
Societies must follow procedures for amalgamation and dissolution.
Societies must allow inspection of documents.

key_procedures: Registration of a Society: Seven or more persons above 18 years subscribe to a memorandum of association and comply with Act and rules, including submitting rules and regulations concerning member admission, meetings, and the governing body. The memorandum must state the society's name, objects, governing body details, and registered office location.
Alteration of Memorandum of Association: (Covered under Section 9, details not in excerpt)
Change of Name, Rules and Regulations: (Covered under Section 10, details not in excerpt)
Amalgamation of Societies: (Covered under Section 21, details not in excerpt)
Dissolution of Societies: (Covered under Section 22, details not in excerpt)
Enquiry by Registrar: The Registrar can conduct an enquiry if a society appears to be carrying on unlawful activity or allowing unlawful activity (as amended).

Appointment of Administrator: If a society cannot hold its general body meeting or elect a new governing body, or in the public interest, the State Government can appoint an Administrator for a short period to manage affairs and facilitate elections.
administration: The Registrar of Societies (or the Inspector General of Registration in Karnataka where no Registrar is appointed) and the State Government are responsible for the administration of this Act. The State Government also has powers to make rules.
important_notes: The Act was drafted generally on the lines of the Mysore Societies Registration Act, 1904, incorporating useful safeguards from that Act.

Amendments have been made over time to clarify powers of delegation for inquiries, allow flexibility in financial year reporting, enhance fees, provide for Administrator appointment and extension of their term, extend the scope to include horse racing, and facilitate water user societies for Participatory Irrigation Management.
Section 3(c) regarding 'promotion of sports' has been omitted.

title: The Karnataka State Civil Services (Prevention of Strikes) Act, 1966
purpose: To provide for the prevention of strikes by civil servants of the State of Karnataka.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to State Civil Servants.

key_definitions.state_civil_servant: A person who is a member of a civil service of the State of Karnataka or holds any civil post under the State of Karnataka.
key_definitions.strike: A cessation of work (including any unauthorised absence from duty) by a body of State civil servants acting in combination, or a concerted refusal, or a refusal under a common understanding, of any number of State civil servants to work.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Karnataka State Civil Services (Prevention of Strikes) Act, 1966. It specifies that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and comes into force at once.
Defines 'State Civil Servant' and 'strike' as used within the Act.
States that no State civil servant shall resort to a strike.
Prescribes punishment for State civil servants who commence, continue, or act in furtherance of a strike. Penalties include imprisonment up to six months, a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.

Provides penalties for any person who instigates or incites State civil servants to take part in a strike, or acts in furtherance of a strike. This includes imprisonment up to one year and a fine up to one thousand rupees.
Outlines penalties for any person who knowingly expends or applies money in furtherance or support of a strike. This includes imprisonment up to one year, a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
States that any person who attempts to commit or does any act preparatory to the commission of an offence under this Act shall be deemed to have committed such offence.

Deals with offences committed by associations, making the association and its responsible persons liable. It includes provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence to avoid liability and also holds members of executive or managing committees, managers, secretaries, or other officers liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or due to their neglect. 'Association' is defined to include any body of individuals whether incorporated or not.
Grants police officers the power to arrest without a warrant any person reasonably suspected of having committed an offence punishable under this Act.

Introduced by amendment, this section stipulates that a person accused or convicted of an offence under section 5 (instigation etc.) cannot be released on bail unless the prosecution has had an opportunity to oppose the application and the court is satisfied there are reasonable grounds to believe the person is not guilty.
Introduced by amendment, this section mandates that the trial of any offence under this Act in any court shall have precedence over the trial of any other offence pending in that court.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No.1 of 1966
main_sections.description: Repeals the Karnataka State Civil Services (Prevention of Strikes) Ordinance, 1966.

important_rules: No State civil servant shall resort to strike (Section 3).
Any State civil servant who participates in a strike is liable for punishment (Section 4).
Anyone instigating, inciting, or acting in furtherance of a strike is liable for punishment (Section 5).
Providing financial assistance to support a strike is punishable (Section 6).
Attempts to commit offences or preparatory acts are treated as offences (Section 7).
Associations can be held liable for offences committed under the Act (Section 8).

penalties: For participating in a strike: Imprisonment up to six months, fine up to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 4).
For instigation etc.: Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to one thousand rupees (Section 5).
For giving financial assistance: Imprisonment up to one year, fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 6).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers have the power to arrest without warrant (Section 9). The prosecution is involved in bail applications for specific offences (Section 9A).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves arrest by police, prosecution for offences, and specific provisions for bail and precedence for trials to ensure speedy justice.

duties: State Civil Servants have a duty not to resort to strikes.
Individuals and associations have a duty not to instigate, support financially, or otherwise promote strikes.
obligations: Any person in charge of an association responsible for its business has an obligation to ensure no offences under the Act are committed, and to exercise due diligence (Section 8(1)).

Members of the executive or managing committee, managers, secretaries, or other officers of an association have an obligation to prevent offences committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect (Section 8(2)).

key_procedures: Arrest without warrant by a police officer for suspected commission of an offence under the Act (Section 9).
Procedure for granting bail for offences under Section 5, requiring prosecution's opportunity to oppose and court's satisfaction of reasonable grounds for belief of innocence (Section 9A).
Trials for offences under the Act are given precedence over other pending trials in court (Section 9B).
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government and its relevant departments. Specific enforcement powers are given to police officers.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in response to apprehensions of organized bodies of Government employees causing dislocation of work by resorting to strikes.
The Act was initially promulgated as an Ordinance and later replaced by this Act, with amendments made by Act 6 of 1967 to enhance penalties and introduce provisions for bail and trial precedence.
The definition of 'strike' includes unauthorised absence from duty.
The Act applies to the entire State of Karnataka.

title: The Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Promotion, Pay and Pension) Act, 1973
purpose: To provide for prospective promotions of civil servants and to regulate the pay, seniority, pension, and other conditions of service of civil servants in the State of Karnataka, including those allotted or deemed to be allotted to serve in connection with the affairs of the State under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It aims to address issues arising from retrospective promotions, double payments, and the determination of suitability for promotional posts.
scope: The Act applies to civil servants of the State of Karnataka, including those who were allotted or are deemed to have been allotted to serve in connection with the affairs of the State under Section 115 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It covers regulations related to promotion, pay, seniority, pension, and other conditions of service.

key_definitions.allottee: A Government servant allotted or deemed to have been allotted to serve in connection with the affairs of the State of Karnataka under or in pursuance of Section 115 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
key_definitions.civil servant: A person who is a member of the civil service of the State of Karnataka or who holds a civil post under the State of Karnataka, and includes an allottee.
key_definitions.final seniority list: An inter-State seniority list of allottees prepared in accordance with the decisions of the Central Government under the provisions of sub-section (5) of Section 115 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
key_definitions.inter-state seniority list: An inter-State seniority list prepared from time to time, on the basis of the seniority in which the eligibility of an allottee to promotion to a higher post or posts is considered.
key_definitions.rules of recruitment: The rules of recruitment made in respect of recruitment to any service, post, office or class of posts or offices.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement dates. Sections 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 12 are deemed to have come into force on November 1, 1956, while other sections came into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'allottee', 'civil servant', 'final seniority list', 'inter-State seniority list', and 'rules of recruitment'.

Lays down rules regarding promotions of civil servants, stating that no civil servant is entitled to retrospective promotion except as specified in the rules, or to be promoted solely based on seniority without determination of eligibility and a written order. It also mandates assessment of work and declaration of satisfactory completion of officiation for continued service in promoted posts.

Deals with the review of promotions of allottees where their seniority in the provisional list differs from the final list. It mandates reviewing promotions made after November 1, 1956, based on the final seniority list and rules of recruitment. If a senior person is found suitable, they are to be promoted prospectively.
