Pay and allowances are to be fixed as if they held the post from the date of eligibility, but without arrears before actual promotion.

main_sections.section_title: Provision relating to reversion of allottees
main_sections.description: This section title indicates it will deal with the reversion of allottees, likely in light of reviewed promotions.

main_sections.section_title: Provision relating to revision of pensions, etc.
main_sections.description: This section title suggests provisions for the revision of pensions and related benefits.

main_sections.section_title: Provision relating to payments to heirs of deceased allottees
main_sections.description: This section title indicates it will address payments to the legal heirs of deceased allottees.

main_sections.section_title: Sections not applicable to certain allottees
main_sections.description: This section specifies certain categories of allottees to whom some sections of the Act may not apply.
This section likely details the process and conditions of officiation in higher posts.
This section, inserted by an amendment, likely provides the power to make rules under the Act.
Empowers the Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
This section likely states that the provisions of this Act override other laws or rules in case of conflict.
This section addresses the repeal of any prior legislation that is inconsistent with this Act.
This section likely provides for savings, meaning that certain actions or situations prior to the commencement of the Act may be preserved.

important_rules: Rule: No civil servant shall be entitled to retrospective promotion to any post or office, except as specified in the rules made under this Act.
Rule: Promotion to any post or office shall not be granted solely on the ground of seniority in a seniority list. An authority must determine eligibility and issue a written order for officiation.

Rule: Continued service in a promoted post requires the competent authority to assess the civil servant's work and issue a written order declaring satisfactory completion of officiation, except as provided in Section 9.

Rule: A civil servant promoted to officiate in a post can only be considered for promotion to the next higher post after being declared to have satisfactorily completed their officiation in the first promoted post, save as provided in Section 9.

Rule: Promotions of allottees made after November 1, 1956, shall be reviewed based on the final seniority list and applicable recruitment rules. If a senior person is found suitable, they shall be promoted prospectively.

Rule: Upon satisfactory completion of officiation, an allottee promoted under Section 4 shall be entitled to initial pay as if they were holding the post from the date of eligibility, but without arrears for the period prior to actual promotion. Their seniority shall be fixed as if promoted on the date of eligibility.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and competent authorities appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through review of promotions, determination of eligibility, issuance of written orders for promotion and officiation, assessment of work, and refixation of pay and seniority as stipulated in the Act and any rules made thereunder.

rights: Right to be considered for promotion based on eligibility and satisfactory performance.
Right to have pay and allowances fixed prospectively from the date of eligibility (though arrears before actual promotion may not be payable).
Right to have seniority fixed in the promoted grade as if promoted on the date of eligibility.
duties: Duty of the competent authority to determine eligibility for promotion and issue written orders.
Duty of the competent authority to assess the work of promoted civil servants and declare satisfactory completion of officiation.
Duty of civil servants to meet eligibility criteria and perform satisfactorily in promoted posts.
Duty to adhere to prospective promotions as regulated by the Act and its rules.
obligations: Obligation to review promotions made based on provisional inter-state seniority lists.
Obligation to ensure that retrospective promotions do not lead to double payments or retrospective reversions causing complications.
Obligation to ensure that promotions are made based on suitability and not solely on seniority, to prevent incompetent individuals from holding promotional posts to the detriment of public interest.

key_procedures: Procedure: Review of promotions for allottees whose seniority in the provisional list differs from the final list, based on final seniority and recruitment rules.
Procedure: Determination of eligibility and issuance of a written order by the competent authority to promote a civil servant to officiate in a post.
Procedure: Assessment of the work of a civil servant in a promoted post and declaration of satisfactory completion of officiation by the competent authority.
Procedure: Refixation of pay and allowances for allottees from the date of eligibility, with prospective promotion, but without payment of arrears for the period prior to actual promotion.
Procedure: Fixing the rank in the seniority list of a promoted allottee as if they had been promoted on the date of eligibility.
administration: The State Government of Karnataka, and potentially departments or agencies responsible for civil services administration.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to address issues arising from court directives for retrospective promotions, which could lead to significant financial burdens on the State and complications in administration.
The Act aims to prevent retrospective appointments to statutory posts, which is considered legally impermissible and can render statutory functions ineffective.
The Act seeks to ensure that promotions are made based on suitability and merit, rather than solely on seniority, to safeguard public interest.
Certain sections of the Act are deemed to have come into force retrospectively from November 1, 1956, aligning with the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

title: THE KARNATAKA TODDY WORKERS' WELFARE FUND ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund to promote the welfare of toddy workers in the State of Karnataka by collecting contributions from employers and employees and establishing an autonomous Board to administer the fund and prepare welfare schemes.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Karnataka and specifically to toddy workers, their employers, and matters related to the manufacture, distribution, transport, storage, or sale of toddy.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 5.
key_definitions.contribution: A contribution payable in respect of a member under the scheme.
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs one or more employees in connection with the manufacture, distribution, transport, storage or sale of toddy, and includes any person holding a license under the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965 for such activities.
key_definitions.employee: Any person employed for wages in connection with the manufacture, distribution, transport, storage or sale of toddy, receiving wages directly or indirectly from the employer, including those employed through a contractor or agent.
key_definitions.Fund: The Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.Scheme: The Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.toddy: Fermented or unfermented juice drawn from an excise tree as defined in the Karnataka Excise Act, 1965.
key_definitions.wages: All emoluments earned by an employee while on duty or on leave with wages as per the employment contract, paid or payable in cash, excluding cash value of food concessions, overtime allowance, bonus, and commission.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government by notification.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'contribution', 'employer', 'employee', 'Fund', 'manufacture', 'member', 'Schedule', 'Scheme', 'toddy', and 'wages'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund and details its composition (contributions from employers and employees, and interest). It also specifies the contribution rates (5% of wages from employer and employee, and 5% as gratuity from employer) and vests the Fund in the Board for administration. The Board can invest surplus funds.
Empowers the State Government to frame a scheme for the welfare of toddy workers, which can include matters specified in the Schedule. The Scheme can be amended by the State Government.

Provides for the constitution of the Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, which will be a body corporate. It specifies that the Board will consist of Directors appointed by the State Government, with equal representation from the State Government, employers, and employees. At least one Director must belong to a Scheduled Caste and one from among toddy tappers. The State Government appoints a Chairman. The term of office is three years.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of the members of the staff
main_sections.description: Details the appointment of a Chief Welfare Fund Inspector (who is also the Chief Executive Officer of the Board) and other Welfare Fund Inspectors by the State Government. The Board can appoint other necessary staff with State Government approval. Conditions of service for these staff are specified.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amount due from employers
main_sections.description: Grants the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or authorized Inspectors the power to determine amounts due from employers. The inquiry process is detailed, with powers similar to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Employers must be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard before an order is made. Appeals against such orders can be made to the State Government or a specified authority.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: Specifies that amounts due from employers, including arrears, can be recovered along with interest (9% per annum) in the same manner as arrears of land revenue.

States that amounts credited to a member's account in the Fund are not assignable, chargeable, or liable to attachment for the member's debts or liabilities. Amounts payable to a nominee upon a member's death are free from the deceased's or nominee's prior debts.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of payment of contribution over other debts
main_sections.description: Ensures that amounts due from an employer to the Fund are prioritized and paid before other debts when the employer is adjudicated insolvent or a company is being wound up, provided the liability accrued before the insolvency or winding-up order.

main_sections.section_title: Employer not to reduce wages, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits employers from reducing an employee's wages or benefits due to their liability for contributions to the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Members of the Board to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members of the Board, Inspectors, and staff appointed under the Act as public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

Prescribes penalties for making false statements to avoid payments (imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹500 or both). It also penalizes contravention of the Act or Scheme with similar penalties if no other penalty is provided. Court cognizance requires a report with the State Government's or specified authority's sanction.

Deals with offences committed by companies, making the company and its responsible persons liable. It includes provisions for directors, managers, etc., who consent to or are negligent in preventing offences.

main_sections.description: This section title is present in the arrangement of sections but not elaborated in the provided text.

important_rules: Contribution to the Fund: Employers must contribute 5% of the wages payable to each employee and an additional 5% as gratuity. Employees must contribute 5% of the wages they receive.
Fund Investment: The Board may invest surplus funds in securities of the State Government or Scheduled Banks.
No Wage Reduction: Employers cannot reduce employee wages or benefits due to their contribution liability.
Public Servants: Board members, Inspectors, and staff are deemed public servants.
Offence Penalties: False statements to avoid payment are punishable. Contravention of the Act or Scheme is also punishable.

penalties: Whoever knowingly makes a false statement or representation to avoid payment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with both.

Whoever contravenes or makes default in complying with any provision of the Act or Scheme (if no other penalty is provided): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Welfare Fund Inspector, Welfare Fund Inspectors, and the Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through determination of amounts due from employers, recovery as arrears of land revenue, imposing penalties for contraventions, and through judicial proceedings for offences. The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector has powers akin to a civil court during inquiries.

rights: Members of the Fund have rights to benefits provided under the Scheme.
Members have a right to appeal against orders determining amounts due from employers.
Nominees of deceased members have rights to the member's credit in the Fund.
Employees have the right not to have their wages or benefits reduced due to employer's contribution liability.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the Fund (5% of wages + 5% as gratuity for each employee).
Employees have a duty to contribute to the Fund (5% of their wages).
Employers have a duty not to reduce wages or benefits due to contribution liability.
The Board has a duty to administer the Fund and the Scheme.
The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Inspectors have duties to enforce the Act and the Scheme.
obligations: Obligation for employers to pay contributions accurately and on time.
Obligation for all to comply with the provisions of the Act and the Scheme.
Obligation to provide accurate information for the purpose of the Act and the Scheme.
Obligation for those found guilty of offences to undergo prescribed punishments.

key_procedures: Framing of the Scheme: The State Government frames a scheme for the welfare of toddy workers, which is published in the official Gazette. The scheme can be amended.
Constitution of the Board: The State Government constitutes the Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board via notification.

Determination of dues from employers: Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or authorized Inspector conducts inquiries to determine amounts due, with powers similar to a civil court. Employer must be heard. Appeals are allowed.
Recovery of moneys: Amounts due from employers are recovered as arrears of land revenue, with interest.
Handling offences: Offences are investigated, and penalties are applied. Court cognizance requires State Government sanction. Offences by companies are addressed specifically.
administration: The Karnataka Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, supported by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 2.10.1984 vide notification No. SWL 85 LBW 84 dated 29.9.1984.
The Board composition mandates equal representation from the State Government, employers, and employees, with specific provisions for Scheduled Caste and toddy tapper representation.
Amounts in the Fund are protected from attachment and are not liable for member's debts.
The Act aims to provide security to toddy workers who are described as among the poorest and unorganized sections of society.

title: THE KARNATAKA TRAFFIC CONTROL ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the control of traffic in highways and public places in the State of Karnataka and other matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It regulates traffic other than motor vehicle traffic on highways and public places. However, Chapter IV and its rules do not apply to areas where the Karnataka Public Conveyances Act, 1959 is in force, to the extent of corresponding provisions.

key_definitions.animal: Means any elephant, camel, horse, ass, mule, cattle, sheep or goat.
key_definitions.driver: In the case of a vehicle, the person in charge or control of the vehicle for the time being, and in the case of an animal, any person driving, leading, riding or otherwise managing or controlling the animal.
key_definitions.highway: Means any public thoroughfare whether a road, street, lane, bridlepath or a foot track, whether surfaced or unsurfaced, or whether on land owned by Government or a local authority or on land belonging to a private person over which the public have or have acquired, a right of way by usage, and includes slopes, berms, barrow pits, foot paths, pavements, side drains, bridges, culverts, causeways, carriageways, other road structures, trees, fences, posts and other highway accessories and material stacks on the thoroughfare or on land attached to the thoroughfare.
key_definitions.motor_vehicle: Means a motor vehicle as defined in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act IV of 1939).
key_definitions.public_place: Means a road, street, way or other place, whether a thoroughfare or not, to which the public have a right of access or over which they have a right to pass, and includes any place or stand at which passengers are picked up or set down by a public vehicle.
key_definitions.public_vehicle: Means any vehicle used or constructed or adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers or goods for hire or reward, other than a motor vehicle.
key_definitions.vehicle: Includes any wheeled conveyance drawn, propelled or driven by any kind of power including human, animal, motor, steam or electric power and includes any barrow, sledge, plough, drag or like vehicle, but does not include a motor vehicle.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its application to the whole of Karnataka, and provisions for its commencement by notification. It also specifies conditions for Chapter IV in areas where the Karnataka Public Conveyances Act, 1959 is in force.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'animal', 'driver', 'highway', 'motor vehicle', 'public place', 'public vehicle', and 'vehicle'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to restrict the use of vehicles
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government or an authorized authority the power to prohibit or restrict the driving of vehicles or animals in the interest of public safety or convenience, or due to the nature of a road or bridge, through notification. It mandates the placement of appropriate traffic signs.

Empowers the State Government or an authorized authority to place traffic signs to regulate traffic other than motor vehicles. It details the meanings of signs as per the First Schedule, allows for Kannada script transcriptions, prohibits unauthorized signs, and allows for the removal of misleading or obscuring signs. It also outlines duties for accidental damage to traffic signs.

Allows the State Government or an authorized authority to designate certain roads as 'main roads' for the purposes of regulations in the Second Schedule, through notification or erection of specific traffic signs.

Mandates every driver of a vehicle or animal to drive in conformity with mandatory traffic signs, the driving regulations in the Second Schedule, and directions from police officers regulating traffic.
Requires drivers of vehicles to make specified signals on occasions mentioned in the Third Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Leaving vehicle or animal in dangerous position
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person in charge of a vehicle or animal from causing it to remain at rest in a position, condition, or circumstance that causes or is likely to cause danger, obstruction, or undue inconvenience to other users of the highway or public place.
Prohibits a driver from towing a person riding a cycle and a cyclist from being towed by any other vehicle.
Prohibits any person in charge of a vehicle or animal from allowing it to stand or proceed on a highway or public place unless it is under adequate control.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of driver to stop in certain cases
main_sections.description: Requires the driver of a vehicle or animal to stop when required by a uniformed police officer or when involved in an accident with a person, animal, vehicle, or property. The driver must provide their name and address and that of the owner upon demand.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of owner of vehicle or animal to give information
main_sections.description: Obligates the owner of a vehicle or animal to provide information regarding the driver's name and address to a police officer upon demand, if accused of an offence under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of driver in case of accident and injury to person
main_sections.description: Requires the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident causing injury to a person or damage to property exceeding twenty-five rupees to secure medical attention for the injured person, convey them to a hospital if necessary, and report the incident to the nearest police station within twenty-four hours.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for control of traffic
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of Chapter II, with different rules for different areas. This includes rules for the removal and...

main_sections.section_title: General provision regarding construction and maintenance
main_sections.description: This section likely pertains to general provisions regarding the construction and maintenance of vehicles, although the detailed text is not provided here.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for construction, equipment and maintenance of vehicles
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules concerning the construction, equipment, and maintenance of vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for control of public vehicles
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for the control of public vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: General provision regarding punishment of offences
main_sections.description: This section likely deals with general provisions for the punishment of offences under the Act.
This section addresses the offence of driving a vehicle recklessly or dangerously.
This section likely outlines the power of police to arrest without a warrant under certain circumstances related to offences under this Act.
This section likely pertains to the provision for summary disposal of cases related to offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before State Legislature
main_sections.description: This section mandates that rules made under the Act must be laid before the State Legislature.
This section states that existing bye-laws will continue in force.
This section deals with the repeal of previous laws and provisions for savings.

important_rules: Drivers of vehicles or animals must conform to mandatory traffic signs and driving regulations.
Drivers must comply with directions given by police officers regulating traffic.
Drivers must stop when required by a uniformed police officer or when involved in an accident, and provide identifying information.
Drivers of vehicles involved in accidents causing injury or significant property damage must secure medical attention and report the incident to the police.
No person in charge of a vehicle or animal shall leave it in a position that causes danger or obstruction.
No driver of a vehicle shall tow a person riding a cycle, and no cyclist shall allow themselves to be towed.

penalties: Section 18 mentions 'punishment of offences', indicating penalties exist, but specific details are not fully provided in the excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers are mentioned in relation to traffic regulation and accident reporting. The State Government or authorized authorities are involved in making rules and placing traffic signs.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through police direction, adherence to traffic signs and rules, and reporting of incidents. The State Government can also make rules to carry out the Act's provisions.

rights: Right to demand name and address of the driver in case of an accident (Section 11(1)(b)).
Right to demand name and address of the driver if alleging an offence under Section 19 (Section 11(2)).
Right to receive information regarding the driver from the owner if accused of an offence (Section 12).
duties: Duty to obey traffic signs and police directions (Section 6).
Duty to stop when required by police or in case of an accident (Section 11).
Duty to provide name and address in case of accident or alleged offence (Section 11).
Duty of owner to provide driver information (Section 12).
Duty of driver in case of accident to secure medical attention and report to police (Section 13).
Duty not to leave vehicles or animals in a dangerous position (Section 8).
Duty not to leave vehicles or animals unattended (Section 10).
Duty not to tamper with traffic signs (Section 4(5)).
Duty to report accidental damage to traffic signs (Section 4(6)).
obligations: Obligation to ensure vehicles/animals are under adequate control when on a highway or public place.
Obligation to report accidents promptly to the nearest police station.
Obligation to comply with any prohibitions or restrictions on vehicle use imposed by the State Government.

key_procedures: Notification and placement of traffic signs for regulating traffic (Sections 3 & 4).
Designation of 'Main Roads' through notification or traffic signs (Section 5).
Procedure for drivers involved in accidents: stop, provide information, secure medical attention, and report to the police (Sections 11 & 13).
Procedure for owners to provide driver information upon police demand (Section 12).
administration: The State Government and authorities authorized by the State Government are responsible for the administration of this Act, including making rules, issuing notifications, and enforcing traffic control measures. Police officers are involved in the direct regulation of traffic and enforcement of certain duties.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1986 to remove the prohibition on two persons riding a bicycle.
The Act came into force on 15.8.1979.
Chapter IV and its rules do not apply to areas where the Karnataka Public Conveyances Act, 1959 is in force, to the extent of corresponding provisions.
The definition of 'vehicle' specifically excludes motor vehicles, indicating a focus on other forms of transport like cycles and animal-drawn conveyances.

title: The Karnataka Treasure Trove Act, 1962
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to treasure trove in the State of Karnataka, ensuring a uniform law across different areas of the state that previously had varying legislation.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to any treasure, defined as anything of any value hidden in the soil or in anything affixed thereto. It governs the finding, reporting, inquiry, declaration, and disposal of such treasures.

key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: An officer appointed by the State Government to perform functions under this Act, or the District Deputy Commissioner if no such officer is appointed.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of Archaeology in Karnataka or any officer authorized by the State Government.
key_definitions.finder: In cases of work done under direction, the person directing the work; otherwise, the person who finds the treasure.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.owner: Includes a person entitled to treasure in land or affixed to land; if land is Government property, the Government is the owner.
key_definitions.prescribed: As prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.treasure: Anything of any value hidden in the soil or in anything affixed thereto.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Karnataka Treasure Trove Act, 1962, and states that it extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including Deputy Commissioner, Director, finder, notification, owner, prescribed, and treasure.

main_sections.section_title: Notice to Deputy Commissioner of finding of treasure
main_sections.description: Mandates that the finder of treasure exceeding ten rupees in value must provide written notice to the Deputy Commissioner regarding its nature, value, place, circumstances, and date of finding, and deposit the treasure or provide security. The owner and occupier of the place also have notice obligations.

Outlines the steps the Deputy Commissioner must take upon receiving notice of treasure, including reporting to the State Government and Director, publishing a notification calling for claimants, and serving notice on the owner and occupier.
States that any person claiming a right to the treasure who fails to appear as required by the notification shall forfeit that right.
Details the inquiry process where the Deputy Commissioner determines who found the treasure, where, under what circumstances, and who likely hid it and when.

main_sections.section_title: Suit by person claiming the treasure in certain cases
main_sections.description: Allows the Deputy Commissioner to adjourn proceedings to enable a claimant to establish their right in a Civil Court if the treasure appears to have been hidden within 100 years by a person who is claiming it or under whom they claim. It also provides for a reward to the finder payable by the claimant.

main_sections.section_title: Treasure to be declared ownerless in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which the Deputy Commissioner may declare treasure ownerless: if it's unlikely to have been hidden within 100 years, if no suit is filed when required, or if a suit is filed but the claim is rejected. It also outlines the reporting process and the right to appeal to the Karnataka Revenue Appellate Tribunal.
States that once treasure is declared ownerless, it will be disposed of according to the provisions of Chapter III.

main_sections.section_title: When no other person claims as owner of place, treasure to be given to finder
main_sections.description: If treasure is declared ownerless and no one other than the finder claims it as the owner of the place where it was found, the treasure is delivered to the finder.

main_sections.section_title: When only one such person claims, and his claim is not disputed, treasure to be divided
main_sections.description: If treasure is declared ownerless and only one person other than the finder claims ownership of the place, and this claim is undisputed, the treasure is divided. If an agreement exists, it's followed; otherwise, it's typically split equally, with the finder's share not exceeding one lakh rupees unless otherwise agreed. The Deputy Commissioner can allot the whole treasure to one party upon payment of compensation to the other or sell it and divide proceeds.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of proceedings when ownership of place where treasure was found is in dispute
main_sections.description: Provides for staying proceedings if the ownership of the place where the treasure was found is in dispute.

main_sections.section_title: Settlement of dispute and division of treasure
main_sections.description: Deals with the settlement of disputes regarding ownership and the subsequent division of treasure.

main_sections.section_title: Division when value of treasure exceeds one lakh
main_sections.description: Addresses the division of treasure when its value exceeds one lakh rupees, likely involving specific procedures or limitations.

main_sections.section_title: Power to acquire the treasure on behalf of Government
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to acquire the treasure on behalf of the Government, upon payment of its value plus an additional one-fifth of that value.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of Deputy Commissioner final and no suit to lie against him for acts done bona fide
main_sections.description: Declares the Deputy Commissioner's decisions final and protects them from suits for acts done in good faith.

main_sections.section_title: Deputy Commissioner to exercise powers of Civil Court
main_sections.description: Empowers the Deputy Commissioner to exercise the powers of a Civil Court in carrying out their functions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on finder, failing to give notice, etc.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for finders who fail to give notice or comply with other provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on owner abetting offences under section 18
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties on owners who abet offenses related to failing to give notice or other violations under section 18.
Confers the power to make rules upon the State Government for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws on treasure trove and savings provisions.

important_rules: Any treasure exceeding ten rupees in value must be reported to the Deputy Commissioner by the finder, owner, and occupier.
The finder must deposit the treasure or provide security.
Claimants to treasure must appear when notified; failure to do so results in forfeiture of rights.
If treasure was hidden within 100 years, a claimant may need to establish their right in a Civil Court.
If treasure is declared ownerless, it is generally given to the finder, or divided between the finder and the owner of the place.
The State Government has the power to acquire treasure on behalf of the Government.

penalties: Penalty on finder failing to give notice or comply with provisions (Section 18).
Penalty on owner abetting offenses under Section 18 (Section 19).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner, with oversight and potential intervention by the State Government and appeal to the Karnataka Revenue Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, notifications, court referrals, declarations of ownership, and imposition of penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right of a finder to the treasure if no other claimant appears or if the owner of the place does not claim it.
Right to a share of the treasure for the owner of the place where it was found, if they claim it and it's undisputed.
Right to establish a claim to treasure in a Civil Court if it appears to have been hidden within 100 years.
Right of appeal against a declaration of ownerless treasure.
duties: Duty of the finder to give immediate written notice to the Deputy Commissioner about found treasure.
Duty of the owner and occupier of the place to give notice about found treasure.
Duty to appear when required by a notification issued by the Deputy Commissioner.
Duty of a claimant to institute a suit in Civil Court if required by the Deputy Commissioner.
obligations: Obligation to deposit the treasure or provide security as required by the Deputy Commissioner.
Obligation to adhere to the division of treasure as determined by the Deputy Commissioner or as agreed upon by parties.
Obligation to pay the finder a reward if a claimant establishes their right in a Civil Court.
Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act.

key_procedures: Reporting of Treasure: Finder, owner, and occupier must report treasure exceeding ten rupees in value to the Deputy Commissioner.
Deputy Commissioner's Inquiry and Notification: The Deputy Commissioner reports to higher authorities, publishes a notification, and calls for claimants.
Claimant Appearance and Suit: Claimants must appear; if treasure was hidden recently, they may need to file a suit in Civil Court.
Declaration of Ownerless Treasure: If no valid claim is established or if conditions are met, the Deputy Commissioner can declare the treasure ownerless.
Disposal of Ownerless Treasure: The treasure is given to the finder or divided between the finder and the owner of the place, subject to conditions and value limits.
administration: The State Government and the Deputy Commissioner are primarily responsible for the administration of the Act. The Director of Archaeology also plays a role. Rules are made by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to create a unified law for treasure trove across the entire State of Karnataka, replacing disparate laws from previous regions.
The value of treasure must exceed ten rupees to trigger the reporting requirements.
A key distinction is made between treasure hidden within 100 years and that hidden earlier, impacting ownership claims.
The State Government has a preemptive right to acquire any treasure found.

title: THE KARNATAKA URBAN WATER SUPPLY AND DRAINAGE BOARD ACT, 1973
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Water Supply and Drainage Board and the regulation and development of drinking water and drainage facilities in the urban areas of the State of Karnataka, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka other than the City of Bangalore. It applies to urban areas within the jurisdiction of local authorities. The subject matter scope covers the investigation, preparation, execution, operation, and maintenance of water supply and drainage schemes.

key_definitions.Board: The Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.building: A house, out-house, stable, latrine, urinal, shed, hut or any other structure, whether of masonry, bricks, wood, mud, metal or other material, but does not include any portable shelter.
key_definitions.drain: Includes sewer, tunnel, a culvert, a ditch, a channel and any other device for carrying off sewage, offensive matter, polluted water, waste water, rain water or sub-soil water.
key_definitions.drainage: The device for carrying off sewage, offensive matter, polluted water, waste water, rain water, or sub-soil water.
key_definitions.local authority: A municipal corporation, a municipal council, a sanitary board or a notified area committee constituted or continued under any law for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka except Bangalore City), and the commencement date.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'building', 'drain', 'drainage', 'local authority', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Creation and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: This section likely deals with the legal creation and incorporation of the Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board.
This section outlines the composition of the Board, including the number and types of directors.
This section details the primary functions of the Board related to water supply and drainage in urban areas.
This section pertains to the financial aspects of investigating water supply and drainage schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation of draft schemes by the Board
main_sections.description: This section describes the process by which the Board prepares draft schemes for water supply and drainage.

main_sections.section_title: Approval of the scheme by the Government
main_sections.description: This section outlines the procedure for obtaining government approval for the schemes prepared by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Execution of approved scheme by the Board
main_sections.description: This section deals with the implementation and execution of approved water supply and drainage schemes by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of the cost of the scheme
main_sections.description: This section details how the costs incurred by the Board for executing schemes are to be recovered.
This section describes the sources and management of the Board's financial funds.
This section lays down the requirements for maintaining accounts and conducting audits of the Board's financial transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of the provisions of the Act
main_sections.description: This section specifies the penalties that can be imposed for violating the provisions of the Act.
This section grants the government the power to frame rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
This section empowers the Board to create its own regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

important_rules: Rule: Schemes must be prepared, approved by the government, and then executed by the Board.
Rule: The cost of executed schemes is recoverable by the Board.
Rule: The Board is responsible for the operation and maintenance of water supply and drainage schemes.
Rule: The Board has the power to levy rates to cover the cost of water supply and maintenance.
Rule: Accounts of the Board must be maintained and audited.
Rule: Penalties are prescribed for breaches of the Act's provisions.

penalties: Penalty for obstructing contractors or removing marks (Section 45).
Penalty for breach of the provisions of the Act (Section 46).
Joint and several liability of owners and occupiers for offences related to water supply (Section 44A).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board, with oversight from the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and trial of offences, imposition of penalties, and actions outlined in various sections including those for non-compliance with notices.

rights: Right of the Board to prepare, execute, and maintain water supply and drainage schemes.
Right of the Board to recover costs of schemes and levy rates.
Power of entry onto premises by authorized persons (Section 63).
Right of user of conduits, lines etc. (Section 55B).
duties: Duty of the Board to regulate and develop drinking water and drainage facilities in urban areas.
Duty of local authorities to provide adequate facilities to the Board (Section 27).
Duty of police officers to assist in carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 54).
obligations: Obligation of the Board to manage its funds and accounts properly.
Obligation of the Board to submit annual reports, statistics, and returns.
Obligation to comply with orders and directions issued by the State Government.
Obligation for licensed plumbers to perform work according to the Act (Section 28F).

key_procedures: Scheme preparation and approval: Investigation -> Draft scheme preparation -> Government approval -> Publication of approval -> Execution.
Recovery of dues: Mode of recovery as prescribed by the Act (Section 60).
Service of notices: Procedures for serving bills, demand notices, and other notices (Sections 66D, 66E).
Handling of offences: Prosecution, trial, and arrest of offenders (Sections 47, 48).
administration: The Karnataka Urban Water Supply and Drainage Board, administered by its Chairman, Managing Director, Directors, and other officers. The State Government also plays a significant role in oversight and direction.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to the City of Bangalore.
Different commencement dates can be appointed for different areas.
The Board's power to appoint staff is subject to government approval for certain key posts.
The Board is considered a local authority for the purposes of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the Indian Works of Defence Act, 1903.
Provisions exist for the Board to write off irrecoverable amounts (Section 43).
The Act specifies that actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected (Section 64).

title: The Karnataka Village Offices Abolition Act, 1961
purpose: To abolish hereditary village offices and their emoluments in the State of Karnataka, and to provide for consequential and incidental matters, with the objective of modernizing revenue administration and eliminating relics of the old feudal system.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to all hereditary village offices and associated emoluments that existed before the commencement of the Constitution.

key_definitions.appointed_date: The date appointed by the State Government for the commencement of the Act.
key_definitions.authorised_holder: A person to whom land associated with a village office has been validly alienated permanently (sale, gift, partition, etc.) under existing laws.
key_definitions.code: Refers to the relevant Land Revenue Code or equivalent law for different areas of the state (Mysore, Belgaum, Gulbarga, Coorg, Madras).
key_definitions.deputy_commissioner: An officer appointed by the State Government to perform functions and exercise powers under the Act, or the District Deputy Commissioner if no specific officer is appointed.
key_definitions.emoluments: Includes lands, assignments of revenue, fees in money or produce, money salaries, and other remuneration granted or continued in respect of a village office by the State.
key_definitions.enfranchised_inam: An inam with proof of enfranchisement as per the Madras Enfranchised Inams Act, 1862.
key_definitions.existing_law_relating_to_a_village_offic: Includes any enactment, ordinance, rule, etc., relating to a village office in force before the appointed date.
key_definitions.holder_of_a_village_office: A person having an interest in a village office under existing law. If held by a group, the whole group is considered the holder.
key_definitions.inferior_village_office: Any village office of a lower degree than that of a Patel or Village Accountant.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.officiator: The person actually performing the duties of a village office, whether or not they have the right to do so.
key_definitions.prescribed: As prescribed by rules made under the Act.
key_definitions.tenancy_law: Refers to the relevant tenancy law for different areas of the state (Mysore, Bombay, Hyderabad, Madras, Coorg).
key_definitions.unauthorised_holder: A person in possession of land associated with a village office without right, or under a void alienation under existing law.
key_definitions.village_office: Every village office with emoluments attached, held hereditarily before the commencement of the Constitution, for duties related to administration, revenue collection, order maintenance, boundary settlement, or other civil administration of a village.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of Karnataka, and empowers the State Government to appoint a date for its commencement.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed date', 'authorised holder', 'Code', 'Deputy Commissioner', 'emoluments', 'enfranchised inam', 'existing law relating to a village office', 'holder of a village office', 'inferior village office', 'notification', 'officiator', 'prescribed', 'tenancy law', 'unauthorised holder', and 'village office'.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Deputy Commissioner to decide certain questions and appeals
main_sections.description: Empowers the Deputy Commissioner to decide questions such as whether land was granted or continued in respect of a village office, and whether a person is a holder of a village office. It also provides for appeals against the Deputy Commissioner's decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of village offices together with incidents thereof
main_sections.description: Provides for the abolition of all hereditary village offices and their associated emoluments.

main_sections.section_title: Re-grant of land resumed under section 4 to the holder of the village office
main_sections.description: Deals with the re-grant of lands resumed under Section 4 to the holders of the village offices.

main_sections.section_title: Re-grant of land resumed under section 4 to authorised holders
main_sections.description: Provides for the re-grant of resumed lands to authorised holders.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of unauthorised holder and re-grant to him in certain circumstances of land resumed section 4
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for eviction of unauthorised holders and the circumstances under which resumed lands can be re-granted to them.
Imposes restrictions on the transfer of re-granted lands.
Specifies the application of tenancy laws in relation to lands affected by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Relief to holder of a village office
main_sections.description: Provides for relief to holders of village offices.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiries and proceedings to be judicial proceedings
main_sections.description: Declares that inquiries and proceedings under the Act are to be considered judicial proceedings.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing laws inconsistent with the Act and includes provisions for savings.

important_rules: Lands granted or continued in respect of hereditary village offices are liable to land revenue after abolition of the offices.
Resumed lands are to be re-granted to the original holders of the village office.
Restrictions are placed on the transfer of re-granted lands for a specified period.
Inquiries and proceedings under the Act are deemed judicial proceedings.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (through Deputy Commissioner and other appointed officers)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, decisions, orders, eviction, re-grant of lands, and application of tenancy laws as specified in the Act and rules made thereunder.

rights: Right to have questions regarding land grants and holder status decided by the Deputy Commissioner.
Right to re-grant of resumed land under certain conditions.
Right to relief for holders of village offices.
Right to appeal against Deputy Commissioner's orders.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding abolition of village offices and re-grant of lands.
Duty of unauthorised holders to vacate lands.
Duty to adhere to restrictions on transfer of re-granted lands.
obligations: Obligation to pay land revenue on lands resumed and re-granted.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for applications and appeals.

key_procedures: Decision of questions and appeals by the Deputy Commissioner (Section 3).
Abolition of village offices and resumption of lands (Section 4).
Re-grant of resumed lands to holders or authorised holders (Sections 5 & 6).
Eviction of unauthorised holders and potential re-grant (Section 7).
Application for relief by village office holders (Section 9).
Framing of rules by the State Government (Section 11).
administration: The State Government, through the Deputy Commissioner and other officers appointed under the Act, is responsible for the administration of the Act.
important_notes: The Act was amended multiple times to address issues like extending time limits for relief applications, voiding certain transfers of re-granted lands, mitigating restrictions on enfranchised inam lands, and clarifying provisions for crop loans.
The Act came into force on 1st February 1963.

title: THE KARNATAKA WAREHOUSES ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the regulation and licensing of warehouses in the State of Karnataka, encouraging the establishment of independent warehouses and making provision for their supervision and control.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to persons carrying on the business of warehousing and to goods stored in licensed warehouses. It does not apply to cloak rooms attached to hotels, railway stations, premises of other public carriers, and the like.

key_definitions.cooperative_society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959.
key_definitions.depositor: A person who tenders goods to the warehouseman for storing, including any person who lawfully holds the receipt issued by the warehouseman and derives title thereto by proper endorsement or transfer.
key_definitions.goods: Any of the articles specified in the schedule to the Act.
key_definitions.licensed_warehouse: A warehouse licensed under this Act.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.person: Includes any company, association, or body corporate.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed_authority: The authority prescribed by rules to carry out a specific provision of this Act.
key_definitions.receipt: A warehouse receipt in the prescribed form issued by a warehouseman to a person depositing goods.
key_definitions.rules: Rules made by the State Government under this Act.
key_definitions.warehouse: Any building, structure, or other protected enclosure used for storing goods on behalf of depositors, excluding cloak rooms and premises of public carriers.
key_definitions.warehouseman: A person who has obtained a license under this Act in respect of their warehouse.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the commencement date to be appointed by the State Government.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'co-operative society', 'depositor', 'goods', 'licensed warehouse', 'notification', 'person', 'prescribed', 'prescribed authority', 'receipt', 'rules', 'warehouse', and 'warehouseman'.
Prohibits carrying on the business of warehousing without a license granted under the Act and compliance with its terms and conditions.
Details the process for applying for and granting a warehouse license, requiring applications in the prescribed form to the prescribed authority and payment of prescribed fees.

Outlines the conditions the prescribed authority must be satisfied with before granting a license, including suitability of the warehouse, applicant's competence, fulfillment of notified conditions, payment of fees, and furnishing of security (with an exemption for certain corporations).
Specifies that licenses are valid for a prescribed period and can be renewed upon application, payment of fees, and continued fulfillment of conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of refusal to grant or renew licence
main_sections.description: Requires the prescribed authority to record and communicate written reasons for refusing to grant or renew a license to the applicant.

Lists grounds upon which a license can be suspended or cancelled, including insolvency, relinquishing control, ceasing business, unreasonable charges, incompetence, or contravention of the Act or license terms.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of suspension and cancellation of licence
main_sections.description: Mandates that the prescribed authority give notice to the warehouseman of the grounds for proposed suspension or cancellation and provide an opportunity to show cause before making an order.
Requires warehousemen to return their license to the prescribed authority upon expiration, suspension, or cancellation, allowing a reasonable time to wind up business.
Provides for the issuance of a duplicate license upon application and payment of fees if the original is lost, destroyed, or defaced, with the duplicate clearly stamped.

main_sections.section_title: Reasonable care of the goods deposited to be taken
main_sections.description: Obligates warehousemen to take the same care of deposited goods as a man of ordinary prudence would take of his own goods.

main_sections.section_title: Precautions against damage or injury to goods
main_sections.description: Requires warehousemen to maintain clean premises, take precautions against pests, and not accept goods likely to damage other stored goods.
Mandates that goods of different depositors be kept separate, unless they are standardized and graded goods that can be pooled, to ensure easy identification and delivery.

main_sections.section_title: Goods deteriorating in warehouse and their disposal
main_sections.description: Details procedures for notifying depositors of deteriorating goods, and their subsequent removal and sale by public auction if not taken delivery of promptly.
Requires warehousemen to deliver goods without unnecessary delay to the depositor upon demand, surrender of the receipt, and payment of charges, and allows for partial delivery subject to agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of warehouseman for shortage or excess in goods stored
main_sections.description: Specifies that warehousemen are not entitled to excess goods from moisture absorption and are not responsible for shortages due to dryage or other causes beyond their control. Disputes regarding causes are to be referred to the appellate authority.
Empowers inspection of warehouses.

main_sections.section_title: Weighers, samplers and graders to obtain licences
main_sections.description: Requires weighers, samplers, and graders to obtain licenses.
Requires the issuance of a receipt for deposited goods.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain warehouses
main_sections.description: Indicates that the Act may not apply to specific types of warehouses as notified by the government.
Deals with the repeal of previous laws and provides for savings.

important_rules: Warehousemen must take reasonable care of deposited goods, equivalent to that of an ordinary prudent person towards their own goods.
Warehousemen must maintain their warehouse clean, free from damp and pests, and prevent storage of goods that could damage others.
Goods of different depositors must be kept separate for easy identification and delivery, except for standardized and graded goods that can be pooled.
Warehousemen must notify depositors of deteriorating goods and, if not taken delivery of, may remove and sell them by public auction.
Warehousemen must deliver goods on demand upon surrender of the receipt and payment of charges, allowing partial delivery as agreed.
Warehousemen are not liable for excess goods due to moisture absorption or shortages due to dryage or causes beyond their control.
Receipts for deposited goods must be issued by warehousemen in the prescribed form.
Weighers, samplers, and graders operating in warehouses must obtain licenses.
Warehousemen and depositors must comply with the provisions of the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944, and related rules/notifications for goods deposited in a warehouse.

penalties: Penalty for carrying on the business of warehousing without a license.
Penalties for contravention of any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder, as specified in Section 33.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority, as defined in Section 2(h).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of licensing, inspection, suspension/cancellation of licenses, imposition of penalties, and by the State Government making rules.

rights: Depositors have the right to receive their goods upon demand, surrender of receipt, and payment of charges.
Depositors have the right to take partial delivery of goods as per agreement.
Depositors can inform the warehouseman of their interest in the goods and request intimation regarding their condition.
Applicants have the right to receive written reasons if a license is refused.
Licensees have the right to show cause against proposed suspension or cancellation of their license.
duties: Warehousemen have a duty to take reasonable care of deposited goods.
Warehousemen have a duty to keep warehouses clean and free from pests.
Warehousemen have a duty to preserve the identity of goods.
Warehousemen have a duty to issue receipts for deposited goods.
Warehousemen have a duty to deliver goods promptly upon demand.
Warehousemen have a duty to comply with the terms of the license and the Act.
Depositors have a duty to surrender the receipt and pay all charges due.
Warehousemen and depositors have a duty to comply with the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944, regarding deposited goods.
obligations: Every person must obtain a license to carry on the business of warehousing.
Warehousemen are obligated to fulfill the conditions for grant and renewal of licenses.
Warehousemen are obligated to take all necessary precautions against damage or injury to goods.
Warehousemen are obligated to notify depositors of deteriorating goods and take action as per Section 15.
Warehousemen are obligated to return licenses upon expiry or cancellation.
Warehousemen and depositors are obligated to comply with the provisions of the Central Act 1 of 1944.

key_procedures: Application for and grant of a warehouse license, including satisfying conditions related to warehouse suitability, applicant competence, fees, and security.
Procedure for suspension or cancellation of a license, involving notice to the warehouseman and an opportunity to show cause.
Procedure for delivery of goods, requiring depositor demand, receipt surrender, and payment of charges.
Procedure for handling deteriorating goods, including notification to the depositor and potential sale by public auction.
Procedure for obtaining a duplicate license if the original is lost or defaced.
administration: The State Government, through the 'prescribed authority' appointed by rules.
important_notes: The Act has been adapted by the Karnataka Adaptations of Laws Order, 1973.
The Act came into force with effect from 01.09.1969 by notification.
The Act aims to bring uniform law in integrated areas of new Mysore for establishment, supervision, and control of independent warehouses.
Section 32A was added by Amendment Act 22 of 1965 to clarify the obligation of warehousemen and depositors to comply with the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944.

title: The Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1998
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the Mysore Palace and its surrounding open space in the public interest, for its preservation, and for matters connected therewith, including its development as a museum and horticultural garden, and to maintain its public character and historical significance.
scope: The Act applies to the Mysore Palace, its immediate surroundings including open space, park, and garden, the Royal Treasure (including Royal Thrones, Royal Crowns, Howdah, Royal Wears, ornaments, pieces of art, regalia, paintings, sculptures, and furniture), and all other movable and immovable property belonging to or found in the Palace. It also covers buildings, temples, and other places of worship within the premises.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The date appointed by the State Government through notification under sub-section (2) of Section 1.
key_definitions.mysore_palace: The Palace of Mysore and the surrounding vacant land more fully described in Schedule I, including buildings, temples, places of worship, the Royal Treasure, Royal Thrones, Royal Crowns, the Howdah, Royal Wears and ornaments, all other pieces of art, regalia, paintings, sculptures, furniture, and all other movable or immovable property belonging to or found in the Palace, excluding items of movables left with the legal representatives or heirs at the time of transfer of charge in 1976.
key_definitions.board: The Board of Trustees constituted under Section 24.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under Section 15.
key_definitions.legal_representatives_and_heirs: The legal representatives and heirs of the late Sri Jayachamarajendra Wadeyar, former Maharaja of Mysore, including their successors in interest.
key_definitions.transferee: A person to whom any movable or immovable property related to the Palace has been alienated by the legal representatives or heirs by way of sale, gift, mortgage, lease, or otherwise on or after April 21, 1998.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1998' and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification, allowing for different dates for different provisions.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Mysore Palace', 'Board', 'Commissioner', 'legal representatives', 'heirs', 'schedule', 'specified date', 'transferee', and 'year'.

Declares that the Act's provisions are enacted in pursuance of Article 31C of the Constitution of India to give effect to the State's policy towards securing the principles specified in clause (b) of Article 39 of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of the palace in the State Government
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the Mysore Palace, along with the right, title, and interest of the legal representatives, heirs, and transferees, shall be transferred to and vest absolutely in the State Government.

Details the implications of the vesting, including the inclusion of all assets, rights, leaseholds, powers, authorities, privileges, and properties (movable and immovable, including treasures, art, etc.) that were in the possession or control of the legal representatives, heirs, or transferees. It also states that vested properties are freed from trusts, encumbrances, and any court orders restricting their use. It outlines the right to prefer claims before the Commissioner and the obligation to intimate mortgages, leases, charges, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Right of prince to live in portion of the palace, etc.
main_sections.description: Permits Sri Srikantadatta Narasimaraja Wadeyar and his wife to reside in a portion of the palace, with provisions for them to move out and receive alternative compensation (land and money).
Deals with the management of the Palace.
Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments.
Establishes the Board of Trustees.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over other laws, contracts, etc., unless otherwise specified.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Abatement of proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894
main_sections.description: Provides for the abatement of any proceedings that were initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the acquisition of the Palace and its surroundings.

important_rules: The Mysore Palace and its surrounding properties are to be transferred to and vest absolutely in the State Government on the appointed day.
All assets, rights, and properties of the Mysore Palace, including treasures and art, vest in the State Government and are freed from encumbrances.
Legal representatives, heirs, or transferees with rights in the Palace can claim compensation before the Commissioner of Payments.
The State Government will provide a specified amount (Rs. 32 crores mentioned in the Objects and Reasons) to legal representatives, heirs, or transferees.
Sri Srikantadatta Narasimaraja Wadeyar and his wife have the right to reside in a portion of the palace.
A Board of Trustees will be constituted for the management of the Palace.
A Commissioner of Payments will be appointed to receive and disburse claims related to the acquisition.
The Act has an overriding effect on other laws and contracts, unless specifically exempted.
Penalties are prescribed for contravening the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act (Section 37).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Board of Trustees, Commissioner of Payments, and Executive Officer (as per various sections related to management, claims, and administration).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a Commissioner, constitution of a Board of Trustees, appointment of an Executive Officer and other officers, making rules, imposing penalties for contravention, and through legal proceedings.

rights: Right of legal representatives, heirs, or transferees to prefer claims for payment before the Commissioner (Section 5(3)).
Right of Sri Srikantadatta Narasimaraja Wadeyar and his wife to live in a portion of the palace (Section 10).
Rights of devotees to perform rituals and customary religious practices at temples within the palace premises.
Rights of legal representatives and heirs to worship the deity located within the palace premises.
duties: Duty of persons in charge of management of the Palace (Section 12).
Duty of persons to account for assets in their possession (Section 13).
Duty to intimate mortgages, leases, charges, liens, or other interests to the Commissioner within the prescribed time and manner (Section 5(4)).
obligations: Obligation to transfer and vest the Mysore Palace in the State Government.
Obligations related to the management and preservation of the Palace and its contents.
Obligations of the Commissioner of Payments regarding the settlement of claims and disbursement of amounts.
Obligations of the Board of Trustees in managing the Palace.

key_procedures: Acquisition and vesting of the Mysore Palace in the State Government on the appointed day (Chapter II).
Claiming compensation by legal representatives, heirs, or transferees before the Commissioner of Payments (Chapter IV).
Examination and admission or rejection of claims by the Commissioner (Chapter IV).
Disbursement of amounts by the Commissioner (Chapter IV).
Constitution and functioning of the Board of Trustees for management (Chapter VI).
Appointment and duties of the Executive Officer and other officers (Chapter VI).
Making and enforcing rules by the State Government (Section 41).
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, with specific roles assigned to the Board of Trustees (constituted under the Act) and the Commissioner of Payments (appointed under the Act). The Executive Officer and other officers are also appointed for day-to-day administration.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions prevail over conflicting provisions in other laws or agreements, except where explicitly stated.
Proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, related to the acquisition of the Mysore Palace and its surroundings are abated.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.
The Act provides for the removal of difficulties by the State Government.
The Board of Trustees has the power to ratify contracts to ensure their continuation.

title: THE MYSORE (RELIGIOUS AND CHARITABLE) INAMS ABOLITION (KARNATAKA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1984
purpose: To amend the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition Act, 1955, to restore the provisions related to the payment of tasdik allowance as they existed prior to the amendment by the Karnataka Inams Abolition Laws (Amendment) Act, 1979, and to re-establish the mechanism for determining the basic annual sum for religious and charitable institutions.
scope: This Act amends the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition Act, 1955. It applies to religious and charitable inams within the state of Karnataka. Specifically, it concerns the calculation and payment of compensation (tasdik allowance) to inamdars (religious institutions) for rights vested in the State.

key_definitions.inamdar: Refers to a religious or charitable institution that holds an inam.
key_definitions.basic annual sum: The amount determined as compensation for the inamdar's rights vested in the State, calculated based on the net average annual income derived from the inam lands.
key_definitions.tasdik allowance: An allowance paid to religious or charitable institutions, which in this context is equivalent to the basic annual sum.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Mysore (Religious and Charitable) Inams Abolition (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 1984. Specifies that this section and section 8 come into force immediately, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on May 1, 1979.

Inserts new sections into the principal Act detailing the determination of the 'basic annual sum', its component parts (including net annual income from lands, excluding certain forest and mineral rights unless expressly conferred), and the deductions to be made (jodi, quit-rent, remuneration to village officers, maintenance of irrigation works, and management costs).
Amends Section 19 of the principal Act to substitute the original provision for calculating compensation with 'the basic annual sum as a tasdik allowance'.
Inserts a new section giving the Deputy Commissioner the power and responsibility to determine the basic annual sum, outlining procedures for applicants to obtain data and make representations.
Amends Section 28 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'amount' with 'tasdik allowance' in subsection (2).
Amends Section 29 of the principal Act to include references to the new section 21 and 'prescribed authority' for determining if buildings or lands fall within specific scopes.

Amends Section 30 of the principal Act by inserting a new subsection (2) authorizing the Deputy Commissioner to delegate inquiry powers to officers not below the rank of Tahasildar, with provisions for review of such inquiries.

Provides for the revival and disposal of applications and appeals that were pending or had abated due to the Karnataka Inams Abolition Laws (Amendment) Act, 1979, and specifies timeframes for preferring appeals against Deputy Commissioner's decisions under section 21 that were prevented by the 1979 amendment.

important_rules: The 'basic annual sum' is to be determined for each inam.

The basic annual sum is calculated as the aggregate of the average net annual income derived from inam lands over five years preceding vesting, with specific exclusions for income from sandalwood, reserved forest produce, royalty on minerals, and ferries unless expressly conferred and recognized by competent authority.

Deductions from the aggregate income include Jodi, quit-rent, annual remuneration to village officers, average annual cost of maintenance of irrigation works, and average annual cost of management incurred by the inamdar.
The Deputy Commissioner is responsible for determining the basic annual sum, and must provide data and an opportunity for representation to interested parties.
The payment to religious or charitable institutions is to be 'the basic annual sum as a tasdik allowance'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner (and authorized officers of the rank of Tahasildar)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the determination and payment of the basic annual sum, and through the prescribed authority for matters concerning buildings and lands under specific sections. The State Government has powers of review over basic annual sum determinations (as per the 2005 Amendment Act).

rights: Right of inamdars to receive a tasdik allowance (basic annual sum) for vested rights.
Right of inamdars or interested persons to obtain data and make representations regarding the determination of the basic annual sum.
Right to appeal decisions related to the basic annual sum.
duties: Duty of the Deputy Commissioner to determine the basic annual sum and to provide due process.
Duty of the State Government to establish provisions for review of basic annual sum determinations (as per the 2005 Amendment Act).
obligations: Inamdars are subject to the deductions specified in section 18 when calculating the basic annual sum.
Inamdars must permit fresh or further inquiries if directed by the Deputy Commissioner.

key_procedures: Determination of the basic annual sum by the Deputy Commissioner, involving calculation of average net annual income and deductions.
Application by interested parties for data and opportunity to make representations before the Deputy Commissioner passes an order.
Communication of the Deputy Commissioner's order to concerned inamdars and applicants.

Review of basic annual sum determinations by the State Government (as per the 2005 Amendment Act), including giving an opportunity to be heard and adjusting excess payments or recovering them as arrears of land revenue.
Referral of questions regarding the scope of certain buildings or lands to the prescribed authority.
administration: Department of Revenue, Government of Karnataka (implied through the roles of Deputy Commissioner and Tahasildar, and the context of land revenue).
important_notes: The Act retroactively restores provisions to May 1, 1979, to address the financial impact of a previous amendment.
Income from sandalwood, reserved forest produce, minerals, and ferries are excluded from the basic annual sum calculation unless rights were expressly conferred and recognized.
The 2005 Amendment Act introduces a provision for the State Government to review and revise the basic annual sum determination made by the Divisional Commissioner.

title: THE MYSORE STATE LEGISLATURE PROCEEDINGS (PROTECTION OF PUBLICATION) ACT, 1968
purpose: To protect the publication of reports of proceedings of the Mysore State Legislature.
scope: This act applies to the whole of the State of Mysore. It covers the publication of reports of proceedings of either House of the Mysore State Legislature in newspapers and the broadcasting of such proceedings by wireless telegraphy.

key_definitions.newspaper: Any printed periodical work containing public news or comments on public news, and includes a news-agency supplying material for publication in a newspaper.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Mysore State Legislature Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act, 1968, and declares that it extends to the whole of the State of Mysore.
Defines the term 'newspaper' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of reports of Mysore State Legislature proceedings Privileged.
main_sections.description: Provides that a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of the Mysore State Legislature published in a newspaper is privileged and the publisher is not liable to civil or criminal proceedings, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice. It also states that this protection does not extend to the publication of matters not for the public good.

main_sections.section_title: Act also to apply to Mysore State Legislature proceedings broadcast by wireless telegraphy.
