main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Act to reports or matters broadcast by means of wireless telegraphy as part of any programme or service provided by a broadcasting station situated within the State of Mysore, applying it in the same way as it applies to newspaper publications.

important_rules: Rule 1: Publication of substantially true reports of Mysore State Legislature proceedings in a newspaper is privileged.
Rule 2: The publisher of a privileged report is not liable to civil or criminal proceedings unless malice is proven.
Rule 3: The protection does not apply to the publication of matters that are not for the public good.
Rule 4: The Act's provisions also apply to reports or matters broadcast by wireless telegraphy from within the State of Mysore.

penalties: If the publication of a report of proceedings is proven to be made with malice, the publisher can be held liable to civil or criminal proceedings.
Publication of matters not for the public good is not protected under this Act and may be subject to legal proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts (civil and criminal)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through civil or criminal proceedings initiated against publishers in courts.

rights: Right to publish substantially true reports of Mysore State Legislature proceedings without fear of civil or criminal liability, provided there is no malice and the publication is for the public good.
duties: Duty to ensure that published reports of proceedings are substantially true.
Duty to ensure that the publication is for the public good.
obligations: Obligation not to publish reports with malice.
Obligation not to publish matters that are not for the public good.

key_procedures: When a report of Mysore State Legislature proceedings is published in a newspaper or broadcast by wireless telegraphy: The act grants privilege unless malice is proven or the publication is not for the public good. If these conditions are met, civil or criminal proceedings can be initiated in court against the publisher.
For broadcasting: The same protections and liabilities apply as for newspaper publications, provided the broadcasting station is within the State of Mysore.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely falls under the purview of the Law Department or Home Department of the State Government.
important_notes: The protection is conditional upon the report being 'substantially true'.
The protection is lost if the publication is made 'with malice'.
The protection does not cover publications that are 'not for the public good'.

title: The Mythic Society (Dissolution and Management) Act, 1976
purpose: To dissolve the Mythic Society, Bangalore, which was registered under the Societies Registration Act and founded for promoting study and research in Indology, Archaeology, Anthropology, Architecture, Art, Ethnology, and allied subjects, and to provide for its management through a newly established Board of Management due to mismanagement and alienation of its properties.
scope: This Act applies to the Mythic Society, Bangalore, and its properties, and its provisions are enforced within the State of Karnataka. It governs the dissolution of the Society and the establishment and management of a Board to carry out its original objectives.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Board: The Board of Management of the Mythic Society established under this Act.
key_definitions.Chairman: The Chairman of the Board of Management.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Board of Management.
key_definitions.Secretary: The Secretary of the Board of Management.
key_definitions.Society: The Mythic Society, Bangalore, with its head office at Nrupathunga Road, Bangalore, deemed to be registered under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Mythic Society (Dissolution and Management) Act, 1976' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on November 3, 1975.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairman', 'member', 'Secretary', and 'Society'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: Establishes the Board of Management of the Mythic Society and declares it as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, empowered to acquire, hold, dispose of properties, and contract, subject to State Government approval for property disposal.

Specifies that the Board shall consist of not more than eleven members nominated by the State Government, with at least three possessing special knowledge in relevant subjects. The State Government appoints the Chairman and the Chairman, with approval, appoints the Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation from office of a member
main_sections.description: Allows a member of the Board to resign by giving notice to the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and casual vacancy
main_sections.description: States that each member holds office for three years. Casual vacancies are filled by fresh nomination, with the new member serving for the remainder of the original term.

Outlines the powers and duties of the Board, including maintaining and managing the Society to promote studies and research in allied subjects, providing for research, assisting in publishing books, receiving gifts and donations, and dealing with its property to advance its objects.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution and transfer of property of the Society
main_sections.description: Dissolves the Mythic Society on the appointed day, transferring all its property, rights, powers, and liabilities to the Board. It also addresses the construction of wills, deeds, or other documents favoring the Society to be construed as favoring the Board, and makes persons holding property of the Society accountable to the Board.

Mandates the creation and maintenance of a 'Mythic Society Fund' by the Board, into which all receipts will be paid and from which all expenses will be met. The fund is operated by the Chairman or an authorized person.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the State Government to give direction
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to issue directions to the Board, which the Board must carry out.
Requires the Board to frame a budget for each financial year and submit it to the State Government for approval, which may be with or without modifications.

Empowers the State Government to supersede the Board if it fails to perform its duties, persistently defaults, or exceeds its powers, after giving the Board an opportunity to make representations. During supersession, the State Government may direct how the Board's powers and duties are exercised, and its property shall vest in the State Government.
Authorizes the State Government to make rules, by notification, to carry out the objects of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board to make regulations
main_sections.description: Allows the Board to make regulations, with the State Government's prior approval, concerning board meetings, quorum, procedures, and the appointment and terms of service of its officers and servants.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Karnataka Ordinance No. 18 of 1975
main_sections.description: Repeals the Mythic Society (Dissolution and Management) Ordinance, 1975, and clarifies that anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: The Mythic Society is dissolved from the appointed day.
All property, rights, and liabilities of the Mythic Society are transferred to the Board of Management.
The Board shall manage the Society's affairs to promote the study and research of specified allied subjects.
The Board shall operate a 'Mythic Society Fund' for its receipts and expenses.
The State Government can issue directions to the Board.
The Board must frame and submit its budget to the State Government for approval.
The State Government can supersede the Board under certain conditions of non-performance or abuse of power.

penalties: Any person in possession of property or documents vested in the Board must account for and deliver them to the Chairman or authorized person. Failure to do so would imply liability to the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government, and the Board of Management of the Mythic Society.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the State Government to issue directions, approve budgets, supersede the Board, and make rules. The Board enforces its mandate through its stated powers and duties. The Chairman or authorized persons can take steps to secure properties.

rights: The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of properties (with State Government approval for disposal).
The Board has the right to contract and sue or be sued.
The Board has the right to receive gifts, donations, bequests, and transfers of property.
The Board has the right to take necessary steps for securing possession of its properties and documents.
duties: The Board has the duty to maintain and manage the Mythic Society to promote specific subjects.
The Board has the duty to provide for studies and research in these subjects.
The Board has the duty to help in producing and publishing books.
The Board has the duty to meet expenses and disbursements from the Board Fund.
The Board has the duty to carry out directions given by the State Government.
The Board has the duty to frame and submit its budget for approval.
obligations: The Board is obligated to apply all transferred property for the purposes for which it is constituted.
The Board is obligated to discharge and satisfy all debts and liabilities of the former Society.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Board: The State Government appoints a date for the establishment of the Board through a notification in the Official Gazette.
Board Member Nomination: The State Government nominates up to eleven members, ensuring at least three have expertise in relevant subjects. The Chairman is also appointed by the State Government.
Secretary Appointment: The Chairman, with State Government approval, appoints a Secretary.
Budget Approval: The Board frames an annual budget and submits it to the State Government for approval.

Superseding the Board: If the Board fails in its duties, the State Government can issue a supersession notification after giving the Board a chance to respond. The State Government then directs the exercise of powers and duties during the supersession period.
administration: The Board of Management of the Mythic Society, under the overall authority and direction of the State Government of Karnataka.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, coming into force from November 3, 1975.
Any property disposed of by the Board requires the previous approval of the State Government.
The State Government has the ultimate power to supersede the Board if it is not functioning correctly.

title: The Prevention of Destruction and Loss of Property Act, 1981
purpose: To provide for punishment of certain acts in respect of property and imposition of collective fine to recover the loss or damage sustained by such acts, following incidents of burning of motor vehicles, looting, and damage of public and private property.
scope: Applies to the State of Karnataka. It covers acts of mischief causing loss or damage to property, especially when committed during periods when assemblies are prohibited or are deemed unlawful assemblies, and also provides for collective fines on inhabitants of affected areas.

key_definitions.mischief: As defined in section 425 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, which involves causing wrongful loss or damage to property.
key_definitions.unlawful_assembly: As defined in section 141 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Prevention of Destruction and Loss of Property Act, 1981, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on June 16, 1981.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for committing mischief in respect of property
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for committing, attempting to commit, or abetting mischief causing loss or damage to property. It also covers causing loss or damage to property during prohibited assemblies or unlawful assemblies. The punishment includes imprisonment and fine.

States that persons accused or convicted of an offence under section 2 cannot be released on bail unless the prosecution has had an opportunity to oppose the application, with a proviso for cases where such an opportunity is not practicable.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to impose collective fine
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to impose a collective fine on inhabitants of an area if they are concerned in, abetting, instigating, harbouring offenders, or failing to assist in the commission of offences under section 2. It outlines the process for notification, proclamation, appeal, exemption, compensation, and recovery of the fine.
Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals the Prevention of Destruction and Loss of Property Ordinance, 1981, and provides that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Any person found guilty of committing or abetting mischief causing loss or damage to property will be punished with imprisonment of at least six months, extendable up to five years, and a fine up to two thousand rupees.
Rule: Individuals accused or convicted of an offence under Section 2 cannot be released on bail without the prosecution's opportunity to object.

Rule: The State Government can impose a collective fine on the inhabitants of an area if they are found to be involved in or aiding offences under Section 2, or failing to assist in apprehending offenders.
Rule: Inhabitants aggrieved by the imposition or apportionment of a collective fine can petition the State Government or a specified authority for exemption or modification within thirty days.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to five years.
Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
Collective fine imposed on inhabitants of an area, with apportionment among them.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is the primary authority for imposing collective fines and making rules. Courts would likely be involved in prosecuting individual offences under Section 2.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Individual offences are prosecuted in courts. Collective fines are imposed by notification, proclaimed, and recovered as fines imposed by a Magistrate, subject to appeals and exemptions.

rights: Right to petition the State Government or specified authority for exemption from or modification of collective fines within thirty days of notification.
Right to a reasonable opportunity of being heard before a decision is made on a petition regarding collective fines.
Right to be exempted from paying collective fine if the inhabitant has suffered loss or damage to their property in the manner stated in Section 2.
duties: Duty to not commit or abet mischief causing loss or damage to property.
Duty to not cause loss or damage to property during prohibited assemblies or unlawful assemblies.
Duty of inhabitants in an area where offences are committed to assist in discovering or apprehending offenders and not suppress material evidence.
obligations: Obligation to pay apportioned collective fine if not exempted or modified.
Obligation to cooperate with authorities during inquiries related to collective fines.

key_procedures: Procedure for imposing collective fine: Inquiry by State Government, satisfaction of involvement of inhabitants, notification in Official Gazette, proclamation in the area.
Procedure for aggrieved persons: Filing a petition within thirty days of notification for exemption or modification, hearing by State Government or specified authority, passing of an order.
Procedure for recovery of collective fine: Recovery in the manner provided by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for fines imposed by a court.
administration: The State Government (of Karnataka) is responsible for administering the Act, including making rules and imposing collective fines.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, deemed to have come into force on June 16, 1981.
Courts may impose lesser punishment than prescribed for offences under Section 2, with reasons to be recorded in writing.
The imposition of collective fine is aimed at deterring inhabitants from being involved in or failing to prevent destruction and loss of property.
The State Government may use collected collective fines to compensate persons who suffered loss or damage to their property.

title: The Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences Act, 1994
purpose: To establish and incorporate a university in the State of Karnataka for the purpose of ensuring proper and systematic instruction, teaching, training, and research in modern medicine and Indian Systems of Medicine.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka. It applies to health sciences education, including modern medicine and Indian Systems of Medicine, and the establishment and functioning of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences.

key_definitions.affiliated_college: A college or institution situated within the University Area and affiliated to the University in accordance with prescribed Statutes, including those deemed affiliated.
key_definitions.approved_institution: A hospital, health centre, affiliated college, or other institution recognized by the University for training purposes required for a degree, diploma, or other academic distinction.
key_definitions.health_sciences: Modern scientific medicine in all its branches (preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative), including surgery, obstetrics, gynecology, pharmacy, dental sciences, nursing, allied subjects, and Indian Systems of Medicine.
key_definitions.indian_systems_of_medicine: Includes Ayurveda, Unani, Homeopathy, Naturopathy, Yoga, and other prescribed disciplines.
key_definitions.university: The Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences, established under section 3 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Karnataka), and the date of its commencement, which is to be notified by the State Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'affiliated college', 'approved institution', 'health sciences', 'Indian Systems of Medicine', 'University', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences with jurisdiction over the whole of Karnataka. It declares the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire and dispose of property, and to sue and be sued. It also specifies the headquarters of the University and its nature as both a teaching and affiliating university.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the extensive powers and functions of the University, including providing instruction and training in health sciences, research, awarding degrees, establishing and administering colleges and institutions, affiliating colleges, appointing staff, managing finances, and generally furthering the objects of the University.

Deals with the exclusive jurisdiction of the University over health sciences education in Karnataka. It prohibits other affiliations without consent and deems previous affiliations to other universities withdrawn or transferred to this University.

Ensures that no person is excluded from any University office, membership, or admission to academic distinctions or courses of study on grounds of sex, race, creed, class, place of birth, religious belief, or political opinion. It allows for exceptions with government sanction, such as exclusively women's colleges or reserved seats for backward classes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the University authorities (Senate, Syndicate, etc.) are responsible for the enforcement of the Act, as guided by its provisions and prescribed Statutes, Ordinances, and Rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the University to grant or withdraw affiliation, recognition, degrees, and through the administrative and academic control mechanisms established by the Act and its subordinate legislation.

rights: Right of students to admission without discrimination (subject to reservations).
Right to receive instruction, training, and academic distinctions.
Right to access University facilities and resources.
duties: Duty of the University to ensure proper and systematic instruction, teaching, training, and research in health sciences.
Duty to maintain the highest possible standards of academic excellence.
Duty to exercise control over students for their health, well-being, and discipline.
Duty to manage funds and property appropriately.
Duty to ensure fairness and transparency in admissions and academic processes.
obligations: Obligation of colleges and institutions to seek affiliation and adhere to University standards.
Obligation of students to abide by University rules and regulations.
Obligation of the State Government to provide notifications and approvals as required by the Act.

key_procedures: Affiliation of colleges: Colleges must seek affiliation from the University and meet prescribed standards.
Granting of degrees/diplomas: Students must pursue approved courses of study, pass examinations, or conduct satisfactory research.
Making of Statutes, Ordinances, and Rules: These are made by University authorities and approved as per procedures outlined in the Act.
administration: The Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences, as established by the Act, is the primary administrative body. The State Government also plays a supervisory and approval role.
important_notes: The headquarters of the University was changed from Mysore to Bangalore by Act 11 of 1998.
The Act prevails over other enactments in case of conflict regarding the establishment and functioning of the University.

title: The Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate in public interest, its transfer to a trust for proper management, preservation of valuable assets (tree growth, paintings, art objects, carvings), and establishment of an Art Gallery-cum-Museum.
scope: The Act applies to the Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate, including specific lands mentioned in Schedule I, movable properties, buildings, jewelry, paintings, and art works found on such lands, belonging to the owners or transferees. It also covers the rights, title, and interests of the owners and transferees in relation to the estate. Geographically, it pertains to the estate within Karnataka.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of coming into force of this Act or any of its provisions.
key_definitions.Board: Board of Trustees established under section 21 of this Act.
key_definitions.Commissioner: Commissioner of Payment appointed under section 12 of this Act.
key_definitions.Executive Officer: Executive Officer appointed under section 23 of this Act.
key_definitions.owners: Deceased Dr. Svetoslav Roerich and deceased Mrs. Devikarani Roerich, to whom the land specified in Schedule I belonged, and includes their heirs or legal representatives claiming title.
key_definitions.Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate: The lands specified in Schedule I belonging to the deceased owners or their transferees, including all movable properties and buildings situated on such lands and belonging to the owners or transferees.
key_definitions.transferee: A person to whom any land specified in Schedule I has been alienated by the owners by sale, gift, mortgage, lease, or otherwise on or after January 1, 1991.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the State Government through notification in the Official Gazette, with different dates possible for different provisions.

Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Commissioner', 'Executive Officer', 'owners', 'Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate', 'Schedule', 'specified date', 'transferee', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting of the Estate in the State Government
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate and the rights, title, and interest of the owners and transferees shall stand transferred to and vest absolutely in the State Government.

Details the consequences of vesting, including the inclusion of all assets, rights, properties (movable and immovable), and documents. It also declares that vested properties are freed from encumbrances and that pending legal proceedings shall continue by or against the State Government or the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Power of State Government to direct vesting of the Estate in the Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to direct, by notification, that the Estate vested in the State Government shall instead vest in the Board with effect from the appointed day. Upon such vesting, the Board becomes the owner, and its rights and liabilities become those of the State Government under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amount to be given to owners, transferees and other interested persons
main_sections.description: Specifies that for the transfer and vesting of the Estate, the Government shall pay an amount of Rs. 5 crores (Rupees five hundred lakhs) by depositing it with the Commissioner, to be disbursed to entitled persons as per Chapter IV.
Declares that this Act has an overriding effect over any other law for the time being in force or any decree or order of any court, tribunal, or other authority to the extent of any inconsistency.
Provides for penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: The Roerich and Devikarani Roerich Estate shall be acquired and vested in the State Government on the appointed day.
Upon vesting, the Estate is freed from all trusts, obligations, mortgages, leases, charges, liens, and other encumbrances.
Owners and transferees remain liable for their liabilities related to the Estate that arose before the appointed day.
The State Government can direct the Estate to vest in a Board of Trustees established for its management.
A sum of Rs. 5 crores is to be paid by the Government for the acquisition, which will be disbursed to entitled persons by a Commissioner of Payments.
This Act has an overriding effect over other laws and decrees.
The Board of Trustees is responsible for the management and preservation of the Estate, including its valuable assets.

penalties: Penalties are prescribed for contravention of the provisions of the Act (as per Section 34).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Board of Trustees, Commissioner of Payments, and appointed Executive Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal provisions for acquisition, vesting, transfer, management, disbursement of amounts, and penalties for non-compliance. Enforcement also includes the power to make rules and remove difficulties.

rights: Owners, transferees, and other interested persons are entitled to receive payment from the acquired amount in accordance with their rights and interests.
Mortgagees, leaseholders, and holders of other interests are entitled to claim payment out of the specified amounts.
The State Government has the right to direct the vesting of the Estate in the Board.
duties: The State Government has the duty to acquire the Estate in public interest and provide for its proper management.
The Board of Trustees has the duty to manage and preserve the Estate, including its valuable tree growth, paintings, art objects, and carvings.
Persons in charge of the management of the Estate have duties as specified in Section 10.
Persons possessing assets, etc., have a duty to account for them (Section 11).
obligations: Owners and transferees are liable for certain prior liabilities related to the Estate.
Holders of mortgages, charges, leases, or other interests must provide intimation to the Commissioner.
The Board of Trustees has an obligation to establish an Art Gallery-cum-Museum.

key_procedures: Acquisition and Vesting: The Estate vests in the State Government on the appointed day and can subsequently be directed to vest in the Board.

Payment and Disbursement: The State Government pays Rs. 5 crores to the Commissioner of Payments, who then disburses the amount to eligible owners, transferees, and other interested persons after examining and admitting claims according to laid-down priorities.
Management of the Estate: The Board of Trustees, supported by an Executive Officer and other officers, is responsible for the management and preservation of the Estate.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government and a Board of Trustees established under the Act. The Commissioner of Payments and Executive Officer also play crucial administrative roles.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it prevails over other laws in case of conflict.
Liabilities of owners or transferees incurred before the appointed day are not enforceable against the State Government or the Board, except as otherwise provided.
The Act provides for the establishment of an Art Gallery-cum-Museum for the preservation and display of art objects.
Amendments made by Act 19 of 2001 allow the Commissioner of Payment to refer matters of doubt or dispute regarding entitlement to receive amounts to the Civil Court.

title: THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND THE SCHEDULED TRIBES (PREVENTION OF ATROCITIES) ACT, 1989
purpose: To prevent the commission of offences of atrocities against the members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, to provide for Special Courts for the trial of such offences and for the relief and rehabilitation of the victims of such offences, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of India except the State of Jammu & Kashmir. It covers offences of atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.atrocity: An offence punishable under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.code: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974).
key_definitions.scheduled_castes_and_scheduled_tribes: Shall have the meanings assigned to them respectively under clause (24) and clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution.
key_definitions.special_court: A Court of Session specified as a Special Court in section 14.
key_definitions.special_public_prosecutor: A Public Prosecutor specified as a Special Public Prosecutor or an advocate referred to in section 15.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title as 'The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989', its territorial extent to the whole of India except Jammu & Kashmir, and the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'atrocity', 'Code', 'Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes', 'Special Court', and 'Special Public Prosecutor'. It also clarifies that words and expressions not defined in the Act but defined in the Code or the Indian Penal Code shall have their respective meanings.

Lists various acts that constitute atrocities when committed by a person not belonging to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe against a member of these communities. It prescribes punishments ranging from imprisonment of six months to five years and fine, with enhanced punishments for specific grave offences like fabricating false evidence leading to conviction or death, committing mischief by fire or explosives, or committing offences under the Indian Penal Code on the ground of caste/tribe identity.

Prescribes punishment for public servants, not belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, who wilfully neglect their duties under this Act. The punishment ranges from imprisonment of six months to one year.

Provides for enhanced punishment for individuals convicted of an offence under this Chapter for a second or subsequent offence, with imprisonment not less than one year and up to the punishment provided for that offence.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code
main_sections.description: States that certain provisions of the Indian Penal Code, including section 34, Chapters III, IV, V, VA, section 149, and Chapter XXIII, shall apply for the purposes of this Act as they apply to the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture of property of certain persons
main_sections.description: Empowers the Special Court to declare forfeiture of property used for the commission of an offence under this Chapter. It also allows for the attachment of a person's property during trial, which can be forfeited to realise any fine imposed.

Establishes presumptions in prosecution for offences under this Chapter. It presumes abetment if financial assistance is rendered to an accused and presumes common intention or object if a group offence is a sequel to an existing dispute.

Allows the State Government to confer powers exercisable by a police officer under the Code (including arrest, investigation, and prosecution) on any State Government officer for prevention or coping with offences under the Act. It also mandates assistance from police and other government officers.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of person likely to commit offence
main_sections.description: Empowers the Special Court to direct a person likely to commit an offence under Chapter II to remove themselves from 'Scheduled Areas' or 'tribal areas' for a period not exceeding two years, specifying the route and time. Grounds for the order must be communicated.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure on failure of person to remove himself from area and re-entry thereon
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure if a person fails to remove themselves as directed under section 10 or re-enters the area without permission. The Special Court may order their arrest and removal.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than six months but extending to five years and fine for various atrocities.
Imprisonment for life and fine for fabricating false evidence leading to capital punishment of an SC/ST member.
Imprisonment for life and fine for committing mischief by fire or explosive substance to destroy a place of worship or dwelling.
Imprisonment for life and fine for committing offences under IPC with imprisonment of 10 years or more against SC/ST persons or property.
Imprisonment for a term not less than one year and up to the punishment provided for the offence for public servants committing offences under section 3.
Imprisonment for a term not less than six months but extending to one year for neglect of duties by public servants.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Special Courts, empowered police officers (or other conferred officers under section 9), and other government officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation, prosecution by Special Public Prosecutors, trial by Special Courts, and imposition of penalties and forfeiture of property. Powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution can be conferred on specific officers.

rights: Members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have the right to be protected from atrocities.
Victims of atrocities have rights to relief and rehabilitation (though specific provisions are not detailed in this excerpt).
duties: Public servants have a duty to perform their roles under this Act without wilful neglect.
obligations: Individuals are obligated not to commit acts defined as atrocities.
Individuals are obligated to comply with orders of removal from areas if deemed likely to commit atrocities.

key_procedures: Investigation and prosecution of offences of atrocities.
Trial of offences by Special Courts.
Procedure for removal of persons likely to commit atrocities from specified areas.
Procedure for arrest and removal of persons failing to comply with removal orders.
Forfeiture of property used for commission of offences or attached during trial.
Presumption of abetment or common intention in certain circumstances.
administration: The Act is administered through Special Courts and by State Government officers on whom powers are conferred, with overall oversight and implementation guided by the Central and State Governments.
important_notes: The Act's provisions regarding Scheduled Areas and tribal areas refer to Article 244 of the Constitution, indicating a specific focus on these regions.
The Act emphasizes the role of Special Courts and Special Public Prosecutors for effective trial and prosecution.

title: The Karnataka Irrigation and Certain Other Law (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965 and the Karnataka Irrigation (Levy of Betterment Contribution and Water Rate) Act, 1957 to enable water users societies to become members of irrigation projects and to entrust supply, levy and collection of water rates to a designated government company.
scope: Applies to irrigation projects and water rate administration in the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and deems commencement from the specified retrospective date.
Amends provisions of the Karnataka Irrigation Act, 1965 relating to participation of water users societies.
Amends provisions relating to levy, supply and collection of water rate and entrusts functions to Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amended statutory powers relating to irrigation management and water rate collection.

rights: Participation of water users societies in irrigation management
duties: Payment of prescribed water rates

key_procedures: Entrustment of water supply and collection functions
Membership of water users societies in irrigation projects
administration: Administered by the State Government through designated irrigation authorities and government companies.
important_notes: Contains retrospective commencement
Linked to restructuring of irrigation management

title: The Karnataka State Law University Act, 2009
purpose: To establish and incorporate a Law University dedicated to study and research of law in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to legal education, affiliation of law colleges and administration of the Karnataka State Law University across the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.university: The Karnataka State Law University established under the Act
key_definitions.academic council: The Academic Council constituted under the Act
key_definitions.syndicate: The Syndicate of the University constituted under the Act

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the Karnataka State Law University as a body corporate with teaching and affiliating powers.
Sets out objectives including legal education, research, legal awareness and professional training.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the University
main_sections.description: Details academic, administrative, financial and affiliating powers of the University.

penalties: Punishment for abetment of examination offences
Disciplinary action for violation of duties
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: University authorities and State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory powers of the University, inspections and disciplinary mechanisms.

rights: Right to admission subject to prescribed qualifications
Right of affiliated colleges to University privileges
duties: Duty of teachers to perform examination work
Obligation of students to maintain discipline

key_procedures: Affiliation and withdrawal of affiliation of law colleges
Appointment of University officers
Conduct of examinations and award of degrees
administration: Administered by University authorities including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate and Academic Council.
important_notes: University jurisdiction extends to the whole State of Karnataka
Overrides other university laws in matters of legal education

title: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2006
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 to address administrative, revenue and land management issues.
scope: Applies to land revenue administration, assessment, grant, regularisation and revenue jurisdiction in the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title and commencement of the Amendment Act.
Introduces amendments to provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

penalties: Penalties for unauthorised occupation or misuse of land
Recovery of arrears of land revenue
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Officers including Deputy Commissioner and Tahsildar
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory revenue proceedings, recovery mechanisms and summary eviction where applicable.

rights: Rights of occupants subject to lawful grant and use of land
duties: Payment of land revenue
Compliance with land use conditions

key_procedures: Assessment and recovery of land revenue
Regularisation and grant of land
Revenue appeals and revisions
administration: Administered by the Revenue Department of the State through designated revenue officers.
important_notes: Amends a principal land revenue statute
Part of continuing reforms in land administration

title: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2004
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 in order to modify certain provisions relating to land revenue administration and land management.
scope: Applies to land revenue administration, grant, use, regularisation and related revenue matters in the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Amendment Act and its commencement.
Introduces amendments to specified provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue authorities under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amended land revenue provisions and revenue proceedings.

administration: Administered by the Revenue Department of the State through designated revenue officers.

title: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: To amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 to make further changes relating to land revenue, land use and administrative procedures.
scope: Applies to land and land revenue matters governed by the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 within the State of Karnataka.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title and commencement of the Amendment Act.
Amends selected provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue authorities under the principal Act
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through enforcement of amended land revenue provisions.

administration: Administered by the State Revenue Department through statutory revenue machinery.

title: The Karnataka Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 in relation to land administration and revenue matters.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka and applies to matters governed by the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title and commencement of the Amendment Act.
Makes amendments to certain provisions of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue authorities under the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying the amended provisions through revenue administration processes.

administration: Administered by the State Government through its Revenue Department and officers.

title: The Karnataka Control of Organized Crimes Act, 2000
purpose: To make special provisions for prevention and control of organized crime and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Karnataka and covers organized crime syndicates, their activities, investigation, prosecution, and trial through special courts.

key_definitions.organized crime: Any continuing unlawful activity by an individual or group using violence, intimidation or coercion for pecuniary or other advantage.
key_definitions.organized crime syndicate: A group of two or more persons acting singly or collectively as a syndicate or gang indulging in organized crime.
key_definitions.continuing unlawful activity: An activity prohibited by law, punishable with imprisonment of three years or more, with more than one charge sheet filed within the preceding ten years.

main_sections.description: Provides the name of the Act, its application to the whole State of Karnataka and commencement.
Defines key terms such as organized crime, organized crime syndicate, continuing unlawful activity and competent authority.
Prescribes stringent punishments including life imprisonment or death in certain cases, along with fines.

penalties: Imprisonment for not less than five years which may extend to life
Death penalty in cases resulting in death
Heavy monetary fines
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Special Courts and Competent Authority appointed under the Act
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation by authorized officers, interception of communications with approval, and trial by Special Courts.

key_procedures: Authorization for interception of communications
Special procedure for evidence and confessions
Trial by Special Courts
administration: Administered through Special Courts, Competent Authorities, and designated investigating officers.
important_notes: Overrides inconsistent provisions of other laws
Special evidentiary rules apply

title: The Karnataka Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To amend various taxation laws in the State of Karnataka to give effect to budget proposals and related matters.
scope: Amends multiple state taxation enactments including agricultural income tax, sales tax, luxury tax, entry tax and entertainment tax.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act and commencement from 1 April 2002.
Amends provisions of the Karnataka Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1957.
Validates certain assessments, levies, and collections made under the amended laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tax authorities under the respective taxation laws
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Assessment, collection and recovery as per amended taxation statutes.

duties: Duty of taxpayers to comply with amended tax provisions

key_procedures: Revised assessment procedures
Validation of past actions
administration: Administered by the commercial tax and revenue authorities of the State.
important_notes: Amendments are consequential to budget proposals
Certain provisions have retrospective validation

Condonation procedure for delayed filings

purpose: To provide for the establishment, incorporation and governance of State Universities in Karnataka and to consolidate laws relating to State Universities.
scope: Applies to all State Universities established or deemed to be established by or under State law in Karnataka.

key_definitions.academic council: The principal academic body of the University
key_definitions.syndicate: The executive authority of the University

Declares Universities as bodies corporate with perpetual succession.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory powers vested in University authorities and oversight by the State Government.

Conduct of examinations

scope: Applies to all State Universities governed by the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title and commencement of the Amendment Act.
Introduces amendments to specified sections of the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By enforcing amended provisions through University administration.

important_notes: Further amendment to the principal Universities Act
Focuses on administrative restructuring

key_definitions.input tax: Tax paid or payable on purchases of goods used in the course of business.
key_definitions.output tax: Tax charged on sale of goods.

Provides for levy of value added tax on sale or purchase of goods.

main_sections.section_title: Output tax, input tax and net tax

Payment of tax

Assessment and reassessment
Appeals and revisions

Provides for self-assessment and audit-based compliance

title: The Karnataka Rent Act, 1999
purpose: To regulate rent and eviction of tenants and to balance the interests of landlords and tenants in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to specified residential and non-residential buildings in Karnataka, subject to exclusions based on rent and area.

key_definitions.landlord: A person entitled to receive rent of a building.
key_definitions.tenant: A person by whom or on whose account rent is payable for a building.
key_definitions.standard rent: Rent determined under the provisions of the Act.

Penalties for violation of rent control provisions

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adjudication by Rent Courts and execution of their orders.

Maintenance obligations of landlord

Eviction proceedings before Rent Court

title: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020
purpose: To provide an independent legislation for governance of Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike with greater decentralization and public participation.
scope: Applies to the municipal governance of the city of Bengaluru.

key_definitions.chief commissioner: The executive head of the Corporation
key_definitions.ward committee: A committee constituted for each ward under the Act

main_sections.description: Establishes the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike as a body corporate.

Penalties for unauthorized constructions

title: The Registration Act, 1908
purpose: To consolidate the law relating to the registration of documents in order to provide public notice, prevent fraud, and ensure legal certainty in transactions affecting property and other rights.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as originally enacted), and applies to compulsory and optional registration of documents affecting immovable property and certain other transactions.

key_definitions.immovable property: Includes land, buildings, hereditary allowances, rights to ways, lights, ferries, fisheries or any other benefit arising out of land.
key_definitions.lease: Includes a counterpart, kabuliyat, an undertaking to cultivate or occupy, and an agreement to lease.
key_definitions.registration: The formal recording of documents by the registering authority under the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the name of the Act, its territorial extent and commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Documents of which registration is compulsory
main_sections.description: Specifies categories of documents relating to immovable property and other transactions that must be compulsorily registered.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of non-registration of documents required to be registered
main_sections.description: Provides that unregistered compulsory documents do not affect immovable property or confer legal rights, subject to limited exceptions.

penalties: Penalties for false statements or impersonation during registration
Penalties for registering officers for misconduct

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory registration machinery, inquiries, refusal orders, and prosecution where applicable.

title: The Karnataka Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for uniform regulation, supervision and administration of Hindu Religious Institutions and Charitable Endowments in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to notified Hindu religious institutions and charitable endowments in Karnataka, subject to exclusions and classifications provided under the Act.

key_definitions.notified institution: A Hindu religious institution or charitable endowment notified by the Government under the Act.
key_definitions.charitable endowment: Property or fund endowed for charitable purposes associated with Hindu religious institutions.
key_definitions.commissioner: The Commissioner appointed under the Act for administration and supervision.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its application within Karnataka and commencement.
Provides for qualifications, appointment and service conditions of archakas.
Provides for constitution and powers of committees for management of institutions.

Penalties for unauthorised alienation of institution property

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, surcharge proceedings, removal of trustees and prosecution.

duties: Duty of trustees and managers to safeguard properties and funds

key_procedures: Notification and classification of institutions
Audit of accounts
Inquiry into maladministration
administration: Administered by the State Government through the Commissioner and statutory committees.
important_notes: Introduced uniform regulation replacing multiple earlier enactments

title: The Karnataka Electricity Reform Act, 1999
purpose: To restructure and reform the electricity industry in Karnataka, establish an independent regulatory commission, and promote efficiency, competition and consumer protection.
scope: Applies to the electricity industry in the State of Karnataka including generation, transmission, distribution and supply of electricity.

Penalties for non-compliance with Commission orders

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through regulatory orders, compliance directions, fines and prosecution.

Duty to meet performance standards

Tariff determination

important_notes: Introduced independent regulation of the power sector

purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to co-operative societies in the State of Karnataka and to promote orderly development of the co-operative movement with State participation and supervision.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory inspections, inquiries, dispute adjudication, recovery proceedings and prosecution.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, stoppage of water supply, recovery of costs, fines and prosecution.

title: The Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for planned development of land, regulation of land use, and preparation and execution of town planning schemes in the State of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to local planning areas, development authorities, planning authorities and land development activities throughout Karnataka.

key_definitions.planning authority: An authority constituted for preparation and enforcement of development plans
key_definitions.development plan: A plan for development or redevelopment of land including zoning regulations

main_sections.description: Provides for preparation, approval and enforcement of outline development plans and regulation of land and building development.
Provides for preparation, approval, revision and enforcement of comprehensive development plans.
Regulates preparation, sanction, execution and financing of town planning schemes including reconstitution of plots and compensation.

penalties: Penalty for unauthorised development
Penalty for violation of sanctioned plans
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Planning Authorities and State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through refusal or revocation of permissions, penalties, demolition orders and prosecution.

rights: Right to apply for development permission
Right to compensation in specified cases
duties: Compliance with development plans and zoning regulations

key_procedures: Preparation and approval of development plans
Grant of permission for development
Regularisation or demolition of unauthorised constructions
administration: Administered by the Urban Development Department through planning and development authorities.
important_notes: Provides for regularisation of certain unauthorised developments
Overrides inconsistent provisions in other laws

title: The Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993
purpose: To establish a three-tier Panchayat Raj system and provide for democratic decentralisation and local self-government in rural areas of Karnataka.
scope: Applies to Grama Panchayats, Taluk Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats across the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.grama panchayat: The basic unit of local self-government at village level
key_definitions.taluk panchayat: The intermediate tier of Panchayat Raj administration

main_sections.description: Provides for constitution, elections, powers, duties and administration of Grama Panchayats.
Provides for constitution, powers, duties and administration of Taluk Panchayats.
Provides for constitution, powers, duties and administration of Zilla Panchayats.

penalties: Penalties for election offences
Penalties for misconduct by members or officers
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, Panchayat authorities and Election Commission
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, suspension, removal, penalties and prosecution.

rights: Right to vote in Panchayat elections
Right to participate in local governance
duties: Duty of Panchayats to implement development schemes
Duty to maintain public services and assets

key_procedures: Panchayat elections
Preparation of development plans
Levy and collection of local taxes
administration: Administered by the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department.
important_notes: Provides reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women
Establishes State Election Commission and Finance Commission

title: The Karnataka Souharda Sahakari Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for recognition, encouragement and voluntary formation of co-operatives based on self-help, mutual aid and democratic management.
scope: Applies to Souharda Sahakari co-operatives registered under the Act in the State of Karnataka.

key_definitions.souharda sahakari: A co-operative registered under this Act based on mutual aid and self-regulation
key_definitions.board: The board of directors of a co-operative

main_sections.description: Provides for registration, corporate status, bye-laws and structural changes of co-operatives.
Regulates membership, board composition, elections and management functions.
Provides for resolution of disputes through the Registrar and appellate mechanisms.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act or bye-laws
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Souharda Sahakaris
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, supersession, liquidation and prosecution.

rights: Right of members to democratic participation
Right to access co-operative services
duties: Compliance with bye-laws
Proper utilisation of funds and assets

key_procedures: Registration of co-operatives
Conduct of elections
Audit and inquiry
administration: Administered by the Co-operation Department through the Registrar.
important_notes: Promotes autonomy with minimal government interference
Allows conversion from co-operative societies under the 1959 Act
